# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK I.
e 3
<meta>catchword: lost bod-</meta>

<margin>The Last Judgment is nothing other than the separation of the pure from the impure, and the good from the evil, and this is to happen through the presence of Christ.</margin>
...the purified celestials will raise up to the heavens. In such a way, the <term>Last Judgment</term> <note>The final trial of humanity at the end of time.</note> will accompany the state of heaven, whereby the pure will be separated from the impure, and the good from the evil. This is alluded to in the poem by Maro <note>original: "Maronis." This refers to the famous Roman poet Virgil (Publius Vergilius Maro).</note> who says:

> Until the long day, when the cycle of time is complete,
> has removed the ingrained stain, and left pure
> the ethereal sense. <note>A quote from Virgil’s *Aeneid*, Book VI, describing the purification of souls.</note>

<margin>I believe in the Holy Spirit.</margin>
Read and consider these things for yourself. That these events will occur through the advent and presence of Christ is clear from this: although the presence and grace of Christ the Savior are present everywhere and always to everyone, mortals nonetheless do not grasp them unless the barrier of the "turning sword" <note>original: "uersatilis gladij." A reference to the flaming sword guarding Eden in Genesis 3:24, often interpreted by Ricius as a metaphysical barrier between the material and divine worlds.</note> is removed, and the rotation and movement of heaven cease. Therefore, when the movement of the heavens stops, the obstacle will immediately be taken away, and in that same moment, the advent and grace of Christ the Redeemer will be present. His bright presence will indeed be salvation and life for the good, who share a common bond with the Savior. But for the wicked, whose filthy and earthly habits are opposed to the purity of the Redeemer (as darkness is to light), the same Savior will bring perpetual misery and irrevocable destruction. For it is innate to the nature of every thing to associate with what is like itself, and it immediately eliminates what is contrary. Therefore, it can be clearly judged from these things that the judgment will occur with the advent and presence of Christ the mediator. Thus the truth is proved: that Christ will come to judge the living and the dead. The clause that follows, **I believe in the Holy Spirit**, is manifest from the previously discussed mystery of the Trinity. For by the inexhaustible bounty of the Holy Spirit, every gift of grace and mercy is poured into us from the Father of lights through Christ the Lord, our mediator.

<margin>The Holy Catholic Church.</margin>
<margin>The communion of saints.</margin>
<margin>By what reasoning believing in the Holy Catholic Church and the communion of saints is necessary for salvation.</margin>
The aforementioned clause is subjoined: **The Holy Catholic Church**. The very nature of salvation demonstrates that it is necessary to believe in this for one's soul. For we admitted at the beginning of our disputation that true salvation is a state in which one possesses and enjoys the <term>Highest Good</term> <note>original: "summo bono." In philosophy, this is the ultimate source of all value and happiness, identified here with God.</note>. No one, however, attains this except through adherence and union with that same Highest Good. We have shown that this exact union is given only in the unique Mediator. Therefore, if individuals or the many are to become sharers of true salvation, it is necessary that they embrace one another and cohere together in a mutual bond—like the various members of a single individual human being—who are all coupled in the Mediator with the Highest Good itself, just as all bodily powers are united in the thinking faculty with the intellectual form of man.

Since, therefore, the **Holy Catholic Church** designates nothing other than the assembly of good and holy men, which it is necessary to join and cling to for eternal salvation, it is rightly necessary to believe not only that the Holy Catholic Church exists, but also the **communion of saints**, through which we are made participants in all the perfections contained within the framework of the entire <term>Mystical Body</term> <note>A theological term for the Church as a spiritual organism with Christ as the head.</note>.

<margin>The forgiveness of sins.</margin>
But because the soul of mortals cannot escape or avoid being somehow defiled by the contagion of the earthly and physical body, it contracts vice. He who desires to be made a member of the Mystical Body of Christ must wipe away all the filth and stain of vices and sins. This cleansing we call the **forgiveness of sins**. Therefore, it is fitting to add the forgiveness of sins to the points mentioned above.

<margin>The resurrection of the flesh.</margin>
Furthermore, since the consummate perfection of anything is to obtain everything that its innate faculty and aptitude requires, and since the rational soul (being the "act" of the body, situated on the horizon of eternity and time) by its very nature craves the company of both God its creator and its own body, it follows that the soul—once it has lost the company of the body—can never be an exact participant in eternal salvation until it recovers the lost body. This necessarily follows the celestial cycle, the consummation of the age, and the Last Judgment; for judgment (as I explained a little before) requires that each of the composite things be dissolved, and that it finally reach that toward which it is inclined by its own nature or by an acquired habit.

Since, therefore, the **resurrection of the dead** is nothing other than the recovery of the once lost...

-># PAUL RICIUS<-

...if it suggests the reassumption of the body, the clause is rightly added, *The resurrection of the flesh.*

<margin>The transmutative skill, which they call **Alchemy**, reveals the nature and qualities of the bodies of those rising from the dead.</margin>
But perhaps you will think to yourself and hesitate, saying: If the last judgment is nothing other than the dissolution of all mixtures, how then is the resurrection of the dead to be believed in that judgment? How can an organic body—which is the greatest mixture of all things that can be born—be reassumed? Know, therefore, that the bodies of those rising will not be joined together by a simple mixture, but rather purified by the release of fire. For those bodies will be very little subject to change or alteration, unlike other bodies piled up through movement. Instead, through the conflagration of fire, having been tested and purged (like the element of the stars), they will rise bright, agile, and pure in every way. 

Indeed, it is by the same law by which even now—through a certain artistry of fire—a substance is drawn from any mixed thing, which those skilled in that art call the <term>quintessence</term> <note>original: "quintam essentiam." In alchemy, this is the "fifth element" or the purest essence of a substance, beyond the four classical elements of earth, air, fire, and water.</note>. This is not because some fifth celestial element is actually present, but because it corresponds to it in a certain proportion. For this substance is brought forth clear (as the senses judge) and pure through the testing of fire, while a mass that is earthy, thick, dark, and useless remains. And that which has been brought forth not only loses none of its vigor, but even exercises its power and work far more precisely and sublimely. For the resurrection of these things will accompany the sound and cycle of the great celestial trumpet; and with the fire blazing, there will be a dissolution of mixtures, an expiation of all things, and a separation of the pure from the impure, and the good from the evil.

<margin>Why the consummation of the age is carried out through **fire**, and not rather through some other kind of destruction.</margin>
But I see you still doubting and asking yourself in secret (and not without reason) what logic suggests that the consummation of the age and the future judgment should happen through a conflagration of fire, rather than by a disaster of waters or some other event and destruction. Pay attention to this and be wise: for the same reason that the "state of heaven" <note>The fixed, eternal condition of the universe after the end of time.</note> follows, the consummation of the age also arrives through fire. For the state of heaven (as you know) happens because the <term>moving soul</term> <note>original: "anima motrix." A concept from Aristotelian and medieval cosmology where celestial spheres are moved by intelligent spirits.</note> of heaven finally fixes its gaze upon the most desired Creator of all things. From this, that soul is then affected by a joy and exultation that is more vehement (as I recounted a little earlier from the opinion of the **man of Cordoba** <note>original: "Cordubensis." This refers to the philosopher Averroes (Ibn Rushd), born in Córdoba, Spain, whose works on the soul and the heavens were highly influential.</note>) the more it enjoys that most beautiful and lovable sight. 

Since, therefore, the moving soul of heaven is by its nature inherent in the body, it is impossible for that immense affection of the soul not to overflow into the body joined to it, in a bodily manner. Now, immense joy and exultation of the spirit bring forth vehement heat and ardor into all the limbs of the body—just as we, who are a <term>microcosm</term> <note>A "little world"; the idea that the human being is a miniature reflection of the larger universe (the macrocosm).</note>, perceive through clear experience. For from a sad thought of the soul, the body itself becomes stiff, foul, and numb, and is finally reduced to wasting away. On the other hand, from joy and pleasantness of spirit, it grows warm, shines, and is made agile. Therefore, just as the "state of heaven" follows from the stable and firm gaze of the celestial soul, so from the abundance of joy and the ineffable delight of the soul, a splendor and light—beyond the usual order of the moving heavens—shines forth in that very celestial and elementary body. By this, ardor, heat, and scorching rays are spread through the whole earthly globe, from which follows the conflagration of fire, the dissolution of all things, their consummation, their purging, and finally, the resurrection of the flesh.

<margin>And life eternal.</margin>
The fact that the Creed closes in the last place with **eternal life** is the reason and end of all the preceding points. You, together with your brothers, **Philadelphus** <note>The "Brother-Lover."</note> and **Philosomatus** <note>The "Body-Lover."</note>, have established the truth of this as the goal, base, and foundation of the whole business through long examination and the most exquisite arguments. Therefore, I think we should by no means linger on further scrutiny of this. But these things, as the logic of an introduction and compendium requires, seem sufficient for a true understanding of the things to be believed, and for the path of eternal salvation. As for the remaining appendices of these matters, and whatever the holy School of Theologians treats concerning them, they turn as if on the hinge of the universal faith and divine wisdom. You will be able to learn and comprehend the certainty of all these very easily and with no labor, provided you thoroughly revolve the individual examinations of this compendium with diligent and repeated reading.

### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK I.

(...O my parent) since those things contained in this sacred symbol <note>The "symbol" refers to the Apostles' Creed, the foundational statement of Christian belief.</note> are open to me, a path lies before me from which a firm hope holds me: that once these foundations are laid, I might easily and with no labor build the entire framework of Theological wisdom upon them. Nevertheless, so that I may bring back these heavenly mysteries with a more solid understanding and faith, I pray you be pleased to lend your ears for a little while, to see if I might resume, in a just and right path, these things explained by you through this long series of discourse. GOMETIUS. A pious and truly praiseworthy request. Come then, (*my son*), and retrace everything as you please.

<margin>Epilogue.</margin>
PHILALETHES. From the beginning, we fixed the immortality of the soul as the end of all things to be desired—just as an archer fixes his mark <note>original: "ut Sagittarij signum." Philalethes uses the image of the constellation Sagittarius, the Archer, to represent the soul's target.</note>—and from the certainty of this, you introduced all other things to be believed for salvation in this manner: Human happiness is granted, which the final clause of the creed calls *eternal life*. But happiness (or "beatitude") signifies the most perfect state of all good things. Among the other things that belong to the most perfect state of the soul, this one is numbered: that the soul, while it enjoys divine company and vision, should also be joined to the body (toward which the soul itself is inclined by its very nature) and recover what was lost. Because it was pleasing to call this the *resurrection of the flesh* in the creed, it is therefore necessary to believe this for salvation. But since eternal life and the blessed union (just like the joining of any separate things) requires likeness and conformity—and since God, to whom to adhere is eternal life, exists as the purest and holiest intellect—it is therefore necessary that the soul itself, being unitable to God, be purified and expiated. This, the creed pronounces as the *remission of sins*; therefore, it is also necessary to believe this for salvation. And since eternal life requires the fullness of all goods, and the order of things permits this to the Mediator alone—while other mortals excel, some in one gift and others in another—it was necessary, so that individuals might become sharers of all goods, that all who are to be saved should be fused into one. These, joined together, we call the *Holy Catholic Church*; therefore, it was fitting to believe in this, together with the *communion of saints*, for salvation. But since the union of saints cannot happen except by a certain spiritual power which binds together and brings into one the vast and varied multitude of members—and such a power is the Giver of true unity and of all goods, God the Holy Spirit—it is therefore necessary to believe in him for salvation. And since eternal life requires both a spiritual and a corporal resurrection of the dead, and the resurrection of the dead demands the end of the age and a judgment (at which the presence of Christ follows), it therefore belongs entirely to the path of eternal salvation to believe that *Christ will come to judge the living and the dead*. And since it belongs to the good and perfection of the human soul that it should be joined to God its creator and to the body at the same time, it must be believed for salvation that the same Mediator rose again and ascended into heaven. But since no one can be granted eternal life without the remission of sins, and the original sin of the first parent could not be remitted except through the death, passion, and burial of the Mediator, and through his descent into the underworld; therefore, one must believe for salvation that Christ suffered, died, was buried, and descended into hell. Furthermore, because no mortal adheres to God the creator except by the intercession of a Mediator who is one with Him in personal unity—whence that Mediator could not be born from any blood-related seed—and since it is discovered that such a Mediator existed in Jesus, the Son of Mary, it is therefore required for salvation to believe in this same Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary. And because eternal life proceeds from the conformity of the human mind with the divine mind—to which the Trinity of persons with a real unity of nature is paramount, which it has pleased us to call Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—therefore, together with the Son and the Holy Spirit, it is necessary for salvation to believe in God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth. These, unless the slenderness of my wit and a failing memory deceive me, are the things which your <term>syntherisis</term> <note>original: "syntherisis." Usually spelled "synderesis," this refers to the innate spark of moral reasoning or a synthesis of principles that guides the mind.</note>, from the beginning of the discourse even unto this end,

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK I. 55

...O father) the things contained in this sacred symbol <note>original: "sacro hoc symbolo"; referring to the Apostles' Creed</note> are now open to me, from which a firm hope holds me: that once these foundations are laid, I might easily and without labor be able to build upon them the entire structure of Theological wisdom. <margin>Epilogue.</margin>
**GOMET.** A truly pious and praiseworthy request. Come then, my son, and weave the whole matter back together as you please. **PHILAL.** From the beginning, we fixed the immortality of the soul as the target of all desirable things (like the sign of the Archer <note>A reference to Sagittarius, the archer, symbolizing a goal or target</note>). From its certainty, you introduced all the other things to be believed for salvation in this manner: Human happiness is given, which the final clause of the Creed calls *life everlasting*. Happiness, moreover, signifies the most perfect state of all goods. Among the other things that belong to the most perfect state of the soul, this one is numbered: that while the soul enjoys divine company and vision, it should also be joined to the body (toward which the soul itself is inclined by its own nature) and recover what was lost. Because the Creed called this the *resurrection of the flesh*, it is therefore necessary to believe this for salvation. But since eternal life and the blessed union (just like the joining of any separate things) requires likeness and conformity—and since God, to whom to cling is eternal life, exists as the purest and holiest intellect—it is therefore necessary that the soul itself, which is to be united to God, be purified and expiated. This the Creed pronounces as the *remission of sins*; therefore, it is necessary to believe this too for salvation. And since eternal life requires the sum of all goods, and the order of things allows this to the Mediator <note>A title for Jesus Christ, acting as the intermediary between God and humanity</note> alone—while other mortals excel, some in one gift and others in another—it was necessary for this purpose that, so individuals might be participants in all goods, as many as are to be saved should be fused into one. These, joined together, we call the *Holy Catholic Church*; therefore, it was fitting to believe this along with the *communion of saints* for salvation. Since, however, the union of saints cannot happen except by a certain spiritual power which joins the vast and varied multitude of members and reduces them into one—and such a power is the Holy Spirit, God himself, the giver of true unity and all goods—it is therefore necessary to believe in him for salvation. Furthermore, since eternal life requires both a spiritual and a corporeal resurrection of the dead, and the resurrection of the dead demands the end of the age and the judgment (which the presence of Christ follows), it therefore pertains entirely to the path of eternal salvation to believe that *Christ will come to judge the living and the dead*. And since it belongs to the good and perfection of the human soul to cling to God its creator and to its body at the same time, it must be believed for salvation that the same Mediator *rose again and ascended into heaven*. Since, truly, no one can be granted eternal life without the remission of sins, and the sin of our first parent's origin could not be remitted except through the death, passion, and burial of the Mediator, and through his descent into hell, it is therefore necessary for salvation to believe that *Christ suffered, died, was buried, and descended into hell*. Moreover, because no mortal clings to God the creator except by the intercession of the Mediator, who is one with Him in personal unity, that Mediator could not be born from any blood-related seed. Since, therefore, it is certain that such a Mediator existed as Jesus, the Son of Mary, it is required for salvation to believe in this very *Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary*. Finally, because eternal life proceeds from the conformity of the human mind with the divine mind—to which the Trinity of persons with a real unity of nature is primary, which it has pleased us to call Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—it is therefore necessary for salvation to believe, together with the Son and Holy Spirit, in *God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth*. These, unless the thinness of my talent and a failing memory deceive me, are the things which your synthesis <term>syntherisis: a technical term in medieval theology referring to the innate spark of reason or conscience that grasps first principles</term> has covered from the beginning of your discourse to this end...

# 54 PAULI RICII,

...so that he might suggest the reassumption of the body, the clause stating the **Resurrection of the Flesh** is rightly added.

<margin>The skill of transmutation, which they call **Alchemy**, explains the nature and qualities of the bodies of those rising again.</margin>
But perhaps you will think to yourself and wonder: if the last judgment is nothing other than the dissolution of all things that have been mixed together, how then can we believe in the resurrection of the dead and the reassumption of an organized body during that judgment? For in that state, the mixing of all things that can be generated is at its peak. You should know, therefore, that the bodies of those rising again will not be put together by mere mixing, but rather purified by the refining power of fire. Indeed, those bodies will be very little subject to transformation or change, unlike other bodies piled up through motion; instead, having been tested and purged by the burning of fire (much like the substance of the stars), they will rise again bright, agile, and pure in every way. This happens by the same law by which, even now, through a certain artistry of fire, a substance is drawn from any mixed thing which those skilled in that art call the **quintessence** <note>original: "quintam essentiam"; the "fifth essence" or purest part of a substance, believed in alchemy to be the most refined and potent element</note>. This is not because some part of the fifth heavenly element is actually inside it, but because it corresponds to that element in a certain proportion. For this substance is brought forth clear and pure (as the senses judge) by the trial of fire, while a mass that is earthy, thick, dark, and useless remains behind. And that which has been extracted not only loses none of its strength but also exercises its power and work far more precisely and sublimely. For the resurrection of these bodies will accompany the sound of the great celestial trumpet and the end of the age’s cycle; and as the fire blazes, there will be a dissolution of all mixtures, an expiation of all things, and a separation of the pure from the impure, and the good from the evil.

<margin>Why the consummation of the age is carried out through fire, and not rather through some other kind of destruction.</margin>
But I see that you are still secretly doubting and asking yourself (and not without reason) what logic suggests that the consummation of the age and the future judgment should happen through a conflagration of fire, rather than through a disaster of waters or any other kind of event or destruction. Pay attention to this and be wise: the very same cause that governs the state of the heavens also brings about the consummation of the age through fire. For the state of the heaven (as you know) happens because the **moving soul** <note>original: "anima motrix"; in medieval cosmology, the spiritual intelligence that moves a celestial sphere</note> of the heaven finally fixes its gaze upon the most desired Creator of all things. From this, that soul is then affected by a joy and exultation that is all the more vehement—as I recently recounted from the opinion of the Corduban <note>Likely referring to the philosopher Averroes of Cordoba, known for his commentaries on the nature of the heavens</note>—the more beautiful and lovable the sight it enjoys. Therefore, since the soul that moves the heaven is by its own nature inherent in the body, it cannot be otherwise than that this immense emotion of the soul overflows into the body joined to it, in a physical way. Great joy and exultation of the spirit bring forth intense heat and ardor into all the limbs of the body, just as we perceive by clear experience in ourselves, who are a **microcosm** <note>original: "mycrocosmus"; the concept that the human being is a 'little world' that reflects the laws and structure of the entire universe</note>. For from a sad thought of the soul, the body itself becomes stiff, neglected, and sluggish, and is finally reduced to wasting away. On the other hand, from joy and the soul’s delight, it grows warm, shines, and is made agile. Therefore, just as the stable and firm gaze of the heavenly soul results in the "station" or fixed state of the heaven, so from the abundance of joy and the ineffable delight of the soul, a splendor and light—intense and beyond the usual order of the moving heavens—shines forth in that celestial and elementary body. By this, a glow, heat, and scorching warmth are spread through the entire earthly globe, from which follows the conflagration of fire, the dissolution of all things, their consummation, their purging, and finally the **resurrection of the flesh**.

<margin>And life everlasting.</margin>
But as for the symbol that closes the Creed in the final place—namely, **Life Everlasting**—it is the reason and the end of all the preceding points. You, together with your brothers **Philadelphus** <note>A name meaning "lover of the brother"</note> and **Philosomatus** <note>A name meaning "lover of the body"</note>, have established the truth of this as the target, base, and foundation of the whole business through long examination and the most exquisite reasoning. For this reason, I think we should dwell very little on any further scrutiny of this. But these points, as the nature of an **isagoge** <note>original: "ysagogae"; an introductory manual or primer used for teaching</note> and compendium requires, seem sufficient for a true understanding of the things to be believed and for the path of eternal salvation. The remaining appendices to these matters, and whatever the sacred School of Theologians treats concerning them, turn like a hinge upon the whole of faith and divine wisdom. You will be able to learn and comprehend the certainty of all these things very easily and with no labor, provided that you weigh and turn over each examination of this compendium with diligent and repeated reading.

### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK I. 55

...since, father, the things contained in this sacred symbol <note>original: "sacro hoc symbolo"; referring to the Apostles' Creed</note> are now clear to me, a path opens from which a firm hope holds me. With these foundations laid, I believe I can easily and without labor build the entire engine of theological wisdom upon them. Nevertheless, so that I might bring back these heavenly mysteries with a more solid understanding and faith, I beg you to lend your ears for a little while, so that I may summarize these points through a long sequence of speech to see if I am following the right and proper path. **GOMETIUS.** Truly, yours is a pious and praiseworthy request. Go on then, my son, and recount everything as you please.

<margin>Epilogue.</margin>
**PHILALETHES.** From the beginning, we set the immortality of the soul as the target (like the sign of Sagittarius) of all desirable things. From the certainty of this immortality, you inferred all the other things that must be believed for salvation in this manner: Human happiness is granted, which the final clause of the Creed calls **eternal life**. Now, happiness signifies the most perfect state of all good things. Among the other things that belong to the soul's most perfect state, this one is listed: that the soul, while it enjoys divine company and vision, should also be joined to the body (to which the soul itself is inclined by its very nature) and recover what it had lost. Because the Creed chose to call this the **resurrection of the flesh**, it is therefore necessary to believe this for salvation.

But since eternal life and the blessed union (just like the joining of any separate things) requires similarity and conformity, and since God—to whom adhering is eternal life—exists as the purest and holiest intellect, it is necessary that the soul itself, which is to be united with God, be purified and expiated. This is what the Creed declares as the **remission of sins**; therefore, it is also necessary to believe this for salvation.

And since eternal life requires the fullness of all goods, yet the order of things permits this only to the Mediator <note>original: "Mediatori"; referring to Jesus Christ as the bridge between God and humanity</note>, while other mortals excel—some in one duty or gift, others in another—it was necessary for this purpose that all those to be saved should be forged into one, so that each might become a participant in all goods. These, joined together, we call the **Holy Catholic Church**; therefore, it was appropriate to believe in this along with the **communion of saints** for salvation.

Furthermore, since the union of saints cannot happen except through a certain spiritual power that joins and brings into one a vast and varied multitude of members, and since such a power is the giver of true unity and all goods—God the **Holy Spirit** himself—it is necessary to believe in him for salvation.

And since eternal life requires both a spiritual and physical resurrection of the dead, and the resurrection of the dead demands the end of the age and the judgment (which the presence of Christ follows), it therefore belongs entirely to the path of eternal salvation to believe that **Christ will come to judge the living and the dead**.

And since it belongs to the good and perfection of the human soul to be joined both to God its Creator and to the body, one must believe for salvation that the same Mediator **rose again and ascended into heaven**.

Moreover, because no one can be granted eternal life without the remission of sins, and the sin of our first parent (or original sin) could not be remitted except through the death, passion, and burial of the Mediator and through his descent into hell, one must believe for salvation that **Christ suffered, died, was buried, and descended into hell**.

Furthermore, because no mortal adheres to God the Creator except through the intercession of the Mediator, who by personal unity is one with Him—whence that Mediator could not be born from any bloodline's seed—and since it is established that such a Mediator existed in Jesus, the Son of Mary, it is required for salvation to believe in this very **Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary**.

Finally, because eternal life proceeds from the conformity of the human mind with the Divine Mind—to which the primary feature is the Trinity of persons with a real unity of nature, which it has pleased us to call the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—it is necessary for salvation to believe in **God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth**, together with the Son and the Holy Spirit.

Unless the thinness of my wit and a failing memory deceive me, these are the things which your *syntherisis* <note>original: "syntherisis"; a term in scholastic theology referring to the innate spark of moral consciousness or the fundamental knowledge of divine law</note>, from the beginning of our discourse to this very end, has explained at length...

## VOLUME TWO
### P R E F A C E.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'P' featuring intricate floral and foliage patterns.</image-desc>
The cultivation of the rough and desolate field of the philosophers having now been completed and fulfilled, we now turn, by the help of the powers above, to till and repair the stony and rocky field of the Jews. Since, however, the deficiency or fault of a thing cannot be removed unless the nature of that deficiency is first thoroughly understood, we must first see from where such great, harsh, and persistent ignorance among the Jews takes its origin. Next, it must be shown in what way their faith is deficient and mutilated, and insufficient for entering the kingdom of heaven. Finally, in the last place, it will be demonstrated that just as a follower of Christian piety is compelled to admit that no Jew participates in the blessed life, so conversely, a Jew (according to Pharisaic and Talmudic foundations) must confess that every faithful follower of Christ is a true Israelite and a partaker in eternal salvation.

***

# T R A C T A T E I.
### CONCERNING THE CAUSE OF THE JEWS' stubbornness and their dull ignorance.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'V' containing a scene of a scholar seated at a desk within a vaulted architectural frame.</image-desc>
The authority of antiquity is always so great among the common people that to doubt it or to inquire into it is considered the greatest outrage and crime—and all the more so when the diligence of such antiquity was taught and instructed not by deceptive human conjectures or the wavering course of reason, but by heavenly and divine inspirations. From this, the wretched later synagogue of the Jews, seduced by the deviations of the ancients, found the origin and growth of its most ruinous error and dull ignorance. Through dull and stubborn thought, they persuaded themselves that it was impossible for that earlier Jewish antiquity—the foster-child of spiritual wisdom and sacred eloquence, to whom the sacrament of faith and secret truth was known above all other mortals almost from the beginning of the ages—to have fallen headlong into such a vast depth of ignorance and insane error that they would despise the very Author of life and Lord of glory with such a fierce and hostile mind. They could not believe their ancestors would treat the Savior (who had been foretold to them long before, who lived among them in familiar custom, and who performed stupendous signs and miracles) with spitting, blows, and whips, and finally a bitter

<meta>catchword: death,</meta>

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK II.

...death, and inflicted the horrible punishment of the cross. Indeed, their madness and faithless ignorance so prevailed that, with hearts now hardened and dulled, they seek no solid truth or spiritual understanding of the Scriptures; nor, in their seeking, do they find or understand. Their minds are so deluded and wretchedly blinded that they do not know how to distinguish or judge between the impiety and hypocrisy of the <term>pseudo-Pharisees</term> <note>Literally "false Pharisees." Ricius distinguishes between the "holy" ancient Pharisees and those who opposed Jesus.</note> and the true, orthodox antiquity of their ancestors. 

However, so that they may understand this more clearly themselves, recognize their unspeakable error, and see that the Pharisees who killed Christ had greatly degenerated from the learning and holiness of the ancient Pharisees, I shall bring forward several testimonies from the **Talmudists** (to whom they grant indubitable faith). These testimonies are proven both by the trustworthy history of **Flavius Josephus** and the uncorrupted authority of the Gospel. 

It must be said, therefore, following the opinion of the **Egyptian Rabbi Moses** <note>This refers to Maimonides (Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon), specifically his work *The Guide for the Perplexed* (Dux seu Director Neutrorum).</note> in his *Guide for the Perplexed*: all ignorance, contention, and discord usually happen for three reasons: namely, the **height** of the thing to be known, the **ineptitude** of the one trying to know it, or the craving for **vengeance, glory, and lust**. The tradition of the Talmudists demonstrates in various places—and not obscurely—that each of these, either separately or joined together, was the cause of the Jewish "perfidy." 

For since the basis and foundation of the truth of faith consists solely in the coming of **Christ the Savior** and the mystery of His redemption, its height and sublimity are so great that (according to the records of the Talmudists) it was not sufficiently revealed or known even to the ministering angels, let alone to the minds of mortals. Therefore, it should not seem strange that this was less known and understood by the dregs of the pseudo-Pharisees and the impiety of the Sadducees. 

For the Talmudists write in the tractate on the **Senators** <note>original: "codice Senatorum," referring to the tractate *Sanhedrin*.</note> in the chapter **Helek**, where they treat many things concerning the coming of the Messiah and His redemption in a long examination, specifically regarding that prophecy of Isaiah saying: 
<margin>Chapter 63.</margin>
**"For the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my redemption has come."** <note>Isaiah 63:4</note> 
**Rabbi Yohanan** says there: "It is written *'in my heart,'* as if He said, 'to my heart I have revealed this secret, but to my limbs not at all.'" And according to the opinion of **Rabbi Lakish**, the sense is: "To my heart I have revealed it, but to the ministering angels not at all." 

To this is turned that oracle of Gospel truth: **"But of that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven."** <note>Mark 13:32</note> Furthermore, the varying and manifold opinions of the ancient and wisest Talmudists concerning the coming and the qualities of the Redeemer declare the height of this mystery. I have touched upon this elsewhere in the Latin language with a brief distinction of clauses; let the studious searcher of truth look for it there. 

In the same way, regarding the dullness and foolishness of those who were found in Jerusalem at the time of the Redeemer’s coming, the writings of the Talmudists (in the same chapter) openly testify: "In the age," they say, "in which the **Son of David** is to come, there will be few students of wisdom; for the strengths of body and soul will grow filthy and waste away because of sorrow and groaning." Again, **Rav Nehemiah** says: "In the age in which the Son of David is to come, the insolence of the sons of Adam will be great and cursed, and the entire kingdom will be turned to heresy, nor will any correction from the elders be of use." For it is written: **"He will see that the hand is weakened,"** <note>Deuteronomy 32:36</note> that is, that the hand of traitors prevails, or that students of wisdom are lacking. So says he. 

That these things should be heard as referring not to the last coming (as some impudently claim), but to the first coming of the Savior, the authority of **Rav** <note>A common title for the 3rd-century scholar Abba Arika.</note> declares more openly in the tractate on the **Sabbaths**, saying: "Jerusalem was not overturned and desolated except because faithful men failed within her." **Rav Judah**, however, asserts that Jerusalem was devastated because the wise were held in contempt there. Here he speaks openly about the destruction of Jerusalem that occurred shortly after the cross of the Redeemer. 

From these assertions of the Talmudists, therefore, it is clearly established how great the height of the mystery of the Redeemer is—inasmuch as it was not known or understood even by the ministering angels—and how great was the foolishness and ineptitude of the Pharisees who were found in Jerusalem at the time of the Lord’s Passion. Regarding their very craving for glory and lust...

-> # THE WRITINGS OF PAULUS RICIUS, <-

...dullness, the same teachings of the **Talmudists** that we have cited bear witness that the hand of the traitors prevailed, that no correction was effective, and that the entire kingdom of Jerusalem was turned toward heresy. You will understand this more fully and clearly if you consider the horrendous feuds and dissensions of the **Pharisees** with the **Sadducees** (especially during the reign of **Hyrcanus**, son of **Simon Maccabee** <note>John Hyrcanus I (reigned 134–104 BCE), a high priest and king of the Hasmonean dynasty. His break with the Pharisees was a pivotal moment in Jewish history.</note>) which lasted until the very destruction of that city. 

For Hyrcanus (as the Talmudists record in the *Book on Betrothals* <note>original: *codice de sponsalitijs*, referring to the Talmudic tractate **Kiddushin**.</note> and the *Volume of the Senators* <note>original: *Senatorum uolumine*, referring to the tractate **Sanhedrin**.</note>) held both the royal and priestly dignity at once. In the fortieth year of his priesthood, having been provoked and driven into a rage by certain leaders of the Pharisees—and especially by **Eleazar**—he turned from a Pharisee into a **Sadducee**. He became a sharp and fierce persecutor and enemy of the Pharisaic religion, ordering the vast multitude of that sect then living in Jerusalem to be slaughtered and destroyed with an impious and cruel spirit. 

Thus it happened—even as his son **Alexander** <note>Alexander Jannaeus, who succeeded his brother and continued the conflict with the Pharisees.</note> later killed six thousand Pharisees, and this calamity grew more and more oppressive—that the remaining Pharisees, who were superior in name, learning, and honesty of life, were forced into flight. They wandered through **Egypt**, **Assyria**, **Babylonia**, and other nations of the Barbarians and Pagans, until the final destruction of Jerusalem. **Flavius Josephus**, a grave writer on Jewish antiquity, recounts this more extensively in the thirteenth book of *Antiquities*, which you should read. 

But the other apostates and <term>pseudo-Pharisees</term> <note>Ricius's term for the corrupt religious leaders who remained in power in Jerusalem, whom he distinguishes from the "true" ancient Pharisees.</note> who remained in Jerusalem agreed with the faction and impiety of the Sadducees, who were driven not by any honor of faith or religion, but only by a desire for empty glory and vengeance. These are the ones whom **Christ the Lord**, the restorer of mortal life and the world, denounced as hypocrites, faithless, vain boasters, unclean, **whitewashed tombs**, leaders of the blind, ravenous wolves, devourers of the poor, and shedders of righteous blood, accusing them of all crimes and outrages. 

It should not seem strange to the Jews that the Pharisees killed their Savior. For such behavior was not rare for the Jews, who in the desert nearly overwhelmed **Moses**—from whom they had received the benefit of life and salvation—with stones. And these same people, led out of slavery, ten times unmindful of the benefit, denied God and returned to idols. I say nothing of **Korah** and the other two hundred and fifty leaders of the Synagogue in Numbers 16; nothing of Moses himself, whom <term>Rabbi Solomon</term> <note>Solomon ben Isaac (1040–1105), known as **Rashi**, the most influential medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud.</note>, the Talmudic glossator, says fell into error out of anger three times in Numbers 31; nothing of the ten sons of **Jacob** who, though they were the lights of the Church and the whole world, were yet overcome by envy and nearly slaughtered their brother **Joseph**; and finally, let me say nothing of **Adam**, that divine and heavenly man, nor of the angels who were companions of **Lucifer**, nor of **Solomon**, etc. It is well known that all of these, though endowed with remarkable wisdom, fell into sins and errors. 

Therefore, it is not at all to be wondered at if this foolish and wicked race of Pharisees was blinded by such a great depth of hidden mystery, and at the same time maliciously struck against that very solid and unshakable <term>cornerstone</term> <note>A traditional Christian title for Jesus, signifying the essential foundation of the faith (see Psalm 118:22).</note>, straying from that narrow path of life and the way of eternal salvation. This indiscriminate and ambiguous use of the name "Pharisee" led the Jews into ignorance and dull-witted stupidity, resulting in a blasphemous and most ruinous error. From that time until this very day, they have not been able to be torn away or uprooted from it by any study, work, or labor; nor is it to be hoped for in the future, until that Judge of all comes with the clouds of heaven, who promises that on that day he will turn away impiety 

<margin>Romans 11</margin> 

from Jacob, and then (as the Apostle witnesses) all **Israel** will be saved.

## TREATISE II.
### THAT THE JEWISH FAITH IS DEFICIENT
#### *and not sufficient for the kingdom of heaven.*

Having therefore understood the cause of the Jews' lack of faith, I now proceed, by divine will, to treat what remains in this place. I shall pierce and conquer the mad stubbornness of the Jews with the weapons of the prophets and their own **Talmudic** writings, so that they may be forced to confess that many things required for a blessed life are missing from the foundations of their faith, whereby their crippled and useless belief shall be refuted. In order that these matters, and those which follow, might be taught and perceived with a clearer understanding, I will first bring forward the foundations of the Jewish faith (which they themselves call "roots" <note>original: *radices*, referring to the Hebrew term **Ikkarim**</note>). Following that, I will subjoin the holy Creed of the Apostles and of Gospel truth in its proper order.

Therefore, the Egyptian **Rabbi Moses** <note>Moses Maimonides (1135–1204), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher. He is called "the Egyptian" because he lived and worked in Fustat, Cairo.</note>, in his explanation of the chapter *Helek* <note>original: *capitis helec*; refers to the eleventh chapter of the Talmudic tractate **Sanhedrin**, where Maimonides first articulated his thirteen principles of faith.</note>, enumerates thirteen roots of the Mosaic Law regarding God:

1. That He exists.
2. That He is one.
3. That He is incorporeal <note>without a physical body</note>.
4. That He is the first of all things.
5. That He alone is to be worshipped.
6. That the gift of prophecy is given to mortals.
7. That **Moses** was a prophet.
8. That the Law was handed down from heaven.
9. That this Law is not to be exchanged for another.
10. That God knows all things.
11. That He rewards and punishes according to each person’s works.
12. That the **Messiah** is to be expected.
13. That there will be a future resurrection of the dead.

These are the points from the Egyptian Rabbi Moses in the first chapter of the *Book of the Sanhedrin* <note>original: *codicis Sanatorum*, referring to the tractate **Sanhedrin**</note>. However, **Albo** (whom they call **Rabbi Joseph Albo** <note>A 15th-century Spanish rabbi and author of the **Sefer ha-Ikkarim** (Book of Roots)</note>), in his *Book of Roots*, varies from this opinion in two points (as far as it concerns us): namely, regarding the coming of the Messiah and the perpetual observance of the Law. He demonstrates with solid arguments and the testimony of the Scriptures that these points should not be numbered among the foundations of the Mosaic Law. If this is admitted, it is very easy to see how a Jew, according to the foundations of his own faith, would be forced to confess that every follower of **Christ** is a participant in the world to come. Nevertheless, so that no room for quibbling or escape remains for my adversaries, I will grant and concede that these two points should likewise be placed among the roots of the Jewish faith. Nonetheless, the Jew will not be able to deny that the true worshiper of the Christian faith is a true Israelite and a sharer in the kingdom of heaven. 

These are the things which the deficient and barely salvific faith of the Jews encompasses. However, the foundations of the orthodox faith are explained in this brief table, called the **Apostles' Creed**. When you look at the believable things contained within it, they are fourteen in number. In other places, however, they are counted as twelve, for the number of Christ's disciples who are said to have been the authors, as described more extensively in the third book of the *Sentences* <note>original: *3. Sententiarum*, referring to the famous theological textbook by Peter Lombard.</note>. The words of the Creed are:

> I believe in one God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth. And in Jesus Christ His only Son, our Lord: Who was conceived by the Holy Spirit: Born of the Virgin Mary: Suffered under Pontius Pilate: Was crucified, died, and was buried. He descended into hell: On the third day He rose again from the dead. He ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of God the Father almighty. From there He shall come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit: The holy catholic Church: The communion of saints: The forgiveness of sins: The resurrection of the flesh: And life eternal.

This is approved by the unanimous opinion of all the faithful as the rationale, base, and foundation of the entire faith and truth. However, to discuss the individual points contained in this Creed, or to investigate the reasons why they vary in many ways from the **Nicene** and **Athanasian** Creeds, or why these Creeds differ among themselves and do not state the exact same things, is by no means part of the task I have undertaken here. Furthermore, I have already explained all the mysteries of this Creed through a long examination of the harmony of the nature of sensible things in my preceding Volume; let anyone who desires to hear and know the natural testimonies and reasonings for the truth of the faith go there. They are called "foundations," which the Latins now call "articles" <note>original: *articulos*</note> and the Hebrews call "roots" <note>original: *radices*</note>, because if even one of them is removed or overturned, the entire Law and faith collapse.

# PAUL RICIUS,

If, therefore, you refer the reviewed roots of Jewish belief to the creed <note>original: *symbolum*, referring to the Apostles' Creed</note> of the orthodox faith, you will clearly find that the faith of the Jews (even though all its roots are approved and contained within the Apostles' Creed) falls short in many things that pertain to the fulfillment of the truth of faith. And for that reason, their belief is by no means sufficient for the blessed life. For indeed, the blessed life requires that we worship God as the author of life—threefold and yet one—and incarnate; and that we profess the same God to have been born of a Virgin, suffered, died, and risen again, none of which the faith of the Jews explains. Moreover, that these things must be believed entirely and necessarily for salvation is gathered either from the order of nature itself and the testimony of sensible things, or is shown from the revealed and untainted authority of the divine utterances. In the first way, I clearly explained this in the preceding Volume to those desiring the truth. In the second way, we shall strive to accomplish that very thing in the present treatise, by the nod of the heavens. Yet first, I thought a steep and difficult question that silently presents itself here should be explained and unraveled in a few words. For a professor of Christian piety no less than a professor of the Jewish faith will doubt, saying that since divine mercy (as **Ezekiel** witnesses) does not wish the death of a sinner,
<margin>1 Timothy 2</margin>
but rather that he be converted and live: and which also (as the Apostle speaks to **Timothy**) wants all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Why then does it happen that the divine utterances repeat so many commandments to be observed, and commemorate various historical events of the times with such great care, yet the belief in these is less than sufficient for salvation? Furthermore, why would God have brought forth those things without which no one can be a partaker of the kingdom of heaven in such a doubtful and obscure sentence, so that the faithlessness and blasphemous errors of many have arisen from it, which daily sprout more and more and undergo increase? To this it must be said that the more powerful cause of this matter (as you knew before) was the height of the thing to be known, which, although it does not withdraw or hide itself from anyone's gaze, the wretched condition of the mortal creature cannot grasp or endure such a brightness of light (much like the vision of an owl). And therefore, the mystery of the incarnation and redemption (as you heard a little while ago from the opinion of the **Talmudists**) was not even known or perceived by the ministering angels. Whence **Augustine** teaches in the seventh book of *The City of God*: that many foretold the Word concerning the sacrament of the incarnation, which they themselves
<margin>Isaiah 29</margin>
nonetheless did not know would come to pass. For the vision of all was like the words of a sealed book: because the speeches (says **Daniel**) are closed and sealed until the preordained time. This, therefore, is one of the causes by which the sacraments of the Trinity, the incarnation, and the passion were set forth and foretold under such great darkness and doubtful speech of the sacred utterance. Another reason for the hiding, however, was lest an occasion be given to the multitude of the Jews for returning to the "vomit of Idols," and to the gentiles for persevering in the worship of the same. For the servitude to Idols rests upon a twin error: that they worship the creature instead of the creator, and they adore many instead of the one God, king of all ages. Since, therefore, the sacrament of the Trinity proves a certain plurality in divine things, and the secret of the incarnation requires that a human creature, born from a female womb, be worshipped together with the divine nature, a suspicion could easily arise as if it were lawful to adore many gods and a creature with the worship of *latria* <note>a theological term for the highest form of worship, reserved for God alone</note> at the same time. Therefore, the providence of the Prophets and other early figures, and the wise **Pharisees**, although they knew the mysteries of the Trinity and the incarnation perhaps more clearly than they themselves uttered them; nevertheless, lest the incautious crowd of Jews, otherwise prone to the worship of idols, should slide back into their former error of worshipping foreign gods, they therefore announced these hidden foundations of the faith under enigma and ambiguity <note>original: *Amphibologia*</note>. Added to this was the fear of the faithful Jews of that time, by which they did not dare to openly profess those things which are of the faith, which that prince of **Kabbalists** and Allegorizers, **Rabbi Simeon** (as **Recanate** <note>Menahem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note> witnesses), clearly taught regarding that principal sacrament of the Trinity in **Deuteronomy**:

### THAT GOD IS THREE AND ONE IS AFFIRMED BY THE TESTIMONIES OF BOTH DIVINE UTTERANCES AND THE TALMUDISTS.

The cause having been recognized, then—why the mystery of the Trinity and the Incarnation were handed down under a cloud of words and types—we must now return to where the discourse departed. And first, I shall show from the manifest testimonies of the sacred word and the Talmudists that belief in the Trinity is in every way necessary for the entrance into life. From many examples, I will bring forward only three here for the sake of brevity. The first is that previously mentioned oracle of Deuteronomy: "Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one" <note>Deuteronomy 6:4; Ricius translates the Hebrew names as "God God our God" to emphasize a triple nature</note>. Whereupon the same Rabbi Simeon, in the book of radiance called the *Zohar* <term>Zohar: the foundational work of the Kabbalah</term>, adapts these three names to the persons of the Trinity, openly pronouncing the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Moreover, that a great and salvific sacrament of faith lies hidden in this brief clause is established by the fact that in the Book of Blessings <note>The Berakhot tractate of the Talmud</note>, the Talmudists unanimously ordain and command that anyone devoted to the Jewish religion must, every single day, morning and evening, with the highest reverence and purity of mind, express these words with a living voice and meditate upon them in the soul. This is because the entire power of blessedness consists in this, according to the testimony of their own morning prayers and praises, which they chant by ancient custom, saying: "Happy are we! How good, how pleasant is our lot, and how beautiful our heritage! Happy are we who every single day, morning and evening, say: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one." But if you ask the Jews and the more recent Talmudists what sort of great and salvific virtue is placed and located in these little words, such that eternal salvation and blessedness accompany their pronunciation and meditation, they can return nothing consistent with reason—except perhaps those who have unrolled the teachings and writings of the Kabbalists, as you shall hear more fully in the fourth volume of this work.

The second testimony of the individual Trinity is provided by that verse of the Psalms: "God, God, the Lord has spoken, and called the earth" <note>Psalm 50:1; original: *Deus Deus Dominus locutus est*</note>. Where the ancient Talmudic sages, in the assembly on the Psalms called the *Midrash Tehillim* <note>original: *Medrastilim*; a traditional homiletic commentary on the Psalms</note>, asking why these sacred names of God are repeated, respond: "Because through these same three names, God created the universe." It is established by the opinion of all that the works of creation were produced through no medium or organ, but emanated, were created, and were founded by the incomprehensible divine power, wisdom, and will alone. Therefore, it must be fearlessly judged and deemed that these three names insinuate nothing else but the divine nature with a plurality of persons. 

The third most constant testimony of the Trinity is the oracle of Isaiah 6, saying: "Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory" <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>, which the entire synagogue of the Jews brings forth and meditates upon with great veneration and worship twice every single day. Indeed, what else does the triple repetition of the same name indicate, but that...

### THE SACRAMENT OF THE INCARNATION, AND THE DIVINITY
### *The secret of the Messiah, shown by the various authority of the Prophets and the Talmudists.*

Concerning the mystery of the incarnation, and the divinity of the Savior, I will likewise bring forward three clear documents of sacred eloquence, and as many testimonies of the Talmudists. The first is that prophecy of Jeremiah in chapter 23, concerning the raising up of the branch of David. This, he says, is the name they shall call him: **The Lord our Just One** <note>original Latin: *Deus iustus noster*; Hebrew: *Yahweh Tsidkenu*</note>, where by the opinion of the Chaldean interpreter <term>the Targum: an ancient Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</term> and all other commentators, the discourse is about the Messiah the Savior. And although the perversity of the Jews, in its usual manner, pulls this text through various twists and turns: nevertheless, the solid authority of the Talmudists in the assembly on the Lamentations (called the *Midrash Ekhah* <note>original: *Medraschecha*; this is the ancient Jewish homiletic commentary on the Book of Lamentations</note>) refutes their stubbornness and ignorance. There, where the question is about the name of the Messiah, and among many and various names (according to the manifold mysteries of the Savior) which are commemorated there, they finally bring forth the opinion of Rabbi Abba <note>original: *Rabi Auahe*</note> himself, asserting that "God" shall be the name of the Messiah, because it is written: "and this is his name, which they shall call him, The Lord our Just One."

The second is the prophecy of Zechariah in chapter 12, saying: "I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the Spirit of grace and mercy, and they shall look upon me, whom they have pierced." Where God, who pours out the Spirit of grace, pronounces himself to have been pierced; which would indeed be unspeakable and execrable to hear, unless we proved that the Divinity, in one person <term>hypostasi: the distinct personhood of Christ</term>, had assumed flesh subject to human passions. The ancient Talmudists (as David Kimhi <note>a famous medieval Jewish biblical commentator and grammarian</note> testifies) wish that very prophecy of Zechariah to be understood as referring to the "Messiah, son of Joseph." Whom (as Rabbi Saadia <note>Saadia Gaon, a prominent 10th-century Jewish philosopher</note> handed down in his *Book of Beliefs*) they said would perish in the war of Gog and Magog and be raised again by the Messiah, son of David. Concerning which war, according to the Talmudic commentary (as Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi: the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note> testifies), the Psalm hints: "Why have the nations raged?" <note>Psalm 2:1</note>. Concerning which also the prophecies of Ezekiel chapter 38 and the oracles of the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note> speak more openly. By "the son of David," those speaking allegorically understand Wisdom, the Eternal Son of God, through whom the humanity of the Messiah (as it was thought) the son of Joseph, was to be raised.

The third authority for the mystery of the incarnation is that of Isaiah chapter 9: "A child is born to us, a Son is given to us, and the government shall be upon his shoulder, and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace." This prophecy, although the insolence of the Jews contends it was said of King Hezekiah: nevertheless, the Chaldean interpreter (whose authority is to be preferred above the authority of all others after the Holy Scriptures <term>Hagiographa: the 'Holy Writings' or Ketuvim section of the Hebrew Bible</term>) explains it as being about the Messiah the Savior. To which also the testimony of the Egyptian Rabbi Moses <note>Maimonides: also known as Rambam</note> in his *Letter to the Yemenites* <note>original: *epistola ad Affricanos*; a famous letter regarding the Messiah and persecution</note> agrees. Even though he turns the words, which designate the divinity of the Savior, toward a different and discordant understanding. Therefore, this prophecy calls the Savior (according to the fact that he was man) a born child. But insofar as he was assumed by the divine nature, it calls him Mighty God, Father of Eternity, and Prince of Peace. To pursue the individual secrets of these matters more widely is not the business of the present moment: for it will be enough for the intelligent man that he holds it as certain from the predictions of the Prophets, and also from the testimony of the ancient Talmudists, that in the Messiah the Savior, the divine nature is fused into one with the human nature: and to believe and profess that the same Christ Messiah is God and man is necessary for salvation. The first testimony of the Talmudists is of the great...

But you know that the wisdom of God, or the Son, is the same as God, who alone, as the tamer and exterminator of sin, its fuel, and the tempter (according to the aforementioned riddle of Eleazar), was to be expected—just as I shall explain more broadly from a supernatural perspective in the fourth Volume.

The second testimony of the <term>Talmudists: scholars of the Talmud, the body of Jewish civil and ceremonial law</term> concerning the mystery of the incarnation is found in the Book of the Senators <note>The tractate *Sanhedrin*</note>, in the chapter *Heleck*, regarding that prophecy of Isaiah <margin>Chapter 52.</margin> about the Savior: *Behold, my servant shall understand; he shall be exalted more than Abraham, he shall be lifted up more than Moses, and he shall be higher than the ministering Angels.* Since, however, only God the creator of things is higher than the entire choir of Angels, it follows (according to the opinions of the Talmudists) that the same Messiah the Savior is both God and man.

The third testimony of the Talmudists is in the discourse on the Psalms called the *Midrash Tehillim* (as Recanati records on the third chapter of Genesis from the opinion of Rabbi Berechiah), saying: "The salvation of Israel is the salvation of the Holy and Blessed God," because it is written: *Just and saved* (but not "Savior"). For the correct understanding of this, know that where the Prophet Zechariah (chapter 9) prophesies concerning the Messiah (*Behold, your King comes, just and a Savior*), in the Hebrew copy it is read in the passive voice as *nosha* <note>Hebrew *nosha* (נִוְשָׁע) literally means 'is saved' or 'has been granted salvation'</note>, which designates not "Savior" but "one who has been saved." Wherefore that most wise elder Berechiah calls this just one "God saved," and therefore judged the Messiah to be God and man at the same time; he says he is "saved" from the salvation of Israel because, according to the dogma of the Kabbalists and Apostles alike, all true Israelites are certain joined members of the head, the Messiah the Savior. And therefore when one member is glorified, all the members rejoice together (says the Apostle); <margin>1 Corinthians 12.</margin> hence the salvation of the members in some way overflows into the salvation of the head—concerning which I will speak more broadly elsewhere.

Finally, gather from these sources the clear and solid testimonies of the Prophets and Talmudists concerning the divinity and the sacrament of the incarnation, and turn them over in your mind.

### THE AUTHORITY OF THE PROPHETS AND ALSO OF THE TALMUDISTS CLEARLY SHOWS THAT CHRIST THE SAVIOR MUST BE BORN OF A VIRGIN.

<margin>Chapter 7.</margin>
The testimony of Isaiah first declares that the Messiah and Savior was to be born of a Virgin, saying: *For this reason, God himself will give you a sign: Behold, a Virgin shall conceive, and bear a Son, and shall call his name Emanuel* <note>original: *Emanuel*, meaning "God with us"</note>. Here, setting aside the impudent <note>The author uses strong polemical language typical of the 16th century to dismiss Jewish interpretations that differed from Christian ones.</note> explanation of the Jews, we gather four sacred mysteries concerning the Savior from this passage. First, regarding the Passion <note>The suffering and death of Jesus.</note>, as it is read shortly before: *Is it a small thing for you to be troublesome to men, that you are troublesome also to my God?* <note>Isaiah 7:13</note> For this rebuke could not have been directed at King Ahaz, since he uttered nothing worthy of reproach, but rather praise, by saying: *I will not tempt God.* Therefore, the Prophet saw and hinted at the trouble of the Passion under a cloud, showing what an impious Pharisaic plague brought against the house of David. The mystery of the Incarnation is also expressed here, along with his birth from a Virgin, when he says: *Behold, a Virgin shall conceive, and bear a Son.* Thirdly, it designates his divinity, when it foretells that he shall be called *Emanuel*, "God with us." This could by no means be understood as referring to Hezekiah (as the Jews argue by way of quibbling), who had already been born nine years before Ahaz took up the government of the kingdom. Finally, in the last place, he suggests his immunity from sin by saying: *And he shall know how to refuse the evil and choose the good,* which the Prophet indicates will happen immediately from his mother’s womb (supported even by the testimony of the Talmudists). Passing over many other places of sacred speech where the stubbornness of the younger Jews <note>Referring to medieval and contemporary Jewish commentators who lived after the rise of Christianity.</note> might argue, I will bring forward only two irrefutable testimonies from the Talmudists. The first is in the homily on Lamentations called *Midrash Eikhah* <note>original: *Medraschecha*</note>, regarding the verse: *We have become orphans.* <note>Lamentations 5:3</note> Rabbi Berachiah says: "You said before me, 'We have become orphans without a Father': For the Redeemer whom I shall raise up from among you shall be without a Father." The second authority of the Talmudists is in the homily called *Midrash Ruth* at the end of the volume. For they say it is written: *God has appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain killed.* <note>Genesis 4:25</note> Namely, that seed which comes from another place—that is, the King Messiah. These are their words. To which that verse of Isaiah is turned: *Who shall declare his generation?* because he was derived or led forth from the land of the living. From this, the Father <note>Referring to God the Father</note> indicates that the Messiah would have his beginning by being born of a Virgin without the union of a male.

We shall explain three testimonies of the Prophets, and just as many from the Talmudists, concerning the Passion of the Savior. That same Rabbi Solomon explains this more openly regarding the Psalm *The King shall rejoice in your strength, O God,* <note>Psalm 21:1</note> saying: "It is good to explain this Psalm regarding David himself for the sake of an answer to cast back at the heretics," specifically because the Psalm itself there openly expressed the Passion of the Savior. Consider then whether it is any wonder that a man does not see the light who willfully closes his eyelids and turns his gaze away from the clear light toward shadowy darkness. ### THAT THE MESSIAH THE SAVIOR MUST RISE FROM THE DEAD, AS TAUGHT BY DIVINE PROPHECIES AND PROVED BY THE TRADITION OF THE TALMUDISTS.

<margin>John 2.</margin>
Concerning the Resurrection of the Savior, the first prophecy is that of Amos 9: *In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.* For according to the opinion of the Talmudists (in the chapter *Heleck*), this must be understood as referring to the Messiah the Savior. There, the Talmudist (on the authority of Rabbi Menahem) calls the Messiah "the son of the fall," because it is written: *In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.* By the "fall" of the tabernacle, he hints at the death of the Savior; by the "raising up," he announces his resurrection. Although the belief of the Jews agrees with the orthodox faith regarding the coming of the Savior, the later Jews wander far from the path of truth regarding the time and the person of the Redeemer. They expect him to still come for their salvation, and they deny and immediately reject that Jesus of Nazareth, the Lord Christ, was the promised Savior. Yet the ancient Talmudists (as the Egyptian, Rabbi Moses <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the famous Jewish philosopher and jurist.</note>, testifies in his final *Book of Judges*) announce nothing certain regarding the time of the Messiah. For even that leader of the Talmudists, Rabbi Akiva <note>One of the most important figures in the Mishnah (c. 50–135 CE).</note> (during the reign of Hadrian Caesar), showed himself to be a follower and servant of a certain leader of a Jewish military faction named Ben Koziba <note>Simon bar Kokhba, who led the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE). "Ben Koziba" (Son of a Lie) was a derogatory pun on his name Bar Kokhba (Son of a Star).</note> (whom Eusebius also mentions in the fourth book of his *Ecclesiastical History*), believing him to be the Messiah and Savior. However, he was killed and wiped out in the town of Betar along with the entire multitude adhering to him, in a wretched slaughter and a new extermination of the Jewish people. Therefore, just as this wisest of the Pharisees thought by a false belief that one who was not the Messiah had appeared, so by a similar error and fallacy he denied that Jesus of Nazareth was the Savior, who was the true Messiah and restorer of the world. We, however, shall strive to show through the most constant testimonies of the Prophets, as well as those of the early Talmudists, that Christ the Savior has come, and that this was Jesus of Nazareth, who suffered under Pontius Pilate. We will do this based on two previously established foundations: First, that (as we hinted before) there are two advents of the Messiah to be believed: the first for redeeming, the other for judging. Second, that the redemption of the Savior (according to the decrees of the Talmudists) concerns spiritual rather than worldly salvation. The first point is shown through the diverse and differing prophecies of the Prophets, which cannot be understood as referring to one and the same advent of the Messiah. For the Prophet Zechariah describes the Savior as poor...

He announces that he will come as a poor man, riding upon a donkey. Daniel, however, says that the same person comes with the clouds of heaven, like a son of man. Regarding this discrepancy, the Talmudists themselves often doubt and wonder (in the *Book of the Elders*, in the chapter *Helek* <note>original: "libro Senatorum capite Heleck" — refers to the Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Sanhedrin, chapter 11 (Helek), which contains extensive messianic discussions.</note>). Since these descriptions cannot be understood as a single arrival, they are convinced that there are two advents of the Messiah. 

The first arrival is in the guise of a poor man, intended to redeem us by his own blood. "Behold," he says, "your King will come to you, just and a Savior," <note>Zechariah 9:9</note> who will speak peace to the nations; and a little later he adds: "You also, by the blood of your testament, have redeemed your captives from the pit." <note>Zechariah 9:11</note> The second advent, however, is for the purpose of judging: "The judgment," he says, "was set, and the books were opened, and behold, with the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man, whom all peoples, tribes, and languages shall serve." <note>Daniel 7:10–14</note> Thus says Daniel. 

Regarding this double advent, the sermon of the elder Rabbi Barachia <note>Rabbi Berechia was a 4th-century scholar known for his homiletic interpretations (midrash).</note> also openly testifies concerning that passage in Ecclesiastes, "There is nothing new under the sun," <note>Ecclesiastes 1:9</note> for he says: "Just as the first redeemer (namely Moses) appeared and then disappeared, so the last Redeemer appears, and thereafter is hidden again" (understand this to mean until the second advent at the end of the age). 

Furthermore, it is shown through various sayings of holy scripture and the Talmudists that the Messiah is to be hoped for more for spiritual rather than worldly salvation. First, because the Talmudists themselves, among the other roots of faith which must be believed for salvation, enumerate the belief in the advent and redemption through the Messiah. This faith would be of very little necessity for salvation if it were understood as a worldly redemption, since the opinion of the Talmudists is clearly held that the reward of good works is to be expected in heaven, and not in this slippery and falling age. This is according to their commentary on that passage in Deuteronomy 7: "Which I command you today to do," for they say, "to do them *today*, but not to receive the reward *today*," <note>A common Rabbinic teaching that "today" (this life) is for action, while "tomorrow" (the world to come) is for reward.</note> asserting that the prize for the commandments is by no means to be hoped for in this world. 

Therefore, since redemption through the Savior (as they themselves teach in the chapter *Helek*) is not to be hoped for except through repentance and good works, and the retribution for good works is by no means to be given in this world, it is proven that the redemption through the Messiah must be expected as spiritual rather than worldly. This very thing is plainly taught by that great Chaldean interpreter, Jonathan, <note>Targum Jonathan, an ancient Aramaic translation and expansion of the Hebrew Bible.</note> explaining that verse of the twelfth Psalm: "You shall draw water with joy from the fountains of salvation" (where, in everyone's opinion, the prophecy speaks of the Messiah). He says there: "And they shall learn a new dogma from the chosen of the righteous." 

So too many of the ancient Talmudists, when they read in the holy scriptures about the Land of Promise, about Jerusalem, or about Zion, wish it to be understood as spiritual salvation. This is especially true where they strive to show (in the *Code of the Elders*, chapter *Helek*) that "Every Israelite has a portion in the world to come." To prove this, they bring forward that passage from Isaiah, saying: 
<margin>Chapter 60.</margin>
"Your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever." <note>Isaiah 60:21</note> It is established that "the land" is the spiritual world or the age to come. Whence also the Egyptian Rabbi Moses <note>Moses Maimonides (Rambam), the famous 12th-century Jewish philosopher and jurist who lived in Egypt.</note> says in his *Tractate on Repentance* that the Prophets suggest eternal life through various metaphors and figures of speech—such as the Mountain of the Lord, the place and way of the sanctuary, the Court of the Lord, the sweetness of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord, the Gate of the Lord, and things of that kind. By these, it can be clearly understood that redemption through the Messiah promises spiritual rather than worldly salvation. 

These two foundations having been established, it must be said that the Messiah the Savior has come, and that this was Jesus of Nazareth, who suffered under Pontius Pilate; this I shall show with a twin argument. First, from the fact that the time which the Prophets designated for the coming of the Savior has passed since the time of the arrival of Jesus of Nazareth. Second, from the fact that the saving work which is hoped for from the Savior's presence has already been completed by the same Jesus of Nazareth, the Christ of the Lord.
