->OF PAULUS RICIUS,<-

the manifold and mobile Ideal reason in the soul (the queen of heaven): which, although it maintains a perpetual order, nevertheless, because it involves itself in fleeting things, it is therefore compared to speech; and for that reason the ancients called fate from "speaking" <note>original: "fatum à fando" — Ricius is using a traditional etymology where *fatum* (fate) is derived from *fari* (to speak), implying fate is the "spoken" decree of God</note>. And yet, if we wish to confess the truth, those three Laws are the three Fates of the Poets, or the three *Parcae*: *Clotho*, *Lachesis*, and *Atropos*. For the poets seem to have looked toward the same thing. Thus, therefore, in the Sephirotic <term>Sephirotic: relating to the Sephiroth, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</term> order there is a threefold Law, which the Law of *Moses* imitates as far as it can. For this too is threefold. First is the Idea of the Law, which was in the mind of *Moses* before the Law was written down, just as it also exists in the minds of all those taught by God. Second is the Written Law, which corresponds to the second Sephirotic Law. Third is the explanation dealing with the literal and earthly works of the Law: which, because it is varied (yet in an immutable way) according to time, place, and persons, therefore corresponds to the third Sephirotic Law. But I return to the Sephirotic Laws. The first Law in the divine mind is called the paradigm; the second in the angelic mind, the exemplar; the third is spoken of in respect to bodies. And it happens in plainly the same way that an Architect first conceives the Idea of the house to be built in his mind; afterwards, he proposes it to others to be learned, engraved in metal or some other material; from which, thirdly, the craftsman draws and learns.

### APPENDIX TO THE TENTH THEOREM.

<margin>Matthew 23.</margin>
For Truth <note>Referring to Jesus Christ</note> commands through his own mouth: saying, "The *Scribes* and *Pharisees* have sat upon the chair of *Moses*: therefore, observe and do all things whatsoever they have said to you." In what manner, however, the chair of the *Mosaic* tradition succeeded step by step from *Moses* until the promulgation of the *Talmudic* book, from one listener to another, I have thought it would not be out of place to repeat here in a few words: provided that you recall to mind those things which I reviewed in the second Volume of this work concerning the various and different types of *Pharisees*, lest the ambiguity of the name confound a correct understanding of the matter.

<margin>These things are handed down elsewhere in another order. But meanwhile it is clear the author erred not a little in the calculation of time.</margin>
For it is read in the traditions of the ancient *Jewish* sages, which they call *Pirkei Avot*—that is, the "Chapters of the Fathers"—that *Moses* received the Law on Mount *Sinai*, and delivered and explained it to *Joshua*; *Joshua* indeed to the Elders, the Elders to the Prophets, the Prophets to the men of the Great Assembly: the last of whom was the high priest *Simeon the Just*, concerning whom the highest praises are sung in the book of *Ecclesiasticus*. Whom also in the Gospel, *Luke* in chapter 2 calls *Simeon the Just* <note>original: "Simonẽ iuſtum" — Ricius identifies the Simeon who held the infant Jesus with the historical Simeon the Just of the Great Assembly</note>, he delivered the Law to *Antigonus of Soho*; he to *Jose* the son of *John*, and to the other *Jose* the son of *Joezer*. Each *Jose* delivered this to *Nittai of Arbela*, and to *Joshua* the son of *Perachiah*. The younger *Talmudists* falsely affirm (on account of the ambiguity of the name) that *Jesus Christ our Lord* was a student of this man, which is false: for by the testimony of the *Talmudic* chapter *Helek* <note>A famous chapter in Tractate Sanhedrin</note>, that *Joshua* flourished in the time of *Hyrcanus* (whom they call *Jannai*); *Hyrcanus*, however (as the history of *Flavius Josephus* teaches), held the kingdom and the priesthood of *Jerusalem* at the same time nearly a hundred years before *Pontius Pilate*; but concerning these things more elsewhere. Therefore, *Nittai of Arbela* and *Joshua* delivered this to *Judah* son of *Tabbai* and to *Simeon* son of *Shetach*; both delivered this to *Shemaiah* and *Abtalion*. These again to *Hillel* and *Shammai*, concerning whom *Josephus* records many excellent things. These delivered it to *Rabbi Jochanan* son of *Zakkai*. Thus far in the Chapters of the Fathers. Then from various *Talmudic* writings they collect those things which follow immediately, just as the *Egyptian Rabbi Moses* <note>Moses Maimonides</note> in the preface to his *Deuteronomy* <note>The Mishneh Torah</note> and *Rabbi Isaac* in his *Astronomical* narration recount: a comrade and colleague to this *Rabbi Jochanan* was *Rabbi Simeon*: whose son was that old man *Gamaliel*, at whose feet the Apostle heard the Law.

<margin>Acts 22.</margin>
This same *Gamaliel* explained the Law to his son, also named *Rabbi Simeon*; he to his son *Rabbi Judah*, whom on account of the greatness of his wisdom and the integrity of his life, they call the *Holy Rabbi* [Rabbi Hakkadosh]; with whose company and constant familiarity (as the *Talmudists* narrate in the last chapter of the book of Blessings) the Emperor *Antoninus* surnamed *Pius* made use. This same *Rabbi Judah*, in the one hundred and twentieth year from the destruction of *Jerusalem*, was the first to condense the explanation of the *Mosaic* Law into a compendium called the *Mishnah*.

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

bound it <note>Referring to the Oral Law being condensed into a written code</note> and began to give it to the common people, which the entire synagogue of the Jews embraces as if delivered by the mouth of Moses. The same Rabbi Judah handed down the explanation of the Law and his code to another, Johanan, who in the three-hundredth year after the destruction of the Temple <note>The destruction of the Second Temple occurred in 70 CE; Ricius follows traditional dating here</note>, set forth that compendium, the *Mishnah*, more extensively and in a clearer style in one volume, which they call the Jerusalem Talmud. The colleagues of this Rabbi Johanan were Rav and Samuel, whose pupil was Rav Huna. He, in turn, had Rabba as a student; Rabba had Rava, whose student was Rav Ashi. Rav Ashi—excelling in learning, modesty of life, honors, and worldly glory—began to forge the Babylonian Talmud in the 436th year after the destruction of the Temple. However, prevented by death, he could not complete the undertaking, which his son, named Mor, along with his colleague Maremar, finished afterwards.

Furthermore, that Talmudic code contains the glosses and commentaries on the aforementioned compendium, the *Mishnah*. It also encompasses all the new regulations established according to the demands of time and place, as well as several mysteries of the sacred word and certain notable deeds and historical events. It was published in the year 4,365 from the beginning of the world (according to the Jewish computation) <note>Approximately 505 CE</note>, and in the 436th year from the destruction of Jerusalem. The whole community of Jews, exiled through various regions of the world, received this code with the highest veneration to be observed and followed in practice, and they still retain it today. Finally, the Egyptian Rabbi Moses <note>Maimonides (1135–1204), known as Rambam</note> enumerates forty generations from Moses down to the time the Talmudic code was given to the public; whoever desires to hear of these more extensively should seek the beginning of his *Deuteronomy* <note>Ricius is referring to the Introduction to the *Mishneh Torah*, Maimonides's code of law, which begins with a commentary on the transmission of the Law</note>. Regarding the junior scholars who came after the Talmudists, although many were men of exceptional learning and integrity, the authority of none of them is easily admitted unless it follows the dogma and footsteps of the Talmudic code. Therefore, I have judged it less necessary to explain their order. I have chosen to narrate here the aforementioned times and succession of the Talmudic canon because I have recognized that many things pertaining to the dogma of the Kabbalists are scattered and handed down in various places of that code.

### APPENDIX TO THE XI. THEOREM.

<margin>
Indeed, by the same progression, the Kabbalists weave the history of the Law, all of which are things created up to man; and again they study how to raise the human intellect from the Law itself to that same principle from which it took its origin. Thus, the intellect, having been raised, soon repeats these things and, weaving a triple engine in each part, turns to governing human affairs by a certain divine fate.
</margin>
For if you attend to the writings and dogmas of the Kabbalists, you will clearly understand that the "gates"—or the steps and limits of things—are suggested in the Law. By these, the human soul (which is the last of all spiritual creatures) and its organic body (which is the furthest offspring of the entire corporeal world) descend from the very Founder of the universe, God, and ascend there again (as if by the ladder which Jacob saw) and seek again their own principle and the origin of eternal life.

Rabbi Simeon <note>Simeon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, the prince of the Kabbalists, teaches in the book *Candor* <note>Likely referring to the *Zohar* (Book of Splendor)</note> that the first element of the book of Genesis <note>The letter *Beth* in *Bereshith*</note>, by its top point, designates the paternal principle, which they call the Supreme Diadem <term>Supreme Diadem: The Sephirah *Keter*, the highest emanation of God</term>. He teaches that the whole word *Bereshith* <note>Hebrew: "In the beginning"</note> refers to the filial hypostasis <note>The second person or "subsistence" of the Divine</note>, which they also call Wisdom <term>Wisdom: The Sephirah *Chokmah*</term>. By the second word, *Bara* (that is, "He created"), it signifies the process or emanation. By the third word, *Elohim* (that is, "God" or "Gods"), it indicates the Spirit of God, to which they ascribe the name of Prudence <term>Prudence: The Sephirah *Binah*</term> in the Sephirotic order.

From this indivisible and eternal Trinity, the Law itself then explains that the whole circuit of creatures, contained in heaven and earth, was created or emanated one by one. It calls the hypostasis of all bodies first of all *Tohu*, which is interpreted as "admirable" or "void." However, that by which that void has distinction and existence, it calls *Bohu*—which, according to its etymology, sounds like "that in which it is"—namely, what the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle</note> call "form." By "darkness," it suggests privation; through the six days of the works of the beginning, it designates six types of mobile things; and through the Sabbath, the seventh type, in which motion ceases. And when, immediately thereafter, it resumes the craftsmanship of the universe (like an epilogue), saying: "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth," it digresses into the history of the human fabric, as the end of all those generable things and of the entire Law, proceeding step by step... <note>catchword: step by step</note>

### APPENDIX TO THE 15TH THEOREM.

Those things which we have within ourselves are better known to us, which is why the doctrine of the soul <note>original: "animastica doctrina"</note> is more familiar to us, because it can be perceived daily. Moreover, there is a common assertion of the Kabbalists and Talmudists that there are as many affirmative commands <note>The 248 *mitzvot aseh*, or "thou shalts"</note> and deeds to be pursued in the Law as there are solid members and bones that support the human body—namely, 248 in number. Furthermore, there are as many prohibitive commands <note>The 365 *mitzvot lo ta'aseh*, or "thou shalt nots"</note> and deeds to be avoided as there are passages of the sinews and veins—namely, 365—by which the ten primary members and the entire organic body are bound together and fused into one. But you should know that from this "bloody image" of the human body, it is not the essence of the great world <note>the macrocosm, or the universe at large</note> that is understood, but rather the mutual dependence and connection of parts; and not only the order of the world, but also of human society is understood from the microcosm <note>the "little world" of man</note>. As Aristotle also teaches, a city should be constructed according to the example of a man; and the Apostle <note>St. Paul</note> says that the Church is the body of Christ the head. Therefore, the Law, delivered in the likeness of man, imitates the structure of man.

### APPENDIX TO THE 16TH THEOREM.

For the Kabbalists hand down a threefold man (in whom the threefold machine of the world also shines), hinted at in the works of the beginning <note>The Creation in Genesis</note>, where the structure of man is expressed three times and in three ways of building. First (according to the true pattern), we read in Genesis 1: *And God created man himself in his own image.* Second, in Genesis 2: *God (Elohim) formed man from the dust of the earth.* Third, in Genesis 5, it says: *In the likeness of Elohim he made (or adapted) him.* For to be "created" (that is, to emanate from the first being) rightly belongs to the human mind <note>original: "mens"</note>, which is truly to be called the "first man." But to "form" <note>original: "formare"</note> belongs to the spirit <note>original: "spiritui"</note>, which immediately gives form to the organic body with life, motion, and nutrition. Truly, to be "made" or "adapted" <note>original: "fieri"</note> belongs to this coarse body, whence by the breathing in (as the text of Genesis 2 teaches) of the breath of life, man was made into a living soul. 

But if you attend to the series of words concerning the structure of man, you will find in one place "likeness" <note>original: "similitudinem"</note> explained equally with "image" <note>original: "imaginem"</note>. In another place, however, neither; elsewhere only "image"; elsewhere "likeness" alone. For concerning the whole composite structure of man, where we read: *Let us make man*, the image is expressed together with the likeness. But a little later (concerning the more important part of the composite, surely), it is written: *and Elohim created man himself in his own image.* There, in the pattern, no mention is made of likeness. Thereafter, concerning the man "formed" in Genesis 2, neither image nor likeness is commemorated. But concerning the "made" or "adapted" man, "likeness" is indeed read, but "image" is wrapped in silence. This one thing, moreover, in every...

You, who are wise, should ponder these things with yourself and revolve them in your mind.

### APPENDIX TO THE XVII AND XVIII THEOREM.

<margin>Romans 12</margin>

<margin>Genesis 1</margin>
No wise and prudent investigator of secret matters should wonder that the Kabbalist strives with such diligent study to adapt the Law of Moses to the human frame <note>original: "humanae compagini"</note>. Since man himself is a <term>microcosm</term> <note>A "small world" that mirrors the universe.</note> (as I mentioned a little earlier), just as he was fashioned according to the habit and example of the "macrocosm" (the great world), so also the Law by which he is ruled must reflect the Law of the great world. However, that celestial Law is known to us from no other source than through its effects and its sensible works; yet we perceive more surely and certainly by our senses those things which we constantly experience within ourselves. Therefore, the parts, operations, and acts of this microcosm instruct us more clearly and safely, and teach us to imitate the celestial Law better than any parts or works of the [wider] universe. Thus, he who desires to gaze upon the beauty of the universe ought to dwell upon this. And for that reason, that wise Architect and moderator of the life of mortals strives greatly to institute the orthodox commonwealth of the Christian flock according to the habit and example of this microcosm: *We, being many* (he says), *are one body in Christ: and every one members one of another. If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling? But now are they many members, yet but one body.* Thus he speaks. Finally, he very carefully gave warnings in this manner of instituting and governing the Christian polity in his letters to the Romans, the Corinthians, and the Ephesians. Hence the ancients said that philosophy is nothing else than "to know oneself"; for philosophy encompasses the knowledge of all things. Man is truly the work of all causes, and the image of all things. So that you may understand this, know that the Kabbalists do not recognize man merely as he is composed of principles or elements, but as he consists in himself of peculiar principles by which he is similar to the great world. For they feel he was made in the image of the world, as Rabbi Joshua explains that passage in Genesis 1: *Let us make man in our likeness*, where he wishes it to be understood that God consulted all the works of heaven and earth to form man—that is, to express the image of all the world's works in man. If it is true that man is the image of the world, and no image (insofar as it is an image) is a part of its own exemplar—since they are relatively opposed and mutually exclude each other—it follows that man is not a "part" of the world; that is, he is not merely a composite of elements or principles which are parts of the world. Therefore, those who consider man as the image of the world, like the Kabbalists, understand the principles in man not as the elements of the great world or similar things, but those which constitute man from his very propagation, such as the menses, sperm, embryo, humors, and the rest: from which, toward the likeli-

<meta>This page continues Ricius’s argument regarding the human being as a microcosm (a "small world") and how the Law of Moses reflects this structure. It specifically delves into the Kabbalistic distinction between the first four books of the Pentateuch and the fifth book, Deuteronomy.</meta>

# PAULUS RICIUS

...man is constituted in the likeness of the greater world <note>the macrocosm</note>, in whom there is nothing that does not have its counterpart in the greater world. Therefore, the Law reveals all things through the human form, as if through the most illustrious image of reality. By knowing this human form, the Kabbalists believe they can attain the knowledge of God, the prediction of the future, and the performance of miracles. For those three things depend upon our connection with the higher realms. This connection with the higher powers is understood through the likeness of man to the world, as you have in the first book of *Celestial Agriculture*, in the proof of the article: "And in Jesus Christ," etc.

In all these things, the Law especially imitates the structure of man. For this reason, those who use allegory do not without consideration divide the Law into male and female. They observe that Moses—not without a great mystery—never speaks of himself in the first person throughout the first four volumes of the Pentateuch; he does not say, "I was feeding your sheep," but rather, "Moses was feeding." Nor is it read anywhere, "God spoke to me," but rather, "to Moses." However, in Deuteronomy, the fifth volume of the Pentateuch, when he wished to explain the Law, he speaks of himself throughout. "I said to you," (he says): "Then you answered me," and "God spoke to me." Thus, throughout that entire volume (excluding its beginning and end), he expresses and speaks of himself.

When the Kabbalists observe and weigh the secret of this variation, they conclude that no other true cause or reason can be given except that in the first four volumes, neither Moses himself nor the human spirit speaks, but rather the Divine Mind, or the **Active Intellect** <note>original: "agens intellectus"</note> as they call it, which plays the role of the groom and the male. In the fifth volume, however, Moses and the human mind speak, which they call the **Possible or Material Intellect** <note>the "intellectus possibilis," the capacity of the human mind to receive knowledge</note>. This intellect, bearing the likeness of the bride and the female, desires to be joined to the Groom (as a woman to a man). The Prince of the Peripatetics <note>Aristotle</note>, in his book *On Physics* <note>original: "de Physico auditu"</note>, did not at all shrink from attributing this relationship to every instance of matter and form.

Hence, in the sacred utterances (as I explained in the preceding volume), we very frequently read that the Divine Mind is called the "man," "husband," and "groom," while the human intellect is called the "bride," "virgin," and "wife." For this reason, the Kabbalists not unjustly ascribe the first four volumes of the Pentateuch to the male, while they attribute the last to the female. From this, in the first giving of the Law <note>in Exodus</note>, in the third commandment <note>the Sabbath commandment</note>, there is the word **Zachor** <gloss>Remember</gloss>; but in the second giving of the Law <note>in Deuteronomy</note>, there is the word **Schamor** <gloss>Observe</gloss>. Now, *Zachor* signifies the male, while *Schamor* signifies the female. These two words contain the entire type of the Law, as is found in the commentary on Ruth and in the *Book of Brightness* <note>The "Sefer Ha-Bahir," an early Kabbalistic text</note>; these things are clear enough to one who understands. For to him who has some light of the supernal wisdom, more will be given and he will abound. But he who has it not, but relies only on worldly wisdom, even that worldly wisdom which he possesses shall be taken away and removed, because, like a mirror image, it is turned away from its original pattern, the light of super-celestial wisdom.

### APPENDIX TO THE 21ST THEOREM

The Kabbalists teach that the final Sephirah <note>known as Malchut or "Kingdom"</note>—which they call the Matron and the Queen of Heaven—is designated by the rainbow in Genesis 9, and by the mirror and the bond or connection in Exodus. No wise man is ignorant of the fact that these attributes belong solely to the nature of the soul. Indeed, regarding that passage in Exodus, "And on the seventh day he ceased" (or rested) "and was refreshed," <note>original: *animavit*, literally 'given soul'</note> the Kabbalists call this the "added soul" <note>the *Neshamah Yeterah*, a traditional Jewish concept of an extra spiritual soul received on the Sabbath</note>. <margin>Chapter 31</margin>

But you, who are wise in this matter, remember here and in similar places that it was once cautioned by the decrees of the holy fathers that the secrets of the Scriptures should not be pronounced using philosophical terms, even if they hold the same meaning as the orthodox view. Both Paul, in his letter to the Romans, and Augustine, in his book of *Retractations*, teach this very thing. Therefore, differences in names and words do not always designate a varied or different concept between the faithful saints and the Gentile sages; consider this carefully.

### APPENDIX TO THE 25TH THEOREM

Not only the authority of the saints, but even sound reason persuades and demonstrates that the Empyrean <note>the highest, most spiritual level of heaven, often associated with fire or pure light</note> heaven exists. For among beings (as we gather from the second book of the Peripatetic <note>Aristotelian</note> foundations of the heavens), one type obtains the highest perfection without the aid of any effort; this is the first, eternal, and incomprehensible Good.
<margin>1. The first Good.</margin>
Another attains perfection (though not the highest) through a single, uniform action, such as the angelic mind.
<margin>2. Angelic Mind.</margin>
Another achieves its perfection through many and various actions, such as the celestial soul.
<margin>3. Celestial Soul.</margin>
But another is so sluggish that it possesses no operation of its own and suffers from a perpetual lack of power (by its very nature); this is human reason, which they call the "potential" or "material intellect," much like prime matter, which is devoid of all perfection.
<margin>4. Human Reason.</margin>
Thus, by that same Law, when we see in the whole scope of physical nature that the Earth is immobile in its place (due to its extreme unsuitability for motion), the order of things and nature requires another equal body which, because of its extreme physical perfection, requires no movement of travel. For the superior perfection of things consists more in a state of rest than in motion, as I discussed more extensively in the first volume of this work. This sublime and immobile body, therefore, the wise theologians call the "Empyrean." The Kabbalists, however (as the *Book of Divine Order* testifies), call it the "Intellectual Heaven."
<margin>The Empyrean and the Intellectual are the same.</margin>

### APPENDIX TO THE 26TH THEOREM

Since we infer the multitude and distinctions of Intelligences <note>Angels</note> through the variety of operations and moving bodies, it is therefore necessary that ten intellectual substances be set over the ten previously enumerated bodies. Lest the manifold way the Kabbalists consider these things should leave you wavering and hesitant, you ought to take note of this one thing: although the animastic order, when compared in its entirety to the angelic mind, holds the condition and name of a woman, nevertheless its parts compared among themselves are assigned the condition and nomenclature of male or female. For the final portion of this entire universal order is recognized as the rational soul; when you refer this to the lower powers—namely, the vital and animal powers—it then plays the part of the male. Because many of the younger students, who boast of the teachings of the allegorists or Kabbalists, are ignorant of this, they affirm many unspeakable and ridiculous things regarding the heavens.

<margin>Macrocosm</margin>

## APPENDIX TO THE FINAL THEOREM.

<margin>1 Corinthians 13.</margin>
<margin>Deuteronomy 10.</margin>
Since man was made according to the pattern of the universe, embracing a threefold machine within himself, if he desires to seek and obtain his wish from God—the giver of all good things—it is necessary that he adapt himself in mind, sense, and body. To prevent the "first Adam" <note>The earthly, fallen nature of man</note> from being distracted, enticed by the woman and his spouse Eve (who was seduced by the serpent's cunning), it is necessary for him to gather all the powers of his framework into one, turning and transferring them toward heavenly things. This method of working and adapting is what the Kabbalists <note>original: *Cabalei*</note> call the "correspondence of channels." This is because anyone who desires to reach the spring of super-celestial waters—which trickle down through various pipe-like passages—and wishes to drink the liquid of eternal life, must also erect his own pipes and channels. The openings of these must correspond exactly to the paths of the sublime channels above. Otherwise, the gushing waters do not flow into the pool, but into external pits (1 Corinthians 13). He who does not properly align his channels will not share in that super-celestial distillation, but will instead draw up "empty gold" <note>A metaphor for a useless or illusory reward</note>. Therefore Moses commands: *Fear the Lord your God, serve Him, cling to Him, and swear by His name* <note>Deuteronomy 10:20</note>. For to "swear by His name" requires the adherence of the mind. Furthermore, the adherence of the mind requires the compliance and service of the body, and that service demands fear. 

Therefore, whoever wishes to obtain his desires from the very spring of all good things must worship Him "in spirit and in truth" (as John says). Since worship, or prayer, is nothing other than the elevation of the mind to God and a stable adherence to Him, the Hebrew word for prayer is pronounced *teffila* <note>original: *teffila*; Hebrew: תְּפִלָּה (*tefillah*)</note>, which signifies a bond and stable adherence. This is according to the word of James: *Let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he who wavers is like a wave of the sea, moved and carried about by the wind. Therefore, let that man not think he shall receive anything from God* <note>James 1:6-7</note>. This is what the Apostle says. 

Even the Pagan Iamblichus <note>A 3rd-century Neoplatonic philosopher</note> declares that he learned this concerning the mysteries from the columns of Mercury <note>The mythical pillars on which Hermes/Mercury supposedly inscribed all knowledge</note>. He says: *The powers that follow the gods are only then first reached when the soul has laid aside its shifting mode of cognition.* And a little later: *Since knowledge occurs through a process of equalization, it follows that we reach the eternal and immovable powers by an eternal, immovable, and simple notion*—which he previously called the "contact of divinity," and which we call "faith," followed by "adherence." 

Therefore, the entire power of successfully praying and obtaining wishes from that Giver of goods—who is near and gives abundantly to all who call upon His name in truth—lies in the adherence and stability of the mind through faith in God. For just as the concepts of the human mind cannot be expressed by any movement or gesture of the tongue or any bodily organ unless the "motive spirit" <note>The subtle substance then believed to carry signals from the soul to the muscles</note> adheres to the "imagining and thinking spirit," so it is with the body. # ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

...with these things added, I shall finish the first part of this volume by the will of the heavens.

### APPENDIX TO THE FORTY-SIXTH THEOREM.

The "channels of the pipes" <note>original: *Canales fistulæ*</note> are to be understood no less in that mystical union which exists between us as the bride and the bridegroom <note>A reference to the soul's union with God</note> than in the physical mechanism of hearing. Thus also the trumpet (of which the Apostle says: *We shall all rise at the last trumpet* <note>1 Corinthians 15:52</note>) is to be understood in the eighth member of both the Archetypal and the corporeal world. This, however, does not happen unless each of the seven members has first completed its own specific sound or work.

### APPENDIX TO THE LAST THEOREM.

Since man was made in the likeness of the universe, encompassing a threefold machine within himself, if he desires to seek and obtain his prayer from God, the giver of all good things, it is worthwhile that he harmonize himself in mind, sense, and body. To prevent the "first Adam" <note>The intellectual or higher self</note> from being distracted—enticed by the woman and his spouse Eve <note>The senses or lower nature</note>, who was seduced by the cunning of the serpent—it is necessary that he gather all the forces of his structure into one, turning and transferring them toward celestial things.

The <term>Kabbalists</term> <note>original: *Cabalici*; practitioners of Jewish mysticism</note> call this method of working and harmonizing the "correspondence of channels." This is because whoever desires to reach the spring of the super-celestial waters—which trickle downward through various pipe-like passages—and wishes to drink the liquor of eternal life, must himself also erect pipes and channels whose openings correspond exactly to the paths of the sublime channels. Otherwise, the gushing waters do not flow into the pool, but into external abysses. <margin>1 Corinthians 13.</margin> And he who does not rightly align his channels will by no means share in that super-celestial dripping, but will instead draw in empty air.

For this reason, Moses commands: <margin>Deuteronomy 10.</margin> *Fear the Lord your God, serve him, cling to him, and swear by his name.* Indeed, "swearing by His name" requires the adherence of the mind. The adherence of the mind, in turn, requires the compliance and servitude of the body; and that servitude demands fear. Therefore, he who wishes to obtain his desires from the very spring of all good things must adore Him "in spirit and in truth" (as John says). 

Since adoration, or prayer, is nothing other than the lifting of the mind to God and a stable clinging to Him, the Hebrew word for prayer is pronounced <term>tefillah</term> <note>original: *teffila*</note>, which signifies a bond and stable attachment. This is according to the words of James: *But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. Let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.* <note>James 1:6–7</note> 

Even the pagan <term>Iamblichus</term> <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher, c. 245–325 AD</note> declares in his book *On the Mysteries* that he learned this from the columns of Hermes <note>original: *Mercurij*</note>. He says: "The powers that follow the gods are only reached when the soul has laid aside its restless mode of knowledge." And a little later, he says that since knowledge happens through alignment, it follows that "we reach the eternal and immobile powers with an eternal, immobile, and simple notion," which (just before) he calls "contact with divinity." And we call this "faith," which is followed by "adherence."

Therefore, the entire power of praying successfully and obtaining one's vows from that Giver of goods—who is near and gives abundantly to all who call upon His name in truth—lies in the adherence and stability of the mind through faith in God. For just as the concepts of the human mind cannot be expressed by any movement or gesture of the tongue or any physical organ unless the "motive spirit" <note>The force that moves the body</note> clings to the "imaginary and cognitive spirit," and just as when some phlegm or bile obstructs the passages and separates the motive spirit from the cognitive one (from which lethargy, paralysis, or numbness occupies the limbs), then the organ afflicted by this symptom can in no way bring forth or explain any concept of the mind or cognitive power through any movement or gesture.

<margin>The Archetypal Man</margin> Thus the Kabbalists also enumerate as many formal or ideal parts of the "Archetypal Man," <note>original: *Archetypi hominis*; the divine blueprint of humanity, often called Adam Kadmon</note> which, on account of their eminence and the incomprehensible nobility of their substance, they designate by ten naked and pure degrees of numbering, or Sephirot. Often, they even contemplate the celestial Archetype and the earthly man together as one individual, whose mover and worker-of-all-things is the King and Creator of the universe, God Himself. This is recounted more fully by Rabbi Ishmael in the book *Kuma* <note>original: *kuma*; referring to the *Shi'ur Qomah*, an ancient text on the divine measurements</note>—that is, *The Stature*—and by Rabbi Simeon in the *Book of Apples*. Therefore, he who considers these things too little, and does not know how to adapt them to these introductory theorems, will be like one unskilled in the art of swimming; when he commits himself to the sea to collect gems, he is soon snatched by the waves and plunged headlong into the deep.

Therefore, ponder these things and revolve them in your mind. As for the remaining theorems, some are clear in themselves and ready at hand for the intelligent reader; others, however, can easily become clear and known to the perceptive and diligent reader who weighs the previously held documents through repeated reading, and who attends to the various modes of allegorizing I have set forth in the appropriate places. Briefly, therefore, for the understanding of the last theorem—

## APPENDIX TO THE 46th THEOREM.

The "pipes" of the channels must be understood no less in that bride who is with us and her groom <note>Likely referring to the mystical union of the soul (the bride) and Christ or the Divine (the groom)</note> than in the physical machine of hearing. Thus also the trumpet (of which the Apostle says: *We shall all rise at the last trumpet*) is to be understood in the eighth member of both the Archetypal and physical world. This, however, does not occur unless each of the seven members has performed its own sound or work.

## APPENDIX TO THE FINAL THEOREM.

Since man was made according to the constitution of the entire universe, embracing a threefold machine within himself <note>Refers to the traditional division of body, soul, and spirit</note>, if he desires to obtain and secure his prayer from God himself—the giver of all good things—it is worthwhile that he adapt himself in mind, sense, and body. To ensure that the first Adam is not pulled apart—allured through his woman and wife Eve <note>original: *Heuam*</note>, who was seduced by the serpent’s cunning—it is necessary that he gather all the powers of his frame into one, and turn and transfer them toward celestial things. 

This manner of working and adapting, the Kabbalists <note>original: *Cabalei*</note> call the "correspondence of channels." This is because he who desires to reach the spring of super-celestial waters dripping down through various pipe-like passages and draw the liquid of eternal life, must himself also erect pipes and channels whose openings exactly match the passages of the sublime channels. Otherwise, the gushing waters flow not into the pool, but into external abysses. (1 Corinthians 13). And he who does not rightly arrange his channels will by no means become a partaker of that super-celestial dripping, but will instead breathe in empty air. 

And for this reason, Moses commands (in <margin>Deuteronomy 10</margin>): *Fear the Lord your God, serve him, cling to him, and swear in his name.* For "swearing in His name" demands the "clinging" <note>original: *adhæsionem*</note> of the mind. This mental clinging requires the obedience and servitude of the body, and that servitude requires fear. Therefore, whoever wishes to obtain his desires from the very fountainhead of all good things must worship him "in spirit and in truth" (as John says). 

Now worship, or prayer, is nothing other than the lifting of the mind to God and a stable clinging to Him; hence prayer is pronounced by the Hebrew word *tefillah* <note>original: *teffila*</note>, which signifies a bond and stable adherence. This is according to that word of James: *But let him ask in faith, hesitating in nothing.* For he who hesitates is like a wave of the sea, moved and carried about by the wind. Therefore, let that man not think that he will receive anything from God. 

This is also what that pagan Iamblichus <note>A 3rd-century Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote on theurgy and Egyptian mysteries</note> declares in *On the Mysteries*, having learned it from the "columns of Mercury" <note>original: *Mercurij*; referring to the legendary inscribed pillars of Hermes Trismegistus</note>: "The attendant powers of the gods," he says, "are only then first reached when the soul has laid aside its restless mode of knowing." And a little later, he says: "since knowledge occurs through equalization, it follows that we reach the eternal and immobile powers with an eternal, immobile, and simple notion," which (just before) he calls the "contact of divinity." And we call this "faith," which is followed by "clinging." 

Therefore, the whole power of praying and obtaining vows from that giver of good things (who is near, giving abundantly to all who call upon His name in truth) is situated in the clinging and stability of the mind through faith in God. For just as a concept of the human mind cannot be expressed by any movement or gesture of the tongue or any physical organ unless the moving spirit clings to the imaginative and thinking spirit; and where some phlegm or bile obstructs the passages and separates the moving spirit from the thinking one—from which lethargy, paralysis, or numbness occupies the limbs of the body—then the organ, which is subject to this affliction <note>original: *Synthomati*; a medical symptom or condition</note>, can by no means bring forth or explain any concept of the mind or thinking power by any movement or gesture. 

So also the very mind of mortals, when (because of the gap created by sensible things and the allurements of the flesh) it is distracted and turned away from the Supernal Mind—to which all elements and bodies of the world are like organs connected to it, obeying its nod—then that human mind, affected as if by numbness or paralysis, becomes unable to receive the conform[ity]... <note>Text ends mid-word: *confor-*</note>

For individuals have individual guardian angels, as it is written in the Gospel; and then the angel favors its own body more than those of others. From this, the worship and invocation of saints (if you consider it) takes its true origin—about which I shall speak more extensively elsewhere, life permitting. 

Finally, gather from these things that the whole reason and power of "adherence" consists in conformity, upon which the basis and foundation of faith, knowledge, meditation, prayer, and all the sacraments depend. And although the more powerful conformity consists in mental work, nonetheless the cooperation of the imagination and the fitting gestures of the limbs provide no small amount of energy, as I have explained at greater length in the treatise on the common nature of the sacraments. From this, the perceptive and diligent reader may clearly judge how much in this wretched and iron age of ours, many who claim for themselves an understanding of the sacred scriptures are insane and defile the sacraments of true piety. Thereupon, the same Kabbalist also performs an imaginative action conforming to the mental one, by fashioning and impressing with a stable concept the sacred face of the names, their shape, points, and elements. By a similar law, he performs external works of the body with a certain modulation of the voice and gestures of the limbs, in various ways according to the variety of things sought and names to be invoked. ...face between his knees; sacred history recounts such things of Moses, Joshua, Elisha, and other Prophets when they implored divine help, for they performed various and diverse bodily acts according to the variety of their requests. The Great Priest Rabbi Ishmael testifies to this very thing in his *Book of Temples* <note>The *Hekhalot*, an early Jewish mystical text describing the "palaces" or heavenly halls.</note>. He taught that a certain unleavened cake, made while invoking specific divine names, when taken with sincere faith and a pure mind, plainly affirms that the soul and heart of the eater are immediately inspired and irradiated by the light of supernal wisdom. This is what the Kabbalists <note>Followers of the Jewish mystical tradition known as Kabbalah.</note> together with the Talmudists <note>Scholars of the Talmud, the central text of Jewish civil and ceremonial law.</note> commonly call *petichat halev* <note>original: "pessihas halef", meaning "opening of the heart".</note>. This is the same word pronounced by the minister of sacred Baptism, saying: "Receive the salt of wisdom," and "*Effeta*," which means "Be opened."

It is also a well-worn and certain fact among more recent Talmudists concerning Eleazar, surnamed Kalir <note>Eleazar ben Kalir, a prolific early medieval Hebrew poet whose hymns are still used in Jewish liturgy.</note>. They assert he was called "Kalir" because, by eating a certain cake, he was suddenly inspired by the heavenly spirit and produced sublime and profound oracles of wisdom in hymnic praises, which are commonly sung by almost the entire synagogue of the Jews on solemn and feast days. Thus Rabbi Johanan, son of Zakkai, so illuminated Master Eleazar—who was previously most ignorant of all letters—at a sudden banquet that, to the greatest admiration of everyone, he suddenly explained the secrets of the Law. There are many more testimonies of this kind from the Talmudists and Kabbalists, which I have decided to pass over in silence here for the sake of brevity and to avoid being tedious.

Hence, I can never sufficiently marvel at the madness of the younger Israelites and Talmudists, who mock the sacred mysteries of Baptism and the Eucharist as if they were unheard-of and fanatical delusions. Nevertheless, because the practice of the ancient Kabbalists of this kind and the secrets of the holy names are shrouded in such great obscurity and a variety of veils—and since they have subsequently fallen into the hands of so many foolish and profane people—it has happened that the truth is now wrapped in lies in many ways. The purity of the matter is everywhere confused and turbulent, so much so that even many of the foremost Kabbalists are now ignorant of which specific actions of the holy names, and what proper action of the mind, imagination, and body, should be applied to each vow and prayer. 

I confess that I myself do not know this either, and therefore I leave the specific and individual secrets of this practice to be explained by men of keener sight, wisdom, and intelligence—those who have unfolded the diverse writings of the ancient Kabbalists on these matters and have penetrated their entire meaning. Yet there is no doubt that all these things are kabbalistically included in the Law <note>The Torah or Pentateuch.</note>, since the Law shows all the works of God, and the angels hold the first place among God's works. Therefore, the Law also explains the angels and their names, offices, places, etc. And as the Kabbalists say, the greatest intention of the Law is concerned with the angelic choir, to which that saying of Stephen also alludes: *You received the Law by the disposition of angels.* 

Thus says Moses of Gerona <note>Moses ben Nahman, also known as Nachmanides or Ramban (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar and mystic.</note> in the beginning of Genesis: "The whole Law is composed of divine names." Thus the Talmud often treats of Metatron, Achteriel, and other angels. And it would be absurd, when Moses recounts divine oracles and many names of perishable things, if he were to apply the extremes without the middle; that is, to pass over the angelic things which are in the middle between God and perishable things. And [Moses of] Gerona says that Solomon learned all these things from the Law when he says in Wisdom 7: *Whatever things are hidden and unforeseen, I have learned.* 

But whoever desires to know all these things—the names, offices, and places of the angels—let him read Rabbi Ishmael in the *Book of Temples* and the *Book of the Measurement of the Stature* <note>The *Shi'ur Qomah*, a mystical text describing the anthropomorphic dimensions of the divine.</note>. Also the *Book of Apples* <note>The *Sefer ha-Tappuach*, an Aristotelian-style dialogue on the soul.</note>, and the *Book of Lights* by Rabbi Simeon, and the *Gate of Light* <note>The *Sha'are Orah* by Joseph Gikatilla, a fundamental manual of Kabbalah.</note>, and the *Book of Brilliance* <note>The *Sefer ha-Bahir*.</note>, and all the commentaries on the *Book of Formation* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah*.</note>. But especially and before all others, the *Book of Temples* by Rabbi Simeon. 

To me, however, it has now seemed more advisable and safer to seek with an anxious and solicitous mind the secrets of no name to be invoked, except that name which is above every name, at which every knee bows, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth. Though this name may be commonly on everyone's lips, yet (says the Herald of Truth <note>Referring to the Apostle Paul in 1 Corinthians 12.</note>)

->PREFACE OF PAULUS RICIUS TO THE EPITOME OF THE GATES OF LIGHT.<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'P' featuring floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>
With the first part of this volume—which concerns the introduction to the Kabbalah—now completed, I proceed, with the help of the heavens, to explain the second part, contained within the summary of the *Gates of Light*. In this compendium (just as in the preceding introduction), although many things are handed down which might offend the ears and minds of the "sons of darkness" <note>A term likely referring to those who are spiritually blind or hostile to mystical inquiry.</note> and those who apply little effort or zeal to investigating the mysteries of divine speech, it nevertheless seemed wicked and impious to deny these things to the pious and prudent "sons of light." <margin>1 Corinthians 1</margin> For in this way, that far-sighted herald of truth, the Apostle, did not shrink from preaching Christ the Savior crucified, even though it was a scandal to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles; this was because, to those who were called, that preaching was the power and wisdom of God. I put this forward not because I boast of being wise in the teachings of the Kabbalists and those who speak in allegories, or as one who has thoroughly unearthed its hidden and profound depths—for I hardly presume to have touched the thresholds and beginnings of its entrance—but I prefer myself to the needy and the scorner. I do not promise to be a Master; rather, what I have opened for the understanding of this doctrine, I have handed down not so much with the spirit of teaching, but of advising and awakening. My goal is that the more perceptive minds of students, supported by celestial light, might be able to climb higher through attentive meditation on these things and penetrate the inner shrines of secrets. For "to him who has" (as I have explained before) "it shall be given, and he shall abound; but from him who has not, even what he seems to have shall be taken away." <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25:29.</note> Having tasted these things first, listen now to Rabbi Joseph of Castile himself (as he is presumed to be), the author of this volume, and attend to him speaking thus (having called upon the Father of Lights).

## THE GATES OF LIGHT.

<image-desc>Large woodcut decorative initial 'E' depicting two scholars seated at a table covered with books and scrolls; one scholar points towards a text while the other looks on.</image-desc>
You have requested for a long time now, my most beloved, that I show you the path of light concerning the Names of God—which it has pleased us to call "measures" and <term>Sephirot</term> <note>original: "sphiros"; the ten divine emanations or attributes in Kabbalistic thought through which the Infinite interacts with the universe.</note>, that is, "enumerations"—by which you might be able to obtain your wish and reach the goal of your desire. Therefore, since I have perceived this petition to be just and have judged the intention itself to be honorable, I was unable to draw back my foot from making you a sharer in the way of light. Now, therefore, be vigilant, so that you may recognize the path which the Most High prefers or scorns. When you have attained it, you shall be heard when you cry out, and you shall be written among the assembly of those who approach closest to the Most High. You shall cherish Him with all the powers of your soul, you shall delight in God, and He will thoroughly fulfill the innermost desires of your heart. You know, therefore (unless perhaps you have heard it), the God of the world, the God in whose sight the heavens and the depths are struck with awe, and by whose fear the whole circle of the earth is shaken. And by His indignation, who shall remain? And who can stand before the fury of His wrath? For He does not trust even His own holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in His eyes; how much more abominable and useless is man, drinking up iniquity like water? And in what way shall one born of woman abuse the holy Names of God, or dare to lay hands upon the crown of the kingdom for his own gain? For our elders established that whoever pronounces the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God (YHVH), considered too sacred to be spoken aloud in Jewish tradition.</note> according to its own letters shall have no part in the world to come.

## RICIUS.

This discourse concerns only the name <term>Tetragrammaton</term>, which is communicable to the Creator alone and to none of His creatures. Therefore, just as it is considered irreverence and contempt when a son calls a parent by their proper name, so it is surely ascribed to rash presumption to call the celestial parent and incomprehensible King of Ages by His own particular name. Since, therefore, contempt and rash presumption toward God excludes one from the salvation of the world to come, it was not without justice that the authority of the ancients decreed that he who utters the great and terrible name of the Creator by its own characters (unless some pious cause urges it) shall not have a part in the future world. To this is added that, just as the Creator of all things, God Himself, is not grasped by any creature exactly as He is, so it was fitting that the Name which designates that incomprehensible Being should not be pronounced as the written letters sound. It was permitted only to the <term>High Priest</term> <note>original: "Pontifici"; referring to the Kohen Gadol in the ancient Temple of Jerusalem.</note> in the sanctuary, only once a year on the day of atonement and the great day of repentance, to express that same name by its own characters. Hence the Apostle decreed to Timothy: "Let everyone," he says, "who calls on the name of the Lord depart from iniquity."

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

## THE AUTHOR.

<margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin>
Indeed, the holy and preeminent Rabbi Hanina, son of Teradion <note>original: "Rabi Henina Tradionis filius"; a famous 2nd-century Jewish martyr who was executed by the Romans for teaching the Torah publicly.</note>, because he explained the Name itself using its own letters—even if he did so not for common or profane use, but for the sake of learning and so that he might know the mysteries of the Most High—could not escape the punishment for such a crime. Who then will doubt that the same might happen to us, poor and weak as we are? For you see what is forbidden in the Law of the Most High: "Thou shalt not take," it says, "the name of God (namely the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, considered too holy to be spoken aloud by many traditions.</note>) your God in vain," although the intent is to warn against perjury. Yet the Law uses the word "vain" here so that (as the Chaldean version <note>Referring to the Targum, an ancient Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible.</note> testifies) the meaning sounds as follows: no one should utter the name of God with their lips for no purpose. For it would have been easier to write, and clearer to understand: "do not swear falsely by the name of God, your God"; yet it is written, "thou shalt not take." Therefore Moses, the teacher of us all (ascending on high), when he learned from the ministering angels the mystery of commemorating the name of the Most High, warned Israel, saying: "When I invoke the name of God, give magnificence to our God." If the angels of heaven are warned about the mention of the name of the Most High, how much more does it concern the son of man, who is reduced to moths and worms? Much less should he, who is easily swayed by thought, presume to fit the Creator's crown to his own use, especially in this age in which we live, where the learning is hidden from us which provides the correct method of commemorating the name of the Most High and His other names—a commemoration (I say) that is suited to the work itself. Therefore, he who strives to mention it achieves nothing more than his own destruction and obtains only a fragment of a clay pot. Regarding this and similar things, our masters said: "Whoever does not revere the glory of his Creator, it would be better for him not to have entered the mechanism of this world."

<margin>Psalm 90 <note>In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 91:14.</note></margin>
Now therefore, my son, hear my voice, and attend with your ears to my counsel; if sinners wish to entice you, do not listen. If they say, "follow us, and we will impart to you the knowledge of the holy names (for you to use)," turn your ears away; do not adhere to their counsel, but rather flee their wicked steps, and you shall pull your feet back entirely from their path. For all names of this kind and their use are snares and the traps of hunters, which lead souls into eternal destruction. And even if the ancient wise men knew the divine names handed down by word of mouth from the Prophets—such as the name of seventy-two letters, the name of twelve letters, and many others of this sort, by which they could perform signs, wonders, and portents in the world—they were by no means accustomed to misuse them for their own benefit. They used them only at that time when the nations were striving to wrench the Israelites away from the true worship of God, or when the sanctification or glory of the Most High God might emerge from some work. Just as Rabbi Meir <note>A famous scholar of the Mishnah.</note>, who rescued his wife’s sister from a brothel, commanded the guard or servant, saying: "When you find yourself in distress, say: 'God of Rabbi Meir, answer me.'" But that same Rabbi Meir, when he saw himself subjected to danger, took flight rather than resort to the use of the holy name. Likewise, one must judge the deeds of Honi the Circle-Drawer <note>original: "Honi Maagalefis"; a Jewish scholar of the 1st century BCE known for his miracle-working prayer for rain.</note>, and Rava <note>original: "Roua"; a 4th-century Babylonian scholar.</note> with King Shapur <note>original: "Sabor Rege"; a Sasanian king of Persia.</note>, and those similar to them. Therefore, the fence of truth and the tradition of the covenant is this: that he who desires to obtain his prayers through the holy names should strive with all his strength in the Law, so that in it he may recognize the meaning of whichever holy names, namely: *Eheieh* (I Am), *Yah*, *Adonai* (Lord), the *Tetragrammaton* (YHWH), *El* (God), *Eloah*, *Elohim*, *Adonai*, *Tzvaot* (of Hosts), *Elohe Tzvaot*, *Shaddai* (Almighty). And let him know and understand that each of the aforesaid names acts as a key for some need of the age. When you have looked upon these more attentively and clearly understood each one, you will determine that the Law and all its commandments hang from them. You will admire the magnificence of Him who spoke and the world was made; you will tremble greatly before Him, you will be struck with awe, and a burning desire to cling to Him will be in you. You will stand closer to the Most High, and your prayer will be calmly heard, according to that verse: "I will exalt him because he has known my name." For the knowledge itself is the root of all things.

# PAULUS RICIUS’S PREFACE TO THE EPITOME OF THE GATES OF LIGHT.

The first part of this volume, which concerns the introduction to Kabbalah <term>Cabala: a tradition of Jewish mysticism that seeks to understand the relationship between the eternal, mysterious Infinite and the mortal, finite universe</term>, having now been completed, I proceed with the help of those on high to explain the second part, contained within this summary of the *Gates of Light*. In this compendium (just as in the preceding introduction), many things are handed down which might offend the ears and minds of the "sons of darkness" <note>A biblical metaphor for those who lack spiritual insight or reside in ignorance.</note> and those who devote less labor and study to investigating the secrets of sacred eloquence. Nevertheless, it seemed wicked and impious to deny these things to the pious, wise, and holy sons. <margin>1 Corinthians 1</margin> For even the far-seeing herald of truth, the Apostle Paul, did not shrink from preaching Christ the Savior crucified, even though it was a scandal to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles; for to those who were called, that preaching was the power and wisdom of God. I set this forth, however, not because I boast of being a master of the doctrines of the Kabbalists and those who speak in allegories—as if I had thoroughly unearthed its hidden and deep things. Indeed, I scarcely presume to have touched the thresholds of its vestibule or its very cradle. Rather, I place myself before the needy and the mockers; I do not promise to be a Master, and the things I have opened for the understanding of this doctrine I have handed down not so much with the intent of teaching, but of warning and awakening. My goal is that the more perceptive minds of students, supported by celestial light, may be able to climb higher through attentive meditation on these matters and penetrate the inner sanctuaries of secrets. For "to him who has" (as I have explained before), "it shall be given, and he shall abound; but from him who has not, even what he seems to have shall be taken away." <note>A reference to the Gospel of Matthew 13:12.</note> Finally, with these things having been tasted beforehand, listen now to Rabbi Joseph of Castile himself (as he is presumed to be), the author of this volume; pay attention as he speaks (having invoked the Father of Lights).

->**THE GATES OF LIGHT.**<-

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'E' depicting a scholar seated at a writing desk in a library. He is surrounded by shelves of books and stacks of volumes on the floor.</image-desc> You have long entreated me, my most beloved, to show you the path of light concerning the names of God, which one may also call "measures" and "sphiros"—that is, enumerations <term>Sephirot: the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</term>—by which you might be able to obtain your wish and reach the goal of your desire. Since I perceived this petition to be just and judged the intention itself to be honorable, I could not draw back from making you a sharer in the way of light. Now, therefore, be vigilant, so that you may know which path the Most High prefers or rejects; for when you have attained this, you shall be heard when you cry out, and you shall be written among the assembly of those who draw closer to the Most High. You shall worship Him with all the strength of your soul, you shall delight in God, and He will thoroughly fulfill the innermost desires of your heart. For you know (unless by chance you have not heard) the God of the world—the God in whose sight the heavens and the depths are struck with awe, at whose fear the whole circle of the earth is shaken, and at whose indignation who shall remain? Who can stand before the fury of His wrath? For He does not trust even His own holy ones, nor are the heavens clean in His sight <note>A reference to Job 15:15.</note>; how much less man, who is abominable and useless, drinking up iniquity like water? In what way then shall one born of woman abuse the holy names of God, or dare to lay hands upon the crown of the kingdom for his own profit? For our elders decreed that whoever utters the Name itself—namely the Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton: the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, considered too sacred to be spoken aloud</term>—by its own letters, shall have no part in the world to come.

->***RICIUS.***<-

The discussion here concerns the name Tetragrammaton, which is communicable only to the Creator and to none of His creatures. Therefore, just as it is attributed to irreverence and contempt when a son calls a parent by their personal name, so indeed it is ascribed to rash presumption to call the celestial Parent and incomprehensible King of Ages by His own principal name. Thus, it was not without justice that the authority of the ancients decreed that he who utters the great and terrible name of the Creator by its characters (with no urgent cause of piety) should have no part in the world to come, because such contempt and rash presumption toward God excludes one from the salvation of the future age. Added to this is the fact that, just as the Creator of all things, God Himself, is not grasped by any creature exactly as He is, so it was fitting that the name which designates that incomprehensible Being should not be uttered as the written letters sound. It was permitted only to the High Priest <note>original: "Pontifici"</note> in the sanctuary to express it by its characters once a year, on the great day of propitiation and repentance <note>Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement.</note>. Hence the Apostle established in the letter to Timothy: "Let everyone who invokes the name of the Lord depart from iniquity."

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV. 139

->THE AUTHOR.<-

Indeed, if the holy and excellent **Rabbi Hanina, son of Teradion** <note>original: "Rabi Henina Tradionis filius"; a 2nd-century Jewish scholar and martyr who, according to the Talmud, was executed by the Romans for teaching the Torah publicly and pronouncing the Divine Name.</note>, was unable to escape the punishment for his crime—even though he explained that very Name using its own characters not for common use or profane purposes, but for the sake of learning and so that he might know the mysteries of the Most High—who, then, can doubt that the same fate might befall us, who are but poor and weak? For you see what is forbidden in the Law of the Most High: *You shall not take the name of God* (namely the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, considered too holy to be spoken aloud</term>) *your God in vain*. Although the primary intent of this commandment is to warn against perjury, the Law uses the word "vain" <note>Latin: "vanum," translating the Hebrew "shav."</note> in such a way that (as the Aramaic translation <note>original: "Chaldaica... æditio," referring to the Targum.</note> testifies) the sentence implies that no one should utter the name of God with their lips for no reason. It would have been easier to write, or clearer to understand, as: *You shall not swear falsely by the name of God, your God*; yet it is written, *you shall not take it up*. <margin>Deut. 32.</margin> Therefore, **Moses**, the teacher of us all (while ascending on high), learned the mystery of commemorating the name of the Most High from the ministering angels and warned Israel, saying: *When I invoke the name of God, give greatness to our God*. If even the angels of heaven are warned regarding the mention of the name of the Most High, how much more does this concern a son of man, who is reduced to moths and worms? Let him not presume, being one who is easily swayed by fleeting thoughts, to adapt the crown of the Creator to his own use—especially in this age in which we live, where the true learning is hidden from us, which provides the proper method for commemorating the name of the Most High and His other names. I mean a "commemoration" that is suited to the actual spiritual work. Therefore, he who strives to mention it achieves nothing more than his own destruction and obtains only a fragment of a broken pottery shard. Concerning this and similar matters, our masters have said: *Whoever does not revere the glory of his Creator, it would be better for him if he had not entered the fabric of this world.*

Now therefore, my son, hear my voice, and attend with your ears to my counsel. If sinners should wish to entice you, do not listen. If they say, "Follow us, and we will impart to you the knowledge of the holy names (for you to use)," turn your ears away; do not adhere to their counsel, but rather flee from their wicked steps, and pull your feet back entirely from their path. For all such names and their usage are snares and the traps of hunters, which lead souls into eternal destruction. And even if the ancient sages knew the divine names handed down by the mouth of the Prophets—such as the **Name of Seventy-Two** and the **Twelve Letters**, and many others of this kind, by which they were able to renew signs, wonders, and portents in the world—they were by no means accustomed to misuse them for their own benefit. They used them only at such a time when the nations were striving to turn the Israelites away from the true worship of God, or when the sanctification or glory of the Most High God might emerge from some work. This was the case with **Rabbi Meir** <note>A famous 2nd-century sage.</note>, who rescued his wife’s sister from a brothel and commanded the guard or official, saying: "When you find yourself afflicted by troubles, say: *O God of Rabbi Meir, answer me!*" Yet this same **Rabbi Meir**, when he saw himself subjected to personal danger, chose flight rather than the use of the holy Name. A similar judgment should be made concerning the deeds of **Honi the Circle-Maker** <note>original: "Honi Maagalēfis"; a 1st-century BCE scholar famous for his ability to pray for rain.</note>, and **Rava** <note>original: "Roua"; a 4th-century Babylonian sage.</note> with **King Shapur** <note>original: "Sabor Rege"; Shapur II, the Sassanid King of Persia.</note>, and others like them.

Therefore, the "Hedge of Truth" and the "Tradition of the Covenant" is this: that he who desires to achieve his vows in the matter of the holy names should study the Law with all his strength. In the Law, he may discern the meaning of all the holy names, namely: **Eheieh** <term>Eheyeh: "I Will Be"</term>, **Yah** <note>original: "Ioh"</note>, **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note>, the **Tetragrammaton**, **El**, **Eloah**, **Elohim**, **Adonai Tzvaot** <note>original: "Edonai Zeuaos"; Lord of Hosts</note>, **Elohe Tzvaot** <note>original: "Elohe Zeuaos"; God of Hosts</note>, and **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai"; Almighty</note>. Let him know and understand that each of these aforementioned names serves as a key to something that the needs of the age require. When you have inspected these more attentively and understood each one clearly, you will determine that the Law and all its commandments hang from them. You will marvel at the magnificence of Him who spoke and the world was made; you will tremble greatly before Him, you will be struck with awe, and an arduous desire to cling to Him will dwell within you. You will stand closer to the Most High, and your prayer will be peacefully heard, according to that saying: <margin>Psalm 90.</margin> *I will exalt him because he has known my name.* For the root of all things is that very knowledge.

# PAULUS RICIUS

Once this is attained, he will cry out, and I will hear him; it is as if He said, whenever he has need of anything and directs his mind toward that Name upon which the desired thing depends, then I will hear. <margin>Genesis 43</margin> For Jacob, in a time of narrow straits, called upon *El Shaddai* <note>original: "El sadai"; interpreted as "God who is sufficient" or "The Almighty."</note>, saying: "May God Almighty grant you mercy." <margin>Daniel 9</margin> And Daniel, pouring out prayers over the sanctuary, said: "Cause your face to shine upon your desolate sanctuary, for the sake of the Lord <note>original: "Edonai," a Latinization of Adonai.</note>." Although our ancestors in the book of *Berakhot* <note>original: "Berachos," the Talmudic tractate on "Blessings."</note> explained that "for the sake of the Lord" sounds the same as "for the sake of Abraham," who was the first to call You "Lord," a deeper inward scrutiny is nonetheless required. And Hannah, imploring the Name of the Most High so that He might grant her a seed, spoke thus: "**Adonai** (namely the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: The sacred four-letter Name of God, YHWH, often substituted with "Adonai" or "Lord" in speech.</term>) **Tzevaot** <note>original: "Zeuoas"; "Lord of Hosts."</note>, if you will indeed look." And although the masters have written something else in the book of *Berakhot*, the aforementioned root and stem lies hidden there.

Given these circumstances, I consider it fitting to show you a certain core root, by which you may be fearlessly supported in this work we are undertaking. It must not escape you, therefore, that whatever names of the Most High are contained in the Law depend upon the Name of the **Tetragrammaton**. Although the Name *Ehyeh* <note>original: "Eheie," meaning "I am."</note> itself is usually called the root of the tree, the **Tetragrammaton** nonetheless holds the place of the trunk (just as *Ehyeh* holds that of the root); from this trunk a bounty of roots is sent forth, and branches are produced in every direction. The other holy names represent the branches and twigs emanating from the trunk, each of which produces fruit in many ways according to its own species. 

Beyond these (which it is a sacrilege to abolish), there are many other attributes attached to each of the aforementioned names. For example, the "surnames" <note>original: "cognomina," referring to descriptive titles or attributes of God.</note> of the **Tetragrammaton** are *Awesome*, *Bearing Iniquity*, and *Passing Over Transgressions*. Attached to **Adonai** (that is, the Lord) are *Great*, *Merciful*, and *Gracious*. To **Elohim** are also attached *Strong*, *Judge*, and *Arbiter*. Furthermore, other attributes are owed to each of these, which are indeed all the words into which the Law itself is resolved. The whole Law, therefore, is found to be woven upon these attributes; the attributes depend upon the holy names, and all the holy names depend upon the Name of the **Tetragrammaton** itself, and in it they are fused into one. Whence the Law itself is called the "Law of the God **Tetragrammaton**." 

Gather from this that if you understand the holy names according to each one's proper kinship, and know which attributes are adapted to each of them, you will then easily perceive all beings as being dependent upon the Name of the Most High. A desire will be planted in you, his heir, and you will be shaken with constant dread and awe in His sight. For you will weigh what the "fear of God" is, and you will attain the "knowledge of the God **Elohim**." <margin>Psalm 90</margin> You will be numbered among those of whom it is written: "I will exalt him, because he has known my Name." Nor will it escape you how much punishment he deserves who mentions the Name of God in vain—let alone he who pronounces the **Tetragrammaton** with its own letters—and far more so the one who uses it, and what great penalties the guilty party is bound to undergo.

But before I approach the purpose of this Volume, I have chosen to begin, not inappropriately, with a certain taste of the matter. Note, therefore, and consider it a certainty, that no one (except Himself) has ever been able to comprehend the true existence of the Most High with the mind; nor is anyone among the whole multitude of heavenly beings considered to know His place, much less the truth of His essence. For you hear what the celestial angels cry out: <margin>Ezekiel 3</margin> "Blessed be the glory of God from His place," that is, wherever His place may be. If this is so among the higher beings, we shall undoubtedly judge it to be even more so for the lower. 

Therefore, whatever is written in the Law—such as "mouth," "hand," "ear," "foot," "eye," and things of this kind—although it suggests the greatness and truth of the Most High, yet what that thing actually shows which is called "hand" or "foot," no created being can truly know or comprehend. Although we were made in His image and likeness, I would not want it to seem to you that His eye has the form of our eye, or His hand the form of our hands. Rather, they announce that within the Most High Himself there is something internal from which all things flow and gush forth; this essence is far removed from the quality and shape of a hand, according to that saying of the Prophet: "To whom have you likened me or made me equal?"

He concludes by asserting that while we use human terms like "hand" or "eye" to describe God, His true essence remains incomprehensible to all created beings.</summary>

### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV. 141

Therefore, no likeness of substance or form properly exists between Him and us. Rather, the description of limbs is intended to make our ears receptive; these "limbs," I say, signal the most high and hidden things that are incomprehensible to the human mind. It is like one who writes with a pen: *Reuben son of Jacob*. Neither these letters nor their shape offer a likeness to the actual substance of *Reuben son of Jacob* himself. Since the Most High wished to adapt us to purity, He constructed the hidden and manifold joints in the human body to mirror the same order as the work of the **Chariot** <term>Chariot: Referring to the "Merkabah" or the Divine Throne-Chariot in Jewish mysticism, symbolizing the structure of the divine realm.</term> in the heavens. Therefore, if anyone remains self-controlled and capable of keeping every limb of his body clean from defilement, that limb becomes the seat of the corresponding hidden heavenly limb which shares the same name—the eye for the eye, the right hand for the right hand.

->RICIUS.<-

<margin>1 Corinthians 6</margin>
The spiritual gifts of the Apostle reveal this secret when he says: *Do you not know that our members are a temple of the Holy Spirit?* But he who pollutes the members of his body with filth and the baseness of sensible things takes away the members of Christ and makes the temple of God into the members of a harlot.

<margin>Genesis 12</margin>
<margin>Genesis 31</margin>
