For instance, if the gaze of the eye is kept from vanity, looking upon nothing wicked, shameful, or base, but only upon those things which concern the glory and worship of the Most High, then that eye is restored to the seat of the hidden heavenly reality to which you adapt the name "eye." Judge the same for the hand, the foot, and every individual joint of the human body. Hence our ancestors, the fathers, say that they themselves are the **Chariot**; for they assert that not just any of the fathers, but the Patriarchs together, constitute the Chariot itself. For *Abraham* took for himself the name of the right; he was made the heir of the measure of the right in the heavens (namely, **Grace** <term>Grace: In this mystical context, the attribute of "Chesed" or loving-kindness.</term>), according to that text: *Abraham journeyed, going and proceeding toward the south.* *Isaac*, however, obtained the measure of the left, according to the text: *And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.* <note>original: "per timorem patris sui Ysaac." In Kabbalistic thought, Isaac represents "Gevurah" or "Fear/Severity."</note> But *Jacob* claimed the middle line for himself, according to the text: *And Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.* Thus, we admit these three fathers as the seats of that Chariot, and here the saying from the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "libri formationis," referring to the *Sefer Yetzirah*, an early and influential mystical text.</note> applies: *Place the thing upon its certainty and the Former upon His seat.* 

However, let it not escape you how any of the "measures" <term>Measures: Translated from the Latin "mensurae," referring to the "Sefirot" or divine attributes/emanations.</term> is accommodated to one of the limbs—as sight to the eye, hearing to the ear, touch to the hands, and movement to the feet. When our ancestors ascribe "measures" to the Most High, you should think the same of these measures as we taught regarding the foot, the hand, and other limbs. For no physical relationship exists between us and the Most High; just as there is no likeness of limbs, so there is no likeness of measures. Because we frequently mention "measures" in this book, take heed, having been forewarned, lest you fall into the error of thinking that God undergoes the limit or quantity of any measure (after our own fashion). But just as with the hand, foot, ear, and eye, the intention of the "measure" presents neither a boundary nor a physical mass, but a subtle example or likeness. 

Indeed, the ancient masters of the **Talmudists** in the tractate *Rosh Hashanah* <note>original: "Ros hasana," the tractate concerning the Jewish New Year.</note> call the Holy Names "measures." There, *Rabbi Yehuda* said: "A covenant was cut for the thirteen measures, so that they might never be prayed in vain," according to the text: *Behold, I shall cut a covenant, etc.* The thirteen measures are: **God** (the **Tetragrammaton**), **God** (the **Tetragrammaton**), **God** (*El*), merciful, and gracious, long-suffering, and of much mercy, and true, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity, passing over transgressions and sins, and blameless. <note>original: "tredecim uerò mensuræ sunt Deus Tetragrammaton..." These are the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy from Exodus 34:6-7.</note> Finally, the highest intention is to understand that none of the humanized measures have any relationship to those that belong to the Most High (except in name only), just as we explained regarding the written name *Reuben son of Jacob*. Hence the masters are accustomed to say: "The measure of flesh and blood is not like that of God the Most High." Having completed this prelude (as a key to what must be said), we shall soon proceed to the treatise on each of the Holy Names written in the Law. Wherever you encounter one of these, I desire to make you learned and erudite, so that you may discern how to draw from the fountain of living waters that gushes forth from every name of the Most High, so that you may...

# PAUL RICIUS,

...which, when you have drunk it and known it, you will achieve a successful outcome of happiness in every endeavor. The foundation and root of the Law is to believe in the name of the Most High; if you walk in a straight path in your thoughts, your ways will be safe, and 

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 4</margin>
your feet will not stumble forever. For King Solomon said: *Guard your foot when you enter the house of God* <note>original: "Custodi pedem tuum ingrediens domum Dei"</note>; by which he surely taught that whoever approaches to implore divine help should first examine himself, observe, and know whether tempters and obstacles are present that might blacken his prayers (so that they are not accepted). If they are present, he should remove them and clear the path of stumbling blocks, following the example of one who seeks the King's court for the sake of obtaining something. For such a person must foresee and know whether the danger of some precipice stands in the way; he should further consider how many doors of the vestibules there are in the royal palace, and judge their guards and doorkeepers, so that if he has an enemy among them, he may reconcile with him. Furthermore, he should scrutinize his garments to see if they suit the King's dignity, so that, being decently adorned, he may be permitted to enter the royal hall. For it is written:

<margin>Esther 4</margin>
*It is not permitted to enter the King’s hall clothed in sackcloth.* Finally, he should examine himself to see whether, in the sight of the King and the standing princes and prelates, he dares to set forth his matter with eloquent speech, and whether his strength is sufficient against contradictors, and if he can resist those who oppose him. To all these things, the harmonious discourse of our ancestors rouses us, by which they assert the great and supreme maxim that the earthly kingdom serves as an example <note>or "indicator"</note> of the heavenly kingdom. Therefore, if the anxiety of flesh and blood employs study and caution in all the aforementioned matters as necessary, it is not to be doubted that these same things must be attended to with all care while one endeavors to approach the majesty and sight of the King of kings. For from the terrestrial element all the way to the celestial bodies, no place is empty, but is filled with a multiform tumult. Some of these spirits are pure and participants in mercy; others, however, are inferior to these, being tempters and harmful, all flying through the darkness. Some minister peace, others the sword; some good, others evil; some life, others death. All of these are encompassed by this lowest "machine" <note>The physical world or the structure of the universe</note> in which we live. On their account, a song has been handed down to us regarding evil occurrences:

<margin>Psalm 90</margin>
*He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High.* <note>Known as the "Song of Evil Encounters" in Jewish tradition, used for protection against demons.</note> Whence a man’s prayer, while seeking the heights (by passing through these throngs), is likened to one traversing suspicious and out-of-the-way places. If he remains capable of the grace of purity, his prayer will not fall into the harm of the accusers; but if he is devoid and empty of this grace, the multiple clouds of fortune’s turns and the ranks of slayers will present themselves to him. Therefore, King David established the Psalms so that the path might be cleared, through which prayer might easily pass. For all the aforesaid throngs are like clouds that twist the ascent of supplications, according to that saying:

<margin>Lamentations 3</margin>
*You have set a cloud against yourself, lest prayer should pass through.* David therefore produced the Psalms, which, when brought forth in order, remove and compel all those who bring obstacles and harm to depart. They are called in the Hebrew language **zemirot** <term>zemirot: Derived from a root meaning both "songs" and "pruning." # ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK 4.

...the tree is now called the trunk. Of the remaining names, some act as the root, some as the branches, and others as the storehouses and treasuries. Each of these is assigned a specific task of operation, much like a treasury that fills and bestows various and diverse inner rooms, each dedicated to a certain thing. In this room, pearls and every kind of gem are stored; in that one, silver; in another, gold; in one, feasts; in another, drink; and in yet another, precious ornaments and garments. If someone were in need of nourishment but did not know the location of the pantry (even if they worked very hard at searching), it would happen that they would wither and perish from hunger and wasting. Even though the cellar abounds with delicacies, sumptuously prepared and with fine dishes, that person perishes—not because their request is refused, but because they are ignorant of the repository of the foods they require. 

We must judge the instruction and knowledge of the holy names in the same way. For some names preside over mercy, prayer, and atonement; some over tears and sobbing; some over accidents, misfortunes, and distress; some over food and sustenance; and some over strength, fortitude, and grace. For this reason, if a person praying in a name that is suited to the desired gift does not know how to direct their mind as is fitting, their vow is denied not by any refusal, but by the dullness and folly of their own understanding. As it is written: 

<margin>Proverbs 19</margin>
*The folly of a man trips up his steps, and his heart frets against God.* <note>original: "Stultitia hominis supplantat gressus eius, & contra Deum feruet cor suum"</note> For the hands of the Most High are open to all, but the ignorance of the petitioner—who does not know how to distinguish the entrances and innermost paths of their desires—renders the prayer empty. Yet the fool thinks the Most High turns His ears away from the prayers of the one crying out, 

<margin>Jeremiah 5</margin> 
to which it is said: *Our sins have withheld good from us.* <note>original: "peccata nostra prohibuerunt bonū à nobis"</note> Therefore, it is necessary to revolve the paths of the Law in the mind and to know the mysteries of the holy names so thoroughly that one possesses an established habit in these specific titles. When one desires to become capable of supplication in the sight of the Most High, they should turn their mind to the name suited to the petition. Then, not only will they attain their vow, but they will also become beloved to those above and pleasing to those below, becoming an eternal heir of both the present and the future world. With this foundation for what is to be said having been laid, we now prepare ourselves, by the nodding spirit of the Most High, to explain each of the holy names recorded in the Law.

->ADONAI<-

For your understanding, note that this is a specific name of the Most High which implies the existence of the Supreme Architect, upon whom everything contained in the universe depends. But the first of the gates and keys by which we approach the spoken (though not written) Tetragrammaton is the name sounding in character and voice as *Edonai*. Since we begin from above and incline downward, in the whole circuit of God's names, it is assigned the rank at the very end and is believed to be the true and consummate mystery of union leading up to *Edonai* itself.

This *Edonai* exists as a treasury and a house of riches for every manner of flooding and the dependency of things emanating through channels and pipes from the spoken Tetragrammaton to *Edonai*.

*Edonai* at the bottom, 

<margin>YHWH (יהוה)</margin>

From there, channels and pipes burst forth, and all flows down to the name *Edonai*, which is the cellar where all the ornaments of the King Tetragrammaton are stored. Furthermore, this name is the great President of created things, who nourishes all by the power of the Tetragrammaton and provides the necessities of life. By its nod they come, and at its command they depart—all those who seek to adhere to the Tetragrammaton with desire.

# OF PAULUS RICIUS,

...they seek, nor is there a path, nor any part—because no one stands before the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, considered too sacred to pronounce</note> itself unless admitted by the guidance of **Edonai** <note>Adonai, meaning "Lord"</note>. And because the King, the Tetragrammaton, claims this very name for Himself in the houses of riches, or in the temple of which He is the host, the Tetragrammaton is usually pronounced in the Law with the same vocal sound as the name Edonai. This is so that it may be known to us that whoever seeks the Tetragrammaton will find Him in the name Edonai.

It should not escape you, however, that fifty-four "squared" names are ascribed to the name Tetragrammaton. These emerge from combinations of the Tetragrammaton itself, and their letters constitute the number 216. These 54 names are the mystery of the outflow of power into all things encompassed by the machine of the world. These (like spirits) regard the letters by which the name is formed that is excerpted from the Law, 
<margin>Exodus 14</margin> 
where it says *the angel went forward*, etc. <note>original: "ubi perrexit angelus". This refers to Exodus 14:19-21. Edonai, therefore, shows its own disposition and the faculty of reigning from the very letters of which it is composed. For *Aleph* <note>The first letter of Adonai (א)</note> signifies the mystery of **Eheie** <note>meaning "I Am," the name revealed to Moses at the bush</note>, which holds the place of the "head" among the other names. *Iod* <note>The final letter of Adonai (י)</note> truly represents the Tetragrammaton, whose seat is Edonai. The *Daleth* and *Nun* <note>The middle letters of Adonai (ד , נ)</note> announce the existence of the 54 names, through which the secret of every kind of inundation, dependence, and the permanence of all things shines forth. 

Therefore, the entire power of reigning and perfecting is committed to Edonai itself, as the word *Edonai* suggests: for in the Hebrew language this sounds like "Lord," because (under the leadership of the Tetragrammaton) it stands as the presiding officer and ruler of the whole world. And since no created thing is permitted to approach the name Tetragrammaton itself except through the intercession of Edonai, the ancients decreed that it should be commemorated at the head of every prayer in such a sequence: *Edonai*—that is, 
<margin>Psalm 50</margin>

It is like a **pool** <note>original: "piscina"</note> into which a river is drawn, by which gardens, fields, and other greenery are irrigated. <margin>Genesis 15</margin>

### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK 4. 147

...for I possess all the keys of the heavenly pools which are included within the domain of the Name <note>original: "Cöl. r." likely referring to the Name Adonai/Malkhut</note>; therefore, if I bestow more upon you, I do not hold any less for myself.

Often also *Edonai* <note>Adonai</note> is called the <gloss>SAPPHIRE STONE</gloss> <note>original: אבן ספיר (Even Sapir)</note>, because it stands as the very foundation of the entire cosmic structure, from which all things seek their benefits. It is likewise called the <gloss>capstone</gloss> <note>original: אבן הראשה (Even Ha-Roshah)</note>, from which beings—whether uncreated or perishable—are brought forth in the work of the beginning. It is called *Sapphire* for this reason: because (like a sapphire) it draws color in every way from the supernal heights and diffuses contrary qualities into created things. For it ministers sometimes good, sometimes evil; now destruction, now life; now sickness, now healing; now poverty, now riches. As it is written: <margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin> *See now that I am He, and there is no God with me: I will kill, and I will make to live; I will strike, and I will heal.* This dimension <note>The Sephirah of Malkhut</note> therefore draws its power from the source of all the Sephirot <note>The ten divine emanations in Kabbalistic thought</note>, pulling toward itself the pools and dependencies of all modes. When all things are brought under its dominion, it provides nourishment and sustenance according to the limit of each, as it is written:
<margin>Psalm 117</margin>
*The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.*
For Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob each took his portion from the higher Sephirot; but David claimed for himself this dimension, which is the lower one. Yet it is the "head of the corner" because the things above lean upon it no less than the things below: the supernal powers lean upon it to distribute force, inundation, and blessing; while the lower things aspire to it insofar as they obtain from it their nourishment, permanence, and the benefits of life. As it is written: <margin>Job 38</margin> *Or who cast its cornerstone?* This is also the stone which is established as the nursling of Israel, as it is written: <margin>Genesis 49</margin> *From there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel.* This very stone is carried by its own desire toward a higher stone, from which it draws an outflow of every kind, as it is written: <margin>Exodus 28</margin> <margin>Genesis 15</margin> *And you shall take two onyx stones, and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel.* And also: *Lord Edonai God, Tetragrammaton Elohim, what will you give me?* <note>original: "Tetragramaton Elohim"; Ricii interprets the combined names as reflecting the flow of divine glory</note> For the dwelling glory <note>Shekhinah</note> draws from above and is itself drawn downward.
Opposed to this stone is another stone, called the *Great Stone*. When it blocks the mouth of the well, it brings dire hardship to Israel until he to whom the right of judging belongs approaches. As it is written: <margin>Genesis 29</margin> *Jacob drew near and moved the stone from the mouth of the well.* And: *And Jacob proceeded to Succoth.* Again: <margin>Malachi 3</margin> *Behold, the day of the Lord shall come.*
Many times this same dimension of *Edonai* is known by the name <gloss>HOUSE OF THE SANCTUARY</gloss> <note>original: בית המקדש (Beit Ha-Mikdash)</note>, because this is the domicile in which the peculiar name of the Most High dwells. For when the Most High chose and sanctified Mount Moriah for Himself, He willed the house of the sanctuary to be built upon it, as it is written: <margin>Isaiah 13</margin> <margin>Exodus 15</margin> *The sanctuary, O Lord Edonai, which your hands have established.* He established that singular lodging for Himself, whence the form of the upper chambers, porches, cellars, and the entire house was constructed according to the likeness of the form of *Edonai*. This was done with the same understanding by which we taught concerning the mystery of the form of the human limbs. But when Israel kicked <note>rebelled</note> or transgressed, the dwelling glory withdrew itself, and the house was made utterly waste and desolate. And when Daniel implored God in prayer that the buildings of the sanctuary might be restored, he turned his mind toward this dimension, saying: <margin>Daniel 9</margin> *Show your face (he said) to your sanctuary, which is deserted for the sake of Edonai*—that is, rebuild the house of the sanctuary, because it is the seat of Adonai.
That which our ancestors declare in the book *Berachos* <note>The Talmudic tractate Berakhot</note> regarding the explanation of this—namely, that it is "for the sake of Abraham," who was the first to call You by the name *Edonai*—is not at all discordant with the truth. For this dimension was the guardian of Abraham, through which he waged multiple and varied wars on his behalf, as it is written: <margin>Genesis 14</margin> *He rushed upon them by night.* And: <margin>Isaiah 46</margin> *Who raised up justice from the east and called it to his feet?* <note>original: "propter ipsum uocauit"</note>—just as it will become clear in the chapter on the dimension of justice (the Spirit permitting).
This same dimension is also commonly called the <gloss>SHEKHINAH</gloss> <note>original: שכינה</note>, which means the "dwelling glory." This glory lived constantly with Israel once the Tabernacle was completed, as it is written: <margin>Exodus 25</margin> *And they shall make for me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst.* A great root <note>fundamental principle</note> must be held here: for from the moment the machinery of the world began to be fabricated, the glory...

...they abound in every kind of wealth and goods. Sometimes *Edonai* <note>The Hebrew name Adonai, often used by Ricius to denote the presence of God in the world</note> is also called <term>באר שבע</term> **Beersheva**: that is, the "Well of the Seven." This is because seven streams are led into it from the seven supernal heights, which are the foundations of the world. However, at the meeting point of this well, there is another well of filthy and shameful waters (outside the wall of the <term>Sephirot</term> <note>The ten creative powers or "spheres" in Kabbalistic thought; the text uses "sphiros"</note>), along with many other types of pits in which a multitude of serpents and scorpions crawl. This is often called the "strange cistern," <margin>Proverbs 23</margin> according to the verse: *A harlot is a deep pit, and a strange woman is a narrow cistern.* Therefore, whoever embraces every kind of wicked depravity shall never be offered a draught of living water from **Beersheva**. Instead, such a person shall fall perpetually into the dire cisterns of perdition, just as they themselves have dug, according to the Prophet: <margin>Jeremiah 4</margin> <note>The text cites Jeremiah 4, but the quote is from Jeremiah 2:13</note> *My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water.* This is the cistern of perdition, whose bottom is full of cracks throughout its base and cannot keep water within itself, but is filled all around by a gathering of vipers and scorpions. Fearing this, David cried out: <margin>Psalm 69:15</margin> <note>The margin says Psalm 6, 8, but the verse is from Psalm 69</note> *Let not the pit shut its mouth upon me.*

Furthermore, the surname <term>ים</term> **Yam**: that is, the "Sea," is often adapted to the same *Edonai*. <margin>Ecclesiastes 1</margin> This is because all the overflow and dependencies of every pool fall into it (just as rivers flow into the sea), according to the verse: <margin>Isaiah 11</margin> *All rivers enter the sea.* For "the Sea" does not imply the water contained within, but rather the vessel that contains it, according to the verse: <margin>Genesis 1</margin> *As the waters covering the sea*, and also: *The gathering of the waters He called Seas.* Therefore, the sea is called a "receptacle of waters." From this sea, various troops of angels are brought forth, and various kinds of celestial creeping things which crawl in the waves that the sea embraces, according to what David declares: <margin>Psalm 104:25</margin> <note>Margin says Psalm 103</note> *This is the great and wide sea, in which are creeping things without number, small animals with the great.* In it, moreover, is a vast multitude of ships and sailors, and many banners extended at the head of the mast, manifold whirlpools, and things of this kind, with which the sea itself fluctuates without ceasing, according to the verse: <margin>Psalm 104:26</margin> *There the ships pass through.* 

On the side of this sea is situated another place, which used to be called the "reedy and Red Sea" <note>Latin: *mare rubrum*, the Red Sea, also interpreted as the Sea of Reeds</note>. It exists near the limits of the earth, which the measure of *Edonai* indicates. From there, judgment rushed upon the Egyptians, whereby that which is the lower Red Sea covered them with its force, as it is written: <margin>Exodus 14</margin> *For God fights for them against Egypt.* Likewise, in hidden matters, the wise call this same measure of *Edonai* the "Sea of Wisdom," since this stands as the receptacle of any wisdom or dependency, and of those things which flow from the supernal wisdom. From its fountain, all who share in wisdom draw and drink. The Most High handed this to King Solomon, as it is written: <margin>1 Kings 4</margin> *And God gave wisdom to Solomon.* For when he had entered this Sea of Wisdom, there shone forth in him a power by which he understood every order of the hierarchies, both in the heavens and the earth, and there was absolutely nothing that remained hidden from him. By the strength of the name *Edonai*, he sat upon the throne of the Most High, by which he subdued the things above and the things below by the power of his kingdom. For the wisdom of God inspired him to act with justice.

Sometimes, the surname <term>כל</term> **Col** [Kol], i.e., "All," is ascribed to the name *Edonai*, since it possesses the universe and lacks nothing. He who strives to obtain anything according to his wish should not pray to any other power or place; for this Name encircles and encompasses all things, and therefore whoever implores it becomes the master of his desire. And if that measure, which is considered more eminent and prior to the dimension of *Edonai* itself, is likewise accustomed to be called "All," <margin>Genesis 24:1</margin> this nevertheless takes its root from elsewhere (as will be explained below). Therefore, because this dimension announces a mystery of blessing, it is written in the Law: *And God blessed Abraham in all* <note>Hebrew: *Bakol*</note>. <margin>Genesis 27:33</margin> This passed from Abraham into Isaac, according to the verse: *And I have eaten of all* <note>Hebrew: *Mikol*</note>. <margin>Genesis 33:11</margin> From Isaac it passed to Jacob, as it is written: *Because God has dealt graciously with me, and I have everything* <note>Hebrew: *Kol*</note>. It is as if Jacob said to Esau: "Do you think that, having taken away the gift I bestow on you, I am left with fewer goods? By no means. I possess all things."

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

...for I possess the keys to all the supernal pools which are enclosed within my domain: therefore, even if I bestow more upon you, I hold no less of anything myself.

Frequently, *Edonai* <note>The divine name Adonai</note> is also called <note>original: "אבן ספיר"</note> **The Sapphire Stone**, because it stands as the very foundation of the entire world’s fabric; from it, all things seek their benefit. It is likewise called <note>original: "אבן הראשה"</note> **the Capstone**, from which the innate or fleeting beings in the "work of the beginning" <note>The creation of the world</note> are brought forth into existence. It is called "Sapphire-like" because (like a sapphire) it draws color from the supernal heights in every possible way, and diffuses contrary effects into created things. For it sometimes administers good, and at other times evil; now death, now life; now sickness, now healing; now poverty, now riches: <margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin> according to the verse: *See now that I, even I, am He, and there is no God with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal.* This dimension <note>The Sephirah of Malkhut</note> therefore draws power from the fountain of all <term>Sephirot</term> <note>The ten divine emanations; the text uses "sphiros"</note>, drawing to itself the pools and dependencies of all modes. With all things brought under its rule, it provides nourishment and livelihood according to the limit of each: <margin>Psalm 117</margin> according to the verse: *The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.* For Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob each took their portion from the higher <term>Sephirot</term>. But David claimed this one, which is lower, as his own measure; it is, however, the head of the corner: for the things above lean toward it no less than the things below. The higher things lean toward it so that they may distribute power, overflow, and blessing into it; while the lower things aspire toward it insofar as they obtain from it the benefits of nourishment, permanence, and livelihood: <margin>Job 38</margin> according to the verse: *Who laid its cornerstone?* This is also the stone which is established as the nursling of Israel: <margin>Genesis 49</margin> according to the verse: *From there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel.* This very stone is carried by its own desire toward the higher stone, from which it draws the flow of every kind: <margin>Exodus 28</margin> according to the verse: *And you shall take two onyx stones, and engrave on them the names of the children of Israel.* <margin>Genesis 15</margin> And that verse: *Lord Edonai God, Tetragrammaton Elohim, what will you give me?* For the indwelling glory draws from above, and is itself drawn below. Opposite this stone is another stone: called the "Great Stone," which, when it blocks the mouth of the well, then brings dire things upon Israel, until he to whom the right of judging belongs approaches: <margin>Genesis 29</margin> according to the verse: *Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth.* And that: <margin>Malachi 3</margin> *And Jacob proceeded to the hearths.* Again, the day of the Lord shall come for them. Many times, this same dimension of *Edonai* holds the title <note>original: "בית המקדש"</note> **House of the Sanctuary**, because this is the domicile in which the unique Name of the Most High dwells: <margin>Isaiah 13</margin> for since the Most High chose and sanctified Mount Moriah for Himself, <margin>Exodus 15</margin> He willed the house of the sanctuary to be built upon it: according to the verse: *The sanctuary, O Lord Edonai, which your hands have established.* He established this singular lodging for Himself; hence the form of the upper chambers, porches, storerooms, and the entire house was constructed in the likeness of the form of *Edonai*—certainly with that understanding by which we taught concerning the mystery of the form of human limbs. But when Israel kicked <note>i.e., rebelled</note> and became transgressors, the indwelling glory withdrew itself, and the house became utterly waste and desolate. And when Daniel implored God in prayer (that the buildings of the sanctuary might be restored), <margin>Daniel 9</margin> turning his mind toward this measure, he said: *Cause your face to shine upon your sanctuary, which is desolate, for the sake of Edonai.* That is, "rebuild the house of the sanctuary again, because it is the seat of *Edonai*." ### PAULUS RICIUS,

<note>original: "...ria ipsa"</note> ...the Glory itself established its seat fundamentally with the lowest things: for the hierarchies of all creatures, according to the order of their ranks, looked toward the supernal beings—the higher toward the higher, and the lower toward the lower. Thus, the **Indwelling Glory** <note>original: "gloria cohabitans"; a Latin rendering of the Hebrew *Shekhinah*, the divine presence dwelling in the world</note> (having established its home here) lingered within. Heaven and earth shared a mutual embrace through a certain bond, according to that passage in <margin>Genesis 2.</margin> *vachulu* <note>original: "uaychulu" (ויכלו); "And they were finished"</note>, that is, "they were perfected"; or (as the word sounds through its letters) "they were contained": heaven, earth, and all their host. For one contained the other, and each was promiscuously filled by the other. The channels, pipes, and spheres executed their work with exact precision; flows of influence migrated so abundantly from the higher beings downward that the name of the Most High filled the lower realms as much as the sublime, according to that verse: <margin>Isaiah 66.</margin> *The heavens are my throne, and the earth is my footstool.*

While this Indwelling Glory served the terrestrial no less than the celestial, Adam became a transgressor, and immediately the orders were thrown into confusion. The pipes and channels underwent a twisting; the flows of the pools were withdrawn. Finally, the Glory took itself away, and a total dissolution of the bonds emerged. Soon after, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob began to bind them back together. Although they attracted that Glory in some manner, they reduced their own bodies into "three seats of glory." However, the Glory did not establish its immobile throne within these fleeting things, but positioned itself above them by "hovering over," according to the verse: <margin>Genesis 17.</margin> <margin>Genesis 8.</margin> *God ascended from above Abraham,* etc. Here also fits the saying of the elders: *the fathers—that is, the patriarchs—are the chariot itself.* <note>A common Kabbalistic and Midrashic concept that the Patriarchs constitute the *Merkabah* or Divine Chariot.</note> 

Therefore, the Indwelling Glory in those times was carried through the air; nor could the "dove" <note>The Holy Spirit or Shekhinah</note> find rest for its feet (just as in the beginning of creation) until Moses, together with Israel, fabricated the sanctuary and its ornaments. They corrected the entanglement of the channels and pipes, arranged the garden beds, and drew the living water back through the arranged pools into the water jar. Then, finally, the Glory <margin>Exodus 25.</margin> returned to the lower regions—not upon the pavement (as in the dawn of creation), but it placed its lodging for itself in the Tabernacle, according to the verse: *And they shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.* It was like a guest who usually travels through wandering provinces; for He said, "I will dwell" (not "below") but "*among them*." That is to say, wherever they might carry their steps, I will go with them, and I will by no means stay in one place, according to the verse: <margin>Numbers 10.</margin> *And when the ark set out...*

Indeed, David grieved over this, desiring to build a stable domicile for the Glory, <margin>Psalm 131.</margin> according to the verse: *As he swore to the Lord... If I enter the tabernacle of my house... Until I find a place for God... because God has chosen Zion... this is my rest forever.* <margin>2 Samuel 7.</margin> Since David sought out a place for the rest of the Glory, saying, "Arise, O God, into your rest," the Glory itself received his firm thoughts. Whence the Prophet Nathan, announcing to him by word: *Go,* he said, *and speak to my servant David: Thus says God, Will you build me a house to dwell in? For I have not dwelt in a house from that day I led Israel out of the land of Egypt, but in a tabernacle and a tent through all the places I traveled with all the children of Israel. Speaking, did I ever speak to one of the tribes of Israel, saying: Why have you not built me a house of cedar?* etc. *You, however, shall not build a house to my name, but the son who shall come forth from your loins, he himself shall build the house for my name.*

Therefore, David prepared gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, onyx stones, gems, crystal stones, and multicolored stones, and every abundance of precious and marble stones. He arranged each ornament of the sanctuary, and established the upper chambers, cellars, bedrooms, courts, porches, and the temple of that same house. He fashioned the form of all these things (with the Holy Spirit as his consultant); which Spirit (I say) provided the image of each place, and the exact measure and weight of the silver, gold, gems, and all other requirements according to the order of the Glory itself, <margin>1 Chronicles 28.</margin> just as it is written: *David gave the description of the porch and of the temple, of the cellars, of the rooms,* etc. *And of all the courts and side chambers he had thought of round about for the treasures of the house of God, and for the works of the house of God, and for all the vessels of the mystery of the temple of God: gold by weight for each vessel of the mystery, and the weight of silver according to the diversity of the vessels and works,* etc. *Even unto the likeness of the chariot made of the gold of the Che-*

...of the Cherubim extending their wings and veiling the ark of the covenant of God, all things came forth, <margin>1</margin> ¶ written by the hand of God to me, so that I might understand the whole work of the pattern, etc. <note>original: "scripta manu Dei ad me..." citing 1 Chronicles 28:19</note> From this it may be seen that in the same order, weight, and form by which the archetype of the chariot <note>original: "quadrigæ archetypum"; a reference to the Merkavah or Divine Chariot from Ezekiel’s vision</note> itself is arranged, David also arranged the entire work of the sanctuary from the mouth of the Most High, so that a seat and a lodging for the Glory might remain there. Solomon succeeded him in this, performing all things according to his father's instructions; then, presently, that very Glory, seeking again this lowest house of the ages, established a throne for itself, according to that saying: *Then Solomon said, etc.* <margin>1 Kings 8</margin> *Building, I have built a house and a most firm habitation for you, a perpetual throne.* And it is written: *Now therefore, O Lord God* <note>original: "Deus Tetragrammaton"; referring to the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, *God of Israel* <note>original: "Deus elohe Israel"</note>, *let your word be established, which you spoke to your servant David. And when Solomon had finished pouring out his prayers, fire descended from heaven and devoured the burnt offerings and the victims, and the majesty of God filled the house. Therefore, the Glory again took up its rest on earth and in the house of the ages; and into the house of the sanctuary, all the tracts, channels, and pipes poured out a blessing, according to that verse: <margin>Psalm 133</margin> *As the dew of Hermon, which descends upon Mount Zion, for there the Lord* <note>original: "Deus Tetragrammaton"</note> *commanded a blessing and life forevermore.* <margin>Psalm 50</margin> And it is written of Zion, the summit of beauty: *God* <note>original: "Elohim"</note> *has appeared.* From the house of the sanctuary, moreover, channels and pipes gushed forth into the seventy nations of the earth, over whom princes preside. Through these channels, all the nations indeed received good things from Jerusalem, according to that verse: <margin>Genesis 12</margin> *And in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed.* 

And because Solomon knew the way of leading forth these springs into any place from Jerusalem, he wished to boast, saying: <margin>Ecclesiastes 2</margin> *I made gardens and orchards, and I planted them with trees of every kind.* Is it not the case that every kind of tree happens to be produced in the same part of the earth? But Solomon knew that from the passages of the region of the Indians is drawn that which he established as pepper; from Arabia, he planted the tree with myrrh; and so it is to be judged equally for the remaining kinds. To this is applied that verse: *Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty.* For from Zion (as if from an irrigating fountain), the Indwelling Glory itself, through the mediation of the sanctuary, pours out an abundance of blessings to all regions of the earth. 

However, you are not ignorant that the Indwelling Glory exhibited itself to Israel alone, according to that verse: <margin>Exodus 25</margin> *They shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them, and I will set my tabernacle among you.* <margin>Leviticus 26</margin> For the Glory itself (as we have written before) is the temple in which the name Tetragrammaton dwells. For the Most High promised himself to Israel, saying: *When you have received my tabernacle, I will not depart from you forever; and even if impurity touches you, my Glory shall never desert you.* To which that verse alludes: <margin>Leviticus 16</margin> *Who dwells with them in the midst of their uncleanness.* Therefore, since the Name of the Most High bestowed such a great gift upon Israel, and the Indwelling Glory lived among them, the Israelites enjoyed all the cellars and treasures of the Name Tetragrammaton, and every kind of inundation, dependence, and blessing. For they held the keys to every hidden storehouse, by which they were able to receive every sort of flow and blessing from the Indwelling Glory, according to that verse: <margin>Leviticus 26</margin> *And I will set my tabernacle among them, and I will walk in the midst of you, and I will be your God* <note>original: "Deum Elohim"</note>. 

The Indwelling Glory is, therefore, like a pledge of the Name of the Most High in the hands of Israel; and while the house of the sanctuary lies waste (on account of their transgression), Israel leads the Glory with them through captivity. For when the name <term>ZEDECH</term> <note>Justice/Righteousness</note> is applied to this measure, then a huge number of legions and battle lines are subjected to its command, whom they call the **Champions**, who carry swords, daggers, spears, bows, arrows, and javelins for battling and brandishing. For this reason, the masters established that it is called "Justice": because by taking away their crimes, it restores them as just men, according to that: *And the neighbor shall not say "I am weak," for the people who dwell therein shall have their iniquity taken away from them,* <margin>Isaiah 33</margin> which seems to echo this sentiment, namely: those who inhabit Jerusalem will not say, "Why do we languish in constant distress?" because this dimension, which is called the House of Mild Judgment, stays there continually, so that (by exacting whatever is owed) they may stand purified from iniquities and sins, just, and ready for the life of the world to come. To this end also belongs that saying: *You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities.* However, because this same measure of justice in Jerusalem at no time...

<margin>Deuteronomy 16</margin>

Moses sought most earnestly for this to be dedicated in the house of judgment of Israel: *If I have found grace (he said) I beseech you, in your eyes, Lord Edonai, let Edonai, I pray, walk in our midst,* etc. <margin>Exodus 34</margin> <margin>Exodus 23</margin> But He judges the nations through the superior judicial house (with an angel and prince as Mediator); no one of those angels or princes is allowed to depart from what is decreed, according to that: *Behold, I will send an angel before you, to guard you on the way,* etc., *be warned by his presence,* etc., *because he will not endure your sins.* But concerning the dimension of justice, which is the courtroom of Israel, it is written: *To the Lord Tetragrammaton, our God Elohim, belong mercies and forgiveness, when we have rebelled against Him.* And it is written: *Edonai hear, Edonai be propitious, Edonai listen,* etc. <margin>Daniel 9</margin> Where it should be noted, that the prohibitive commandments of the Law <note>The "negative" commandments: "Thou shalt not..."</note>, through the excess of which a judgment of retribution and vengeance is to be expected, are three hundred and sixty-five in number, just as the number of days in which the period of the solar year is completed, in which a person can transgress. But because **Edonai** is that very merciful measure that absolves all iniquity and all our crimes, therefore **Edonai** is expressed in a threefold utterance, joined to letters which, according to the number of prohibitive mandates, composes 365. <note>This likely refers to the "gematria" or numerical value of the letters in a specific prayer or divine name configuration equaling the 365 days/commandments.</note> This same measure, when it proposes to execute judgment upon Israel, then covers itself with the garments of grace and mercy,
<margin>Hosea 11</margin>
according to that: *How shall I give you up, Ephraim? How shall I hand you over, Israel?* etc. *My heart is turned within me, my compassions are kindled together.* For when Israel breaks out into repentance, the very dimension of justice is tormented by pain on account of the judgment to be carried out in Israel; therefore when it judges, it reproves them not harshly, but piously (just as a father does his son), <margin>Proverbs 4</margin> <margin>Job 5</margin> according to that: *Whom God loves, He corrects, and just as a father's will breathes upon his son.* And it is written: *Blessed is the man whom God corrects,* etc. <margin>Deuteronomy 8</margin> Let your heart not be ignorant that not otherwise than a man corrects his son, does God **Tetragrammaton**, your God **Elohim**, correct and rebuke you. There is also placed in this dimension everything in the Law for the name **ANI** <note>Hebrew: *Ani*, meaning "I"</note>: that is, **I**: because this measure exists as the courtroom of Israel, which brings the punishment of vengeance for them, and quite often warns Israel of the crime and the fear of its judge, since it cannot happen that the work of judging itself should not be carried out, according to what is written everywhere: *And you shall fear your God.*

<meta>This page continues the discussion of divine "measures" or Sephirot, specifically focusing on how the state of Israel's righteousness affects the flow of divine grace from the higher realms down to the lower "sphere" (likely Malchut, the Indwelling Glory). ### ON HEAVENLY AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV. 153

[...fallen from the] heavens: for while Israel practices justice, it draws from all the heights above toward this all-encompassing flood, dependence, mercy, and grace—from all things (I say) that exist above this sphere. But when Israel turns away from the ways of the Most High, then this measure—whose leaves fall away like an orchard suffering from a lack of water—lies needy, parched, and prostrate. 

Just as the fruits fall from a tree, so the wretched Israelites fall everywhere into reproach and mockery. For when this heavenly proportion is unable to "consume" or receive anything from the powers above, it cannot produce or pour anything into Israel itself. In such a state, it is called **Neser**: a word that sounds like the term for a tree whose fruits and leaves **Noser**—that is, they fall off. <note>The author is playing on the Hebrew root *N-Sh-R*, which relates to an eagle (*nesher*) but also to the falling of leaves or hair (*nashar*).</note> We have already established that the root of the tree is the name of the Most High, and the other divine names are like branches. Therefore, when the Indwelling Glory <note>The Shekhinah, the presence of God on earth.</note> can grasp nothing from the higher realms, the Israelites become needy, parched, and hungry; they fall from her just as leaves fall from a tree trunk.

Sometimes, however, this dimension overflows with wealth; at other times it lies needy and diminished—full at one moment and exhausted at another, according to the scripture: *As the eagle stirs up her nest,* etc. <margin>Deut. 32</margin> And when Israel turns to repentance, He restores that dimension to the state it held before, so that the channels of the heavenly pool drip into her through the restoration of the "pipes" or spiritual conduits. Replenished most richly on all sides, she regains her strength, according to the verse: *Who satisfies your desire with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.* <margin>Psal. 102</margin>

This dimension called **Neser** (the Eagle) is accompanied by a great host of winged eagles, which are called the "chariots" of the Eagle itself. To relieve the Israelites of the Egyptian burden, these were carried over them in Egypt, according to the verse: *You have seen what I did in Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings.* <margin>Exod. 19</margin> The fullness and excellence of these eagles who make up the "chariot" follows the fullness and excellence of Israel’s devotion to the Law and commandments; likewise, the diminishment of these powers follows when the Israelites depart from them.

Because this very dimension must be attached to the higher realms to draw down the divine flood, the Most High granted Israel a power: the ability to bind it to those higher things with a certain bond. This is the mystery of <term>תפלה</term> **Tephila**: that is, a joining, a coupling, or an ornament of the hand, according to the command: *And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand.* <note>Tephila refers here to both "prayer" and the "Tefillin" (phylacteries) worn during prayer as a sign of the covenant.</note> 

<margin><image-desc>A hand-drawn manicule pointing towards the text from the left margin.</image-desc></margin>
Therefore the masters have taught that whoever recites the morning reading of the <term>שמע</term> **Sema**—that is, *Hear, O Israel*—without these ornaments, bears false witness against himself, and every path is closed to him so that his prayer cannot enter. For one *tephila* (prayer or coupling) depends on another *tephila*—namely, the coupling of the mouth [speech] and the coupling of the hand [action]. This "coupling of the hand" opens the gates by which one may enter the name **Edonai** <note>Adonai, meaning Lord.</note>, and from there reach the name of the Most High. For this reason, it is commanded to put on these ornaments while reciting the morning *Sema*. 

The elders said that on Sabbaths and other solemn feast days, these are not times when the ornaments must be worn, regarding which grand mysteries are proposed: for on all these days, the entrances to the divine are already standing open. Therefore, the times of the Sabbaths and other celebrated days are excepted, because the days themselves are a "sign," and one sign does not require the connection of another sign.

Furthermore, the word used by the Law, the Prophets, and the Hagiographa <note>The third section of the Hebrew Bible, including Psalms and Proverbs.</note> is <term>כה</term> **Ko**: that is, "Thus" or "So." This measure is the gateway of all the heights, and it designates the mystery of the Holy Spirit, through which the entire choir of Prophets enters the mechanism of prophecy. This is why the Prophets so often begin their speeches with this phrase: *Thus [Ko] says the Lord.* 

Abraham began to establish this measure among the lowest things (as I discussed earlier), and he was the first to adapt the name **Edonai** to it, saying: *Lord God [Adonai Elohim], what will you give me?* <margin>Genes. 15</margin> The Lord answered him that there was no order of stars, nor any being among the higher or lower ranks, that could promise him offspring; that could only happen through the power of the dimension **Ko**. For this is the "gate of prayers," through which the threats of the stars are driven back and petitions are granted. This dimension transforms judgment into mercy; it gives life for the dead, health for the sick, and fertility for the sterile. From there...

### PAUL RICIUS,

<margin>Genesis 15.</margin>
<margin>Genesis 22.</margin>

For all things depend upon it, and it provides an entrance like a door for all. For this reason, the Most High promised Abraham: *Thus [Ko] shall your seed be* <note>original: "Sic erit semen tuum." Ricius is highlighting the Hebrew word "Ko" (כֹּה), meaning "Thus," as a specific mystical vessel or dimension.</note>: as if He had said, "With this measure intervening, you shall hold the path to enter toward the fountain of all springs and the origin of all that is begotten, even unto that place which is called the sign of all fatal signs." <note>The "sign of all fatal signs" refers to a supreme spiritual decree or "Mazal" that sits above ordinary astrology.</note> From this place, the living liquid of the beings above flows out into all the fatal signs. <margin>Numbers 6.</margin> Aaron and his sons, saying, Ko [Thus]*; that is, *Thus shall you bless*, etc.

And when a measure of this kind has been blessed and filled, then the blessing, the downward flow, and the dependence apply to Israel, according to that verse: *And they shall put
<margin>ibid.</margin> my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them.* For the priestly blessing is enclosed within the *Ko* measure, according to that which David sang: *and your holy ones [or those full of grace] bless you.* In Hebrew they bless *Ko*; concerning which it is likewise written:

We, however, bind these ornaments to the left hand, because from the left-side dimension—which is the side of fear and strength <note>The Sephirah of Gevurah (Strength/Severity).</note>—virtue goes forth into the measure, *Ko*.

And since this proportion, *Ko*, fought battles on behalf of David, he therefore sang: *By you*—in Hebrew, *By Ko*—*I shall run accoutred*, or *into the armed ranks*; <note>Psalm 18:29. Ricius interprets "by thee" (Hebrew *be-khah*) as a reference to the measure *Ko*.</note>
<margin>Psalm 37.</margin> for by the virtue of this dimension David laid low and pursued his enemies. This same measure also defeated the Kings on behalf of Abraham, as we have published in the discourse on *Justice*. It is this measure which displays the wonders and portents of the age, and which brought the ten plagues upon Egypt. In this matter, I would wish you to be instructed: it pleased the elders that Egypt be placed in the second rank after the land of Israel. However, the prince of the Egyptians is one of the chiefs of the lords of the nations, so much so that he claims for himself among the celestial signs that which holds the place of the first-born—namely, the sign of Aries [the Ram], whose rising is in the month of Nissan, which is accepted as the first of months, according to the verse:
<margin>Exodus 12.</margin> *This month shall be to you the first of months.* Since, therefore, Pharaoh clung to his own prince and remained entirely ignorant of the name *Tetragrammaton* <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, considered the highest and most holy.</note> because he was dedicated to this [other] Lord, the Most High dispatched Moses to him. Moses was to explain to him that there exists a certain Lord and Presider over the universe of all princes and armies of the world, who is Himself (I say) the Most High, whose portion and possession is Israel. Moses also forewarned Pharaoh to release Israel; for Israel is ruled by no force of celestial sign or star, but by the will of the Most High. The name **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: "Tetragrammaton." The four-letter, unpronounceable Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note> must be hidden while it is read: for it is forbidden to pronounce it by its own letters except in the sanctuary, nor is it permitted to utter it except by its specific title: *And this is my memorial* <note>Exodus 3:15</note>, namely the **Tetragrammaton** of the temple, the name **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai." The Hebrew word for "Lord," used as a substitute for the YHWH name.</note>; as if to say, as often as you find the name **Tetragrammaton**, pronounce it by the title **Adonai**, according to that saying of the wise: "I am not called by the voice with the same characters by which I am written: for I am written with the letters *Yod-He* <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton.</note>, but I am pronounced **Adonai**." In both of these readings in which the name **Eheie** <note>original: "Eheie" (אֶהְיֶה), meaning "I Will Be."</note> and the **Tetragrammaton** are commemorated, the word **Ko** <note>Hebrew: כֹּה (Ko), meaning "Thus" or "So."</note> is written. Because it is the gate through which we approach these two: for three (as I explained before) names are at the head, **Eheie**; in the middle, the **Tetragrammaton**; and at the end, **Adonai**. Because, therefore, the vocal commemoration of the name **Tetragrammaton** is made by the title **Adonai**, in these two readings mention is made of the word **Ko**. And when, by the command of the Most High, Moses approached Pharaoh in this measure, he opened his speech in the gate of the name **Tetragrammaton**, according to that verse: <margin>Exodus 6.</margin> *Then came Moses and Aaron saying to Pharaoh, **Ko**:* that is, *thus says the God **Tetragrammaton**, the God **Elohim** of the Hebrews,* etc. To which Pharaoh answering said: *Who indeed is the God **Tetragrammaton**, whose voice I ought to obey?* To whom Moses replied: *If the name of the Most High is hidden from you: know that the first door, through which we enter into knowledge of Him, is that which is called **Ko**: by which both the heavens and the earth are created:* according to that verse <margin>Isaiah 42.</margin> **Ko**: that is, *Thus says the God **El**, the God **Tetragrammaton** creating the heavens,* etc. This is the very same one which pays back punishment to all the wicked and the transgressors, according to <margin>Exodus 8.</margin> that verse: *Nor did you listen unto **Ko**:* that is, *hitherto, **Ko**.* That is, *thus says the God **Tetragrammaton**, by this you shall know that I am the God **Tetragrammaton** in the midst of the earth, behold I will strike:* that is, *I will strike with the rod which I hold in my hands:* for He brought every plague in the measure, **Ko**. On account of which the Most High forewarned Israel, that it should conduct itself cautiously with the measure **Ko**, lest (with the meter of dread and power leading) it seethes and becomes embittered into wrath: But let it apply effort (so that it does not scatter the world) to bring in mercy and blessing: according to that <margin>Numbers 6.</margin> verse **Ko**: that is, *Thus shall you bless the children of Israel:* that is, draw toward that blessing, grace and mercy, so that the blessing may also dwell in you. But the contrary of this must be avoided with the greatest care: for its concussion afflicts most bitterly: according to that <margin>Deuteronomy 25.</margin> verse: *Which is written, he shall strike him with forty lashes, and let him not add:* That is, if the sinner receives these forty lashes, the forty blows of the measure **Ko** will not afflict him. Which, if these punishments were inflicted by you, would offer themselves as far more cruel: To which let it thereafter be joined, *lest he strike him further* **maka raba**: <note>original: "maka raba" (מַכָּה רַבָּה), meaning "a great blow."</note> that is, *with a great striking*, as if it hints, unless someone receives forty lashes in this world, he will not be able to avoid the lashes of the future world with the harshest blow: for which the elders said, it is not to be read *Macho*, but *miko*: that is, *from **Ko**.* But **Raba** <note>Great</note> composes the number **207**, according to the number of prohibitive mandates (the transgressors of which pay the penalty with lashes), which the Law itself contains. ...the minister of the temple on the day of propitiation <note>The Day of Atonement, or Yom Kippur.</note>, on which it was permitted to enter the Holy of Holies to attain pardon, indulgence, and blessing, as well as the benefits sought throughout the course of the whole year, could not be admitted or enter except with this measure as a guide; indeed, even Moses never approached the sight of the Most High <margin>Levit. 1.</margin> unless first led by the hand of **Zos** <note>Hebrew: זאת (Zot), meaning "This" (feminine). For the unravelling of this, notice that where the Law writes an utterance depending on **Dibur**: that is, *speech*, such as **Vayedaber**: that is, *God spoke*, there the measure of strength [fortitude] is shown, and it is the business of the Written Law; but the utterance **Emira** [saying] suggests the measure of the Kingdom, and its intent concerns the Law delivered by mouth [the Oral Law]. For "spoke," which is written at the beginning of the clause, shows the Written Law; but "saying," which is uttered at the end, designates the Oral Law. And through such a pair—namely, the "speaking" and the "saying"—the Law itself is constructed and perfected everywhere, as that verse hints: <margin>Exod. 34.</margin> *Write for yourself these speeches: for according to the mouth of these speeches I have struck a covenant with you*. Therefore, the covenant was established upon the Written Law when it is joined to the Law brought forth by the mouth. Now, however, hear the sum of this mystery: the tablets of the covenant are <margin>Deut. 10.</margin> placed in the Ark, according to that: *And you shall put them in the Ark*. But the Written Law is explained through the Law delivered by mouth: for the temple of the Written Law is the Oral Law. As I have taught...

...for "-nai": <note>The final syllable of the name Adonai.</note> that is, the Lord is the temple of **Adonai** <note>original Latin: "Edonai," a transliteration of the Hebrew 'Adonai' meaning 'Lord.'</note> and the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>; and these two <margin>Proverbs 16</margin> Laws embrace one another like the twin fawns of a doe. Regarding anyone who would separate them, it is written: *And the whisperer separates the leader*, <note>A common Kabbalistic interpretation of Proverbs 16:28, suggesting that separating the Oral Law from the Written Law causes a rift in the divine order.</note> and such a person is as if he were a worshiper of no God at all. For this reason, whenever the Law records that "God spoke to Moses, saying," it points to these twin Laws together. Just as it says: <margin>Song of Songs 1</margin> *Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth*; and when the Israelites failed in both the Written Law and the Law handed down by mouth <note>The Oral Law, or Mishnah/Talmud.</note>, the Prophet rebuked them, saying: <margin>Isaiah 5</margin> *Because they have held the Law of the God of hosts in contempt* (that is, the Written Law) *and made void the words of the Holy One of Israel*, namely, the Law handed down by mouth.

The sign that supports our claim—that "speaking" is the measure of strength, while "saying" is the measure of the kingdom—is this: <margin>Exodus 6</margin> *And God [Elohim] spoke to Moses, and said to him: I am the Lord [Adonai].* For in that passage, he attaches the name **Elohim** to the act of "speaking," which expresses the meter of strength; but to "saying," he joins: *I am the Lord [Adonai]*, which suggests the measure of the kingdom. 

When you have learned these things, consider that this measure is called the Law issued by mouth: because the Written Law of God inhabits that oral Law as if it were a tabernacle and a courtyard. But because the many wonders and inner secrets hidden within the Written Law shine forth through the promulgated Oral Law, it is said: *when any matter of judgment is hidden from you*—that is, something deep and veiled in the Written Law—it follows: <margin>Deuteronomy 17:8</margin> *You shall do according to the word of the mouth of that which they declare to you.* 

Therefore, understand and revolve this in your mind; by weighing this further, examine how the Oral Law possesses no flow or dependence except that which the Written Law imparts. Nor is any path of entry to the Written Law allowed except through the Oral tradition, just as the Name **Adonai** draws its blessing from the height of the name **Tetragrammaton**, and no approach to the **Tetragrammaton** is found except with **Adonai** as the guide, as the things already said more clearly teach. Thus, these Laws provide a reciprocal support to each other, and both are finally fused into one, as it says: <margin>Zechariah 13</margin> *God is one and His name is one.*

Therefore, once all things in the measure of **Zos** <note>Hebrew: זאת (Zot), meaning "This" (feminine), identifying the Divine Presence or the Sephirah of Malchut.</note>, called **Adonai**, have been explained, one thing remains to be set forth that should not be lightly valued, but rather kept in the heart. For this measure, when it absorbs multiform vigor from higher levels, leads sometimes to destruction and sometimes to life. It snatches this person to the heavens and thrusts that one to the depths; it makes one faint and restores another to health, disposing all things according to what the rectitude of judgment demands. For there, nothing is unjustly twisted, nothing is surrendered to oblivion, and no favoritism is allowed. Therefore, just as it draws from the higher powers, so it receives various surnames of the heavens, such as the name of strength and fear suited to the meter of **Elohim**, of whom the "judgment hall of the sublime" is spoken. By this, all created things (with a middle line intervening) are judged with a just judgment to the right and to the left. When the measure of the stronger one determines that mortals are to be scattered, cut down, and destroyed in judgment, then **Adonai**—which is the storehouse of all things gushing from above—executes the judgment of God [**Elohim**] with which it is filled. For this reason, it is then called by the name **Elohim**. From this, it is customary for it to be named after the measure of the stronger one from which the judgment arises, as if the name of the one delegating fits the legate. 

In this Law, the Lord **Adonai**, the God **Tetragrammaton**, the God **Elohim**, and **Sadai** <note>Hebrew: Shaddai, meaning Almighty or Omnipotent.</note> (that is, the Almighty) are very often named according to the exuberance of the flow granted to it from a higher meter. For drawing from the supernal source, because it attains the fullness of perfection and completion, it receives the surname **Shaddai**. Under this guidance, it puts to flight the ranks of those who strike and destroy, according to the song in Psalm 91 <note>The Latin text cites Psalm 100, likely following a different numbering or a specific liturgical reference.</note> regarding evil events: *He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High shall abide in the shadow of the Almighty [Shaddai].* Because this measure, through which we enter the name **Tetragrammaton**, represents the appearance of a vestibule, it is established that the name **Shaddai** should be inscribed on the doorposts from the outside, in the encounter with the reading that begins: <margin>Deuteronomy 11</margin> *And it shall come to pass, if you shall hearken diligently...* <note>Referring to the Mezuzah, the parchment placed on doorposts containing the Shema, with the name Shaddai visible on the back.</note>

It is worth the effort to know that this threefold measure of **Shaddai**, **Elohim**, and **Adonai** (with the **Tetragrammaton** as the author, fosterer, and minister of all things) is triple...

...is clothed in a kind of fire: for when He is brought forth by the name **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadaï," the Hebrew name meaning Almighty.</note>, He is colored with a cloak of burning fire, and the phalanxes of all filthy spirits tremble and are cast down in fear at His sight; they are scattered at His nod and break into the caves and ways of the earth. But when He is expressed as **Elohim** <note>The name of God associated with justice and severity.</note>, He is covered in a burning fire tinged with redness, and judging the highest and lowest things alike, He dissolves and weakens both the impious and the just by fire; from this, all those placed in the execution of judgment demand the right to judge. For this measure is established (by the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> residing within it) so that it may distribute death, life, disease, health, punishments, and healing; it casts down the lofty and recalls them to the heights. When, however, He is uttered by the voice of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai," the Hebrew word for Lord.</note>, He is clothed in a color of fire that all created things fear and dread. Sitting upon the sublime throne of the kingdom like a prince and lord, He is adorned with royal jewels, and as the most steadfast presiding officer, He shines forth over the entire Chariot <note>The *Merkavah*, or divine celestial vehicle.</note> of both superior and fleeting beings through the mediation of the **forty-two letter name** <note>A mystical name of God in Kabbalistic tradition composed of 42 letters.</note>, concerning which it is written: <margin>Psalm 8</margin> *O Lord [Elohim] our Lord [Adonai], how effective is your name in all the earth, you who display your praise above the heavens.* <margin>$\Sigma$</margin> With these things revealed concerning the measure of **Adonai**, examine again how, just as in the bond of true union there are three names—namely **Ehyeh** <note>The name "I Am," associated with the highest crown.</note>, **Adonai**, and the **Tetragrammaton**—so in the human framework, three dependent connections shine forth: the **Soul**, the **Spirit**, and the **Mind**. It is necessary, therefore, for the soul to be connected to the spirit, the spirit to the mind, and the mind to **Adonai** itself, so that it may be as written: <margin>1 Samuel 25</margin> *And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life.* <note>The Latin text cites "1 Kings," following the Vulgate numbering where 1 & 2 Samuel are 1 & 2 Kings.</note> Truly, because this measure holds the lowest place when it descends from the highest to the lowest, and holds the beginning when we ascend from the lowest to the highest, the final *He* <note>The letter 'H' (ה), the last letter of the name YHWH.</note> of the name **Tetragrammaton** announces it. By this letter, which constitutes a unity with the nine higher levels, it is intended that by its guidance, whoever is able should attain the name **Tetragrammaton** and strive to cling to it, according to the verse: *and you shall cling to him.* <margin>$\Sigma$</margin> Finally, it remains to be heard that whenever the elders commemorate the **Assembly of Israel** <margin>Leviticus 20. Deuteronomy 32.</margin> <note>original: "Keneset Yisra'el."</note>, they show that it is the same measure as the prescribed names of **Adonai**. For it contains within itself the entire assembly of Israel; they meet within it together and are gathered there into one. By this same measure, the Israelites are separated from all nations, as it says: *And I have separated you from the peoples, that you should be my own possession*; and again: *When the Most High assigned the nations their inheritance, when he divided the sons of Adam, he fixed the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel.* For this reason, this measure is accustomed to be called the **Land of Israel** <note>original: "Eretz Yisra'el."</note>; for it is divided into the portions of the twelve tribes. Again, in the Song of Songs, it is called **Kallah** <note>original: "Kalo," meaning Bride.</note>, that is, the **Bride**. However, I have thought it best to pass over the explanation of these things in silence for now, because the following sections will unfold them all more extensively. But keep this, at last, collected in summary: namely, that the name **Adonai** is the great temple in which are stored all the ways of the "overflow," which break forth in beauty (that is, led by the **Tetragrammaton**) from the head of the crowns called **Ehyeh**. For in that very temple, the rivers proceeding from the thirteen heights of the crown flow down together; they leap and spring forth from the thirty-two paths of wisdom, from the fifty gates of understanding, from the seventy-two bridges proceeding from the waters of supreme mercy, from the forty-two types of flaming fire (exceeding the measure of the stronger one), and from the seventy channels moving through the middle line. By the way of eternity and praise, they are joined and unite into the measure called **El Hai** <note>The Living God.</note> (that is, the **Foundation** <note>The Sephirah *Yesod*.</note>), and from there they turn into the cistern or well itself: I mean, they turn from the Foundation into the upper pool, which is called **Adonai**. You should not think, however, that all these things break forth together continuously, but only when the name itself is so complete that the **Tetragrammaton** is called "One God." For then all those heights flow together with one mind into the name **Adonai**, and because of the wealth of the overflow emanating into it from the nine higher **Sephirot** <note>original: "Sphiros," the divine emanations.</note>, it is accustomed to lavish an abundance of good things upon individuals according to the limit of each one's nature. # THE WORKS OF PAULUS RICIUS

...diminish, and the flows of grace and mercy increase. But more often, on the contrary, the impious remove the pipes and channels of grace and mercy, and they add and establish more channels of judgment. For this reason, very sharp and cruel things come forth through the name **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai," a phonetic Latin rendering of the Hebrew word for Lord.</note>, by which the age is oppressed by various hardships; the highest pipes and channels are blocked, and external passages burst forth. Thus, evils surge back like whirlpools of filthy water; wherever there is grief and affliction, kingdoms are plundered, scepters fall, empires are cast down, provinces are overwhelmed, armies are routed, and the most savage captivities and slaughters emerge. Unexpected deaths, frequent funerals, and finally, all manner of pitiable and lethal things happen. Conclude, therefore, that this name **Adonai** takes on the quality of whatever is carried into it from within or without—whether good or evil—according to that phrase: *the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.* 

<margin>1 Kings 16 <note>In the Vulgate Bible used by Ricius, 1 Kings corresponds to 1 Samuel in modern translations. This refers to 1 Samuel 16:12.</note></margin>
For if its influence is drawn from the side of grace, it is given the name "Good." If it is drawn from the side of judgment—that judgment, I mean, which is drawn from the other internal powers—it is again called "Good," as that passage suggests: *and he was ruddy, with beauty of the eyes, and a goodly appearance.* But if the judgment should flow from external hordes, that will be the worst evil and a wicked disposition. Consider this: whenever the name **Adonai** exists from the side of grace, or from the judgment of those who flow into it from within, it receives the title of "Good," into the mystery of which we speak. "Blessed is the Judge of Truth" <note>A reference to the Hebrew blessing *Baruch Dayan HaEmet*, said upon hearing of a death.</note>; and concerning this, they established a blessing over those slain at Betar <note>original: "beter." This refers to the Roman siege of Betar during the Bar Kokhba revolt. Jewish tradition holds that a specific blessing—"He who is good and does good"—was added to the Grace After Meals when the dead of Betar were finally allowed to be buried.</note>: "He who is good and imparts good." But if he brings forth judgment from those dwelling outside, it is then called an "evil disposition." Yet if, on the other hand, he absorbs the spirit of grace and mercies, then the entirety of the age is nourished by the most abundant mercy and grace, as is perceived from this: *To the Tetragrammaton of God, to our God Elohim, belong mercies and forgiveness.* Therefore, keep this balance to be weighed stored in your closed breast, lest the liquid flow out and be wasted. May the Most High, in His ineffable piety and the abundance of His graces and generosity, impart to us the teaching of this learning, and show us the path of truth, through which we may approach His most holy name, perform what is pleasing to Him, and merit the life of the world to come, Amen.

The second (according to the grades of the heights) of the holy words is the name **El Hai**: that is, called "The Living God." For this name, holding the last place among the nine heights—which we call *Sephiroth* <note>original: "sphíros." The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals Itself.</note> or "mirrors"—diffuses and transfers from all the higher ones. Insofar as it receives the dimension of grace, it is called **El** <note>The Hebrew name of God associated with the attribute of Chesed or Mercy.</note>. From the fact that it absorbs life, it is called "Living." Since these two adhere to one another, both are usually called "The Living God." When it diffuses this vigor of life into the measure of **Adonai**, that name is called "The Land of Life." This is because, gathering life into itself from the highest things, it imparts the gift of most abundant life no less to the angelic and celestial choirs than to the multitude of the whole world, according to that passage:

<margin>Genesis 1</margin>
*Let the earth bring forth the living soul according to its kind.* For this sequence of letters, according to the mystery of wisdom, designates the soul of every moving thing: namely, of reptiles on dry land, fish in the sea, cattle, beasts, birds, and the animal and vital soul of the human race and of the angels. It demonstrates the forces of the entire sky and the stars according to each of their kinds, and it announces the celestial soul and mind that sits within man.

Concerning which the elders teach: *Let the earth bring forth the living soul according to its kind,*
<margin>☛</margin> saying: This is the soul of the Messiah, which is truly admirable and powerful in the sight of these...

...are the utterances: moreover, the literal meaning of the text supports this opinion in its own way: that is, whatever kind of being it may be—whether of the heavenly, the middle, or the perishable kind, or even the soul of the Messiah <note>original: "Masie," a Latinization of Mashiach (Messiah).</note>—yet let not the followers of philosophy rebuke me if I have said that even an angel participates in a soul. For indeed, no created thing (among living beings, it is understood) is admitted in which the soul of life does not dwell according to its own kind. For each thing claims as much soul for itself as the limits of its own matter require. Therefore, the entire choir of souls, both among the celestial and the fallen, draws life from the "earth of life," **Edonai** <note>original: "Edonai," Ricius's phonetic spelling of the Hebrew name for the Lord, Adonai.</note>, under the leadership of **El Hai** <note>original: "El hai," meaning The Living God.</note>: that is, the living God, who from the source of life, interceding by the Tree of Life, transfers life into the name **Edonai**. Because this name, by the will of **El Hai**, provides the gifts of living to all animate creatures, prayers were established at the beginning of the year <note>A reference to the liturgy of Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year.</note>: *Be mindful of us for life,* where the intention is directed toward **El Hai** and **Magen** <note>original: "magen," meaning shield or protector.</note>: that is, the protector. For this reason, consider that the life of the world to come, which belongs to the longed-for measure of **El Hai**, must be applied to the measure of **Edonai** when drawn down by prayers. 

<margin>Psalm 41 <note>In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 42:2.</note></margin>
