<margin>Joshua 3</margin>
To this point Joshua declared: *In this you shall know that the living God El dwells among you, and He shall make you the heirs of your enemies.* Since, therefore, we must join the heights and the **Sphiros** <note>original: "sphíros," referring to the Sephirot, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah.</note> to the measure of **Edonai**, it is the custom in the blessing which continually follows the morning Psalms to say: *You who choose the songs of the Psalms, King El Hai of the ages.* Therefore, whoever desires to become a partaker of life or any other benefit should raise his mind toward the dimension of **El Hai**. For he who clings purely to the name **Edonai** will be joined to **El Hai** according to His will, concerning which it is written: 

<margin>Deut. 4</margin>
*You who cling to the Lord Tetragrammaton* <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, *to your God Elohim, you are all alive today.* Sometimes this dimension is also called **Elohim Haim** <note>original: "Elohim haim," the Living God (plural in form).</note>: that is, the living God or Gods, as it is said: *He is Elohim Haim*: that is, the living [God] and the King of the world. And when the measure of **El Hai** is marked by the meter of **Edonai** and called **Elohim**, and is filled with life, we read that both are then called **Elohim Haim**. From this, through the channels and pipes, the race of living creatures drinks most abundantly of the capacity for living.

Supporting this is that saying of the elders: *The Holiest One said to Moses, "You have given me life by your utterances."* And unless Moses had done this, destruction would have soon rushed upon everyone. Therefore, as long as this overflowing measure produced fruit and the fruit of fruit, Israel remained alive; but when these last things were produced, they paid the penalties for their crime. Therefore, he who proves worthy to attain this mystery will easily be able to perceive how much vigor exists in the drawing of **El Hai** into the dimension of **Edonai**. 

It is uttered as **Elohim Haim**, although the measure of **Edonai** is similarly named: because the measure of **El Hai** itself imparts life to no one except according to the requirement of just judgment; for no favoritism of persons is prescribed there, as if he had spoken of judgment together with the dimension of **Haim** <note>original: "haim," meaning life.</note>. This is why, at the head of the year, which is determined to be the Day of Judgment, we commemorate these measures together with **Magen** (that is, protector) in the first blessing, saying: *Remember us for life, O King who is pleased by life, and write us in the book of life, for your sake, Elohim Haim, El Hai, King, Helper, Savior, and Protector.*

This dimension is also frequently read as **El Sadai** <term>אל שדי</term> <note>El Shaddai</note>: that is, the God who is sufficient. For through Him, vigor, perfection, life, inundation, and every superior flow drips sufficiently into the name **Edonai**, as the elders declare in the book **Hegiga** <note>The Talmudic tractate Hagigah.</note> (that is, of the solemnities). **Sadai** <note>Shaddai</note>, for by this name the Maker of things says "enough" <note>A traditional Jewish etymology of Shaddai: "She-dai" (Who is enough/sufficient).</note> to His world, though it might seem to sound as if the world were extending itself wider and wider until its own architect imposed a limit upon it. <margin>Genesis 28.</margin>

But since there are also pools of wicked waters—dead and foul waters—called from the impetuous floods of rushing waves and from strange cisterns, which gush and leap forth bringing out filthier whirlpools, therefore the Most High, in His anger, reproached and rebuked Israel.

Therefore, the foundation called **El Hai** carries the measure of **Adonai** like a constructed house. ...he must be listened to, as even perishable things perceived by the senses suggest this by analogy; for a higher magnet placed above draws iron located below, as fire, air, and water clearly demonstrate. Everywhere to this dimension the surname **Zadic** <note>original: "צדיק ZADIC"; the Hebrew term *Tzadik*, meaning "The Righteous One." In Kabbalah, this refers to the Sefirah *Yesod* (Foundation), which acts as a channel for divine energy.</note>—that is, "the Righteous"—is given, because this dimension sustains all these lower things. 

<margin>Proverbs 10.</margin>
Regarding this it is read: *And the righteous is the foundation of the world.* He is called "Righteous" because he pours every kind of overflow and good into the name **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonaï." Representing the Sefirah *Malkhut* (Kingdom), the recipient of divine flow.</note>. But examine and listen to one thing worthy of remembrance here: there are three names: The Righteous, Justice, and Justification. "The Righteous" corresponds to the measure of **El Hai** <note>original: "El hai"; The Living God.</note>; "Justice" to **Adonai**; and when the Righteous imparts his gift to her, it has been pleasing to call this kind of overflow and dependency "Justification." For these three terms coincide in one: the Righteous is to provide, Justice is to receive, and Justification joins them both together. To this, again, turn the sharp edge of your mind. When the Righteous bestows gifts of goods upon Justice, she herself is customarily called the "Land of Life." But if the pipes and channels of this Righteous one are pulled back, so that they do not flow into the measure of Justice, then she abounds with death-bearing passages, and provides the calamities and windings of the world's destruction. On the contrary, however, when she is united by the bond of justification, she offers delights instead of punishment, and life instead of destruction, 

<margin>Proverbs 10.</margin>
according to that saying: *And justification* <note>In many Latin Bibles, *iustitia* (justice/righteousness) is used here; Ricius uses it to mean the act of connecting the divine flow.</note> *delivers from death.* Therefore, by this path one may determine that whoever aspires to inherit the land of life must necessarily cling to the dimension of the Righteous; thus he himself will also be called "righteous," whereby he will emerge as a faithful cultivator and possessor of that same land of life. 

<margin>Isaiah 60</margin>
Of which it is said: *And your people shall all be righteous, they shall inherit the land forever.* Now it is sufficiently known to you what the elders express here. "All Israel," they say, "have a portion in the world to come," as it is said: *And your people are all righteous,* etc. But as far as you may judge the magnitude of the fault in crimes, I thought this one thing should by no means be shrouded in silence. Behold, we have now taught exactly that when the dimension of **Adonai** is annexed to the measure of the justice of **El Hai**, then, rich in all goods, she most abundantly provides for each one, makes the whole world fruitful, and fills it with gifts of every kind. But when the same influence recedes, the measure of **Adonai** is left empty and void of goods. The first indeed happens while the children of men, purged from filth, keep the Law and the commandments; the second happens when, having spurned the Law, they strive for vain pleasures and pursue wicked crimes. For then **Zadic**, withdrawing and turning away, gathers himself by flying up to the highest realms, whence the channels and pipes all waste away, and the dimension of **Adonai** is left parched and destitute, as that sounds: *Because of evil itself the righteous man is taken away.* 

<margin>Ecclesiastes 7. Psalm 13.</margin>
Solomon also writes: *There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness.* And it is read: *God looked down from heaven to see if there is any who understands,* etc. *They have all turned aside, they have together become useless, there is none who does good,* etc. He brings forth "there is none who does good" because the power is granted to mortals to build up, lay waste, and shatter innumerable things in the upper realms; 

<margin>Psalm 118. Isaiah 27.</margin>
to which applies: *It is time for God to act, they have subverted your Law.* Similarly it is said: *Or let him take hold of my strength, let him make peace with me; let him make peace with me.* Examine, therefore, how great is the power of the righteous who embrace the Law, to whom it is given to join all the <term>Sefirot <gloss>the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which God is revealed</gloss></term> <note>original: "sphiros"</note> and to compose a most perfect relationship between things above and things below. Through them, heaven and earth are fused into one, and through them (with **Zadic** adhering), the measure of **Adonai** shall be called the Living God. Oh, happy man now scrutinizing these sublime things with his investigation! How worthy and sweet his future portion, how blessed the womb that bore him! 

<margin>Psalm 103:</margin>
Of whom it is written: *Let your father and your mother be glad,* and *God rejoices in His works.* So, on the contrary, a wicked, vile, and filthy man is the minister through whom **Zadic** is pulled back to the upper realms, leaving the measure of **Adonai** sterile and parched.

For this reason the elders warn us, saying: *A man should always consider himself as much liable to guilt as he is worthy of reward,* explaining the meaning of which **Rabbi Shimon son of Eleazar** says: "Because both the world and mankind..."

# PAULUS RICIUS,

Every human being is judged according to the abundance of their actions. For if someone performs even a single meritorious work, they align both themselves and the world toward the merit of grace. But if they commit a crime, they are not only made wretched themselves, but they bend the entire universe toward the guilt of their sin. Thus, you see the way in which a single column called **Zadic** <note>original: "Zadic"; the Hebrew *Tzadik*, meaning "The Righteous One."</note> sustains the weight of the entire age; because of this, it is written: *And Zadic—that is, the righteous—is the foundation of the world,* etc. This dimension also carries the title of "Good" everywhere, as in: *Tell the righteous man that he is good.* For the flows that run down from the heavenly oracles—indeed, those that break out into this unchangeable machine from the measures of strength and fear—if they pass through the temple of the righteous, they all turn toward the good and the benefit of the matter. Therefore, the Sages rightly declare (as they say) that nothing evil is sent down from the heavenly powers.

<margin>Micah 1.</margin>
However, where it is read that *evil descended from God, the Tetragrammaton,* <note>The Tetragrammaton refers to the four-letter holy name of God, YHWH.</note> it must be understood as coming from the storehouses existing outside the fabric of the spheres. Indeed, many treasuries of scourges exist there, which it has pleased men to call "evil." For these frequently invade the temple of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai." The Hebrew name for Lord, associated here with the manifest world or the Sefirah Malkhut.</note> and rush into the age of mortals. Regarding this figure, it is written:

<margin>Micah 1.</margin>
*Because evil descended from Adonai,* <note>original: "mees Edonai"; a Latinization of the Hebrew *me-et Adonai* (from/with the Lord).</note> as if evil wished to descend, not indeed *out* of God, but from something that is *with* God. Therefore, it is not read: *It descended from Adonai* <note>original: "me Edonai"; implying a direct origin from God's essence.</note>—which would sound as if it came from God himself—but *from with Adonai.* This also proceeds to the point that the Law itself explains in the work of the Beginning:

<margin>Genesis 1.</margin>
*And God saw that it was good,* etc. And at the end of the work, it is written: *Behold, it was very good,* etc. Regarding this, in the book of **Bereshit Rabbah** <note>original: "Berescis raba"; a classical Jewish commentary (midrash) on Genesis.</note> the ancient sages explain: *Very good* means death. From this, understand that even death—which follows the measure of the righteous—is considered "good" and "life." For the righteous (they say), even after they have fallen asleep, are numbered among the assembly of the living. To this also belongs the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.** For since the temple of **Adonai** is called the Tree of Knowledge of the sacred things, it draws fullness from the oracle of the Good. Whatever revolves among beings (no less destruction than life), we decree that it is turned into good. But if, through the dimension of the righteous, the pipe-like channels do not flow into the house of justice or the Tree of Knowledge, then that very temple of **Adonai** performs the office of the "outer plague," which is called the worst. From there, God crushes, devastates, and scatters the age with the terrifying lightning of storms, just as the fair reasoning of judgment demands. For this reason, we are convinced that the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil is brought forth by a measure of this kind. Hence, concerning

<margin>Exodus 2.</margin>
**Moses**, since he stood dedicated to this oracle of the Good, the Law proclaims: *And she saw him, that he was good.* From this, as they say, the house shone all around with glowing light. Nor should it escape you that the temple of **Adonai**, most often called **Elohim** <note>A name of God associated with justice and the natural order.</note>, when it intended the fabric of the universe, consulted the measure of the Good, by which it shaped and completed all things exactly according to their forms. Regarding this sense, it is written in the work of the Beginning:

<margin>Genesis 1.</margin>
*And Elohim saw that it was good.* And sometimes this dimension is brought forth as **Sechel Tof** <note>original: "שכל טוב Sechel Tof"; Hebrew for "Good Intellect" or "Good Understanding."</note>—that is, "good intellect," etc. By its help, we are carried toward the glowing mirror for the sake of intuition, and the path is opened through which we attain wisdom from the truth of the name Tetragrammaton. To the persistent worshiper of the Law and the commandments, this measure—namely, good intellect—offers itself as a companion, as is clear from that verse:

<margin>Psalm 111.</margin>
*The fear of the Lord (Tetragrammaton) is the beginning of wisdom; a good intellect is to all who do them.* And great indeed is the mystery of this, namely what is written:

<margin>Proverbs 16.</margin>
*The one who understands a matter (or "in the word") finds good.* So also, when David had presented himself to such a measure, he was accustomed to say: *Le David maskil*—that is, "To David the

<margin>Title. Psalm 32.</margin>
understanding one." <note>A *Maskil* is a musical or liturgical term in the Psalms often translated as a "contemplative poem" or "teaching."</note> Finally, every utterance referring to understanding is turned back into that same oracle. And whoever knows the symbolic meaning of grace will easily be able to see what "good intellect gives grace" means. However, the "understanding man" and the "prudent man" differ: for the prudent man drinks from the fountain of prudence, but the

<margin>Proverbs 13.</margin>
understanding man feeds on the first and last Good. This dimension is read again by the name **Salom** <note>original: "שלוס SALOM"; Hebrew *Shalom*, meaning Peace.</note>—that is, "Peace." For when (as the previous sections reveal) the Israelites are weighed down with integrity and righteousness, the temple of **Adonai** overflows with all the wealth of rewards. But those doing the opposite suffer the opposite, unless they return to the repentance of these righteous...

It reconciles them, and with every distinction cut away, it fuses and composes them into one. Because of this, for a certain time, the name Tetragrammaton is brought forth as one; and since no blessing is sent down except with this very oracle of peace as a leader, it is written: *The Tetragrammaton gives strength to his people; the Tetragrammaton blesses his people with peace.* Regarding this, the foremost of the Sages say: We know of no vessel that contains every form of blessing as peace itself does, which the highest Giver of all good things granted to Israel, as it is read: *May God turn his face toward you and grant you peace.* Therefore, since peace occupies the final place among the most excellent "mirrors" <note>specula: likely referring to the Sefirot as mirrors or emanations of divine light.</note>, the priestly blessing and the daily prayer always conclude by commemorating peace. Indeed, by its authority, all those who desire to become companions of the life of the world to come approach, and by its nod, they depart.

Observe here that mystic story of the ancients: they say that while Moses was penetrating to the heights above, he beheld the Most High fastening crowns to the letters of the alphabet. The Creator himself, pausing, said to Moses: "Has peace itself utterly vanished from your city?" Moses, answering, said: "What servant would presume to greet the Lord with peace?" Nevertheless, the Creator said: "I would not have considered it out of place if you had offered me some help." Immediately, Moses began: "*Now,*" he said, "*let the power of the Lord Adonai be magnified.*" And a little further on it is read: *I have pardoned according to your word,* and *as I live,* etc., as if he wished to say: "You have given me life by your words." These are their words. For such a measure of peace, while it dwells in the Temple of **Adonai**, pours the power of living into it. How strong and powerful, then, is the strength of peace, which even aids those in the heights, as the scriptures show: *He who makes peace in his high places.* Thus, a man who is a faithful guardian of the Law and the commandments reconciles the heavenly hosts (as I might put it) through peace; upon this rests that verse: <margin>Isaiah 27</margin> *Or let him take hold of my strength, let him make peace with me; let him make peace with me.*

Sometimes the title <term>זכרון</term> **Zikoron** <note>original: "Zikoron"; Hebrew *Zichron*, meaning "Remembrance."</note> is bestowed upon this; that is, "remembrance." For there, whatever good lies hidden in the individual works of the world is sent back to memory; and depending on what kind of remembrance this was, all things undergo judgment by that Law. For this reason, the Law itself calls the beginning of the year "a remembrance" (or a "memorial day"). Indeed, the beginning of the year typically refers to the temple of **Adonai**. "Remembrance," however, reveals the oracle of **El Hai** <note>original: "El hai"; Hebrew for "The Living God," usually associated with the Sefirah Yesod.</note>. Since the hidden order of wisdom has decreed that the execution of judgment upon us takes place at the beginnings of the year, and that all the deeds of mortals be offered to the sight of **Adonai** for examination, we then turn our prayers toward the measure of **El Hai**, praying: *Remember us for life, O King who delights in life, and write us in the book of life for your sake, O **Elohim**,* <note>original: "Elohim"; the divine name associated with judgment and the Sefirah Binah.</note> *the life of **El Hai**.* But because this dimension calls back to memory whatever is covered by oblivion, we conclude our prayer at the start of the year by saying: *You who remember the covenant.* For that measure shows the entrance to both the covenant and remembrance. From this, David also, aspiring to this oracle, says: *A Psalm of David, for remembrance.* He says the same: *The remembrance of the offering,* and *the offering of remembrance,* which remembers iniquities. From there, the punishment of the adulterous woman is paid, for this is the offering of jealousy, which jealousy (I say) inhabits this place, as it is read: *The zeal of the Tetragrammaton of hosts does this.* Let it not be ignored, however, that the same is meant by "remembrances" and "re-visitations." But re-visitations are in the hand of **Adonai**, while remembrances are conducted under the leadership of **El Hai**.

Therefore, since the entire machine of the world is led to the peak of perfection when these two measures are glued together, the Architect of the world commanded the day of the Sabbath in a twofold way after their example: through <term>זכור</term> **Zochor** <note>original: "Zochor"; Hebrew *Zakhor*, meaning "Remember."</note> (that is, "Remember"), as a type for the day and the oracle of **El Hai**; and through <term>שמור</term> **Samor** <note>original: "Samor"; Hebrew *Shamor*, meaning "Keep" or "Observe,"</note> as a mystic sign for the night and the temple of **Adonai**. For the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> puts forth two such words. For the sake of this teaching, notice that the three higher lights—I mean the Crown <note>Keter</note>, Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>, and Prudence <note>Binah</note>—consist in unity. And when they are bound together and adhere to one another, the spherical shrines... <meta>catchword: lubra (shrines)</meta>

# PAUL RICIUS,

Beneath <note>original: "Iubra"; likely a typo for "Infra" (below) or "Intra" (within)</note> the union with the six lower measures <note>The six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod, often called the "Six Days of Creation."</note> all the way to that same **El Hai** <note>Hebrew: "The Living God," a name associated with the Sefirah Yesod (Foundation).</note>—which is called the foundation and the Sabbath—Prudence <note>Prudentia: The Sefirah Binah (Understanding).</note> initiates the process. But the seventh is the Sabbath, which in its order equals the oracle of the Foundation, to which we have given the name **El Hai**. It is fitting, therefore, for the blessing and the place of the sanctuary to be adapted to the Sabbath, as it is written:

<margin>Genesis 2.</margin>
And the God Elohim blessed the seventh day and sanctified it: because in it he rested, etc. He who rightly keeps the Sabbath is therefore considered as the chariot and the seat of the oracle of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, associated here with the central Sefirah, Tiferet.</note>: hence rest is announced as the Sabbath, as in that passage:

<margin>Psalm 131. Exodus 20.</margin>

<margin>Isaiah 26 <note>Likely a reference to Isaiah 56:2.</note></margin>

For the pattern of the Sabbath is the measure **El Hai**, to which (as pleased the wise) that saying is applied: "Who will give his fruit in his time." To this the Prophet also agrees, saying: "To the eunuchs (he says) who keep my Sabbaths," etc. Do not think, however, that the leaders in Israel are literal eunuchs and are the only ones to rightly celebrate the Sabbaths, but rather that the Prophet warned the righteous through a certain similarity to eunuchs—those who restrain their marital use during the six working days and seek the marriage bed on Sabbath nights. For the word "to guard" <note>custodire</note> which is read in that same place puts forward the female sex, as it is written: "Be guarded from everything I have said to the woman." Regarding this riddle, it is customarily said: "**Remember**" <note>memento</note> belongs to the day, but "**Guard**" <note>custodi</note> belongs to the night. To the righteous who keep this dogma, the Father of Lights soon promises, saying: "And I will

<margin>Judges 13.</margin>

lead them into my holy mountain" (into the shrine, namely **El Hai**) "and I will make them joyful in my house of prayer," in the temple, namely **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"; the Sefirah Malkhut.</note>: which twin oracles designate "**Remember**" and "**Guard**." But he who profanes the Sabbath will be declared a denier of the worship of the Most High God; for indeed, in seeking the higher things from the depths, we encounter the Sabbath as the first root of the tree; wherefore it was permitted for that very thing to be called the foundation of the world. Because the mental spirits fly out from the light of **Adonai** under the lead of the measure **El Hai**, therefore on the Sabbath day (as the wise enigmatically state) another soul is added to man, which is taken away at the end of the Sabbath, as it typically hints: "And on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed" <note>original: "animavit"; Ricius highlights the Latin root "anima" (soul) to refer to the "extra soul" (Neshamah Yeterah) given on the Sabbath.</note>. He who is not blinded by light will now clearly see and penetrate this mystery. Through the dimension of the Sabbath, the final measure, **Adonai**, is annexed to all lower things; for which reason the seventh day is called the Sabbath. And since you, Prudence <note>Binah</note>, gather the two higher Sephirotic lights into the six subject dimensions, therefore the shrine of Prudence is counted as the seventh when you ascend from the lowest parts to the higher. Finally, the measure of this world, **El Hai**, presents the number seven; but the Prudence of the future world [presents eight], through which all liberty and exact redemption breaks forth. Hence the wise command the one praying to join "redemption" to "prayer": for **El Hai** represents the hidden part of redemption, and **Adonai** represents that of prayer. Wherefore, beginning the prayer, while one says: "Lord, open my lips," let him intend his mind with all his strength toward the oracle of redemption, and think by what Law it is to be joined to the temple of **Adonai**. For from this, the ancient Samuel <note>A sage of the Talmud known for his rulings on prayer.</note> of the wise brought glory to himself, saying: "I have placed redemption next to prayer": for he gathered the supernal channels into the redemption of Israel, the vigor of which then rested in the house of **Adonai**. Thus, this man wove the Sephirotic assembly into one whole. If Israel were to observe exactly two Sabbaths to perfection, the chains of their captivity would be immediately loosened. <margin>Genesis 48.</margin>

<margin>Exodus 13.</margin>

It is worthwhile to distinguish that, although (as it pleased the great sages) what the Sabbath truly is remains known to no one, yet the reward of the Sabbath has become known through the Prophets. For it stands as something exceptional among good things, a light hidden from the six days of the beginning, into which not every creature is worthy to fix its own gaze.

### PAULUS RICIUS,

...is [fini]shed <note>likely continuing from "finitur" on the previous page</note>, next to the temples of **Edonai** <note>original: "Edonaí"; a variant of Adonai, representing the Sefirah Malkuth (Sovereignty)</note>, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, and **Eheie** <note>Hebrew for "I Am," associated with Keter (Crown)</note>: finally, the whole Sephirotic order will be gathered together (with the Sabbath or the measure of **El hai** mediating). The oracle of **El hai** <note>Hebrew for "The Living God," associated with the Sefirah Yesod (Foundation)</note> is the same. <insert>Covenant</insert> **BERIS**: that is, "covenant," as it is written in the Law: for every word of the Law that sounds like "covenant" suggests one of the three Sephirotic lights, namely **El hai**, **Edonaí**, and **Bina**: that is, Understanding. But the covenant of Understanding is the covenant of the mouth, the covenant of the tongue, the covenant of the lips: for it is written: *Because through the mouth of these words I have struck a covenant with you.* <note>Reference to Exodus 34:27</note> The covenant of **El hai**, however, is called the covenant of peace, the covenant of the Sabbath, and the covenant of the bow <note>the rainbow</note>. The Creator of the world also instituted for us the covenant of circumcision, so that through it we might be made sharers with **El hai**. But the covenant of **Edonaí** concerns the covenant of the Law, which stands joined between **El hai** and the covenant of Understanding: and since the temple of **Edonaí** clings to the measures of **El hai** and Understanding, it adapts the surname of "covenant" to itself: according to the enigma of the "covenant of the tongue" and the "covenant of the flesh." The same is revealed by the showing of circumcision, as that saying of the wise reveals: *If one has circumcised and has not uncovered the crown of the circumcised member, the circumcision itself is considered as nothing:* <note>A reference to the Jewish legal requirement of 'priah' or uncovering the glans</note> for the circumcision of the member and the showing of the crown represents the hidden **Edonaí**: and when the showing is lacking, the first Sephirotic oracle, through which one enters the house of the **Tetragrammaton**, will be judged to be missing. This dimension is also pronounced <insert>Sign</insert> **Oos**: that is, a "sign," because from there wonders and signs are renewed in the world: which is why, surely, if in the exit from Egypt, when redemption had been joined to prayer, so many portents and prodigies shone forth, <margin>Exodus 2. Exodus 31.</margin> to which this accords: *And God [Elohim] saw (or looked upon) the children of Israel, and God [Elohim] knew.* <note>Exodus 2:25</note> And also that: *And I remembered my covenant.* The Sabbath is also called a sign (which the measure of **El hai** also refers to), as it is written: *Between me and the children of Israel, it is a sign forever.* <margin>Genesis 17.</margin> Similarly, we have learned that circumcision, which shows this very Sephirah of **El hai**, is called a sign: as in that: *Circumcise the foreskin of your flesh, etc.* <margin>Genesis 9.</margin> So likewise the bow is called a sign, just as it is written: *I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant, etc.* The covenant of the bow, as we expressed before, announces the covenant of **El hai**. Therefore, whenever you hear the utterance of a "sign," understand the dimension of **El hai**, which explains the mystery of remembrance: for the same **El hai** calls back into memory all the children of the world: But the sign of the covenant of the Sabbath and of circumcision reconciles only the children of Israel to Him: while the sign of the covenant of the bow is applied to everything which the circle of the lands embraces. <margin>Genesis 21.</margin> Finally, as a type of this oracle, the Law itself expresses the name <insert>Oath</insert> **Scefua**: that is, "oath": for although the word referring to an oath is equal in pronunciation to the word **Sceiuea**: that is, "seven": by which agreement Abraham also brought forth to Abimelech **Seua**: that is, "seven" (saying) *Receive seven ewe lambs from my hand,* therefore he called the place **Beerſceua**: that is, the "well of seven," because they both swore there. <margin>Genesis 26.</margin> It is also written again: *And he called them seven [Sceiuea],* therefore the name of the city is **Beerſceua** <note>Beersheba</note>: but here no mention was made of the oath which is read before, because the city itself depends on the mystery of "seven," while the place of the well depends on the mystical **Scefua**: that is, of the "oath." But so that this enigma may be more clearly open, notice that whoever girds himself for prayer betakes himself to the inner shrines of the seven oracles which open the archetype of the seven days of the world: where everything depends on the measure of **El hai**, which opens the mystery of the Sabbath. <margin>Exodus 31.</margin> Moreover, the Sabbath and the seventh day are the same, into which (I say, the seventh) as we have said, every oath is turned: as it is read: *And on the seventh day he ceased and was refreshed [or 'animated']:* from which it happens that he who <margin>1 Samuel 25.</margin> takes the name of God in an oath, swears indeed by the soul and life, as in that: *As God lives, and as your soul lives, etc.* For the name **El hai** decrees the life of your soul: through which the gift of the life of the earth is poured out into the universal choir of souls which fly out from **Edonaí**. Therefore, he who presumes to swear falsely, truly spurns and despises God **El hai**, and the seven Sephirotic lights likewise. But in what sense an oath is brought forth **badonaí**: that is, *in God*, while a vow is **ladanaí**: that is, *to God*, the things to be said below will explain: for a vow offers the example of the Great Sabbath, namely the seventh, which exists more sublimely: but an oath offers the Sabbath which is lower.

### OF CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

...the minister of the temple on the Day of Atonement <note>original: "propitiationis die"; the Yom Kippur ritual</note>, on which it was permitted to enter the Holy of Holies to obtain pardon, indulgence, and blessing—as well as those benefits sought throughout the course of the whole year—could not be admitted or enter except with this "measure" as a guide. Indeed, even Moses never approached the sight of the Most High except with **Zos** <note>Hebrew: *Zot* (זאת), meaning "this." In Kabbalistic thought, this feminine pronoun refers to the Sefirah of Malkuth or the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence that mediates between God and the world.</note> first leading him by the hand, according to that verse: *And the Lord [Tetragrammaton] called to Moses and spoke to him from the tabernacle of meeting, saying, etc.* <margin>Levit. 1.</margin> Who was it that called to Moses? It was the **small Aleph** <note>In the Hebrew text of Leviticus 1:1, the first word *Vayikra* (And He called) is traditionally written with a miniature letter Aleph, which mystical commentators interpret as a sign of humility or a specific divine attribute.</note> of the word *Vaikra* <note>Hebrew: *Vayikra* (ויקרא), "And He called."</note>: that is, "and He called," and thereafter God spoke to him. From where did the speech break forth? It broke forth from the Tabernacle of Meeting. What the Tabernacle of Meeting represents, I have already revealed. This same **Zos** is also the protectress of Israel in times of adversity, about which David declares: *If an army should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear; if war should rise against me, in Zos [this]*—that is, in her—*I am confident.* <margin>Psalm 27.</margin> <note>The original cites Psalm 36, but the quote is from Psalm 27:3.</note> This **Zos** constantly consoles Israel while remaining with them in captivity, according to that verse: *And Zos: that is, this your stature is like a green palm tree.* <margin>Cant. 7.</margin> <note>Song of Songs 7:7</note> Under her guidance, Israel earned both the Written Law and the Law handed down by mouth <note>The Oral Torah</note>, for which it is written, *Zos: that is, this is the Law, when a man dies in a tent.* <margin>Numer. 19.</margin> <note>Numbers 19:14</note>

We also attain the understanding of the Written Law through her dictate, for she exists as the mystery of the Oral Law. With her as guide, Israel inherited this land, as it is written in Numbers 34: *Zos: that is, this is the land which falls to you as a possession.* <margin>Numer. 34.</margin> She is likewise the chief of those goods by which we obtain the life of the world to come, according to that verse in Isaiah 54: *Zos, namely, this is the possession or heritage of the servants of the Lord [Tetragrammaton].* <margin>Esai. 54.</margin> Through her foresight, Israel receives gifts of every kind of good, regarding which it is said in Genesis 48: *Vezos: that is, and this is what their father spoke to them, and he blessed them.* <margin>Gen. 48.</margin> <note>Hebrew: *Vezot* (וזאת), "And this."</note> So too, by her authority, Moses made Israel a sharer in the blessing; for it is written *Vezos: that is, and this is the blessing.* This is also the measure by which Judah was made master of the kingdom, as is drawn from Deuteronomy 33: *Vezos: that is, and this [he said] to Judah.* <margin>Deuter. 33.</margin> The Most High also warns and exhorts Israel to guard and observe her, and that they should handle her cleansed of all filth, where it is said in Deuteronomy 23: *Let nothing foul or shameful appear in you, lest He turn away from you.* <margin>Deut. 23.</margin> And it is written in Deuteronomy 32: *If only they were wise, they would understand Zos: that is, this; they would look to their end [nouissimum]*—as if he had said: <margin>Deuter. 32.</margin> "If only they would draw a good understanding from the fountain of wisdom toward the measure of **Zos**, then they would eat of the fruits of the righteous one who is good, and they would look to the end." For from a spacious place, they shall draw from the river of prudence into the measure of **Zos**, which is called **A’heris**: that is, "the end" or "the future." <note>Hebrew: *Acharit* (אחרית), meaning end, future, or latter days.</note> Toward this tends that verse of Genesis 48: *Gather yourselves together, and I will tell you what will happen to you in the end of days.* <margin>Gen. 48.</margin> And that of Jeremiah 30: *There is hope for your end.* <margin>Hierem. 30.</margin> The Law hints at this same measure whenever it commemorates *uaiomar*: that is, "he said," or whatever depends on an utterance.

**EMIRA** <note>Hebrew: *Amirah* (אמירה), a saying or utterance.</note>: that is, "the word," such as *Koomar*: that is, "thus said God." For the explanation of this, note that where the Law records an utterance depending on *dibur* <note>Hebrew: *Dibur* (דיבור), speech or word.</note>: that is, "eloquence," such as *uaiedaber*: that is, "God spoke," there a measure of strength is shown, and it is the business of the Written Law. But the utterance **Emira** suggests the measure of the Kingdom, and its intention concerns the Oral Law. However, because one of these Laws offers aid to the other and they preserve each other mutually, it pleased the Most High that this very mystery should shine forth for us in the Law. Therefore, the Law everywhere declares: *And the Lord [Tetragrammaton] spoke to Moses, saying.* For "spoke," which is written at the head of the clause, shows the Written Law; but "saying," which is brought forth at the end, designates the Oral Law. Through these two—namely, "speech" [*locutionem*] and "utterance" [*dictionem*]—the Law itself is everywhere constructed and perfected, as that verse suggests: *Write for yourself these words: because through the mouth of these words I have struck a covenant with you.* <margin>Exod. 34.</margin> Thus, the covenant is established upon the Written Law when it is joined to the Law issued by the mouth. <margin>Deut. 10.</margin> Now, however, hear the sum of this mystery: the tables of the covenant are placed in the Ark, as in: *And put them in the Ark.* The Written Law, however, is explained through the Oral Law: for the temple of the Written Law is the Law brought by the mouth. <meta>This page continues the exposition on the Hebrew word "Zos" (Zot, meaning "this"), identifying it with the Sefirah of Malkuth (Kingdom) and the Oral Law. It explores the mystical relationship between the Written and Oral Laws and the various Names of God.</meta>

...I will trust. <note>Refers to the end of Psalm 27:3, "In *this* [Zot] I will trust."</note> For Adonai <note>original: "Edonai"</note> is the temple of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, often considered too sacred to pronounce.</note>, and these two Laws embrace each other like twin fawns of a gazelle. <margin>Proverbs 16</margin> And regarding him who would separate them, it is written: *And a whisperer separates the leader* <note>Proverbs 16:28; here "the leader" symbolizes the unity of the divine attributes.</note>, and he is as if he were a worshiper of no God at all. For this reason, whenever the Law records that "God spoke to Moses, saying," it points to these twin Laws together, as in the verse: *Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth.* <margin>Song of Sol. 1</margin> And when the Israelites abandoned both the written Law and that delivered by mouth [the Oral Law], <margin>Isaiah 5</margin> the Prophet rebuked them, saying: *Because they have held the Law of the God of Hosts in contempt* (that is, the written Law) *and have made the words of the Holy One of Israel void*—referring, of course, to the Law delivered by mouth. 

The sign that supports our claim—that "speaking" <note>original: "loquutionem"</note> is the measure of strength <note>associated with the attribute of Gevurah</note>, while "saying" <note>original: "dictionem"</note> is the measure of the kingdom <note>associated with the attribute of Malkuth</note>—is found here: <margin>Exodus 6</margin> *And God [Elohim] spoke to Moses, and said to him: I am the Lord [Adonai].* For there, he connects the "speaking" to the name *Elohim*, which expresses the meter of strength; but he joins the "saying" to *I am the Lord [Adonai]*, which suggests the measure of the kingdom. 

Since you now know these things, consider that this measure is called the "Law issued by mouth": for the written Law of God inhabits that Law brought by the mouth just as a spirit inhabits a tabernacle or an altar. But because all the wonders and the inner sanctuaries hidden within the written Law shine forth through the promulgated Oral Law, it is said: *When some matter of judgment is hidden from you* (that is, something deep and veiled in the written Law), <margin>Deut. 17:2</margin> it follows: *And you shall do according to the word of His mouth which they declare to you.* 

Understand, therefore, and revolve this in your mind, examining it by weighing this fact: that the Oral Law performs no flowing or dependent function except that which the written Law imparts to it; nor is any path of entry into the written Law permitted except through the Oral Law. In the same way, the name *Adonai* <note>original: "Edonai"</note> draws its blessing from nowhere else than the name *Tetragrammaton*, nor is any access to the *Tetragrammaton* found except with *Adonai* as the guide, as the things already said teach more plainly. These Laws, therefore, provide a reciprocal support to one another, and both are finally fused into one, according to that verse: <margin>Zechariah 14</margin> *The Lord is one and His name is one.* 

Now that all things regarding the measure *Zos* <note>Hebrew: *Zot* (זאת), meaning "this," representing the Shekhinah or the Sefirah Malkuth.</note>, called *Adonai*, have been explained, one point remains to be set forth—one that should not be lightly esteemed, but rather kept in the heart. For this measure, when it absorbs multiform vigor from higher sources, leads sometimes to destruction and sometimes to life. It snatches this man to the heavens and thrusts that one to the depths; it makes one faint and restores another to health, and disposes all things according to what the rectitude of judgment demands. For there, nothing is unjustly twisted, nothing is surrendered to oblivion, and no respect of persons is admitted. 

Therefore, as it draws from the higher powers, so it receives various surnames from the celestial beings: such as the name *Elohim*, suited to the meter of strength and fear, which is also called the "praetorium of the sublime." There, all created things are judged by a just judgment (with a middle line intervening) to the right and to the left, whenever the measure of the Stronger One decrees that mortals are to be scattered, cut down, or destroyed. *Adonai*, which is the storehouse of all things flowing from above, then executes the judgment of the God *Elohim* with which it is filled; for which reason it is then called by the name *Elohim*. Hence, it is accustomed to be named after the measure of the Stronger One from which the judgment arises, as if the name of the one delegating fits the one delegated. 

By this Law, the Lord *Adonai*, the God *Tetragrammaton*, the God *Elohim*, and *Shaddai* <note>original: "Sadai"</note> (that is, the Almighty) are very often named according to the exuberance of the "overflow" granted to it from a higher meter. For, drawing from the supernal fount, because it obtains the fullness of perfection and completion, it receives the surname *Shaddai* <note>The name Shaddai is often interpreted etymologically as "He who is sufficient" (*She-dai*).</note>. Under this leadership, it puts to flight the ranks of those who strike and plunder, according to that song of evil events in Psalm 91: *He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High shall abide in the shadow of Shaddai.* Furthermore, because this measure—through which we enter the name *Tetragrammaton*—represents the appearance of a vestibule, it is ordained that the name *Shaddai* be inscribed on the doorposts from the outside, <margin>Deut. 11</margin> occurring in the reading which begins: *And if you will diligently listen...* <note>Refers to the Mezuzah, the parchment scroll placed on doorposts containing the Shema and "V'haya im shamoa" (Deut. 11:13), often with the name Shaddai visible on the back.</note>

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

...clothed in a kind of fire. For when God is brought forth under the name **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai"; the name traditionally translated as "Almighty"</note>, he is colored with a cloak of burning fire; all the ranks of filthy spirits tremble with fear and are cast down in his presence, scattered at his nod, and break into the pathless caves of the earth. But when he is expressed as **Elohim**, he is covered in a burning fire stained with redness; judging the highest and the lowest alike, he consumes and weakens both the wicked and the just. From this, all those placed in the execution of judgment demand the right to judge. For this name is established (by the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> residing within it) to distribute death and life, sickness and health, punishment and healing; it casts down the high and restores them to heights. However, when he is brought forth with the voice of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"; meaning "Lord"</note>, he is dressed in the color of fire, which all created things fear and dread. Sitting upon the high throne of the kingdom like a prince and Lord, he is adorned with royal jewels. He shines forth as the most steadfast protector of the entire **Chariot** <note>original: "quadrigæ"; referring to the *Merkavah*, the divine chariot-throne in Jewish mysticism</note>, both of the heavenly and the perishable realms, through the mediation of the **Name of Forty-Two Letters**. Concerning this, it is written:
<margin>Psalm 8</margin>
> O God, our Lord, how effective is your name in all the earth, you who display your praise above the heavens!

It is necessary for the soul to be connected to the spirit, the spirit to the mind, and the mind to **Adonai** himself, so that it may be as written:
<margin>1 Samuel 25 <br/> ☞</margin>
> And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life.

Because this measure holds the last place when we descend from the highest to the lowest, and serves as the beginning when we ascend from the lowest to the highest, the final letter *He* [ה] of the name **Tetragrammaton** announces it. Since this letter constitutes a unity with the nine higher attributes, it is fitting that by its guidance, whoever attains the name **Tetragrammaton** according to their strength should strive to cling to it, according to the verse: *and to Him you shall cling.*

They leap and spring forth, and are joined and united by the way of eternity and praise into the measure called **El Chai** <note>original: "El hai"; the Living God</note>—that is, the **Foundation** <note>The Sefirah of *Yesod*</note>. From there, they turn into the cistern or well itself; I say they turn from the Foundation into the supernal pool which is called **Adonai**. For then all those heights flow together with one mind into the name **Adonai**, and because of the richness of the flood emanating into it from the nine higher <term>spheres<gloss>Sefirot</gloss></term>, the Creator is accustomed to bestow upon each individual an abundance of goods according to the limit of their nature. <meta>This page continues the exploration of the divine names and their role as conduits for the celestial flow. Having previously discussed the name Adonai as the vessel of sovereignty, Ricius now describes how human actions affect the quality of what this vessel receives and introduces the next name in the hierarchy: El Chai.</meta>

# PAUL RICIUS,

...diminish [the flow], and increase the flows of grace and mercy. But more often, on the contrary, the wicked remove the pipes and channels of grace and mercy, and they add and establish more channels of judgment. Wherefore the sharpest and cruelest things go forth into the name **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note>, whereby the age is oppressed by various hardships, the highest channels are blocked, and outward passages break out. And so, like whirlpools of filthy waters, great evils surge back; wherever there is pain and affliction, kingdoms are plundered, scepters fall, empires are overthrown, provinces are overwhelmed, armies are routed, the most brutal captivities and slaughters emerge, fevers, sores, hunger, plague, sorrow, weeping, desolation, innumerable diseases, unexpected deaths, frequent funerals—finally, all things pitiable and lethal come forth. Conclude, therefore, that **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note> undergoes such an appellation as that which is carried into him from within and without, whether good or evil, according to that saying: "the tree of the knowledge of good and evil." For if a drawing is led out from the side of grace, the surname "good" is bestowed upon him; if from the side of <margin>1 Samuel 16 <note>original: "1. Regum 16." In the older Latin Bible, 1 and 2 Samuel are titled 1 and 2 Kings.</note></margin> judgment—judgment, I say, which is drawn from internal ranks—again he is called good, as that passage hints: "and he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes and goodness of appearance." But if judgment should emanate from external troops, that will be the worst evil and a depraved disposition. Consider this, however: as often as the name **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note> exists from the side of grace, or the judgment of those who flow into him from within, he receives the name "good," into whose mystery we speak: "Blessed be the Judge of Truth," and according to this, the ancients established a blessing over the slain: "who art good and impartest good" <note>Ricius is referencing Jewish liturgical blessings. "Blessed be the Judge of Truth" (Baruch Dayan HaEmet) is said upon hearing bad news or a death, while "Who is good and does good" (HaTov veHaMeitiv) is said for good news.</note>. But if he should bring forth judgment from those living outside, it is then called an evil disposition. But if, otherwise, he absorbs the spirit of grace and mercies, then all things of the age are most richly nourished by mercy and grace, as is perceived from that: "Because to the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Name of God, YHWH</note> our God, the **Elohim**, belong mercies and propitiations." These things are therefore to be weighed in the balance and stored in a closed heart, lest the liquid flow away despised. May the Most High, therefore, with ineffable piety and the amplitude and munificence of His graces, impart to us the teaching of this learning, and show the path of truth, through which we may approach His most holy name, perform things pleasing to Him, and deserve the life of the world to come, Amen.

->MY SOUL HAS THIRSTED FOR GOD THE **ELOHIM**,<-
->*and for the living God **El**. When shall I come and visit*<-

The SECOND (according to the grades of the heights) among the holy words is the name **El Chai** <note>original: "El hai"</note>: that is, called the "Living God." For this name, holding the last place among the nine heights—which we call **Sephirot** <note>original: "sphiros"; the ten emanations or "spheres" through which the Divine manifests in Kabbalistic thought</note> and mirrors—draws grace and life from all the higher ones, and pours and transfers it into **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"; corresponding to the Sephirah *Malkhut* or Kingdom</note>, as can be learned from the things already tasted. Therefore, insofar as it receives the dimension of grace itself, it is called **El**; but because it absorbs life from there, it is called **Living** <note>Latin: "vivus"</note>. Since these two adhere to one another, both are usually called the **Living God**. And when it pours this vigor of life into the measure of **Adonai**, he himself is named the "Land of Life," **Adonai**. For, gathering life into himself from the highest things, he imparts the gift of most abundant life no less to the angelic and heavenly choirs than to the multitude of the whole circle of the lands, according to that: "Let the earth bring <margin>Genesis 1</margin> forth a living soul according to its kind." For this series of letters, according to the mystery of wisdom, designates the soul of every moving thing—namely, of creeping things on the dry land, of fish in the sea, of cattle, of beasts, of birds—and demonstrates the animal and vital soul of the human race, the soul of the angels, and the forces of the whole heaven and the stars according to each of their kinds; and it announces the supernal soul and mind sitting beside man.

Concerning which the elders hand down: "Let the earth bring forth a living soul according to its kind," <margin>☞</margin> saying: This is the soul of the **Messiah** <note>original: "Masie"</note>, truly a thing to be wondered at and powerful to one who contemplates these things...

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

<margin>Psalm 42 <note>original: "Psalm 41." Ricius uses the Vulgate numbering.</note></margin>
<margin>Joshua 3</margin>
<margin>Deuteronomy 4</margin>
<margin>Numbers 14</margin>
...are the utterances; as for the opinions, that which the literal text brings forth supports this, each in its own kind: that is, whatever kind it may be—heavenly, intermediate, or perishable—and the soul of the Messiah. Yet let not the followers of philosophy rebuke me if I also say that an **angel** is a participant in a soul; for no created thing (among the living, I should add) is admitted that a soul of life, according to its own kind, does not inhabit. For each thing claims as much of a soul for itself as the limits of its matter require. Therefore, the entire choir of souls, both the celestial and the falling, draws life from the **Earth of Life** <note>A Kabbalistic term for the final Sefirah, Malchut, which receives the divine flow.</note> which is **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note>, led by **the Living God** <note>original: "El haï"</note>. That is to say, by the **Living God**, who from the source of life—with the **Tree of Life** <note>The central axis of the Sefirotic system.</note> intervening—transfers life into the name **Adonai**. Because this name, by the will of the **Living God**, provides the gifts of living to all animate beings, certain prayers were established at the beginning of the year <note>Refers to Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year.</note>: *Be mindful of us for life*, where the intention is directed toward the **Living God** and the **Shield** <note>original: "magen"</note>—that is, the protector. Wherefore, consider that the life of the future age, from the longed-for measure of the **Living God**, ought to be applied and drawn by prayers to the meter of **Adonai**. Longing for this, David said: *My soul thirsted for God, for the powerful God, for the Living God* <note>original: "ad Deum Elohím, ad Deum El uiuum"</note>. Through the connection of these names, Israel attains all its vows and puts its enemies to flight; no enemy is so fierce or strong that he does not lose his strength in conflict with them. Regarding this, Joshua declared: *By this you shall know that the Living God dwells among you, and He shall make you heirs of your enemies.*

Since, therefore, we must join the heights and the spheres to the measure of **Adonai**, it is the custom to say in the blessing that constantly follows the morning Psalms: *You who choose songs of praise, King, the Living God of the ages.* Therefore, whoever desires to become a possessor of life or any other benefit should lift his mind to the dimension of the **Living God** <note>original: "El haï"</note>. For he who remains pure and cleaves to the name **Adonai** shall be joined to the **Living God** himself according to His will; as it is written: *You who cleave to the Lord your God* <note>original: "Deo Tetragrammaton"</note>*, to your God* <note>original: "Elohím" </note>*, are all alive today.*

Sometimes this dimension is also called the **Living God** <note>original: "Elohím haïm"</note>, as it is said: *He is the Living God and the King of the world.* And when the measure of the **Living God** <note>original: "El haï"</note> is noted by the meter of **Adonai** under the word **God** <note>original: "Elohím"</note> and is filled with life, we read that both are then called the **Living God** <note>original: "Elohím haïm"</note>. From this source, through channels and pipes, the race of living beings drinks in the faculty of living most abundantly. When Moses raised himself toward heaven, he forged the meter of the **Living God** into the measure of **Adonai**, as is drawn from that passage: *Let the power of Adonai be magnified now, I beseech you.* For the power of **Adonai** suggests the mystery of life which the **Living God** transmits; because a little further down it is written: *I have pardoned according to your word, but as I live...* From this it became known to us that Moses drew life into the dimension of **Adonai**. The saying of the elders supports this: *The Holiest One said to Moses, "You have given me life by your utterances."* And unless Moses had done so, destruction would soon have rushed upon everyone. Therefore, as long as this overflowing meter brought forth fruit, and the fruit of fruit, Israel remained alive; but when these were at last spent, they paid the penalties for their crime. Therefore, he who is worthy to attain this mystery will easily be able to perceive how much vigor exists in the drawing of the **Living God** into the dimension of **Adonai**.

However, it is pronounced as the **Living God** <note>original: "Elohím haïm"</note>, although the meter of **Adonai** is similarly named; because the measure of the **Living God** imparts life to no one except according to the requirement of just judgment. For no favoritism of persons is prescribed there, as if he had spoken of judgment together with the dimension of **Life** <note>original: "haïm"</note>. For this reason, because the Day of Judgment is determined at the head of the year <note>Rosh Hashanah</note>, we likewise commemorate these measures together with the **Shield** <note>original: "magen"</note>—that is, the protector—in the first blessing, saying: *Remember us for life, King who delights in life, write us in the book of life, for your sake, O Living God, the Living God, King, Helper, Savior, and Protector.* <note>This is a translation of the "Zochrenu" and "Melech Ozer" additions to the Amidah prayer during the Ten Days of Repentance.</note>

This dimension of the **Living God** is also frequently read as <insert>אל שדי</insert> **God Almighty** <note>original: "El Sadai"</note>: that is, the God who is sufficient. For through Him, vigor, perfection, life, inundation, and every superior flow drop sufficiently into the name **Adonai**, as the elders announce in the book of **Hagigah** <note>original: "hegiga"; refers to the Talmudic tractate *Chagigah*.</note>. **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai"</note>—for by this name the Maker of things said "Enough!" <note>The Hebrew name Shaddai is traditionally interpreted as "She-dai," meaning "He who [said] enough."</note> to His world. Although it might seem to sound there as if the world were extending itself further and wider until its own Architect imposed a limit upon it, the interior sense is that the measure of the **Living God**...

# THE WORKS OF PAULUS RICIUS

**Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai"</note> provides nourishment to every one of the created beings, until they all alike cry out, "Enough, enough!" <note>The name *Shaddai* is traditionally interpreted through the Hebrew word *dai*, meaning "enough" or "sufficient."</note> And when the measure of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note> is filled with the power of **El Shaddai**, it then demands for itself this title of **El Shaddai** (as the previous explanations make clear). Thus, the individual goods flowing from the higher realms proceed into the name of **Adonai** through the measure of **El Shaddai**,
<margin>Genesis 28</margin>
as that verse sounds: *And may El Shaddai*—that is, the God who is sufficient or almighty—*bless you.*

This dimension also says "Enough" so that pains and hardships may not afflict one further by becoming more bitter in the future; for this reason, Jacob prayed in the name of **El Shaddai**. This measure also sometimes earns the title: **The Fountain of Living Waters** <note>original: "Meqôr mayim ḥayyim"</note>, because from a more sublime pleasure—originating from the **Crown** <note>The first Sefirah, Keter.</note> which is called "The Infinite"—waters of this kind break forth, from which the life of all living things is derived. But because there are also pools of wicked waters, dead and foul waters, and those called the impetuous floods of rushing waves and foreign cisterns—which gush and leap forth, producing shameful whirlpools of water—the Most High, in his fury, rebuked and scolded Israel, saying: *My people have committed two evils; they have abandoned me, the*
<margin>Jeremiah 2</margin>
*fountain of living waters, to dig for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water.* And it is written: *The gathering or the hope of Israel is the Lord* **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>; *all who abandon you shall be put to shame,* etc. It is also written: *Because they have abandoned the fountain of living*
<margin>Jeremiah 7, Jeremiah 17</margin>
*waters, the Lord Tetragrammaton.* There is, therefore, a manifold reason why this measure may be called the fountain of living waters: first, because it migrates from that same supernal pleasure, through which all things exercising the act of living acquire their permanence by the abundance of life; second, because just as a living animal moves here and there by performing various tasks, so these flowing waters run diligently everywhere to irrigate fields, meadows, vineyards, and orchards, and to provide for every benefit of human affairs. Furthermore, for anyone searching for that life which is true in the sight of the Most High, this kind of water opens a shining path in the manner of a river, which leads the one following its peaks back to its very origin, according to that verse: *From Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth* (that is: **From the gift to the rivers of God, and from the rivers of God to the heights**).
<margin>Numbers 21, Deuteronomy 30</margin>
And according to this sentiment, one must hear what the Law warns: *See, I have placed before your face life and good itself, and death and evil itself.* For he who is bound to the dimension of **El Chai** <note>The Living God.</note> attains life and good; but he who departs far from it and moves backward encounters evil and destruction. For all things are balanced against one another in a diverse series, as that verse hints: *God* **Elohim** *made even this to correspond to that.*
<margin>Ecclesiastes 7</margin>
This same measure is also called **Yesod** <note>original: "Iessod"</note>: that is, the **Foundation**. For just as a foundation supports a house that has been built, so the expression of **Adonai** is supported by the measure of **Yesod**, which is called **El Chai**. From this, in the book *Chagigah* <note>original: "hegiga," a volume of the Talmud dealing with festival offerings and mystical themes.</note> (that is, of the solemnities), the sages declare: *A single column supports the world, whose name is* **Tzadik** <note>original: "zadic"</note> (that is, the **Righteous One**),
<margin>Proverbs 10</margin>
as it is said: *The Righteous One is the foundation of the world.* However, one must consider that not every foundation is seen with the same Law built upon it. For one kind of foundation is cast deeper, while the construction itself is lower; another occupies the middle of the building; and another, being the base, constitutes a higher structure, according to the triple machine—the upper, middle, and lower—upon which that rests: the lower, the second, and the third. That is, the higher face for the higher, the middle for the middle, and the lower for the lower, the mystery of which is **Holem, Shurek, and Hirik** <note>These are the Hebrew vowel points for 'o', 'u', and 'i'. In Kabbalistic symbolism, *Holem* (above the letter) represents the upper world, *Shurek* (in the middle) the intermediate, and *Hirik* (below) the lower world.</note>. This also agrees with that saying of the ancients: *Consider,* they say, *that the dimension of the Most High is not like the measure of flesh and blood.* For in the latter, the mass looms above while the support and base stand below; but the Most High resides in the sublime, while the weight hangs downward, as it is written: *Thus says the Lord Tetragrammaton, the high and lofty one.* Therefore, the foundation called **El Chai** carries the measure of **Adonai** like a constructed house. For this reason, **Adonai** always burns with a continuous desire to fly toward the measure of **El Chai**, nor is this sense heard with a wavering mind...

He must be heard, since even fleeting things perceived by the senses suggest this very principle by way of a likeness. To this [measure] is also everywhere given the surname **ZADIC** <note>Hebrew: *Tzadik*, meaning "The Righteous" or "The Just."</note>: that is, the **Just**, because this dimension supports all the lower things.

For this, it is read: *And the righteous is the foundation of the world.* He is called "Just," however, because he pours every kind of inundation and goodness into the name of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai"</note>. But examine and listen here to one thing worthy of commemoration: there are three names: **The Just**, **Justice**, and **Justification**. **The Just** indeed corresponds to the measure of the **Living God** <note>original: "Ethai," likely a variant or typo for "El Chai"</note>; **Justice** corresponds to **Adonai**; and when the Just imparts his own gift to the latter, it has pleased [the authorities] to call this kind of inundation and dependency **Justification**. For these three terms coincide into one: **The Just** so that he may provide; **Justice** so that she may receive; and **Justification** joins them both. Turn the sharp edge of your mind to this again: when the Just distributes the gifts of good things to Justice, she herself is customarily called "The Land of Life." But if the pipes and channels of this Just one are withdrawn, so that they do not flow down into the measure of Justice, then she abounds with death-bearing passages, and administers the destruction, calamities, and complexities of the age. <margin>Isaiah 60</margin>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Sefirah of Yesod (the Foundation), referred to here as "The Righteous" (Zadic/Tzadik), and its role as the channel connecting the higher divine realms to the lower world (the Temple of Adonai/Malkuth). # PAUL RICIUS,

Every person is judged according to the abundance of their actions. For if anyone performs a single meritorious deed, they dispose both themselves and the world toward the merit of grace; but if they commit a crime, they are made miserable and pull the whole world into the guilt of their sin. Thus, you see the way in which a single column, called **Zadic** <note>Hebrew: *Tzadik*, meaning "The Righteous One." In Kabbalah, this corresponds to the Sefirah of Yesod.</note>, sustains the mass of the entire age. For this reason it is written: *And the Righteous: that is, the righteous is the foundation of the world,* etc. This measure is everywhere given the surname of "Good," as in the verse: *Tell the righteous that it is good.* For the influences that flow down from the heavenly oracles—and indeed those which burst forth from the measure of strength and fear into this unshakable machine—if they pass through the temple of the righteous, they all turn toward the good and the benefit of the matter. Therefore, the Sages rightly declare that nothing evil is sent down from the heavens. 

As for what is read, that "evil descends from the Lord **Tetragrammaton**" <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, this must be understood as coming from the storehouses existing outside the spherical fabric. Indeed, many treasuries of scourges exist there, which it has pleased men to call "evils." These frequently invade the temple of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonai," referring to the Sefirah of Malkuth or the physical world.</note> and rush into the late age of mortals, regarding whose figure it is written: *For evil came down...*
<margin>Micah 1</margin>
*...from the Lord [Adonai].* It is as if evil wishes to descend, not indeed *from* God, but from the things which are *with* God. Therefore, it is not read: "It descends *from* the Lord" <note>original Latin: "me Edonai," representing the Hebrew "me-YHVH"</note>, which sounds as if it were from God's essence, but...
<margin>Micah 1</margin>
...*from with* the Lord <note>original Latin: "mees Edonai," representing the Hebrew "me-et Adonai," implying from a place near or under God’s authority rather than His essence.</note>. This also proceeds to what the Law itself explains in the Work of the Beginning: *And God saw that it was good,* etc. And at the end of the work it is written: 
<margin>Genesis 1:b</margin>
*Behold, it was very good,* etc. Here, in the volume of **Genesis Rabbah** <note>original: "Berescis raba," a collection of ancient Jewish explanations (Midrash) on the book of Genesis.</note>, the ancient sages explain: *Very good:* that is, "death." From this, understand that even death—which the measure of the righteous follows—is considered "good" and "life." For the righteous (they say), even after they have fallen asleep, are counted among the assembly of the living. 

To this is also added the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. For since **Adonai**, which is called the Tree of the Knowledge of Sacred Things, draws fullness from the Oracle of Good, whatever dwells among beings (no less destruction than life) we decree to be turned into good. But if, through the dimension of the righteous, the channels do not flow like pipes into the house of justice or the Tree of Knowledge, then that same Temple of Adonai performs the office of the outer things (which are called the worst plagues). From there, He crushes the age with the horrific sound of storms, laying it waste and dissipating it, just as the equal reckoning of judgment demands. Wherefore, we are convinced that the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil is brought forth by a measure of this kind. Hence, concerning...
<margin>Exodus 2</margin>
...Moses, since he stood dedicated to this Oracle of Good, the Law reports: *And she saw him: because he was good.* From this, as they say: *And the house shone brightly all around.* 

Nor should it escape you that the Temple of Adonai is most often called **Elohim**. When it intended the fabric of the universe, it consulted the measure of "Good," by which it fashioned and completed all things according to their forms with exactness. Regarding this sense, it is written in the Work of the Beginning: *And Elohim saw that it was good.* This dimension is also sometimes expressed as **Sechel Tob** <note>Hebrew: *Sekhel Tov*.</note>: 
<margin>Genesis 1</margin>
that is, **Good Intellect**, etc. For by its help, we are brought to a bright mirror for intuition, and the path is opened through which we attain wisdom from the truth of the name **Tetragrammaton**. To the persistent cultivator of the Law and the commandments, this measure—namely, Good Intellect—offers itself as a companion, as is evident from that verse: 
<margin>Psalm 110</margin>
*The fear of the Lord [Tetragrammaton] is the beginning of wisdom; a good intellect is to all...*
<margin>Proverbs 16</margin>
*...who do them.* Great indeed is the mystery of this, namely, where it is written: *He who understands a matter (or the Word) finds good.* Thus, when David had presented himself to such a measure, he was accustomed to say: **Le David maskil** <note>Hebrew: *Le-David Maskil*, a title for several Psalms meaning "A Maskil [contemplative poem/instruction] of David."</note>: that is, *To David...* 
<margin>Title</margin>
*...the understanding.* Finally, every utterance referring to intelligence is converted into that same... 
<margin>Psalm 32</margin>
...oracle. And he who knows the symbolic sense of grace will easily be able to see what it means that "Good Intellect gives grace." However, "understanding" and "prudent" differ: 
<margin>Proverbs 13</margin>
for the prudent man drinks from the fountain of prudence, but the understanding man feeds on the first and last "Good." This dimension is read again by the name **Salom** <note>Hebrew: *Shalom*.</note>: that is, **Peace**. For when (as the preceding things reveal) the Israelites are burdened with probity and rectitude, the Temple of Adonai overflows with all the riches of rewards. But doing the contrary, they suffer the contrary; but if they return again to repentance, the... <note>catchword: "righteous"</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Sefirah of Yesod (the Foundation), here characterized as the "Oracle of Peace" and the bridge between the lower world (the Temple of Adonai) and the higher divine essence (the Tetragrammaton).
