### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

If any of the righteous should reunite these things and straighten their complexities, then the oracle of peace—the good temple of **Adonai** <note>original: "Edonaï," the divine name associated with the Sefirah of Malkuth, representing the physical world or the "Temple."</note>—shows itself as an interpreter to the God **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>. It reconciles them, and having cut away every distinction, it melts them down and composes them into one. Because of this, the name Tetragrammaton is brought forth as one at that hour; and because no blessing is sent down except with this very oracle of peace as the leader, it is written:
<margin>Psalm 28</margin>
*The Tetragrammaton gives strength to his people; the Tetragrammaton will bless his people in peace.* On this point, the masters of wisdom say: We know of no vessel (they say) that encompasses every form of blessing as peace itself does, which the highest giver of all good things granted to Israel, as it is read:
<margin>Numbers 6</margin>
*May God turn his face toward you and establish peace for you.* Therefore, since peace holds the final place among the most excellent mirrors, the priestly blessing and the daily prayer always conclude by commemorating peace. For by the command of this peace, whoever desires to become a companion of the life of the world to come approaches, and by its nod, they depart.

Indeed, take note here of that mystical saying of the ancients: they say that while Moses was penetrating the upper realms, he beheld the Most High attaching crowns to the elementary letters. The Creator himself hesitated and said to Moses: "Has peace itself utterly vanished from your city?" Moses, answering, said: "What servant would have the presumption to greet the Lord with peace?" Nevertheless, the Creator said: "I would not have returned had you not offered me some help." Immediately, Moses began:
<margin>Numbers 14</margin>
"Now," he said, "let the power of the Lord **Adonai** be magnified." And a little further down it is read: "I have forgiven according to your word, but as I live," etc. <note>This refers to a midrashic tradition where God expects Moses to greet Him with "Peace," and Moses later invokes God's mercy to stay His hand from destroying the Israelites.</note> It is as if He wished to say: "You have given me life by your words." These are their teachings. For such a measure of peace, while it inhabits the "Eden" of Adonai, pours the virtue of living into that very place. How valid and powerful, then, is the strength of peace, which even assists the heavenly beings, as the scriptures show: *He who makes peace in his high places.* Thus, a man who is a faithful guardian of the Law or the commandments reconciles the heavenly ranks (if I may put it that way) through peace. Upon this rests that verse:
<margin>Isaiah 27</margin>
*Or let him take hold of my strength, let him make peace with me; let him make peace with me.*

Sometimes the surname <term>זכרון</term> **Zikoron** <note>Hebrew: *Zichron*, meaning "Remembrance" or "Memorial."</note> is bestowed upon this place; that is, "Remembrance." For there, whatever good lies hidden in the individual works of the world is restored to memory. According to the nature of this remembrance, all things undergo judgment by the Law. This is why the Law itself calls the beginning of the year "a day of remembrance" or "a memorial day." For the beginning of the year typologically
<margin>Leviticus 23</margin>
refers to the temple of **Adonai**. "Remembrance," however, opens the oracle of **El Hai** <note>Hebrew: *El Chai*, meaning "The Living God," associated with the Sefirah of Yesod.</note>. Since, therefore, the hidden order of wisdom has decreed that the execution of judgment upon us takes place at the beginnings of the year, and that all the deeds of mortals be offered to the sight of **Adonai** for examination, we then turn our prayers toward the measure of **El Hai**, praying: "Remember us for life, O King who delights in life, and write us in the book of life for your sake, **Elohim** of life, **El Hai** of life."

But because this dimension brings back to memory whatever things are covered by oblivion, we fulfill our prayer at the beginning of the year by saying: "You who remember the covenant." For that measure shows the entrance to both the covenant and remembrance. From this, David also breathed toward this oracle:
<margin>Psalm 38</margin>
"A Psalm," he said, "by David, for remembrance." The same is said:
<margin>Numbers 5</margin>
"A remembrance of offering, and an offering of remembrance, which calls iniquities to mind." For from that place, the punishment of the adulterous woman is repaid, since this is the "offering of jealousy." And this jealousy, I say, inhabits this place, as it is read:
<margin>2 Kings 19</margin>
"The jealousy of the Tetragrammaton of hosts does this." Yet let it not be unknown that the same thing is implied by "remembrances" and "re-visitations." But re-visitations are in the hand of **Adonai**, while remembrances are acted out under the leadership of **El Hai**. Therefore, since the entire machine of the world is led to the summit of perfection by the joining of these twin measures, the Maker of the world commanded the day of the Sabbath in a two-fold way after their example:
<margin>Exodus 20</margin>
through <term>זכור</term> **Zochor** <note>Hebrew: *Zachor*, meaning "Remember."</note>, that is, "remember," as a type for the day and the oracle of **El Hai**; and
<margin>Deuteronomy 5</margin>
through <term>שמור</term> **Samor** <note>Hebrew: *Shamor*, meaning "Keep" or "Observe."</note>, that is, "keep" (or "observe"), as the mystery of the night and the temple of **Adonai**. For the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> puts forth two such words. For the sake of this doctrine, notice that the three higher lights—I mean the Crown, Wisdom, and Prudence <note>The three highest Sefirot: Keter, Chokmah, and Binah.</note>—consist in unity. # ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

If Israel were to observe exactly two Sabbaths, the bond of their captivity would be immediately dissolved. But if you ask doubtingly: Why then, on the day that wise man <note>Likely referring to a specific Talmudic sage or the collective "ideal" sage.</note> joined prayer to redemption, was Israel not released from the prison of exile? You must know that a single man can only bind as much as a single individual's portion requires; for if a unified Israel were to rightly compose these twin dimensions, the greatest liberty of all would immediately follow. 

It should not be ignored that the measure of **Edonai** <note>original: *Edonai*, a variant of *Adonai* (Lord), referring here to the Sefirah of Malkhut (Kingdom/Presence).</note> is also sometimes called the Redeemer, namely when redemption itself clings to it, and when it is sent from the oracle of **El hai** <note>original: *El hai* (El Chai), "The Living God," referring to the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation).</note> to protect and rescue the righteous from the punishments of the wicked and the whirlwind of scourges. Likewise, it is then brought forth as the **Redeeming Angel** <term>מלאך הגואל</term> <note>original: *Malakh ha-Goel*.</note>, which Jacob expressed saying: *The Angel himself who redeemed me from all evil*, etc. <margin>Genesis 48.</margin> for it is right for it to be called by an elegant name. 

But so that this may shine more clearly in the mind, turn your ears here. The measure of the **Jubilee** <note>The Jubilee occurs every fifty years; in Kabbalah, it is associated with the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding).</note>, occupying the higher seventh [rank], stands as the oracle of the highest redemption and liberty; through it, the measure of **El hai** obtains the power of life and rescue. From Egypt, by the command of the same Jubilee (with El hai interceding), Israel went out free; upon which this rests: <margin>Exodus 13.</margin> they went up **vahemisim** <note>A mystical reading of the Hebrew *hamushim*.</note> from the land of Egypt. For it should not be read as *vahamushim*, which sounds like "armed," but as *Vahemisim*, which suggests "fifty," as it is <margin>Leviticus 25.</margin> written: *The Jubilee itself is the vahemisim year*, that is, the fiftieth. It is read again: *And redemption is made for him, and he shall go out in the Jubilee*; and further: *And in all the land of your possession, grant redemption to the land.* Finally, the sum comprising all these is: *And in the year of this jubilee you shall return, every man to his own possession.* <margin>Leviticus 25.</margin> 

Therefore, the Sabbath representing the dimension of **El hai** is the lower seventh; but the Jubilee is the higher seventh. But we complete the Jubilee in seven Sabbaths of years, and the Sabbath in six days and into the seventh Sabbath, namely the day. As to why the Jubilee is counted as the beginning of the eighth measure, the treatise on the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> pronounced as **Elohim** <note>The name Elohim is often associated with the Sefirah of Binah in this context.</note> explains this; for it decrees a high mystery (as you shall hear). Nor should it escape you that the Jubilee and the life of the world to come are called the **Great Sabbath**, because it occupies the higher seventh order. While **El hai** is the lower seventh Sabbath, to which the shrine of **Prudence** <note>The Sefirah of Binah (Understanding).</note> bestows all kinds of wealth and most munificently proffers the gifts of immense liberty and life. 

Thus, if you desire to make yourself a companion of life and redemption, remember to celebrate most exactly the Sabbath, which like a vestibule opens the entrance to the world to come and the Great Sabbath. To this corresponds the verse: *and you shall call the Sabbath a delight* (namely, the Sabbath which is with us) *and the holy one of the Tetragrammaton glorified* (namely, the higher seventh), where the elders declare: *and glorified by the holy God*; <margin>Isaiah 58.</margin> that is, the **Day of Atonement**. For although all atonement leaps forth from the Jubilee, through it forgiveness migrates into the temple of **Edonai**. 

It is worth knowing that although (as it pleased the greater sages) it is clear to no one what the Sabbath is for us, yet the reward of the Sabbath of the Prophets has become known: for it is some excellent good, a light hidden from the six days of the beginning, into which no creature deserves to fix its own gaze. Therefore, be watchful not to pass over the triple festive refreshment of the Sabbath, which presents the type of union and the connection of our Sabbath with the Great Sabbath; for by this triple refreshment on the Sabbath day, the observer is deemed to perform the union of the Most High name, according to that mystic saying: <margin>Zachariah 14.</margin> *God is one and his name is one*; namely in the three and seven. Moreover, from the three distresses of **Gog and Magog** <note>The apocalyptic war preceding the Messianic age.</note> he shall be deservedly rescued. One of these Sabbath feasts concerns the name **Edonai**, which on that day assumes a bond with higher things. The second regards the name **Tetragrammaton**. The third turns toward the oracle of **Prudence**, which remains joined to the more sublime shrine of **Eheie** <note>original: *Eheie* (Ehyeh), "I AM," the divine name associated with Keter (Crown).</note>, for which this is brought forth: <margin>Isaiah 58. Genesis 2.</margin> *And you shall call the Sabbath a delight*, etc. and *A river went out from pleasure to water the garden*, etc. For pleasure, the river, and the garden announce the highest bond of union; wherefore, by observing this triple festive refreshment, you cluster the ten **sephirotic lights** <note>original: *sphiristica lumina*, the ten emanations of God.</note> into one...

->**OF PAULUS RICIUS,**<-

is placed, beside the temples of **Edonai** <note>original: *Edonai*, a common Renaissance Latin transliteration of *Adonai* (Lord), representing the Sefirah of *Malkhut*.</note>, **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, and **Eheie** <note>original: *Eheie* (Ehyeh), "I Am," the name associated with the highest Sefirah, *Keter*.</note>: finally, the entire **Sefirotic** <note>original: *sphiristicus*, referring to the *Sefirot*, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah.</note> order will be forged together (through the mediation of the Sabbath, or the measure of **El hai** <note>original: *El hai* (El Chai), "The Living God," associated with the Sefirah of *Yesod*.</note>). This same oracle is **El hai**. **Beris** <term>ברית</term> <note>original: *Beris* (Berit).</note>: that is, "covenant," is written in the Law; for every expression of the law that sounds like "covenant" hints at one of the three Sefirotic lights, namely **El hai**, **Edonai**, and **Binah**: that is, **Prudence** <note>In this context, *Prudentia* is the standard Latin translation for the Sefirah *Binah* (Understanding).</note>. But the covenant of Prudence is the covenant of the mouth, the covenant of the tongue, and the covenant of labors; for it is written: *For according to the mouth of these words I have made a covenant with you.* <note>Referencing Exodus 34:27.</note> Truly, the covenant of **El hai** is called the covenant of peace, the covenant of the Sabbath, and the covenant of the bow <note>The rainbow of Noah.</note>. The Creator of the world also instituted for us the covenant of circumcision, so that through it, we might be made sharers with **El hai**. But the covenant of **Edonai** concerns the covenant of the Law, which stands joined between **El hai** and the covenant of Prudence. And since the temple of **Edonai** clings to the measures of **El hai** and Prudence, it adapts the surname of "covenant" to itself, according to the riddle of the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the outflow. The same is revealed by the showing of circumcision, as the tradition of the wise states: *If one has circumcised and has not uncovered the crown of the circumcised member, the circumcision itself shall be reckoned as nothing* <note>A reference to the ritual of *Priah*, or uncovering the glans, essential for a valid Jewish circumcision.</note>; for the circumcision of the member and the showing of the crown represents the hidden part of **Edonai**. When the showing is lacking, it will be judged that the first Sefirotic oracle—through which one enters into the **Tetragrammaton**—is missing. This dimension is also pronounced:

**Oos** <term>אות</term> <note>original: *Oos* (Ot).</note>: that is, a "sign," because from there wonders and signs are renewed in the world. This is why, surely, at the departure from Egypt, when redemption was joined to prayer, so many portents and prodigies shone forth; with which that passage accords: *And God (Elohim) saw (or looked upon) the children of Israel, and Elohim knew them.* <margin>Exodus 2.</margin> As well as this: *And I remembered my covenant.* Furthermore, the Sabbath (which refers to the measure of **El hai**) is called a **sign**, as it is written: *Between Me and the children of Israel, it is a sign forever.* <margin>Exodus 31.</margin> Similarly, we have learned that circumcision, which shows this very Sefirah of **El hai**, is called a sign: as in that verse: *You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, etc.* <margin>Genesis 17.</margin> In the same way, the bow is named a sign, just as it is written: *I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant, etc.* <margin>Genesis 9.</margin> Now the covenant of the bow, as we expressed before, announces the covenant of **El hai**. Therefore, whenever you hear the utterance of a "sign," understand it to be the dimension of **El hai**, which explains the mystery of remembrance; for the same **El hai** calls all the children of the world into memory. But the sign of the covenant of the Sabbath and of circumcision reconciles only the children of Israel to Him; whereas the sign of the covenant of the bow is applied to all things which the circle of the lands encompasses. Finally, as a type of this oracle, the Law itself expresses the name:

**Scefua** <term>שבועה</term> <note>original: *Scefua* (Shevuah).</note>: that is, an "oath"; for although the word referring to an oath is equal in pronunciation to the word **Sciuea** <term>שבע</term> <note>original: *Sciuea* (Sheva).</note>: that is, "seven." By this same logic, Abraham also presented to Abimelech **Seua** <margin>Genesis 21.</margin>: that is, "seven" (saying): *Receive seven ewe lambs from my hand,* therefore he called the place **Beerfceua** <note>Beersheba.</note>: that is, the "well of seven," since they both swore there. And it is written again: *And he called them "seven,"* <margin>Genesis 26.</margin> therefore the name of the city is **Beerfceua**; yet here no mention was made of the oath which was read before, because the city itself depends on the mystery of "seven," while the location of the well depends on the mystical **Scefua**: that is, the "oath."

But so that this riddle may lie open more plainly, observe that whoever prepares himself for prayer betakes himself to the inner shrines of the seven oracles which reveal the archetype of the seven days of the world: where everything depends on the measure of **El hai**, which opens the mystery of the Sabbath. Now the Sabbath and the seventh day are the same thing, into which (into the seventh, I say) every oath is directed, as we have said: <margin>Exodus 31.</margin> as it is read: *And on the seventh day he ceased and was refreshed* <note>original: *animavit*, literally "took breath" or "was souled."</note>. Thus it happens that he who takes the name of God in an oath, swears indeed by the soul and by life, as in that verse: <margin>1 Kings 25.</margin> *As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, etc.* <note>1 Samuel 25:26 in modern bibles.</note> For the name **El hai** decrees life for your soul; through which the gift of the life of the earth is diffused into the entire choir of souls which fly forth from **Edonai**. Therefore, whoever presumes to swear falsely, spurns and despises God **El hai**, and likewise the seven Sefirotic lights. But in what sense an oath is uttered **Badonai** <note>original: *badonai*, "In Adonai."</note>: that is, *in God*, whereas a vow is uttered **Ladanai** <note>original: *ladanai*, "To God,"</note>: that is, *to God*, the things to be said below will explain. For a vow presents the example of the Great Sabbath—namely the seventh which exists more sublimely—while an oath presents the Sabbath which is lower.

### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

Lower down: The Law itself brings forth this measure by the name **Hok** <term>חק</term> <note>original: *Hok*; a statute, decree, or fixed limit.</note>: for the supreme architect of all things established everything, and distinguished all by a boundary and measure hanging from His height. For only this kind of wonderful name transcends every limit without being limited itself; to which that saying applies: *He has set an end to darkness, and he himself searches out every limit.* <margin>Psalm 118 <note>In the Vulgate/Hebrew numbering, this is likely Job 28:3 or Psalm 119:96.</note></margin> It is also written: *I have seen an end to every perfection, but your commandment is exceeding broad:* as if he had said, all created things undergo a boundary except for the measure called **mizua** <term>מצוה</term> <note>original: *mizua* (Mitzvah); a commandment.</note>: that is, the commandment. In the Sefirotic circle <note>original: *sphiristica areola*; referring to the diagram or conceptual arrangement of the ten Sefirot.</note>, this is shown first from the lower to the higher, and last from the higher to the lower; indeed, it is enclosed by no boundary or end, but surrounding all things, it assigns a boundary and dimension to each. It is called a "commandment" for this reason: that by its nod, every work of the Most High is brought forth, as in that phrase: *The Law itself and the commandments:* <margin>Exodus 13 <note>Likely Exodus 24:12.</note></margin> For the Law implies the written Law, but the "commandment" suggests what is promulgated by the voice.

But when you hear in the Law **Hyka** <term>חקה</term> <note>original: *Hyka* (Chukkah); the feminine form of "statute."</note>, which sounds like a feminine statute—as it is read: *And you shall keep this institution* <note>original: *hahukakasos* (ha-chukkah ha-zot).</note>—it must be understood as the oracle of **Edonai** <note>Adonai, the divine name associated with the Sefirah of Malkhut (Kingship/Physical Reality).</note>, just as **Hok** is the oracle of **El hai** <note>El Chai (The Living God), the name associated with the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation/Generative Power).</note>. Therefore, whenever you encounter **Hok** or **Hyka** in the written Law, you should weigh that a mystery lies hidden there, which fixes a wavering and nodding thought.

The Law also very frequently calls such a sanctuary **Hari** <term>הרי</term> <note>original: *Hari* (Har); mountain.</note>: that is, a mountain. But the interpretation of "mountain" is manifold: for the oracle of **El hai** reveals Mount Zion; Mount Moriah indicates the temple of **Edonai**; but the mountain of Esau is the seductive measure of Israel. <margin>Psalm 48</margin> Moreover, Mount Zion corresponds to light, because from there that very light first shone forth, as it is written: *From Zion, the perfection of beauty, God (Elohim) appeared.* And although the temple of **Edonai** is considered the vestibule for all created things in equal measure, the overflowing of Mount Zion drips onto Mount Moriah, which inhabits the Jerusalem of **Edonai**. Through this, the name **Edonai** gains strength and speed of operation, as in that verse: <margin>Psalm 134 <note>Psalm 135:21.</note></margin> *Blessed be God from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem, etc.* That is, God dwells in Jerusalem <margin>Psalm 132</margin> through the mediation of Zion. As it is read: *Like the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountains of Zion, for there the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> commanded the blessing, etc.* Indeed, the mountains of Zion are the oracles of victory and confession <note>Ricius is likely linking Zion to the Sefirot of Netzach (Victory) and Hod (Glory/Confession).</note>, from which the good oil flows down onto Mount Zion, and from there into Jerusalem.

But the mountain of Esau stands out as a rigid wrestler on the left, according to that mystical saying: <margin>Exodus 17</margin> *The Lord has a war from generation to generation.* This mountain stands in the way of the construction of Mount Zion and the dedication of the altar on Mount Moriah, until the period or time comes when the punishment of vengeance is brought upon Edom itself. And while the mountains of Zion—I mean **Tetragrammaton Zeuaos** <note>YHWH Tzevaot (Lord of Hosts).</note> and **Elohim Zeuaos** <note>Elohim Tzevaot (God of Hosts).</note>—are covered with the garments of vengeance, we read that they are proclaimed as Saviors, according to this: <margin>Obadiah 1</margin> *And saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau.* This refers to the mountain of the shameful Esau, specifically his grandson Amalek, against whom God has a war. For the rigid translator <note>Or "adversary."</note> called **Samoël**, the Prince of Esau <note>Samael, the traditional angelic accuser and patron of Edom/Esau in Kabbalistic thought.</note>, who also strives to break the covenant of peace, is set against Mount Zion. When that mountain is judged by God (as will soon be added), there shall be the kingdom, which is the mystical enigma of Mount Moriah, the Jerusalem, and the hidden inner chamber of **Edonai**.

Here it is not permitted to pass over in silence that four troops are suggested to the empire of **Edonai** (or the kingdom of the indwelling Glory) and to Jerusalem itself, a chariot and a throne bearing the oracle of **Edonai**. These we read are named the mountains of **Erarat** <note>Ararat.</note>, as it says: <margin>Isaiah 2</margin> *And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the house of God shall be prepared on the top of the mountains* <margin>Isaiah 18</margin>—that is, at the head of the four troops of Glory. This also fits: *All you who dwell in the world and are inhabitants of the earth, when the banner of the mountains is lifted up, you shall see, etc.* For the banner of **Edonai** shall stand, to whom Moses dedicated an altar while fighting Amalek on the summit of those mountains—namely, the four living creatures <note>The *Chayot* of Ezekiel's vision.</note> over the four troops. And there are, furthermore, mountains such as those of **gebaniti** <note>Possibly *Gevinnim* (peaked/curved mountains) from Psalm 68.</note>, that is, of darkness, and many others of this kind, all surrounding Mount Moriah on the outside. Upon this it rests: <margin>Song of Songs 6</margin> *There are sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and young women without number; but my dove, my spotless one, is only one, etc.* <margin>Psalm 124</margin> It is also written: *Jerusalem is surrounded by mountains.*

<header>OF PAULUS RICIUS,</header>

...is finished, near the temples of **Adonai** <term>Edonai</term> <note>original: *Edonai*; a Latinization of the Hebrew *Adonai*, meaning "Lord," associated with the Sefirah of Malkuth (Kingdom).</note>, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God (YHVH).</note>, and **Ehyeh** <term>Eheie</term> <note>original: *Eheie*; "I Will Be," the name associated with Keter (Crown).</note>: finally, the entire **Sefirotic** <term>sphiristicus</term> <note>relating to the Sefirot, the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah.</note> order will be fused together (through the mediation of the **Sabbath**, or the measure of **El Chai** <term>El hai</term> <note>original: *El hai*; "The Living God," the name associated with the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation).</note>). This same measure is also the oracle of **El Chai**. **Berit** <term>ברית BERIS</term> <note>original: *BERIS*; Hebrew *Berit*, meaning "Covenant."</note>: that is, a "covenant," as it is written in the Law. For every expression of the Law that sounds like a "covenant" suggests one of the three Sefirotic lights: namely **El Chai**, **Adonai**, and **Binah** <term>bina</term> <note>Binah means "Understanding."</note>: that is, Prudence. But the covenant of Prudence is the covenant of the mouth, the covenant of the tongue, and the covenant of the lips: for it is written: *Because through the mouth of these words I have cut a covenant with you.* <note>Exodus 34:27.</note> The covenant of **El Chai**, however, is called the covenant of peace, the covenant of the Sabbath, and the covenant of the rainbow <note>original: *arcus*; the bow.</note>. The Creator of the world also established for us the covenant of circumcision, so that through it we might be made sharers of **El Chai**. The covenant of **Adonai**, moreover, concerns the covenant of the Law, which stands joined between **El Chai** and the covenant of Prudence: and since the temple of **Adonai** clings to the measures of **El Chai** and Prudence, it adapts for itself the nickname of "Covenant": according to the riddle of the "covenant of the tongue" and the "covenant of the member" <note>original: *effuforij*; literally "of the pouring out," referring to the male reproductive organ. Ricius is referencing a classic Kabbalistic parallel from the *Sefer Yetzirah* between the organ of speech and the organ of generation.</note>. The revelation of circumcision discloses the same, as that saying of the Sages brings forth: *If one has circumcised the foreskin of the circumcised member but has not revealed the crown of the member, the circumcision itself shall be considered as nothing:* for the circumcision and the revelation of the crown of the member represents the hidden things of **Adonai**: and when the revelation is missing, the first Sefirotic oracle, through which one enters into the house of the **Tetragrammaton**, will be judged to be absent. This dimension is also announced as:
**Ot** <term>אות Oos</term> <note>original: *Oos*; Hebrew *Ot*, meaning "Sign" or "Letter."</note>: that is, a "sign," because from there wonders and signs are renewed in the world: for which reason, surely, if during the departure from Egypt—when redemption had been annexed to prayer—so many portents and prodigies shone forth, it accords with that text:
<margin>Exodus 2.</margin>
*And God <note>original: *Elohim*.</note> saw (or looked upon) the children of Israel, and God <note>original: *Elohim*.</note> knew them.*
<margin>Exodus 3 <note>Likely Exodus 2:24-25 or 6:5.</note></margin>
And also: *And I remembered my covenant.* The Sabbath is also called a sign (which the measure of **El Chai** also reflects), as it is written:
<margin>Genesis 17 <note>Actually Exodus 31:17.</note></margin>
*Between me and the children of Israel, it is a sign forever.* Similarly, we have learned that circumcision—which shows forth this very Sefirah—is called a sign: as in that text:
<margin>Genesis 9 <note>Actually Genesis 17:11.</note></margin>
*Circumcise the foreskin of your flesh, etc.* Likewise, the rainbow <note>original: *arcus*; the bow.</note> is also named a sign, just as it is written:
<margin>Genesis 9.</margin>
*I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant, etc.* The "bow of the covenant," as we expressed before, announces the covenant of **El Chai**. Therefore, whenever you hear the utterance of a "sign," understand the dimension of **El Chai**, which explains the mystery of remembrance: for the same **El Chai** calls back into memory all the children of the world. But the sign of the covenant of the Sabbath and of circumcision reconciles only the children of Israel to this; whereas the sign of the covenant of the rainbow is applied to all things that the circle of the lands encompasses. Finally, as a type of this oracle, the Law itself expresses the name
**Shavuah** <term>שבועה Scesua</term> <note>original: *Scesua*; Hebrew *Shavuah*, meaning "Oath."</note>: that is, an "oath": although the word referring to an oath is equal in pronunciation to the word **Sheva** <term>Sciuea</term> <note>original: *Sciuea*; Hebrew *Sheva*, meaning "Seven."</note>: that is, "seven": by which
<margin>Genesis 21.</margin>
reason Abraham also brought to Abimelech **Sheva** <term>Seua</term>: that is, "seven" (saying) *lambs receive from my hand*, therefore he called the place **Beersheba** <term>Beersceua</term>: that is, "the well of seven," since they both swore there.
<margin>Genesis 26.</margin>
And it is written again: *And he called them **Sheva** <term>sciuea</term>:* that is, "seven," therefore the name of the city is **Beersheba**: yet here no mention was made of an oath (which is read earlier), because the city itself hangs from the mystery of "seven," but the location of the well from the mystic **Shavuah**: that is, of the "oath." But so that this riddle may appear more clearly, notice that whoever girds himself to pray betakes himself to the inner chambers of the seven oracles which reveal the archetype of the seven days of the world: where everything hangs from the measure of **El Chai**, which opens the mystery of the Sabbath. Moreover, the Sabbath and the seventh day are the same, into which (into the seventh, I say) as we have said, every oath
<margin>Exodus 31.</margin>
is converted: as it is read: *And on the seventh day he ceased and was refreshed <note>original: *animauit*; literally "took breath" or "was souled."</note>:* whence it happens that he who takes the name of God in an oath, swears indeed by the soul and the life, as in that text:
<margin>1 Kings 25 <note>1 Samuel 25:26.</note></margin>
*As God lives, and as your soul lives, etc.* For the name **El Chai** decrees life for your soul: through which the gift of the life of the earth is diffused into the entire choir of souls that fly out from **Adonai**. Therefore, whoever presumes to swear falsely, spurns and despises God **El Chai**, and likewise the seven Sefirotic lights. But in what sense an oath is uttered **b'Adonai** <term>badonai</term> <note>original: *badonai*; "by Adonai."</note>: that is, *in* God, while a vow is **l'Adonai** <term>ladonai</term> <note>original: *ladonai*; "to Adonai."</note>: that is, *to* God, the things to be said below will explain: for a vow presents the example of the "Great Sabbath," namely of the seventh [Sefirah] which exists higher up; but an oath belongs to the Sabbath which is lower.

below: Even this measure, the Law itself brings forth under the name **Hok** <term>חק</term> <note>original: *Hok*; a Hebrew word for a "statute" or "decree," often implying a law whose reason is not immediately obvious.</note>: that is, a statute. For the supreme architect of all things established everything, and distinguished all things with a limit and measure hanging from His high [name]. <margin>Psalm 118.</margin> <note>The author likely refers to Job 28:3 in the Vulgate numbering or a similar passage.</note>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exposition of divine names and spiritual geography, moving from the concept of "statutes" to the symbolic significance of Zion, the nature of national guardian angels, and the various manifestations of divine Grace (Hesed).</meta>

Furthermore, observe: when the Israelites leave Jerusalem and Mount Zion, their feet stumble upon the mountains of darkness and among the other ranks of those living outside. For nowhere but on Mount Zion, in Jerusalem, and on Mount Moriah are the Israelites kept safely enclosed by a rampart and protected from dangers and incursions, as that passage <margin>Jeremiah 13</margin> sounds: *Give glory to God before the darkness comes, and before your feet stumble upon the mountains of darkness,* etc. However, the Most High made it known that He claimed Mount Seir as an inheritance for Esau, because that mountain exists as a place polluted by squalid and horrid briars and filth, which the hairy demons <note>original: *pilosi dæmones*; a reference to the Hebrew *Se'irim*, often translated as satyrs or goat-demons, which share a root with the name *Seir*.</note> inhabit (whom the wicked progeny of Esau worship). Indeed, Esau took for himself that demon who, being rejected among the crowd and series of demons, takes a seat near the ground. To this fits the verse: <margin>Genesis 36</margin> *These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land.* <margin>Ibid.</margin> For this reason it is written of Esau: *And he went into a land away from the face of his brother Jacob,* and the same is hinted at: *Behold, I have made you small among the nations, you are greatly despised,* etc. For other nations are ruled by more exalted leaders, as in that: <margin>Daniel 10</margin> *Behold, the prince of Javan <note>original: *Iauon*; the Hebrew name for Greece.</note> (that is, of the Greeks) comes, and the prince of the kingdom of Paras (that is, of the Persians).* The same judgment is to be made concerning the rest of the seventy nations. Thus Ishmael also appoints twelve presiding over him; Esau alone took the lowlier leaders of the demons as his inheritance. <margin>Jeremiah 40</margin> <note>The author likely refers to Obadiah 1:4.</note> And what is read of Esau—*If you exalt your nest like the eagle,* etc.—is for this reason: because he has as his prince the soul of the spheres of Mars named Samael <note>original: *Samoël*; in Kabbalah, Samael is the guardian angel of Esau/Edom and is associated with the planet Mars and severity.</note>, who imparts force and strength to those demons. However, he is by no means inscribed in the assembly of the seventy princes who always remain in their proper order. Therefore it is read: <margin>Exodus 17</margin> *The Lord has a war against Amalek* (who is the grandson of Esau) *from generation to generation.* <margin>Psalm 101</margin> <note>Psalm 102 in modern Bibles.</note> "From generation to generation" refers typologically to the same thing as: *God is my memorial from generation to generation,* etc. This same impious Prince Samael is the devil and the accuser in the heights against Israel, of whom it is read (while the time of liberty hastens): <margin>Exodus 3</margin> <note>The text likely means Obadiah 1:4 again.</note> *If you should climb into the heights like an eagle, I will bring you down from there, says God.* 

Sometimes we also call this measure **Zion** <term>צִיּוֹן</term>. <margin>Obadiah 1</margin> For Zion and Jerusalem mystically encompass **The Living God** <term>אֵל חַי</term> <note>original: *El hai*.</note> and **The Lord** <term>אֲדֹנָי</term> <note>original: *Edonai*; a variation of Adonai, associated with the Sefirah of Malkuth.</note>, to be remembered and guarded. Which is also sometimes called **Holy** <term>קֹדֶשׁ</term> <note>original: *Kodesh*.</note>, the "Whole." For whatever flows from the higher oracles is collected into this measure, from which the Lord <note>original: *Edonai*.</note> also migrates into Eden. Likewise, it is sometimes read as **Time** <term>עֵת</term> <note>original: *Es* or *Et*.</note>, as is drawn from that: <margin>Ecclesiastes 3</margin> *He made everything beautiful in its time.* For there is one time for good and another for evil, as in: *A time for giving birth, a time for dying,* etc. For when this "time" (the oracle of the Lord) adheres to the measure of the good, which is the Living God <note>original: *El hai*.</note>, it obtains the name of "good." But when it has been separated from Him, it then suggests the "Lord" to time externally; wherefore it shall also be called an "evil time." Similarly, this same Living God is promised by the surname **This** <term>זֶה</term> <note>original: *Ze*; masculine "this" in Hebrew.</note>, by which the Lord <note>original: *Edonai*.</note> is also usually called when joined to it, namely **This** <term>זֹאת</term> <note>original: *Zos* or *Zot*; feminine "this" in Hebrew.</note>. 

Such an oracle is also brought forth as **The Mighty One** <term>אִישׁ</term> <note>The OCR says "Euir" and links it to Jacob. This likely refers to *Abir Yaakov* (אֲבִיר יַעֲקֹב), the Mighty One of Jacob. *Euir* is a transliteration variant of *Abir*.</note>, that is, the **Mighty One of Jacob**. For from prudence the hawk is strengthened for flight, according to the mystery of the greater and lesser Sabbath. He is called the Mighty One of Jacob, not the Mighty One of Isaac or Abraham, because a certain spherical light shines forth from the oracle of Jacob, which is accustomed to be pronounced as the "middle line" <note>In the Sefirotic tree, Jacob/Tiferet is the central pillar, balancing Mercy (Abraham) and Severity (Isaac).</note>. Often this is also called the **Mighty One of Israel**, as is read: *Therefore says the Lord God of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel.* 

It is also very often expressed by the surname **Grace** <term>חֶסֶד</term> <note>original: *Hesed*; specifically "lower grace" in this context.</note>. For grace is tripartite. The first indeed, bursting forth from the higher fountain, is called the more sublime Grace, in which no judgment is mixed, but it reflects thanks on all sides with mercies; this is usually called "the good graces." <margin>2 Samuel 7</margin> To this fits that verse: *And my grace shall not be taken away from him,* etc., and that: <margin>Psalm 21</margin> <note>Psalm 22 in modern Bibles.</note> *Because the king trusts in God, in the mercy of the Most High he shall not be moved.* Another is the grace of the world, namely the grace of Abraham, as is read: <margin>Micah 7</margin> *Give truth to Jacob, and grace to Abraham,* etc. Since indeed the "fear of Isaac" (that is, the measure of judgment) sometimes brings itself to the grace of Abraham and opposes it, as it is written: <margin>Habakkuk 2</margin> <note>Reference to Habakkuk 3:4.</note> *And there was the hiding of his strength.* And as is drawn from that: <margin>Exodus 15</margin> *Your right hand has crushed the enemy,* etc. Therefore the grace of Abraham is by no means asserted to be pure, but rather complicated by judgment. The third is expressed as the faithful graces of David, namely the graces of the oracle of the Living God <note>original: *El hai*.</note>, which from the good graces and the graces...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of spiritual dimensions, focusing on the movement of divine influence from the higher Sephirot (divine emanations) down toward the earthly realm, specifically through the "measure" or Sephirah known as El Hai (the Living God, associated with Yesod) and its relationship to the prayer of Israel and King David.</meta>

<page-num>171</page-num>
<header>ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.</header>

The graces of Abraham <note>original: *Abrae*; referring to the Sephirah of Hesed/Mercy, associated with the patriarch Abraham</note> flowing down, when they apply themselves to the dimension of David <note>The Sephirah of Malkuth/Kingdom</note>, are themselves called the "graces of David." Therefore, having heard these things, know that the measure of **El Hai** <note>Hebrew: *El Chai*, "The Living God," usually associated with the Sephirah of Yesod (Foundation)</note> is established as the purifier and examiner of the supplications to be accepted or rejected, which the oracle of **Edonai** <note>A variation of *Adonai*, meaning "My Lord"</note> puts forward. For there, with a vast multitude of gatekeepers and troops, it is decided: if it recognizes prayers as just and worthy to be admitted, they are offered to the shrine of the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter name of God (YHWH), representing the highest level of divine manifestation</term>; but the vain and futile ones are immediately thrust away from the face of the Most High. There are, however, in the temple of **El Hai**, certain **gates of tears**, which are accustomed to be opened three times a day, through which tearful prayers are by no means refused entry. 

But take note here: although the prayers of individuals may frequently be poured out in vain when separate, the prayer of a gathered multitude can never be torn away by any of the gatekeepers or prefects. What we have said regarding prayer, however, must be understood as applying when Israel dwells in the land assigned to it alone and in Jerusalem. For if the many and innumerable people should offer prayer while they are in exile, the testers or plunderers—the presiding spirits of the nations—stand by the prayer, not only of individuals but even of the multitude, so that they may utterly devour and annihilate it. For this reason, according to the institution of the elders, every prayer outside the land of Israel must be directed toward Jerusalem; otherwise, no prayer will approach the sight of the Most High. 

Gather, therefore, that **El Hai** looks upon and receives the honest and just prayer from the hand of **Edonai**: whence they are fused into one measure, **Edonai**, through which he inserts himself into all those oracles higher than himself until he reaches the place of **Prudence** <note>original: *prudentiæ*; referring to the Sephirah of Binah</note>, by which he then adheres to **Wisdom** <note>original: *sapientiæ*; referring to the Sephirah of Chokmah</note>, and to that which is given the surname **Will** <note>original: *uoluntas*; referring to the Sephirah of Kether, the Crown</note>.

<margin>Psalm 51:15</margin>
For this reason, at the beginning of a petition, we are accustomed to start with: *Lord, open my lips.* 

<margin>Psalm 19:14</margin>
At the conclusion, however, we pray: *Let the words of my mouth be pleasing in your will,* <note>The author interprets the Latin *uoluntati* (will/pleasure) as a reference to the highest Sephirah, Kether/Will</note> through which we ascend into a higher peak: that is, the **Crown** called the **Infinite**. Thus, the orderly arrangement of prayer composes the entire **sphiristic choir** <note>The choir or system of the Sephirot</note>; for prayer produces the same bond of heights through words as burnt offerings accomplish through works, as it is written: *And we shall render the calves of our lips,* etc. So much for the oracle of **El Hai**; now, however, let us prepare ourselves (having sought celestial aid) for the other divine names, which must be weighed according to their degrees of height.

We have learned to read these two names placed in the third and fourth series of heights: **אלוהים צבאות** *Elohim Zeuaos*: that is, **God of Hosts**; and **יהוה צבאות** *Edonai Zeuaos*: that is, **The Lord God of Hosts**. 

<margin>Psalm 84:8</margin>
Indeed, both are sometimes uttered as one, according to the verse: *Lord God, Elohim of hosts, hear my prayer.* 

<margin>Psalm 80:7</margin>
And sometimes each of them is mentioned separately: as it is held when it is said: *God, Elohim of hosts, convert us, let your face shine and we shall be saved.* 

<margin>Psalm 46:7</margin>
And similarly when it is read: *The Tetragrammaton of hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our strength.* We, however, place both together in that sum, because they embrace and expand one another, and both are prepared to pour the floods gushing from the higher Sephirot through the channels and pipes into the measure of **El Hai**. And they impart their matter to all things rightly and justly—one from the side of **Grace**, the other from the side of **Judgment**. For they transfer into **El Hai** both measure and judgment, and mercy and grace. Nor does the oracle of the **Tetragrammaton Zeuaos** draw into the shrine of **El Hai** a grace higher than the grace and world-wealth of Abraham; but the dimension of **Elohim Zeuaos** draws to it strength, judgment, punishment, and fear. 

Wherefore the measure of **El Hai** was deliberately called **Kol**: that is, **All**; because it embraces judgment and mercy simultaneously. Since, therefore, King David of Israel was a friend to the measure of **El Hai**—being the fourth foot of the chariot <note>In Kabbalah, the "Chariot" is supported by four "feet" or patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and David</note>—mercy, grace, and judgment accompanied him. 

<margin>1 Samuel 16:12</margin>
As is elicited from that passage: *And he himself was ruddy and beautiful to look upon,* etc. For insofar as he was **ruddy**, he is indicated to have been a most fierce fighter against the enemies of the Most High; but insofar as he was **beautiful in his eyes**, the appearance of a most pious leader of Israel is hinted at.

And when he is described as "fair to look upon," it implies that he has penetrated the secrets of the Law with the sharpness of his mind, 
<margin>Psalm 118</margin>

All the struggles of the age draw their origin from there, and the mystery of "jealousy" or "zeal" breaks forth in the same way, as it is written: *The zeal of the **Tetragrammaton Sabaoth** <note>original: *Zeuaos*; a transliteration of the Hebrew *Sabaoth*, meaning "of Hosts"</note> accomplishes this.* From this, the Prophets taste the spirit of prophecy, as in: *Thus says the God **Tetragrammaton Sabaoth**,* etc. 
<margin>Jeremiah 7</margin>
Only the monarch of the Prophets <note>Moses</note>, because he adapted himself to the higher-flying name of the **Tetragrammaton**, did not operate under the name of the **Tetragrammaton Sabaoth**. For he had no need to look through the mirrors of the "hosts" <note>the lower celestial armies or emanations</note>, since, as 
<margin>Numbers 12</margin>
the wise men teach: Moses alone enjoyed the vision of the most radiant mirror. For it is read: *I speak to him mouth to mouth.* But the assembly of other Prophets gazed upon mirrors that were not radiant, as in: *If there are prophets among you, I, the **Tetragrammaton**, make myself known to him in a mirror, and I speak to him in a dream.* 
<margin>Hosea 12</margin>
Likewise: *And in the hands of the Prophets I have used parables,* etc. For just as there are three orders established in the sacred scriptures—namely, the Law, the Prophets, and the Hagiographa <note>the "Holy Writings," the third section of the Hebrew Bible</note>—so too we find three distinct levels in the celestial heights: namely, the fountain, the river, and the pool. Moses, then, obtained the very fountain of hidden waters; hence his prophetic knowledge stood out as lucid and clear. The Prophets, however, reaching the lower springs of the river, behold the spirit of prophecy mixed with images, after the manner of a torrent, which the mud and clay of the earth have made murky and foul. But the Hagiographers, drawing from the pool, drink what is a collected and less pure mass of waters. Having summarized these things as an epitome, we propose to soon compile more exactly these two remaining names.

The name called **Elohim Sabaoth** <note>original: *Elohim Zeuaos*</note> is a "measure" <term>Measure: In this context, a *Sephirah* or divine attribute</term> lying on the left side. Taking strength and judgment from Prudence <note>the Sephirah *Binah*</note> and Fear <note>the Sephirah *Gevurah*</note>, it struggles both in the heights and in the depths, and it prepares and carries out war on behalf of the **Tetragrammaton Sabaoth**. 
<margin>Isaiah 24</margin>
To this applies: *The Lord of Hosts shall visit the host of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth,* etc. For when the Most High mandates the destruction of some nation or the desolation of a kingdom, He first punishes its prince in the celestial heights, as 
<margin>Exodus 14</margin>
happened in Pharaoh’s struggle with the Israelites. For it is read: *And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt,* etc., as if there exist six hundred chariots not from Egypt, but from the celestial realms. For the Prince of Egypt <note>the spiritual guardian or "angel" of the nation</note> was joined with **Samael** <note>a major figure in Hebrew lore, often associated with severity or the Accuser</note>; hence he added to himself six hundred chariots beyond the Egyptian ones. For just as the contention roared among mortals then, so also they clashed in the sharpest agony above.

Therefore, it was worthwhile for the name **Edonai** <note>Adonai; "My Lord"</note> to be clothed in a triple type of garment: namely, the garment of the kingdom and the beauty of the empire of Jacob; the garment of grace from the side of Abraham <note>the Sephirah *Hesed*</note>, by which he might protect Israel; and the garment of war and strength from the side of Isaac <note>the Sephirah *Gevurah*</note> to fight the Egyptian phalanxes in the celestial realms, according to that mystical passage:
<margin>Exodus 14</margin>
*Vayissa, Vayavo, Vayet* <note>original: *Vagissa, uaiano, uagyet*</note>; that is, *and he moved*, *and he came*, and *and he stretched out*, which designate the three aforementioned garments. The same dimension is also called **Hod**: that is, 
<margin>1 Chronicles 29</margin>
"splendor" (or "praise"), as is read: *To You, O God, is the magnificence and the strength, the beauty, the victory, and the splendor <note>Hod</note>.* For this measure claims this title for itself when it draws from the oracle of strength to strike down enemies, emerges as the victor of the struggle, and defends and protects the beloved of the Most High. To this it alludes: *And my splendor <note>original: *hodi*</note> was turned upon me into destruction.* Since, therefore, it administers victory and works of wonder, all confession is turned toward this point; and whatever confession is expressed by David in the Psalter is raised up toward these twin **Sephirotic** <note>original: *sphiristica*</note> lights. It also pleased the elders that the same be called "the taught of the wise": *The taught of the wise,* they say, *spread peace more abundantly in the world.* The symbolic nature of this is surely not hidden from those who labor in the doctrines of hidden things. ...just as he established another pillar called **Jachin** <note>original: יכין *Jochim*; one of the two pillars of Solomon's Temple, representing "He shall establish"</note> in the mystery of victory. For the word **Boaz** <note>original: בועז</note> sounds like "in strength," because it takes its power from fortitude and its virtue from prudence. From here gush forth the **Seraphim** <note>original: *Seraphin*</note> angels, whom we know are called "six-winged," a name that suits them well: for by the rush of their flame, they consume all those who look upon the work of the Chariot <note>original: *quadrigæ*; a reference to the *Ma'aseh Merkabah*, the mystical study of Ezekiel's vision</note> without the proper reverent worship. They busy themselves in the **Chashmal** <note>original: *Hasmel*; the mystical "amber" light or angelic fire mentioned in Ezekiel</note> and they scorch and burn those individuals who abuse the sacred names of the crown. These again (Victory and Confession, I mean) are usually called **Shechakim** <note>original: שחקים *Sehakim*; Hebrew for "clouds" or "skies," often referring to a specific level of heaven</note>: that is, the "grinding heavens" or "cloudy ones," who, as it seemed to the wise, grind and provide food for the righteous. For the **Dew of Hermon** (as you know) drips upon the mountains of **Zion**. Finally, whenever the term **Shamayim** <note>original: *Somaim*; Hebrew for "Heavens"</note> is written, it is proposed as the mystic union of the two higher names, **El** and **Elohim**—that is, of magnificence and fortitude. In the midst of these, like a firmament in the middle of the waters, stands the **Tetragrammaton** <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, pronounced as **Adonai** <note>original: *Edonai*; "Lord"</note>. But whenever the "Heavens" are written as **Shechakim**, it suggests the secret of the names **Tetragrammaton**, **Elohim**, and **Sabaoth** <note>original: *Zeuaos*; "of Hosts"</note>—namely, of victory and confession. In the middle, reconciling both, is the name **El Hai** <note>"The Living God"</note>. Therefore, from **Shamayim** into **Shechakim** a flow overflows; from **Shechakim** into **El Hai**; and from **El Hai** into **Adonai**, upon which this verse rests:
<margin>Isaiah 45</margin>
*Drop down, **Shamayim** (the Latin edition says "pour down, O heavens") from above, and let the **Shechakim** drip with justice.* These same names—**Tetragrammaton**, **Elohim Sabaoth** (namely victory and glory)—are referred to as the **Etzem HaShamayim** <note>original: עצם *Ezem hassomaim*</note>:
<margin>Exodus 24</margin>
that is, the "substance of heaven," as in: *And like the substance of heaven in its clarity.* For the substance and strength of these flows from the place called **Shamayim**. Indeed, those taught in wisdom are not ignorant that such measures of **Shamayim** are actually wisdom itself, from which all substances draw their power. Furthermore, do not let it escape you that the substance, or bone, is located in the back of a man under the name **Luz** <note>original: *luds*; a legendary indestructible bone from which the body is said to be resurrected</note>, in which both the root of the human structure and its vigor consist. From it the heart, liver, brain, and the genitals themselves take their origin. Its substance is produced from a well-balanced particle of seed, and even when the human structure is dissolved by death itself, its limbs scattered and bones withered, this very substance does not suffer corruption or decay. It is not burned by fire, nor crushed by a millstone, nor worn down by any blow, but remains and does not cease to exist through the ages. This same bone enjoys sweetness and joy after the death of the righteous, and suffers dire punishments after the death of the wicked. This very thing has its root and draws its origin from the substance of **Shamayim**.

There are indeed twin dimensions (as we touched upon before), the place from which each of the Prophets obtained their oracles of prophecy; but **Moses** alone received the spirit of prophesying from the name **Tetragrammaton**.

Lest you think, however, that the rest attained the gifts of prophecy solely through the leadership of an angel—since you should know that many are recorded in the sacred volumes as being joined to angels, whom we by no means claim are enrolled in the brotherhood of the Prophets—the ray of the **Tetragrammaton** shone upon all of them. Yet for the humbler ones, it shone through the four leading spheres: **Adonai**, **El Hai**, **Elohim Sabaoth**, and **Adonai Sabaoth**, which are the same as Kingdom, Foundation, Confession, and Victory <note>these correspond to the lower Sephirot: Malkhut, Yesod, Hod, and Netzach</note>. Therefore, whenever the Prophets of the Most High proclaim that they hear the utterances of the **Tetragrammaton**, consider that this happens only through the mediation of the four aforementioned spheres. **Moses**, however, applied himself to the **Tetragrammaton** itself with no mediator; for his gaze was directed into its radiant mirror, whereas the gaze of others was directed into the somewhat cloudy name **Adonai**, as is read:
<margin>Exodus 6</margin>
*And I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as **El Shaddai** <note>original: *El scadai*; "God Almighty" or "God who is sufficient"</note>; but by my name **Tetragrammaton** I was not known to them.* But where the Scriptures sometimes say the prophetic rays shine through an angel (such as that of Abraham: *The angel of God called to him from the heavens*; or that of Zechariah:
<margin>Zechariah 4</margin>
*And the angel who talked with me answered, etc.*), do not think anything rashly or impulsively about this. At another time, you will weigh these deep mysteries of wisdom. As for what the wise think regarding the Hebrew phrase **Vayikra** <note>original: *uagíchra*; "And He called," the first word of Leviticus</note> in the *Great Gloss* of Leviticus: they say "and He called to Moses," but not in the same way it is written of Abraham.

# OF PAUL RICIUS,

...ham: and the angel of God called to **Abraham**: though an angel calls and a word speaks, in the case of **Moses**, the Creator says: It is I myself who calls, I myself who speaks <note>Ricius is contrasting the indirect prophecy of the Patriarchs via angels with the direct, "face-to-face" prophecy of Moses</note>. I will soon explain where these things lead. Whatever prophets must be prepared and adorned before the prediction of a prophecy—whether they prepare themselves or an angel of God assists in this preliminary adaptation—**Moses** recognized himself as suitable and always ready for the shrines of prophecy, as it is written: "Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord [the **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: *Deus Tetragrammaton*; the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>] will command you." 

Moreover, do not overlook the fact that when people approach the Lord [the **Tetragrammaton**] to pray for the birth of children, it is necessary to turn the mind toward the temple of victory and praise (just as **Hannah** prayed). From there, the name **Elhai** <note>original: *Elhai*; "The Living God," associated with the Sephirah of Yesod/Foundation</note>—from which the oracle also comes in **Adonai** <note>original: *Edonai*; "The Lord"</note>—where the hosts of heaven and earth hang, may draw and bring forth an abundance of strength. <margin>1 Kings 1</margin> For from him, all virtue flows and spreads into herbs and plants, into trees and shrubs, and into every kind of living creature. 

Nor should one thing escape you: in seeking three gifts that are beyond the usual course of nature—namely, children, life, and sustenance—it is necessary to ascend to the high sign, the inaccessible oracle of **Eheie** <note>original: *Eheie*; "I Am," the name associated with Keter, the highest crown of the Sephirot</note>. For life, consider the case of **Hezekiah**: <margin>2 Kings 20</margin> "Behold, he will add to your days," etc. For it is not written "I will add," but "He will add." For children, consider the case of **Hannah**: <margin>1 Kings 1</margin> "And she prayed over the Lord [the **Tetragrammaton**]"; for it is not written that she prayed "to" God. For sustenance, as it is written: <margin>Psalm 55</margin> "Cast upon God what you hope to be given (or your care), and he himself will nourish you," etc. 

Thus, whatever you implore from the heavens, it is not permitted to stop at the sphere or the name which the petition itself has taken on. Rather, one must approach the **Father of Lights**, the sublime crown from which all things take their origin, using the very voice of the appropriate name. From there, descending again, one must return to the limit of the heights. When this is rightly performed, you will obtain whatever vow was requested, as it is written: <margin>Psalm 145</margin> "God is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth." 

Sometimes we learn that these twin oracles are called **Ma Kom haeza** <note>original: *Ma Kom haeza*; Hebrew for "this place"</note>; that is, the place of excellent counsel, namely the headquarters <note>original: *praetorium*; the Roman general's tent or seat of judgment</note>. As we read: <margin>Isaiah 44</margin> "Because the Lord of Hosts [**Tetragrammaton Zeuaot**] has purposed, and who shall annul it?" (or weaken it). Although there is wisdom in counsel, its completion and outcome dwell in the temple of victory and confession, upon which it leans (translating word for word): "And his name shall be called **Wonderful** or **Hidden Counselor**, **Mighty God**, **Everlasting Father**, **Prince of Peace**," etc. <margin>Isaiah 9. Isaiah 14.</margin> For **Wisdom** itself is hidden; the **Counselor** is Prudence; **El** (God) is Magnificence; **Mighty** is Fortitude; **Everlasting Father** is Beauty; **Prince of Peace** is the Foundation, which involves both Victory and God. 

It is written: "and who shall annul it," because only the vigor of Prudence (to which the word "who" refers) is able to loosen the bonds of a vow. Therefore, when the choir of prophets knew this great mystic secret was carved out, they were accustomed to softening the judgment of the higher court, as it is written: "The righteous man rules over the fear of the Lord [**Elohim**]." 

Furthermore, this must be held: a certain **Angel** stands at the two oracles of victory and confession. He is appointed to decree the absolute judgments of the great court over the children of this age, and twin scribes pay him obedience. Indeed, he is capable of removing decreed judgments before they strike the world, or turning them toward something better according to works of repentance. In these temples, there is another presiding official subject to the command of the name **Tetragrammaton**, who exercises care over many cellars and riches. Other ministers are also subject to him, who are tasked with receiving the souls extinguished by the command and judgment of the court or by the sword among the nations, and placing them in storehouses. 

There are also other places of the same oracles called the **Cup of Consolation**, from which comfort and strength are sent down to the mournful and wailing. Moreover, we find elsewhere in these same temples chambers called the **Cup of Trembling** [fury], from which the calamity of vengeance is poured upon the wicked and unworthy. There are, besides these, many repositories filled with precious garments, with which the souls deserving to approach the sight of the supreme Father are covered. There even exist within these oracles inner shrines where the cultivators of wisdom cling, through whose intercession they penetrate the hidden things in the heavens...

### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

Not to mention many other things, of which the following great dimensions will indicate something; these mysteries imply something hidden and involved: truly, the Tetragrammaton Sabaoth <note>original: *Zeuãos*; "Lord of Hosts"</note> of the right wheel refers to the mystical **Netzach** <note>original: נצח *Neza*; the seventh Sephirah, meaning "Victory" or "Eternity"</note>, as the writings suggest. To you, the Tetragrammaton is magnificence, strength, beauty, victory, and confession, because the oracle of victory—I say—bestows grace upon Israel. As it is said: "Will his grace fail *la-nezach*?" <note>original: *laneza*; "forever" or "unto eternity"</note>. For three lights of providence shine forth, called the "eye of mercy"—namely, grace, beauty, and victory—and when their rays are poured out and properly joined in the Sephirotic <note>original: *sphiristica*; referring to the Sephirot, the ten attributes of God in Kabbalah</note> hierarchy, the entire machinery of the world rejoices and exults; for then the works of God stand perfected on every side. Likewise, this measure of Netzach, the Tetragrammaton Sabaoth, when it stands below, often executes the punishment of judgment according to the deeds of mortals. But if, through the flow of the channels, it seeks that origin which resides higher up (namely the "eye of mercy and will," inhabiting the summit of the Crown <note>original: *verticem coronae*; referring to Keter, the highest Sephirah</note>), by which pleasant judgments are established for Israel, then even if the Israelites fall into sin, the immunity of those decrees would by no means be withdrawn or lifted. This is because the shrine of the Diadem <note>A term often used for the Sephirah Malchut or the divine presence</note> transcends the limits of man; it is touched by no "otherness," nor is it turned by repentance or sorrow. Conversely, the opposite may happen: for when it lies lower down under the root of Beauty <note>original: *pulchritudinis*; referring to the Sephirah Tiferet</note> (in the manner of a human), it is granted that repentance may divert and pull it back. For that is the place whose name is "Man," as it is said: "and the likeness of the appearance of a man was upon it from above." <margin>Ezekiel 1</margin>

In this temple, many unanimous houses of judgment are also established, being the advocates for Israel, called *Netzachim* <note>original: *Nezaim*; plural of Netzach</note>: that is, "Victories" or "Eternities." According to the archetype of this, Solomon manufactured and erected the right pillar named **Jachin** <note>original: *Iachim*; "He will establish"</note>, and he who is not ignorant of the mystery of the two pillars, Jachin and **Boaz** <note>original: *Boaz*; "In Him is strength"</note>, will be able to perceive and determine by whose Law (under the guidance of **Elhai** <note>The Living God</note> and **Adonai** <note>original: *Edonai*; The Lord</note>) the minds, spirits, and souls are governed. He will also know how any of the bodies of the world and their paths, as well as the limbs of the human frame, claim their form and appearance from the Tetragrammaton when the springs of the flood are joined to that Name, as Deuteronomy 32 suggests: "He made you and prepared you." Therefore, weigh these things and keep them in your heart. Indeed, many hidden things are here which it would be wrong to bring forth with a pen, but one who is master of his mind will be able to attain them; for the secrets of God are to be revealed to those who fear God.

<note>The Tetragrammaton: The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>

THE FIFTH of the sacred names by which (like a pillar) the higher and lower Sephirot <note>original: *sphiros*</note> are supported is the name **Tetragrammaton**. We find other holy names grafted into it (like leaves and branches onto the trunk of a tree); its beauty and power turn the gaze of all toward itself, and through it, all things perform the duty of persisting. It is written in the Law in various and venerable ways. For it is often read without the addition of another name, such as in Exodus 13 and 6: "The Tetragrammaton spoke to Moses," and "The Tetragrammaton said to Moses," and elsewhere even more frequently. Often, another of the holy names is annexed to it, as in Genesis 2: "In the day that the **Tetragrammaton God** <note>original: *Deus Tetragrammaton, Deus Elohim*</note> made the heaven and the earth." For in the entire work of the "Beginning" <note>referring to the creation account in Genesis 1</note>, only the name **Elohim** is read; but when the Law itself takes up the discourse concerning the completion of creation—"these are the generations of the heaven and the earth," etc.—then for the first time is "Tetragrammaton Elohim" brought forth. For it unites and completes the entire Sephirotic choir for the Tetragrammaton. Therefore, as long as things were subject to the act of making, you will find only the name Elohim written; but when they reached their limit and consummation, the name Tetragrammaton is read. For as we have mentioned before, the name Elohim is frequently clothed by **Adonai** <note>original: *Edonai*</note>, wherefore Adonai itself for a time...

<meta>This page continues Paul Rici’s exploration of the Divine Names and their role in the Kabbalistic structure of the universe. Having previously discussed the attribute of Netzach (Victory), he now moves into the interplay between the names Elohim and the Tetragrammaton, illustrating how God balances strict Justice with Mercy to sustain creation.</meta>

->**PAUL RICI,**<-

The name **Elohim** <note>original: *Elohim*; the Hebrew name of God associated with justice and the creation of the natural world</note> is appropriate because the ancient "weighers" <note>the sages or Kabbalists</note> say that in the beginning He created the world through the "measure of judgment." However, when they realized that the world could not maintain its stability through the measure of judgment alone, He joined the measure of mercy to the dimension of judgment, as it is written:
<margin>Genesis 2</margin>
> "In the day that the **Tetragrammaton Elohim** <note>original: *Tetragrammaton Elohim*; the four-letter name YHWH joined with Elohim</note> made the heaven and the earth."

Therefore, whenever you hear the **Tetragrammaton** <note>the sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH, often associated with Mercy</note> in the Holy Scriptures, consider it a perfect work in which the oracles of both judgment and mercy breathe together.
<margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin> To this fits the verse:
> "The works of the Creator are perfect, for all His ways are judgment," etc.

The "judgment" which the Hebrew expression calls **mishpat** <note>original: *miſepat*; meaning justice or balanced judgment</note> is composed of **din** <note>original: *din*; strict law or judgment</note>; that is, it is gathered from judgment and mercy in every way. For Jacob entered the measure of *mishpat* because, as a "perfect man," he lived between two tents: the tent of Abraham (representing Grace) and the tent of Isaac (representing absolute Judgment). As it is written: 
> "It is the *mishpat* [judgment] of the God of Jacob,"

This is typically suggested by the straight blast of the trumpet 
<margin>Psalm 46</margin> belonging to the **Tetragrammaton**. The "taratantara" <note>original: *taratantarizatio*; an onomatopoeic term for the broken, staccato sound of a trumpet or shofar, known in Hebrew as the *Teruah*</note> sound of the trumpet belongs to **Elohim**, which is easily understood from this:
> "Elohim has ascended through the taratantara blast, the Tetragrammaton through the voice of the trumpet."

Furthermore, we sometimes read the **Tetragrammaton** itself joined in a two-fold way to the name **Adonai** <note>original: *Edonai*; "Lord," the name associated with the Sephirah of Malchut or Sovereignty</note>; for often the Tetragrammaton follows Adonai, according to the verse:
<margin>Habakkuk, at the end</margin>
> "The Tetragrammaton Adonai is my strength."

Pay attention to this, however: whenever the Scripture mentions these two names together, the sound of the name **Tetragrammaton** is transferred to the pronunciation of **Elohim**. Indeed, it is read with the same vowel points as the name Elohim. We believe this is done so that we may perceive (through the intervention of the Tetragrammaton) that Wisdom is annexed and gathered to the Kingdom or the oracle of **Adonai**. For the connection of these words, passing from the supreme beginning through the entire Sephirotic <note>original: *sphiriſticam*; relating to the ten Sephirot or divine attributes</note> garden, indicates that an inundation flows into the measure of **Adonai**.
<margin>Genesis 15</margin> But when the Tetragrammaton is placed after the name **Adonai**, as in:
> "Adonai Tetragrammaton, what will you give me?" etc.

then, starting from the lowest things, we seek those which are higher, even unto the origin of the Will. Nor should it slip from memory that **Adonai Elohim** designates (as I explained before) Justice and the higher indwelling Glory, as well as Justice and the lower indwelling Glory. When
<margin>Zechariah 14</margin> these are gathered into one, the entire machinery of the world is then refreshed with riches and every 
<margin>Psalm 117</margin> bounty of good things, which is what this verse points toward:
> "The Tetragrammaton is one God, and His name is one."

Sometimes we also read the **Tetragrammaton** added to the name **El**—that is, God—as in:
> "And may the Tetragrammaton shine upon us,"

which is joined in such a way that it is understood that the entire fabric of the world is ruled at that time by a more sublime grace and great mercies, with every sting of deceit immediately driven away and judgment set aside. Thus, the Sephirotic oracles then deserve a marvelous height: the celestial spheres are calmed, the earth smiles with shining light, the air glitters, the seas exult, every living thing applauds, and all the works of God rejoice and congratulate themselves on every side for their happy gift. And sometimes the **Tetragrammaton** itself is written next to the names **El** and **Elohim**, just as **El Elohim Tetragrammaton** Himself knows, etc., and that:
<margin>Psalm 49</margin>
> "A Psalm for Asaph: El, Elohim, Tetragrammaton has spoken and called the earth."

Therefore, when you see these names joined in this way, understand that the machinery of the world is being moved and revolved by the sublime court of the "Three Judges" sitting upon the throne, according to the necessity of each work—whether for good or evil, for death or life. I say the "Three Judges" of **Magnificence**, **Strength**, and **Beauty** <note>These correspond to the Sephirot of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note>. We also frequently encounter—not in the Law, but in the books of the Prophets and the Hagiographa <note>the "Holy Writings" or Ketuvim</note>—the name **Zebaoth** <note>original: *Zeuaos*; "of Hosts"</note> added to the Tetragrammaton. This is so that it may be known to us that the Tetragrammaton, with the help of an excellent court, pours its judgment (**mishpat**) into created things, whether it be for benefit or for
<margin>Isaiah 5</margin> loss and hindrance; upon this relies the verse:
> "And the Tetragrammaton Zebaoth shall be exalted in judgment (that is, *mishpat*), and the holy God [El] shall be sanctified in righteousness."

And sometimes these three names are woven together, such as:
> "Tetragrammaton Elohim Zebaoth, turn us, make your face to shine..."
