### ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK 4.

...may your face shine and we shall be saved, <note>original: *luceat facies tua & saluabimur*; a reference to Psalm 80</note> by which the measure of grace, mercy, judgment, and fear is opened to us. These are destined to stand before their own oracles, so that in the temple of victory, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> and in the shrine of confession, **Elohim** (which are these four spherical lights) equally take on the measure of **Elhai** <note>original: *Elhai*; "The Living God," associated with the sphere of Yesod</note>. For the name **Zeuaos** <note>original: *Zeuaos*; a transliteration of *Tzevaot* or Sabaoth, meaning "of Hosts"</note> implies three things: namely, Victory, Confession, and Foundation, <note>These correspond to the Sephirot Netzach, Hod, and Yesod</note> for all of which the dimension of **Edonai** <note>original: *Edonai*; a transliteration of *Adonai*, or "Lord," associated with the final sphere, Malkuth</note> is later expected. Therefore, you, my beloved son, wherever you encounter the joining and the distinctions of these names in the Law and the sacred letters, fix the sharpness of your mind and the intuition of your light more deeply. Weigh carefully where their symbolic meaning tends, for if you accomplish this, you will look upon the hidden and abstruse path of the scriptures, as well as the sacred inner chambers of the Law and the intimate entrances of divine things. You will render the Most High appeasable and mild to your supplications, and you will claim grace in the sight of mortals and those above for ages to come. Yet, let no one waver or contend with strong argument, asking why we presume to grant such highness to the name **Tetragrammaton**, or why we determine that the globe of eternal and falling things flows and persists from it. Let him know that in these things a solid and invincible **Cabalistic** <note>referring to Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition</note> certainty is not lacking, by which we are made masters and are able to bring forth and demonstrate shining proofs excerpted from the Law, by which reason itself can be satisfied no differently than by a sensible omen.

->**N**<-OW, therefore, let us approach the task of explaining something concerning the characters of the sacred **Tetragrammaton**, as far as the purpose of our Volume allows. The first letter of this word is **Iod** [י], which is the mental point, into which the intuition of no created thing happens to be carried. It is not lawful for a man to turn his thought upon that tiny thing, but it is commanded that one stand by faith, even if he cannot reach the limit of its essence. This very element **Iod** is called the "hiding place of wisdom," as in that passage: *And my wisdom is found from nothing* <margin>Job 28.</margin> <note>original: *Et sapientia mea me ain inuenitur*; a mystical reading of Job 28:12 where "where" (ayyin) is read as "nothingness" (Ain)</note>, from which the entire construction of the world is brought forth. Again, this same **Iod** is read to be called "will" and "thought" without end. Nor should it escape you that the mystical **Iod** of the name **Tetragrammaton** refers to the second sphere, whose name is **Wisdom** <note>the sphere of Hokhmah</note>. Indeed, you should know that the "Infinite Crown" <note>Keter, the highest sphere</note> is signaled not by the character **Iod** itself, but only by its upper apex. The second letter of the name **Tetragrammaton**, namely **He** [ה], shows the measure of **Prudence** <note>the sphere of Binah</note>, from which the flood of life is sent down into all the spherical oracles that are below; you shall expect a fuller treatise on this in its own chapter. The third letter of the aforementioned name, namely **Vau** [ו], shows six spheres according to the number of the element itself representing them: three from the middle of its character upward, and three from the middle downward. Upward, indeed: **Magnificence**, **Fortitude**, and **Beauty** <note>Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note>. Downward, however: **Victory**, **Confession**, and **Foundation** <note>Netzach, Hod, and Yesod</note>. You will hear more profound and admirable things regarding these characters of the **Tetragrammaton** hereafter, in which your heart will surely rejoice. The fourth letter is again written as **He** [ה], and in the spherical choir it denotes the outermost **Kingdom** <note>the sphere of Malkuth</note>, through which the union of the Most High Name is perfected, since the distinction of things arises from there downward. Therefore, the name **Tetragrammaton** embraces the ten spheres, and from it hang all the holy names of God. Why then do you—a little man who is but ash—dare to take such a great oracle of God in vain and bring it forth? If the trunk of a tree is shaken, will not its branches be moved, the fruit fall, and the leaves be shaken? Indeed, only the great High Priest was permitted to commemorate this very name in the sanctuary, but outside it was not allowed at all. With these things understood, remember (as the wise men establish) that it would be most wicked for anyone to erase the sacred names, yet their surnames—such as "Merciful," "Clement," and many such—are left to be washed away according to one's will. The holy names are indelible: **Eheie**, **Tetragrammaton**, **Ioh**, **El**, **Eloha**, **Elohim**, **Tetragrammaton Zeuaos**, **Elohim Zeuaos**, **Scadai**, **Edonai**. <note>These are the ten primary Names of God in Kabbalah: Ehyeh, YHWH, Yah, El, Eloah, Elohim, YHWH Tzevaot, Elohim Tzevaot, Shaddai, and Adonai</note>. Into the **Tetragrammaton** itself, the rest of the holy names are inserted, by which the celestial leaders, like chains...

the chains of the ring hang. Indeed, the transient attributes <note>original: *delebilia cognomina*; literally "erasable surnames," referring to the divine titles that describe God's actions rather than His essence</note> are judged as the instruments of the holy names; from these, power and strength are bestowed upon the seventy nations which are ruled by the command of seventy princes. And just as the princes (excluding **Ehyeh**, **Yah**, and the **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: *Eheie, Ioh, Tetragrammaton*; these are the highest names of God in Kabbalistic thought, associated with His pure essence</note> when expressed as **Elohim**) are annexed to the other sacred names, so too the peoples of these princes are attached to these attributes, which stand as the clients and attendants of the holy names.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;You should know, however, that the attributes and instruments of the name **El** (which signifies "of grace") are: Great, Gracious, Powerful, Merciful, Slow to Anger or Clement, Rich in Grace, Holy, Freely Working, and Forgiving. But the Name that bears the weapons of war, namely **Elohim**, has subordinate attributes: Robust, Judge, Judging without Indulgence, Strong, Vigorous, Vehement, Man of War, Visiting Sins, and Paying Retribution. The name **Tetragrammaton**, to which is ascribed an examination woven with the judgment of mercy, claims for itself these attributes: Awesome <note>original: *horribilis*; in a theological sense, this means "dread-inspiring" or "full of majesty" rather than "terrible"</note>, Sustaining Iniquity, Passing Over Faults, Truthful, High, Sublime, Guarding Grace, Dwelling Eternally, and Holy. But let it not escape you that the bond of the entire "chariot" <note>original: *quadrigarum*; a reference to the *Merkabah* or Divine Chariot in Jewish mysticism</note> and of the whole machine consists of these three names, two of which—namely **El** and **Elohim**—depend in turn upon the third, the **Tetragrammaton**. **El** is on the right, **Elohim** is on the left, and the **Tetragrammaton** is in the middle, toward which everything tends.

See the **Tetragrammaton** sitting upon his throne, and the entire host of the heavens standing about him on his right and on his left, etc. For the heavens in this clause speak of the mystery of **El Elohim**. David declares the same: **El Elohim**, the **Tetragrammaton** has spoken, and called the earth. Likewise, the Law suggests: **El, Elohim, Tetragrammaton** himself knows. To each of these three names, therefore, nine prescribed attributes are destined, by which the Ruler of the world executes judgment upon individuals according to each person's readiness. For whatever the condition or measure of the recipient may be, such a dimension of his own gifts does he pour out from the heavens into that very person.

Israel, however, has the name **Tetragrammaton** as its peculiar protector. But the leaders of the Gentiles adhere to the other names and attributes, which serve the **Tetragrammaton** as wings and garments; regarding this, it is written: "And the **Tetragrammaton** chose you, that you might be for him a peculiar people out of all peoples." And also: "Because the portion of the God **Tetragrammaton** is his people." And furthermore: "Because your name is called upon your city and your people," etc. For he has chosen for himself two parts in this machine from the seventy celestial leaders: one part of the place, and another part of the people of that same place, according to the pattern of the seventy lineages of the sons of Noah. But the God **Tetragrammaton** took for himself the people of Israel and the city of Jerusalem.

For the God **Tetragrammaton** never comes forth to the nations except in a royal robe or a warlike cloak <note>original: *paludamento*; a Roman general's cloak</note>, just as among mortals a king is accustomed to stand by and be present with his leaders and ministers. But to the assembly of Israel, as if among his own household and intimates, he appears and offers himself dressed only in inner garments, having laid aside the state robe and royal toga—yet he is not entirely uncovered or naked. However, to the holy men and monarchs of Israel, he stands and rests "naked," with every attribute cast aside (just as one clings to the embraces of a spouse), which is what is meant by: "And I will betroth you to me forever." This is also declared by the verse: "I have put off my tunic, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I restore them to their soiled state?" etc. For while the Israelites are exiles, the Most High is clothed in the tunic of the attributes (to which the leaders of the nations cling); when He returns in glory, dwelling among the "soiled," the God **Tetragrammaton** will be stripped of the garment of attributes and "wings." Therefore, Israel shall see him with a clear gaze of the eyes, as it is written: "Your teacher shall no longer be hidden (if I may put it so), and your eyes shall see your teacher." Yet it must not be thought that at that time the seventy such leaders in the heavens will perish or be destroyed; otherwise, you would say the image of the sublime chariot was diminished, since it is orderly surrounded by seventy...

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

The presiding princes surround [the center], who (as wise men conscious of secrets) together with their seventy crowns of necklaces forge the shape that the Sacred Scriptures present as **Man**, such as in the verse: *It is better to rely on God, the Tetragrammaton, than to trust in man, etc.* <margin>Psalm 117</margin> <note>original: *melius est inniti Deo Tetragrammaton quam confidere in hominem*; the Tetragrammaton is the sacred four-letter name of God, often translated as LORD</note>. For the entire chorus of these princes gazes toward the Tetragrammaton itself, so that they may draw from it the power of existence, through which nourishment and the comforts of life may be imparted to the provinces and peoples over whom they are set. Therefore, it is asserted to be profane and shameful to turn toward any of these in hope, since they are by no means in control of their own right (just like the holy ones of Israel), but are moved by the mercy of God, the Tetragrammaton. Indeed, four leaders of these dukes are decreed, who harass the delinquent people of Israel with punishments, disasters, and various waves of storms; they establish and erect a gap or obstacle between the Tetragrammaton and His people. These are usually called the five **husks** <note>original: *cortices*; refers to the *qliphoth*, the shells or shards of spiritual impurity in Kabbalistic thought</note> and the **foreskin**. Three of these are exceedingly hard, but the fourth, closer to the Tetragrammaton itself, is thin, soft, and small; the vision of Ezekiel <note>referring to the mystical vision of the "Chariot" in Ezekiel 1</note> announces all of these. But when Israel turns back to God, God, the Tetragrammaton, takes the Assembly of Israel back into companionship for a time, and just as the force and empire of the husks is removed in the higher realms, so too in this age they will have no power to bring harm or loss to the nations; rather, all the inhabitants of the earth will provide support and service to the community of Israel. But enough on these matters for now.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;However, I did not think that one of the three names—**El**, **Elohim**, and **Tetragrammaton**—should be suppressed in silence. Therefore, whenever we assert that **El** <note>The Hebrew name of God associated with kindness and mercy</note> represents grace and mercy, and **Elohim** <note>The Hebrew name of God associated with justice and severity</note> represents dread judgment and fear, it must not be thought that fear and judgment exist on one side and pure grace on the other. Instead, consider that fear is enfolded and wrapped in grace, and grace in fear. Only the **supreme crown** <note>original: *hyperbolicum diadema*; refers to *Keter*, the highest of the ten Sephirot or divine emanations</note> is in no way touched by judgment or dread, but overflows and abounds most richly with mercy and grace. Truly, the oracle of **Wisdom** <note>the Sephirah *Chokmah*</note>, following the higher crown, raises its gaze toward the upper things and prevails in mercy; but as it looks down lower, it breaks forth into the measure of judgment. If you refer this same thing to **Prudence** <note>original: *prudentia*; here referring to the Sephirah *Binah* or "Understanding"</note> (the temple where it resides), it will take up and put on the title of grace and mercy; and the further the distance from the supreme crown, the more the dominance of the dimension of judgment is intensified. Finally, from these twin oracles of Wisdom and Prudence, when the remaining sacred names and their surnames come forth, whatever occupies the right side flows from the vein of Wisdom; and whatever is placed in the series on the left returns from the temple of Prudence. Therefore, in the right-hand areas, mercy and grace are suitable for and present in all things; but on the left, judgment and fear. Those things existing in the middle, according to the oracle of the **Tetragrammaton**, have claimed for themselves an equality of grace and fear. In no crown, however—the most excellent one excepted—is fear found completely absent; rather, to each is given a name according to that which abounds within it. But if you hear the **Tetragrammaton** itself called frequently by the surname of judgment, consider that this happens not because judgment is primarily in it, but because, like a judge, it performs its duty through the support and service of others. Hence, they decree that whatever the supreme crown brings forth receives an **androgynous** <note>original: *androginosam*; a "male-female" image, signifying the union of opposites or complete balance</note> image (so to speak). From this, one can discern and behold the type of the **Cherubim** of the Ark of the Sanctuary and the whole chariot woven by **Solomon**. Keep this always stable within your heart. For a great, essential mystery of faith and law lies hidden here. But if you desire to see the proportion of the mixture in any measure, listen with attentive ears to what I shall put forward. Just as we have put forward concerning the parts of the chariot, so we assert by hinting at the elements of the world. For **fire, air, water, and earth** are given to the higher beings as well. For we divide the elements themselves into three, and one as the base that receives the others; so we also speak of the three more powerful oracles of God and their seat. Fourthly, for fire agrees with the oracle of **Elohim**, water with the dimension of **El**, and air with the measure of the **Tetragrammaton**, which is the conciliator and middle point between both aforementioned; and **Adonai** <note>original: *Edonai*; the name of God meaning "My Lord," usually associated with the physical world or the Sephirah *Malkhut*</note> te...

# PAUL RICIUS,

... [In the same way] that the earth is established as the dwelling place of the entire celestial machinery <note>original: *sphiristicæ machinæ*; referring to the system of the Sephirot, the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</note>, it is the receiver of all others and is adapted to them. Just as on earth any perishable thing performs its work according to the vigor of the predominating element, so too in the heights, such an effect is caused and brought forth in the measure of <term>Edonaï</term> <note>Adonai, a Hebrew name for God meaning "Lord," associated with the final Sephirah, Malkhut (Kingdom)</note> as the abundance of these three names provides. For the oracle of **Adonai** itself, as much as its power sustains itself, is a judgment on every side; it receives and does not bestow, just as the pre-eminent crown <note>referring to Keter, the highest Sephirah</note> is fundamentally mercy, which grants and receives nothing. Yet the temple of **Adonai** is capable of collecting within itself all grace and judgment trickling down from the higher realms. For this reason, it is reasonably called the "door" and the "vestibule" through which the prayer of the righteous enters; but let these things suffice for now. If you compare what we have just brought forward regarding this kind of measure with the things tasted in the first chapter, you will be able to unlock and discern the hidden inner chambers of the pleasant secrets of wisdom. 

Therefore, having completed these matters, we have decided to explain certain other titles, which, even if they do not exist in such high loftiness as those just touched upon, nevertheless seem to reveal the ineffable sublimity of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>the four-letter name of God, YHVH, which was considered too sacred to pronounce</note> in some way and provide a path by which we may more easily be carried into the higher realms. The assembly of Kabbalists, therefore, is accustomed to call the **Tetragrammaton** itself by the title of the **middle line**: because it is a wide banner to which the order of the entire chariot is attached from above, from below, and from both sides. From it, all holy names hang, according to the letter <term>Vau</term> <note>the third letter of the Tetragrammaton, which looks like a vertical line</note> of the name **Tetragrammaton** itself, which is depicted in the form of a line. 

The same name is also titled the **Tree of Life**; that is, the tree to which the oracle of Prudence, called "Life," is joined. For this reason, the Law <note>the Torah</note> says it was planted in the middle of the garden, from which again the written Law is considered to have been issued. For Moses alone applied the **Tetragrammaton** itself and the mirror of things. Therefore, the Creator declares this man's house to be faithful, in a way that even the first Adam had not remained. You should not be ignorant of the fact that the entire Law presents the image of the name **Tetragrammaton**. For this reason, if even a single letter were taken away or added, it would be considered a sacrilege for this to be called the "Law of the **Tetragrammaton** of God." For the Law, just like the **Tetragrammaton**, is woven from right and left according to the prohibiting and commanding mandates. 

Furthermore, the Law is encompassed by seven "sphiristic" oracles <note>the seven lower Sephirot</note> (as the ancients remind us), saying that the Law was handed down in seven voices. Moreover, in the entire Law, this dimension is usually called <term>אמת</term> **EMES** <note>Emet</note>, that is, truth or the truth. For just as all extremes and sides decline toward the middle—namely, the **Tetragrammaton**—so also the word **EMES** is gathered from the letters at the extremes and those in the middle <note>Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, Mem is the middle, and Tav is the last; together they spell 'Emet' (Truth)</note>. For the seal of the Most High (as it pleased the elders) is **EMES**, so called because the **Tetragrammaton** itself—like a judge on whose left stand attendants and accusers, and on whose right stand protectors and supporters—establishes the decided boundary of judgment. Thus, between the letters **Aleph**, **Mem**, and **Tau**, from which the word **EMES** is forged, we see the pleasing supporters arranged on the right from **Aleph** to **Mem**, and the grim and criminal ones on the left from **Mem** to **Tau**. 

To this measure is also given the title <term>תפארת</term> **TIFEERES** <note>Tiferet</note>: that is, beauty. This is because the **Tetragrammaton** alone functions as if it were clothed in all the "sphiristic" names and titles, from the ornament of whose connection Beauty itself emerges. And although according to Kabbalistic dogma, the measure of Prudence is usually called <term>פאר</term> **PEER**: that is, adornment, it is not, however, titled **TIFEERES** (Beauty). For Prudence itself exists as the chief of the robes with which the **Tetragrammaton** is decorated; therefore, *Peer* is its peculiar title. But Beauty dwells in the **Tetragrammaton** alone, which fits that verse: <margin>1 Chronicles 29</margin> *To you, O God, the Tetragrammaton, belongs magnificence, strength, and beauty.* 

The **Tetragrammaton** is also read by the title <term>דעת</term> <margin>Proverbs 3</margin> **DAAS** <note>Da'at</note>: that is, knowledge, as in that verse: *The Lord (Tetragrammaton) by wisdom founded the earth; by prudence he prepared the heavens; by his knowledge (Daas) the depths burst forth, etc.* For just as every split or eruption is usually effected between two sides, so too this sort of thing breaks forth between Wisdom and Prudence, and between the right and the left—

But Israel, which claims for itself—guided by the middle line <note>The central column of the Sephirotic tree, representing balance and the path of Tiferet</note>—the Tetragrammaton reaching toward the primary crown, which lacks limits, flies forth with a winged mind and spiritual feathers. For from Abraham came the base Ishmael; Isaac fathered the wicked Esau; but Jacob alone was a complete man, in whom the venom of the serpent (and the leaven of the mass <note>A metaphor for original sin or the "evil inclination"</note> had been almost emptied out) produced a bright sprout of sons, who with one mind (as is the opinion of the elders) pledged: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord <note>original: *Deus Tetragrammaton*</note> is our God, the Lord <note>original: *Deus Tetragrammaton*</note> is one."

These seals, I say, are divided into four standards <note>original: *vexilla*</note>, and the months are split into the four seasons of the year. Therefore, ponder these things in your mind and gather that all the armies of both the higher and the "falling" <note>original: *deciduae*; referring to the lower, physical world</note> cosmic machine are led in their works and their very office of existence by the command of the most holy Tetragrammaton. This dimension is also frequently called <term>Nora</term> <note>original: נורא; meaning "Awesome" or "Terrible"</note>: that is, "inspiring awe," because in this middle line of grace, he balances judgment. Jacob was the first to bring forth this title, who (as I mentioned before) claimed this measure for himself. For it is written: *And seeing it, he said, how awesome is this place.* <note>Genesis 28:17</note> Just as the portion of Abraham is called "Magnificence" <note>Chesed</note>, and that of Isaac "Strength" <note>Gevurah</note>, so too does our petitionary prayer testify, saying: *God of Abraham, God of Isaac, God of Jacob, the great, strong, and awesome God.* Quite often this oracle is also called by the title <term>Mischpat</term> <note>original: משפט; meaning "Judgment" or "Justice"</note>: that is, judgment gathered together by the mercy of grace. For the judicial chambers of the name Tetragrammaton are called <term>Mischpat</term> (just as the courtroom of <term>Edonai</term> <note>Adonai/The Lord</note> is called <term>Zedech</term> <note>original: צדק; meaning "Justice"</note>).

Because of this, when the name <term>Edonai</term> performs judgment alone, no mercy or grace is admitted; for that name exists in itself as utterly stripped and devoid of grace. If it ever does become a participant in grace, that is entirely permitted to it by the gift of the Tetragrammaton; for only as much grace as the Tetragrammaton gives exists within it. Indeed, there are three oracles (as we taught before): the highest, <term>Eheie</term> <note>original: אהיה; "I Am/Will Be"</note>, is completely full of mercy. The middle, the Tetragrammaton, balances grace and judgment. The lowest, however, is <term>Edonai</term>, from which judgment is extended and sent forth. Therefore, when Israel breaks out into crimes, the upper channels are closed, nor does the Tetragrammaton spend any of its grace upon the temple of <term>Edonai</term>, and thus the dimension of <term>Edonai</term> is left empty and void. 

Consequently, the following result stirs up rigid seditions among mortals, causes bloody slaughters, and administers famine and pestilential plagues. It does not withdraw itself from the ruthlessness of these scourges until it has inflicted the punishments deserved by the guilt of the crimes. Regarding this matter, the Law warns us: *Beware of his presence,* it says, *and do not rebel against him, for he will not endure your transgressions.* <note>Exodus 23:21</note> However, when Israel corrects itself and restores its innocence, then the channels are mutually inserted into the springs, by which mercy is sent down from that higher courtroom into the temple of <term>Edonai</term>. This causes the entire machine of fleeting things to exult in happiness and prosperity; whatever lower riches it enjoys, mortals, having been made kinship with the heavenly beings, may persist in this age safe in peaceful quiet. Very often also this measure... <note>The sentence continues on the next page.</note>

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

...is expressed by the pronoun <insert>אתה</insert> *Atah* <note>Hebrew: "You"</note>. For to the three prescribed oracles—Adonai, the Tetragrammaton, and Ehyeh—three surnames correspond: I, You, and He. "I" belongs to the temple of Adonai, as in the verse: *I kill, and I make alive; I have wounded,*
<margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin>
*and I will heal.* <note>original: "Ego occidam, & uiuere faciam, uulnera intuli, & ego sanabo."</note> The pronoun "You," however, suits the dimension of the Tetragrammaton, according to that verse: *You are awesome.* <note>original: "Tu horribilis." A reference to Psalm 76:7, highlighting the direct but formidable presence of the four-letter Name.</note> "He," on the other hand, is assigned to the sanctuary of Ehyeh: for he says, *He is the one desiring grace.* And again: *And He, being merciful, forgave their sins.* The reason why the temple of Adonai has claimed the pronoun "I" for itself is because it assists Israel more closely; without any intermediary, it sees and cares for their individual works. But the Tetragrammaton, since it looks down upon and judges mortals from a more remote place, therefore claims for itself the pronoun *ATA* <note>Atah: "You"</note>, through which we humbly seek benefits and offer our vows in all our supplications. However, because the measure of Ehyeh transcends all powers of both angelic and human intelligence without limit, the pronoun "He" is destined for it, which designates only that which is absent and distant. Nor did Moses, the greatest of Prophets and teacher of the wise, ever receive the utterances of this Name except through the mediation of the Tetragrammaton; indeed, he was not even able to cross the thresholds of Prudence, for (as the elders relate) fifty gates of Prudence have been established in the world, and
<margin>50 Gates.</margin>
Moses reached all of them except for one that remained secluded. <note>The "50 Gates of Understanding" (Binah) is a classical Kabbalistic concept; Moses is traditionally said to have reached the 49th gate.</note> Therefore, to these three oracles, these three names are applied: Ehyeh to "He," Tetragrammaton to "You" (*Ata*), and Adonai to "I" (*Eni* <note>Ani: "I"</note>). These are truly the great and hidden secrets of wisdom which they offer and hand down; you must weigh and examine them according to your strength. Thus far we have traversed five sacred names of God; now, with ineffable mercy as our guide, we proceed to the explanation of the remaining five.

The name Elohim obtains the sixth rank among the holy names of God: that is,
<margin>Elohim: that is, God.</margin>
God. As previous discussions mention, the Overseer of Judgment has established his seat for himself on the left side, from which either a mournful or a joyful judgment rushes down upon the children of the age. Many judicial houses are attached to this name, each of which executes and completes its duty with a firm and solid judgment. For this reason, if a judgment goes forth from there for the benefit of a matter, then God will be addressed by the name Tetragrammaton or *El*. But if it is turned toward harm or loss, the name Elohim demands it for itself. Because all created things take shape according to the promptness of that judicial palace, which provides for them, the Law (Torah) expresses and introduces only the name Elohim throughout the Work of the Beginning <note>The creation account in Genesis 1.</note>. For to none of the things that exist was anything granted, except insofar as its right demands according to the thirty-two paths of wisdom—paths, I say, by which the Book of Formation <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah*, an early foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note> opened its beginning. until the verse: *And God [Elohim] saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good.* In this place, it pleased the elders to suggest that "very good" even includes death itself. Nevertheless, the world cannot persist by the measure of harsh judgment alone (as we touched upon before); therefore, the Law soon
<margin>Genesis 2.</margin>
added the Tetragrammaton to the name Elohim, where it says: *These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God [Tetragrammaton Elohim] made the heaven and the earth.* For by the oracle of Mercy, the measure of the dire judgment of Elohim is appeased and softened. For if Lot, the nephew of Abraham, had been left under the command of that judgment, he could never have taken flight, but the sulfurous fire would have devoured him along with the crowd of Sodom. Therefore, when Lot had been led outside, the angels warned him, saying: *Do not look behind your back.* But while Abraham was leading him by the hand—Abraham being dedicated to this very measure—the oracle of grace protected him.

But the lower judicial palace, which is likewise often called by this name, is the upper temple of Adonai, which executes the judgment of the higher palace; for which reason it is frequently accustomed to be called "Elohim" instead of Adonai. <meta>This page continues the discussion of divine names and their metaphysical functions. -># PAULUS RICIUS,<-

Whoever—whether angel or human—carries out judgment, the name **Elohim** <note>A Hebrew name for God that represents the attribute of Justice and Law; it is also used in the Bible to refer to human judges or angelic powers</note> fits him, as it says in Exodus 22: *Let the cause of both come before Elohim* <note>original: "Ad ipsum Elohim ueniat causa utriusque." In many English Bibles, this is translated as "the judges."</note>. And also in Exodus 22: *You shall not revile the Elohim* <note>original: "Elohim non detrahes."</note>. From this, it was also chosen to call the leaders of the seventy nations **Elohim** or **Aherim** <note>original: "Eherim," likely a transliteration of the Hebrew "Aherim" meaning "others" or "strangers," as in "other gods."</note>—these are the ones who depend upon the seventy crowns of the sanctuary surrounding the Temple that stands in the middle. These are called "foreign gods," for the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter Name of God (YHWH)</note> imparts holy power to each of them, by which they are able to rule the nations reduced under their subjection. 
<margin>Exodus 20</margin>
But Israel alone has the **Tetragrammaton** as its leader. For this reason, He says to them at the beginning of the commandments in Exodus 20: *I am the Lord <note>original: "Deus Tetragrammaton"</note> your God, etc. You shall have no foreign gods before me, etc.* For we assert that these twin commandments are the trunk of the entire Law, which (as the elders teach) all Israel received from the mouth of the Most High without any intermediary. To this is added the word of the Prophet in Micah 4: *All people walk each one in the name of his god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord <note>original: "Dei Tetragrammaton"</note> our God forever.*

Furthermore, the name **Elohim** holds the measure of the coming world, though it is inscribed with the characters and name of the **Tetragrammaton**, and for that reason it is uttered with the voice of **Elohim**. This is because it obtains the power of judging from the oracle of strength or the more sublime judgment-hall; yet because mercy is folded and wrapped within them, it is written with the same elements as the **Tetragrammaton**. This measure is also called **גבורה** **GEVURAH**: that is, "Strength" or "Fortitude," because it inflicts force upon the wicked and repels the enemies of the Most High; nor does any force exist so wild that it would dare to fight or resist it. Sometimes, as I mentioned above, this same supreme judgment-hall is found written with the name **זכו** **Zechus**, that is, "Merit," because there all the merits and sins of mortals are recorded. 

It is also sometimes called **צפון** **Zafon**, which sounds the same as "North" or "Hidden." For since the measure of grace draws the riches of good things most abundantly from the living fountain of mercy—so that it may bestow benefits upon those who ask—all such rewards then come to a halt and linger there, on the side of the North, touching the measure of the Left. They remain there until a just examination of the petitioner is undertaken, so that if he proves worthy of his request, his vows may be fulfilled; if not, they are not. Whatever is lovely and pleasant that passes into the oracle of judgment lies hidden there in the cellars and treasuries of the North wind, until the one praying can entreat this dimension to be favorable to him. For this reason, the abundance of riches and all desired comforts lie hidden there without any gap, as that verse suggests: *Gold comes from the North.* 
<margin>Job 37. Proverbs 3.</margin>
Hence the elders determine that he who desires the wealth of gold should turn toward the North, as it is written: *Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and honor.* 

Nor should it be overlooked that vast dwellings exist in the region of the North, inhabited by a sordid crowd of angels, where multiform abysses, horrendous and hidden caves, and innumerable secret pits are dug out. These are tangled with sharp briars, strewn with stinging thistles, filled with deadly monsters, and fortified by assemblies of other wild beasts. These come forth with one mind, draw up their battle lines, exercise their strength, and cunningly invade, run, push, and stand by. Thus, whenever a northern judgment goes forth to overturn kingdoms, desolate provinces, or prostrate empires, they immediately break out in a dire whirlwind of storms to the ruin, destruction, and slaughter of mortals, and they inflict and carry out the scourge decreed for the wretched. 
<margin>Jeremiah 1</margin>
Concerning these, Jeremiah says: *From the North all evil shall be spread.* For this reason, when the Law decrees sacrifices for the pardon of sins, it ordains that they be sacrificed only on the North side. Therefore, in the end times, when the light of the empire of the great and twisting dragon shall be extinguished (the one who dwells deeper within the curtain of the Northern region, who distorted Eve with sordid and deadly poison, brought death to Adam, and who exists as the minister and leader of all punishments), as the Prophet promises by the mouth of the Most High: *And I will remove the* 
<margin>Joel 2</margin>
**Zephoni** <note>Hebrew word for "the Northern one," often associated with a hidden or northern threat</note>—*that is, the Northern one—far from you,* then all sacrifice and worship in the North shall cease. But these matters have been touched upon briefly, though they require a longer...

This measure is also designated by the name **Pahad** <note>Hebrew: פחד, meaning 'Dread' or 'Fear'; it refers to the Sephirah of Gevurah/Judgment</note>: that is, fear or dread. It is so called because from it are drawn forth horrific judgments and a flame of parching fire is emitted, which is frequently read as the most holy "burning fire." Here, in this measure of fear, are founded many impassable lakes, the abysses of eternal ruin, and the depths of Gehenna—that is, the dwellings of hell, which are often called "Night" because of their misty darkness,

as it is written: *Every man has his sword girt on his thigh because of fear in the night*; and also: *You shall not be afraid for the terror of the night*, etc. This measure Isaac claimed for himself (as the previous points suggest), for the strength of fear possesses every scepter and power of command, as in that verse: *Dominion and fear are with him, who makes peace in his high places*, etc. You must not be ignorant, however, that this divine oracle **Elohim**, even if the name "burning fire" is within it, administers opposite and conflicting effects through a single and simple power: to kill and to make alive, to scatter and to protect, to wound and to heal. Furthermore, consider that it is lawful for any messenger or official who executes this judgment to be called by the name **Elohim**, etc. I believe this suffices for the investigation of the name **Elohim**; if you keep these things fixed in your heart, you will certainly see hidden and delightful things of the Law revealed through wisdom.

The **s**eventh of the holy names is **El** <note>Hebrew: אל</note>: that is, the presiding *God of grace and mercy*, whom **Abraham** had as his companion, according to the verse: *And he called there upon the name of the Tetragrammaton, the El of the world*, etc. Here it is worthwhile to distinguish that the great assembly of the **Elohim** Senators <note>A metaphor for the divine powers or angelic hosts associated with Judgment</note> contains ten times three hundred ranks of judges, who carry out the judicial decrees of the leaders, whether they result in loss or gain. For this reason, all the abundance of good things which they withhold from the delinquent, they gather and store up, and finally the righteous shall inherit it in the end. To this end it was said: *That I may cause those who love me to inherit substance* <note>original: "Ut hæreditare faciam dilectos meos." Ricci is referencing Proverbs 8:21. The Hebrew word for "substance" or "something" is 'Yesh' (יש), which has a numerical value of 310.</note>: that is, "something," a word which in its characters totals three hundred and ten in number. When these troops (by the decree of judgment) propose to discharge a fault through punishment, if any of the righteous knows how to approach the measure of **El**, which shines everywhere with grace, he will be able to soothe the rushing force and the glowing wrath of judgment, and to transform unpleasant things into joyful benefits. For it is within the right of this name to bestow good things even on those who do not perform good works, just as it is the custom of the oracle of **Jacob** to impart the gifts of good things only to those who are truly good themselves, upon which is based that verse: *You will give truth to Jacob and grace to Abraham.*

->The Lord (YHWH)<-

**I**n the series of holy names, the eighth sounds and exists as one thing in voice, but another in the letters with which it is woven: for its elements are the same as those of the name **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four letters YHWH</note>, but we see that it possesses the pronunciation and the vowel points of the word **Elohim**. This measure relates to **Prudence** <note>The Sephirah of Binah</note>, and is placed in the third rank of the sublime oracles, becoming the knot of the entire spiritual choir. It is composed of the characters of the Tetragrammaton because it is attached to Mercy (I mean, to the Crown of the Most High). However, the lips sound the name **Elohim** insofar as it stands as a participant in judgment, since the vigor of judgment is poured out from there into every dimension, and its seat is established as the temple of strength, called **Elohim**. Do not be ignorant, however, that the name read by itself sometimes denotes Prudence, more often Strength and Kingdom; but when it is attached to the name **Zebaoth** <note>original: "Zeuaos," a transliteration of the Hebrew 'Tzevaot' meaning 'of Hosts'</note>, it then shows the left column joined to Strength. But when it is spoken as the **living Elohim** (or of life), it suggests the measure of the **Foundation** <note>The Sephirah of Yesod</note>, and the temple of the Kingdom, which licks up life from that nourishment. In the creation of the world, the same oracle of Prudence is designated by the most holy name, by which all things that adapt the number seven to themselves are supported, strengthened, and raise their gaze. # ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

but they exist forever as a dwelling place of pleasant mercy and entreatable redemption. Wherefore this very Prudence <note>Hebrew: *Binah*; the third Sephirah, representing the Divine Mother and Understanding</note> is usually called *Nachalah* <note>original: נחלה</note>: that is, the **Inheritance** of Jacob, which has no limits, and is also read as the "breadth of the river." For among the seventy leaders <note>Refers to the seventy nations or their angelic princes</note>, there is no lictor, attendant, or robber who is permitted to enter a shrine of this kind; for this reason, its greatness is never struck by an oppressor, nor is its abundance closed off by any narrowing of fear. This same measure is also brought forward by the wise under the name *Teshuvah* <note>original: תשובה</note>: that is, **Repentance**, or conversion. From here, minds fly forth, just as from the beauty of the spirit and from the kingdom of the soul. These three—mind, spirit, and soul—until they return to the sanctuary, are entwined and folded together in a mutual bond with Prudence. For the soul clings to the spirit, the spirit to the mind, and the mind indeed to Prudence; but if the sinful soul undergoes the guilt of excision <note>Hebrew: *Kareth*; being "cut off" from one's people or the divine source</note>, then the soul is severed from the spirit. Unless the penitent one corrects themselves, they are made devoid of the world to come. But if, having been purified again, the soul renders itself innocent, it is grafted back into the spirit from which it had been torn away, and returns into the life of the world to come through Prudence. For this reason, Prudence is rightly read under the name of "the conversion of repentance."

It is also customary, according to the dogma of the Kabbalists, for this same dimension to be called *Tzedek* <note>original: צדק</note>: that is, **Superior Justice**, because judgment first arises from there. This looks toward the Lower Justice <note>associated with the Sephirah Malkuth</note> according to the mystical name *Adonai* <note>original: Edonai</note> uttered as the four-lettered name of God <note>original: Tetragrammaton; YHVH</note>, *Elohim*. <margin>Deuteronomy 16.</margin> For this reason the Law commanded justice, saying: *Justice, and justice shalt thou follow.*

This same Sephirah, when dwelling above, is called **Glory**. For as long as Israel is the guardian of the commandments and the Law, this Glory breaks out into the entire garden of the Sephiroth, and from there the Kingdom (that is, the lower indwelling Glory <note>The *Shekhinah*</note>) visits the world with whatever riches of good things it possesses. But if Israel does the opposite, the Glory itself then presents a cloudy outcome of affairs, <margin>Deuteronomy 4.</margin> according to that saying: *Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord <note>original: Tetragrammaton</note> is God <note>original: Elohim</note> in heaven above, and upon the earth beneath,* etc. To this is added that other verse: <margin>Ruth 4.</margin> *And the women her neighbors gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi,* etc. For in these places, the root of this birth is grafted; for between two such indwelling glories, he decreed a peculiar inheritance for himself, just as it is read: *Zion is the city of David, but you must consider this.* Furthermore, this measure of Prudence is called *Mekor Chayim* <note>original: מקור חיים</note>: that is, the **Fountain of Life**. For it (as is established before) pours forth through all the rewards of life, drawn from the more sublime machine of mercy. It is also called **Propitiations** or **Indulgences**, for in it the type of Lebanon shines back, as it is written: <margin>Song of Solomon 4.</margin> *Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse.* For the grace of the Most High decreed that one single day be established in the cycle of the year in which the filth of sins might be wiped away, and Israel might show itself white; which the Law itself calls the Day of Atonements <note>Yom Kippur</note>, because on that day Prudence is connected to the Kingdom. Wherefore Prudence washes away and deletes every foulness infecting the sanctuary of the Kingdom caused by the crimes of mortals. Therefore, these twin measures, as protectors, commemorate the merits of Israel, which is why that day is read with the plural expression "Atonements"—namely, the atonement of the Superior Mother <note>Binah</note> and also of the Lower Mother <note>Malkuth</note>. It is written, *You shall call Prudence "Mother."* Since, therefore, on such a day Israel applies itself to the purifications of Prudence, the Law prohibits the use of the marriage bed <margin>Leviticus 23.</margin> on the day of atonement, which is nevertheless permitted on the Sabbaths and other celebratory days. <margin>Genesis 20.</margin> The mystery of this is by no means hidden from the wise, and it is written: *And yet indeed she is my sister; she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife,* etc. Turn the sharp edge of your mind toward this, for the conclusion of the inner chamber of the day of atonements refers to such a thing. We also call this same shrine of Prudence the **World to Come**. For this (as we have touched upon frequently) is the fountain of eternal life, through which we pray during the ten continuous days at the beginning of the year: *Remember us for the life of the world to come.* They call Prudence the "World to Come" because from there, a rich flow breaks out and comes without any interval; and although we may state that this is pulled back by the sins of men, we do not believe it is entirely contracted, but rather that it drips drop by drop, so that the whole structure of the world is not overwhelmed. We assert that desolation would rush in from every side were it not for those external channels. But when, through righteous works, it...

# PAUL RICIUS

...it adorns Israel, the world rejoices in the greatest abundance of goods, and the celestial and earthly <note>Literally: "falling" or "perishing" machine, referring to the physical world.</note> machine applauds everywhere; existing as something auspicious and safe, it finally emerges as abundantly happy. To this [Prudence] furthermore the **Great Trumpet** is attributed, as it is written: *In that day, the clangor of a great trumpet or horn shall sound.* <margin>Isaiah 27</margin> For it adapts to itself the name of the **Jubilee**, by whose sounding of the trumpet the release from earthly captivity is announced to the inhabitants, and the highest liberty is heard. For a wisdom more sublime than all the leaders of the nations resides here; therefore, by its command alone is Israel snatched from the oppression of the nations. If you should ask why the clangor of the trumpet did not precede the redemption from Egypt, you must know that the Israelites were subjected to the burden of the Egyptians only for a time. But the present captivity—in which all the governors of the nations and all the kindreds of the earth fiercely distress and trample upon the people of Israel—requires the lightning-bolt of an extraordinary power and seeks the sound of the Great Trumpet. However, because the leader of the Egyptians held the summit among the monarchs of the nations, it was necessary for the vigor of the High-Thunderer <note>A poetic epithet for God.</note> to burst forth in showing portents and performing miracles.

Sometimes this same measure is called "Fortitude": for it is written: *Who shall speak the fortitudes of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHVH. The quote is from Psalm 106:2: "Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord?"</note> or make all his praise to be heard?* <margin>Psalm 106</margin> But the name "Fortitude," when uttered individually, fits the measure of **Fear** <note>The Sephirah Gevurah (Strength/Severity).</note>: because often, when the Israelites fall into sin, Fortitude itself is unable to resist the stumbling blocks of its attendants (if I may put it that way), as if not all strengths inhabited it. But tireless **Prudence** <note>The Sephirah Binah.</note> is blunted by no force, nor is any prince ever permitted to reach its thresholds; for it is walled in by all kinds of strength, by which every harmful offense is rooted out. With an invincible hand, it restores, redeems, and loosens the chains of every captivity.

Sometimes this Prudence is also brought forth under the name of "Praise": <margin>Psalm 32</margin> for (as we have written before) just as we pour out entreaties and prayers to the name *Adonai* <note>original: Edonai; refers to the Sephirah Malkuth/Kingdom</note>, so also we bestow the honor of praise through the oracle to Prudence. From Prudence shine forth wonderful and distinguished deeds, for which, by right and merit, ineffable praise must be offered. Praise, therefore, reaches higher than prayer; for the former is directed toward the Kingdom, the latter toward Prudence <note>Ricius here distinguishes between the petitionary prayer sent to the lower "Kingdom" and the higher "Praise" sent to "Understanding."</note>. For to pray for what the poverty of the petitioner requires is common to all: but praise of wisdom belongs only to the excellent, as it is written: *Praise is fitting for the upright.* <margin>Psalm 33</margin>

Furthermore, the divine oracle refers to this as the first type of the letter **He** (ה) in the name Tetragrammaton, just as the second **He** (ה) of the same Tetragrammaton signifies the Temple of the Kingdom. For by the same reason that the shrine of Prudence provides for seven oracles, so also the dimension of the Kingdom imparts goods to each of the created things (according to the ability and readiness of each nature). The former stands as the vestibule for the higher temples, the latter for the lower; the former is praise, the latter prayer; the former is propitiation, and the latter is also propitiation. This one is eightfold, and that one is also eightfold. The former is the **Greater Nurturer** <note>Latin: *Abas alumnúsue maior*; referring to the "Upper Mother" Binah</note> from whom the whole "sphiristic" <note>Referring to the Sephirot of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.</note> order is nourished; the latter is the **Lesser Nurturer**, from whom the angelic machine is fed—the Sun, the Moon, the army of the heavens and stars, and all the earthly ranks take up their strength for living and persisting according to the limit of each nature.

Wherefore the seal of the most holy Tetragrammaton is committed to these twin names: for Prudence, to which the first *He* (ה) of the Tetragrammaton is assigned, is written with the characters by which the Tetragrammaton is composed, but in voice and points <note>Vowel points.</note> it sounds as **Elohim**. But the Kingdom indeed is equated to the name Tetragrammaton, yet in characters and pronunciation, it is expressed as **Adonai** <note>original: Edonai</note>. Thus these two oracles look toward each other and are referred to everywhere in the Law; when it is written *Adonai*, the Tetragrammaton is pronounced *Elohim*, or the Tetragrammaton is pronounced *Elohim Adonai*. By their "sphiristic" coupling, the whole union is perfected, and the Lord Tetragrammaton shall be one, and His name one. But enough of these things for now; let us now approach the explanation of the remaining names of God.

<meta>This page continues the technical kabbalistic explanation of the divine names, specifically focusing on the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God) and its relationship to the Sephirot (divine spheres). It follows the previous page's discussion on the Sephirah of Prudence (Binah).</meta>

->ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV. 189<-

[The letter Yod] <note>original: "Iod"</note> signifies the **Crown**, and the remainder of its mass indicates **Wisdom**. Indeed, **Prudence**, which is determined together with the two superior ones, is marked by the first <hebrew>ה</hebrew> [He] of the name Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God: YHVH (Yahweh/Jehovah).</note>. Therefore, the first two characters of the Tetragrammaton reveal the three more sublime lights of the spheres. However, the third letter, <hebrew>ו</hebrew> [Vav], contains six oracles: three indeed from its middle upward—namely **Magnificence**, **Beauty**, and **Fortitude**; and three again from its middle downward—namely **Victory**, **Praise** (or Glory), and the **Foundation**. The final sphere, which is the tenth, is demonstrated by the last <hebrew>ה</hebrew> [He] of the same Tetragrammaton. Thus, the two prior elements of the Tetragrammaton, hinting at the three supreme dimensions, compose by themselves that divine name **Ioh** <note>original: "Ioh", usually transliterated as Yah.</note>. The last two letters, however, construct nothing by themselves. This happens because the three higher measures offer light to the seven lower ones, but the later ones provide no light to the more sublime. Although the word "Ioh" especially indicates the measure of Wisdom, it nevertheless explains the whole structure of **Mercy**—that is, the three higher lights—equally. For this reason, if you prepare your strength, whenever you hear the name **Ioh** in the sacred scriptures, you will be able to attain the contemplation of prophetic wisdom.

<margin>Exodus 17</margin>
For example, it is written in the Law: *Because the hand is upon the throne of Ioh, there is a war of God against Amalek*, etc. For the wicked **Amalek** comes from the ancient serpent and is grafted there; that is, the serpent who, while he wounded Eve with his venom, cut down the plant of Adam and separated the leader. <margin>suspended voice</margin> And although Israel subsequently stood upon Mount Sinai—from where the plague is said to be removed—nevertheless, the spot on the Moon by no means vanished. When Amalek approached, he increased the lunar spot and touched the palm of Jacob's thigh, by which the kingdom of the house of David was broken. Therefore, supported by the wound of the serpent, as you see, the letters **Vav** and **He** (the last of the name Tetragrammaton) were harmed, while the first ones, **Yod** and **He**, remained unharmed, because they dwell in the more sublime heights, where none of the [hostile] leaders are permitted to fly. <margin>hand</margin> Therefore, the "hand upon the throne" is Yod-He—that is, Ioh—for the war of the Tetragrammaton against Amalek.

Look forward to these things, and as often as you encounter the name **Ioh**, examine it most diligently; you will find the hidden secrets of wisdom. Sometimes the word <hebrew>יש</hebrew> **Iesc** <note>original: "Iesc", transliterated as "Yesh", meaning "Being" or "There is".</note>—that is, "something" or "it is"—also corresponds to the name **Ioh**. <margin>Genesis 28</margin> For the first dimension (that is, the **Crown**) is read to be called more sublimely <hebrew>אין</hebrew> **Ain** <note>original: "Ain", meaning "Nothing" or "Naught".</note>, that is, "Nothing." <margin>Yesh</margin> This is because in the contemplation of this sphere, the eyes of every mind grow dim, tongues fall silent, every voice is hushed and reduced to nothing. For this reason, among the characters, no element (except for the apex of the letter **Yod** <insert>Yod (except the apex)</insert>) is said to indicate the Crown itself. <margin>Ain</margin> But the second sphere succeeding the Crown, called **Wisdom**, reveals the truth of its own way of being. Therefore, it was permitted to call it by the surname **Iesc**. Jacob was the first to reveal this, saying truly: *Iesc (that is, God the Tetragrammaton) is in this place.* This was more condescending to Jacob himself than it was to Isaac and Abraham, because the Tetragrammaton, promising to Jacob, said: *And you shall be spread abroad to the East, the West, the North, and the South,* etc., where no limits of possession are established—something we read was by no means promised to the other fathers.

Israel, the master of the life of the coming age, attains the same measure, as it is written: <margin>Proverbs 8</margin> *I will cause my beloved to inherit Iesc, and I will fill their treasures,* etc. <margin>three hundred ten worlds</margin> Indeed, the structure of mercy involves **three hundred and ten worlds**, which the elders define as being destined as the reward for the righteous. <note>In Hebrew gematria, the word Yesh (Iesc) has a numerical value of 310.</note>

This same dimension is also frequently found named **Wisdom**, but not everywhere does "Wisdom" refer to this specific level. For frequently, "Wisdom" denotes the tenth sphere, namely the Temple of the **Kingdom**; as in, <margin>1 Kings 4</margin> *God the Tetragrammaton gave wisdom to Solomon,* etc. But the more exalted Wisdom, to which the letter **Yod** of the Tetragrammaton corresponds, was hidden even from **Moses**, the teacher of all the Prophets. Indeed, even he did not know all the gates of Prudence, let alone the Wisdom residing higher than Prudence, <margin>Job 28</margin> about which it is written: *And Wisdom is found from Ain (Nothing),* etc. For God (**Elohim**) understood its way, and *Hu*—that is, *He*—knew its place. <margin>Hu</margin> For only Prudence (called **Elohim**) opened the approach and showed the way to Wisdom; and only <hebrew>הוא</hebrew> **Hu** (that is, the superior Crown) gazes upon the place of this Wisdom, about which it is also read:

It interprets the biblical war with Amalek as a spiritual attack on the lower letters of the divine name.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Ricius's exposition on the mystical meanings of the letters in the Tetragrammaton (YHVH) and their correspondence to the Sephirot (divine emanations). # PAUL RICIUS,
<meta>catchword: machines</meta>

<margin>Psalms 129, 91. Ecclesiastes 7. Proverbs 9, 11, 15.</margin>
"The Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> founded the earth in wisdom," etc. Therefore, apply your study so that whenever you hear the name of **Wisdom**, you understand it as sounding from those twin letters of wisdom <note>Referring to the Yod and the first He of the Tetragrammaton.</note>. We must not omit, however, that this higher wisdom is never separated from **Prudence** <note>The Sephirah Binah.</note>; these two are simultaneously conferred by the excellent oracles of the **Crown** <note>The Sephirah Keter.</note> and **Mercy**. Since they fold together in an inexplicable knot, the name **Ioh** <note>original: "Ioh", the two-letter name Yah (Yod-He).</note> does not change its character at all. But a lower wisdom—that is, the final *He* of the name Tetragrammaton—is led away from the letter *Vav* when Israel falls into sin; wherefore, gathering itself into its higher part, the *Vav* is covered and hidden, as in the passage: "Who hides his face from the house of Jacob." It also pleased the wise men of the Kabbalists <note>original: "Cabalistarum"</note> to call the same **Razon** <note>Hebrew: רצון, meaning "Will".</note>: that is, **Will**. For the beginning of drawing the vow into Sephirotic <note>original: "sphiristicam"</note> dependence and appearance is judged to be from the supreme **Crown**. But by what path an outflow of this kind breaks forth, that immediately escapes the intuition of all created beings. It is this same Will by which the machine of the world is renewed, and wonders, signs, prodigies, and portents are performed. This same measure is also sometimes called **Omek** <note>Hebrew: עמק, meaning "Depth".</note>: that is, the **depth of thought**; for the abyss of this will is inscrutable, and its boundaries are utterly absent, concerning which it is said: "Out of the depths I have cried." And again: "Your thoughts are very deep." Wherefore it is also read as **Mahascaua** <note>Hebrew: מחשבה, meaning "Thought".</note>: that is, **Thought**. This is the "thinkable point" which typically demonstrates the beginning of the flow of the vow in the work of creation. This also shows the letter *Yod* of the name Tetragrammaton (which dwells enclosed within the sacred temple of the Crown), and upon that same point, the sincere machine of Mercy is extended into the infinite. It is enunciated in a plural sense as "thoughts" because there are thirty-two paths of wisdom fixed to the supreme Crown, which no one can see or discern unless he draws them from the fountain of Prudence. He who draws, however, is not immersed in the water of the origin, but standing outside, he is given to drink of the liquid from the drawing of the Waterman or the pitcher; according to what Solomon implies: "The deep, the deep, who [mi] <note>Ricius plays on the Hebrew word 'Mi' (who) being associated with the Sephirah Binah.</note> shall find it?" etc. The "deep deep" suggests Wisdom and the Crown; "who," however, suggests Prudence. Furthermore, any word designating "latency" or "hiding" hints at and refers to this same thing, such as: "They are hidden from me and I do not know." This is also uttered as **Girea** <note>Hebrew: יראה, usually 'Yirah', meaning "Fear" or "Awe".</note>: that is, **Fear**; for everyone who turns toward this hyperbolic fountain must be afraid, lest he wander further than the right of thinking permits, just as we read of Moses, whom a great terror shook in the sight of God [Elohim]; for it is written: "The fear of the Lord [Tetragrammaton] is the beginning of wisdom," and again: "The end of gentleness is the fear of God," as well as: "The fear of God is wisdom itself." Know, however, that fear is split into two: one internal, the other external. By the internal, we dread the horrible and weighty sight of the Most High; by the external, we fear the punishment of pain. The former is more sublime than love; the latter, struck down by horror, leaves behind things to be avoided. It is your task, therefore, to discern these twin kinds of fear at the opportune time.

<margin>Genesis 2. Isaiah 64. Genesis 2.</margin>
The Law also refers to this same measure by the name **Eden** <note>Hebrew: עדן</note>: that is, **Pleasure**. For in this fountain is established the origin through which all things flow and descend from the supreme Crown, upon which it leans: "and a river went out of Eden to water the garden." The river indeed, as we have stated before, designates Prudence; Eden is Wisdom; the garden is the Kingdom <note>The Sephirah Malkuth.</note>, which Prudence waters by means of the other intervening six <note>The six Sephirot from Chesed to Yesod.</note>. To this is added that mystical saying in the chapter *En dorsi* where they say: "Eye has not seen, O God [Elohim], but you." Where was Adam, then? He was indeed in the garden; yet do not think that "garden" and "Eden" denote the same thing; for it is read: "and a river went out of Eden," that is, out of pleasure. These are their words. You, however, if you make yourself worthy, will hear these deep and abstruse speeches by word of mouth.

The tenth name of the holy words is **Eheie** <note>Hebrew: אהיה, meaning "I Am".</note>, adapted to the Crown of the head, the understanding of which no one attains unless [he understands] it as belonging to Mercy...

<summary>Ricius explains that divine Wisdom (Chokhmah) is known by many names—including Will, Depth, Thought, Fear, and Eden—and describes how it flows from the Crown into the lower Sephirot. He emphasizes the distinction between internal awe of God's majesty and external fear of punishment.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Ricius's discussion of the Sephirot (divine emanations), moving from the nature of Wisdom and Will to the supreme Sephirah, the Crown (Keter), and its role as the source of infinite mercy and the origin of all existence.</meta>

# ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

The leader of this divine machine is the center, which is surrounded by twelve combinations <note>These are the permutations of the four-letter name of God, the Tetragrammaton.</note>. Like these combinations surrounding the Name, thirteen oracles of mercy respond to them. As I have explained previously, those who fly toward this divine machine—even if they are found guilty by judgment and defined as hopeless debtors—will, through the ineffable bounty of this mercy, drive away every harm. They immediately turn away the whirlwind of storms and do not allow the full force of clouded fortune to approach.

<margin>Exodus 3</margin>
For this reason, when the Israelites were in the oppression of Egypt and were not yet worthy of the prize of redemption, the name **Eheié** <note>Hebrew: *Ehyeh*, meaning "I AM."</note> shone forth. Seeking the assembly of the Israelites, God said to Moses: "**Eheié** [I AM] has sent me to you." Because the prophetic Synagogue of the ancient wise men knew how to connect the sublime sanctuary of **Eheié** [the Crown], the oracle of the **Tetragrammaton** [the attribute of Mercy], and the kingdom of **Edonai** <note>A Latinized spelling of *Adonai*, meaning "Lord," representing the Sephirah of Kingdom (Malkuth).</note>, they were accustomed to shaking off the dread of punishment and the rigid threats of the covenants in every event. To this refers the verse: "May the Tetragrammaton [the Lord] shine upon us," etc. For whenever you see the "light of his face" written in the sacred books, understand it as the proclamation of supernal mercy.

<margin>Numbers 6</margin>
Therefore, the priestly blessing established by the Law says: "May the Tetragrammaton make his face to shine upon you and be gracious to you." And also:

<margin>Psalm 4</margin>
"Many say: who will show us good? Lift up the light of your face upon us, Tetragrammaton," etc. The same measure of **Eheié** is also suggested by the apex of the letter *Yod*, as we touched upon above. Likewise, the pronoun <term>הוא</term> **Hu** <note>Hebrew for "He" or "It."</note>—that is, "He"—shows this, because residing in the highest hiding places, He presents Himself openly to no one. To understand exactly by what step this dimension of mercy opens itself to the other oracles, and how the measure of judgment in the Law transforms itself into grace, requires that instruction be handed down from mouth to mouth <note>A reference to the oral tradition of Kabbalah.</note>.

Furthermore, that sanctuary of the Crown, because of its inscrutable height, is read as <term>אין</term> **Ain** <note>Hebrew for "Nothing" or "Naught," referring to the Infinite (Ein Sof) beyond comprehension.</note>: that is, **Nothing**, according to the verse:

<margin>Psalm 120</margin>
"I will lift up my eyes to the mountains, from whence [**Ain**] comes my help." <note>Ricius is punning on the Hebrew word *Ayin* (whence/where), reading it as the divine name *Ain* (Nothingness/The Source).</note> For from there the remedy for every weakness, and the comfort and joy of the sorrowful, breaks forth into the temple of **Edonai** [the Lord]. This is the straight letter *Nun* <term>ן</term> turning into the bent *Nun* <term>נ</term>; clearly the straight *Nun* designates the machine of mercy, while the bent one designates the Kingdom.

The measure of the Crown is also found called <term>קדם</term> **Kedem**: that is, "Ancient" or "the East." For this, being the first of all beings, provides the beginning of existence to all things. Upon this rests the verse:

<margin>Genesis 2</margin>
"And the Tetragrammaton Elohim planted a garden in Eden *mi-kedem*": that is, from the east, or from the beginning. For the planting is in the garden, and the garden is in delight, which finally break forth together from the "East." Therefore, whenever the sacred letters bring forth the word **Kedem**, consider what high thing lies hidden there. Indeed, that ancient branch of division (the Tower of Babylon) had withdrawn from the "East" and presumed to build another name for itself, as it is read:

<margin>Genesis 11</margin>
"And let us make a name for ourselves," etc. Then the partitioning of mortals into many-tongued nations emerged. Until that time, the inhabitants of the same earth-zone had used a uniform speech, as it is written:

<margin>Genesis 11</margin>
"Now the earth was of one lip [language] and of the same words, and as they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and dwelt in it," etc. You, therefore, consider this, and by this example examine the proclamation of **Kedem** everywhere; you will surely comprehend the marvelous and hidden mysteries of the Law.

The oracle **Eheié** is also commonly called <term>כתר</term> **Keter**: that is, **the Crown**. For just as a diadem surrounds a royal head, so this measure encompasses the Sephirotic <note>original: "sphiristicum"</note> order, for which the hosts of both heavenly and earthly beings long and aspire.

Again, the name **Head of Laban** is usually applied to it: that is, the **White Head**. For this whitens and makes pure whatever crimes and sins Israel may have; for (as is well known) whiteness is the primary genus among colors. Finally, whatever is seen as a foul infection is removed. Just as the dimension of the Crown is established as the head of brightness, so outside the "head" a place is found where the greatest darkness dwells; to this refers the phrase: "Who separates between the holy and the profane, between light and darkness."

There is also another **Laban**, namely the Aramean—the deceiver and waylayer of men—who constantly strives to lead them into the dark measure of gloom. He truly sought to root out the Patriarch Jacob and his progeny and stock (as is his custom).

<margin>Genesis 30</margin>
But the power of the Most High, for whom Jacob established himself as a seat, together with the virtue of the rods...

<meta>This page concludes Book IV of Riccius's work, finishing the allegorical interpretation of Laban and the Tree of Knowledge, and transitioning toward the practical application of the ten "keys" or Sephirot discussed in the volume.</meta>

# PAUL RICCIUS ON CELESTIAL AGRICULTURE, BOOK IV.

...by virtue [of those rods], in which once the bark was removed, a whiteness shone forth that rescued him and his own, and protected them from all dangers <note>This refers to the story in Genesis 30 where Jacob uses peeled branches to influence the breeding of Laban's flocks; Riccius interprets the "whiteness" revealed under the bark as a symbol of divine protection and purity.</note>. Whoever, therefore, knows the symbolic source of this whiteness will be able to envision both the hidden beginning and the end of **Lebana** <note>original: "Lebana"; this is the Hebrew word for the Moon (*Levanah*), but also shares a root with Laban, meaning "white."</note> (that is, the Moon). For the ancient serpent, hanging from the power of Laban the Aramean, cast filth onto the Moon (on account of the first man’s transgression); for that first man, namely Adam, driven by his foreskin <note>In this mystical context, the "foreskin" represents a state of spiritual uncircumcision or the "husks" (*kelipot*) of impurity that resulted from the Fall.</note>, ate from the tree while it existed as both good and evil. But if he had shown restraint for only a single hour, whereby he might have claimed for himself a portion and place away from the reclaimed foreskin, the tree itself would have taken the name of "good" and not "evil." Through this, it would have been permitted for him to feed according to his desire and achieve indelible life, according to the mystery of the Tree of Life associated with the Tree of Knowledge, while only the good is admitted, as it is read: <margin>Deuteronomy 30</margin> "See, I have set before you life itself and good, death and evil," etc.

Thus, there is a wonderful and solid virtue in the Israelites' keeping of God’s commandments; for where the first Adam was unable to wait a single hour, <margin>Leviticus 19</margin> Israel observes a delay of three years. For it is written: "For three years they shall be as uncircumcised to you," etc. For there are three layers to the wall of the foreskin <note>Riccius is referring to the Kabbalistic concept of the three "impure husks" that conceal holiness.</note>, and in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy for praises to the God of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter divine name, YHWH.</note>, etc. For the fourth wall (as I have written above) remains thin; but in the fifth year you shall eat its fruit so that its produce may be an addition for you, etc. If Adam had likewise eaten the fruit in the fifth state, never would such a great punishment have been brought upon the world. 

Whenever, therefore, you hear the word **Laban** in the Law, or anything depending on it, sharpen the edge of your mind and weigh with a focused examination whether the understanding of the letter sounds like the white and innocent Laban, or the shameful and wicked Aramean <note>Riccius contrasts the historical Laban—often viewed as a deceiver—with the mystical "Laban," which represents the pure "Whiteness" of the highest Sephirah, Keter.</note>. Remember, however, that not only the Crown [Keter], but likewise the three higher oracles embraced by the most holy name of God, escape human understanding in this world, though in the future a rich knowledge of them will be granted to us. 

Gather together these ten keys, then, by which you will be able to enter the many-formed and hidden storehouses and the secret inner chambers of treasures, to which the entrance is granted to few indeed. Therefore, turn over each of the ten chapters of this present volume, and weave together the Law begun with the sacred surnames; add also the sacred surnames to the divine names, and compare the holy names everywhere with the name of the **Tetragrammaton**. Nor should you pass over the surnames with a light glance or in haste, but rather discern how each is adapted and fits with the sacred names and the **sphiristico** <note>A Latinization of "Sephirotic," referring to the ten emanations of God in Kabbalah.</note> assembly. If you perform this with burning faith, you will emerge as a companion of the sublime inner chambers of the Law; you will be made a participant in the ineffable secrets of God, and you will be enrolled in the number of those to whom the divine words promise: <margin>Psalm 90</margin> "I will strengthen him, because he has known my name." 

Therefore, dwell joyfully upon this summary as if it were the vestibule of a fortress to be unlocked, so that you may more readily perceive those things which I shall hereafter attempt to explain by the nod of the Most High. May He make us worthy of His inscrutable and lofty mercy, so that we may persist as steadfast cultivators of the desired doctrine and as executors of that same Law, proven by love, and that at last what is written may shine forth in us:

<margin>Isaiah 54</margin>
> Your sons shall be taught by God, and great shall be the peace of your sons. 
-> Amen. <-
