->### JOHN REUCHLIN<-

...when no eye has ever seen it, O God, besides you. <note>original: "cùm nec oculus quidem uidit nunquam, ô Deus præter te." A reference to Isaiah 64:4, often cited in mystical literature to describe the hidden rewards of the afterlife.</note> For there is a *Shabbaton* <note>original: "שבתון"</note>, a Sabbath of rest, and a *Sabbath of Sabbaths*, in which all pure souls, having finally cast off the stain of sin, will return freely to the prepared inheritance. They shall be sent into a possession truly our own and proper to us, which we have acquired and now hold through the soul of the Messiah. He is of the tribe of Judah, the seventh from the Patriarch Abraham <note>Reuchlin uses a symbolic genealogy here to link the Messiah to the number seven/Sabbath.</note>, acting as a representative in the highest horizon of the world, according to the scripture: *And it shall send out its roots over the Jubilee.* <note>original: "Et super Iubileum mittet radices suas."</note> Jeremiah 17. That most excellent Cabalist, *Sopher Ama*, interprets this in the book *Ha-Din* <note>original: "הדין," meaning "The Judgment."</note>—that is, the book of the governors—regarding the verse of the nineteenth Psalm, "Day unto day": <gloss>Each shall return to his family and to the inheritance of his fathers; that is to say, they shall ascend through the powers to the place of their emanation, which is the river of God full of water.</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: "איש אל משפחתו ואל אבותיו ישוב כלומר שיתעלו בכחות אל מקום אצילותן שהוא פלג אלהים מלא מים"</note> These are the words of Rabbi Ama; and these are the waters which are above the heavens in the intelligible World, <gloss>which is from the Holy Spirit</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: "שהיא מרוח הקדוש"</note>, where those who observe the Sabbath enjoy and feed upon the inheritance of their father Jacob, as *Isaiah* said.

Truly, this is the very Sabbath of the Cabalists, to be sanctified at all times. In it, we follow the will not of the flesh, but of the soul, and we meditate on divine things, intending nothing contrary to them. This stands as a law for all nations, since it has blossomed out of nature itself. For you, to whom the Law of *Moses* was not given, the ceremonies of the Jews do not bind you to serve by the letter of the number—as *Iarchas* <note>A legendary Indian sage mentioned in accounts of Apollonius of Tyana.</note> once recognized and Apollonius denied. Nor will I extort a specific number of observances from you; rather, I ask for a quiet and tranquil mind, devoted to God alone and to divine matters. This consists mostly in "analytical speculation," <term>analetica speculatione</term> <note>Simon refers to a process of resolving complex things back to their divine origins.</note> just as this discussion between us is what you have so greatly desired.

Then **Marranus** said: "It must certainly be completed. For I have begun to treat the Cabala as quite beautiful, now that you have shown us more than clearly that we not only can, but indeed *ought* to deal with the truth of the highest things today. Do you not ask the same as I do, **Philolaus**?" 

And **Philolaus** replied: "Most certainly. For indeed, we have now boarded the ship of this discipline, and we already feel at the very prow that the Cabala is nothing else but—to speak in the Pythagorean manner—**symbolic theology**. In this, not only are letters and names signs of things, but things themselves are signs of other things. We have noticed that almost all of Pythagoras’s philosophy was snatched from the Cabala; he likewise transferred the symbolic method of teaching to the Greeks. For this reason, I and this companion of mine earnestly pray that you continue by speaking and teaching us."

Then **Simon** said: "I would not presume to be so boastful as to dare to 'teach' you, nor would it be entirely safe in such a perplexed matter, not yet known to all my people—especially to those learned in the Roman fashion. This is true despite the very few things that the Count **Giovanni Pico della Mirandola** <note>A famous Italian Renaissance philosopher who first introduced the "Christian Cabala" to Europe.</note> and our own **Paulus Ricius** <note>A Jewish convert to Christianity and scholar who served as a physician to Emperor Maximilian I.</note> published formerly, which even to this day are not sufficiently understood by the Latins. For I fear that if I were to teach such foreign doctrines, the crowd of the envious might shamefully bark at me—just as has happened to many good men before. They condemn everything they do not know, and in their zeal for malice, they easily twist words into a sense foreign to the speaker's intent. *Cicero* calls such people 'calumniators'; if it is grammatically permissible to say so, I would call them 'Calumnians' <note>This is a sharp pun on *Colonienses*, the theologians of the University of Cologne, who were Reuchlin's primary enemies in his legal battles.</note>, whom you yourselves are also accustomed to call 'Pharisaical theologians.'

I will therefore pursue first what they intend last. For they take care to spend all your study and your entire labor on this one purpose: that in this life they may attain happiness, and in the future, a perpetual blessedness according to each person's capacity. They trust that this can happen most of all through this medium. Indeed, if at some point they diligently and actively grasp that which they feel is effective for the state of both Worlds, the possession of this, following its attainment, is perfect rest. For even all animals, however brute they may be, are seen to desire their own happiness when those things which they think best for themselves are...

<meta>This page continues Simon’s discourse on the ultimate goal of the soul. Having discussed the Sabbath of Sabbaths, he now describes the mystical process of seeking divine truth and the ascent of human reason toward God.</meta>

->### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.<-

...they may enjoy and reach those things that bring satiety to their desires. You see an ox grazing in some flowery and green meadow, not eating everything, but by deliberate choice seeking now this herb, now that. Suddenly it easily leaves one behind, and completely passes over another, until it arrives at the nourishment that is agreeable and invigorating to itself, in which it settles and rests. In this same way, the Cabalists, after traveling through the widest fields of the sciences and meadows of contemplation adorned with every pleasantness, taste many and various herbs of every scent, so that finally, having surveyed the entire pasture, they may find that **divine Moly** <note>original: "Moly." In Homer's *Odyssey*, this is a magical herb given by Hermes to Odysseus to protect him against Circe's magic.</note>. Although its root is black, its flower, in Homer’s opinion, is white and like milk; when this is found, it seems that all miseries are driven away, and they have achieved the happy end of their desire in this world. Indeed, the virtue of the Moly is this: the root represents difficult works, while the flower represents the tranquility of souls. One could not believe this to be anything other than the true happiness of the present age. 

Future beatitude, however, is the apprehension of the highest good, above which there is no good, and from which all goodness comes, which no mere creature can fully comprehend. But it is said to be apprehended when it is approached as closely as each person’s capacity allows—just as if someone catches the hem of a garment, they may be said to have caught the man wearing it. But that good which is named **God** cannot be clearly reached by us due to the fragility of our condition, except by ascending steps and ladders. These are certainly extended from the super-celestial realms to the earth—just as you are accustomed to speak of the **Homeric chain** <note>original: "Homericæ catenæ." A reference to the Golden Chain in the *Iliad* that connects Heaven and Earth.</note>, but as we Jews say according to the divine oracles, in the likeness of the **ladder of our father Jacob** <note>original: "scalæ Iacob." Referring to the ladder in Genesis 28:12 where angels ascend and descend.</note>. It is like a certain golden rope or cord directed toward us from heaven, or like a visual line penetrating various natures. 

For you behold the sun, whose ray travels to our sight through the sphere of Venus, through the sphere of Mercury, through the sphere of the Moon, through the sphere of Fire, and through the sphere of Air. It touches the opaque body of a concave mirror and is reflected from there to tinder or dry wool, which it vehemently ignites into ashes by its splendor. The appearance of that same flame reaches our eyes and is received by the interior sensation; once received, it is judged by the **estimative faculty** <term>estimatio: a psychological term in medieval philosophy for the faculty that perceives "intentions" or non-sensory qualities, like a sheep perceiving a wolf's danger.</term>. Finally, it is traversed by **Reason** <note>original: "ratio"</note> by returning along the path through which the entire present operation proceeded. 

Then, Reason prudently shows us in what way the internal forms are carried through the **animal spirits** <term>spiritus animales: in ancient and medieval medicine, these were subtle fluids that traveled through the nerves to facilitate sensation and movement.</term> to the imagination and the judgment of the estimation. It shows how external things are received by internal ones, and how the species is directed from the flame through the transparent medium to the pupil of the eye. It shows by what path the flame arose from the fire of the concave mirror, and how the ray was able to ignite it. Finally, it shows in what way the splendor is continued through many media that are not of the same nature as itself; and again, by what proportion the air is to be compared to the fire, the fire to the sphere of the Moon, and the remaining spheres to the others. Our Reason disputes each of these points through the journey of composition and resolution, walking back and forth, up and down, thinking now on this, now on that. It does not cease its reasoning until it has returned—by way of the **phantasm** <term>phantasma: a mental image derived from sense perception.</term>, the image, the intentions, the splendor, the light, and the illumination—to the very sun of which we speak. 

First, it considers the flame of the tinder which the eyes had seen; then, that its intention was produced from the thing seen through the **transparent medium** <note>original: "diaphanon"</note> to the eye outside and was also received within. It considers that the tinder is of the earth, that the splendor is of the air, that the flame is of fire, and that the brightness is an accident adhering to the transparent medium. It considers that it passes through the lucid and clear, whether that be air, or fire, or something celestial, according to the energy and peculiar operation of the **substantial form** <term>forma substantialis: the essential nature that makes a thing what it is.</term>. Then, always adapting its meditations to that which is more noble, having left matter behind, Reason begins to dispute within itself concerning **Form**. It does not speak of artificial form (for the scrutiny of such does not belong here, and is more rightly called "figure" than "form"), but only of natural or superior form. Thus Reason proceeds and finds some forms to be particular (existing "now" and "here"), while others are universal (existing "always" and "everywhere"). Then it finds some forms existing within particular bodies (giving them their being), others as co-existing forms (providing them with their specific qualities), and others entirely **separated** from corporeal essences in their power and operation—though for that reason they sometimes lose the name of "form"...

->### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.<-

...they are called either gods, or angels, or intelligences, or blessed souls, or by any other name belonging to the mind. However, whatever things are universal are called by many who have learned deeply not merely forms, but **Ideas** or **Species**. 

In this way, reason will indeed ascend as long as it is able, until it becomes exhausted by its own discursive wandering, finding that it cannot comprehend those forms that are neither within bodies nor attached to them—as if they were not subject to the laws of nature. Soon, reason summons the **intellect** as a support. Just as the intellect clearly abstracts the basic matter from the specific form of a certain donkey buried in a field—which nature then clothes with the form of grass blooming in the spring—so too the intellect attempts to abstract form itself simply from matter. 

This, however, it finds to be an arduous task full of labor; for it is easy to abstract matter from form <note>In Aristotelian thought, "matter" is the underlying substance, while "form" is what makes a thing what it is. It is easier to think of "stuff" without a shape than "shape" without any "stuff."</note>, but difficult to abstract form from matter. Therefore, that intellect elevates itself to a purer state, so that it may allow the higher Mind to flow into it. Relying on the clarity of this Mind, the intellect recognizes that some forms are entirely absolute—independent of bodies in their essence, power, and operation. Because of this, they are enclosed by neither place nor time, and one must truly consider them to be above the heavens, where motion and time cease. 

From this point, the intellect instructs our will to believe that there are certain beings beyond the heavens leading the most excellent life, which they enjoy for all eternity. There, it begins the **Second World** <note>original: "Mundum secundum," referring to the intelligible or archetypal world above the physical world.</note>, filled with living lights and the purest minds. This is the most secret place, which the human soul can enter through powerful contemplation—transcending the sphere of the Sun with the mind’s eye much more sharply than the physical eye can ever do. 

Just as we do not look at the sun unless the sun first shines upon us, so too we are unable to see divine reality unless it also sees us; for the Divine is itself "all eye," and brighter than the sun. We comprehend the sun through solar light; likewise, we comprehend divine things through divine light. And if we, with our physical sight, can grasp not only the sphere of the Sun but even the higher stars and the very heights of heaven, how much more should our mind—which infinitely surpasses physical power—be able to look higher and see the contents of the **Archetypal World**? For the concave and convex of the highest heaven are joined with such proximity that the horizon of eternity seems to be at no distance at all from that outer curve. 

Believe me, we gaze upon the divine things of that other world mutually, and they in turn gaze upon us, like two directly opposite mirrors reflecting each other back and forth along a single line of vision.

**Philolaus** then said: "Everything you teach, Simon, is Pythagorean, and proper to the **Italian philosophy** <note>The "Italian philosophy" refers to the school of Pythagoras, who lived in Southern Italy.</note> which Marranus and I discussed briefly yesterday."

To this, Simon replied: "I do not know what you choose to call Pythagorean, but I know that these things I have proposed are **Cabalistic**, handed down by the ancient Cabalists and all contained within the Divine Law of the Hebrews. From this arises that enumeration of the **Fifty Gates of Understanding**, which the Cabalists study so sweatily and which were received divinely by Moses, the servant of God. He also handed down the knowledge of these gates to us, his descendants, as they explain the condition of the entire universe. 

<note>Hebrew: "Thus our masters said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all of them were handed to Moses except one, for it is said: 'You have made him a little less than the gods [Elohim].'"</note>
כך אמרו רבותינו חמשים שערי בינה נבראו בעולם וכלן נמסרו למשה: חוץ מאחד שנא' ותחסרהו מעט מאלהים: 

That is to say, our Masters have already said: Fifty gates of understanding were produced in the world, and all of them were handed over to Moses except for one, because it is written: *You have made him a little less than the gods.* <note>Psalm 8:5. Reuchlin translates the Hebrew "Elohim" here as "gods" (Latin: *dijs*), following a common humanist and angelic interpretation.</note>

Regarding this discourse of the Cabalists, **Ramban** <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, also known as Nachmanides (1194–1270), a leading medieval Jewish scholar.</note> said in the beginning of his commentary on Genesis that everything handed to Moses through these gates of understanding is contained in the Divine Law of the Jews—either in the literal sense, or the allegorical sense, or through words, or through arithmetic calculations <note>Gematria</note>, or through the geometric shapes of the letters (whether as written or transformed), or through the harmonies resulting from the shapes of the characters, their junctions, their separations, their twisting, their straightness, their lack or excess, their smallness or greatness, their crowns <note>The "tagin" or decorative flourishes on certain Hebrew letters.</note>, their closure, their opening, and their order. 

And through that Law, the most wise King **Solomon** also obtained from the divine spirit everything that he knew. Concerning him, it is written in the Book of Kings that God gave him wisdom and very much prudence, like the sand on the seashore; and the wisdom of Solomon grew greater than the wisdom of all the people of the East and the Egyptians, and his wisdom was...

->### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III. 689<-

...he was wiser than all men, and he discoursed about trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he spoke also of beasts, of birds, of creeping things, and of fish. Beyond these things, Gerundensis <note>original: "Gerundensis"—referring to the 13th-century scholar Nachmanides, also known as Ramban, who lived in Girona.</note> confirms our opinion and concludes thus: *“And all this he knew through the Torah, and everything is found within it through its expositions”* <note>original Hebrew: וכל זה ידע בתורה והכל נמצא בה בפירושיה</note>; that is, he knew all these things through the Law, and found everything in it through his own expositions, through grammatical subtleties, through its letters, and through its "curlings" <note>original: "calamistrationes"—this refers to the *tagin* or decorative "crowns" found on certain Hebrew letters in a Torah scroll, which Cabalists believe hold hidden meanings.</note>. Moreover, this happened to him after he had fully attained the method of the forty-nine gates of intelligence <note>The "Fifty Gates of Intelligence" (Binah) is a Cabalistic concept representing levels of understanding; tradition says Moses reached the 49th gate, but only the 50th remains hidden.</note>, which open the knowledge of all created things. For all things are universally distributed into five conditions. For they are either elements, or things made of elements, or souls, or celestial bodies, or super-celestial incorporeal beings. Each of these perhaps receives ten considerations, the headings of which are as follows: the most general genera, special genera, general species, the most special species, and individual things, which further consist of matter and form (or something proportional to both), and are narrowed down into singular differences, properties, and accidents. 

These ten modes—of both essences and intelligences—multiplied by five, open the fifty gates through which we enter into the inner secrets of the creatures designated by those eminent marks in the works of the six days [of creation], which were studiously grasped and received by the Cabalists. Now, by this artifice, that enigmatic knot proposed by the Count of Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, a famous Renaissance philosopher and contemporary of Reuchlin.</note> among his *Nine Hundred Conclusions* will easily be unraveled. For he said thus: *"He who shall know what the number ten is in formal arithmetic, and shall know the nature of the first spherical number, shall know the secret of the fifty gates of intelligence, and of the great Jubilee, and of the thousandth generation, and the kingdom of all ages."* These are Mirandola's words. 

Therefore, I would wish that a flat sphere or circle of ten numerical figures be drawn around a center which is five; for five is the middle of the ten, and in its circumference, the individual numbers of the decimal calculation should be described. Let the diameter pass from the minimum to the maximum: that is, from one to nine, the division of which will create two semicircles. On the right side of the sphere, after the one and before the nine mentioned above, let two, three, four, and five be placed; on the left side, after the one and before the nine, let five, six, seven, and eight be placed, and let lines be drawn through the center from two to eight, from three to seven, from four to six, and from five to five. Then, if you subtract from each maximum as much as it exceeds five (which is the center of the decimal sphere) and add that same amount to its minimum (which fell short of five), the results from both opposite numbers will always rise as an equalized five and five. Therefore, when the points of the lines are compared in turn, every numerical description of the lines results in five and five. 

The number five, therefore, in the circle of the decimal revolution, is called "spherical" because, as you have seen, all numbers of the sphere are reduced to five. This is done through the five lines drawn in the sphere, each of which contains ten. Thus, when that spherical number is multiplied by ten, the fifty are born—whether you call them the gates of intelligence or the years of the Jubilee. Its "double proportion" <note>A term from formal arithmetic relating to ratios.</note>, which is the formality of arithmetic, when multiplied by itself, will procreate the "thousandth generation." If you continue to do this perpetually, infinity will appear, which is the Kingdom of All Ages, named *Ensoph* <note>original: "Ensoph"—the *Ein Sof*, the Infinite or "Without End," representing God before any self-manifestation.</note> by the Cabalists; it is the Deity itself without a garment. For God produced the remaining things "clothed in light as with a garment," so that there might be light from light; and thereafter, with the light of His garment, He created the Intelligible World of separate and invisible spirits, which the Cabalists call "Heaven," as you have often heard from me. 

In this way, I understand the words of the wisest and greatest Rabbi Eliezer, who, when he proposed the question of whence the heavens were created, answered: *"He took from the light of His garment"* <note>original Hebrew: מאור לבושו לקח</note>. These things are recounted by Moses Maimonides, the "Shower of the Perplexed" <note>Reuchlin uses a Latin title for Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed* (*Moreh Nevukhim*).</note>, in Chapter 26 of Book 2; and by the younger Rabbi Joseph of Castile <note>Joseph Gikatilla, a prominent 13th-century Cabalist.</note> (or of Cuenca) in the second volume of the *Garden of the Nut* <note>Gikatilla's work *Ginat Egoz*.</note>. Moses, the servant of God, ascended this far, so that he might know the light of His garment, and the Sabbath...

<meta>This page continues the discourse of Simon the Cabalist, who is explaining the "Fifty Gates of Intelligence"—a hierarchical ladder of understanding that leads from the physical world up to the divine essence. He is currently discussing the limits of human knowledge, even for figures as great as Moses, Joshua, and Solomon.</meta>

->### JOHANNES REUCHLIN<-

...the Sabbath of Sabbaths, and the Jubilee mentioned above, and the thousandth generation, all of which is nothing other than the higher World of Ideas, of angels, and of souls. Therefore, since he was unable to transcend the garment of God or to see His face, it is rightly said that he stopped at the limit of the fifty gates of intelligence, which some of our people believe to be the *Resurrection* <note>original Hebrew: תחיית, *Techiyat*</note>. However, I do not agree with them; rather, I think it is the essence of God, which the *Tetragrammaton* <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH, which Cabalists consider the key to all reality.</note> symbolically indicates, and it is a World incomparable by any grasp or proportion. For God said to Moses: "You cannot see my face." Or more truly: "And my faces shall not be seen, but I will call the name Tetragrammaton before you," in Exodus 33, which the Cabalists explain: *I will call before you that great name which you will not be able to see* <note>original Hebrew: אקרא לפניך בשם הגדול שלא תוכל לראותו</note>; for so Ramban <note>Nachmanides, the 13th-century commentator.</note> writes. From this it clearly appears that God, being identical to His own Tetragrammaton, was not seen by Moses. This is surely the principle of all gates, above every creature, existing before the beginning of creation, of which we read: "God created heaven and earth." The Chaldean translation of Onkelos <note>An influential ancient Aramaic translation of the Torah.</note> sounds like this: "The Tetragrammaton created heaven and earth." God the Tetragrammaton therefore created all things—He whom I have heard you call the *Tetractys* <note>A Pythagorean term for the number ten, which Reuchlin identifies with the ten letters of the expanded name of God.</note>. Moreover, Rabbi Eliezer said, as it stands in his chapters: *Until the world was created, there was only the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His name* <note>original Hebrew: עד שלא נברא העולם היה הקב''ה ושמו בלבד</note>. Other Cabalists also assert this with the testimony of Moses the Egyptian <note>Moses Maimonides.</note> in the 29th chapter of the second book of *The Perplexed*: *From the beginning, when there was no thing at all, there was nothing but the name of God and His wisdom* <note>original Hebrew: שלא היה שום דבר נמצא כלל אלא השם וחכמתו</note>. Therefore, before there was any of the creatures according to the doctrine of the Cabala, there was nothing but God, His name the Tetragrammaton, and His wisdom.

Certainly our tradition contains only these three, which constitute the first gate of creation that was by no means open to our teacher Moses. Wherefore it is said that he investigated the divine Law only through forty-nine gates. Joshua, however, had one less, namely forty-eight. For so we have received in the book of the explanations of the alphabet by Rabbi Akiba: *And after the death of Moses, one gate was hidden from Joshua, and forty-eight gates remained to him; and Solomon labored over that gate to restore it, but he was not able* <note>original Hebrew: מהתו של משה נתעלם מיהושע שער אחד ונשארו לו מח שערים ושלמה נתקשה על אותו שער להחזירו ולא היה יכול</note>. The Cabalists have received it so because it is written of Moses in Deuteronomy 34: "There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses." Therefore, Joshua was not able to ascend as far as Moses had ascended; for that reason, he is affirmed to be one degree lower. Concerning Solomon, however, we read in Ecclesiastes 12 that he sought to find pleasant words; but the Cabalists add that God commanded him: "Write correctly the words of truth." We say these were the things handed down and received through the way of the Cabala, so that he would not dare to write anything else except what he had received; and that was two degrees lower than the reception of Moses.

After God, the second gate is the Archetypal World, which is called "Heaven," created by God the Tetragrammaton in wisdom, according to the Jerusalem Targum <note>A collection of Aramaic translations and expansions of the Hebrew Bible.</note> which, in place of *In the beginning* <note>original Hebrew: בראשית, *Bereishit*</note>, put *In wisdom* <note>original Hebrew: בחכמא, *Be-chokhma*</note>. This confirms what we have said: that in wisdom God the Tetragrammaton created heaven, the chamber of the angels. This was not clearly explained by Moses, lest a raw and rustic people—either through not understanding—might hold it cheap or find an occasion for idolatry. But this visible world is understood as the "earth," which we affirm to be the third among the gates. Through "the void" we shall think matter is symbolically noted, the fourth gate of intelligence. Through "the empty"—that is, privation—the fifth. And the sixth is the abyss of their natural appetite. Then follow the remaining gates for the works of the six days. For already the marks of the four elements indicate four gates; and the pure element of fire, according to Moses the Egyptian in the 26th chapter of the second book of *The Perplexed*, is called "darkness," the spirit "air," and "water" the elemental moisture.

He details how subsequent leaders like Joshua and Solomon possessed progressively less access to this divine wisdom, and begins mapping the gates onto the elements and the story of creation.</summary>

# ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

Light is the substantial form <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, the "substantial form" is the essential nature of a thing.</note>; day represents the "accidents" <note>Secondary properties like color or weight that do not change a thing's essence.</note> which most help us to know what a thing is. Night signifies hidden properties. Evening is the way of corruption, and Morning the way of generation. "One Day"—which for a specific reason is not called the "first day" but "day one"—signifies the composite whole brought forth into the light. On the second day, the waters above the firmament are the universal types of things. The firmament is the horizon of eternity and time. The waters beneath the firmament are the natural influences of the celestial bodies. On the third day follows the other visible and material heaven, namely the nineteenth gate; then the earth we walk upon, then the seas we sail, and then the plants, seeds, wood, and fruit. On the fourth day come the luminaries, signs, seasons, days, years, splendor, the Sun, and the Moon—planets by which the others are understood through the communication of heat and cold, dryness and moisture. Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter (along with their Sun) heat and dry; Mercury and Venus (along with their Moon) moisten and cool, even if these seven spheres are specifically distinguished. Furthermore, the remaining stars designate the thirty-ninth gate. Then, on the fifth day, living souls come forth, which is the life of mortals: the creeping things in the waters, whales, and fish; and generally the flying things, and specifically the birds. On the sixth day, the progressive animal on the earth, the terrestrial reptile, cattle, and beasts. Finally, the fiftieth gate, which is man. These are the forty-nine modes of knowing created things, the <term>Gates of Understanding</term> <note>original Hebrew: שערי בינה, *Sha'arei Binah*</note>, and the supreme gate is the one Creator of all, fully known by no man except the Messiah; for he himself is the light of God and the light of the nations, and therefore he both knows God, and God is known through him.

For the Royal Prophet David cries out to God: "Send forth your light," which Rabbi Solomon the Frenchman <note>original: *Rabi Salomon Gallus*; this refers to Rashi, the famous 11th-century Jewish commentator from France.</note> interprets as <note>original Hebrew: המשיח שנתדמה לאור שג' ערכתי נר למשיחי</note> "the Messiah, who is compared to light, because it is written: I have prepared a lamp for my Christ." And Isaiah says: "I have given you as a covenant for the people, for a light to the nations." And again: "The nations shall walk in your light." Furthermore, Aristotle wrote what I believe to be true: that vision cannot happen without light, as we read in his book *On the Soul*: <note>original Greek: ουχ ορατον ανευ φωτος</note> "Nothing is visible without light." Therefore, as we walk toward the inspection of all things, it is very helpful to bring a light for the journey, so that we may choose with mature foresight a path by which we can proceed without injury to our feet. Toward this end, the Cabalists received certain luminous tracks and illustrious experiments, which they named the <term>Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom</term> <note>original Hebrew: ל"ב נתיבות החכמה, *Lamed-Bet Netivot Ha-Chokhmah*</note>. These are mentioned in the *Book of Creation* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah*, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note>, which begins thus: <note>original Hebrew: בשלשים ושתים נתיבות פלאות חכמה חקק יה יהוה צבאות שמו</note> "With thirty-two wondrous paths of wisdom, Yah, the Lord of Hosts [the Tetragrammaton Zabaoth], engraved or carved His name."

Concerning this, Rabbi Jacob Cohen wrote that by saying "wondrous," it signifies that these paths are secret, stored away, and hidden—confirming this interpretation through the Targum <note>An ancient Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Bible.</note>. And the commentator Rabbi Isaac, in his work on that same book of <term>Creation</term> <note>original Hebrew: יצירה, *Yetzirah*</note>, testifies that the ancient sages—men of heart, gentle and upright, who were highly practiced in the Cabala through the foundations of the Law—taught us that our ancestors and fathers walked through many ways until they finally stood in those paths which are called the "admirable things of wisdom," handed down by Zadkiel <note>In Jewish tradition, Zadkiel is the angel of mercy and memory, sometimes associated with instructing Abraham.</note> to our father Abraham in the tradition of the covenant. These are his words. I shall therefore recount them to you, my excellent listeners, if you judge them worthy of your esteem.

And Philolaus said: "Proceed, I beg you."
And Marranus added: "Indeed, I implore you both to weave together the story you have begun."

Then Simon said: "The thirty-two paths stretch from the highest peak to the lowest base. They are to be noted in this way, of which the first is the <term>Miraculous Intelligence</term> <note>original Hebrew: שכל מופלא, *Sekhel Mufla*</note>. It is called so by some, but it would be much more correctly named the 'Hidden Intelligence.' For Rabbi Solomon the Frenchman, in his book on Deuteronomy chapter 30, proves that this word <note>original Hebrew: מובלא, *mufla*</note> signifies 'hidden' <note>original Hebrew: מבונה, *mivuna*</note> in the verse: 'For this commandment which I command you today is not above you.' There he teaches it should be read as 'it is not hidden from you,' and the same is shown through the Chaldean translations cited there. It is a light giving understanding to things preceding without beginning, and it is named the 'First Glory,' since no mere creature...

...it is able to approach His essence and truth. The second is שכל מקודש <note>Sekhel mequddash</note>, that is, the **Sanctifying Intelligence**. It is the foundation of eternal wisdom, which is called the parent of faith, because faith is infused by its power. The third is שכל שלם <note>Sekhel shalem</note>, that is, the **Perfected Intelligence**. It is the concentration of the principles [of things], which does not take root except to lead some things back into the inner chambers of its majesty, which are founded by the preceding one. The fourth is שכל טהור <note>Sekhel tahor</note>, that is, the **Pure Intelligence**. It purifies the Cabalistic emanations <note>Latin: numerationes, referring to the Sephirot or divine countings</note> and corrects their representation, as well as their boundaries and extremes, so that they might exist without division or cutting. The fifth is שכל מוהיר <note>Sekhel mahir</note>, that is, the **Radiant Intelligence**. It is called the "second splendor" by the Cabalists. The sixth is שכל מתנוצץ <note>Sekhel mitnotsets</note>, that is, the **Resplendent Intelligence**. It is called the throne of splendor; it illuminates the brightness of the luminaries and pours out from its own prefect over surfaces and heights. The seventh is שכל מנהיג <note>Sekhel manhig</note>, that is, the **Guiding Intelligence**. It is the throne of glory itself and perfects the truth of spiritual communications. The eighth is שכל נמרש <note>Sekhel namrash</note>, that is, the **Differentiated Intelligence**. It is called the "fitting union" and is the proper quality of Prudence itself, which is derived from the higher wisdom. The ninth is שכל נצחי <note>Sekhel nitshi</note>, that is, the **Triumphant** or **Eternal Intelligence**. It is called the Paradise of Pleasure, prepared for the holy ones. The tenth is שכל מועשר <note>Sekhel mu’ashar</note>, that is, the **Enriched Intelligence**. It prepares the holy ones in faith so that they might be enveloped by the Holy Spirit; this is what is called <term>Tiferet</term> <note>Hebrew for "Beauty," the central Sephirah of the Tree of Life</note> in the higher state. 

The eleventh is שכל צחורי <note>Sekhel tsahuri</note>, that is, the **Intelligence of Clarity**. It is the essence of those purities called *tsahurot* <note>Pure or white things</note>, because from it arises the vision for prophets who see with true sight. The twelfth is שכל קבוע <note>Sekhel qavu'a</note>, that is, the **Fixed Intelligence**. It is a notable rapture from which spiritual virtues flow, like one infusion from another, according to the energy of the one flowing in. The thirteenth is שכל נסתר <note>Sekhel nistar</note>, that is, the **Hidden Intelligence**. It illuminates only the powers of those intellects who, through abstract thought, see hidden things. The fourteenth is שכל מאיר <note>Sekhel me’ir</note>, that is, the **Illuminating Intelligence**. It is <term>Hashmal</term> <note>Hebrew: חַשְׁמַל</note> itself, the angel of Ezekiel, appearing like amber; it is the instructor of the mysteries of the holy creatures <note>The Hayot or "living creatures" from Ezekiel's vision of the Chariot</note> of the sanctuary and their intentions. The fifteenth is שכל חזות <note>Sekhel hazut</note>, that is, the **Intelligence of Vision**. It arranges the order by which one is allowed to ascend the degrees of ascent. The sixteenth is שכל נאמן <note>Sekhel ne’eman</note>, that is, the **Faithful Intelligence**. Through it, the virtues of grace are increased according to the lives of those in whom they dwell. The seventeenth is שכל נסיון <note>Sekhel nisayon</note>, that is, the **Probationary Intelligence**. It is the trial and preceding proof in which the gift of the Blessed God consists toward all the holy ones. 

The eighteenth is שכל קיים <note>Sekhel qayyam</note>, that is, the **Sustaining Intelligence**. It is the virtue that operates within the Cabalistic emanations; if anything is lacking in them, it clothes them in the rationale of its own sanctity. The nineteenth is שכל רוחני <note>Sekhel ruhani</note>, that is, the **Spiritual Intelligence**. It provides for all created things, and through it, the Cabalists know the truth of the higher essence. The twentieth is שכל מעמיד <note>Sekhel ma’amid</note>, that is, the **Establishing Intelligence**. It makes creation itself stand in the "Pure Darkness." And the Masters of the Cabala say that this is the darkness according to the verse: "Darkness is round about Him" <note>Psalm 97:2</note>. The twenty-first is שכל מחודש <note>Sekhel mehuddash</note>, that is, the **Renewing Intelligence**, through which all created things in this world are repaired and renewed. The twenty-second is שכל בית השפע <note>Sekhel beit ha-shefa</note>, that is, the **Intelligence of the House of Abundance**. From the midst of its infusion are drawn the secrets and the hidden things which dwell in its shadow and cling to the study of the production of diligence, promoting one to the heights. The twenty-third is שכל הפעולות <note>Sekhel ha-pe’ulot</note>, that is, the **Intelligence of Activities**. It is the collection and totality of spiritual operations, so called because of the influence that gathers in it from the source of the higher sea and the sublime glory. The twenty-fourth is שכל נבדל <note>Sekhel nivdal</note>, that is, the **Separate Intelligence**. Through it, the influence of graces is collected, and it pours out abundance into all, as though from the cisterns or pools of blessings appropriated from itself. The twenty-fifth is שכל כללי <note>Sekhel kelali</note>, that is, the **Universal Intelligence**. By this, astrologers, through the judgment of the stars, gather universal events and perfect their knowledge of them through their spheres and orbs. The twenty-sixth is שכל נעזר <note>Sekhel ne’ezar</note>, that is, the **Assisting Intelligence**. It runs to support all the operations of the planets and other celestial influences. ### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...of [the Sun] and Moon according to their conditions. The twenty-eighth is שכל מרגש <note>Sekhel murgash</note>: that is, the **Bodily Intelligence**, which gives form to every body that is corporealized beneath the spheres, as well as their magnitude. The twenty-ninth is שכל החפץ המבוקש <note>Sekhel ha-chefetz ha-mevuqqash</note>: that is, the **Intelligence of the Sought-After Delight**; it receives the divine infusion so that it may participate in the "irrigation" <note>A Cabalistic metaphor for the flow of divine energy or grace</note> of that infusion over all created things. The thirtieth is שכל מורגש <note>Sekhel moragesh</note>: that is, the **Intelligence Exciting the Senses**, by which beings beneath the highest sphere and all types of mixed elements are created. The thirty-first is שכל דמיוני <note>Sekhel dimyoni</note>: that is, the **Imaginary Intelligence**, by which all created figures and images are varied and altered according to the surfaces of things and their inherent natures. The thirty-second is שכל מוטבע <note>Sekhel mutba</note>: that is, the **Natural Intelligence**, by which the nature of material things beneath the sphere of the Moon is brought to its final perfection.

I have summarized in this brief catalog, for you who are so eager for external teachings, what our ancestors have treated in many books with much difficult study concerning both the "Fifty Gates of Prudence" and the "Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom." This subject is surely worthy of a better teacher and involves much "sweat," yet it has the greatest power to urge us to live almost always in the company of angels, contemplating the highest and most divine matters. If we begin to be familiar with these things, nothing will be difficult for us to say or do. That familiarity is won through the letters of the alphabet, which are the angels' own gift to us.

If we apply these letters to the ten Cabalistic "numerations" <note>The Sephirot, or the ten stages of divine emanation</note>, the number thirty-two immediately arises. This is what we read in the *Book of Formation* <note>The Sefer Yetzirah, one of the oldest and most foundational books of Jewish mysticism</note>: עשר ספירות בלימה ועשרים ושתים אותיות <note>original Hebrew: Eser Sefirot Belimah ve-Esrim u-Shtayim Otiyot</note>, which means: "Ten numerations of nothingness, and twenty-two letters." Therefore, many writers combine these ten properties (which deserve to be contemplated in silence) and the twenty-two letters to form this total sum of "paths." I have arranged them in this order according to my own custom, though others do not always observe the same sequence.

But indeed, if we carefully apply that assembly of letters to the fifty "gates," we find from that calculation the blessed series of the seventy-two angels. It is from these that the *Semhamaphores* <note>A Latinization of "Shem HaMephorash," the "Explicit Name" of God</note>—that is, the great explanatory name of the most high God—is said to consist. For when twenty-two is added to fifty, they produce seventy-two. These are the mighty angels of the whole earth, through whom it is believed that Moses, that worker of miracles, divided the sea with his hand until it was dry, for they are the "angels of division." As it is written: *And God divided the earth according to the number of His angels.*

Indeed, in the *Book of the Gates of Justice* <note>Sha'are Tzedek</note>, which Rabbi Joseph Ben Carnitol <note>Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305), a Spanish Cabalist</note>, a celebrated master in the Cabala, wrote, we read among other things: ונשארו כל אומות מסורות ביד ע' שרים <note>original Hebrew: ve-nish'aru kol umot mesurot be-yad 70 sarim</note>, which means: "And all nations were left delivered into the power of seventy prefects"—that is, the prince-angels. To these, Recanati <note>Menahem Recanati (1250–1310), an influential Italian Cabalist</note>, a most skilled Cabalist, in his commentary on Genesis 48, assigns those seventy palm trees near the twelve springs which you know from the scriptures <note>A reference to Elim in Exodus 15:27</note>.

Furthermore, it is certain that there were two pillars there, one of cloud and one of fire, over which two angels were placed. Therefore, we may reasonably believe that in that same parting of the sea and the liberation of the children of Israel, the seventy angels of the world and those two "pillar" angels came to Moses' aid in the service of salvation. This salvation comes to us plainly from the ineffable *Tetragrammaton* <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> through seventy-two names, which are gathered and explained from Sacred Scripture in Exodus 14, from the verse beginning "And the angel... taking himself up" <note>Exodus 14:19</note> until the end of the passage where it reads "and the water was divided" <note>Exodus 14:21</note>. These are certainly sacred seals for us, stored in our memory in this present age; they are symbols by which angels were called to help humanity, to the praise and glory of the ineffable God. Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator</note> wrote of this in his exposition of the Talmud, as testified by the scholar of Gerona <note>Nahmanides (1194–1270), also known as Ramban</note> in the beginning of his commentary on Genesis. Therefore, these are the characters of the symbols, which I draw for you with my finger:

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between Simon the Cabalist and his students, Marranus and Philolaus. Simon is moving from the general theory of the "Thirty-Two Paths" to the practical demonstration of how the names of the 72 angels are extracted from the book of Exodus.</meta>

### JOHANNES REUCHLIN

I will demonstrate the matter, if the powers above are present and if you are ready to listen to me. 

"We are most ready," they both say, "we who have faced such great dangers on our journeys and spent such great sums for this very reason. But proceed," they say, "so that we may learn something of those angels whose names, **Marranus** says, he has never heard before; **Philolaus** believes the same." 

"Certainly," Simon says, "just as those angels have never been seen, so their names are unknown to me; but we shall love the pursuit best if you proceed without ceasing." 

Then **Simon** says: "That there were many angels who converged for such a great and wonderful work of **Moses**, when he divided the waters so that the **Israelites** might cross with dry feet, we can discover from **Scripture** itself, lest anyone think me a deceiver. For the divine words in that place are these: <note>Exodus 14:19</note> *ויסע מלאך האלהים* <note>original: "Vayisa malakh ha-Elohim"; translation: "And the angel of God moved"</note>. It is not as you pronounce it in *Latin*: *And the angel of the Lord, lifting himself up*. For *Adonai* <note>The Hebrew name for Lord</note> is not placed here, which we interpret as 'Lord,' but *Elohim*, which you likewise read daily translated as 'angels' in the verse: *You have made him a little lower than the angels* <note>Psalm 8:6</note>. And: *In the sight of the angels I will sing praise to you* <note>Psalm 138:1</note>. Yet it is not written here as it frequently is elsewhere as 'the angel of *Elohim*.' Instead, it is memorably written as *ha-elohim* <note>The God/The Angels</note> with the definite article intervening, as if the **Sacred History** wished to say: 'Through this angel of the cloud preceding the camp, recognize that there are also many other most powerful angels present, the princes of the world.' 

The **Talmud** agrees with us in the *Mechilta* <note>A legal and midrashic commentary on Exodus</note>, where **Rabbi Nathan** seeks the solution to this question from our master **Simeon ben Jochai** <note>The traditional author of the Zohar</note>, my kinsman. 'I ask,' he said, 'why it is written everywhere as the "angel of *Adonai*," but here as the "angel of *ha-elohim*"?' To which he responds: *אין אלהים בכל מקום אלא דיין* <note>original: "Ein Elohim be-khol maqom ella dayan"; translation: "The word 'Elohim' in every place signifies nothing other than a judge or a ruler"</note>. Therefore, that angel is understood to have been present together with the seventy rulers of the provinces, and for that reason he is called *malakh ha-elohim*, the angel of those rulers or prefects; and again, another angel of fire was the companion of those same rulers. Thus, by the best right, seventy-two merit recognition, whose signs you have already seen described by me. If you wish—because you do wish, for I know you are eager—I will teach you by what path they are drawn out from the Sacred letters. 

Now take these three verses: *ויסע ויבא ויט* <note>Exodus 14:19, 20, and 21. Each verse in Hebrew contains exactly 72 letters</note> and, in the manner of an upright column, write each one down in the **Cabalistic** fashion from right to left, so that the letters of each verse follow one another continuously from top to bottom. Then place the first character of the first verse, which is named *Vav*. Next, take the last character of the second verse in reverse order, which is *He*. Then, finally, return to the beginning of the third verse, which you will find is again *Vav*. When you have joined these three characters in that order, the memorial of the first angel is born: *Vav He Vav* <note>The first of the 72 names of God/Angels</note>. And the second is *Yod Lamed Yod*. And the third is *Samekh Yod Tet*. So also for the remaining names, always in groups of three. By the present method, with the three columns erected as they ought to be, any explanatory sign of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> will be forged. 

Oh, look, consider, and contemplate well: is this not the height of joy, surpassing all the gladness of this age, to remember the holy nods of **God** and the divine countenances which the **Hebrews** call **Malchim**, the **Greeks Angels**, and the **Latins Gods**? To handle in mind and hands things so pure, so pious, and so consecrated; to converse studiously with those most learned forms, whose splendor is seen only by the keen-sightedness of the blessed spirits, who love us fraternally more than is the custom of all mortals—and they do not just value us, but truly love us. The very walls seem to me to dance and to congratulate us men that, by the goodness of **God**, it has come to pass that through certain seals and skillful markings <term>charagmata <gloss>inscribed marks or symbols</gloss></term> of human weakness, we are admitted into the joyful assemblies of the angels, according to the capacity of our strength. With them, let us rejoice and be glad with a tranquil heart; let us worship and venerate them, and bestow upon them the honor due to such a sublime nature, by whom we are in turn loved, instructed, and guarded."

Then **Marranus** says: "I see the characters indeed, but I do not hear the sounds of the names; by what pronunciation therefore..."

### ON THE ART OF THE CABALA, BOOK III.

...I do not know by what pronunciation the angels may be invoked. To this **Simon** replied: Just as they are seen by the eyes, so are they heard by the ears; and just as they see us, so do they hear those who call upon them. I will explain in two words how this can be: *In spirit and in truth* <note>John 4:24</note>, so that the angels have such ears as our minds have tongues. And just as divine spirits speak with the tongues of angels, so may human spirits listen with the ears of their minds. Therefore, they do not impose names upon themselves out of a necessity because they wish to be named and summoned openly; rather, they hand down <term>signacula memorativa</term><note>Latin: "memorial signs" or "memory-markers"</note> because they desire to be remembered by us. You should not think that all divine power lies hidden merely in the voice.

These symbols, therefore, require a frequent memory of the angels, whose diligent remembrance leads us into the love of God, and in turn, love leads into a mutual dwelling. For we frequently remember those whom we love strongly, as the proverb says: *Lovers remember all things.* For this reason, God granted us the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Name of God: YHWH</note>, not so that we might call Him by it—for it is ineffable, and rightly called by you **Anechphoneton** <note>Greek: "unutterable"</note>, that is, not vocally expressible. For what did the Creator respond to **Moses** when he asked, "What is your name?" He certainly said this: *I.H.V.H.*: *This is my name forever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation* <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. The **Tetragrammaton** is, therefore, a name for eternity, but for the generation of mankind, it is only a memorial, because no human voice can compose a name that could equal the nature of divinity.

We know the angels by their works; therefore, we likewise pronounce names according to those same works of power: such as **Raphael** from medicine <note>Hebrew: "God heals"</note>, **Gabriel** from manliness <note>Hebrew: "God is my strength"</note>, and **Michael** from awe and wonder, which is interpreted as *Who is so strong?* <note>Commonly interpreted as "Who is like God?"</note>. As for their own proper names, we are ignorant of them; the weakness of our mortality is not able to find them, nor to impose them once found, except insofar as it is granted to us by divine revelation. 

From the numbers and figures handed down by God, the most contemplative men set about forming names for themselves according to the wills of the angels, just as children are taught to compose words from letters—whether Hebrew, Greek, Roman, Arabic, or Egyptian. It is not that the voice to be enunciated needs letters of that kind, but rather because of the weakness of our memory. These names are like "notations" which stir our senses by either figure or voice; in turn, the senses move the imagination, the imagination moves the memory, memory moves reason, reason moves the intellect, the intellect moves the mind, and the mind moves the angel. 

A certain philosopher among your people, of distinguished name, **Maximus of Tyre**, wrote something on this subject quite elegantly in his eighth dissertation, *Whether one should pray to God* <note>original Greek: ἐν τῷ εἰ φωνὴ τῇ αλεξέωρ ἢ πρώτης ἐπιθυμίας</note>. From this, it becomes known to you by conjecture that it is enough if you read the three verses—previously decoded by me out of reverence and veneration for the seventy-two angels—in the sequence dictated by the **Holy Spirit**. By your affection for them, you shall apply yourselves to the most burning love and ecstatic adoration of the name of the most high God. Consider carefully that just as the number seventy-two proceeds from the number of the **Tetragrammaton** by an arithmetic proportion, so the seventy-two angels are produced from the "signet" of the Creator by a certain divine outflow. 

Since any Hebrew letter designates a specific number, from **Iod**, **He**, **Vav**, **He**, seventy-two arises in this manner: 
*   **Iod** <note>Y</note> denotes ten; 
*   **He** <note>H</note> five; 
*   **Vav** <note>V/W</note> six; 
*   **He** <note>H</note> again five. 

By the art of arithmetic <note>Specifically the method of "expansion" or Gematria</note>, the total is collected thus: 
*   **Iod**: 10
*   **Iod, He**: 15 
*   **Iod, He, Vav**: 21 
*   **Iod, He, Vav, He**: 26 

Now combine these individuals: Ten, fifteen, twenty-one, and twenty-six, and seventy-two arises. 

Reflecting on these things with yourselves, you will clearly understand that to invoke spirits, a spiritual voice is needed, not a clamor like that of the **Priests of Baal**, to whom it was said by the Prophet **Elijah** in the third book of Kings <note>1 Kings 18:27</note>: *Cry with a louder voice, for perhaps your God is in a lodging-place, or on a journey, or surely he sleeps and must be awakened.* But if we use any prayer in our supplications, it is not done so that we may move God or the angels with syllables or words as if we were dealing with mortals, but so that we may stir our own powers into their fire, and fix our confidence in them like an anchor. Just as sailors, when calling a ship into port, are accustomed to throw out a rope or extend a cable to pull themselves toward the land—even though the land is immobile—by that effort they bring themselves toward the land...

->### THE ART OF THE CABALA BY JOHANN REUCHLIN<-

...they pull themselves. In the same way, through the perceptible signs established in any manner, we seem to draw the invisible divinity to us; yet, in truth, we—who are mobile—are drawn toward the immobile divinity. All sacraments and ceremonial rites stand firm upon this secret foundation. It is for this reason that we use meaningful signs and the voice; for this reason we use hymns and songs; for this reason the drum and the strings, cymbals and the organ, and other musical instruments of that kind. We do this not to "soften" God as if He were a woman, nor so that He might be captured by our flatteries and adulations. Rather, it is so that by exalting God and divine things, we may acknowledge the lowliness of our own condition, most humbly profess our subjection and obedience, and turn all human pleasure toward divine matters. In short, by this means we conceive an intense and burning love for the divinity. This love, more than anything else, makes us capable of receiving all graces.

Because of this, we stretch out our palms and expand our arms; we pray while kneeling or standing. We are also commanded to take a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, a turtle-dove, and a pigeon, and divide them down the middle <note>This refers to the "Covenant between the Pieces" in Genesis 15:9-10</note>. We slay the ram caught in the thicket as if with a sword and burn it with fire <note>Genesis 22:13</note>. We smear the <term>Thau</term><note>The Hebrew letter Tav (ת), which in ancient scripts looked like a cross or a mark, used to protect the Israelites' homes in Egypt</note> with blood upon the doorposts of our houses. We look upon the Bronze Serpent, and we fashion images of the Cherubim and other figures. We speak composed words and make vows; we enter the Sanctuary and look with astonishment at the High Priest clothed in such varied and wonderful finery. All these things and their like are done for our own sake, so that they might move us, incite us, direct us, and ultimately convert us—namely, from visible things to invisible ones. They increase faith, confirm hope, and finally, through <term>Anacephalæosis</term><note>Greek: "recapitulation" or "summing up"</note>, they transfer that true charity among us, which is most pleasing to God, into the love of divine things.

These are the dogmas of the Cabalists, as the third book of the *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "perplexorum"</note> by **Moses the Egyptian** <note>The famous Jewish philosopher Maimonides (1138–1204)</note> says, where it is written:
עבודת השם והזכרון השם תמיד ויראתו ואהבתו : ושמירת המצות כולן ויש אומרים בשם ית' ב"ה שהוא חברתי לכל : 
<gloss>original Hebrew: "The service of the Name [God] and the constant remembrance of the Name, His fear and His love, and the keeping of all the commandments; and some say in the Name of the Blessed One, He who is a companion to all."</gloss>
That is to say, the intention of such ceremonies is the frequent memory of God, and the fear and love of Him, and the observance of all the commandments, and that there be belief in God most high, which is necessary for everyone.

To be sure, oppressed as we are by the heavy mass of the body, we greatly need things that can stir the soul from its drowsiness. Just as a noble horse, exhausted by a long journey, is roused to strength when the trumpet sounds—unable to stand still, its ears twitching—and as an elephant, sluggish with laziness, rises into boldness when shown fire; so too is our virtue weakened by secular affairs. It requires external and physical impulses, whether of voices or figures, so that the vigor of our minds may press on more robustly in a spiritual way. Our contemplation is carried into the heights with all the more sharpness the more we were previously struck with astonishment. For this utility, the merciful angels have often devised figures, characters, forms, and voices, and proposed them to us mortals. These are both unknown and stupendous, signifying nothing according to the customary use of language, but leading us through the utter wonder of our reason into a constant investigation of intelligible things, and then into the veneration and love of those very things. For these do not signify according to the convention or pleasure of man, but according to the pleasure of God.

Hence, that most learned man of your age and sect, the **Count of Mirandola** <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a key figure in Christian Cabala</note>, brought this point to you when he said among his *Conclusions*: "In magic, non-meaningful words have more power than meaningful ones. For any word has power in magic insofar as it is formed by the voice of God, because that in which nature first exercises magic is the voice of God." These are the words of Pico.

Then **Philolaus** said: We men, sleepy and snoring as we are, would be moved by a greater awakening by names of this sort if they moved more than just one sense—if they appeared not only to our sight through figures and characters, but also struck our ears at the same time with an articulate voice. Therefore, I greatly desire, if it were possible, not only to see these things painted, but to be taught to hear them as well.

Then **Simon** replied: In my opinion, those who need an external motion must be considered very sluggish and, if I may say so with your permission, truly dull. And yet, we are born such that one thing always affects one person more than another, and the same thing does not...

### ON THE ART OF THE CABALA, BOOK III ###
<header>ON THE ART OF THE CABALA, BOOK III</header>

all equally. "To these points I agree with you, most learned Simon," Marranus said, "for our own writers also affirm that angels appear to men in different ways according to the condition and nature of the one seeing them. On this subject, Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407 AD), an influential Early Church Father known for his eloquent preaching.</note> writes extensively in his commentary on Matthew, eventually writing these words concerning Joseph: 'An angel appears in a dream; and why not openly, as he did to the shepherds, to Zechariah, and to the Virgin? That man was intensely faithful and did not need such a vision' <note>original Greek: κατ’ ὄναρ φαίνεται ὁ ἄγγελοϚ: καὶ διὰ τὶ μὴ φανερῶς καθὼϚ τοῖς ποιμέσι καὶ τῷ ζαχαρίᾳ καὶ τῇ πϑένῳ, σφοδρὰ πιστὸϚ ἦν ὁ ἀνὴρ. καὶ οὐκ’ ἐδεῖτο τῆ ὄψεωϚ ταύτηϚ</note>." To which Simon replied: 

"And you are quite right; the Cabalists think no differently, saying that the visual power in Abraham was stronger than in Lot, and for that reason 'men' appeared to Abraham, but 'angels' to Lot <note>Referring to Genesis 18 and 19; Abraham's higher spiritual state allowed him to see the divine messengers in a more 'humanized' or direct form.</note>. But perhaps we shall speak of these things in another place. Now, as it pertains to our case: there is a great diversity among men, as you well know. Some are sufficiently satisfied—and perhaps content—to have seen angels in human form; others in the form of fire; others in the form of wind and air; others in the form of a river and water; others in the form of birds; others in the form of gems, minerals, or precious stones; others in the energy of prophecy; others in a certain spirit dwelling within themselves; others in the shape of letters and characters; others in the sound of a voice; and so on through many types of visions found in Holy Scripture. 

However, since these characters of the seventy-two names <note>Refers to the *Shem HaMephorash*, the 72-fold name of God derived from Exodus 14:19-21.</note> will by no means seem to satisfy you, I will demonstrate the correct way—not only in the characters already mentioned, but also in those to be mentioned hereafter—how a word that can be articulately pronounced may be formed from the shape of the letters. We have God Himself as the author of this art. For we read in Exodus 23: 
> 'Behold, I send my angel before you, to guard you on the way and to lead you into the place I have prepared. Be attentive in his presence and hear his voice; do not provoke him, for he will not forgive your crimes, because **my name is in him**.' 

By this we understand that the name of an angel must, by the highest rite, sometimes encompass the name of God. Therefore, when the Cabalists were unable to pronounce the name of any angel significantly, they were accustomed to utter the whole together with the help of some name of God which they attached to it. For just as they see these three characters <term>רפא</term> <note>RP' (Rapha)</note> or <term>גברי</term> <note>GBRY (Gabri)</note> or <term>מיכ</term> <note>MYK (Mich)</note> used improperly to signify the name of an angel unless the name of God, <term>El</term>, is added—as in Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael—so they also, in attempting to imitate Holy Scripture in other angelic names, say Raziel, Jophiel, Zadkiel, Peliel, Malthiel, Uriel, and others in a similar manner. 

Indeed, just as the Romans name their Capitoline God 'Best and Greatest'—'Best' because of his benefits and 'Greatest' because of his power, according to Cicero’s testimony in his speech to the priests *For His House*—so the nation of the Jews calls its God <term>Iah</term> <note>יה - often associated with the attribute of Mercy (Chesed).</note> because of His benefits, and calls Him <term>El</term> <note>אל - associated with Power or Might (Gevurah).</note> because of His power and virtue. For so the Cabalists say regarding the words of King David, when he says: *If you, Lord (Iah), should mark iniquities, O Lord, who could stand?* They say: <term>יה שהוא עולם הרחמים אדני שהוא עולם הדין</term> <note>original Hebrew: 'Iah, which is the world of mercy; Adonai, which is the world of judgment.'</note>, as found in chapter 8 of the *Gates of Light* <note>A reference to *Sha'are Orah*, a foundational Cabalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla.</note>. Regarding *El*, you read thus in Numbers 16: *O El, most powerful God of the spirits of all flesh, shall your anger rage against all because one man sins?* 

Therefore, God is 'Best' to us because He is most merciful, and 'Greatest' because He is most powerful, which these two divine names, *Iah* and *El*, represent. If you join either of these to any of the seventy-two names, you will surely produce a distinguished 'oxytone' <note>A word with the grammatical accent on the last syllable.</note> word. This must certainly be done by always pronouncing them so that they become trisyllabic words, and the aspirations—written with this unique mark *h*—should come from the bottom of the chest with a strong breath, like the double 'spirit' of the Latin letter *h*; and everywhere *Iah* should be uniquely pronounced with a consonant *i* <note>i.e., like a 'Y'.</note>. Similarly with *El*: for both of these words, even in the composition of names, are uttered as single syllables, and the accent falls upon them. 

There are, therefore, seventy-two sacred names, which together are called the *Semhamaphores* <note>Shem HaMephorash: the Explicit Name.</note>—that is, the explanatory name of the most holy Tetragrammaton. They are to be enunciated thus, through the invocations of angels by men dedicated and devoted to God, with fear and trembling: Vehuiah, Ieliel, Sitael, Elemiah, Mahasiah, Iela...

### JOHANNES REUCHLIN
<header>JOHANNES REUCHLIN</header>

...hel, Achaiah, Cahethel, Haziel, Aladiah, Lauiah, Hahaiah, Iezalel, Mebahariel, Hakamiah, Louiah, Caliel, Leuuiah, Pahaliah, Nelchael, Ieiaiel, Melahel, Hauiah, Nithhaiah, Haaiah, Ierathel, Seehiah, Reiaiel, Omael, Lecabel, Vasariah, Iehuiah, Lehahiah, Chauakiah, Manadel, Aniel, Haamiah, Rehael, Ieiazel, Hahahel, Michael, Veualiah, Ielahiah, Sealiah, Ariel, Asaliah, Mihael, Vehuel, Daniel, Hahasiah, Imamiah, Nanael, Nithael, Mebahiah, Poiel, Nemamiah, Ieialel, Harahel, Mizrael, Vmabel, Iahhael, Anauel, Mehiel, Damabiah, Mauakel, Eiael, Habuiah, Rochel, Iabamiah, Haiaiel, Mumiah. <note>This list constitutes the 72 names of the angels of the Shem Ha-Mephorash, derived from three verses in Exodus 14:19-21.</note>

These excellent men <note>Simon refers to the angels as "men" here, following the biblical tradition where messengers often appear in human form.</note> are now ready at hand. With them, one might not only whisper secret conversations from the deepest recesses of the heart, but even exchange clear and distinct words, calling upon each one by his own symbolic name. Although they are rulers of individual regions, they hold nothing that is not shared. For even though they dwell in the supercelestial world, they nevertheless care for these lower things. For if this happens through natural influences—that they are contained in the heavens while simultaneously governing earthly affairs—it is much more so by the nobler, thinner, and simpler powers of the higher world. Such offices are likewise granted to them so that they may penetrate our world, and in turn be penetrated by ours. 

To this end, I shall use the assertion of your Plotinus <note>The OCR reads "tini," likely referring to the Neoplatonist philosopher Plotinus.</note> in his book *On Intelligence, Ideas, and Being*, where he says: "The sensible world is determined by only one place. But the intelligible world is everywhere." It is as if he were saying that the latter surrounds, orders, preserves, and penetrates this world of ours. Moreover, pay attention to what the wise masters of the Cabala assert here, which is worthy of great admiration, saying:

> There is no herb or plant below 
> that does not have a star in the firmament that strikes it and says: "Grow." 
> <note>original Hebrew: של כל עשב ועשב מלמטה שאין לו מזל ברקיע שמכה אותו ואומר לו גדל — This is a famous Midrash from Genesis Rabbah 10:6.</note>

They were supported in this opinion by the Sacred Scriptures, as we read in Job, chapter 38: "Do you know the laws of the heavens, or can you establish their rule (or their prefect, or their leader, or their executor) over the earth?" <note>Job 38:33.</note> Therefore, let not the vast anxieties of the earthly orb or the cares of lower things hold you back—matters for which the above-named angels are destined by the creator's distribution—from referring them back to the nine choirs of the supercelestial hierarchies. 

For since an angel is "otherness" (just as God is "identity"), and the first otherness is the number two <term>the binary</term>, we correctly believe that the number of angels arises from the multiplication of two. Now, the cubic multiplication of two is two times two times two, which equals eight, the first cube. If you distribute eight angels into each of the nine choirs, there will be seventy-two, for that is nine times eight. 

Return now, if you wish, through the choirs to the cube, and through the cube to your Tetractys <note>The Tetractys is a triangular figure of ten points used by Pythagoreans, which Reuchlin here links to the Hebrew name of God.</note>—which we call the Tetragrammaton and the Romans call the "four-foldness." From that, return to the binary (which signifies the angelic nature), and from that same point to the unity that is God, the Best and Greatest. You will surely experience that if we apply our study to the angels, we may also be joined to God through the angels by the unspeakable Tetragrammaton: **Yod, He, Vav, He** (יהוה). In this Name, the most noble nature of those angels first shines forth. For if, in these four letters יהוה, you place **Yod** four times, and descending, **He** three times, **Vav** twice, and **He** once, soon the sum of seventy-two will arise for you <note>This refers to the "Pyramid" of the Tetragrammaton: (Y) + (Y+H) + (Y+H+V) + (Y+H+V+H) or 10 + 15 + 21 + 26 = 72.</note>. This is the explanatory sum of the unutterable and incomprehensible name of God, to which all sacred names refer. While there is a huge abundance of such names, each is a title; this one alone is God's own and appropriated name, which is why it is called "The Explicit Name" <term>Ha-Meforash</term>. 

These seventy-two are called a single symbolic name, because their intention is to signify the one God, the Best and Greatest, though through many and various accounts of the angels—just as we identify a prince through his courtiers, or an emperor through his army. And indeed, the Masters of the Cabala venerate and worship these names greatly; through them, devoted men perform wonders—even more wonderful than I am permitted to speak. However, I will cite a most learned man as a witness in this cause, Recanati <note>Menahem ben Benjamin Recanati (1250–1310), a prominent Italian Cabalist.</note>, in his commentary on Exodus 14, who affirms that these characters and these letters are:

> Living beings 
> and signs above, as the essence of the Chariot; and they are appointed to do everything according to their power 
> and their actions, and they are visions for the Cabalists.
> <note>original Hebrew: חיות וזות למעלה כעיקר המורכבה והם ממונים לעשות כל דבר כחם ופעולותיהם ורועים למיקובלים</note>

That is to say, they are characters flying above the foundation of spiritual wisdom, and they are administrative spirits or powers...

# ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...perfected to do all things through them, and their operations are known to the Cabalists; thus far says Rabbi Menahem Recanati <note>Menahem ben Benjamin Recanati (1250–1310) was an influential Italian Kabbalist known for his mystical commentary on the Torah.</note>. And according to Rabbi Akiba <note>A foundational sage of classical Rabbinic Judaism and a primary figure in the Mishnah.</note>, they proceed from the throne of God's glory. But let no one, led by vain superstition, think that all things are conferred upon the mortal human condition from heaven by angels, and not rather that all things are done by the majesty of God himself even through the angels, as Nebuchadnezzar testifies in Aramaic in the Book of Daniel: <note>original: וּבְמִצְבְּיֵהּ עָבֵד בְּחַיִל שְׁמַיָּא וְדָארֵי אַרְעָא</note> "And according to his will he acts in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth" [Daniel 4:35]. For this reason, the Cabalists have received from the Book of Psalms pious prayers to be offered to God through seventy-two verses. Each of these verses contains the *Tetragrammaton* <term>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, often considered too holy to pronounce</term> along with the name of one of the 72 angels—with one exception, for good reason, which indicates the beginning of Genesis. They lift their minds to God as much as possible through these verses, ascending strongly from angel to angel. Amidst the praises of God, they move from one to the next, tending always toward the sublime. The angels assist them in this, so that, having left behind worldly anxiety, the soul may be carried toward God according to its capacity—just as a very light feather is lifted to the heights and the heavens by the aid of the thinnest breath of spirit. See and hear the prayer of these verses with the Tetragrammaton and the angels; I will point out both to you with my finger and my voice as follows:
