<meta>This page continues the dialogue where Simon, the Jewish Cabalist, begins a detailed explanation of the foundational structures of Cabala, specifically the ten Sefirot or divine emanations, following the group's eager request for more knowledge.</meta>

### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

->Oo 4<-

<meta>catchword: desires,</meta>

Both spoke eagerly, therefore proceed without delay. Soon Simon said: "The *ten numerations* called by the Cabalists <term>עשר ספירות <note>ten Sefirot</note></term> are treated by many of us in manifold ways; some in the manner of a tree, others in the form of a man, so that mention is often made of the root, trunk, branches, and bark. Often, indeed, also of the head, shoulders, legs, feet, and the right and left sides. These are the ten divine names which we mortals conceive regarding God, whether they are essential, personal, notional, or common, and they are named thus: <term>כתר <note>Keter</note></term>: that is, the Crown; <term>חכמה <note>Hokhmah</note></term>: i.e., Wisdom; <term>בינה <note>Binah</note></term>: that is, Prudence or Intelligence; <term>חסד <note>Hesed</note></term>: that is, Clemency or Goodness; <term>גבורה <note>Gevurah</note></term>: that is, Gravity or Severity; <term>תפארת <note>Tiferet</note></term>: that is, Ornament <note>often translated as Beauty</note>; <term>נצח <note>Netzah</note></term>: that is, Triumph; <term>הוד <note>Hod</note></term>: that is, Confession of Praise; <term>יסוד <note>Yesod</note></term>: i.e., Foundation; <term>מלכות <note>Malkhut</note></term>: i.e., Kingdom.

But above the Crown is placed <term>אין סוף <note>Ein Sof</note></term>: i.e., Infinity, and it is an abyss—shall I speak or remain silent? The matter is certainly one of profound speculation and a kind of immense ocean, into which all our contemplation is submerged, and once submerged, is swallowed up by a certain gaping void. Do you not remember how much the novices—now almost the teachers of God's word among all nations—toil day and night almost solely on the concepts of attributes? Some of them call these 'perfections' in divine matters, others 'attributes,' whether negative, affirmative, absolute, or relative and connotative. These things you can now easily learn, I believe, from the Cabalistic book, the *Compendium of the Gate of Light* <note>original: "Portæ lucis"</note>, which *Paulus Ricius*—an outstandingly learned man, formerly one of ours, now a Christian—collected from a certain Rabbi from *Castile* <note>Joseph Gikatilla</note>, and from the *Introductions* <note>original: "Isagogis"</note> which he wrote on the Cabala. Likewise, on that matter, that great Master of Cabala, *Rabbi Joseph*, son of *Carnitolis*, wrote the book: <term>שערי צדק <note>Sha'are Tzedek</note></term> *that is, the Gates of Justice*. Many commentators have written much regarding the 'tree' of the ten numerations, unrolling this involved cause and reducing almost the entire Old Sacred Scripture into these ten numerations, and through them into those ten names of God, and through those into the one name of the *Tetragrammaton* <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>. They affirm that the *Infinite* <note>Ein Sof</note> is the *Alpha* and Omega, who said: *I am the first and I am the last.* And that <term>כתר <note>Keter</note></term>, that is, the Crown of the kingdom of all ages, is a fountain without a bottom, and the <term>אב הרחמים <note>Av ha-Rahamim</note></term>: that is, the Father of Mercies. His mystery is that which *Ehieh* <note>I AM</note> seals through *Emeth* <note>Truth</note>: that is, essence through truth. Just as that noble author *Eliezer Haklir* says: <term>אמת חותמו <note>Emeth hotamo</note></term>, that is, *Truth* is His seal. Arithmetical reasoning proves this; following it, if we multiply *Ehieh* by *Ehieh*, there arise four hundred and forty-one, which together are <term>אמת <note>Emeth</note></term>: that is, true or truth, just as <term>אדני שלום <note>Adonai Shalom</note></term> that is, the Lord is Peace. <note>original: "Ehieh" (א-ה-י-ה) sums to 21. 21 times 21 equals 441. "Emeth" (א-מ-ת) also sums to 441: Aleph=1, Mem=40, Tav=400.</note> They reduce many more things to this, such as the 'Great Aleph,' the fear of the Lord, inaccessible light, the days of eternity—as it is written: 'His going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity.' So writes the distinguished Cabalist *Tedacus Levi* in his book on the ten numerations. To the second numeration, however, which is Wisdom, these things are referred from the attributes or properties: primogeniture; *Yes*: that is, being <note>original: "Ies"</note>; the primitive Law; the letter *Yod*, the first letter of the *Tetragrammaton*; the land of the living; the thirty-two paths; the seventy forms of the Law; war; judgment; *Amen*; the book; the holy; the will; the beginning; and other things of that kind. And perhaps it is a wonder that the second numeration is called 'the Beginning'; for one reads in *Racanati*, an excellent Master of Cabala, regarding the start of Genesis in this way: <term>ואילי תשאל למה קראת ראשית <note>Ve-ilai tishal lamma karata Reshit</note></term>, that is: 'And perhaps you will ask, since Wisdom is the second numeration, why it is called the Beginning.' For it is written in the book *Bahir*: <term>אין ראשית, אלא, חכמה <note>Ein Reshit ella Hokhmah</note></term>, that is, 'There is no Beginning except Wisdom.' To which I would seem to respond correctly that the very infinity of the three highest numerations of the Cabalistic tree—which you are accustomed to call the three persons in divine matters, the most absolute essence—since it is withdrawn in the abyss of darkness, immanent and at rest, or, as they say, looking toward nothing, is therefore called <term>אין <note>Ayin</note></term>: that is, Nothing, or non-being and non-end: that is, <term>אין סוף <note>Ein Sof</note></term>. This is because we, punished with such thin poverty of intellect regarding divine things, judge those things which do not appear just as we judge those things which do not exist. But when it shows itself so that it is 'something' and truly exists, then the dark *Aleph* is converted into the bright *Aleph*: for it is written: 'As is its darkness, so is its light,' and it is then indeed called the 'Great Aleph,' when it goes out...

He also discusses the mystical arithmetic linking God's name "I AM" to "Truth" and explains why Wisdom is considered the "Beginning."</summary>

# ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

That which is said by the Cabalists as *Beli mah* <term>בלי מה <note>Beli mah: Literally "without what" or "nothingness."</note></term> is understood by others as "without" or "beyond" and "what": that is, apart from the *quiddity* <note>The "what-ness" or essential nature of a thing.</note>. It is as if one said "ten apart from the 'what'," namely, excepting the essence of God. Hence they usually interpret *Belimah* to mean that which is beyond that which is ineffable; others derive it from this: "Bridle your mouth from speaking and your tongue from conversing" <note>original Hebrew: בלום פיך ולשונך מלדבר</note>: that is, by restraining or constricting your tongue lest you speak, as these are Sacred words which are not to be betrayed to the common people.

I should now speak of the angelic princes and the demonic prefects, whom the Cabalists place at the sides of Mercy and Severity—a matter truly requiring much speech, if we were not already passing midday and carried toward the evening. For who could explain such great things in so short a time? Who could so quickly finish with the thirty-five princes of purity and the seventy princes of Ishmael on the side of the fourth numeration <note>The Sefirah of Chesed (Mercy/Love).</note>? Likewise, who could sufficiently explain, even in passing and superficially, the thirty-five princes of guilt and the seventy princes of Esau in the fifth numeration of gravity and fear <note>The Sefirah of Gevurah (Power/Judgment/Fear).</note>? These matters require their own volumes, and certainly quite large ones; therefore, leaving these aside for the present, let us proceed to the art.

The happiness, I say, of the most contemplative men—according to their choice—is found to depend upon meditation on the Law (that is, the twenty-four books which we Hebrews call the *Yesra* <note>From the Hebrew *Esrim ve-Arba*, meaning "Twenty-Four," referring to the books of the Tanakh.</note>) by day and night, as gathered from the Sacred Letters. For it is written, among other things: "Blessed is the man... who shall meditate on His law day and night." It does not say "who reads," nor "who writes," nor "who speaks," but "who meditates." This is lest perhaps the writing or reading of the Law, being sometimes finished and ending, might compel happiness to likewise cease and end. But he, finally, who compels the thoughts in his heart to that place—so that having dismissed carnal things, he meditates on the spiritual things of the law—he, I say, is blessed, for he shall see God with a clean heart.

For in my judgment, there was not such a great need for diligence regarding the histories of Holy Scripture, which are as open to the Hebrews as Titus Livius is to the Latins. Likewise for the mandates and precepts, which have a set number, and for the religious rites and ceremonies, which are performed even by the unrefined and unlearned commoners—often not without vice and sin—such that they do not deserve that great happiness which consists in bodily senses, nor do they require such assiduous, continuous, and diligent meditation day and night. But it is demonstrated that a far greater happiness can be found in the higher levels of theory, which tends toward the Cabalistic understanding of the Law to such an extent that it imbues our minds with spiritual meditation and forms them, as it were, into its own likeness.

This is the conspicuous meditation on the law, which was finally delivered from the mouth of God to Moses after the law was given in fire, and after the stone tablets were broken and then repaired. For first, as the traditions of the Cabala assert, God wrote His law in a fiery globe by means of "black fire upon white fire." For as Ramban of Gerona <note>Moses ben Nahman, also known as Nachmanides (1194–1270).</note> says: "It appears to us through the Cabala that the writing was in black fire upon the back of white fire" <note>original Hebrew: שבא לנו בקבלה שהיתה כתובה באש שחורה על גבי אש לבנה</note>. Hence that passage stands in Deuteronomy 33: "From His right hand a fiery law for them." 

And then the letters were, as they say, confused and massed together. Those who were most studious, looking upon them speculatively and considering them diligently while led by the Holy Spirit, could easily choose, read, collect, and form them into any words whatsoever—from here and there, up and down, back and forth, forwards and backwards—forming a sentence signifying good in good things, and evil in evil things. But Moses, having been taught by God, reduced them all into order to be given to the people, so that everyone might know and observe those things which belonged to the Law; and from there the law was distinguished into books and placed in the Ark, just as he received it from the Lord. 

Nevertheless, the art of ordering and varying the letters and interpreting the Holy Scripture most sweetly for the elevation of the mind was received then from the Divine Majesty; yet, as a most divine matter imperceptible to the unrefined, he did not disclose it to the common people. He delivered it "mouth to mouth" only to the chosen Joshua and the seventy elders, from whom afterwards the chosen ones always received it; and from this "reception" (as you heard before) it was named Cabala. Even the most learned doctors of the Christians agree somewhat with this, many of whom I—though a Jew—have nonetheless gladly read, creeping into the enemy camp like a scout. Concerning our Moses, for instance, Gregory Nazianzen <note>St. Gregory of Nazianzus (c. 329–390), a Greek theologian and Church Father.</note>, that man surnamed "the Great Theologian" among the Greeks, says...

# JOHANNES REUCHLIN
[page 706]

...[Grego]ry <note>original: "gus" – likely completing the name "Gregorius" (Gregory of Nazianzus) from the previous page.</note>, in his book on the *State of Bishops*, speaks thus: "Receive the law: a statute for the many, but for those who are above the many, the law of the spirit." <note>original Greek: Δέχεσθε νόμον, τοῖς μὲν πολλοῖς θεσμόν, τοῖς δὲ ὑπὲρ τοὺς πολλοὺς, νόμον τοῦ πνεύματος</note> This means: they receive the law—the many receive the law of the letter, while those who are above the many receive the law of the spirit. Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, an early Christian mystic.</note> in the first book of *Theology* says: "It is willed that it be written on solid and stony tablets on both sides, through both the manifest law and the hidden law. One side is for the many who remain below, and the other for the pious who reach toward the heights." <note>original Greek: βουλεται οὕτως ἐν πλαξὶ στεῤῥαῖς καὶ λιθίναις ἐγγράφεσθαι ταῖς ἀμφοτέρωθεν διά τε τοῦ φαινομένου τοῦ νόμου καὶ τοῦ κρυπτομένου. τὸ μὲν τοῖς πολλοῖς καὶ κάτω μένουσι, τὸ δὲ τοῖς εὐσεβέσι καὶ ἄνω φθαίνουσι</note> From these words, it appears to some very learned men that your own people have seen that Moses delivered the text of the Law to the common people, but reserved the secret theory, the parables, and the symbols for himself and the more excellent men. 

And we have heard that this art of <term>Cabala <note>The Jewish mystical tradition of scriptural interpretation.</note></term> was divided into three ways, according to the testimony of Solomon, who says in the twenty-second chapter of Proverbs: "Surely I have written to you in a threefold way with a fitting meaning, that I might make known to you the rightness of the words of truth." For our people are accustomed to speak in this way when mention of the Cabala is made, so that they call it "words of truth" <note>original Hebrew: אמרי אמת</note>; that is, words of truth written as "the words of the truth" <note>original Hebrew: אמרי האמת</note>, which means according to the way of truth, which is the Cabala. This custom was frequent among the Egyptian, the man of Gerona <note>Referring to Nahmanides, the 13th-century sage from Gerona.</note>, and others. 

Others, however, present five parts of the Cabala, as Rabbi Hamai does in the *Book of Speculation*, which he names thus: "Rightness, and combination, and prayer, and intelligence, and calculation." <note>original Hebrew: ישרות והשבון ותפלה והשכל – Reuchlin lists five, though the Hebrew here lists four major categories: Rectitude, Combination, Prayer, and Intelligence; "Calculation" usually refers to Gematria.</note> Your Pico della Mirandola writes in his *Nine Hundred Conclusions* in these words: "Whatever other Cabalists may say, I distinguish in the first division the science of Cabala into the science of <term>Sephiroth <note>The ten emanations or attributes of God.</note></term> and <term>Semoth <note>Literally "Names" – the mystical study of divine names.</note></term>: that is, of numbers and names, as if into the practical and the speculative." But Rabbi Joseph and Abraham of Salerno and the much greater part of Cabalists follow King Solomon, in that they clearly believe that art can be not only contemplated but also practiced in a threefold way, according to the triple condition of all things: number, figure, and weight—indeed, reducing those five parts into these three. 

Since the whole business is allegorical—one thing being understood for another, or through another—the meaning itself is one thing in place of another. We shall speak openly: either a word is placed for a word, or a letter for a word, or a letter for a letter. First, a word is often taken for another word, either through transposition, which is called <term>metathesis <note>Rearranging the letters of a word to form a new one.</note></term>, or by a number equal to that included in the words <note>This refers to Gematria, where words with the same numerical value are linked.</note>. A letter is placed for a word, either at the beginning, or at the end, or anywhere by a mark placed above it <note>This refers to Notarikon, or acronyms.</note>. A letter is placed for a letter through alphabetical revolution <note>This refers to Temurah, or letter substitution ciphers.</note>, so that the whole, as I said, finally completes an Arithmetical, Geometrical, and Musical proportion. 

For example, in that passage of Psalm 21: "O Lord, in your strength the king shall rejoice," we understand this Cabalistically as referring to the Messiah, saying: "O Lord, the <term>Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note></term>, in your strength the king shall rejoice (it is understood: 'or he works')." For the Messiah is the strength of God, and he rejoices in the strength of the Tetragrammaton; I am led to this by this word "he shall rejoice" <note>original Hebrew: ישמח (Yismach)</note>, whose letters if transposed, will be "Messiah" <note>original Hebrew: משיח (Mashiach)</note>. 

Likewise, in another place, the Lord said to Moses: "Since my angel shall go before you" (Exodus 23). Who is this angel according to the Cabalists? Some say it is Michael: for by transposing the letters of "my angel" <note>original Hebrew: מלאכי (Malachi)</note> it becomes Michael. Others, taking this according to the rules of the Cabalistic art, affirm that it is <term>Metattron <note>Metatron, the highest angel in Jewish mysticism.</note></term>, because God said, "for my name is in him." In "Metattron," there is the name <term>Sadai <note>Shaddai (Almighty).</note></term> through the equal number included in the two words <note>Both "Metatron" (מטטרון) and "Shaddai" (שדי) have a numerical value of 314 in Gematria.</note>, which the man of Gerona wonderfully embraces in the place cited before. 

Do you now see two symbolic ways of the Cabala? Do you not also wish to see the third—a letter replaced for a word? Read Isaiah chapter 65: "He shall be blessed in the God Amen." Who is this God? The Cabalists will answer that it is "Amen" <note>original Hebrew: אמן</note> through "Amen": that is, "The Lord, the faithful King" <note>original Hebrew: אדוני מלך נאמן (Adonai Melekh Ne'eman) – the word "Amen" is treated as an acronym for this phrase.</note>; for these three words are noted by the three initial letters of the word "Amen," as Recanati wrote on Exodus 15. The fourth species and third part of Cabala is literary commutation, where a word written with certain letters symbolically designates another word composed of other letters, and this is done through that alphabetical revolution according to the *Book of Creation* of Abraham, made with twenty-two variations.

->### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.<-

For it is there that they read so many alphabets. An example is provided to us by **Mazpaz** <note>original: מצפץ</note>, a name of God which is written with these four letters: **Mem, Tsade, Pe, and Tsade**. Regarding this, your countryman Pico della Mirandola <note>original: "Mirandulanus uester"</note> says: "The name of God of four letters, which consists of Mem, Tsade, Pe, and Tsade, ought to be appropriated to the kingdom of David." Since this name is clearly not read in the text of Holy Scripture, I ask, what is it held to be a symbol of? The Cabalists respond that it is a symbol and a seal of the ineffable <term>Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, considered too holy to pronounce.</note></term>, and it proceeds from the last alphabet, which is the twenty-second of the book called the **Sefer Yetzirah** <note>original: "Sepher Ietzira," or the "Book of Formation," a foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note>, and is called **Atbash** <note>original: "Athbas," a substitution cipher where the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>. For in that system, **Yod** is exchanged for **Mem**, **He** for **Tsade**, and **Vav** for **Pe**, so that **Mazpaz** becomes **Adonai** <note>Note: The text links Mazpaz to the Tetragrammaton Y-H-V-H through the Atbash cipher.</note> **Yod, He, Vav, He**.

I have just spoken of things pertaining to the "art," whether it be by transferring, transposing, or commuting words, syllables, or letters, according to the four methods by which the senses of the scriptures are ingeniously and skillfully allegorized. As for those things which stand without such "art" and are done by tradition alone—which I call <term>Atechna <note>Greek term meaning "without art" or "unskilled," here referring to knowledge received through tradition rather than derived through systematic methods.</note></term>—I have informed you more than enough. However, both of you, since this is your profession, have already acquired no small amount of knowledge about them through your own study: namely, the way in which simple things are abstracted from the composite, and higher things from the lower, and how almost everything is referred back to the **Intelligible World** or the super-supreme and incomparable world.

By reading the Holy Letters, several arguments for piety can often come into our minds, which first lure us toward the admiration of divine things and then into a love for them. Yet these cannot be handed down by any certain "art." For example, the idea that **Gabriel** is of stronger virtue than **Michael**, because it is read of him in Daniel: "A double virtue, flying in flight" <note>Referring to Daniel 9:21; Simon interprets the phrasing as suggesting superior speed or power.</note>. Of Michael, however, it is only said that he "came to help." Therefore, among the intelligences, Gabriel is philosophically considered the virtue of the **Active Intellect**, and Michael the virtue of the **Passive Intellect**. So writes **Rabbi Levi Ben Gershom** <note>Also known as Gersonides (1288–1344), a famous medieval Jewish philosopher and astronomer.</note>, who is called by the Latins **Master Leo de Banolis**.

Philolaus said: "It seems to me, Simon, that what you call *Atechnon* (tradition) contributes a great deal to the Cabalistic art. For unless the revelations of the ancestors were kept in hand—which you rightly think do not fall under the 'art'—everyone would be granted the reckless license to interpret and twist Holy Scripture wherever they wished. This is just as we have heard certain common sophists do, who in this age seem to have brought those most holy oracles of the divine spirit into nearly public contempt with their syllogisms. But now, since I believe everything must be applied to what has been revealed, a certain line is drawn, beyond which truth cannot stand; thus, the 'artful' works of the worst men do not decline into idleness."

Then Simon said: "You speak the plain truth. For there is almost nothing else that is more errantly twisted to suit any man’s whim than the oracles—though this is not always out of malice, but often more from ignorance. For who would commit a crime against the sacred on purpose? Thus **Saul** was once deceived by the ambiguity of a word and wandered from the oracle's meaning. For God had promised in Exodus 17: **I will blot out the memory of Amalek** <note>original Hebrew: אמחה את זכר עמלק</note>. Saul believed that if he removed the males, he would satisfy the command, because the word **ZKR** <note>Z-K-R</note> could signify a 'male' <note>Hebrew: *zakhar*</note>. God, however, intended the memory of Amalek to be blotted out through this word **ZKR**, which also designates 'memory' <note>Hebrew: *zekher*</note>. For at that time, there was not yet the distinction in Scripture by points and accents, which only began in the years of Ezra. Therefore, **ZKR** without vowel points, sounding as both 'memory' and 'male,' gave Saul the occasion for his ruin."

To this Marranus added: "A similar thing happened to both Italians and Greeks regarding the word **phōs** <note>Greek: φώς</note>, which signifies both a 'man' and 'light.' From this, the worshippers of the **Saturnalia** were once deceived by the ambiguity; they sacrificed some man to Saturn every year, when that sacrifice could just as well have been performed with lit lights <note>candles</note> according to the oracle, to appease Saturn. Thus that foolish people finally came to their senses under the teaching of **Hercules**. It is also a pitiable thing in our own age how much foolish men and certain proud sophists err through their lack of skill in languages. This might be bearable, were they not to contend that they have not erred, and were they not to show deadly envy toward those who point out the way. But, O our leader, proceed more fully with the Cabalistic art, the beginning of which you have already started."

Then Simon said: "The opinion of the more skilled (as we have said) is that this art consists of three things. The first is the computation of numbers..."

<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of the three branches of the practical Cabala: Gematria, Notarikon, and Temurah. It transitions from linguistic methodology to philosophical theology, discussing the nature of God as both "Being" and "Non-being" and his relationship to numerical unity.</meta>

[page 708]

->### JOHN REUCHLIN<-

...computation, which is named **Gematria** <note>original: גימטריא</note>: that is, Geometry, which is, as it were, a numerical measurement of things in relation to one another, which nevertheless depends upon Arithmetic. Because of its abstract simplicity, it is not graspable by any senses, and therefore is not subject to the crude skill of the senses. It is therefore called a part of Geometry rather than Arithmetic, although in truth both are effective in this art. Next, syllables are sometimes changed so that the word itself is transformed, or the word is simply reversed. Second, there is the method where a letter stands for a whole word; this is called **Notarikon** <note>original: נוטריקון</note>, from the marks of Notaries <term>shorthand <note>A system of abbreviations used by Roman scribes and later scholars to record speech or text quickly.</note></term>, for there every letter is marked at the top so that it serves as a sign for some whole word. Third, this art consists in the changing of letters, when one is ingeniously substituted for another, and it is called **Temurah** <note>original: תמורה</note> or Commutation. This is why **Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla** <note>original: "R. Minor Salernitanus," a likely reference to Gikatilla, whom Reuchlin elsewhere associates with the title "The Lesser."</note> called the books he wrote on this art **The Garden of the Nut** <note>original: "Hortum nucis," Hebrew: אגוז (*Egoz*)</note>, because the three letters of this word designate the three functions of the Cabalistic art. For the letter **Gimel** <note>original: ג</note> signifies **Gematria** <note>original: גמטריא</note>, the **Nun** <note>original: נ</note> signifies **Notarikon** <note>original: נוטריקון</note>, and the **Tav** <note>original: ת</note> signifies **Temurah** <note>original: תמורה</note>. Thus, these are the parts of the whole craft: **Gematria**, which is Arithmetical; **Notarikon**, which is like a notary's shorthand; and **Temurah**, the exchange of elements. To this title, the author alludes to the verse of Solomon in the sixth chapter of the Song of Songs: *I went down into the garden of the nut.* For the first part, I shall begin with that which is the principle. And it is written in Zechariah that the **Lord Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> will be **One** <note>original: אחד (*Echad*)</note>: that is, One, and his name **One** <note>original: אחד (*Echad*)</note>. Or perhaps more truly, the Lord God will be **Aleph** <note>original: א</note>: that is, the principle, just as you Greeks say **Alpha and Omega** <note>original: "Alpha & ω"</note>, and **One** <note>original: אחד (*Echad*)</note>: that is, One, as he who is the principle of unity. For he is above all unity and is the eternal origin of every unity. Truly, he is not called "one" in the same way he is not called "a being," because he is above all, and from him flows whatever exists. Hence, by the most contemplative scholars, he is called **Non-being** <note>original: אין (*Ayin*)</note>, as we read in Exodus 17: **Is the Lord among us, or is he Non-being?** <note>original: היש יהוה בקרבנו אם אין (*ha-yesh YHWH be-kirbenu im ayin*)</note>. However, it is read in the book *The Way of Faith* <note>original: "de Via fidei"</note> and in the *Book of Speculation* <note>original: "Speculationis," likely the *Sefer ha-Iyun* attributed to Rabbi Hamai</note> that he is both: **Being and Non-being** <note>original: היש ואין (*ha-Yesh ve-Ayin*)</note>, since both those things which are and those which are not are from him and exist after him. So also he is One, because he is the cause of all unity, and unity exists after him; and he is nothing, both in the sense of things that follow him and things that do not exist, as in the *Book of Speculation* by **Rabbi Hamai**, who after many words says: **All things are derived from his unity, and he himself is not similar to any one thing** <note>original: "צלום מאחדותו והוא אינו כלו דמות" - Reuchlin's translation follows: "all things are derived from his unity, and he is not like any image."</note>. And not only do our people confess this, but even your own authors, whom you prove to be most wise, assert it. For **Dionysius the Areopagite** <note>A 5th-6th century Christian theologian and philosopher.</note> in his book *On Mystical Theology* subscribed to this same opinion concerning God, saying: **Because he is neither number, nor order, nor one, nor unity** <note>original: "ὅτι οὔτε ἀριθμός ἐστιν, οὔτε τάξις, οὔτε ἕν, οὔτε ἑνότης"</note>. What then is he? **Maimonides** <note>original: "Maimonides," the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> answered: "The more I think, the less I understand." And it happens to me that when, having passed beyond all created things, I ascend above every being, I find nothing but an infinite sea of nothingness, and the fountain of all entity flowing perpetually from the shadows. O altitude! O depth! O enormousness! But it ought to seem enough for us to know of him what he himself has revealed to us: that he is the Principle, that is, **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, numerical value 1.</note>, and the **Tetragrammaton** <note>YHWH</note>, which is signified by the Principle and denotes the divine essence, which is nothing other than **Existence** <note>original: הויה (*Havayah*, an anagram of YHWH)</note>: which certainly is almost the same as the essence of the **Lord** <note>original: יהוה (*YHWH*)</note>. For by an equal value, the Scripture has joined both as belonging to him who is the first and the last, in Exodus 9: **Behold, the hand of the Lord is Existence** <note>original: הנה יד יהוה הויה (*Hineh yad YHWH hoyah*), traditionally translated as "the hand of the Lord is upon..."</note>, as if to say, he is the end of the works and miracles of God, as is clear in the ten plagues of Egypt. For elsewhere that word is not found in this way. Solomon, however, indicates by the testimony of this word a present essence. But the fact that the **Tetragrammaton** began [with the letter **Iod**] was clearly done for our sake, so that we might recognize him as the point and the completion of every number: that is, of every single thing. For **Iod** <note>The letter י, value 10.</note> signifies ten. And in the resolution of the name **Tetragrammaton**, it is the tenth letter in the sequence of **YHWH** <note>This refers to the expansion of the name where letters are spelled out or counted in sets.</note>. Where after the **Tetragrammaton** is found **Existence** <note>original: הויה (*Havayah*)</note>, which is his symbol...

# ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...that is, of Being through numerical equality <note>original: "per æqualitatem numeri," referring to Gematria, where words with the same numerical value are considered spiritually linked</note>. And it signifies no less the essence of the Creator, as in *Exodus 3: I Am [Ehieh] has sent me to you* <note>original: "Ehieh misit me ad uos"</note>; not that essence which remains within, but that which flows outward. For the seal of God is **Truth** <note>original: "אמת" (Emet)</note> with which **I Am** [Ehieh] sealed the World, and it is called **Truth** <note>original: "אמת"</note>: that is, the true thing, precisely because it is born into itself by Arithmetical multiplication. Then follows **Iah** <note>original: "יה"</note>, the name of the essence of merit and retribution, as in the *Psalms: If you, Iah, should mark iniquities.* Thus, you see three essential names in the **Four-Letter Name** <note>original: "Tetragrammato," referring to the name YHWH</note>. The Ineffable denotes the primary essence. **I Am** [Ehieh] denotes the essence in things, and **Iah** denotes essence in merits; they are predicated on "what" a thing is. Therefore, it is called **What** <note>original: "מה" (Mah)</note>: that is, the "quiddity" or essence. For the **Four-Letter Name** [Tetragrammaton] *The Lord our God, the Lord* <note>original: "יהוה אלהינו יהוה"</note> through numerical equality signifies **What** [Mah]; for both contain the number 45 <note>In Gematria, the letters of Mah (Mem-He) total 45, and the specific expansion of the name YHWH used here also totals 45</note>. And when Moses said, *What is his name, what shall I say?* He answered him, **I Am** [Ehieh].

Then consider diligently the words of the Holy Spirit, which are not placed in the same passage of Exodus 3 in vain: *Thus shall you say to the children of Israel* <note>original: "כה תאמר לבני ישר"</note>: that is, *What is my name, what?* And look at their terminal letters; you will have the **What** [Mah] as a three-letter ineffable **Lord** [YHWH] whose beginning is **I Am** [Ehieh]. The middle is **Iah** [Yah]. The end is infinity. For its parts are *Ihi, Ihu, Ihi* <note>original: "יהי יהו יהי"</note> which we divide into three intervals. The first is *Ihi*. The second is *Ihu*. The third is *Ihi*. All of these serve being and essence. Regarding the **Four-Letter Name** [YHWH], we read in *Exodus 15: My strength and my song is Iah.* Regarding the same **Four-Letter Name** in that place: *And he has become my salvation.* Regarding the **Four-Letter Name** in *Genesis 1: Let there be light.* These last two words contributed greatly to the craftsmanship of the World and the existence of things: *Let there be light, and there was light.* <note>original: "יהי אור ויהי אור" (Yehi or v'yehi or)</note> *And there was evening, and there was morning: Let there be a firmament, and let there be a distinction, and it was so. Let the earth bring forth, and it was so. Let there be lights, and it was so. Always adding this: and there was evening, and there was morning.* In all these things, so that they might truly exist, we find the ineffable name present in a feminine and hidden manner.

But we see only **God** <note>original: "Elohim"</note> expressed in those six days. Yet when the World already appeared to be perfect, after the various and admirable works of the most divine virtues were completed, at last, so that a triumph might be celebrated for its merit and a feast day proclaimed, behold, the **Four-Letter Name** [Tetragrammaton] as King of kings and Lord of lords entered with **God** [Elohim], and then it was said for the first time: *These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God [Tetragrammatus Elohim] made the heaven and the earth.* Here the **Four-Letter Name** first sounded publicly in the ears of all creatures, by which we understand the mercy of God joined with justice; for in whatever place of Holy Scripture the **Four-Letter Name** joins itself to **God** [Elohim], there we notice the property of mercy and justice together. It is sometimes composed with **Lord** <note>original: "אדני" (Adonai)</note> as in the prayer of Habakkuk: *The Lord God [Tetragrammatus Adonai] is my strength,* and by reading it thus, we understand the power of the **Four-Letter Name** to descend to the spoken **Lord** [Adonai] himself.

But if it is found in the reverse order, **Lord** [Adonai] **Four-Letter Name** [Tetragrammatus], as in *Genesis 15: Lord God [Adonai Tetragrammate], what will you give me?* then we conceive in the mind that the numerations—that is, the divine properties—ascending from the lower to the higher, take hold of the supreme light. It also happens sometimes that the name **El** <note>original: "אל" (God/The Mighty One)</note> is found joined. *In Psalm 118: El the Lord God [El Tetragrammatus Elohim]* and it is said thus: *The Lord God of gods [El Elohim Tetragrammatus] has spoken and called the earth* in the fiftieth Psalm. Then the ineffable name denotes grace clothed in severity. Sometimes it is read, and that only in the Prophets and the Holy Writings <note>original: "Hagiographis," the Ketuvim section of the Hebrew Bible</note>, as **Lord of Hosts** [Tetragrammatus Sabaoth], as in *Psalm 46: The Lord of Hosts [Tetragrammatus Sabaoth] is with us; the God of Jacob is our protector.* And in this way, it suggests the property of judgment. And for this reason, the Prophets use that style when rebuking with severity. Concerning explanations of this kind, you may search more broadly in the book *The Gates of Light* <note>original: "Portæ lucis," the Sha'are Orah by Joseph Gikatilla</note>, and most extensively in the book *The Gates of Justice* <note>original: "Portaru iusticiæ"</note> by **Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla** <note>original: "Rabi Ioseph Carnitolis"</note>. Furthermore, concerning the thirteen properties of the same **Four-Letter Name**, which the Lawgiver Moses invoked in *Exodus 34* to this effect: *O Lord [Tetragrammate], Lord God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in mercy and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, taking away iniquity, passing over transgression and sin, and...*

**OF JOHANNES REUCHLIN**

<warning>Right margin text is partially obscured by the binding gutter.</warning>

...the guilty shall not be cleared, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation <note>original: "nocens non innocētabitur, uisitans iniquitatem patrum super filio filiorum filios in tertiam & quartam progeniem"; a quote from Exodus 34:7</note>. I call upon you here, O men: for it is a pleasure to speak this truth certainly without falsehood, since much study would be required for anyone who wished to publish all the mysteries of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The "Four-Letter Name" of God, YHWH</note>, for which there is no end to be found, just as there is no end to the substance of God. Therefore, starting from the proper name of the divine essence, I shall show the derived names. For it is customary, according to the decree of the grammarians, that we form common names from proper ones. These names are **El**, **Elohim**, and **Eloha** <note>original: "אל אלהים אלה"</note>, each of which draws its origin from the ineffable **Tetragrammaton**. This name has four letters—behold, four—and it designates the number 26—behold, twenty-six—which together are the symbol of the one God—behold, one. Join these individual parts, namely four, twenty-six, and one, and the result is **El** <note>original: "אֵל"; In Gematria, El (Aleph=1, Lamed=30) totals 31. Reuchlin derives this from 4 letters + 26 value + 1 (the unity) = 31</note>. If you add the termination of the Tetragrammaton to this, it is called **Eloha** <note>Adding the letter 'He'</note>. 

Now concerning **Elohim**, it is said that its final *Mem* does not signify the thing itself, but is a grammatical inflection, which is apparent from this: for if it must be read through a suffix or in a construct state with a following word, there is no doubt that the letter *Mem* is dropped. Therefore, if at the beginning of the Tetragrammaton, **Iah** <note>The first two letters, Yod-He</note>, you add **El** in reverse order, it becomes **Iohi**; and by assuming the grammatical declension, which is *Mem*, it will be pronounced **Elohim**. This is often written using the letters of the Ineffable name, yet it is nonetheless pointed with the same vowels <note>referring to how the vowels for Elohim are often applied to the letters YHWH in Hebrew manuscripts</note>. In the **Kabbalah** <note>The Jewish mystical tradition</note>, the conversion of order is frequent, and great is the power and praise of its virtue, since in whatever way the syllables are transposed, the letters remain the same without diminution, even though they often change their meanings. Abraham mentions this in the *Book of Formation* when he says: *Male in AMSh and female in AMSh* <note>original: "זכר באמש ונקבה באמש"; citing the Sefer Yetzirah regarding the three "mother letters" Aleph, Mem, and Shin</note>; that is, the transposition of letters indicates a change in the thing itself. For example, **El** and **Lo** <note>original: "אל & לא"</note>: that is, **God** and **Not**. While this occurs frequently elsewhere, it is exceedingly wonderful in this ineffable name, for however much its letters are turned this way or that, they always signify one and the same thing: namely, the Being and Essence of God who said: *I am the Tetragrammaton, and I do not change.* 

This will be more manifest to you by this usage. Let the **Tetragrammaton** be resolved into twelve variations: for we cannot proceed further, and whatever is found will serve no other than the Essence, of which they are the symbols:

-> יהוה  יהוח  יהוח  יהיה  ההיו  והיה <-
-> יההו  וחיה  יההו  חיהו  חיהה  ההוי <-
<note>These are the 12 permutations of the name YHWH, often called the Twelve-Letter Name in mystical practice</note>

Therefore, these twelve names are considered as one among the **Kabbalists**, as all signify the same thing, although there are twelve expository passages which they apply from Holy Scripture to each one, perfectly referring to it—not for the sake of exposition, but only as a mnemonic device, lest they fall into oblivion. For instance, if I were to say: *Be attentive and hear, O Israel, today*, which is read in Hebrew as: **Hasket ve-shema Yisrael ha-yom** <note>original: "הסכת ושמע ישראל היום"; Deuteronomy 27:9</note>. If you take the first letters of these four words, they make **YHWH**, which is the name of the Essence and the resolution of the **Tetragrammaton**. Let the others be formed similarly from other verses. 

But let us remain a little while in the first part of the **Kabbalah**, while we still see certain necessary things to be known. For now that we have taken what was necessary from the second part, let us approach this art, if you will, piece by piece and part by part <note>original: "membratim cælimqz"</note>, provided we do not linger too long on each one, so that the day's work passes within the day. Indeed, I will now briefly cite again what I touched on before, so that it may stick more firmly: that God before creation was **Ineffable**; in creation, He was named **Elohim**; and after creation, dwelling in the world as if in His temple, He is called **Adonai** <note>Lord</note>. Whence we read in Psalm 11: *The Tetragrammaton is in his holy temple, the Tetragrammaton’s throne is in heaven*, he who rules over all his works. For He himself is, as Scripture says in Deuteronomy 10: *The God of gods and Lord of lords, the great El.* Therefore, the **Temple** is noted in the **Kabbalah** as **Adonai**, and vice versa, through numerical equality <note>In Gematria, both Adonai (אדני) and Heikhal (היכל - Temple/Palace) equal 65</note>. Just as in **Adonai** as if in a **Temple** <note>original: "templo"</note>, the Ineffable **Tetragrammaton** is to be adored, and God is to be loved, according to the threefold world, as in Jeremiah 7: *The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord.* There remains another appellative name, which is **Shaddai** <note>Almighty</note>, Exodus 6: *I am the Tetragrammaton, and I appeared to Abraham, Isaac...*

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the divine names from page 710, specifically transitioning from the derivation of the name 'El' to the distinctions between 'El Shaddai' and the 'Tetragrammaton,' and the practical application of Kabbalistic methods like Gematria and letter transposition.</meta>

### ON THE ART OF THE KABBALAH, BOOK III.

...by **El Shaddai** <note>God Almighty; original: "El Sadai"</note>, but my name **Tetragrammaton** <note>The ineffable four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> I did not make known to them. In this passage, only this is called His name because it is unutterable, for this alone is proper to the Most High God, insofar as He is none of the things that exist, but is above all things, having no regard outside of Himself. Other names are also appellatives of other properties and relations, such as **Shaddai**, which the Latins translated as "Omnipotent," but in Hebrew it more aptly signifies "Self-sufficient," content in Himself, and lacking nothing, which the Greeks more correctly interpret as *autarkēs* <note>original: "αὐτάρκης", meaning self-sufficient or independent</note>. For grammatically we say *She* <note>Hebrew: ש</note>: that is, "which," and *dai* <note>Hebrew: די</note>: "suffices" or "is enough." Furthermore, if you hear the word "the Name" used alone in the sacred texts, let the **Tetragrammaton** immediately come to your mind, which par excellence <note>original: "κατ’ ἐξοχήν"</note> and hyperbolically is called the "name above every name," however much in daily speech every thing that has existence has a name. Moreover, because **Shaddai** has no need for the help of another, He appeared to the patriarchs as **El Shaddai**: that is, as the Strong One who is content in Himself. He appeared as the **Tetragrammaton** so that, as one who is sufficient in Himself, He might perform miracles and wonders; however, He did not make them know that the name **Tetragrammaton** is that name in which a man, as a co-worker and delegate of God, can perform miracles—concerning this, I spoke more clearly in *Capnion on the Miracle-Working Word* <note>A reference to Reuchlin's own previous work, "De Verbo Mirifico"</note>. There is, besides, a ministering spirit of **Shaddai** itself called **Metatron**, so named because of the equality of his number <note>In Gematria, both Shaddai and Metatron equal 314</note>, who is held to be the leader and shower of ways, which we shall discuss more clearly later if you remind me. There is also another name, **Sabaoth**, which in Hebrew is read as *Tzabaot* <note>Hebrew: צבאות</note>: and thus they are called "hosts" or "armies," the first of which consists of entirely separate intelligences and angels; the second of the movers of the spheres and the assisting powers; the third of souls informing bodies. These are not found except following the name of God. Whence also "Holy, Holy, Holy" is read three times, followed by the **Tetragrammaton Sabaoth**, in the sixth chapter of Isaiah and in other places similarly.

You have now heard the state of the whole first part of the Kabbalah, and by what instruction it proceeds. For since it consists entirely in the permutation of sacred words, and since any words may be altered in two ways, we must necessarily admit that this part contains two species: one which is done by the transposition of syllables or words, and the other by the equality of numbers. For example, if I read in the fortieth chapter of Isaiah: *Mi eleh bara* <note>Hebrew: מי אלה ברא</note>: that is, "Who created these?" and I Kabbalistically transpose these two, turning *Mi* <note>Who</note> into *Eleh* <note>These</note>, then the beginning of Genesis, *Elohim bara* <note>God created</note>, actually returns in place of *Mi eleh bara*, so that the meaning stands: Who created these? God created them. And Ezekiel sat by the river **Chebar** <note>original: "Chobar"</note>: that is, at the influence of the **Cherub**; for if **Chebar** <note>Hebrew: כבר</note> is transposed, it becomes **Rekeb** <note>Hebrew: רכב; meaning chariot or vehicle</note>. And Noah found grace (Genesis 6); for by converting *Noach* <note>Hebrew: נח</note> it becomes *Chen* <note>Hebrew: חן; grace</note>. All similar things happen through metathesis <note>The rearrangement of letters</note> because of the primary confusion of letters that had appeared in the globe of fire, so that it was permitted to draw letters out as if from chaos and read them here and there, forward and backward; thus the first species of the first part is completed. Now I have determined to show some examples by approaching the second member of the first part, so that you may understand the matter more clearly and hold it more firmly in memory. 

It is read concerning Isaac and Rebecca in the 25th chapter of Genesis: *Vayeater Rivkah ishto*: that is, "And his wife Rebecca conceived." From this, it is granted to us to divine: what did Rebecca conceive? Surely, as the words indicate, Rebecca conceived *ishto* <note>Hebrew: אשתו; "his wife"</note>. But you, most learned men, consider what *ishto* is in this second species of the first part through **Gematria** <note>Hebrew: גימטריא</note>: that is, the measurement of numbers. You will find that according to the equality of the number, it signifies *Esh u-Kash* <note>Hebrew: אש וקש</note>: that is, "Fire and stubble"; for each contains within itself seven hundred and seven. Rebecca therefore conceived fire and stubble, which the sacred utterances confirm by the testimony of Obadiah, who says: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Esau stubble." Similarly, when we hear that the law was brought forth in wisdom (*Chokhmah*). Let us see what that wisdom is which is suitable for bringing forth the law. Certainly, they are edicts and interdicts, commands and prohibitions. The symbol, however, is **Taryag** <note>Hebrew: תריג</note>: that is, the wisdom of all the commandments of God; for when you pronounce the four elements <note>letters</note> of that word according to their own spellings <note>spelling out the names of the letters</note>, the number of the six hundred and thirteen commandments of God—which our doctors call **Taryag**—will be forged from them. <meta>This page continues the technical discussion of Kabbalistic methods. Having previously touched upon Gematria (the numerical value of letters), the speaker now moves into the history of the Hebrew alphabet and the second major method of interpretation: Notarikon (the use of letters as shorthand or acrostics).</meta>

7 12 JOHANNES REUCHLIN
In this type of speculation, one must first consider that the characters, elements, and letters of the Law were originally set down alone. It is a fact worthy of memory to the scholar <note>original: "erudito"</note> that they were readable here and there, yet distinct without any accents or vowel points. Third, each of the primordial alphabets signifies a specific number; even the five terminal letters <note>The Hebrew letters (Khaf, Mem, Nun, Pe, Tzadi) that take a different shape when appearing at the end of a word.</note> were only later invented by the wise Ezra along with the vowel points. For the original twenty-two letters, by which all scripture was depicted from the beginning, are still used by the Kabbalists to this day; they "locate and dislocate" them <note>The Kabbalistic practice of rearranging letters (Temurah) to find hidden meanings.</note> for the pleasure of any delightful contemplation. Finally, we must strive for a universal rule: although it is the task of the Kabbalist to read one thing and understand another, let everyone observe this canon inviolably—finding good in the good, and evil in the evil—lest one apply black to white, or day to night. 

Then Marranus said: "I would think of that sort of thing no differently than if someone accepted a 'Dorotheus' for a 'Theodorus,' or a 'Demonicum' for a 'Nicodemus,' or a 'Philodemum' instead of a 'Demophilus.' Just as the Greeks are accustomed to say *somatophilon* and *philosomaton* <note>original: "σωματφίλον και φιλοσώματον"; meaning 'body-loving' and 'lover of the body'—Marranus is joking that rearranging letters or names changes the meaning entirely, sometimes into its opposite.</note>." 

Admon replied: "Certainly, what you say has some relevance, but you will soon grow weary of listing examples because of the poverty of other languages. Compared to Hebrew, which is the fountain of all languages, they are poor and impatient with their own limitations; they adopt the idioms of other nations because they do not possess a full set of numbers, nor do they allow for such useful composition. For this reason, this art can by no means be translated into the speech of another people. If I did not know you were equally skilled in Hebrew, I would have discussed these small matters of Kabbalah with you in vain, nor would I be doing so now. 

But let us hurry; let us move to the second part of this instruction, which is called **Notarikon** <note>Hebrew: נוטריקון; a method of shorthand where each letter of a word stands for an entire sentence, or the first letters of a sentence form a new word.</note>. This is a shorthand <note>original: "laconismum"</note>, which is a certain secret convention accepted among Kabbalists, where individual letters without the joining of syllables designate certain words. This is in the manner of notaries and scribes, and was once the secret practice of military leaders, who brought forth the secrets of the mind through single letters arranged without a sequence. As the commentary of the Grammarian <note>likely referring to Marcus Valerius Probus</note>—as Aulus Gellius writes—is quite curious regarding the hidden significance of letters, perhaps it is no different in the practice of this art. For example, if someone agrees that the letter **Yod** <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet (י).</note>, because of its nature as an indivisible point, represents the ineffable **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, which we commonly interpret as 'the Lord.' Just as that same name is signified by three **heights** <note>Hebrew: עליונות (*elyonot*); referring to the three highest emanations or Sephirot.</note>, which are one and the same **crown** <note>Hebrew: עטרת (*atarot* or *atarah*).</note>, they are accustomed to mark it with three points. For the Kabbalists say: *This name, in its wisdom, is three Yods...* <note>original: "זה בחכמתו השם ג' יודין"</note> that is, regarding this mystery, they write the Name with three Yods, as:

<image-desc>Three Hebrew letters Yod (י י י) arranged horizontally, each surmounted by three small vertical decorative strokes or crowns (tagin).</image-desc>

Where the single four-letter name is written with three single letters, which is approved by common usage. 

There was also once, in the days of Antiochus Eupator, a man named **Judas**, son of Mattathias, a noble warrior and a leader in war for the laws, the temple, the city, and the citizens. He was most fierce against the Jews' enemies. When Antiochus and his army were rushing against them, Judas, warned by an angel, gave his fellow soldiers this noble sign as a password: **M-K-B-I** <note>Hebrew: מכב'י (Maccabee).</note>. He exhorted them to behave bravely under these four letters, promising that it would be a sign of victory from God. The Jewish soldiers accepted it with joyful hearts as a source of great consolation; fighting powerfully under that seal, they slew fourteen thousand in Antiochus's camp, as well as a huge number of elephants and those who had been placed upon them. 

Because of this, it happened that the leader of the war, Judas, who was previously known as such, was thereafter called by everyone **Maccabee**, because these four characters sounded as such when syllabicized. And since they were victors in so many battles by the power of that sign, the military tribunes and the wise men of Israel marveled, asking Judas how so many triumphs had occurred under this sign he had given? Judas Maccabeus responded that in that sign was the presence of the Omnipotent Ineffable One. He showed them those words of Moses in Exodus 15, saying: **Who is like unto thee among the strong, O Lord?** <note>original Hebrew: "מי כמוך באלים יהוה" (*Mi Kamokha Ba'elim Adonai*).</note>. These four characters designate these words as their initials, where it is clearly perceived to signify the name Tetragrammaton, and to be in truth—

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Notarikon, a Kabbalistic method where letters of a word stand for entire sentences, or initials of a sentence form a new word. # ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...a memorable symbol of the divine name of 72 letters <note>A reference to the *Shem HaMephorash*, a 72-letter name of God derived from Exodus 14:19-21.</note> through numerical equality. Moved by this, those who were of the army of Judah <note>Judas Maccabeus</note>, fighting again, overthrew no fewer than thirty-five thousand men, as the records indicate. They were wonderfully delighted by the presence of God, blessing the almighty Lord, the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, in their native tongue. From this, you understand that an entire word can be signified by a single letter, whether that letter stands alone or helps to complete another collective word. Just as a whole expression is said to mark an entire sentence equally, as in the fifth chapter of Daniel: *Mene, Tekel, Peres* <note>original Hebrew: "מנא תקל פרסין"</note>; that is, **Numbered, weighed, divided**. These indeed represented this to Nebuchadnezzar: God has **numbered** your kingdom and finished it. It has been **weighed** in the balance and found wanting. Your kingdom has been **divided** and given to the Medes and Persians. Thus, either one expression scattered through letters creates many, or many expressions retracted through certain of their letters gather into one; hence, from many, one, and from one, many.

That this is in no way strange is shown by the frequent use of two monosyllables, as they say Virgil <note>original: "Maronem," referring to Publius Vergilius Maro</note> wrote in his poems: *"Yes and No are the well-known monosyllables all men frequent; if these were removed, there is nothing left of men that speech could turn over."* Therefore, almost all conversations of all men signify **is** and **is not**. For this reason, in this art, who would wish to doubt that a single letter can denote a whole expression, and a single expression an extended sentence? And conversely, in the same way, a single sentence can denote a chosen and intended expression. From this arises a certain occult and admirable technology of letters <note>epistolary cryptography</note>, which I have often imitated. In grave dangers and at the highest risk of affairs, I wrote a letter in the German language which I intended to be understood by a Latin man in Tuscany or Etruria; and in a reverse manner, I wrote in Latin what I wanted a German man, unskilled in Latin, to know. I would wish you to receive this, whatever it may be, with a grateful mind and in your deepest senses, for it is no small thing; store it away diligently.

In practice, if we work correctly, letters of this kind come to us in four ways:
1. They are taken from the **beginning** of a word to signify something else, as in the opening of Genesis: *Yom Ha-Shishi Vaykhulu Ha-Shamayim* <note>original Hebrew: "יום הששי ויכלו השמים"; meaning "The sixth day. And the heavens were finished"</note>. Behold, the initials form the Tetragrammaton <note>Y-H-V-H</note>.
2. Or from the **end** of any words, as in Psalm 1: *Lo khen ha-reshaim* <note>original Hebrew: "לא כן הרשעים"; meaning "Not so the wicked"</note>, which when transposed make *Amen* <note>original Hebrew: "אמן"</note>. For he wanted this to be understood: "Not so the wicked," because they will not say "Amen," and therefore they shall be sent into Gehenna <note>a place of spiritual punishment or purification</note>.
3. Or they are those which offer themselves **individually**, each one through an entire expression gathered into one, as in Psalm 3: "Many rise up against me." Who are these "many"? The Kabbalists answer: *P-R-S-V-M* <note>original Hebrew: "פ ר ס ו מ"</note> are the **P**ersans (or Romans), **B**abylonians, **I**onians (Greeks), and **M**edes.
4. Or finally, a letter is not intended in relation to the constitution of other words, but each is taken according to the **signification of its own property**. For example, when mention is made of the two ages, the letter <term>Yod</term> signifies the world to come, and the letter <term>He</term> the present age—that is, this world. Genesis 2: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth *be-hibaream*" <note>original Hebrew: "בה' בראם"; meaning "when they were created"</note>; that is, **in He He created them**.

Doubtless, this last consideration of the letters pertains to the substance of the character in itself, and not at all to an accidental relation to another, like the three above. For in this designation they signify either—according to grammatical instruction—the things themselves as first presented by their position, or numbers ordered by the discipline of arithmetic, or certain ratios applied to the words of our Masters, or finally, every creature proceeding from the First Cause and reducible again into the First Cause. Regarding the **primitive position** of the letters, they show it thus:
*   <term>Aleph</term> is a way or instruction. Whence Job 33 says: *I will teach*—that is, I will instruct—*you in wisdom*.
*   <term>Beth</term>, a house. Psalm 23: *I will dwell in the house of the Lord*.
*   <term>Gimel</term>, retribution. Psalm 116: *Because the Lord has dealt bountifully (retributed) with you*.
*   <term>Daleth</term>, a door, gate, or entrance. Genesis 19: *And they drew near to break the door*.
*   <term>He</term>, behold. Genesis 47: *Behold, here is seed for you*.
*   <term>Vav</term>, a hooked peg. Exodus 26: *The hooks shall be of gold*.
*   <term>Zayin</term> <note>OCR: "Sdain"</note>, weapons. 1 Kings 22: *And they washed the armor (weapons) according to the word of the Lord*.
*   <term>Heth</term>, terror. Job 7: *You scare me with dreams*.
*   <term>Teth</term>, a turning away (by metathesis *thet*). Proverbs 4: *Do not decline (turn) to the right or to the left*.
*   <term>Yod</term>, a confession of praise. Genesis 49: *Your brothers shall praise you*...

...of yours. **Kaph** <note>original: *vola*, meaning the palm or hollow of the hand</note>, as in Ecclesiastes 4: "Better is a palm full of rest." **Lamed**, meaning "teach me to do your will." **Mem** <note>original: *aquae*</note>, meaning waters, as in Isaiah 55: "All you who thirst, come to the waters." **Nun**, meaning offspring <note>original: *filiatio*</note>, as in Isaiah 14: "Son and grandson." **Samekh** <note>original: *appositio*</note>, meaning a placing upon, as in Deuteronomy 34: "Because Moses placed—that is, laid—his hands upon him." **Ayin** <note>original: *oculus*</note>, meaning eye, as in Exodus 21: "An eye for an eye." **Pe** <note>original: *os*</note>, meaning mouth, as in Exodus 4: "[Who] made man's mouth?" **Tsade**, meaning sides <note>original: *latera*</note>, as in Exodus 25: "Six branches shall go out from its sides." **Koph**, meaning a revolution or circuit <note>original: *revolutio uel circuitus*</note>, as in Exodus 34: "At the return of the year's time, in the circuit of the year." **Resh**, meaning poverty <note>original: *egestas*</note>, as in Proverbs 10: "The fear of the poor is their poverty." <note>Others, however, interpret this as 'inheritance.'</note> **Shin**, meaning tooth <note>original: *dens*</note>, as in Job 4: "And the teeth of the young lions are broken." **Tav**, meaning a mark <note>original: *signum*</note>, as in Ezekiel 9: "Mark the sign of the Tav upon the foreheads of the men." 

This is the grammatical explanation of the letters, just as people are accustomed to assigning names to various things, whether primary or derivative. I believe nothing here is foreign to a higher revelation, should one be a student of figurative speech. 

Then **Philolaus** spoke: "It seems we must become 'alphabetarian' old men," he said, "who need a spelling-book. For in the meantime, with much study, we have been reduced back to the alphabet." 
**Marranus** replied: "Certainly we are becoming children again; this is your 'Pythagorean palingenesis' <note>From the Greek *palingenesia*, meaning rebirth or reincarnation—a central Pythagorean doctrine.</note>, Philolaus." 
To which **Simon** said: "Do not reject it. This is truly a great matter, even for philosophers—if you believe your Plato—and not at all ridiculous, as it seemed in the *Cratylus* to the young men: to know the letters. For we have nothing else," he said, "by which to judge the truth of primary names." 

<note>original Greek: ἐπ’ ἀνθρώπων ὄνομα γραμμάτων ἡ μίμησίς τυγχάνει οὖσα τῆς οὐσίας, ὀρθότατόν ἐστι διελεῖν τὰ στοιχεῖα</note> 
That is: *Since the imitation of essence among men happens through syllables and letters, it is most correct to first distinguish the elements.* 

From this, I believe they are called 'elements' as if they were 'material ones' <note>original: *hylata*, derived from the Greek *hyle*, meaning matter</note>; that is, the materials from which the greatest things are made out of the smallest, as in that saying of Hesiod: *If you add a little to a little, and put it all together, a great heap will soon be made.* 

**Simon** continued: **Philolaus** says: "You speak truly in all things, for we were only joking with your permission." 
Then he said: "I shall pass to the numbers of the discipline of Arithmetic, which are designated by Hebrew letters. For there is no other language in the whole world whose letters represent any numbers so perfectly. Nevertheless, the later Greeks <note>The 'novice' Greeks who adopted the alphabetic numeral system later than the Semitic peoples.</note> attempted to imitate the Jews, so that they might also display numbers using their own alphabet. But it was necessary for them to devise two extra figures <note>Specifically the *stigma* for 6 and *koppa/sampi* for 90 and 900.</note> for the sixtieth and ninetieth, which are not literally part of the alphabet's order. For these two are schemas and <term>inventions</term> <note>original: *figmenta*—artificial constructs</note> of men led by a zeal for imitation. We cite the books of Homer as witnesses to this. Not even the Romans explain many numbers with letters, a subject you once read in Priscian the Caesar <note>Priscian, the famous 6th-century grammarian</note>, writing to Symmachus about numbers, weights, and measures. 

Let us therefore make four grades of numbers: the first is of units, the second of tens, the third of hundreds, and the fourth of thousands. 

The first grade is marked by the shapes of the alphabet from Aleph to Teth. There are nine symbols, referring individually to the nine numbers: 
א ב ג ד ה ו ז ח ט 
that is: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. 

The second order of tens also contains nine shapes of the alphabet: 
י כ ל מ נ ס ע פ צ 
that is: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety. 

The third grade of hundreds similarly has nine characters: 
ק ר ש ת ך ם ן ף ץ 
that is: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred, nine hundred. 

The fourth grade is of thousands, in which one must return to the shapes of the earlier numbers, although they ought to be larger in stature, so that it is called a 'Great Aleph.' It is written as a broad Aleph and is pronounced with a *patach* like an Italian 'a.' Thus, a 'Great Beth' signifies two thousand. From there, it continues up to nine thousand, and finally a 'Great Yod' for ten thousand; in this order, some are accustomed to marking the figures with points <note>or 'crowns'</note> for height. Thereafter, they do not use figures, but words: 
רבו רבותים
that is: a thousand thousand, two thousand thousand, and the rest. 

The Kabbalists have greatly loved this path of alphabetical numbers. They say that a period of two thousand years preceded the beginning before the world was made. This is because before the word *Bereshit* <note>original: בראשית—meaning 'In the beginning'</note>, the Scripture places a 'Great Beth'...

### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.
->DE ARTE CABALIST. LIB. III.<-

...saying, **Bereshit** <note>Hebrew: "In the beginning," the first word of Genesis</note>. Thus our wise men explain that passage in Proverbs 8: *The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from then.* However, whatever exceeds thousands is regarded as being in the place of the infinite. For the limit of numbers in the sacred scriptures is thousands; for instance, when David wished to show the infinity of value in Psalm 119, he said: *The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver*; that is, without number. Now let us briefly review the third species of the substance of the letters, which refers to certain intentions of our Masters. For example, **Aleph-Beth** signifies "prudence" to them, and **Gimel-Daleth** the "rewarding of the poor," and **Mem**—that is, **Meamar**—evidently signifies "open speech" and "hidden speech," and so on for the others, which we shall recite a little further below, as they are quite frequent in Talmudic usage.

The fourth species of these letters consists in all established and created things, which is of the greatest importance to students of this Cabala, so that they may more easily call the creatures back to the Creator—which is indeed the greatest and most singular pursuit of that discipline. Therefore, I will place each of the letters in its own order, so that you may know each individual element specifically, and so I shall begin. 

From **Aleph** to **Yod**, the orders or choirs of angels are signified. The philosophers call these "separate intelligences" and "incorporeal and insensible liberal forms," which have proceeded and derived from the power of God, who has no form, nor image, nor likeness. For he said in Isaiah 40: *To whom have you likened me, that I should be equal?* and a little before: *To whom then have you made God like? Or what image will you set up for him?* Furthermore, this dwelling place is named **Olam ha-Malakhim** <note>Hebrew: "The World of Angels"</note>: that is, the angelic age, or the Angelic World. 

Next, from the letter **Kaph** to the letter **Tsade**, the orders of the heavens are designated. These are dispensed by the influence of the angels, having been gifted by the power of God the Creator, and it is called **Olam ha-Galgalim** <note>Hebrew: "The World of the Orbs"</note>: that is, the age of the orbs or spheres. 

Furthermore, from **Tsade** to **Tav**, there intervene the four elements with their forms, and all mixed things together, both living and non-living, which depend upon the power of God, from whom being and living flows into them, as it says in Isaiah: *Creating the heavens and stretching them out, establishing the earth and those things which sprout from it, giving breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those who tread upon it, or walk in it.* They are directed, moreover, by the influences of the angels and the spheres, and that whole realm is called **Olam ha-Yesodot** <note>Hebrew: "The World of the Elements"</note>: that is, the age of elements. In it is man, who is called **Olam ha-Katan** <note>Hebrew: "The Small World"</note>: the small age, which the Greeks call the **microcosmon** <note>Greek: "microcosm"</note>: that is, the minor World, or more correctly, the Little World. For in man himself the properties of all creatures, both the highest and the lowest, shine forth. 

Perhaps we shall repeat these things more usefully to memory if we demonstrate of which things the individual letters are held to be symbols—a truly pleasant matter, celebrated by the most ancient authors, lest there ever be those in the future who mock this art as thin or meager. 

**Aleph** is therefore the mark of the highest and most exalted things, which subsist in the first outflow of divine goodness, such as the angels who are called **Haioth ha-Kodesh** <note>Hebrew: "The Holy Living Creatures"</note>: that is, animals of the sanctuary, or rather, lives without a medium beneath God. These angels, by the power of God, purify, illuminate, and perfect those proximately below them, which in common parlance is called their "influence." 

**Beth**, the second letter, signifies the second rank of angels from God himself, who are called **Ophanim** <note>Hebrew: "Wheels"</note>: that is, forms or wheels. They are derived in the second place from the power of God through the prior intelligence, and they themselves also flow from God into lower things. The wise have also said that **Beth** is the mark of Wisdom. 

**Gimel** represents, from the superior essences, the angels who are called **Aralim** <note>Hebrew: "Valiant ones" or "Thrones"</note>: that is, great, strong, and robust angels, who descend in the third order from the goodness of the divine majesty. They are illuminated by the power of God through the second intelligence, and they likewise flow into lower things. 

**Daleth** is the symbol of the fourth emanation among the heavenly beings of those who are called **Hasmalim** <note>Hebrew: "Glowing ones" or "Electrum"</note>, and they are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the third intelligence, and by that power they flow into lower things. 

**He**, the letter, designates superior beings of the fifth emanation from God himself, which are the **Seraphim** <note>Hebrew: "Burning ones"</note>: that is, Seraphim. They are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the fourth intelligence, and by that same power they flow into lower things.
