### JOHANNES REUCHLIN
->BOOK III<-

...of the sixth order, who are called **Mallachim**: that is, angels <note>Hebrew: *Malakhim*, meaning "messengers"</note>. They receive influence from the power of God through the medium of the fifth intelligence, and by that same power they flow into lower things. **Zayin** is the sign of the higher blessed spirits of the seventh order, who are named **Elohim**: that is, gods <note>Hebrew: *Elohim*, a name for God that here refers to a specific rank of angels</note>. They are influenced by the divine power through the angels of the sixth order, and by that same power they flow into lower beings. 

**Het** <note>Hebrew: ח</note> is the sign of the higher beings of the eighth emanation, and they are the angels who are called **Bne Elohim**: that is, sons of Gods <note>Hebrew: *Benei Elohim*</note>. They are infused with the power of **El** <note>Hebrew: "God"</note> through the angels of the seventh order, and by that same power of God they flow into the lower beings. **Tet** is the sign of the angels of the ninth emanation, who are called **Cherubim** <note>Hebrew: *Keruvim*</note>. They are influenced by the power of God through the medium of the intelligence of the eighth order, and by that same power they flow into lower things. 

**Yod**, the tenth letter, signifies the essence of the intelligences of the tenth emanation; they are called **Issim**, the noble and patrician ones <note>Hebrew: *Ishim*, "men"</note>. These are lower than all the other hierarchies. They are illuminated by the power of God through the ninth order, and by that same power they flow into the sons of men, providing knowledge, science, and life-giving industry. This is why those endowed with such a faculty are called **Ishim**: that is, men of noble intelligence. Regarding them, Psalm 49 says: *All you sons of the earth and sons of men* <note>original Latin: "Quicq[ue] & filii hominum"</note>, which is properly read as "both the common sons and the noble sons," as if to say, both the rustic and the noble. 

We take this denomination from the order of intelligences themselves. For there is in us an intelligent, highest part of the soul which Aristotle calls **nous** <note>Greek: *νοῦν*, mind or intellect</note>, which alone comes to us from the outside. From there proceed prophetic visions and great and holy dreams; it is called the **active intellect** <note>Hebrew: *Sekhel ha-Poel*</note>, which serves as the boundary of the Angelic World.

Next follows **Kaph**; this letter designates the **Primum Mobile** <note>term: the "first moved" sphere, the outermost shell of the universe that drives the motion of all other spheres</note> from **El Shaddai** <note>Hebrew: "God Almighty"</note> himself as the first immediate cause, though communicated through the spirit of rational life, which is the angel **Metattron** <note>Hebrew: *Metatron*, the prince of the presence</note>. He is called the active intellect of the physical World, providing a path for the penetration of forms into all lower things; therefore, he flows by divine power into everything that is mobile. 

**Final Kaph** signifies the circuit of the fixed stars, which is named the eighth sphere in relation to us. However, in terms of its descent, it is the second orb, divided into the twelve signs of the zodiac, which we call the "wheels" <note>Hebrew: *Galgalim*</note>. It is influenced by the power of God through the medium of its own intelligence and flows into lower things through this letter. 

**Lamed** is the sign of the first sphere of the planets, which are called **Labu** <note>perhaps a variation of *Levav*, heart, or a corruption of a planetary term</note> as if they were "walkers," whom the Latins call **errones** <note>wanderers</note>, after the likeness of the stars, which is why they call them **planets** <note>Greek: *πλανῆτας*, wanderers</note>. It is called the seventh orb, attributed to Saturn, which we name **Shabbatai** <note>Hebrew: *Shabbatay*, related to the Sabbath</note>; it is influenced and it flows. 

**Open Mem** represents the sphere of Jupiter, which is named by us **Tzedek** <note>Hebrew: *Tzedek*, meaning "Justice"</note>. It is influenced by the power of God through the medium of the higher intelligence and by that same power flows into lower things. 

**Closed Mem** is the symbol of the sphere of Mars, which we call **Maadim** <note>Hebrew: *Ma'adim*, "the red one"</note>, of the fifth orb. It is influenced by the power of the Creator through the nearest higher angel, and by that same power it flows to the lower. 

**Nun** signifies the greater light, which is called **Shemesh**: that is, the Sun <note>Hebrew: *Shemesh*</note>. Its orb is also called **Chamah** <note>Hebrew: *Hammah*, "the hot one"</note>. It is influenced by God through the medium of the sixth intelligence, which it then flows into lower things. 

**Final Nun** indicates the sphere of Venus, which is called by us **Nogah** <note>Hebrew: *Nogah*, "brightness"</note>; it is established by the power of God and flows by the mediation of the seventh intelligence. 

**Samekh** <note>Hebrew: ס</note> is the symbol of the scribe, who is called **Cochab** <note>Hebrew: *Kokhav*, "star"</note>, and in Latin is called Mercury. He is influenced by the power of God from those above, and by that same power flows into the lower. 

**Ayin** <note>Hebrew: ע</note> is the mark of the sphere of the Moon, which is called by us **Yareach** <note>Hebrew: *Yareaḥ*</note>, and it appears as the left eye of the World. It is the last of the star-bearing orbs, and because of this it is sometimes called **Levanah** <note>Hebrew: *Levanah*, "the white one"</note>. All these things are committed to the faculty of Astrology. 

**Pe** signifies the intellectual soul, both individual and universal. It is influenced by the separate intelligences into which it is infused by God, both in the celestial spheres and in the world of elements, and in all living things, higher and lower. 

**Final Pe** denotes the animal spirits, which are directed by the higher intelligences by the power and command of God. 

**Tzadi** <note>Hebrew: *Tsade*</note> symbolizes matter, both the intelligible matter of the heavens and the sensible matter of the elements and all mixed things. They are directed by divine power through separate intelligences into their own forms. 

**Final Tzadi** shows the forms of the elements, which are...

### ON THE CABALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

Air, Water, and Earth. These are ruled by divine power through the angels called **Issim** <note>Hebrew: *Ishim*, literally "men," the tenth and lowest rank of angels in the hierarchy of Maimonides</note>, and by the power of the heavens, and by the power of prime matter, which is the fountain and origin of all elements. **Koph** <note>Hebrew: ק</note> is the symbol of inanimate things and minerals, and of those things which are called "elemented" and mixed. These are directed by divine power through the celestial spheres and the separate intelligences, which are called **Issim**. They flow into the lower things in the region of the four elements. 

**Resh** <note>Hebrew: ר</note> signifies all things that grow, such as fruits, crops, and the plants of the earth; they are influenced by the power of God through the celestial bodies and the separate intelligences named **Issim**, and also by the temperaments of the elements. 

**Shin** <note>Hebrew: ש</note> designates all sentient things, including the creeping and walking things of the earth, the fish of the waters, and the birds of the air alike, and whatever irrational creatures have vital movement. These are ruled by the power of God from the celestial bodies and the intelligences we call **Issim**, and by the temperaments of the elements. 

**Tav** <note>Hebrew: ת</note> is the symbol of Man and human nature, which is the perfection and end of all creatures. It is directed by God through the temperaments and qualities of the elements, according to the influences of the heavens and through the specific duties of the separate intelligences, the **Issim**, who are of an angelic condition. Just as they are the end and consummation in the World of Angels, so is Man the end and perfection of creatures in the World of the Elements—or rather, in the World of All Things. For he was created out of two worlds, as it is written: *The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.* 

These matters are treated more abundantly by our ancestors, whose descendants (among whom we count ourselves) clearly show a most burning love for the Sacred Scriptures, having striven to give an explanation for even the smallest details. For example: concerning the letter **Aleph**, it is written in the book *Ha-Bahir* <note>original: "הבהיר", The Book of Brilliance, an early and influential Cabalistic text</note>, where Rabbi Amorai sat and disputed: why is **Aleph** placed at the head of the Alphabet? The answer is: because it existed before all things, even before the Law <note>The Torah</note>. Menahem Recanati mentions this concerning Rabbi Rahumai, the author of that book, in his first distinction on Genesis. 

Furthermore, for what reason does **Beth** follow immediately? Surely because it was the beginning of the Law <note>The first letter of the first word of Genesis, *Bereshit*, is Beth</note>. And why was **Gimel** not named "Gidel," since in the Sacred Scriptures the word *Gadal* <note>meaning "to grow large"</note> is placed before it, and *Gamal* <note>meaning "to wean"</note> follows it in Genesis 21, where it is written: *And the child grew [va-yigdal] and was weaned [va-yigamal]*? Wise men certainly did not disdain to investigate such equal points as these. 

However, there are also some who, for the sake of brevity, passed over giving certain explanations and only wrote those things which simply pertain to the matter, since they always endeavored to hasten toward higher things with all diligence and study. One such was Rabbi Jacob Cohen in his book titled *Exposition of the Holy Name* <note>Hebrew: "פירוש השם הקדוש", *Perush Ha-Shem Ha-Kadosh*</note>. For concerning the Alphabet, he speaks briefly thus: 

Aleph: **Air** <note>Hebrew: *Alif*</note> 
Beth: **Life** <note>Hebrew: *Chayyim*</note> 
Gimel: **Peace** <note>Hebrew: *Shalom*</note> 
Daleth: **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note> 
He: **Sight** <note>Hebrew: *Re’iyah*</note> 
Vav: **Hearing** <note>Hebrew: *Shemi’ah*</note> 
Zayin: **Smell** <note>Hebrew: *Reyach*</note> 
Het: **Speech** <note>Hebrew: *Dibbur*</note> 
Tet: **Infusion** <note>Hebrew: *Le’itah*</note> 
Yod: **Bed** <note>Hebrew: *Mishkav*</note> 
Kaph: **Wealth** <note>Hebrew: *Osher*</note> 
Lamed: **Business** <note>Hebrew: *Melakhah*</note> 
Mem: **Water** <note>Hebrew: *Mayim*</note> 
Nun: **Path** <note>Hebrew: *Halokh*</note> 
Samekh: **Spirit** <note>Hebrew: *Ruach*</note> 
Ayin: **Laughter** <note>Hebrew: *Sechok*</note> 
Pe: **Seed** <note>Hebrew: *Zera*</note> 
Koph: **Suspicion** <note>Hebrew: *Chashad*</note> 
Resh: **Sleep** <note>Hebrew: *Sheynah*</note> 
Shin: **Grace** and **Fire** <note>Hebrew: *Chen* and *Esh*</note>

It is as if he were enumerating them with these words: Air, life, peace, wisdom, sight, hearing, smell, speech, infusion, lying down, wealth, business, water, path, spirit, laughter, seed, suspicion, sleep, grace, fire, power. These and other things like them which you have heard, I have gathered as briefly as I could from the monuments of the fathers, so that I might offer you at least some taste of this literary profession. For the distinguished author Rabbi Akiba wrote about these things with no small care, and many of our most learned men, whom we deem worthy of great honor, have imitated him. For they said that in the exposition of the Alphabet many meanings lie hidden. 

And Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra, concerning this in the book titled *The Mystery of the Law* <note>Hebrew: "סוד התורה", *Sod Ha-Torah*</note>, says: *And the truth is that it is good for the wise man to learn the source of wisdom* <note>original: "והאמת כי טוב הוא למשכיל שילמך מוצאת החכמה"</note>. Yet he says we should not labor in this literary art for all the time of our lives, nor be twisted days and nights in the volumes of Rabbi Judah (who is said to be the first Hebrew grammarian <note>Judah ben David Hayyuj</note>), or in those twenty books which Marinus <note>Jonah ibn Janah</note> composed on literary instruction, or the twenty-two which Samuel Nagid <note>Samuel ibn Naghrillah</note> published on the same subject. Thus far Abraham Ibn Ezra; nor did that most prudent man, so skilled in letters, think so in vain, regarding...

# BY JOHANNES REUCHLIN

...for we are born for greater and higher things. I have just spoken of the four considerations pertaining to the substance of the letter; now, in my opinion, we must conclude what we began some time ago regarding the accidental relationship of letters, which is called <term>נוטריקון</term> <note>original: "Notariakon" — a method of shorthand or forming new words from the initials or final letters of other words</note>, that is, Notariacon. In this part, we consider which letter signifies which word. It has three species. For when some sign is taken from the beginning of a word, and, as is usually done, is marked with dots above, it is called <term>ראשהתיבות</term> <note>original: "Rashei Tevot" — literally "heads of words," or acrostics</note>, that is, the head of a word, and is customarily written like this: <term>ל״ח</term> <note>An abbreviation for "le-chayim," meaning "to life!"</note>. Similarly, when it is taken from the limit and end of any given word, then it is named <term>סופי התיבות</term> <note>original: "Sofei Tevot" — literally "ends of words"</note>, that is, the end of a word, which they are accustomed to represent in this way: <term>מ״ס</term>. But if individual marks are derived from each of the letters of any word, then we call that by the general name Notariacon. To this Philolaus said: "O our Simon, how secret and hidden these things are to outsiders!" Then he [Simon] said: "Perhaps I shall show you much more hidden things in this third part of Kabbalah, which is called <term>תמורה</term> <note>original: "Temurah" — meaning exchange or permutation</note>, where there is a mutual substitution of one letter for another; and this happens as many times as the alphabets are permuted. They are permuted twenty-two times, following the number of the letters, because we read twenty-two letters of the Jews. It will always be permissible to take one of any two joined letters for the other, and that combination is called <term>צירוף</term> <note>original: "Tziruf" — meaning combination or joining</note>. For example, if I were to join these six letters of the Latin alphabet — *a b c d e f* — two by two, so that under the first yoke are *a* and *b*, under the second *c* and *d*, and under the third *e* and *f*. Suppose I wished to urge someone skilled in this art through a letter that, when about to petition a prince, he should fall at his feet. Thus I write *d b c f*, which he will understand as *Cade* <note>original: "Cade" — Latin for "fall!" (imperative). Here, D replaces C, B replaces A, C replaces D, and F replaces E based on the pairs a-b, c-d, e-f</note>, and so on with others. This whole operation results from an alphabetical revolution, so that one letter succeeds another in its own combined yoke: namely, *a* for *b* and *b* for *a* in turn, similarly *c* for *d* and *d* for *c*, and likewise *e* for *f* and *f* for *e*. This proceeds even more easily in Hebrew, with nothing standing in the way, because the sounds which the Latins call vowels are not placed within the order of the Jewish alphabet. Moved by this in ancient times, our father Abraham said — as is read in the second chapter of the book <term>Ietzira</term> <note>original: "Sefer Yetzirah" or "Book of Formation," a foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> — 'Aleph with all, and all with Aleph,' and no differently, 'Beth with all, and all with Beth,' and so with each individual letter. Therefore, to make this more manifest by example, I shall bring forth the twenty-two alphabets which Abraham, in that same volume of creation, arranged quite skillfully and usefully."

### ON THE KABBALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

This mixture of the twenty-two elements is by no means to be understood in a crude or unlearned fashion: for all these things are spirits. Thus it is written in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "Ietzira" (Sefer Yetzirah), the foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>: "And with that spirit, God engraved twenty-two letters: three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples; and each of them is a spirit." These things have been handed down to us so that we might contemplate them spiritually with great joy, not for the purpose of speaking against them or mocking them. Rather, we must embrace the mysteries of the scriptures with pious faith. For by believing in the letters, we more easily behold higher things, and we trust that we can find hidden things within the letters, just like the word of God in the midst of the darkness, when He said to Moses: "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you." Indeed, they shall believe in the **32** <note>original: "לב" (LB) — the numerical value is 32, referring to the "32 Paths of Wisdom" composed of the 10 Sephirot and the 22 letters</note> forever.

For it is necessary for a Kabbalist to believe strongly, not like an old woman, and to receive the mandates of the fathers regarding the letters with singular love, a joyful mind, and a happy heart, with joy and confidence, as says Psalm 70: "Let them exult and be glad **in you**" <note>original: "בך" (BK) — the Hebrew word "in you" has the numerical value of 22, which Simon interprets as the 22 letters of the alphabet</note>, that is, in the twenty-two [letters] who seek you. For you should know that the twenty-two letters are the foundations of the World and the Law, as is treated extensively in the second book of the *Garden of Nuts* <note>original: "Horti nucis" — refers to the work *Ginnat Egoz* by Joseph Gikatilla</note>, which you have either read or will read.

Then Philolaus said: "Certainly, I have never read nor seen such books, though I have searched with no small effort to find where they might be hidden."

And Marranus said: "I do not know by what agreement this kind of stingy 'Tantalus-play' <note>A reference to Tantalus, suggesting the books are kept just out of reach</note> regarding books happens, so that they do not even freely give them to a friend, or sell them for any amount of money."

Then Simon said: "It is a statute for us that the secrets of the Law are not to be given to strangers, but to a **Sage** <note>original: "חכם" (Chacham) — a wise man or counselor</note>, that is, to a wise Counselor. Not only to a domestic counselor, nor only to a wise man, but specifically to a wise counselor who is not outside the Law and is not unlearned. I pray you do not take this poorly. For often, because of imminent danger during our long dispersion, the concerned assembly of the fathers prudently decreed: **'However, he should flee from that into which he recently fell'** <note>original: "ברם שהוא ברח ממה שנפל בו באחרונה"</note>, following the authority of our Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides</note>, who enumerates the causes and recites everything in chapter 71 of the first book of the *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "Perplexorum" (Moreh Nevukhim)</note>. But I hope you will take these and other matters of our people in good part; therefore, setting aside that dispute, I shall proceed with the third part of the Kabbalistic art. 

You have heard concerning the two hundred and forty-two combinations of letters, and the two hundred and thirty-one permutations of conjugations, beyond the commonly used Alphabet, in which they are also accustomed to connect any two letters in their own order for mutual exchange. This matter is commonly considered a meager thing and perhaps held in contempt by the unskilled at first glance, but it is nonetheless something that should be highly exalted by men. As it is read in Psalm 12: **"When vileness is exalted among the sons of men"** <note>original: "כרום זלות לבני אדם"</note>. To which Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi</note> cites there what is said in the Psalm: "The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner." 

I pray you, do not consider it carelessly, for it is not written in vain: **Gematria** <note>original: "גמטריא" — the system of assigning numerical value to letters</note>. For Kabbalistically, **Gematria** signifies two hundred and forty-two: for that is the total of all the combinations described above. You should venerate those two hundred and thirty-one variations with fitting honor. For all things that exist and all things that are spoken arise from them. Concerning these 'Gates,' as they call them, our Father Abraham said in the *Book of Formation*: **"It is found that every word and every creature proceeds from one [source]"** <note>original: "נמצא כל הדבור וכל היצור יצא מא"</note>. Indeed, with their help, we can easily arrange our own salvation, because we are to be led back through the consideration of all created things to the one Creator, according to human capacity for knowledge—which is our salvation and eternal life. This is done by God through His name, returning again into God. He Himself is His very name, the four-letter name, blessed forever and ever, which the Psalmist showed when he said: 'And they shall know that you, your name is the Tetragrammaton, you alone are the Most High over all the earth.' <meta>This page continues the dialogue where Simon is teaching Philolaus and Marranus about the mystical manipulation of the Hebrew language. Having discussed the "substantial" nature of the letters, he now moves into "accidental relations"—the specific techniques of Notarikon, Gematria, and Temurah.</meta>

# JOHANNES REUCHLIN

For we are born for greater and higher things. I have just spoken of the four considerations pertaining to substantial matters; now, in my opinion, I must conclude by discussing the accidental relationship of letters which we began a while ago. It is called <term>Notarikon <note>original: "נוטריקון", a method of shorthand using the first or last letters of words to form new meanings or acronyms</note></term> and <term>Gematria <note>original: "גמטריא", the system of assigning numerical values to letters to find hidden connections between words</note></term>. We consider Notarikon in the sense of what each individual letter signifies. It has three species. When the mark is taken from the beginning of a word and, as is customary, is noted with marks at the top, it is called <term>Rashe Tevot <note>original: "ראשהתיבות", meaning "heads of words"</note></term>, and is written in the usual way. Likewise, when it is taken from the boundary or end of a given word, it is then named <term>Sofe Tevot <note>original: "סופהתיבות", meaning "ends of words"</note></term>, which they usually represent in the manner of <term>So <note>original: "סוֹ", an abbreviation for Sofe Tevot</note></term>. If, however, individual notes are drawn from every single letter of any word, we then call that by the general name Notarikon.

To these things Reuchlin says: "O our Simon, how secret and remote these things are to outsiders!" 

Then Simon says: "Perhaps I shall show you much more hidden things in this part called <term>Temurah <note>original: "תמורה", meaning "exchange" or "permutation"</note></term>, where a mutual exchange of letter for letter occurs as often as the alphabets are permuted. They are permuted according to the number of letters twenty-two times, because we read that there are twenty-two letters of the Jews. With any of the eternal letters joined together, it will be permitted to take one for another, and that method is called <term>Tziruf <note>original: "צירוף", meaning "combination" or "joining"</note></term>."

"For example, if I were to join the first six letters of the Latin alphabet, **a b c d e f**, in pairs, so that under the first yoke are **a b**, under the second **c d**, and under the third **e f**. If I wished to write a letter to someone skilled in this art—perhaps as one about to petition a prince—that he should 'fall' [Latin: *cadat*] before his feet, I would write **d b c f**. He would understand this as **Cade** <note>Latin: "Cade" is the imperative "Fall!" or "Yield!" If A=B, B=A, C=D, D=C, E=F, and F=E, then 'Cade' becomes 'Dbcf'</note>, and so it goes for others."

"This entire workmanship comes from the revolution of the alphabet, so that letters succeed each other by a mutual exchange, each bound to its own 'yoke' or pair: namely, **a** for **b**, and **b** for **a**; similarly **c** for **d**, and **d** for **c**; and likewise **e** for **f**, and **f** for **e**. This proceeds even more easily in Hebrew, without any obstacle, because those sounds which the Latins call vowels are not placed in the order of the Jewish alphabet. Therefore, in an ancient age, our father Abraham was moved by this when he said, as is read in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "Ietzira" (Sefer Yetzirah)</note> Chapter 2: 'Aleph with all, and all with Aleph; and Beth with all, and all with Beth,' and so on for each one. Therefore, to make this more manifest by example, I will bring forth twenty-two alphabets, just as Abraham arranged them quite skillfully and usefully in that same volume of creation."

<note>These are tables of "Temurah" or letter substitutions. The first is "Albam," the second is a variant, and the third is the famous "Atbash" cipher where the first letter is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>

This mixture of twenty-two elements is by no means to be understood in a rustic or unlearned way: for all things are spirits. So it is written in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "libro Ietzira", referring to the *Sefer Yetzirah*, one of the oldest and most important Kabbalistic texts</note>: "And God engraved with that spirit twenty-two letters—three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples—and each of them is a spirit." Therefore, these things have been handed down to us for spiritual contemplation with great joy, not for speaking against or for mocking, but for embracing the mysteries of the scriptures with pious faith. For by believing in the letters, we more easily contemplate higher things, and we trust that hidden things can be found in the letters, like the word of God in the midst of the darkness, which He spoke to Moses: "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you." Indeed, they shall believe in the **22** <note>original: "כב", the numerical value of the Hebrew letters Kaf and Bet</note>—that is, the twenty-two—forever.

For it is necessary for a Kabbalist to believe not like an old woman, but strongly, and to receive those things which are the commands of the fathers in the letters with singular love, and a pleasant and joyful mind, with gladness and trust, as in Psalm 70: "Let them exult and be glad in the **22**"—that is, the twenty-two—"who seek you." For you must know that the twenty-two letters are the foundations of the World and of the Law, as is treated extensively in the second book of the *Garden of the Nut* <note>original: "Horti nucis", referring to *Ginat Egoz* by Joseph Gikatilla</note>, which you have either read or will read. 

Then Philolaus said: "Certainly, I have never read nor seen such books, although I have searched with no small effort to find where they might be hidden."

And Marranus said: "I do not know why there is such a great scarcity of these kinds of books, so that they do not even publish them generously for a friend, or sell them for any price."

Then Simon said: "It is decreed for us that the secrets of the law are not to be given to strangers, but only to a **wise counselor** <note>original: "ליועץ חכם"</note>. Not just to a domestic counselor, nor just to a wise man, but to one who is both a wise counselor, who is not an outsider and is not unlearned. I pray you do not take this poorly. For often, because of the imminent danger during our long dispersion, the assembly of our fathers carefully and providently decreed: **that he should flee from that into which he fell last** <note>original: "ברח שהוא ברח מומה שנפל בו באחרונה", a maxim regarding the protection of secrets and avoidance of past errors</note>, according to our Egyptian author Moses <note>referring to Moses Maimonides</note>, who enumerates the causes and recites the events in chapter 71 of the first book of the *Guide for the Perplexed*. But I hope you will take these and other things of our nation in good part; therefore, having dismissed that dispute, I shall proceed with the third part of the Kabbalah."

"You have received, concerning the combinations of letters, two hundred and forty-two permutations, and two hundred and thirty-one conjugations—besides the commonly used alphabet—the two letters of which they are accustomed to connect in their order for mutual exchange. This is a matter commonly thought meager and perhaps held in contempt by the unskilled at first glance, but it is one that should be greatly exalted among men. As is read in Psalm 12: **'In exalting the despised things among the sons of men.'** <note>original: "ברם זלזות לבני אדם"</note> To which Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi</note> cites there what is said in the Psalm: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.' Indeed, I pray you do not consider it carelessly, for it is not written in vain: **Gematria** <note>original: "גמטריא"</note>. For Kabbalistically it signifies two hundred and forty-two <note>Simon here links the word Gematria to the number of combinations he just mentioned</note>; for all the combinations described above are that many, and you should venerate those two hundred and thirty-one variations with fitting honor."

"For all things that exist and all things that are spoken arise from them; for regarding those 'gates,' as they call them, our father Abraham said in the *Book of Formation*: **'And he brought forth every word and every creature...'** <note>original: "ויוציא כל הדיבור וכל היצור"</note> ...existing and proceeding from them. We can easily arrange these for our salvation by their aid, since we are to be led back through the consideration of all created things into a useful human knowledge of the one Creator, which is our salvation and eternal life. This is done by God through His name, returning again into God. He Himself is His own four-letter name, blessed forever and ever, which the Psalmist showed when he said: 'And they shall know that you alone, whose name is the **Tetragrammaton**, are the Most High over all the earth.' Therefore, this name alone is called **Shem HaMephorash** <note>original: "Senhamaphores", meaning the 'Explicit' or 'Distinct' Name of God</note>: that is, the name..."

# JOHANN REUCHLIN'S
### ON THE KABBALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...expounding the essence of God. An experiment of this is taken from the first part of the craft. There is another name of God succeeding into the place of that one, which is written with twelve letters, the explanation of which will be received in the second part. There is another name besides, which is most conveniently treated in this third part of Kabbalah: that of the forty-two characters. Not that a single pronunciation of one name consists of forty-two letters—for it is known to any intelligent person, and in the writings of Moses Maimonides <note>Maimonides was a preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher; Reuchlin often cites him to bridge rational philosophy and mystical tradition.</note>, that a single name written out that way can nowhere be found. Rather, there are many names complexly intertwined among themselves and within themselves, aggregated from many letters, which lead the Kabbalist through certain hidden ratios to the purity of the knowledge of the God of the Tetragrammaton <term>Y-H-V-H<gloss>The four-letter name of God, often rendered as Yahweh or Jehovah</gloss></term>, which similarly signifies 42 through arithmetic <note>Reuchlin refers to Gematria, where the numerical values of the letters in the expanded spelling of the Tetragrammaton can total 42.</note>. Forty-two characters of this kind, through such names, are hereafter called "one name" because they ultimately signify only one thing; just as, conversely, other composite and collective names often signify many things for a single reality. It could therefore happen in the present circumstances that our intellect might be led toward God through some things that could not be explained except by many and diverse words. Nor is that a wonder, since ingenious craftsmen are accustomed to track a spring through many and diverse rivulets. In this way, from the abyss of His own fountain, God brought forth all things, and they flow back to that infinite whirlpool:

<note>original Hebrew: "ויאמר ברבי ער להעמיד כל הדברים במעין המחשבת וה... בת מאמר במעין אין חקר ואין מספר לאורה המתעלמת ב... בהוספת החשך המוסתרת בכלל ארבעים ושנים אותיות"</note>
*He spoke through the great master to establish all things in the fountain of thought and... in the word of the fountain that has no searching and no number, for the light hidden in... by the addition of the concealed darkness within the totality of the forty-two letters.*

These are the words of the most contemplative teacher, Hamai, in the book *Ma'ayan* <note>original: "מעין", meaning 'Spring' or 'Source'</note>, that is, the *Speculative Book*, which he himself usefully cites in the *Sefer Ma'ayan HaChokhmah* <note>original: "ספר מעין החכמה", meaning 'The Book of the Spring of Wisdom'</note>, although a man of such integrity would not have lacked for testimony. Now I will attempt to see if I am able to interpret these things into English, at least so that the meaning suffers no harm. *As he foretold,* he says, *the thing in the word, and the word in the thing, until he should restore all things to the fountain of radiance, and the radiance into the word, as if into a fountain whose power is no less, nor its number, toward the inaccessible light hidden by an increase of darkness in the universe of forty-two letters.* Thus far Hamai.

Furthermore, this name—so venerable and to be worshipped—designated by forty-two letters, is called by the most excellent of the wise (may their memory be a blessing <note>A traditional Jewish honorific for the deceased: "Zichronam Livracha".</note>) <term>Kadosh u-Mekudash<gloss>Holy and Sanctified</gloss></term>. Therefore, it was hidden from the unrefined and the unworthy through the mixing of the alphabet’s revolution, and was revealed through the alphabetic combination only to those leading a contemplative life, such as Jeremiah. It is said that Jeremiah used to read often in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>original: "libro Ietzira", the Book of Formation, a key text on the mystical creation of the world through letters.</note>, as is found written in the *Sefer Bitachon* <note>original: "בספר בטחון", the Book of Confidence or Trust</note>, whose author is Rabbi Judah, who was a Hebrew. And when Jeremiah had worn the *Sefer Yetzirah* with his hands much and often by night and day, a <term>Bat Kol<gloss>Daughter of a Voice; a divine echo or heavenly proclamation</gloss></term> is said to have come to him, which compelled him to toil over that same volume for three years.

And so, after a space of three years, when the joining and treatment of the characters finally pleased him so that he might give work to them, suddenly a "new man" was created for him and his companions <note>This is an early account of the creation of a Golem—a living being formed from dust and animated by the sacred letters.</note>. And on his forehead was written: <term>YHVH Elohim Emet<gloss>The LORD God is Truth</gloss></term>. Then it is said that the recently created man, carrying the writing on his forehead, waited no longer, but with a knife in a quickly moved hand, he removed and took away the first letter in *Emet* <note>Truth</note>, that is, the *Aleph*. Thus there remained the rest in these words: <term>YHVH Elohim Met<gloss>The LORD God is Dead</gloss></term>.

Because of this matter, Jeremiah was struck with indignation and tore his garments, and said to him: "Why do you remove the *Aleph* from *Emet*?" He, responding, said: "Because they have failed everywhere in faithfulness to the creator, who created you in his image and likeness." Jeremiah said: "How then shall I take back this vow?" He replied: "Write the alphabets in reverse in this dust arranged in the space according to the understandings of your hearts." And they did so. And that ash became dust and ash in their sight, and thus it disappeared. Wherefore Jeremiah and those with him asserted that they had received the virtues and powers of the alphabets and elementary permutations from God himself: for the arrangement of their conjugation...

# ON THE KABBALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...he knew before creation. From there, this Alphabetic Kabbalah—that is, the "reception"—passed down to posterity, through which the greatest secrets of divine things are revealed. For when we have revolved that great name, which is to be extolled with all our might, through all the combinations of letters from the last to the first, then the divine knowledge of it will liberally show itself to us. It will offer its faculties to our will and mercifully submit them, if it finds us worthy, and endowed and fortified with purity of mind, sincerity of faith, firmness of hope, and ardor of love.

For our fathers—as Rabbi Tarphon, Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>original: "Rabi Moyses Aegyptius," referring to the philosopher Maimonides</note>, and Rabbi Hamai and others have written—did not wish to reveal that name to any mortal according to the precepts of our Masters, unless he be truly worthy. For they said that it is not to be handed down except to the humble, and to him who stands in the middle of his days, not to the wrathful, nor the drunkard, nor one defiled by evil morals, but to a peaceful man, who speaks pleasantly with creatures, and who guards it with purity. For such a man is beloved above and desired by those of us below, and the fear of him falls upon all creatures.

But so that I may reveal that name to you in the manner of the Kabbalists, I will first divide the 42 letters into seven words; then each word into two small phrases, each of which contains three letters according to the idiom of the Hebrew language. Therefore, having performed the arithmetic multiplication by saying six times seven, there will be forty-two—namely, the entire collection of the letters of that name. I submit this to the inspection of your eyes in this character-set thus: **שגזבהמ : שגתחצא מאזאגב ימבתהא צתגחפז תגאזמא נאצפפש**.

Indeed, while I comprehend each and every letter in this verse, immediately another two-syllable part of one of the seven phrases is born for me. For each phrase of this so precious name is known to consist of six characters, yet only in Hebrew, and not in any other language. For in Latin more will be needed, such as **Sagathbama, Sagaththechaz, Miathazab, Iemibatha, Zethaghapaz, Thegazama, Naazpapas**, which are found in the volumes of the ancients even unto this day, though they are foreign and unknown to the Roman tongue. But they are not to be despised because they are harsh and "barbaric" <note>In the Renaissance, "barbaric" often referred to languages other than polished Latin or Greek, especially those that sounded rough or strange.</note>.

No one should use eyes so blurred in the sight of sacred things that he despises the hidden matter; no one should indulge his ears in such delights when hearing divine things that he only venerates, praises, and follows those things which are pleasant to the senses, beautiful to the eyes, soft to the touch, and charming in speech. Rather, let him grasp spiritual things more than physical ones, constant things more than fleeting ones, and true things more than those that are merely painted over. For indeed, rough and terrifying things often precede the presence of God.

Remember what happened to the Prophet Elijah, when he hid within the caverns and in a cave on Horeb, the mountain of God. Was it not said to him thus: "Behold, the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Y-H-V-H<gloss>The four-letter name of God, often substituted with 'The Lord'</gloss></term> passes by, and a great and strong wind overturning mountains and shattering rocks before the **Tetragrammaton**; but the **Tetragrammaton** was not in the wind. And after the wind an earthquake; but the **Tetragrammaton** was not in the earthquake. And after the earthquake a fire; but the **Tetragrammaton** was not in the fire. And after the fire a still, small voice." And in that voice spoke the glory of the **Tetragrammaton** to him, which is named **Glory** <note>original: כבוד (*Kavod*)</note>.

So you, after the horrid and thorny desert, after the mountain and the rocks, after the wind and the earthquake, after the fire and the voice, in the very vestibule of the caverns and caves—having dismissed the multitude of worldly occupations—you will hear the glory of God speaking to you: "What are you doing here?" Go further, as is related in the Third Book of Kings, chapter 19 <note>In modern Bibles, this is 1 Kings 19.</note>. Therefore, we must not stand here, but must return with the Prophet Elijah on our way through the desert. This means traveling through these bristling revolutions of "barbaric" connections and tangled brambles into the way of Sacred and Canonical Scripture—our true way, which is the truth of the utterances of God—so that we may anoint the king in Syria, who from his anointing is called the **Messiah** <note>original: "Messiha," from the Hebrew *Mashiach*, meaning the Anointed One</note>.

For we shall walk through the conjugations of the twenty-two alphabets for so long, until we come to the highest and first Alphabet with vigilant care and untiring diligence. For it is necessary for us to run skillfully through each combination until the voice of God is revealed, and the open text of the most sacred Scriptures offers itself to us. That voice of God, indeed, from all the alphabets...

He emphasizes that the student must look past the "harsh" sounds of these names to find the divine "still small voice," using the biblical story of Elijah on Mount Horeb as an allegory for the Kabbalistic process.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Reuchlin’s exploration of the Name of Forty-Two Letters, moving from the mechanical structure of the name to its mystical power and its relationship to the Biblical account of Creation and the Christian Trinity.</meta>

### JOHANNES REUCHLIN

...from the first to the last—namely, the twenty-second—it pours down its virtue and strength abundantly, so that these combinations are thought to have a somewhat greater efficacy. They are not considered merely for their significance, but rather because names with primary significance excel, just as a ray of the Sun burns more fiercely than the Sun itself from which it flowed. This is found in the *Conclusions* of the Count of Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a key figure in the development of Christian Kabbalah.</note>, where he says: *Any word has power in Magic insofar as it is formed by the voice of God.* Therefore, the virtue, operation, vigor, efficacy, ornament, and perfection of the present Name of Forty-Two Letters depends on the voice of God, when we intend to hunt through all the connections and nets of the Alphabets until we find the seven names comprised of forty-two letters anywhere in Holy Scripture. 

For example: if it is sought from the first and twentieth Alphabet <note>Referring to the Atbash cipher, a substitution system where the first letter is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>, let these seven words, which could be the foundation of any verse of Divine Scripture, be set before me safely as they were mentioned above. Likewise from that and the nineteenth, and so on through all of them down to the first, which receives its name from its beginning, like the rest, and is seen to be called **אתבש** <note>original: "Atbash"</note>, that is, *Albath*. From its combination, let us borrow this example:

->אבג דהו זחט יכל לםנ סעפ צקך רשת קלר רצץ לרו קנו קבץ צזח<-

This is simultaneously a divine name of forty-two letters received from the permuted alphabet of the *Book of Formation* <note>original: "libri Ietzira," referring to the Sefer Yetzirah, an ancient Jewish mystical text on cosmology and the Hebrew alphabet.</note>. For our father Abraham placed only the permuted and arranged letters in that book of creation, since he did not doubt that the straight order of the common alphabet was known to everyone. Others are accustomed to combine this in a similar way, saying: **א ג ה ז** <note>The letters Aleph, Gimel, He, Zayin.</note> as Rabbi Hamai taught in his *Book of Speculation* <note>Sefer Ha-Iyun, a 13th-century mystical text.</note>, and he describes a name of forty-two letters produced from that same combination as follows: **אקבעבו טנפשות זטוגבש וכהתו בספוטש ושיהא**, which, like the others, symbolically signifies its own property of God the Blessed. 

For just as the four-letter name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH.</note> denotes God as He is above all being, and *Ehieh* <note>original: "Ehieh," meaning "I Am."</note> represents God as Being, and *Adonai* represents God as the Lord of all, and *Shaddai* as needing nothing; in the same way, the Name of Forty-Two Letters—whether received from transposed or straight combinations—designates God insofar as He is the creator of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. For this reason, those twenty-three divine names <note>Refers to various permutations of the 42-letter name.</note>, each of which is depicted with forty-two figures, are said to be derived from two verses of Holy Scripture according to the orders of the twenty-three alphabets: *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth: and the earth was without form and void.* <note>Genesis 1:1-2.</note> 

Beginning from the first letter *Beth* and terminating in the last letter *Beth*, which when read in Hebrew as they were dictated by the Holy Spirit, complete forty-two figures, provided we always place letter for letter under one and the same yoke of combination. Other Kabbalists are found speculating on more sublime things, who transcend creation and creatures and persist in the contemplation of the Deity alone. This they graciously grant—under a figure—to the most worthy men devoted to God, through the holy name of twelve characters and the name of forty-two letters, received and written **בספר אגרת הסודות**, that is, in the *Book of the Epistle of Secrets* <note>Sefer Iggeret Ha-Sodot.</note>. There, in response to the question of Antoninus the Roman <note>A legendary dialogue between the Emperor Antoninus and Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi (Rabbi the Holy).</note> concerning the most holy Unions, Rabbi the Holy responded that from the Tetragrammaton flows a name of twelve letters: **אב בן ורוח הקדש**, that is: *Father, Son, and Holy Spirit* <note>Reuchlin is here interpreting Jewish Kabbalah through a Christian lens, finding the Trinity in the Hebrew names.</note>. From this is derived a name of forty-two letters, which is pronounced thus: **אלהים בן אלהים רוח הקדש אלהים שלשה בשלשה באחד אחד בשלשה**, that is: *God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, three in three in one, and one in three.* 

Oh, how great is this height, how great the depth, which is apprehended by faith alone! 

**Philolaus:** "Indeed, Simon," he said, "how much thanks must be given to you, who shows these things to us so lucidly and clearly—if indeed anything in this art can be clear, and not rather the greatest part of these things remain shut up in envelopes and seem difficult to the unlucky." 

**Marranus:** "Hush, I beg you, Philolaus," he said. "Let him continue, don't you see? Evening is approaching, and he has almost finished his daily task. Now you, Simon, speak whatever remains." 

Then he [Simon] said: "I have completed the entire art and..."

<meta>This page continues the transition from discussing the Name of Forty-Two Letters to the Name of Twelve Letters, exploring how divine names were protected and substituted in Jewish liturgy and the mystical methods used to interpret them.</meta>

# ON THE KABBALISTIC ART, BOOK III.

...unless there are some things you think remain in detail concerning certain names of God, and of angels and powers, and consecrated seals, by whose force and power many have promised they would perform many things that might seem miraculous to the common people. And Marranus said: Perhaps forgetfulness has seized you, for you were also going to speak about the name of twelve letters, although you affirmed it was the subject of the second part, which has already passed. Then Simon said: There is little I need to explain about that, except that after the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name, YHWH.</note> began to be debased by the frequent and common use of wicked men—whereas before it was handled with such care and concern, with such reverence and so prudent a restraint, and was handed down only to suitable and chosen priests every seven years so that they might learn to bless the people in the sanctuary through it—then, to preserve the majesty of this name, the priests were forbidden to use it in prayer. Its pronunciation was permitted only to the High Priests once a year on the days of fasting and atonement. Therefore, in its place, they substituted for the others the name of twelve letters, which was somewhat more sacred than the name <term>Adonai</term> <note>Hebrew for "My Lord," the standard substitute for the Tetragrammaton.</note>, yet far less divine than the ineffable Tetragrammaton, for the priests to use in their blessings. It was customary for this name to be written as a <term>Notariacon</term> <note>A Kabbalistic method of forming acronyms from the first or last letters of words.</note> using these four letters **אגלא** <note>AGLA: Originally an acronym for *Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai* ("You are mighty forever, Lord"), though here Reuchlin equates it with the following phrase.</note> with marks on the head of each letter, and to be pronounced thus: **הקדוש ברוך הוא** <note>original: "Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu," meaning "The Holy One, blessed be He."</note>. Through this, they would later deliver the blessing commanded by God in the sixth chapter of Numbers over the people in place of the Tetragrammaton, like so:

> May the Holy One, blessed be He, bless you and keep you: May the Holy One, blessed be He, make His face shine upon you and be merciful to you: May the Holy One, blessed be He, lift up His face toward you and give you peace.

In this place, Salomon Trecensis <note>Solomon of Troyes, better known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud.</note>, the ordinary commentator on Holy Scripture, writes thus: **לכך הכהנים פורשים כפיהם לומר חס בה שמר. אחריני שנו הנה זה עומד אחר כתלינו משגיח מן החלונות מציץ מן החרכים בין האצבעות** <note>original: "Therefore the priests spread their palms to say [the blessing]. Others teach: 'Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the lattice' (Song of Songs 2:9) between the fingers."</note>: that is, "Therefore the priests spread out their hands, saying: The Holy One, blessed be He, stands behind us, just as it is written: 'Behold, He stands behind our wall, looking through the windows between the fingers of the priests.'" I hold this written so on the parchment of an ancient codex, although certain printed paper volumes lack these words. Our people most firmly believe, and in no way doubt, that the blessing expressed in this form is the cause of as much prosperity as it would have been if the name Tetragrammaton (which they now pronounce as *Adonai*) had remained in those prayers. For this change was made to honor the Tetragrammaton, lest, being so often repeated, it should finally fall into neglect—which may God, the Best and Greatest, avert above all things.

You have before you the entire Kabbalistic garden: that is, one divided into three flowerbeds, which are <term>Gematria</term> <note>The calculation of the numerical values of Hebrew letters.</note>, <term>Notariacon</term>, and <term>Thmura</term> <note>Temurah: the art of letter substitution and permutation.</note>, growing with infinite roots, herbs, and flowers, with all its adornment looking toward one gardener who waters, plants, and gives the increase—God, the Best and Greatest, incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnamable, whose name is also the incomprehensible, ineffable, and unnamable Tetragrammaton, from which flows and is derived everything that is sacred in sacred things. For whatever other symbols, marks, sacraments, or signs of divine things are found, they surely draw their origin from this very source. For example, **בוגו** <note>original: "BUGU"</note> signifies **יהוה** <note>original: "YHWH"</note>, the one God, through the first part of this art, **גימטריא** <note>Gematria</note>, by operating arithmetically, as was explained above. Yet that same name **יהוה** symbolically represents the entire Tetragrammaton itself through the second part of the Kabbalah, as Joseph Bar Abraham <note>Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305), a Spanish Kabbalist.</note>, a citizen of the district of Salem, writes in the second volume of the *Garden of the Nut* <note>original: "Hortus nucis" (Ginat Egoz), Gikatilla's famous work on the mystical meanings of Hebrew letters and names.</note> in these words: **י תמורתו כ ובו ה תמורתו ו ובו ו תמורתו ז** <note>original: "Yod its substitution is Caph, and so He its substitution is Vav, and so Vav its substitution is Zayin."</note>: that is, "Yod, its change is Caph; and likewise He, its change is Vav; and likewise Vav, its change is Zayin." By this we observe that God is one and most unified in His essence, than which nothing is more one, although many things are said of Him according to other relations, on account of which He is called **Elohim Kadoshim** <note>original: "Elohim Kadoshim," meaning "Holy Gods" (Joshua 24:19).</note>: that is, "Holy Gods"; and **Elohim Haijim** <note>original: "Elohim Hayyim," meaning "Living Gods" (Deuteronomy 5:26).</note>: that is, "Living Gods"; and in Malachi 1, He speaks of Himself thus: **ואם אדונים אני איה מוראי** <note>original: "Ve-im Adonim ani ayyeh morai," meaning "And if I am Lords, where is my fear?"</note>: that is, "And if I am Lords, where is my fear?" In which place God calls Himself "Lords" in the plural. According to His immanence, therefore, He is one; according to...

# JOHN REUCHLIN, BOOK III

...however, there are more departures [from the singular], as when He said: "Let us make man in our image and likeness." <note>Genesis 1:26. Reuchlin is addressing the classic theological question of why God uses the plural "Us" in the creation of humanity.</note> This was not because it was the custom of the holy language for those in supreme majesty to speak of themselves in the plural, as Rabbi Saadia writes in his book *Emunot* <note>original: אמונות (*Emunot*); "Beliefs," referring to Saadia Gaon's *Book of Beliefs and Opinions*.</note>, that is, "Of Beliefs." For this is a weak argument, since He [God] speaks in the singular elsewhere: "I will make him a helper like unto himself." <note>Genesis 2:18</note>. 

These Kabbalists do not unwillingly admit this plurality in divine matters in various ways; whence they assert that the three first Kabbalistic enumerations: *Keter, Chokhmah, Binah* <note>original: כתר חכמה בינה; Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding, the three highest Sephirot or emanations of God.</note> are one crown of the supreme king, as Rabbi Asse writes in the book *YHVH* <note>original: יהוה; Reuchlin refers to a work on the Tetragrammaton.</note> of Singulars or Collections. You see by this example that we freely use all the methods of Kabbalah back and forth and indiscriminately—namely, the universal transposition of letters and syllables, then numerical calculation <note>Known as Gematria.</note>, capital notation <note>Known as Notaricon.</note>, and literal notation with each of the species which I disclosed in my previous discourse. 

For thus we explain the name <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> so that it is *Va* and *Ya*, and *YHVH* <note>original: יהוה</note> arises: that is, the essence which is the first of all things, from which all true and good beings exist. Whence *Ehyeh Adonai* <note>original: hieh Adonai; "I am the Lord."</note> signifies arithmetically as much as *Elohim* <note>original: אלהים; God.</note>, whose number is 86. <note>In Gematria, the letters of Elohim (1+30+5+10+40) sum to 86.</note> Just as *Mah* <note>original: מה; "What," often used as a mystical name for God's aspect of concealment.</note> is a sign of *Elohim* himself, if it is extended thus: *A-L-H-I-M* <note>Reuchlin is referring to a "filling" or expansion of letters to reach the same numerical value.</note>: that is, 86. And *Yah* <note>original: יה</note> is the name Tetragrammaton, because it is 26. <note>The value of YHWH: 10+5+6+5 = 26.</note> Which, if it is extended, makes 112, and designates <term>Tetragrammaton Elohim</term> <note>26 (YHWH) + 86 (Elohim) = 112.</note>: that is, the Lord God, regarding whom he first writes: "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God [Tetragrammaton Elohim] made the earth and the heaven." <note>Genesis 2:4</note>. 

Moreover, the principle of every Tetragrammaton is *Yah* <note>original: Iah/יה</note>. And the middle of *Elohim* itself is *Yah*, and in *Ehyeh* is *Yah*. All of which is the perfection of *YHVH* itself: that is, the essence. If one says *Hu* <note>original: הו; "He"</note>: that is, "He" himself, and *Hu* is divine being. Whence it is a common daily saying that "being itself" is called something divine, necessary, and incorruptible. Often everything that is, when it is for the sake of this, must necessarily be, nor can it then happen not to be. Therefore, the power of that essence was led into operation through the Word of God when He said *Yehi* <note>original: יהי; "Let there be"</note>: that is, "Let there be." By which word, the universal <term>Ideas</term> <note>Refers to the Platonic/Kabbalistic archetypes of all things.</note> and most absolute intellectual powers were created in one sum, because He himself commanded thus: "Let there be light," and soon there was light.

This university [of ideas] was followed by the nature of the angels assigned to ministry, when He said, *Vayehi khen* <note>original: ויהי כן</note>: that is, "And it was so," which designates the prince and great priest who is named Michael, a shining proof of the angelic condition, which is constituted from unity and the number one hundred. <note>Michael’s name is often associated with the number 101 in Kabbalistic gematria, signifying his status as the chief of the heavenly host.</note> Whence they think that on the first day, the Ideas were poured out and produced outside the first cause as the most absolute forms as to being and acting. But on the second day, the angels were created from here. For on the first day He did not say "And it was so," but on the second day, when the firmament of heaven was made. According to Rabbi Eliezer, they were created from the light of His garment. For God was clothed in ten garments when He created the world, as the Kabbalists say, and from the light of His last garment He snatched and created the heavens—not indeed the sensible ones, but those invisible and intellectual ones, spiritual entities <note>original: הוות ורוחניות (*havot ve-ruchaniyot*)</note>, of which the Psalmist says: "The heavens declare the glory of God" <note>Psalm 19:1</note>, where it is not written just *Shamaim* <note>original: שמים; "Heavens."</note>: that is, the heavens which are the spheres, which Rabbi Ama notably remarked in the Book of Hidden Things [commenting on] Psalm 18 <note>Psalm 19 in modern numbering.</note>. 

[Instead it is] *Ha-Shamaim* <note>original: השמים</note>, to which is added the article *ha*, as is read in the summary argument of Genesis: "In the beginning God created *Ha-Shamaim*": that is, those distinguished heavens, those famous ones, those admirable ones, never seen nor visible to mortal eyes. For other heavens which are not written with the article *ha* are indeed the firmament, yet they are called by the name "heavens," wherefore it is written, "and God called the firmament heavens." And it is called the firmament of that invisible heaven in which is that which is called "The Heaven of Heavens," whence it follows: "Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven." Surely that extension in the manner of a skin, as if inscribed with letters by the lights and stars, is called *Rakia* <note>original: רקיע; expanse or firmament.</note> because of its local expansion, which we call "firmament" due to its firmness. For the invisible heaven did not need lights, since it is spiritually illustrious through itself and mentally illuminated by the first cause. Therefore they are named "separate intelligences," of which the author of [the Book of] Causes <note>The *Liber de Causis*, a medieval Neoplatonic text.</note> says: "Every intelligence is full of forms," which while it understands, is said to hear and see...

### ON THE KABBALISTIC ART, BOOK III

Therefore Moses says: "Hear, O heavens, the things I speak." <note>Deuteronomy 32:1</note> And David: "The heavens declare the glory of God." <note>Psalm 19:1</note> And God says in Hosea: "I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth." <note>Hosea 2:21</note> From this the prophetic light descends, which is called <term>the illuminating mirror</term> <note>original: אספקלריא המאירה (*aspaklaria ha-me'irah*); a technical term in Kabbalah for the highest form of prophecy, uniquely attributed to Moses.</note>, which belonged to Moses. For the vision of other prophets was <term>the non-illuminating mirror</term> <note>original: אספקלריא שאינה מאירה (*aspaklaria she-einah me'irah*); referring to a lower, more obscure form of divine revelation.</note>, and that is called "earth," of which some mention was made in our first discourse. Indeed, I seem to believe rightly that for this reason our wise men have said: "The appearance of Moses was like the appearance of the Sun, and the appearance of Joshua like the appearance of the Moon." <note>A traditional comparison found in the Talmud (Bava Batra 75a), suggesting Joshua's light was a reflection of Moses' brilliance.</note> In the creation of sensible things, therefore, God uses this symbol of <term>spiritual things</term> <note>original: רוחני (*ruchani*); meaning spiritual or incorporeal beings.</note>, so that the ministry of angels—created together with natural things—might be designated under the common name "Michael," as a generic name for the angelic species. 

This is symbolically signified through that phrase, <term>and His spirit within him</term> <note>original: ורוחו בו (*ve-rucho bo*). Reuchlin is likely using Gematria (numerical equivalence) here to link this phrase to the name Michael.</note>, recited in the following five days of work according to the first part of the Kabbalistic art by an equality of number. Through this, it is established that all angels are of the same species. Furthermore, individual bodies, whether celestial or earthly, have their own rectors of virtues and prefects of operations—both those that are rational, such as the stars of the heavens and men, and those that are irrational, such as beasts and the elements. This is certainly proved by the philosophers, especially the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle's school of philosophy.</note>, because every spherical heaven, besides its own essential form, has an "assistant intelligence" as the motor of its orb. This is called an "angel" because, being sent to this office, it completes the commands of the Creator with understanding and will, acting as a medium of power between God and nature. From this power, operations occur in things which their nature either would not do, or would not do in such a way—operations which others say come from a "hidden property" and others because "it is such." 

For although the motion of the heavens and stars is naturally circular, to be moved from East to West or vice-versa is not a matter of nature, but of <term>will</term>. Now, an angel has free will, whereas nature is constrained to a certain instinct alone, whence it always acts in the same way. But angels do not move the orbs always in the same way. Thus it happens that changes in these lower things do not always occur in the same way. For the angelic condition exercises the greatest force and power over corporeal things. For this reason, the <term>agent intellect</term> <note>A concept in medieval philosophy—the "active" part of the mind that allows for human knowledge—which many thinkers identified with a specific angelic being.</note> from which forms flow is named an "angel," as Rabbi Moses Maimonides testifies, and he calls him the <term>Prince of the World</term> <note>original: שר של עולם (*Sar shel Olam*).</note>, as our wise men have said. He is called <term>Metatron</term> <note>A high-ranking angel in Jewish mysticism, often described as the celestial scribe or the mediator between God and the world.</note>, by whom indeed all singular human, animal, and natural virtues are governed, which are likewise called "angels." Their multitude is infinite to us, but to the Creator, it is certain, delimited, and finite. 

<term>Genesis Rabbah</term> <note>original: Bresith Raba; an ancient collection of rabbinic interpretations on the Book of Genesis.</note> mentions this, where it is read that the Creator daily creates a company of angels, whom others call "forms," because they are formal substances with which the entire sphere of things that can be born or perish is filled without number. Your <term>Hesiod</term> <note>An ancient Greek poet.</note> accepted this no differently; for in his *Works and Days* he says: "For thrice ten thousand are the immortals of Zeus upon the much-nourishing earth, guardians of mortal men, who indeed observe both justice and wretched deeds, clothed in mist, going everywhere upon the earth." <note>original: Reuchlin provides the Greek: τρὶς γὰρ μύριοί εἰσὶν ἐπὶ χθονὶ πολυβοτείρῃ ἀθάνατοι Ζηνὸς... which he then translates into Latin.</note> 

In the likeness of these, they name two powers of the will in man as two angels: <term>the author of good and the author of evil</term> <note>original: יצר טוב ויצר רע (*yezer tov ve-yezer ra*); commonly known as the good and evil inclinations.</note>, as is read in the <term>Midrash Tanchuma</term> <note>A collection of homiletic teachings on the Torah.</note>, which Rabbi Assé cites in his collection. The Latins call such Hesiodic guardians assisting the body "spirits." Whichever of them is destined for the care of lower affairs is called <term>Mamona</term> or <term>Mammon</term>, which the Greeks call <term>daemon</term>, certainly not in a bad sense. 

To be sure, a "daemon" is one thing, and a "demoniac" <note>original: dæmonium.</note> is another, which we think to be a diminishing of divinity; for that reason, as a diminutive, it is excluded from divine things. However, I plainly confess that for Homer and the most ancient writers there was another use for that word, many of whom preached laudable and venerable things about the "daemon" of <term>Socrates</term> <note>The "daimonion," a divine inner voice that Socrates claimed warned him against making mistakes.</note>, which Apuleius interpreted as "The God of Socrates." That the Latins called them "spirits" in the likeness of winds took its origin from us, who call the same beings <term>spirits</term> <note>original: רוחות (*ruchot*); meaning both "winds" and "spirits" in Hebrew.</note>. # JOHANNES REUCHLIN

...to which **Rabbi Tadacus Levi**, in his book *On the Ten Enumerations*, after explaining the four winds—the Northern, the Southern, the Eastern, and the Western—at last writes: <note>original: ארבע רוחות ברא ארבע מלאכים וממונין עליהון ביומה ובלילה</note> "He created four winds and four angels, and they are appointed over them by day and by night." Then follows in the same passage: that **Michael**, who belongs to the side of clemency and mercies, is established as the <term>Memuna</term> <note>original: *mona*, likely a shortened form of the Hebrew *memuna* (ממונה), meaning an overseer or official.</note>, that is, the prefect over the eastern wind until midday and until night. And **Raphael**, who is likewise from the side of clemency, rules the western wind. Then **Gabriel**, in the power of judgment and severity, is the prefect over the northern wind for the half of the night and "two measures of the world." **Norial** <note>Also known as Uriel in other traditions; here associated with the South.</note> presides over the south. Thus far **Tadacus Levi**.

Furthermore, those angels have many more beneath them in their respective ranks, which the book <term>Siddurin</term> <note>original: סידורין (*Siddurin*); referring to a book of "arrangements" or mystical orders, often related to liturgy or secret teachings.</note>—that is, the book of secrets—contains; and in the **Porta Lucis** <note>The *Gates of Light* (*Sha'are Orah*) by Joseph Gikatilla, a fundamental text of 13th-century Spanish Kabbalah.</note> it is read thus:

> Know that there is no empty place there, but everything is full of multitudes: some of them are pure, possessing grace and mercy, and there are below many foul, harmful, and evil creatures, and they all stand and fly in the air. And between the earth and the firmament there is no empty place, but all is filled with multitudes: some for peace, some for war, some for good, and some for evil, some for life, and some for death. And all this is in the lower habitation in which we dwell.

Thus says **Joseph of Castile** <note>Joseph Gikatilla, often referred to by his place of residence in Spain.</note>. But far be it from our holy purpose that we should proceed to dispute much concerning those squalid and most foul demons, those enemies of the human race, who are called the "exterior powers"; or those who are thought to inhabit the upper region of fire; or those who wander in the air near us; or those terrestrial ones who terrify the land; or those who inhabit lakes and rivers and often trouble the sea itself; or those who sometimes invade men under the earth, those who dig wells and mines, or who provoke the gaping of the earth, agitate flame-vomiting winds, and shake foundations; and finally, those who flee all light and splendor, inscrutable and utterly shadowy, who harass not only the human race but even brute animals, thrusting their speech into them without sound.

Against the machinations of these beings, there are some among our people who believe they have experienced much, and they do not doubt that sweet things attract good spirits, while we repel malignant ones by opposite passions. Supported by sacred and divine names and characters duly applied, they are pleased to take up the task of exposing a man to the dangers of the journey by using a very thin parchment—which is called "virgin," as if it were sincere, clean, and immaculate—to foreshadow the purity of the actor. Then they inscribe these characters: **צמרכה** <note>original: *Tzamarka*; a protective name formed by taking the first letters of the first five verses of Genesis: *Bereshit, Bara, Elohim, Et, Ha-shamayim*.</note>, but on the outside, on the rougher part, these signs also: **בוווו** <note>A symbolic ligature often used in amulets to represent divine protection.</note>. By this binding, they instruct those who hope most firmly in God, the creator of all diversity, to fear no machinations of wicked men.

They reveal the mystery thus: these are the symbols of the first five verses of Genesis, both the beginnings and the ends, according to the second part of the Kabbalistic art. Long ago, concerning <term>physical ligatures</term> <note>A "ligature" in this context is a charm or amulet tied to the body.</note>, **Costa Ben Luca** <note>Qusta ibn Luqa (820–912), a Syrian Christian physician and translator known for his works on physical and spiritual effects on the body.</note> explained things that were not purely physical, yet were approved as proven by experience; he says: "If you hang the little finger of an aborted fetus on a woman, she will not conceive as long as it hangs from her neck." But now, if the words with which the Almighty Creator made Heaven and Earth are bound [to someone], will anyone think, they ask, that they achieve nothing?

Truly, the men of my school believe much indeed, following the great Master **Akiba**, who wrote in the <term>Sefer Yetzirah</term> <note>The *Book of Formation*, one of the oldest and most influential texts of Jewish mysticism.</note>: that one wishing to seek and obtain his desires should turn himself to the clemency and mercies of God by using these characters: **בסתם בפסתם בספסים דיו נסים** <note>original: *Bastam, Bafastam, Baspasim, Diyonisim*; these are mystical permutations of divine names believed to hold great power.</note>, which are found to be miracles worthy of Holy Scripture, of which sort many others are found, with which almost all Kabbalistic books are filled. Others also study to fashion illustrious seals from the divine letters, which may prevail against men's ill health and other troubles, having been proven by long use. Such is that one, for example, which **Rabbi Hama** describes in the book...
