### ON THE TEACHINGS OF THE KABBALISTS.

This is to be understood not only of the physical spheres, but of those supramundane wheels to which souls return, just as they first proceeded from them—as is more clearly contained in the **Theology of the Hebrews** <note>Meaning the Kabbalah.</note>. Regarding this return of souls to the places proportioned to them and from which they departed, the **Academics** <note>The followers of Plato's Academy.</note> along with their **Plato** say that they return to their own planets—perhaps speaking more deeply than many realize. Our own **Theologians**, however, say that they return to those choirs of angels in conformity with which they lived. I say that they return to those supramundane dwellings to which the way and the door is He who said: *I am the way, I am the door; if anyone enters through me, he will be saved* <note>original: "Ego sum uia, ego sum ostium: per me si quis introierit, saluabit̃." References John 14:6 and John 10:9.</note>. For passage is not given through **Christ** to the planets, nor to the angels, but to **God** and the **Eternal Father**; in whose house and in whose vastness of divinity those many and eternal mansions exist.

And from this, **Astronomers** (if they hold any truth) determine by forecasting that a person is "Saturnine," "Martial," "Jovial," "Venerean," "Mercurial," "Solar," or "Lunar." Indeed, there are various effects, inclinations, and behaviors in men, arising not only from matter being variously disposed (as some believe), but from a varied influence and a diverse form—not a diversity of species, but one that is peculiar and personal. Although their degrees are varied and distributed by Him who, remaining the same, "divides to each as He wills" (as the **Apostle** says), the secondary celestial causes nevertheless cooperate, disposing our bodies so that they may harmonize with our souls; because, according to **Aristotle**, "form is given according to the disposition of the matter." 

For if our body is dominated by some lower planet, such as the **Sun**, God pours into it a soul that passes through the higher Sun, **Tiphereth** <term>Tiphereth</term> <note>The sixth Sephirah on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, associated with Beauty, the Heart, and the spiritual Sun.</note>, and imbibes its influence, clothing itself with that property of the solar Tiphereth. How man draws from these planets is taught by **Plato**, **Plotinus**, and the other Academics. They say the soul, in its descent, receives from **Saturn** reasoning, intelligence, and speculative power; from **Jupiter** the powers of acting and practice; from **Mars** irascibility and the heat of spiritedness; from the **Sun** the imagination of knowing and the nature of forming opinions; from **Venus** concupiscence and the movement of desire; from **Mercury** the vigor of interpreting, pronouncing, and penetrating; from the **Moon** the power by which it can plant, generate, and grow. 

And so that it may receive from the universe and produce a certain whole, it draws these things even from the supreme **septenary** <note>The group of seven planets or spheres.</note> (as **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>Referred to here as "Mercurius" in the Latin text.</note> suggests), or rather from the entire **archetype**; and there it assumes its **guardian spirit**, which never leaves it until it reaches its end. Concerning these, Christ said: *Their angels always behold the face of my Father* (etc.). Therefore, the conclusion says that the **Great North** <note>original: "Magnus aquilo."</note>—that is, the supramundane **Ghebura** <term>Ghebura</term> <note>The fifth Sephirah, meaning "Strength" or "Severity," traditionally associated with the North.</note>—is the "fountain of souls" in an executive sense, as I said, though not of all souls. It does not mean that some souls are missing whose origin was not the "North" of Ghebura but other **Sephiroth**; rather, it means that all souls receive their origin from Ghebura, and descending from there, they pass through the remaining Sephiroth, clothing themselves in their properties. The same may be said of the remaining lower and upper planets which correspond to each other. For just as if all bodies were dominated by the Sun, they would be of the same temperament, so too if all souls passed through the same Sephirah, they would enjoy the same virtue, talent, memory, and character. The opposite of this is clearly evident, for there are various kinds of men.

->KABBALISTIC DOGMA: When Solomon says in his prayer in the Book of Kings: "Hear, O heaven," by "heaven" we must understand the green line which encircles the universe.<- <note>This "green line" (*Kav HaYarok*) in Kabbalah refers to a mystical boundary or the source of physical matter/darkness.</note>

**FRIAR ARCHANGELUS:** Not only should those things said about the harmony of man with the heavens and the health to be received from them be believed, but it must also be thought that he draws some utility from them by which he becomes better. For first, let him draw **light**, which puts to flight the darkness and those who work evil, as the **Psalm** says: *The sun has risen, and they* (the evil spirits) *have gathered* and will be placed in their dens—that is, in wicked men—as long as the night approaches. For this light of the Sun possesses a certain likeness of that Light which said: *I am the light of the World; while you have the light, walk in the light, lest the darkness overtake you.* And just as the princes of darkness become stronger in the darkness itself, so also the angels of light, who favor us, receive an increase of strength from the light...

...they receive from light, not only Divine light, but solar and celestial light; through all things the Divine and supreme light shines, infusing a certain power of heaven into lower things. For from the **Father of lights** <note>A biblical reference to God from James 1:17.</note>, from whom every gift [is given], comes both being, and motion, and generation, and every working power, as much in the heavens as in the elements, plants, animals, and men. But all those things receive [these gifts] through means and instruments, certain nourishments which are called natural. Men, however, beyond these, receive that from which they compose such multifaceted characters, as astronomers assert. 

This happens by means of the **green line** <note>original: "lineæ uiridis." In Kabbalah, the *Kav ha-Yarok* is the "Green Line" that surrounds the world and from which darkness and the created order emerge.</note> or the "tent" which encompasses all things, whose power first communicates with the soul; from there, penetrating through the heavens, it reaches not only the stars, but even the innermost parts of the spirit. We also receive a very great bond from the heavens, which disposes us to harmonize our behaviors. But (as has been said) this flow is dependent on the **green line**, which just as it encircled the whole **Archetypal World** <note>The highest realm of creation in Kabbalistic thought, containing the divine blueprints.</note>—namely, the ten **Sephiroth** <note>The ten creative powers or attributes through which God interacts with the universe.</note>—so it circles and encompasses this whole lower, greater world, the heaven. 

Many things which come together into one, whether by art or nature, are glued together by a divine mystery. Stones are glued together by lime, woods by nails, or by glue made of cheese or fish; limbs are bound together by nerves and skin. And because the force of nature is stronger than art, it binds more firmly. But since the Divine power is the strongest of all, it not only binds but also unites. And this is the power of that holy and great Name itself, concerning which it is written: *O Lord our Lord, how admirable is your name in all the earth* <note>original: "Domine Dominus noster, quàm admirabile est nomen tuum in uniuersa terra." Psalm 8:1.</note>; namely in both the upper and lower earth, in both binding and connecting all parts and their members together. 

In the likeness of this name, God commanded that a Temple be built, which bears the image of that heavenly city. As was later added in that Volume called **Paralipomenon** <note>The Book of Chronicles.</note>: *I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name may be in it; which I chose, so that it might be built to my name.* But not only the stone temple and the whole greater structure of the World, but even the rational and human fabric is bound by that name. 

For when the human family was divided into Abel and Cain (for in Abel a Divine family is built, and in Cain a Diabolical family), this one, who was according to the flesh and was evil, persecuting him who was according to the spirit, killed Abel. But humanity was restored again in **Seth**, and began to multiply in **Enos**, the son of Seth. So that they might be joined by a proper bond, the Scripture says: *Then the name of the Lord began to be invoked* <note>original: "Tunc cœptũ est inuocari nomen Domini." Genesis 4:26.</note>; although faulty texts have: *He began to invoke the name of the Lord.* For it was invoked and placed between them like a bond, a glue, and a union. 

Just as in **Deuteronomy**, after giving the precept concerning the bond of charity which those who belong to God must have—Priests, Levites, elders, handmaids, strangers, and orphans—through offering, feasting, living together, and the like, it then added: *That my name may dwell there*; namely, connecting all things. **Jeremiah**, speaking for the chosen family, says: *But you are in us, O Lord, and your name is invoked upon us.* And lest this be thought omitted in our homeland, John says that those who were sealed had his name—that is, the **Lamb**, which is **Jesus** <note>original: ישו (Yeshu)</note>—and the name of his Father—that is, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: יהוה (The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH).</note>—written on their foreheads. 

This Name is therefore the universe; that is, connecting all things: the highest with the highest, the lower with the lower, the highest with the lower, and the lower with the highest. These upper and lower parts are divided into twelve parts just like the **Zodiac**, according to the revolutions <note>The twelve permutations or "revolutions" of the four letters of the name YHWH.</note> of the Tetragrammaton name. One angel is said to preside over each of these twelve revolutions. And they correspond by influence not only to the twelve gates of the city of **Jerusalem**, but also to the twelve signs of the starry heaven. Of these, **Aries** is the chief gate of ascent, and **Cancer** of descent; the others truly agree with one of those two. And just as only one name is given under heaven by which we can be saved (which is the same as the Tetragrammaton), so every good influence is granted to us from those twelve revolutions. The Patriarchs, the twelve Apostles, the twelve celestial gates, and the seven planets of heaven favor us; however, this occurs through the ministry of the seven angels presiding over them, for they move all things and govern all things. This also happens through the influx of the twelve **Signs** <note>The constellations of the Zodiac.</note> and the twelve revolutions of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH. In Kabbalah, this name can be permuted into twelve different combinations or "revolutions."</note>, because the seven lower planets receive their influence from the seven archetypal planets, which are the seven lower **Sephiroth** <note>The ten creative emanations of God in Kabbalistic thought.</note>. And although there appears to be a discrepancy in the numbers of the planets and the signs, there is nonetheless a very great harmony in the root of both, which is the **quaternary** <note>The number four.</note> and the **ternary** <note>The number three.</note>; if these are joined, they constitute the **septenary** <note>The number seven.</note>. If, however, one is squared by the other—saying three times four, or four times three—they yield twelve. Furthermore, the planets agree with the signs in their qualitative and elementary virtues and their better powers; hence, each of the planets has its domicile in some sign and its exaltation in another, receiving from each of them some power and nourishment. Nor do the seven presiding intelligences of the planets have any less harmony with those twelve minds that preside over the twelve signs. John mentions each of these in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. See my declaration there. Virtue exists primarily in God’s great name, the Tetragrammaton יהוה <note>original: "tetrag. יהוה"</note>, and is afterwards diffused into those twelve and seven angels, through whom it is extended into the twelve signs and seven planets, and consequently into all the ministers and instruments of God himself. So it is also in this World, or the mystical spiritual body. For the virtue of the great name יהוה [YHVH] existing in **Jesus** ש <note>original: "Ieſu ש" — Christian Kabbalists added the letter Shin (ש) to the Tetragrammaton to form the name of Jesus (YHShVH), known as the Pentagrammaton.</note> and filling him with every kind of perfection, is afterwards diffused into those twelve Apostles, as if into the twelve signs and the principal foundations of the celestial and spiritual edifice after Christ. For (as the Apostle says) we are built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, from whom also the seventy-two disciples, and the Bishops, and all Prelates—who stand in the place of the ancient Fathers and those who were laid as the first foundations of this sacred building—and consequently all who are ruled by them, [receive influence]. Thus the heavens receive from the Angels that from which they may flow and favor what is good; but those [Angels] receive from the great name, the Tetragrammaton. Its virtue is first in God, and afterwards diffused into those twelve and seven angels, through whom it is extended into the twelve signs and seven planets, and consequently into all the ministers and instruments of God himself, as I have said. Solomon, seeing this when the temple was built and his prayer was made, desired the favor of the twelve revolutions of the great name so that they might favor the twelve tribes of Israel; and so that he might invoke all these revolutions at once, he approached their foundation, saying: "O Heaven of the Tetragrammaton, whose twelve revolutions encompass both the **Archetypal World** <note>The divine realm of pure ideas.</note> and this lower world divided into twelve parts: hear my prayer." For although **Plato** says that heaven is the cause of all good things, he himself understands this as the archetypal heavens—that is, the **Ideas**, which are the means and instruments through which the Supreme Craftsman, observing the order of things, operates. Yet the principal cause is God himself, from whom (as Saint James says) every best gift and every perfect gift emanates; to which the Apostle agrees, saying: "From him, and through him, and in him are all things" <note>Romans 11:36.</note>. That is, all virtues and powers, because he is the **green line** <note>original: "linea uiridis." The Kav ha-Yarok, a Kabbalistic concept representing the boundary and source of all creation.</note>—that is, full of the influx of every color, just as the color green does not refuse the mixture of any color. For thus the Tetragrammaton is the source of all influxes; moving all things, it draws them to itself, just as a center draws all the lines of a circumference and leads them into itself. For it is the center, and the circle, and the sphere, embracing and filling all things, and leading all lines into itself; therefore it is placed in **Tiphereth** <note>The sixth Sephirah, representing Beauty, Balance, and the Heart.</note> in the middle of the Sephiroth, like a center, from which center the twelve lines—namely, of the twelve revolutions—depend, as does the entire spherical order, as I have declared in the **Gate of Light** <note>original: "Porta lucis." Likely referring to Joseph Gikatilla's *Sha'are Orah*, a foundational Kabbalistic text.</note>.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how the celestial bodies and the Sephiroth influence the creation and nature of the human soul. It transitions from the structural harmony of the heavens discussed on page 757 to the specific "presuppositions" regarding how the Sephiroth (divine emanations) and the planets shape human life and wisdom.</meta>

# THE COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS

Through whose favor all things are created and nourished; they are furthermore called "days" and are named the "days of *Bereshit*" <note>Hebrew: "In the beginning," referring to the six days of creation in Genesis.</note>. The second presupposition is that when we speak of the Sephiroth of the "Building" <note>A Kabbalistic term for the seven lower Sephiroth that govern the manifest world.</note>, it must be understood as the Sephiroth below *Binah* <note>The Sephirah of "Understanding."</note>, because *Nezach* <note>Victory</note> and *Hod* <note>Splendor</note> are counted as one single unit, and thus seven remain. In [six] God created the world, but on the seventh day—namely *Binah*—He rested.

The third presupposition: when the Sephiroth are named "absolutely" <note>Meaning, without further qualification.</note>, it is to be understood as referring to all ten. The fourth presupposition: that *Ghebura* <note>The Sephirah of "Strength" or "Judgment."</note> is the "great North." From [the Sephiroth] all souls proceed; although these Doctors <note>The Kabbalists.</note> seem to hold that they proceed from *Binah*. It is true that souls depend primarily on the whole Trinity, but they hang especially upon the Holy Spirit—namely, regarding their essential being—and then they [descend] through *Ghebura* first, and successively into the other Sephiroth. Therefore Moses said: "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life." For "to breathe" is the property of the Holy Spirit. Origen <note>An early Christian theologian (c. 184–253 AD).</note> says that the Holy Spirit gives life to all things.

The soul, therefore, comes immediately from the Holy Spirit. And since after its coming-into-being it first [enters] into the first chamber, they enter into *Ghebura*. For this reason, souls are said to [originate] from *Ghebura* with respect to the other lower Sephiroth of the Building. And so they pass from one Sephirah into another until they enter a Sephirah that shares a property with the lower planet designated for the body of that soul, which that soul is meant to animate.

And just as the lower planet—under whose [sign] a man is born—flows into and imparts its influence to the body thus conceived, so the higher planet <note>The archetypal Sephirah corresponding to the physical planet.</note> corresponding to the lower planet shapes that soul with its own influx, so that the soul and body participate in the same qualities. For "the form is according to the disposition of the matter" <note>A philosophical rule: the soul (form) adapts itself to the physical nature (matter) of the body it inhabits.</note>. If the body is "Solar," the soul will drink in the influx of *Tipheret* <note>The Sephirah of "Beauty," associated with the Sun.</note>, the archetypal Sun. All things which have no free motion or climb no other path by which they might be carried [back] to the beginning from which they departed, [possess] only the instinct they call "natural." This is implanted by nature, as the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> say, or (to use their words) because it happens in [most] cases and frequently. For thus they defined natural things.

But as the truth of the matter [stands], these things were given by the Supreme Craftsman <note>God.</note>. Those who are partakers of the gift of God’s reason and liberty climb the path of their own will or love, according to that [saying] of Augustine: "My love is my weight" <note>Original Latin: *Amor meus, pondus meum*; Augustine meant that love acts like gravity for the soul, pulling it toward its destination.</note> or "my path; there I am carried, wherever I am carried." Nature often contributes great force to this and draws [one], so that they run more easily by their own will. For the progress of wisdom and learning, men who are "well-hearted" in body and allotted a good soul come forward, disposed toward the good, with Phoebus <note>The Sun/Apollo.</note>, Venus, and Mercury favoring them—if we wish to follow the Platonists. And this is either by disposing the body, or because the Intelligences presiding over those stars favor them with their influx, or (as the Pythagoreans say) because in its descent, the soul puts on the nature of those Intelligences, just as light seems darkened by the color of the glass through which it passes—red, sky-blue, green, or yellow.

Others [reach] dominion more easily if their birth and virtue grant it, and if the Sun and [Jupiter] and such things favor them—if what the astronomers hand down is true. They run through various virtues by a natural course according to the varying disposition of the body and the favor of the heavens. But they attain nothing good unless the supernal power, the source of all good, favors them. For wisdom is not acquired by one’s own strength, as the Sage <note>Solomon, the traditional author of Ecclesiastes.</note> testifies, saying: "I applied my heart to know wisdom, and I understood that man can find no reason for the works of God, of those things which are done under the sun." This is because wisdom is given by God, according to the sentiment of James: "If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all abundantly" <note>Referring to the Epistle of James 1:5.</note>. And even if souls are distinguished by the Craftsman in different [grades], there is nevertheless one common origin and one birth for all, as we saw above. There is, therefore, one entrance into life for all, and a similar exit—namely, without any knowledge or virtue, since the soul from the beginning is like a **blank slate** <term>tabula rasa: literally a "scraped tablet," a philosophical concept describing the mind as a clean slate at birth, before any sensory input or experience.</term>, in which nothing is depicted. Which seems to be what that Sage infers because of this...

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS

(ignorant I came forth from my mother’s womb) I desired, and understanding was given to me; I called out, and the spirit of <term>wisdom</term> <note>original: "sapientiæ"</note> came. But Plato, whom many from his Academy follow, when he had seen many learning without difficulty—or rather many times knowing things they had not learned—supposed that the species and forms of things (and consequently doctrines) were created together with the soul, but were hindered by the senses and bodily bonds, so much so that through study, time, and exercise, the species that were within are shaken out. Hence some of the Ancients said that the soul, entering the body, drinks from the Lethæan whirlpool <note>The River Lethe in Greek mythology, whose waters caused forgetfulness.</note>: that is, from forgetfulness. Nor was this opinion first invented and published by Plato, but received from the more secret Theologians <note>A reference to the "Prisca Theologia" or "Ancient Theology," a lineage of secret wisdom that thinkers like Pico della Mirandola believed connected Moses, Hermes Trismegistus, and Plato.</note>, who believe that all souls were produced by their progenitor, perfected in all their forms, just as the soul of the first-formed [Adam] had been produced, which he himself obscured by transgression; from the contagion of whose sin, our souls also, entering the body, are obscured and entirely put to sleep. And just as it was said to the first parent himself regarding physical food, and perhaps regarding both:
> In the sweat of your face, or of your nostrils (that is, of your spirit), you shall eat your bread: <note>Genesis 3:19. The author notes that "nostrils" refers to the "breath of life" or spirit.</note>
so that voice and harsh sentence seems to me to thunder upon us all:
> In your sweat and labor you shall eat your bread, both of your body and of your soul,
which is doctrine and the knowledge of things. For we must act and sweat, if we wish either to learn anew (as the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>The followers of Aristotle, who believed the mind is a blank slate (tabula rasa) and learns only through experience, unlike the Platonists.</note> say) or to draw out that doctrine which the most generous Distributor poured clearly into our souls from the beginning. But it was soon clouded over by the fault of our first parents with a veil, which God in His kindness has deigned to remove from the eyes of some. For David did not learn letters: and from a shepherd, he was made a Prophet and the foremost Teacher of divine things. With which he so filled his hymns that all poets, however exquisite, yield to him by a long interval. Thus Isaiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, and the other Prophets, and also the Apostles, to whom He said:
> I will give you a mouth and wisdom.
Solomon also, in a dream of one night, God filled with such great wisdom for managing affairs and lower things: and not one among all the ancient Kings stood equal to him (even by a long interval). And this by means of the anointing of the Holy Spirit, or of the sacred Name, of which it is said in the Canticles:
> Your name is oil poured out.
When Christ had handed over the anointing and power of this Name to those whom He knew to be suitable and chosen by the Father, He said:
> Father, I have manifested Your name to the men whom You gave to me.
Some, however, were prepared with this anointing in the mother's womb, as we read of John [the Baptist] and Jeremiah. Whether this was through the infusion of new <term>wisdom</term> (which I believe), or through the removal of the veil so the intellect might be set free and, with revealed face, be able to transcend from clarity to clarity, God knows. For I yield to the truth and to the Holy Scriptures confirmed in that truth, from which we have that God made all things "very good": namely, in their own complete perfection. For just as He filled the growing trees with fruits, the use of which He granted to the first-formed: so He is believed by many to have made rational trees <note>A metaphor for human souls.</note>, whose fruits are gathered and whose cultivation is commanded with the labor and sweat of the Spirit and the exercise of all powers. And this has its beginning when souls enter the night of the body. For just as a shadow blocks the light of the Sun, so the body blocks the powers of the soul.

To the conclusion: (Souls from the third light)—that is, from <term>Binah</term> <note>The Sephirah of Understanding.</note>—the <term>Sephiroth</term> are called by various names, just as Christ is called Jesus, Son of God, Messiah, Word, Wisdom, Redeemer, etc. So the <term>Sephiroth</term> are named in different ways: they are called <term>Sephiroth</term>, numerations, dimensions, days of the building, light, as above. Souls therefore proceed first from <term>Chokmah</term> <note>The Sephirah of Wisdom.</note> as far as their ideal being is concerned, secondly from <term>Binah</term> through creation, then (on the fourth day), that is, to <term>Gevurah</term> <note>The Sephirah of Strength or Judgment.</note>, namely [through the process] of creation by the Holy Spirit (going out from there); descending from <term>Gevurah</term>, they enter into other <term>Sephiroth</term>, until they find the <term>Sephirah</term> proportionate and matching with the planet ruling the body of that soul, and they enter the night of the body.

<sig>T</sig>

By whose favor all things are created and nourished; they are, moreover, called gods and are named the days of <term>Genesis</term> <note>original: "bresit" (Bereshit), the Hebrew word for "In the beginning," often used to refer to the act of creation.</note>. The second presupposition is that when speaking of the <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself.</note> of the Structure, it must be understood as the Sephiroth below <term>Binah</term> <note>The third Sephirah, meaning "Understanding." It is often considered the "Supernal Mother" from which the lower Sephiroth emerge.</note>, because <term>Netzach</term> <note>The seventh Sephirah, meaning "Endurance" or "Victory."</note> and <term>Hod</term> <note>The eighth Sephirah, meaning "Splendor" or "Majesty."</note> are counted as one, and thus seven remain. God created the world, but on the seventh day—that is, in Binah—He rested. The third position: when the Sephiroth are named absolutely, it must be understood as the ten. The fourth presupposition: that <term>Gevurah</term> <note>The fifth Sephirah, meaning "Strength" or "Severity," associated with the "great north" in mystical geography.</note> is the "great north"; from here souls proceed, although these Doctors seem to hold that they proceed from Binah. It is true, in fact, that souls primarily depend on the whole Trinity, but especially upon the <term>Holy Spirit</term> <note>original: "Spiritu sancto"</note> regarding their essential being; then they pass through Gevurah first, and successively into the other Sephiroth. Therefore, Moses says: "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life." For to breathe is the property of the Holy Spirit. <term>Origen</term> <note>An influential early Christian theologian (c. 185–253 AD) who wrote extensively on the pre-existence of souls.</note> says that the Holy Spirit gives life to all. The soul, therefore, comes immediately from the Holy Spirit; and because after its creation it first enters the "first chamber," it enters into Gevurah. For this reason, souls are said to be from Gevurah with respect to the other lower Sephiroth of the structure.

And so they pass from one Sephirah to another, until they enter some Sephirah where they share a property with a lower planet destined for the body of that soul, which that soul is meant to animate. And just as the lower planet, under whose influence a person is born, flows into and imparts its influence to the body thus conceived, so the higher planet corresponding to the lower planet informs the soul with an influence proper to itself, so that soul and body participate in the same qualities. For the form follows the disposition of the matter. If the body were of a "solar" nature, the soul will drink in the influence of <term>Tipheret</term> <note>The sixth Sephirah, meaning "Beauty," which corresponds to the Sun in the celestial hierarchy.</note>, the archetypal Sun. All those things which have no free motion follow no other curriculum or path by which they might be carried back to the summit from which they departed, except the instinct they call "natural." This is implanted by nature, as the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>The followers of Aristotle, known for their focus on natural philosophy.</note> say, or (to use their words) because it happens "in most cases and frequently." For thus they defined natural things.

But to speak the truth of the matter, these were granted by the Supreme Craftsman. Those, however, who are sharers in the gift of reason and freedom from God: these ascend the path of their own will or love, according to <term>Augustine</term> <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD).</note>: "My love is my weight (or my path); I am carried there wherever I am moved." Nature many times contributes great force to this, and they run more easily by being drawn by it. For men who are well-disposed in body, and have been allotted a good soul and are well-inclined, reach progress in wisdom and learning, with the favor of <term>Phoebus</term> <note>Apollo, associated with the Sun and intellectual light.</note>, <term>Venus</term>, and <term>Mercury</term>, if we wish to follow the <term>Platonists</term>. And this happens either by disposing the body, or because the Intelligences presiding over those stars favor them with their influence, or (as the <term>Pythagoreans</term> <note>Followers of the ancient philosopher Pythagoras, who believed in the harmony of the spheres and the transmigration of souls.</note> say) because in its descent the soul puts on the nature of those Intelligences, just as light seems to take on the color of the glass through which it passes—red, celestial blue, green, or saffron.

Others reach dominion more easily if their birth and virtue provide for it, and if the Sun and Jupiter and such favor them, if the things the Astronomers hand down are true. They run through various virtues by a natural path according to the various disposition of the body and the influence of the favoring sky. But they attain nothing good unless the supernal power, the source of all good, favors them. For wisdom is not acquired by one's own strengths, as <term>Solomon</term> <note>The biblical king traditionally viewed as the author of Ecclesiastes and the epitome of wisdom.</note> testifies, saying: "And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and I understood that of all the works of the Lord, man can find no reason for those things which are done under the sun." This is because wisdom is given by God, according to the sentiment of <term>James</term> <note>The Apostle James (James 1:5).</note>: "If any man lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all abundantly." And even if souls are distinguished by the Craftsman into different grades, yet there is one common origin for all and the same birth, as we saw above: there is therefore one entrance into life for all, and a similar exit—namely, without knowledge or any virtue—because the soul from the beginning is like a <term>blank slate</term> <note>original: "tabula rasa," a clean slate upon which experience writes.</note> on which nothing is painted. With which it seems singular what that Wise Man infers, because of this (namely because no...

### ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS

...ignorant, I came forth from my mother’s womb) I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me <note>This is a quotation from the Book of Wisdom 7:1–7, where Solomon describes his own pursuit of wisdom</note>. But Plato, whom many from his Academy follow, when he saw many people learning without difficulty—indeed, often knowing things they had never been taught—judged that the types and forms of things, and consequently doctrines, were created together with the soul. However, he believed they were hindered by the senses and bodily bonds, so that only through study, time, and exercise are those innate forms shaken loose. For this reason, some of the Ancients said that the soul, upon entering the body, drinks from the Lethaean whirlpool <note>original: "gurgite lethæo"; a reference to Lethe, the river of forgetfulness in Greek mythology</note>: that is, it drinks of oblivion. 

Nor was this opinion first invented and published by Plato, but was accepted from the more secret Theologians. They believe that all souls were produced by their progenitor, perfected in all their forms, just as the soul of the <term>Protoplast</term> <note>A term for the "first-formed" human, Adam</note> had been produced. He, however, darkened that soul through his transgression; and from the contagion of that sin, our souls are also darkened and entirely put to sleep as they enter the body. And just as it was said to the first parent himself regarding physical food (and perhaps regarding both): *In the sweat of your face* <note>original: "In sudore uultus tui"; from Genesis 3:19</note> or of your nostrils—that is, of your spirit—*you shall eat your bread*, so that same voice and harsh sentence seems to me to thunder unto us all: In your sweat and labor you shall eat your bread, both of your body and of your soul, which is doctrine and the knowledge of things. 

For we must act and sweat if we wish either to learn anew (as the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>The followers of Aristotle, who believed the mind starts as a blank slate and learns through experience</note> say) or to draw out that doctrine which the most generous Distributor infused clearly into our souls from the beginning—but which was soon obscured by the fault of our first parents behind a veil. This veil God, in His kindness, has deigned to remove from the eyes of some. For David did not "learn his letters," yet from a shepherd he was made a Prophet and a preeminent Teacher of divine things. He filled his hymns with such things that all poets, however exquisite, fall far behind him. So too Isaiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, and the other Prophets, and even the Apostles, to whom He said: *I will give you a mouth and wisdom.* Solomon also, in the dream of a single night, was filled by God with such wisdom regarding the conduct of affairs and lower things that not even one among all the ancient kings was like him (even by a great distance). 

And this occurs through the mediation of the anointing of the Holy Spirit, or of the Holy Name, of which it is said in the Canticles: *Thy name is oil poured out* <note>original: "oleũ effusum nomen tuũ"; Song of Songs 1:3</note>. When Christ had handed down the gift and power of this Name to those He knew to be fit and chosen by the Father, He said: *Father, I have manifested Your name to the men You gave me.* Some, however, were reached by this gift even in the mother’s womb, as we read of John and Jeremiah. Whether this happened through the infusion of new wisdom (which I believe), or through the removal of the veil so that the intellect, being unhindered and with an unveiled face, could transcend from clarity to clarity, God knows. For I yield to the truth and to the Holy Scriptures confirmed in that same truth, from which we hold that God made all things "very good"—that is, in their own complete perfection. 

For just as He filled the vegetative trees with fruits, the use of which He granted to the first-formed humans, so many believe He made "rational trees" <note>An analogy for human souls</note>, whose fruits are gathered and whose cultivation is commanded, along with the labor and sweat of the Spirit and the exercise of all powers. And this labor begins when souls enter the "night" of the body. For just as a shadow blocks the light of the Sun, so the body blocks the powers of the soul. 

To conclude: (Souls [proceed] from the third light) that is, from <term>Binah</term> <note>The third Sephirah, meaning "Understanding"</note>. The <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>The ten divine emanations in Kabbalistic thought</note> are called by various names, just as Christ is called Jesus, Son of God, Messiah, Word, Wisdom, Redeemer, etc. In the same way, the Sephiroth are named in different ways: they are called "numerations," "dimensions," "days of the structure," and "light," as stated above. Therefore, souls proceed first from <term>Chocmah</term> <note>The second Sephirah, meaning "Wisdom"</note> regarding their ideal being; secondly, they proceed from Binah through creation. Then (on the fourth day), that is, to <term>Ghebura</term> <note>The fifth Sephirah, meaning "Strength" or "Severity"</note>—namely, after their existence of creation from the Holy Spirit—descending from there from Ghebura, they enter into the other Sephiroth until they find a Sephirah that is proportionate and in harmony with the planet dominating the body of that soul; then they enter the "night" of the body.

Having previously discussed the nature of the soul and its descent into the body, the text now shifts to an interpretation of the Six Days of Creation, the symbolism of the Cedar of Lebanon, and the distinction between the "Work of the Beginning" (natural science) and the "Work of the Chariot" (divine science).</meta>

### COMMENTARY BY ARCHANGELUS

**KABBALISTIC DOGMA.** Regarding the six days of Genesis, we must understand them as six buildings proceeding from the Beginning <note>original: "Bresit"; a reference to *Bereshit*, the first word of the Torah meaning "In the beginning"</note>, just as Cedars proceed from Lebanon.

**FRIAR ARCHANGELUS.** Among plants, the palm and the cedar are celebrated above all others, the former being the most excellent of all trees, and the latter of all plants. Speaking of the cedar, I say that the Doctors disagree among themselves in determining what kind of wood it is. However, Dioscorides <note>A 1st-century Greek physician and botanist</note> and Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, a Roman naturalist</note> say it is what is called *Thya* <note>original: "Tya"; likely *Thuja* or a similar resinous tree</note>, which provides a resin called *cedria* <note>cedar oil or resin</note>, which is extremely useful for toothaches. For, when applied, it breaks the teeth and settles the pain; it has many other properties that we omit for the sake of brevity. 

Nevertheless, all the Sages agree on this: that Shittim wood <note>original: "lignũ sethim"; the wood used to build the Ark of the Covenant</note> and the cedar, which they call by their own term, are exactly the same thing. Indeed, this tree was celebrated by the Divine Harpist <note>A reference to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms</note>, because it is the "Tree of Adonai," planted by Him in Lebanon—that is, in the supramundane forest, the garden of delights, or in that most radiant and eminent Mind. For "Lebanon" signifies both "high" and "white" <note>In Hebrew, *Laban* means white; the name Lebanon refers to the snow-capped peaks</note>. Therefore, this tree, along with the palm, is a sacred mystery, for they signify the saints and the primary Leaders of God, planted by Him.

**The Conclusion (Regarding the six days of Genesis, etc.).** Whatever the lovers of human arts learn from Holy Scripture through natural science is like good gold, and is called the Work of the Beginning <note>original: "opus de Bresith"; in Hebrew, *Ma'aseh Bereshit*, referring to natural philosophy or physics</note>. But that which we receive through spiritual science is called the Work of the Chariot <note>original: "opus de merchana"; in Hebrew, *Ma'aseh Merkavah*, referring to metaphysics and the study of the divine realm</note>, and is equated to the finest and purest gold. 

Hence they write that the Work of the Beginning is the wisdom of nature, and the Work of the Chariot is the wisdom of Divinity. Therefore, they say there are two Worlds: the first is intellectual and is called the World to Come <note>original: "holam hauo"; Hebrew: עולם הבא, *Olam Ha-Ba*</note>, which is the higher world. The second is sensible <note>perceptible by the senses</note> and is called This World <note>original: "holam hazah"; Hebrew: עולם הזה, *Olam Ha-Zeh*</note>. This is held by the more secret Theologians who, speaking of the Name of Forty-Two Letters <note>A mystical Kabbalistic name of God</note>, say: "The cultivator of such things is beloved above and desired below, and he inherits two worlds: the present world and the world to come." 

This double order is distinguished by the fact that the happy and blessed Kabbalist transfers and translates all study, every work, every counsel, labor, and diligence—indeed his entire intention—from the sensible world to the intellectual world. The Talmudists, however, remain in the sensible world, and their soul does not transcend the soul of this universe. Although they may freely proceed toward God and the blessed spirits, they do not approach God as He is—remaining absolute—but rather as the Craftsman and the Cause of things, occupied with the created world. They assign Angels to daily ministries and the execution of divine commands, always bringing the contemplations of the highest things down to the lower world. Yet, the faculty for these things is borrowed from the senses and drawn toward their own desire. 

Truly, sometimes the Talmudists and the Kabbalists communicate back and forth with one another, like the active and contemplative lives, although they often interpret the same context of Holy Scripture differently. Just as in the present case of the six days of the world's creation: the Talmudists take them as solar days, but the Kabbalists take those days as archetypes <note>ideal forms existing in the divine mind</note>. 

It is the doctrine of the most wise Solomon that "He who lives forever created all things at once." This is echoed by Augustine, Albertus Magnus, and the Master of the Sentences <note>Peter Lombard, author of the standard medieval theological textbook</note>, along with the Hebrews and all who think correctly. For a finite and determined power requires time for its actions, but an infinite power does not. Such is the Craftsman—certainly not as poorly measured by the accursed Arab <note>A common polemical reference to the philosopher Averroes</note> and others who said that God does not work by infinite power because an infinite work was not produced. For although He used interminable power in the making, and could have put that same infinite power into the work, He enclosed it within the boundaries He willed, and brought it forth just so. Since, therefore, He produced all things by His command and word, as the Prophet says: *He spoke and they were made; He commanded and they were created* <note>Psalm 33:9</note>. For when the word was spoken, "Let there be light,"...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Six Days of Genesis" mentioned on the previous page. Having established the metaphor of the Cedars of Lebanon and the Beginnings, the author now addresses the philosophical and theological problem of "time" during creation, arguing that the six days represent an intellectual order rather than a chronological sequence.</meta>

# ON KABBALISTIC DOGMAS.

[...if the] firmament, or the sphere of the heavens, [was produced] in the midst of the waters, or if the earth produced green plants, everything would have come forth at once. Why then was there such a delay, and why was light made only until the space of a day passed and evening came? And why was the sprouting of the earth delayed until the third day, and the production of the Sun, Moon, and stars until the fourth? And why was the spawning of the waters given only on the fifth? And why was the shaping of man celebrated on the sixth? And why was the seventh appointed for rest? Let them say if they have any answer. Augustine rightly ridicules those who deserve to be ridiculed: those who imagine that God seeks out time in his actions. Hence Origen, among the men of sense, does not admit those who think the first, second, and third days—in which evening and morning are said to occur—happened without the Sun, Moon, and stars, or who think the first day existed without the heavens. Indeed, they do a great injury to the Smoke <note>Likely a reference to the "divine cloud" or "vapor" of creation</note> and to the Eternal Craftsman, to whom all things are present, while they suppose Him to act through time and successively; His measure is eternity, and He possesses all of it at once. Therefore, regarding this entire structure, which was completed all at once, Moses himself—repeating that which he seemed to have distinguished by days—asserts that it was produced together in one and the same day, saying: *these are the generations of the heaven and the earth, when they were created in the day that the Lord God created the heaven and the earth, and every shrub of the field before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field before it grew.* <note>original: "i-ſtæ ſunt generationes cœli, & terræ, quādo creatæ ſunt in die, quo creauit Dominus Deus cœlū, & terrā, & omne uirgultum agri, antequā eſſet in terra, & omnem herbam agri, antequam germinaret." Genesis 2:4–5</note> But God Himself, speaking with Job, says: *Behold behemoth, whom I made with you.* <note>original: "Ecce behemot, quem feci tecum." Job 40:15</note> This most clearly hints that the evil angel—who is said by almost everyone to have been produced on the first day with the Angels of Light—was also fashioned at the same time as man. 

However, the three days assigned to the building, and the three to the ornamentation, and the seventh which closes the circle of days and is said to be destined for rest: these are not days distinguished by the circuit of the Sun. We must therefore refer that division of days not to time, but to the order of production and the sequence of things produced. This is because, according to Augustine, the ancient theologians, distinguished philosophers, and the more skilled poets—such as Hermes Trismegistus, Alcinous, Hesiod, and Euripides—Heaven and Earth were once mixed together as a kind of chaos; later, having been separated, they gave birth to individual things: trees, birds, wild beasts, and the race of mortals. 

And if all the works of the Supreme Craftsman are said to be fashioned with a great mystery and a great sacrament, it is no less so regarding the number six <note>original: "senarius"</note> by which the entire structure is described as being divided. For the number six (as the mathematicians teach) is the first perfect number; this is because it results exactly from the combination of its parts <note>Factors</note>—namely, one, two, and three. Hence it is called <term>nuptial</term> <note>original: "γαμῶν" (gamōn); a Greek term used by Pythagoreans to signify marriage or union</note> by the Pythagoreans, because its own parts, when placed beside one another, beget it. It is also for this reason that it is procreated from the first even and the first odd number, as if from a male and female, one being led into the other: for if you join twice three, or again three times two, the number six arises from both sides. Furthermore, any of the said aliquot parts combined make up the Six, such as six times one, three times two, or twice three. Indeed, no number more harmonious could be found for the construction of the World than the six, which consists of the "double proportion" <note>The ratio of 2:1</note> which its parts contain closely within themselves. This is the proportion of four to two; these numbers joined together return the six. You will hardly find this in other numbers, except in those that preserve the nature of the six, such as twelve, eighteen, etc. 

The number six, as the first perfect number, also suits the Supreme Craftsman, God, or His structure. Just as nothing is lacking in Him, so in the number six, when distributed through its members, nothing is left over, nothing is missing, nothing exceeds, nothing flows out, and nothing flows in; it does not require outside help, but is equal, tempered, and stands and consists by its own parts and strengths. Therefore, when God had produced His work by dividing it according to this number, Moses said: *Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.* <note>original: "Perfecti ſunt igitur cœli, & terra, & omnis exercitus eorū." Genesis 2:1</note> Thus Augustine teaches that God perfected His works in six days; he believes that a mystery and the parts of time are signaled by this number. For this reason, we even need numbers to perceive the sacraments of God and Nature—not indeed merchant numbers <note>Practical arithmetic used for trade</note>, but more hidden and "formal" numbers (as Syrianus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher</note> calls them), which are intellectual and ideal. Therefore, just as the Cedars proceed from Mount Lebanon, so the dimensions—or the six lower Sephiroth—proceed from the three primary dimensions. These six lower dimensions are called the "Fabric." 

Just as the World (as we have said) has six extremities, by a similar logic, the two structures of the celestial building possess six Sephiroth, which are called the extremities of that building. Therefore, beneath the equator, the habitation must be most intemperate and the men blackest.

Indeed, Scripture says that God placed man in a "Paradise of pleasure." This is also confirmed by reason: because beneath the equator, it is always the equinox; since the heat is intensified during the day, it is equally diminished by the cold at night. Furthermore, both hot and cold planets flow there and shine upon it equally and directly; therefore, the "complexion" <note>The biological balance of qualities</note> is rendered most temperate. ### ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS.

...near the summer tropic, the Sun is at the apogee <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the Earth</note> of its eccentric circle. But when it is near the winter tropic, it is at the opposite of the apogee, closer to the earth. Second, the cause of heat is the direction of the warming rays: and for this reason, the regions under the **Torrid Zone** <note>The area of the Earth between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn</note>, which is bounded by the two tropics, are hotter than the regions existing outside the Torrid Zone in any of the other four zones. The third cause is the duration of the warming body, and because of this, the regions in the Torrid Zone around the tropics and directly under them are hotter than the regions around the equator and those existing under it: because the Sun, when it describes the equator <note>When it passes over the equator during the equinoxes</note>, moves more quickly than when it describes the tropics. Thus, the ray is less fixed upon the targeted earth. 

And likewise: because the Sun lingers for a greater time near the Zenith of those who are close to the tropics than near the equator. For when it reaches the beginning of Aries and Libra, it makes greater and more notable declinations from the equator than it does around the beginning of Cancer and Capricorn. The most evident argument for this is taken from the increase and decrease of artificial days and nights <note>"Artificial days" refer to the period of daylight from sunrise to sunset</note>: for days and nights increase and decrease more perceptibly around the equinoxes than around the solstices. Also for this reason, in the months of July and August, the heat is more intense in northern regions than in the months of May or March, even though the Sun is closer to them in the month of June: because the Sun has lingered longer in the northern signs and toward the North Pole in July or August than it did in June. 

Also for this same cause, on summer days, we feel greater heat after midday than at midday or before, although at midday the Sun is closer to our Zenith; this is because after midday, the Sun's stay above our horizon has been longer, and heat is continually added upon heat, causing it to grow and intensify. Among these three causes of heat, the third is the most principal and greatest for the reasons given: namely, because the area has been warmed for a longer duration. The second cause, following that one, is the stronger direction of the rays; the smallest cause of heat, however, is the proximity of the warming body. Hence, in summer the Sun is sometimes further from us because it is in the apogee of its eccentric orbit, yet it warms our region more than in winter when it is near the opposite of the apogee, because the Sun in summer, approaching the Zenith above our heads, shines more directly upon us. 

Thus, regarding the question, we must speak (saving better judgment) through two conclusions. The first is that habitation under the equator is more intemperate due to excess heat than the habitations of the **fourth and fifth climates** <note>In ancient geography, "climates" were zones of latitude; the 4th and 5th were considered the most pleasant Mediterranean and European regions</note>, which seem the most pleasant of all. The second conclusion: habitation under the equator is much more temperate than under the tropics and around the tropics, because there is less excess of heat. For the Sun's stay around the tropics is greater (as we have said), although there is greater proximity of the Sun at the equator and sometimes more direct radiation. 

This is confirmed by the natures and complexions of men: for the **Ethiopians** <note>A term used historically to refer to people of sub-Saharan Africa</note> living near the summer tropic are very black, very dry, and of short stature; but under the equator, people are found to be pale, of good complexion, and of longer life. The response to the arguments of both opinions is easy: for it does not follow (as the first opinion says) that if regions always appear hotter and more intemperate to those proceeding from the fourth climate toward the summer tropic, they should also appear so to those proceeding from the tropic toward the equator, for the reasons stated. 

Furthermore, regarding what the second opinion brings forward from **Isidore** <note>Isidore of Seville, a 7th-century scholar whose "Etymologies" was a standard reference in the Middle Ages</note> and from the pages of Holy Scripture, we concede that such a place can exist. But we say that the pleasantness of that place (called the **Earthly Paradise** <note>original: "Paradisus terrestris"</note>) is not from the quality or nature of that region, but from the location of Paradise itself. For because it is in the highest place (as Isidore says), it transcends a great part of the middle region of the air; thus it happens that neither winds, nor whirlwinds, nor rains are generated there, nor is the heat intensified there by the reflection of rays. And the decision of the conclusion is clear: namely, that such a place of habi—

### COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS

...a habitable place: but as for that place being Paradise, of which the Scripture speaks, it is not admitted by the Kabbalists. For it is not terrestrial in the common sense, but was created before the fabric of the World, as Jerome rightly feels, who in his commentary on the Book of Genesis says: for Paradise, the text has *gan eden*, that is, a "garden of delights." <note>Jerome refers to the Hebrew terms *gan* (garden) and *eden* (pleasure/delight).</note> Symmachus <note>An 2nd-century translator of the Old Testament into Greek</note> translated it as a "flowering Paradise." Furthermore, regarding what follows—"toward the East"—the Hebrew says *mi-kedem*: which Aquila <note>Another early Greek translator</note> rendered as "from the start"; Symmachus and Theodotion, however, rendered it as "from the beginning," by which it is most clearly proven that before God made the heaven and the earth, God had already prepared Paradise. Thus far Jerome: that Paradise is therefore celestial and divine, and an entrance is granted when a person, turned away from sin and uplifted in heart and world, returns. For then he sees **GOD**, applies his mind to the kingdom of heaven which he possesses (which is within us), and is in Paradise itself—all of which are the same thing. 

And this is the "turning sword" <note>original: *rumphea uerfatilis*; the flaming sword of the Cherubim in Genesis 3:24</note> which the Cherubim holds for the guardianship of Paradise itself—namely, "turning away." If one is turned away from God toward creatures, then He expels the one thus turned away from the tree of life and from the delights of Paradise itself. But if the turning is away from sins and creatures toward God, then through the Cherubim one attains a vision <note>The name "Cherubim" was often etymologically interpreted by medieval scholars as "fullness of knowledge" or "vision."</note> and a return to that same Paradise from which he had been exiled. 

Therefore, metaphorically (according to the Kabbalists), Moses speaks of Paradise, always implying an anagogical <note>A spiritual or mystical interpretation leading the mind upward</note> sense: since that garden is not terrestrial (as is commonly believed), but celestial and divine, planted by the celestial farmer and craftsman—certainly in the "earth," yet not in this filthy earth, but in the "earth of the living." This is figured through that Promised Land, of which it is said: *You brought a vine out of Egypt, you cast out the nations and planted it; you planted its roots and it filled the earth.* <note>Psalm 80</note> And lest anyone be deceived believing he speaks of this thick, physical earth, he adds a little lower: *Visit this vine, and perfect that which your right hand has planted, and look upon the son whom you have confirmed or strengthened for yourself.* 

Behold how beautifully he hints that this better vine, and consequently all the trees of Paradise, are planted in the Son and in the Divine Word; for He says: *If anyone does not abide in me, he shall be cast out like a branch and wither, and be cast into the fire.* <note>John 15:6</note> By this Word, therefore, are not only the Trees, but all things planted and sustained, as John says: *What was made in Him was life.* <note>John 1:3-4</note> And with Paul: *Upholding all things by the word of His power* <note>Hebrews 1:3</note>—which is also called the Book of Life. And: *In your book all were written* <note>Psalm 139:16</note>—written, that is, under eternal images and archetypes. And the Word itself, with all things contained in it at once, is in the Father: and therefore we are planted in the Father, in whom He is, as He says: *As you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us.* <note>John 17:21</note> 

In these things, therefore, are true riches and pleasures. Whence Paradise is a garden of delights, watered by that river of pleasure of which the holy harper <note>King David</note> says: *They shall be inebriated by the abundance of your house, and you shall give them to drink from the torrent of your pleasure* (namely, from the fountain of which it follows) *for with you is the fountain of life.* <note>Psalm 36:8-9</note> 

Mercurius <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Egyptian sage</note> affirms that the elements and principles of nature, and also the beautiful World, flowed from Him who is the source of all things and, as the most fertile of all, contains the entire power of generating without the aid of any contrary. Hence Pan <note>The Greek god of nature, whose name means "All"</note> is spoken of by the poets (signifying "The All"), whom the Arcadians, thinking him to be the Sun, used to worship. He is indeed the True Sun, not celestial but supramundane and divine. His image was of this sort: he bore horns on his head which denote the kingdom and power he holds in the upper and lower realms. His beard was long, extending the rays of light or divine goodness down to the lowest depths. The lower part of his body was shaggy because of the brushwood, mountains, rocks, and wild beasts; but the upper part was smooth, whence he is said to ride upon the level plains of the upper air. He plays a pipe of seven reeds: that is, the harmony of the seven planets, in which there are sevenfold sounds that complete the *diapason* <note>The musical octave</note>, that is, the perfect consonance. The staff in his hands is the power by which all things are governed. They depicted him laughing, to represent his everlasting happiness...

It connects the Platonic "First Cause" and the Neoplatonic "One" with the Kabbalistic Sephiroth, explaining how the divine unity flows into the multiplicity of the world and how humanity returns to that unity through the "Son" and the "structure" of Paradise.</meta>

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS

...and they delighted, bringing in Echo, which is a voice emitted in hollow places or against any objects arranged to resonate; for a voice expresses a word and the concept of the mind. Therefore, by a voice or a saying, God fabricated the World and all its members, and He governs by a voice, issuing commands. He also manifests His love toward us through many cries: and He delights in a reciprocal love (which is the resonating Echo). These are the delights which He has with the sons of men. He wore the starry skin <note>original: *Hebridem*—likely a typo for *nebridem*, the fawn-skin worn by the god Pan, which was traditionally said to represent the starry heavens</note> upon his breast. Because by a single skin, and by a single act or nod, He contains the gathering and the power of all the stars. But what the poets called Pan (that is, "the All," containing everything), the philosophers called the "first cause" and the "principle of all causes," granting to all causes their ability to flow into things. For whatever a secondary cause does, it executes by the power of the first cause, which flows more strongly than the secondary one, as Proclus <note>A 5th-century Neoplatonist philosopher who heavily influenced medieval Christian and Jewish mysticism</note> says, asserting thereafter that all things have their essence from the first being and the first cause, and they live from the first life; and they exist immediately from the first and highest intelligence. It is necessary that this [intelligence] be fruitful of all those things which excel in others. It is in itself supremely happy and blessed; but happiness (as Speusippus <note>Plato’s nephew and successor as head of the Academy</note> defines it) is a good accumulated from all goods. Blessed, moreover, is he who lacks nothing, and who has whatever he wants, as the blessed Augustine and Plato assert. Therefore, nothing is lacking to Him who contains all things, like a true sphere of all; as Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many mystical and alchemical texts were attributed</note> said. And since nothing exists outside the sphere of the World, so nothing is outside the divine circuit which embraces all things; He contains every number, being Himself the true unity—which is the principle and root of all numbers, granting to all things that they be numbered. Every number or multitude (according to Proclus) is from the one; nor would anything be "one" while simultaneously making a multitude with others (as he continues), unless it acquired unity for itself through participation in the One. No one doubts that this "One" and most ancient being is God, who, before He communicated a particular unity to lower things, poured Himself out into the first number, namely into the ternary <note>the number three</note>, and from there into the denary <note>the number ten</note> (according to the Hebrews), as if into ten ideas and measures of all numbers and of all things to be made; for this reason, no further number can be given. This ten, when gathered together, returns to the One from which it had its beginning, so that the ten is the end and completion of numbers, and the beginning of the decades. Imitating this series of numbers as a true model, all things strive to return to that One from which they proceeded, just as branches from a trunk or a root, rays from the sun, or streams from a fountain: for all creatures do not have being from themselves, but from God, who is the fountain and origin of all streams, etc. Therefore it is wisely said:

> God is He in whom we live, move, and have our being: <note>A reference to Acts 17:28</note>

All things are indeed rooted in the unity of the infinite essence. Therefore, all things are said to be "one." And that "one" is the tenth supreme *sephirah* <note>The *Sephiroth* are the ten emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>, regarding which the conclusion says that it is more correctly called "Paradise"—the whole building: that is, all ten *sephiroth* together, rather than just the tenth. It is one: because Paradise is true pleasure, which is found only in God; for it is a satisfying pleasure that is found only in God. Whence David, desiring this satiety, said:

> I shall be satisfied when your glory appears. <note>Psalm 17:15</note>

The true garden of Paradise, therefore, is the tree containing all ten *sephiroth*. In which tree there are ten particular trees that produce various effects. Others say that Paradise is only in *malchut* <note>The tenth Sephirah, associated with the physical world, the Kingdom, and the "Shekhinah" or Divine Presence</note>, which is called the "kingdom" and the "land of the living." Others say it is in *tipheret* <note>The sixth Sephirah, meaning "Beauty," often associated with the Son or the heart of the divine tree</note>, for He is Christ, the father of all. We were first born from the eternal Father, through the Son, into whom the seed of ideas had been poured; afterward, we were regenerated again through the Son as man. For when the image was disturbed and the likeness utterly lost, we were not worthily called sons of God the Father; therefore it was necessary for us to be born anew through baptism. In the first generation, He formed us according to the "ideal idol" <note>An archetypal or perfect mental image</note>. In the second, however, according to that "idol" which is painted in the book of predestination and life: that is, in the Word regenerating us, in whom all are written, and to whose degree of perfection they are to be led. Nor do they have from there only a name and a painted image, but they receive a certain power from there, just as children from parents through

# COMMENTARY BY ARCHANGELUS

...the seed separated from them. Nor would it have been enough for our most pious father to transform himself into a spiritual man, unless he also prepared the foods appropriate for him. This occurred when he said: **Take, and eat, this is my body**, etc. <note>original: "Accipite, & manducate, hoc est corpus, &c." — Matthew 26:26</note> Thus he instructed us. The doctrine created by the Word contains the fullness of all Gospel truth; if we wished to explain this doctrine, our weak powers would not suffice, nor (to use the words of John) **could the whole world contain it**. <note>original: "nec totus Mundus capere posset" — John 21:25</note> And although he taught this in the temple, on the mountains, in the synagogues, and in various places, he delivered the sum of his doctrine most effectively upon the cross. 

Our heavenly Father enriched us with treasures. For they are called riches (as Marcus Varro <note>A Roman scholar and writer (116–27 BC), often cited by Renaissance humanists for definitions</note> teaches) because they make us rich. And his treasures are the graces of wisdom and glory; without these, even if we possess lesser things, we are most poor. Yet the Best Father, not content with the things mentioned above, left at his end even greater tokens of his love; not only in that he laid down his life, but because he bequeathed a most opulent <term>testament</term> <note>Meaning both a legal will and a divine covenant</note>: he bequeathed that than which nothing greater can be imagined: for he bequeathed the eternal and most blessed kingdom of happiness, which he promised he would give immediately to the thief, when he said: **Today you will be with me in paradise**; <note>original: "hodie mecum eris in paradiso" — Luke 23:43</note> that is, today you will enjoy my essence, which is the object of bliss. 

And for this reason, the thief was at his right hand. For at his right hand are eternal delights; these the prophet Haggai <note>The text attributes the quote "you will fill me with joy" (Psalm 16:11) to Haggai, though it is traditionally Davidic</note> foresaw when he said: *you will fill me with joy*, giving, namely, from the eternal delights which are at your right hand. Furthermore, he was our **Head**, not just our Father; for he did not wish to be alone in the things written above, but wished also to unite us all together into the same body, than which no greater union is given. He himself was made its head, so that he might govern all the members and flow into them; for just as all the internal senses are in the head—from which the members are seen to be governed by the head as by a leader, and filled with power like streams filled from a fountain—all these things, according to a spiritual influx, proceed from our head, Christ. 

Hence Paul says: **By the grace of God I am what I am**; <note>original: "Gratia Dei sum, id quod sum" — 1 Corinthians 15:10</note> because all that we are flows into us through Christ alone. Neither reason, nor intellect, nor anything for knowing divine things exists in us unless it is supplied by the head, which is the **true light illuminating everyone**. <note>original: "lux uera omnes illuminans" — John 1:9</note> For just as when the head is cut off, no strength remains in the members, so when Christ departs from a man, life departs, and from him ceases every operation and movement that pertains to that spiritual life. Therefore, if we wish to have any favor for the inner man, it must necessarily flow from him, **from whose fullness** (as John says) **we have all received**; <note>original: "de cuius plenitudine... omnes accepimus" — John 1:16</note> and those who are in the kingdom of bliss receive it even more fully. 

Therefore, some say well (as this present conclusion states): that in the middle of Paradise is placed the great Adam, Christ the heavenly Messiah, who came to make satisfaction for the earthly Adam. And his place in the <term>archetype</term> <note>The "archetypal world" or *Olam Ha-Atzilut* in Kabbalah, the highest realm of divine emanation</note> is called **Tiferet**, <note>original: "Thiphereth" — the sixth Sephirah, representing Beauty, Balance, and the Heart</note> in the middle of the **Sephiroth**. <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> For Christ holds the middle position between the divine persons; and to show this by his deeds, he took care to always hold the middle place—in his entrance, in his life, in his departure, and in his kingdom. He was born in the middle of two animals <note>Traditionally the ox and the ass in the manger</note>; he debated in the middle of the teachers; being in the middle of his disciples, he taught them; at the end of his life, he was placed in the middle of two thieves; in the judgment, he will stand in the middle of the chosen and the rejected; and in his kingdom, he has always held and will hold the middle place, existing as the advocate and mediator between the Father and us. 

Finally, he is the one remaining in that divine archetypal world, in which **Abraham**, full of piety, is placed on the right by the Hebrew theologians; **Isaac**, truly of the most severe justice in sacrifice, is placed on the left; but in the very center is **Jacob**, in whose house, as the oracle testifies, our Mediator reigns forever, having returned to where he came from. He did this so that he might lead us, having been made true Israelites, to that place; for not without cause did he say: **I have not come except for the lost sheep of the house of Israel.** <note>original: "non ueni nisi ad oues, quæ perierunt domus Israēl" — Matthew 15:24</note> That place is called **Tiferet** (as I said above); and because of this, the Kabbalists say that we are to be blessed in Tiferet itself. It is better, however, to say that he is in all ten Sephiroth, because Christ says in rewarding...
