...preparing the harts: <note>Refers to Psalm 29:9, "The voice of the Lord makes the harts to calve," often interpreted in Kabbalah as the preparation of souls or spiritual vessels</note> for what preparation is made from the voice of the Lord for those visible creatures? Or what doctrine ever descends to them from the voice of the Lord? They are spiritual beings: whose form and image that animal holds, which is disposed by the voice of the Lord to pursue the serpent kind. This is the nature of the Evangelical Law: which prepares servants—that is, those cleansed by the washing of baptism—for battle: and arrays them under Christ against that ancient serpent, the devil. In the archetype, however, the deer and the goat represent those divine powers, called the **Sephirot** <term>Sephirot: The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</term>, and the lower dimensions, **Gedulah** <term>Gedulah: "Greatness," often synonymous with Chesed (Mercy)</term> and **Ghebura** <term>Ghebura: "Strength" or "Judgment"</term>; which are also called **Hod** <term>Hod: "Splendor" or "Majesty"</term> and **Nezach** <term>Nezach: "Victory" or "Endurance"</term>. By these divine powers or properties, the most wise Solomon testifies in his Songs when he says: *I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes and harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor awake my love.* <note>Song of Solomon 2:7</note> The bond of this oath is through the tribunal of justice, from which punishments for crimes proceed. Hence, by swearing and entreating through these, he submits and binds himself to all censures and sentences emanating from those tribunals, so that the oath cannot be dissolved: but he may receive the reward for observing the sacrament, or punishment for its transgression. And because the lower measures, which are called fawns, are also called "breasts"—namely, those which suckled all the Prophets—it is said in the Songs: *Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.* <note>Song of Solomon 4:5</note> This refers to **Malchut** <term>Malchut: "Kingdom," the lowest Sephirah</term>, which is the lowest of all. And through this one-horned hart <note>original: "ceruam unicornem"</note>, the three who preceded Moses prophesied: because the order of the Sephirot had not yet appeared; for as yet the Sephirot were not divided into a tree with right and left sides. For God contained within Himself grace and glory: but in the time of Moses, God began to open the left hand of justice in the punishment of transgressors; while in the time of Christ, He opened the right hand of the numbered emanations, showing mercy. Wherefore, in ancient times, Malchut was called "one-horned" <note>original: "unicornis"</note>: because the Sephirot were not yet divided into right and left (as I said); but in the time of Moses, they were divided: wherefore they became known to him through the higher Sephirot.

It must be said otherwise, that those prophesying before Moses (as the more secret parts of the Torah say) prophesied through the one-horned hart. The harts are the breasts of the higher divinity (as I said), and the fawns of the harts are the lower breasts, from which (as I said) all the Prophets were suckled. And just as the breasts are two-fold, so is their light. For one is the light of prophesying, but the other is the power of performing miracles. Elisha was not ignorant of this: because he asked from Elijah, as he ascended into heaven, for a "double portion of his spirit": that is, both powers—the power of prophesying and the power of performing miracles. But since we never read of anyone performing miracles before Moses, it is therefore said that they prophesied only with a "single horn" and by the power of that hart: that is, by the influence of the font of prophesying. The perpetration of miracles pertains to the power of prophesying. For both belong to the prophetic spirit: namely, effective prayer, the operation of virtues, and the revelation of hidden things. For concerning Abraham, the Lord said to Abimelech, who had taken Abraham’s wife: *Restore the man his wife, and he shall pray for you: because he is a prophet.* <note>Genesis 20:7</note> You see: the operation of miracles performed by the prophets is clear: just as Elisha healed Naaman the Syrian, and multiplied the bread; he brought back the iron from the water, and raised the son of the Shunammite; as did Elijah, who raised the son of that Sidonian woman and closed the heavens. And many similar things were done by the prophets after Moses. Note that the work of the prophets is not only to predict future things, but to reveal the hidden things of Scripture. Just as Moses did, and Haggai, or Ezra: each in his own way—one through scripture manifested the sacraments of the Law. So also he who reveals hidden things performs the office of a prophet: just as Elisha knew of the gifts that Gehazi had received from Naaman. It must be said otherwise and learned: for in the fourth book of Kings <note>Known as 2 Kings in modern Bibles</note> it is read that when Elijah came with Elisha into Jericho, the sons of the prophets said to Elisha: *Do you know that the Lord will take away your master from you today?* To which he responded: *I know it, be silent.* From which it is clear...

Neither the sons of the prophets nor Elisha <note>original: "Helisaeus"</note> foresaw in the spirit the future rapture of Elijah; they knew of the event, but they did not know the symbolic meaning <note>original: "figuram"</note> of that rapture, nor what would further become of Elijah. Indeed, they were ignorant that it signified the ascension of Christ into heaven, and how Elijah was to come in the time of the Antichrist to preach the second coming of Christ. Therefore, both the sons of the prophets and Elisha possessed only a simple prophetic spirit regarding the future rapture of Elijah. 

And so Elisha, desiring to know what would become of Elijah, said to him as he was being carried toward Paradise: *I beseech you, Lord, that the spirit which is in you be made double in me* <note>A reference to 2 Kings 2:9</note>. It was as if he were saying: "Let me know in a double spirit what this rapture of yours prefigures, and let me know and foresee the future mysteries concerning Christ the Messiah promised in the Law, which I cannot foresee except through a double spirit and prophetic light." To him Elijah replied, "You ask a difficult thing." It was as if he said, "It is difficult, and granted to few, to attain such a double prophetic spirit." 

Elijah said this because he himself, in a double spirit, had foreseen through his own rapture how Christ, after his passion and resurrection, was to ascend into heaven and receive universal dominion and judicial power over all creatures; and how He was to come at the end of the world to judge all nations; and how Elijah himself was to come before Christ to preach His second advent; and how he was to be slain by the Antichrist. This double spirit, therefore, Elijah obtained from the Lord for Elisha, as is evident in that passage. 

It is clear, then, how the simple prophetic spirit reached only the temporal deeds and material matters of that people, the city, and the temple. But the double spirit was that which not only foresaw and reached the future deeds and materials of the Old Testament, but through them transcended even to the mysteries of Christ and the Church prefigured in them. Thus, transcending those material things, it arrived at the prophetic knowledge of Christ and the Redeemer. This privilege was not granted to the fathers preceding Moses; for this reason, they prophesied through the "one-horned doe," **Malchut** <term>Malchut: "Kingdom," the tenth and lowest Sephirah, associated with the physical world and the presence of the Divine on Earth</term>, as I have said.

->**KABBALISTIC DOGMA**<-

*Wherever in Scripture mention is made of the love between male and female, it mystically signifies for us the union of **Tipheret** and **Cheneceth** of Israel, or **Beth** and **Tipheret**.*
<note>Tipheret represents the "Beauty" or "Harmony" of the Divine Male principle; Cheneceth (Knesset) Israel represents the "Assembly of Israel" or the Divine Female principle, often equated with the Shekhinah.</note>

**FRIAR ARCHANGELUS:** Orpheus said that Love was older than all the Gods; but Agathon, and those following him, said he was younger. Love is indeed younger, as Agathon pleases, who contemplated the "intelligible being" of the Gods, as they exist in the archetype. By this being, Love is younger, through which (as Trismegistus <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic wisdom</note> and Plato in the *Symposium* agree) God, according to the likeness of that intelligible and ideal being, produced all the Gods—namely, the intelligences—into particular forms. 

Orpheus, however, contemplated them as already produced in particularity; those existing in particular forms are "after" the Love through which they were produced, though they were "prior" in their ideal being. Orpheus adds, saying: *Love is blind.* Hence (as the poets imagine), Love is described with veiled eyes, because the lover is sometimes carried away by such an impetus of love that it darkens reason so that he cannot see. Thus, he performs the works of a child rather than a sensible man; for this reason, Love is also painted as a boy. 

But Orpheus and Plato climb higher, saying that Love is above the intellect. This is because love is sometimes carried toward the Love of Divine things which it does not yet know. Nor does the statement of Augustine <note>St. Augustine of Hippo</note> stand in the way: "that the will is not moved except toward what is foreknown," and "that we cannot love the unknown." For that is understood regarding the love which is held through natural discourse, and not regarding that love which is implanted in our nature. By this natural love we love God, though He is unknown, and sometimes we love a creature very little known, but through a certain natural "pre-sensation." Just as it happens that at the mere presence of someone whom he feels to be "conforming" to himself, a man loves; and he fears and shudders at what is "disconforming." Just as a sheep shudders at the presence of a wolf, and a man in the night trembles at the presence of an enemy whom he does not see. So also many are carried by Love toward the celestial beings, whom they know very little. And such an inclination created things have from God,

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the metaphysical foundations of the universe, shifting from the specific prophetic examples of the previous page to a broad philosophical and theological exploration of Love (Amor) as the primary force of creation, order, and unity in both Platonic and Christian thought.</meta>

<page-num>786</page-num>
### ARCHANGELUS'S COMMENTARY

...who through his wisdom arranged all things. As the wise man <note>A reference to Solomon, the traditional author of Proverbs</note> testifies, divine wisdom speaks thus: "When he prepared the heavens, I was present; when with a fixed Law and circle he hedged in the depths. When he established the heights and balanced the fountains of waters; when he surrounded the sea with its boundary and placed a Law for the waters, lest they should pass their limits; when he laid the foundations of the earth, I was with him, composing all things." <note>original: Proverbs 8:27-30</note> Such is the power of this principle that no work of magic can be performed without Love. For by Love the contrary elements are joined together to constitute some good; according to the view that the elements and all other things were united in ancient chaos through friendship and love. 

Whence it pleased Anaxagoras <note>A pre-Socratic Greek philosopher</note> that all things were generated and corrupted through friendship and strife. For while there was a universal sympathy among all things, everything was one chaos; but while friendship of the same kind was tightened and corroborated, those parts were gathered together, and there appeared either an animal or some other such thing. But when that universal friendship made with all things was relaxed, these parts stood apart from those universal things and were united with their own kin. For Plato posited two Venuses, or two Loves, as he had recognized: that from right love all good things proceeded, and from distorted and oblique love all evils. 

As Pausanias <note>A character in Plato's *Symposium*</note> testifies in that same place: since Love is twofold, who would deny that Venus is twofold? One is indeed older and born in heaven without a mother, whom we call Heavenly <note>original: "coelestem"</note>; the other is younger, the progeny of Jupiter and Dione, whom we call Vulgar and Common <note>original: "vulgarem & communem"</note>. From one of these, every action of ours—which is otherwise indifferent—proceeds. For our action is good or bad only insofar as it is directed by a good or bad love. For that which is done with good and right love is honorable, and that which relies on oblique love is base and unseemly. 

Plato himself pursues this discourse there, which I leave to be read in its proper place. Of these two Venuses, the Academics <note>Followers of Plato's school</note> say one is Ethereal and the other is Aerial. The former is pure, chaste, and ordered, agreeing with Jupiter, connecting higher and divine things. The latter is disordered, slippery, varied, and lascivious, joining lower, animate things. About this Venus, so many obscene things are said by the poets; she is the cause of all evils, just as the other is the cause of all goods. Hence Augustine says: "Two loves made two cities: the regulated and good love of God and neighbor, even to the contempt of self, made the City of God; the love of self, even to the contempt of God, made the City of the Devil." <note>A reference to *The City of God*, Book 14</note> 

Whence Venus is so named by the grammarians because she "comes" <note>original: "veniat"</note> to all things, whether to do evil or good. As Orpheus sings in his hymns: "You generate all things that are in heaven and on earth, urging mortals and the immense race of beasts with raging love-potions" <term>philtris</term>. All things are filled with love, and nothing is void of it, just as all things are filled with air, which nature seeks to fill out of an abhorrence for a vacuum. For by love (says Boethius) the heavens are joined, and the elements agree in their established positions. 

By love animals dwell together; the city is preserved, and every Commonwealth <term>Respublica</term> receives its growth. By love, God fabricated and governs the world, because (according to Plato) the nature of the Good is to diffuse itself and to love. Hence Pherecydes of Syros said that God was transformed into Love so that he might create the World. Empedocles also says that the highest sphere is contained within intellectual love. And because God created out of love, he also contains all things through love, and demands love from us, so that being connected to one another by love, we may finally be united with Him, that all things may be one, as they were from the beginning. 

Indeed, of all the things he requires of us, the chief is love itself. Divine love (says Dionysius) <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian Neoplatonist</note> did not permit the King of all to remain within himself without offspring. And just as he diffuses himself into all things outside himself, so he delights to draw all things to himself through love—especially man, in whom all things are included. Therefore, when man is united to him, all things are. And Dionysius concludes all these things from the mind of Hierotheus, saying: "Love..."

<meta>This page continues the exploration of Love as a cosmic force, moving from the Platonic and ancient Greek interpretations of "Two Venuses" to a synthesis with Kabbalistic theology, specifically identifying these forces with the Sephirot Tiferet and Malkhut.</meta>

<header>ON THE KABBALISTIC DOCTRINES. 787</header>

Whether we call it Divine, or Angelic, or spiritual, or animal, or natural: let us understand it as a certain innate and mixing power, which indeed moves higher things toward the providence of lower things, reconciles equals to social communion with one another, and finally warns all lower things to turn themselves toward better and more sublime things. And because Love and Venus are sought in all things: therefore the Cypriots used to depict her with both sexes, with a long beard and yet in female clothing. And Ariphanes called her *Aphroditos* <note>original: "aphroditom" - a masculine form of the name</note>, not *Aphrodite*: because she is found in every sex and every soul. She is also called Lucifer <note>The morning star, literally "light-bringer"</note>, as if "bearing light," namely that of the Sun, or bringing us to the light itself; for this reason she is called Phosphorus <note>original: "phosphoros" - the Greek name for the morning star</note>. For we see that all things said of the dual Venus are found in the dual air, namely in this turbulent air and in the pure ether. For from here she leads toward offspring and marriages through the power of the spirit brooding upon it, which is an aerial power; whence both spirit and air, or wind, are called by the same name by those who name things according to their properties. However, the turbulent air is described in Juno <note>The Roman goddess of marriage and queen of the gods, associated here with the lower atmosphere</note> as hostile to the supreme Venus and to those who rejoice in her favor. But finally, Venus, by the protection of her Jupiter, prevails over the worse and hostile fortune. 

Truly, according to the Kabbalists, there are two Venuses: <term>Tiferet</term> <note>The Sephirah of Beauty, Harmony, and the Sun</note> and <term>Malkhut</term> <note>The Sephirah of Kingdom, the physical world, and the Moon</note>, which are called the "two loves," even if they are one love through reciprocity. Whence Solomon in the Song of Songs introduces the bridegroom <term>Tiferet</term> and the bride <term>Malkhut</term> speaking to one another, especially in those words:

> Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth: <note>original: "Osculetur me osculo oris sui" from Song of Songs 1:2</note>

which are the words of the bride <term>Malkhut</term> addressing <term>Tiferet</term> himself, asking that dimension to flow into her the gift of the Holy Spirit, or <term>Binah</term> <note>The Sephirah of Understanding</note>, which is called the "mouth of the Sephirot." And although those things which are inward are the same as God, and consequently always full of Divinity: nevertheless <term>Malkhut</term> cannot communicate the good influx—received from the higher dimensions—to created things unless this is commanded of her by those higher ones. And this happens when created things are well-ordered toward God through the observation of the commandments: therefore it is said in Deuteronomy: "Keep the commandments, and you shall abound in good," <note>original: Deuteronomy 28:1-11</note> namely in the influx of <term>Malkhut</term>; otherwise, you will be cursed in the city, in the field, etc. Whence in the Song of Songs, <term>Malkhut</term> complaining about the Synagogue, says:

> I am black. <note>original: "Nigra sum" from Song of Songs 1:5</note>

The Hebrew text has <term>שחורה</term> *Sechora*: which is the same as the dawn; and it comes from *Sechar*, which is called the dawn, which occurs when the light of the Sun begins to appear, the darkness having been expelled. Therefore the bride <term>Malkhut</term> compares herself to the dawn. When Solomon speaks of two loves, or of a dual love, he understands it as the bridegroom <term>Tiferet</term> and the bride <term>Malkhut</term>: the first is the super-mundane Sun always illuminating; the second is the Moon, which is a mirror not shining by itself. And when the *Knesset* <note>original: "chenezet" - meaning the assembly or congregation</note>, that is, the Synagogue of the Jews, or now the Church, conducts itself well toward God through the observation of the commandments: then the Moon-bride is illuminated through the good influx received from the Sun-bridegroom: and then she pours a good flow into the Synagogue then, and now into the Church. 

But when the aforementioned Synagogue behaved badly regarding the Law and the precepts, then the aforementioned bride would say: "My bridegroom looks at me with a stern eye, flowing into me bad influences, which I am forced to flow down into the Synagogue, showing myself as black by infusing evils: such as the captivity by the hands of Nebuchadnezzar and others." And this is the duty of a good and skilled judge: namely, to applaud good citizens, but to correct the wicked with a rod. Because of this, the bride says:

> I am black, namely to the wicked: but beautiful, namely to the good, among the children of Jerusalem.

The "children of Jerusalem" are our souls: therefore she complains, saying that such children are the cause of her blackness: that is, the privation of the good influx not received from her husband-Sun. They are also the cause why she is black against them by punishing them with scourges: therefore it follows: "Like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon." <note>original: Song of Songs 1:5</note> A "tent" is taken for a pavilion, which are multi-colored and have cracks through which things outside can be seen; so were the curtains of Solomon dyed with diverse colors. Therefore the curtains of Solomon are <term>Malkhut</term>, who exists full of many-colored influxes, which she uses toward created things according to their merits or demerits. And this is what our Savior says:

...who through his wisdom, disposed all things. As the wise man testifies, introducing divine wisdom <note>original: "inducē/uinam sapientiam" - likely *inducens divinam sapientiam*</note> speaking thus: "When he prepared the heavens (namely, I was present): when with a certain law and circle he walled in the depths. When the ether was established <note>original: "æther/bat" - likely *ether uegetabat* or *vibrabat*</note> above, and he balanced the fountains of waters: when he surrounded the sea with its boundary <note>original: "mar/ter" - likely *mari terminum*</note>, and set a Law for the waters, lest they should cross their limits: when he laid the foundations <note>original: "appe/fundamenta" - likely *appendebat fundamenta*</note> of the earth, with him I was composing all things." <note>This is a paraphrase of Proverbs 8:27-30, personifying Wisdom (Sophia) as a co-creator with God.</note> Of such great power is [Love] that no work of magic can be done without Love: for by Love the contrary elements are joined, so that they constitute some good thing: according to Plato, the elements and all other things were united in ancient chaos through friendship and love. Hence it pleased Anaxagoras <note>A pre-Socratic philosopher who proposed that "Mind" (Nous) acted upon a chaotic mixture of all things.</note> that through friendship and strife all things should be generated and destroyed: for while there was a universal friendship of all parts, all things were one chaos: but while the friendship of the same kind was tightened and strengthened, those parts were collected together, and there appeared either an animal, or something else of that sort: but when that universal friendship was relaxed, and made with all things, parts of this kind stood apart from those universals and were united with their own kin: for Plato established two Venuses, or Loves, which he had recognized: that from right love all good things proceeded: and from evil and crooked love all bad things: as Pausanias testifies in the same place <note>Referring to the speech of Pausanias in Plato's *Symposium*.</note> saying: since Love is twin, who would deny that Venus is twin? One Venus indeed is older, and born in heaven without a mother, whom we call Celestial: the other indeed is younger, begotten from Jupiter and Dione, whom we call Vulgar and Common. From one of these every action of ours, which is indifferent, proceeds; for our action is good or bad only insofar as it is directed by a good or bad love: for what is done by a good and right love is honorable, and what relies on crooked love is base and unseemly. Which Plato himself pursues at greater length in that place, which I leave to be read in its own location.

Of these two Venuses, the Academics <note>Followers of the Platonic school.</note> say one is ethereal, the other indeed aerial: the one is pure, chaste, ordered, agreeing with Jupiter, connecting higher, divine, and spiritual things: the lower is disordered, slippery, varied, and lascivious, joining animals and lower things. And concerning this Venus so many obscene things are said by the poets: because she is the cause of all evils, just as the other is of all goods. Hence Augustine says: "Two loves made two cities: the regulated and good love of God, and of neighbors, even to the contempt of oneself, made the city of God: but the inordinate love of self even to the contempt of God made the city of the Devil." <note>A famous distinction from Augustine’s *The City of God*.</note> Whence the power of this love is called Venus by the grammarians: because she "comes" <note>original: "ueniat"</note> to all things, namely evil and good. <note>The author is using a common Medieval etymological pun, linking *Venus* to the verb *venire* (to come).</note> Which Orpheus sings in his hymns: "You generate (he says) all things, whatever are in heaven and on earth, urging mortals, and the immense race of wild beasts with raging charms." And all things are filled with love: and nothing is empty of it, just as all things are filled with air: which fills the appetite of nature abhorring a vacuum.

For by Love (says Boethius) the heavens are joined, and the elements agree in their opposites. By Love animals live together: the city is preserved, and every Republic receives increase. By Love God fabricated and governs the world (according to Plato) because the nature of the good is to diffuse itself, and to love, as Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian Neoplatonist.</note> teaches. Hence Pherecydes of Syros said that God was transformed into love before he created the world. Empedocles also says: that the highest intelligible sphere is contained by love. And because God created out of love, he also embraces all things with love, and demands love from us, so that connected to one another by love, we may finally be united with him, so that all things may be one, as they were from the beginning. And the sum of all things which he requires from us is love itself. Divine love (says Dionysius) does not permit the King of all to remain in himself without offspring. And just as he diffuses himself into all things outside himself, so by love he delights to draw all things to himself, especially man, in whom all things are concluded: Therefore, when he is united, all things are united. # ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS.

Whether we call it Divine, Angelic, spiritual, animal, or natural: let us understand it as a certain innate and mixing power, which moves higher things to provide for the lower, reconciles equals to social communion with one another, and finally admonishes all lower things to be converted toward the better and more sublime. And because Love and Venus are sought in all things: therefore the Cyprians <note>Refers to the ancient inhabitants of Cyprus, a center for the cult of Aphrodite/Venus.</note> used to depict her with both sexes, indeed with a long beard but in female clothing. And Aristophanes called her *Aphroditos*, not *Aphrodite*: because this power is found in every sex and every soul. She is also called Lucifer, as if "bearing light" <note>original: "lucifer ... quasi ferens lucem"</note>, namely the light of the Sun, or bearing us to the light itself; therefore she is called Phosphorus <note>original: "phosphorus" — the Greek name for the morning star, literally "light-bringer."</note>.

For we see that all things said of the dual Venus are found in the dual air, namely in this turbulent air and in the pure ether. From here she leads to offspring and marriages through the power of the spirit brooding upon her, which is the true airy power; hence both spirit and air—or wind—are called by the same name by those who name things according to their properties. However, the turbulent air is described as Juno, who is hostile to the supreme Venus and to those who enjoy her favor. But finally, Venus, by the protection of her Jupiter, prevails over the worse and hostile fortune.

But according to the Kabbalists, there are two Venuses: <term>Tipheret</term> <note>Meaning "Beauty," the central Sephirah representing the Sun and the masculine principle.</note> and <term>Malchut</term> <note>Meaning "Kingdom," the final Sephirah representing the Moon, the Earth, and the feminine principle.</note>, which are called the "two loves," even if they are one love through reciprocity. Hence Solomon in the Song of Songs introduces the groom (Tipheret) and the bride (Malchut) speaking to one another, especially in those words: "Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth": which are the words of the bride Malchut addressing Tipheret itself, asking that dimension to flow into her the gift of the Holy Spirit, or <term>Binah</term> <note>Meaning "Understanding," a higher Sephirah often associated with the divine Mother or the source of the Holy Spirit.</note>, which is called the "mouth of the Sephirot." 

And although those things that are within are the same as God, and consequently always full of Divinity: nevertheless Malchut cannot communicate the good influence received from the higher dimensions to created things unless she is commanded to do so by them. And this happens when created things are well-ordered toward God through the observation of the commandments: therefore it says in Deuteronomy: "Keep the commandments, and you shall abound in good," namely in the influence of Malchut; otherwise, "you shall be cursed in the city, in the field, etc." 

Hence in the Song of Songs, Malchut, complaining about the synagogue, says: "I am black." The Hebrew text has <term>שחורה</term> *Shechorah*: which is the same as the dawn; and it comes from *Sechar* <note>original: "Sechar" — likely referring to the Hebrew *Shachar* (dawn). The author is connecting the word for "black" (*Shachor*) with the "dawn" (*Shachar*).</note>, which is called the dawn, which happens when the light of the Sun begins to appear after the darkness has been driven out. Therefore, the bride Malchut compares herself to the dawn. 

Therefore, when Solomon speaks of the two loves, or of the dual love: he understands it as the groom Tipheret and the bride Malchut: the first is the supra-mundane Sun, always illuminating; the second is the Moon, which is a mirror not shining by its own light. And when the <term>Chenezer</term> <note>original: "chenezer" — a Latinization of the Hebrew *Knesset Yisrael*, the Assembly or Community of Israel.</note>, that is, the synagogue of the Jews, or now the Church, conducts itself well toward God through the observation of the commandments: then the Moon-bride is illuminated through the good influence received from the Sun-groom: and then she pours out a good flow, formerly into the synagogue, but now into the Church. 

But when the aforementioned synagogue conducted itself poorly regarding the Law and the precepts, then the aforementioned bride said: "My groom looks at me with a grim eye, flowing into me bad influences, which I am forced to let flow into the synagogue, and to show myself as black by flowing in evils: such as the captivity by the hands of Nebuchadnezzar and others." And this is the duty of a good and skilled judge, namely to applaud good citizens, but to correct the bad ones with a rod. Because of this, the bride says: "I am black," namely to the wicked: "but beautiful," namely to the good, among the "daughters of Jerusalem." 

The "children of Jerusalem" are our souls: therefore she complains, saying that such children are the cause of her blackness: that is, the privation of the good influence not received from her husband, the Sun. They are also the cause why she is black against them by punishing them with lashes: therefore it follows: "Like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon." A tent is taken for a pavilion, which are multi-colored and have cracks through which things outside can be seen: thus the curtains of Solomon were dyed in various colors. Therefore, the curtains of Solomon are Malchut, who exists full of many-colored influences, which she uses toward created things according to their merits or demerits. (Do not gaze upon me because I am dark) <note>original: "rare quòd fusca sim", quoting Song of Songs 1:6</note> that is, sprinkled with the many various colors mentioned above. (The sun) <term>Tipheret</term> <note>The Sephirah of "Beauty," representing the masculine principle and the "Supramundane Sun."</note> my bridegroom (has discolored me) namely by pouring his influence into me and removing the good things from me. Hence the Psalm: *Your throne is like the Sun, and the Moon is always in my sight.* Therefore the bride herself says: (He has discolored me) he does not pour good light into me now, which is why I am filled with evil influences. And, in the <term>Kenezet Israèl</term> <note>Hebrew: "Knesset Yisrael," the Assembly or Community of Israel.</note>: that is, the synagogue, or the rulers and prelates, who through an evil end and a very bad example had corrupted their subjects.

And almost through the entire Song of Songs, this love is discussed—and not only in that song, but always through the entire Law. Confirming this, David says: *Once he spoke* <note>original: "Semel locutus est", quoting Psalm 62:11</note> namely to the whole Israelite people on Mount Sinai: *These two things I heard*, contained in that Law: because you are God, namely the one and true, and to you is the power, that is, you can demand good and evil influx upon us—to pour in good from the union of Tipheret with the female Malchut; but from their separation, evil. For if Israel worked well, it received that good influx; likewise, it suffered evil. And therefore it follows: *because you render to each according to his works.* For in the Archetypal World there is such an order that all good influences proceed from Tipheret; for he is the supramundane sun, in whose likeness the celestial Sun, a body in its own favor, pours life into lower things through the Moon by its influence and light. For the Moon is the mother of the planets, joining in herself the influences of the higher planets like a woman. Therefore, these two dimensions—when the commandments are observed and when we transgress the Law—one is separated from the other: that is, Tipheret does not flow into Malchut, clearly to our detriment; and then <term>Gheburah</term> <note>The Sephirah of "Severity" or "Judgment."</note> interposes itself, sending in anxieties and scourges. So beautifully Isaiah <note>The text attributes this to Isaiah, but it is actually Jeremiah 1:14.</note> says: *From the north, all evil shall be spread abroad* namely the evil of punishment; for Gheburah is the northern part.

The love of these two dimensions, therefore, is so that they may flow well into us. Also the love of the male and female in Scripture, which signifies the union of Israel and Tipheret; the prophet Hosea speaks of this union or dispensation, saying: *I will betroth you to me in faithfulness.* And in Ezekiel throughout: for God had claimed the Israelite people as His own peculiar treasure. God commanded the prophet Hosea to take a wife of harlotry and father children of harlotry. This was not done to the detriment of the Prophet, but for instruction, as Jerome feels, citing the praised Xenocrates, who made Polemon—who was devoted to luxury among female lute-players and flute-players, and coming among immodest women crowned with ivy—obey wisdom. They also extol Socrates, who transferred Phaedo from a brothel to the Academy. But omitting these, this was a type of Christ, who took the assembly of Gentile and Hebrew adulterers as his bride; which is supported by that word of Jeremiah: *But you have played the harlot with many lovers, yet return to me, and I will receive you.* And God commanded Hosea’s son to be called Israel, and his daughter <term>Lorechama</term> <note>Hebrew: "Lo-Ruhamah," meaning "Not Pitied" (Hosea 1:6).</note>. Indeed, this whole story is metaphorical and full of mysteries: for it holds the type of God, who first received the infamous synagogue which had played the harlot with many; afterward he received her as pure, from whom he received the son, Israel: that is, the seed of God, Christ Jesus, who through his human nature saved her who had been a harlot; and afterward the daughter Lorechama...

Hence, according to the Law, a priest—who must be immaculate—is not permitted to be joined to multiple women. Although it is permitted to others to avoid greater inconveniences, this is understood as the spiritual bride, of whom the carnal bride is a figure and a <term>sacrament</term> <note>In this context, a visible sign of an inward sacred mystery.</note>. This bride is one—namely, the Church—constituted from all those Queens, concubines, and young women.

Indeed, all are allotted the name of "females," and rightly so; for all of us, who are made fruitful by the face of God, and who in our working hold the lower and "feminine" position (while God holds the superior and "masculine" one), are deservedly called females in respect to God himself. Yet, in respect to the lower part, which is considered female, we hold the place of the male. Just as the heavens, in respect to the earth which is made fruitful by them, have a masculine character; but in respect to the angels and God, from whom they receive influence, they have a feminine character, as is written at length by the ancient theologians. By "concubines" and "young women," the households are also understood—not the free ones, but the servile. Speaking of these households, the Apostle says: *Abraham, the father of faith, had two sons: one by a bondwoman, who was born according to the flesh; and the other by a freewoman... which things are an allegory.* <note>Galatians 4:22-24</note> For these are the two testaments. By these are also understood the Gentiles, who committed fornication with foreign gods; but coming to Christ, they are admitted into the Church, which is called the "one dove" and the "one chosen by her mother above," gathering into one family the synagogue and the Gentile people.

And this was necessary. For Christ the Messiah was bound to raise up the seed of his brother Moses, who died without children of salvation; for through the Law no one was saved. He speaks, therefore, of Christ the Bridegroom and the Synagogue, whom Christ assumed to raise up the seed of his brother Moses, who died without the offspring of salvation; because through the Law of Moses no one was saved, as has been said elsewhere. ### THE COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS

...of Christ, who is located in Tipheret <term>Tipheret: The sixth emanation (Sephirah) on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing Beauty, balance, and the heart. Christian Kabbalists identified this Sephirah with Jesus Christ.</term>: as the beautiful one, perfecting all things: for from his fullness we have all received.

**KABBALISTIC DOGMA:** Whoever shall be joined with Tipheret at midnight, every generation shall prosper for him.

***FRIAR ARCHANGELUS***
The sacrament of marriage is indeed the greatest, so much so that when the creation was perfected and Adam was introduced into it as the high priest, a wedding was immediately celebrated. Marriage was ordained by God for our first parents; for when the man and woman were brought forth, it was said: *Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.* <note>Genesis 1:28</note> And again, where it treats the specific production of each spouse, after the name was formed from the dust of the earth, it is added: *It is not good for man to be alone: Let us make him a helper like unto himself.* <note>Genesis 2:18</note> But the Hebrew truth <note>original: "Hebraica ueritas," referring to the original Hebrew text of the Bible</note> has it: "one who may be in his sight," <note>Hebrew: "ezer k’negdo," literally "a helper against him" or "in his presence"</note> namely, for the purpose of producing children.

Recognizing this mystery, Paul said: *This is a great sacrament concerning Christ and the Church.* <note>Ephesians 5:32; many older translations use "sacrament" where modern ones use "mystery."</note> And just as Holy Scripture, having described the creation, first deals with marriage, in the same way it concludes with the sacrament of the wedding. Christ compared the whole arrangement of the kingdom of heaven to the wedding which a King made for his son. And John, closing all the mysteries of Holy Scripture in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>—into which he commands, under the threat of plagues, that nothing be added—says: *Let us be glad and rejoice, for the marriage of the Lamb is come: and his wife has prepared herself.* <note>Revelation 19:7</note> From this it is implied that no one can attain that eternal kingdom without regeneration, which is accomplished in this heavenly marriage through new and heavenly parents.

This position is not contradicted by that word of Christ, the bridegroom: *In heaven they shall neither marry, nor be given in marriage: but shall be like the Angels of God.* <note>Matthew 22:30</note> For the order of things is such that when the thing signified arrives, the sign ceases; and when the truth arrives, the symbolic figure ceases. Hence the Apostle, not ignorant of Gospel truth, when he was speaking specifically about marriage, said: *for the figure of this world passes away.* <note>1 Corinthians 7:31</note> For these carnal weddings are a figure and a sacrament of the true wedding celebrated in heaven. Therefore, when the true weddings arrive, this carnal coupling will cease.

And although Christ says: *What God has joined, let no man separate,* <note>Matthew 19:6</note> he does not mean by these words that carnal weddings would be celebrated in heaven. It is indeed decreed in heaven which spouse each person should have in carnal marriage—just as all things that happen in this world are decreed, whether concerning animals or plants. However, these plants or animals are not generated in heaven; in the same way, carnal marriages are decreed in heaven but celebrated on earth, as a sign and sacrament of the true wedding, as has been said.

And in this union, not only Israelites are regenerated, but also other men (as I said in the preceding conclusion), just as the Prophet sings: *In all nations, your salvation: therefore let all peoples confess to you.* <note>Psalm 67:2-3</note> And the Apostle asks: *Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also of the Gentiles?* And clearly afterward: *For there is one Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him.* <note>Romans 3:29, 10:12</note> To prove this, the Apostle himself brings forward that passage from Hosea: *I will call those who were not my people, 'my people.'* <note>Hosea 2:23; Romans 9:25</note> But God made those who were not his people his own because he regenerated them as his own people from those who were not, and made them his household and of the house of Israel. For "Israel" signifies an "heir of God," or "one who fights under God." <note>Traditional etymologies for the name Israel</note> Hence all those regenerated through Baptism can rightly be called the "house of Israel."

Now to the point: For the same John says again: *Blessed are they who are called to the marriage supper.* <note>Revelation 19:9</note> For the Lord and prince of that city, while he lived among humans, compared the kingdom of heaven and the sum of all human business to a wedding. Since, therefore, these most celebrated weddings of all are being conducted, let us see who the bridegroom is, and the bride, by what feasts, what contract, or what union they are perfected. The Bridegroom is Tipheret, the super-mundane Sun, Christ; who, speaking of himself, says: *The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding for his son,* who is Christ. The Bride is any soul consenting to this contract; and consequently, the Church and the gathering of the faithful is the bride, of whom Hosea says: *I will betroth you to me*

...faith: weddings are the gifts brought to the bride, which were the greatest of all. From his fullness, everyone has received; for he has earned grace and glory for all. He covers the nakedness of all, and he is able to give to all souls that from which they may conceive and bring forth the fruits of good works, as Paul testifies: *God is able to make all grace abound in you, so that you may abound in every good work.* <note>2 Corinthians 9:8</note> These weddings were initiated through the Holy Spirit. With the Spirit himself dictating, God invites us so many times through the Prophets to this contract, according to that word of Hosea: *I will betroth you to me forever* (as mentioned above); *I will betroth you to me in justice and judgment, in mercy and compassion.* <note>Hosea 2:19</note> For in the Law of Moses, the stern bridegroom betrothed in judgment and justice—which is <term>Gheburah: The Sephirah of Strength, Severity, or Judgment on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.</term>—but in the Law of the Gospel, he betrothed in mercy, piety, and grace—which are <term>Ghedulah: Also known as Chesed, the Sephirah of Greatness, Mercy, or Loving-kindness.</term> and <term>Chesed: The Sephirah of Mercy or Loving-kindness, often synonymous with Ghedulah.</term>—showing himself merciful and kind in the Messiah.

And for the making of this union, the middle of the night is a very opportune time. Note that the natural night contains twelve hours and four watches; this is clear in the Gospel: *if he comes in the first watch,* etc. <note>Luke 12:38</note> For each watch has three hours; the same may be said of the day. In every watch, whether of the night or the day, the guards of the Angels are changed. Hence it is said: *Upon your walls, O Jerusalem, I have set watchmen.* <note>Isaiah 62:6</note> The Prophet speaks here of the watchmen placed upon the walls of the lower Jerusalem, as some assert. It is also understood through allegory as the Church of God, upon whose walls and bulwarks God himself has placed not only pastors and bishops, but Angels—just as John teaches us when writing to the seven Angels of the seven Churches of Asia, who were given for the protection of both the Churches and the Bishops presiding over them. And because this Church is distributed into twelve principal portions—by which both the ancient family <note>The twelve tribes of Israel</note> and heaven itself are divided:

Hence (as John himself provides at the end of his vision), the names of the twelve Angels were on the twelve gates of the heavenly Jerusalem descending from heaven, surely guarding the city from attackers, so that no greater trouble is introduced from the outside than the citizens enclosed within can bear. *For God is faithful, who does not suffer you to be tempted beyond that which you are able.* <note>1 Corinthians 10:13</note> And these guards defend by the power of the Emperor triumphing on the cross, just as the Apostle himself suggests, saying: *Thanks be to God, who has given us the victory through Jesus Christ our Lord.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:57</note>

And those guardian Angels, because they are assigned from midday until the middle of the night, are terrifying; they are called the "night horrors" that trouble the soul, and therefore they are called the "powers of darkness" opposing us. For between them and us, enmity was placed by God, and they disturb us. Just as from the innate enmity between the lamb and the wolf (as I said above), the mere approach of the wolf—even if not seen—terrifies the lamb. Powers of this kind truly thrive in the night and in darkness. Hence the Psalmist sings, saying: *You have appointed darkness, and it has become night; in it, all the beasts of the forest shall pass through: the lion cubs roaring to seize and seek their food for themselves.* <note>Psalm 104:20-21</note> And because they are enemies of the light, there follows: *The sun has risen, and they are gathered together, and they shall be placed in their dens.* <note>Psalm 104:22</note> Job supports this when he says: *They were rebels against the light.* <note>Job 24:13</note> And again: *If the dawn suddenly appears, they think of the shadow of death, and they walk in darkness as if in light.* <note>Job 24:17</note>

Similarly, even those good guardian Angels from midday until the middle of the night are terrifying, as I said. Because of this, from midday until morning, there is more fear than before. These are the Angels assigned to <term>Gheburah: Judgment/Severity</term>. However, those who are assigned from midnight until midday are benevolent and merciful, coming forth from the southern <term>Ghedulah: Mercy/Greatness</term>, offering our prayers before God. At such an hour, the <term>Zohar: The "Book of Splendor," the foundational text of Jewish Kabbalah.</term> says that God descends into Paradise, shows himself to the holy ones, and confers any graces whatsoever to those who ask. This is clear through Solomon, who says: *While all things held a middle silence, and the night in her course was at its midpoint, your almighty word came from your royal throne* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 18:14-15</note>—namely, to the holy ones. The influences of the heavens of the Archetypal World <note>The original, divine blueprint of the universe</note> are then opened, and then we easily attain graces. Therefore, David used to rise in the middle of the night to obtain grace, which is shown by that which...

The Kabbalists also say that he who knows his wife at such an hour (especially at the midpoint of the night on Friday as the Sabbath arrives, and not otherwise) will have a prosperous generation. Such people will never lack offspring, and they will procreate good sons (as they say). These are called <term>Eunuchs: Here used metaphorically for those who exercise spiritual discipline or "castrate" their worldly desires to focus on the Divine.</term>, to whom God promises not only sons but also temporal goods. The same may be said of anyone who, through prayer, clings to God in the middle of the night.

FRATER ARCHANGELUS. In Exodus 6 it is said: *I am the Tetragrammaton, and I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El Shaddai, but my name, the Tetragrammaton, I did not make known to them.* <note>Exodus 6:2-3. The Tetragrammaton refers to the four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> By this alone is His name called "ineffable" <note>Unspeakable or beyond description</note>, because this belongs only to the Supreme God, insofar as He is none of the things that exist, but is above all things, having no regard for anything outside of Himself. Other names are descriptive of other properties and relations, such as *Shaddai*. The Latins translated this as "Almighty," but in Hebrew it is more aptly signified as: "Self-Sufficient," content in Himself, and lacking nothing. *Shaddai* is therefore a name of God that terrifies demons, and it occurs frequently in the sacred writings. Speaking of this name, Rabbi Moses Maimonides in the book *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "Hannebochim", a Latinized form of the Hebrew "Moreh Nevukhim"</note> says: the name *Shaddai* <note>שדי</note> is composed of the relative particle *She* <note>ש</note>, which means "who," and the word *Dai* <note>די</note>, which signifies "sufficiency." Therefore *Shaddai* is the same as *Asher Dai*: that is, "He who is sufficient" or "He who suffices." For this reason, this name is never found among the Hebrews used for anyone except God alone. This is not surprising, since it is suited only to Him who is self-sufficient, or who is sufficiency itself—which perhaps is most fitting for Him. As David says: *I said to my Lord, you are my God, for you do not need my goods.* <note>Psalm 16:2</note> All other things need the support of another, or of God. Whence the philosopher <term>Algazel: Al-Ghazali, a major Persian theologian and philosopher.</term>, in the book titled *On the Names of God*, says: God alone is simply and absolutely wealthy and the giver of wealth. For He depends on no other, neither in substance nor in qualities, but with all things pertaining to Him, He is entirely free from all dependency. Then he concludes: "He is thus absolutely wealthy and self-sufficient in truth, who needs no other; and this is God alone." Of all others, this is said only metaphorically or in a limited sense. Thus far Algazel. 

And this name *Shaddai*, etc. Aristotle in the 7th book of the *Politics* says: With God as witness, happiness is not in external things, because He is happy without anything outside Himself, since He has all things from Himself. <term>Albertus Magnus: A medieval German Dominican friar and philosopher.</term> says: there is no true "being" except His, who said: *He Who Is sent me to you.* <note>Exodus 3:14</note> For that being is from itself and through itself; all other things are neither from themselves nor through themselves, but only exist insofar as they participate in His being. Many believe that in this sense the antiquity of the Egyptians fashioned the inscription on the robe of Pallas <note>Likely referring to the Temple of Isis at Sais, where the inscription "I am all that has been, and is, and shall be" was found.</note>: "Pallas is all that was, is, and will be, and whatever you see; whose veil no wise man has ever lifted." It is feared, because that being of His is infinite, diffused throughout and yet enclosed in particular things, by which—as if by certain veils—He is hidden so that He cannot be grasped. Of which Isaiah says: *I fill heaven and earth.* <note>Jeremiah 23:24, though here attributed to Isaiah.</note> Therefore He needs nothing. And this name *Shaddai* is one of the ten principal surnames of the Tetragrammaton. And every Psalm has one of the surnames of the Tetragrammaton favoring that Psalm; and *Shaddai* favors that Psalm: *He who dwells in the help of the Most High* <note>Psalm 91</note>; hence...

# ON KABBALISTIC DOGMAS

### Yy 3

...that this Psalm terrifies Demons. No one should ignore that the name **Shaddai** [שדי] has three letters, noted in Hebrew (as seen above), which with the addition of vowel points make **Shaddai** [שדי] <note>original: "sadai"</note>. By rearranging the letters in this way, **Shid** [שיד] <note>Hebrew for a type of demon or spirit</note>, it composes the name of the Devil; for that is the Chaldean name signifying a Demon. This is explained in another way, but first, it must be noted that Hebrew numbers are twofold: namely, the "major" and the "minor." The first arises from the individual values of all the specific letters of a word, so that it is their total sum. Thus, in this name **Shaddai**, the major number is 314 <note>Shin (300) + Daleth (4) + Yod (10) = 314</note>. The other is the minor number, also called the "unequal" number: this takes one unit from every hundred and one unit from every ten, leaving any number less than ten as it is. In this way, **Shaddai** [שדי] signifies 8, because the letter *Shin* [ש] yields 300—and thus in the minor number gives 3 by taking one for each hundred—the *Daleth* [ד] gives 4 and remains whole, and the *Yod* [י] signifies ten, from which one unit is taken. Thus, their sum will be 8, and such is called the minor number. Similarly, **Satan** <note>OCR reads "fathan," a common misreading of the long 's' in "Sathan"</note> [שטן] and the name **Y-H-W-H** [יהוה] <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> yield the same minor number in this way: **Satan** [שטן], *Shin* [ש] 300, *Teth* [ט] 9, *Nun* [ן] 50, which all yield the minor number 17 <note>3 + 9 + 5 = 17</note>. **Yod He Waw He** [יהוה], 10, 5, 6, 5, which all yield the minor number 17 <note>1 + 5 + 6 + 5 = 17</note>, as I said above.

FRIAR ARCHANGELUS: For the Moon is the last of the planets, closing and completing their arrangements. She is numbered in the first place among the planets when starting from below, and she is called a more principal planet than others. She arranges all these lower things, for all the planets flow into her as the final recipient of all the influences from above, to be communicated to the lower realms. She governs various things, being placed in different signs, so that by always being varied, she produces various effects. Through frequent conjunctions with the planets and other stars, she becomes as a "wife" to them all to receive their qualities; as the mother of all lower things and the mediator between both—namely, the higher and the lower—she communicates with all of them. And although she is the last planet, she nevertheless communicates with the higher ones, especially the Sun. As often as she is joined to the Sun, she is filled with offspring and life-giving power, which she pours into the moistened and prepared lower things. From her, the series of things also begins in the celestial realms, which Plato calls the "chain" <note>The Great Chain of Being</note>, by which every single thing or cause is connected to another. Everything depends on her until one arrives at the supreme cause of all, from whom everything comes. 

As to why she is called the "greater" planet, we say this is according to observation: because the decrees of the Moon are more closely attended to than those of other planets. This is either because of the familiarity she has with us, or because she appears larger than others (aside from the Sun), or because she is more varied in her motion, or because she is the receptacle of all other influences (as I said), or because her motion is more perceptible to the common people (as Ptolemy says) and also to the wise who claim this doctrine for themselves. But the more prudent also look to the decrees of other stars, forecasting from their aspects longer winters, powerful and lasting winds, snows, hails, and such things. These are distinguished from the various aspects of the fixed stars and the wandering stars <note>The planets</note>, whether those effects proceed from the stars themselves, or from the presiding intelligences, or from God commanding that they execute and signify those things—or as if they compel as instruments. 

Nevertheless, the Moon principally concurs. Thus the "God-bearing Moon," which is called <term>Malchut: "Kingdom," the tenth and final Sephirah, representing the physical world and the manifest presence of God.</term> by the more secret theologians, is the last among the Archetypal planets, closing and completing their arrangements. She is numbered first in the Sephirotic order when beginning from below. For this reason, she is said to be a more powerful <term>Sephirah: One of the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah.</term>, or <term>Midah: A divine "measure" or attribute.</term>, or enumeration, or property, or attribute, or "day of creation," or planet, than the other dimensions. For she arranges all these lower things; for the higher <term>Sephirot: The plural of Sephirah; the ten divine powers.</term> flow down into her, and she into created things... <meta>catchword: multi- (the next word is 'multiformis' or 'manifold')</meta>

# COMMENTARY BY ARCHANGELUS

...producing many kinds of effects: for she follows their characters when she meets and is joined with them; she is indeed the "wife" of all the Divine names—not only of these, but also of the surnames and additional titles, which are finite, or rather countless, just like the stars of heaven. She mediates between the higher and lower things, namely between God and created beings, between the archetypal patterns and the Angels, and between us and the heavens—and even between us and the Angels—by sharing the influence received from those above her. 

Although she is impregnated by all the celestial beings (as I said), it is especially by the Sun, who is called the male and her husband, whom the Hebrews call **Tipheret** <term>Tipheret: The sixth Sephirah, meaning "Beauty," often associated with the Sun and the harmonious balancing of the divine realm</term>. He, when joined with her, brings her to life. And this is what Isaiah says in the person of God: *Shall I, who make others bring forth, be myself barren?* <note>original: "nunquid ego qui aliis parere facio, ipse sterilis ero?" Reference to Isaiah 66:9</note>. She then shares this offspring with created things that have been moistened by grace. For the series of things in the archetypal influences begins from her: a chain arises because all the Divine influences are gathered together within her. By these influences, those who adhere to the supreme cause, the **Ensoph** <term>Ein Sof: The Infinite, the unknowable Godhead before emanation</term>, are able to descend to the lowest level. 

And so **Malchut** <term>Malchut: The tenth and final Sephirah, "Kingdom," representing the physical world and the presence of God in creation</term> is called the "first" **Sephirah** <note>She is considered "first" when counting upwards from our material world</note>. She is an archetypal planet more than the other Sephirot because she acts more closely with us than the others; even though she receives influence from higher dimensions, she receives the light of good influence most greatly from the sun, **Tipheret**. And because she receives "seed" from all the Sephirot, she is the spouse of them all. 

Thus, if the influence flows from the "right side," she sends down peaceful rains upon us; if from the "left side," the opposite. For this reason, she is more varied in her movement—that is, in her effects—than the other higher beings. Not only is the archetypal Moon, **Malchut**, made fruitful by the proper names called the "ten enumerations" <note>The ten Sephirot</note>, but also when she meets with other additional titles that are not determined by number. These are called "stars" by reason of the multitude and clarity of their influences. Therefore, the Moon is not improperly called "another Sun" by some: for those things which the Sun generates above by a masculine power, she receives—along with the offspring of the other planets—and bestows upon the lower world, which is subject to her. 

For this reason, her movement is observed more than the others, as if she were giving birth to the concepts of all things. From **Mercury**, she receives the power that mixes the humors; from **Venus**, that which leads to forms suitable for birth; from **Mars**, strength and spirit; from **Jupiter**, the natural spirit and the nourishment of all things; from **Saturn**, structure and stability. But from the **Sun**, who contains every kind of power (as all astronomers assert), she receives every kind of offspring and light. All of these she unfolds in various ways, according to her own changing temperament, her cycle, and her different alignments, both with the planets and with other stars. Now she is at her peak, now she is lacking, now she is distant at the edge of her orbit; now full of light, now halved, now she is scarcely seen, and later she is entirely hidden. 

Therefore, it is not without reason that the supreme Moon, called **Malchut**, is compared to her: she draws from the celestial fountains through derived channels and bestows these gifts on lower things according to the readiness of those who receive them. Although she receives from all the Sephirot, she does so most powerfully from the Sun: as often as she is joined to him, she is filled with offspring and life-giving power, which she pours into the moistened and well-prepared lower beings. Every single thing also depends on her until one reaches the supreme cause of all, **Binah** <term>Binah: "Understanding," the third Sephirah</term> or **Chesed** <term>Chesed: "Mercy" or "Kindness," the fourth Sephirah</term>. 

**Malchut** is the "Gate of Entry" to the Sephirot: she does not shine with a good influence of her own, except for what she takes from those above. Therefore, when deprived of their influence, she is called "Night." For just as the planet Moon does not shine of itself unless it is looked upon by the Sun, so the super-worldly Moon, **Malchut**, does not shine with good influence unless she is beheld by **Tipheret** in the archetype. This will happen especially after the Judgment, of which the Psalms say: *And the night* (namely, Malchut) *shall be illuminated like the day* <note>original: "Et nox... sicut dies... illuminabitur" from Psalm 139:12</note>; that is, **Malchut** will be illuminated by **Tipheret** himself with as much light as **Tipheret** now possesses. Then **Malchut** will be free from evil influences. Whence Isaiah says: *The light of the Moon* (namely, Malchut) *shall be as the light of the Sun* (that is, Tipheret), *and the light of the Sun, Tipheret, shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days* <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>. That is, the light of **Tipheret** shall be like the light...

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS
795

**Sephirot**: which are called "days," by reason of the Divine light existing within them. The Sun is celestial fire, as Plato says, cooking <note>original: "decoquens"; here meaning a process of refining, maturing, or digesting through heat</note> all things that pertain to the nourishment of the "great animal" <note>A Neoplatonic term for the universe itself, seen as a living, breathing entity</note>. He was called **Apollo** (as the Platonist Speusippus <note>A nephew of Plato and head of the Academy</note> prefers) because he is the "sole container" <note>Speusippus likely derived Apollo from the Greek "a-pollon," meaning "not many," implying unity</note>; nor do the conjunctions of the stars bring about their effects until they are impregnated by the seed of **Phoebus** <term>Phoebus: A common epithet for Apollo, meaning "bright" or "radiant"</term>. To him the cock—who ensures that the eggs of hens are fertile—is also dedicated. Hence Chrysippus <note>A Stoic philosopher</note> was of the opinion that Apollo is named from *a* (which means "without") and *poly* ("multitude"), as if he alone were the one containing the power of the heavens and the stars. For this reason, the Latins call him **Sol**, as if he were "shining alone" <note>original: "solum lucentem"</note>. And the Assyrians call him **Adad**, which in their language signifies "alone."

The Hebrews, however, call him <term>shemesh</term> <term>שמש</term>, which can be interpreted as "proper" or "his own," because his light and its benefit belong uniquely to him. Other stars, however, have both light and benefit imparted to them by him; and he shines so much more excellently as that celestial fire is more sublime than this elementary fire [on earth]. Both provide heat, but the celestial fire does so by driving inward, reaching even the most remote places, so that the power of its rays penetrates into the bowels of the earth: by this power, he "cooks" and perfects the metals, which this elementary fire afterwards purges. He was also called **Vulcan** <note>The Roman god of fire and smithing</note> from his greater fiery force and violence; or because he is *canus*—that is, white/hoary—as he flies in the flame. But that celestial one is called **Phoebus** from his appearance and splendor, whence the Ancients fashioned him as the most beautiful of all.

Furthermore, they called him the inventor of medicine, because of his life-giving heat and beneficial power. That Sun, or celestial fire, puts to flight lions, wolves, and every wild thing hostile to us; also, through the meeting of rays and "aspects" <note>The angular relationships between planets in astrology</note>, when the stars and those images [the zodiac] agree in a certain peculiar harmonious assembly, many things are brought about in the elements. And the power of all these is sown through the Sun, as if through the true "cock of heaven," who pours out both the general power of life and the seeds of particular virtues. The stars, having been impregnated by his seed—especially the Moon—pour out the offspring upon us in their proper time, acting like a womb <note>original: "matrix"</note>. She is the mother, not only of the Sun’s influence, but also of the other planets (as I said above), from all of whom she receives seed and influxes from the higher realms and grants them to us as a domestic mother.

We can recognize this in the "Minor World" <note>The Microcosm, or the human being</note>. For in the heart of man, which holds the image and power of the Sun, is the source of common life and the virtue of all the members of the whole body. For all things that are in the body receive nourishment from the heart, as well as the power of life and motion which passes from the heart to the brain (which is Lunar), and from there is spread to all members of the body through the veins and nerves descending from it. And if man receives favor from the whole of heaven, he draws it most especially from the "Heart of Heaven," which is the Sun, since man is "Solar" (as the Arabian astronomers say) and enjoys this privilege by a certain peculiar gift.

All these things agree with the archetypal and Divine Sun, who "cooks" the food not only of the Great World [the Universe] but also of the Minor World, namely man, who according to the theology of the Hebrews is decorated by the influx of both Suns. This is shown by his beautiful and upright stature, his subtle humor, his clear spirit, his preeminent imagination, and his zeal for truth and glory; in many things man possesses a symbol of both Suns, and a peculiar image of Him—the more perfect he is, the more clearly it is expressed.

Hence **Christ**, the prince and head of men, is called "the Sun" in many places; from the fullness of his light, life, and all good things (as John says) we have all received. We also draw from other planets and stars, but by the power of the Sun, who nourishes them with his own seed or power. Just so, in His mystical body, we receive from other members by His power—for those members are like stars in the great mystical body, as Daniel and Paul testify. And the Divine Sun consists of many fires—that is, of the influxes of many archetypal stars. These manifold divine stars cannot bring their effects to pass without the seed and influx of this Sun. Since he is the <term>tetragrammaton</term> <term>יהוה: The four-letter name of God, YHWH</term>, from which his twelve <term>avayot</term> <term>Avayot: Permutations of the name YHWH, often associated with the twelve signs of the zodiac or months</term> hang. For this reason, he can be called Apollo: that is, containing the power of all divine measures; for all divine names and surnames...

# COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS
796

<note>original: "uina à tetrag. pendent"</note> Divine things hang from the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note> (as has been shown) over that Sun. Therefore, he alone shines; that is, the light of a good influx is his own property. And he warms all things—both aquatic, human, and Angelic, both far and near—to such an extent that he exceeds them in his dependence. Hence he can be called **Vulcan**, by the greater of his powers <note>Archangelus associates the Sun with the Roman god of fire, Vulcan, to emphasize its transformative heat</note>. For this reason, he is called white, because he flies, being ready in his influence and swiftness. Wherefore he is called most beautiful, through whom all things are beautiful: even leading the soul from deformity to conformity by giving it life and blessing it. He puts to flight the light of that lion <note>Refers to the demonic forces often symbolized by a devouring lion</note>, and whichever Diabolical beasts infest us, as **David** sings: *The Sun has risen and they are gathered together, and they shall lie down in their dens* <note>Psalm 104:22</note>. Yet he even provides food for them out of his beneficence. Whence it follows: *The young lions*—that is, the demons—*roar and seek their food from him.* If many things occur in these lower regions by the gathering of archetypal virtues, it is never without the gathering of this Sun. Impregnated by his virtue, the stars—and most especially the Moon, <term>Malchut</term> <note>The tenth Sephirah, representing the physical world or the "Kingdom"</note>—pour forth their offspring upon us, like a mother of all effects produced by the assembly of the celestial stars. These things, however, are principally accomplished by <term>Tipheret</term> <note>The sixth Sephirah, "Beauty," associated with the Sun and the heart of the Sephirotic tree</note>, the Sun, as if from the heart and fountain of all things; for they receive from him the nourishment of life and the power of motion.

The conclusion therefore says: *Let the light of the non-shining mirror be made*—that is, the Moon or <term>Malchut</term>—*like the light of the shining mirror*—that is, <term>Tipheret</term>. *Then the night*—that is, <term>Malchut</term>, which does not shine of itself—*will be as the day*—that is, like the other <term>Sephirôt</term> <note>The ten emanations of God in Kabbalah</note>. For then the night shall be illuminated like the day; specifically, <term>Tipheret</term> will be there, and <term>Malchut</term> also, and every other created thing will be illuminated by this light on the day of judgment. But most especially all humans will be, provided they are not wrapped in the darkness of sins so that they cannot grasp that light. Indeed, the more one is disposed toward it, the more one is drenched in that light, as the Light itself testifies concerning **John the Baptist**, saying: *He was a burning and shining lamp* <note>John 5:35</note>. But that true light burned and shone much more; to which John, returning the favor of his testimony, said: *He shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit* <note>Matthew 3:11</note>, who is truly the light by which the Lamb illuminates the church triumphant, which lacks all darkness, as John says: *And there was no night there, because its lamp was the Lamb* <note>Revelation 21:23; 22:5</note>.

### BROTHER ARCHANGELUS
Not only are those things true regarding the suitability of man with the heavens for receiving health from them, but also regarding the utility derived from them so that we may become better. For humans receive from the heavens that which composes their various characters and lives, as all astronomers affirm, decreeing this man to be benign because of **Jupiter**, that one impetuous from **Mars**, another splendid from the **Sun**, and many things of this kind. We also receive great power from the assembly of the heavens, which disposes us to harmonize our characters, unless by our evil disposition we turn that harmony into a clattering noise. For light is drawn from the celestial bodies, which puts to flight the darkness and those who do evil. This light possesses a certain image and vehicle of the divinity and of that light which says: *I am the light of the World; while you have the light, walk in the light, lest the darkness* (the Demons) *overtake you* <note>John 8:12; 12:35</note>. 

Demons are properly divided into two kinds (according to **Porphyry** and **Proclus** <note>Neoplatonic philosophers who wrote extensively on the nature of spirits and the soul</note>). One is the genus of substantial and intellectual souls of Demons. The other is a genus of material powers; and these are the animal appetites always warring against the spirit. Hence they can be called **Satans**, which means "adversaries," as the Apostle clearly reports: *The flesh,* he says, *lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh* <note>Galatians 5:17</note>. For these are opposed to each other. These forces, or animal appetites, **Paul** elsewhere calls the "Law of the members," saying: *I see another Law in my members, fighting against the Law of my mind* <note>Romans 7:23</note>. This we have not only from him, but from **Plato**, Porphyry, and Proclus, especially where they treat the soul and the Demon. There are also good Demons <note>In the Greek sense of 'daimon,' meaning a guiding spirit or lesser divinity, not necessarily evil</note>. For a wise Demon...

According to our theologians, there are many kinds of demons: but **Michael Psellus** <note>A 11th-century Byzantine monk and philosopher known for his work on demonology</note>, following the thought of **Plato**, **Porphyry**, and **Proclus**, reduces them to four primary kinds: namely, the earthly, the watery, the airy, and the fiery. For the earthly ones oppose us through the flesh; the watery through the blood mixed with phlegm; the airy through a spirit of swelling pride; and the fiery ones precipitate us into ruin through boiling and inflamed anger. There are also some who are of the East, others of the West, others of the South, and others of the North. Of these, the first group tempt through divinations; the following ones through despair; the third through an excessive confidence which they have in the goodness of God; while the Northern ones strive to turn mortals away from God through rebellion, to their own destruction. For they have become such a "bad tree" that they can produce nothing but bad effects or fruit; for *a bad tree cannot produce good fruit* <note>original: "non enim potest arbor mala bonos fructus facere"; a reference to Matthew 7:18</note> (according to the truth of Christ). Gathering these various deceits together, **Pope Leo** says: "The ancient enemy does not cease to extend the snares of temptation everywhere, so that he might corrupt the faith of believers. For he knows to whom he should offer the allurements of the flesh, into whom he should pour the poison of envy, for whom he should set the incitements of luxury. He knows whom he may trouble with sorrow, whom he may deceive with joy, whom he may oppress with fear, and whom he may seduce with wonder.
