And just as the princes of darkness become stronger in the darkness itself (as I have said), so also the **Angels of light**, who favor us, receive increases of strength from light—not only divine light, but also solar and celestial light. Through this light, that divine and supreme light, shining forth, pours a certain virtue into the heavens, and through them into the lower regions. For from the *Father of Lights*, from whom every best gift comes <note>James 1:17</note>, proceeds being, motion, generation, and every working virtue, both in the heavens and in the elements, plants, animals, and humans. But all those things receive a certain nourishment through the heavens, as if through media and instruments; these are called "natural gifts." This light of the Sun puts to flight the dark princes and their troops; whence it is said in **Job**: *When they see the Dawn, they think it the shadow of death* <note>Job 24:17</note>. And, just as the night, being deprived of light, favors them so that they are more powerful, so the light weakens them so that they lose their strength. Demons prevail more in the night than in the day because they are from the "left" <note>In many mystical traditions, the "left side" represents the attribute of Judgment or the source of harsh/dark forces</note> and darker side. Whence the **Apostle** calls them "the powers of darkness," and **Christ**, speaking to those incited by them to his death, said: *This is your hour and the power of darkness* <note>Luke 22:53</note>. Whence it is necessary that they flee to the shadows, and when the light (which is hostile to them) recedes, they prevail somewhat. This is evident in the case of the "evil Angel" wrestling with **Jacob**, who, as the Dawn approached, said: *Let me go, for the Dawn is rising* <note>Genesis 32:26</note>. He was being overcome by Jacob as the shining Dawn arrived. Therefore the **Psalm** says: *You have appointed darkness, and it has become night; in it all the beasts of the field shall pass through: the young lions roaring that they may seek their food for themselves* <note>Psalm 104:20-21</note>. Of whom **Peter** says: *Your adversary the Devil, like a roaring lion, goes about seeking whom he may devour* <note>1 Peter 5:8</note>. Afterward **David** adds: *The Sun has risen, and they are gathered together* <note>Psalm 104:22</note>; for (as I said) they lose their strength. It follows: *Man shall go forth to his work*; for then demons do not have such great power to harm men in the light as they do in the night. Toward this light and splendor (according to **Zoroaster** <note>Often cited in Renaissance texts as a source of "Ancient Theology" or Prisca Theologia</note>), one must hasten. In the **Angels**, it is a glowing intelligence and a poured-out joy. In **Man**, it is the clear course of reason. In the **Heavens**, it is visible splendor. In **Fire**, it is vital vigor. In transparent bodies, it is color. In dark bodies, it is a certain beneficial and generative power. They taught that public prayers and Psalm-singing should be done with lit candles. And God, to whom these sacred rites are offered, requires this—namely, that all sacrifices be offered with light, and that on the altar, that which shines should always burn.

**KABBALISTIC DOGMA.** Although there may be a manifold coordination of "chariots" <note>The "Merkabah" or Divine Chariot in Kabbalistic mysticism</note>: nevertheless, as far as pertains to the mystery of the *phylateria* <note>Phylacteries or "Tefillin," the ritual prayer boxes worn by Jews</note> there are two chariots to be arranged, so that from 2, 3, 4, & 5 one chariot is made: and these are the four phylacteries which the letter *Vau* <note>The third letter of the Tetragrammaton, often associated with the "Son" or the six central Sephirot</note> puts on. # ARCHANGELUS’S COMMENTARY

[...the robe has] seventy-two bells and seventy-two pomegranates, which signify the seventy-two nations and languages that were divided at the building of the Tower of Babel. These served as a sign for the high priest, so that he might first offer a sacrifice for the people, symbolized by those twelve stones resting upon his breast; then he was obliged to offer it for the seventy-two nations. And if, by chance, it happened that the people of Israel were not found worthy because of their sins, while that divine influence was still active, such a prayer would pass to the seventy-two nations and benefit them. This is why the nations have many times prevailed against Israel. The high priest, therefore, wore these aforementioned stones, as well as the pomegranates and bells, so that he might be more mindful and more effectively moved to pray for them.

I have spoken of the planets having a cross; for this reason, images of the Crucified One and of other saints are permitted, so that their merits and the benefits shown to us might be remembered, and that our heart might be lifted up toward Him. For it is very fitting to offer help to the spirit through the senses. Indeed, Christ taught us this: in performing miracles, He utilized the aid of nature. This is evident in the water which He converted into wine at the wedding feast <note>The Wedding at Cana, John 2:1–11</note>; for that matter was already disposed to take on that form. Christ did this, not because He could not produce wine unless the matter of water was supplied—since He made the world out of nothing (according to that saying of **John**: <note>original: "omnia per ipsum facta sunt"</note> all things were made through Him)—but He could also have made wine without water. He did it, therefore, to signify (as He did elsewhere) that He, the author of nature, always uses natural means or causes as long as nature supports Him.

From this principle, even for the purpose of instructing the eyes of the man born blind, He took dust to make clay—from which the entire first human body was also fashioned. So too, in providing us with the Divine food and drink, He took bread and wine. From this we are taught that miracles are not to be sought where nature can provide help, because that is to abuse divine power, and to give way to curiosity or vain glory for one who desires miracles without necessity. Therefore, Christ rightly ordered those water-pots to be filled with water because, as we have said, water is the closest matter to wine. For wine is nothing other than water distilled through the vine. Thus, the form was introduced into a matter already prepared, without a great departure from the natural process. There are, however, other mysteries <note>original: "sacramenta"</note> included here which I will leave aside for now. Likewise, in the sacrament of the altar, water is added to the wine, which is easily transformed into it; the wine into blood; and the host of bread easily takes on the form of flesh.

Regarding the point of the conclusion: the author says that <term>Vau</term> <note>The Hebrew letter Vav (ו), which has the numerical value of six and represents the connection between heaven and earth.</note> is the Tree of Life. That is, whoever wishes to attain the fruits of this Tree of Life—namely, grace and glory—must wear phylacteries <note>leather boxes containing Torah verses, worn during prayer</note>. For in this tree of *Vau* is <term>Tipheret</term> <note>Beauty or Harmony; the sixth Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, often associated with the Son or the Messiah.</note>, which contains the influence of all the other <term>Sephirot</term> <note>the ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalah</note>, namely the higher ones: for instance, the second enumeration <term>Chochmah</term> <note>Wisdom</note>, the third <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding</note>, the fourth <term>Gedulah</term> <note>Greatness or Mercy</note>, and the fifth <term>Gheburah</term> <note>Strength or Judgment</note>. From these four is made a single chariot <note>The "Merkabah" or divine throne-chariot</note> of four wheels, which is contained in the *Vau* tree of life, *Tipheret*. Therefore, the Jews skilled in this science, desiring help from those four aforementioned dimensions, placed those four dimensions before themselves and said:

> We ask You, Lord God, that through *Vau* (that is, the Messiah, who is the Tree of Life, into whom those four higher dimensions flow) You might hear us.

Although Christ is the Tree of Life, and the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, He nonetheless received His doctrine from the Father. For just as a tree passes all its strength from the seed, when the earth is broken and irrigated by an influence from above, so Christ possessed His seminal power from the Father. For the Father Himself, called the "Fruitful Memory," produced the seed or sprout in that tree, which was irrigated and is continually irrigated by the higher influence of the Father—namely, by the Father continually producing the Son himself. Just as the holy Doctors <note>theologians of the Church</note> explain the saying of the Prophet: <note>original: "Ego hodie genui te"</note> *I have begotten you today*; for the Father has always begotten, and daily begets the Son. Just as the Sun has always produced, and continually produces its rays. This tree, which is Christ, is nourished in the "land of the living," which is the Divine essence communicated to Him by the Father, as the wise men rightly explain that saying of Christ: <note>original: "Quod dedit mihi Pater, maius est omnibus"</note> *That which the Father gave me is greater than all*: that is...

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS. 801

...divine essence. And this tree is said to be situated in the middle of Paradise because Christ is the middle person between the Father and the Holy Spirit. It is also because (as the more secret theologians say) in the archetype <note>The "archetype" refers to the divine world of ideas or the Sephirotic tree before physical manifestation.</note> there is a certain immense space having a "right" of grace and a "left" of justice. In the middle, however, is the tree of life, providing life, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. These trees are the same thing, though named with different words because of their various effects. For Christ, in that He contained the Word that gives life to all things, named Himself "the life" and "the bread of life." Yet, in that He declared Himself the judge of all, He was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for one does not know how to judge well who does not know how to distinguish good from evil. Therefore, so that Christ might openly hint that He holds this middle place, He willed to be born in the midst of animals, to dispute in the midst of the doctors, to dwell in the midst of His disciples, to die in the midst of thieves, and finally, as the one who will judge all, He will stand in the midst of the good and the evil, so that He may give to each what is his own. Thus, the oracle of Gabriel said: "Jesus shall reign in the house of Jacob forever." <note>Luke 1:32-33</note> For Jacob, in the archetype or in the heavenly mansions, holds the middle position between Abraham, who holds the right, and Isaac, who possesses the left. Therefore, it is most fitting that a judge should sit between the right hand of piety and the left hand of justice, so that he may temper the latter with the former. Hence David, desiring this help and divine influence, said: "Look upon the face of your Christ," <note>Psalm 84:9</note> meaning the one to come, who would be our mediator. And in Genesis, God says: "I will remember the sign of my covenant," <note>Genesis 9:15</note> that is, Christ, who is the covenant between God and man. 

In the second chariot, there are four wheels: namely the sixth, *Tipheret* <term>Tipheret: the Sephirah of Beauty or Harmony</term>; the seventh, *Nezach* <term>Nezach: the Sephirah of Victory or Endurance</term>, which is strength; the eighth, *Hod* <term>Hod: the Sephirah of Splendor or Glory</term>, which is beauty; and the ninth, which is *Iesot* <term>Yesod: the Sephirah of the Foundation</term>, which is the foundation and the pact. And in praying, they would say: "Lord God, we ask you to help us through these four." They placed these four names before their eyes so that they might be moved more and more toward devout prayer. Thus Abraham, while living in Gerar, swore an oath of faith with that King by setting out seven ewe lambs, which prefigured the seven *Sephirot* <term>Sephirot: the ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalah</term>. For "to swear" and "to make seven" are written with the same letters in Hebrew. It is as if he said: "I swear by the seven lower dimensions, so that they may not flow to me unless I return to you what I have promised." Wherefore <gloss>שבע</gloss> <note>Sheva</note> signifies "to swear" and <gloss>שבע</gloss> signifies "to make seven." The Pharisees also represented these Sephirot through their fringes <note>The *tzitzit* or ritual tassels</note> and widened them to show themselves as observers of the influence of those Sephirot and worthy of such favor. Christ rebuked them, teaching that we are made more worthy of such divine influence through purity of heart than through the outward appearance of pretense. The conclusion says: (That which clothes *He*) <gloss>ה</gloss> <note>The letter He, the final letter of the Tetragrammaton YHWH</note> is the last letter and the seal of *Malchut* <term>Malchut: the tenth Sephirah, "Kingdom," representing the physical world</term>, into which the influence of those four last wheels, or phylacteries <note>Prayer boxes containing scripture</note>, or Sephirot, descends. Therefore, the phylacteries on the garments of the Jews were not in vain—which were worn as four: in front, behind, on the right, and on the left—so that those phylacteries and fringes might commit the divine phylacteries to their memory, and that they might have recourse to them with trust.

FRIAR ARCHANGELUS: The Hebrews have these two words, *Diber* <gloss>דבר</gloss> and *Amar* <gloss>אמר</gloss>, both of which mean "he said." Where our translator has: "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying to him." This word *vagiomer* ("and he said") refers to *Malchut*, while *vaidaber* ("and he spoke") refers to *Tipheret*. And just as it pertains to the Sun to influence life in the planets, and to the Moon to execute it—because by the favor of the superior, the favor of the inferior is also moved—so in divine matters, by the favor of the Sun, *Tipheret* is moved, and by the Moon, *Malchut*. All divine dimensions have their effect from this. However, the remission of sins sometimes comes immediately from the supreme crown, *Cheter* <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah, "Crown"</term>, called the Father; sometimes from the Son, *Chomah* <term>Chokhmah: "Wisdom"</term>; and sometimes from *Binah* <term>Binah: "Understanding"</term>, the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Son, it is clear when He said to Magdalene: "Your sins are forgiven you." Likewise concerning the Holy Spirit, when He said the same: "Receive the Holy Spirit; whose [sins you shall forgive...]"

### COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS.

...forgiven sins, etc. Concerning the Father, the Hebrews (especially in the *Zohar* <note>The *Zohar*, or "Book of Splendor," is the foundational work of Jewish mysticism known as Kabbalah.</note>) say that whoever could directly approach the presence of the Father would immediately obtain grace without any other mediator. For this reason, Christ, when teaching how to pray, said: "When you pray, say: **Our Father**." Paul likewise calls Him the "Father of mercies and the God of all consolation." <note>2 Corinthians 1:3</note> Therefore, if *Keter* <note>original: *cheter*; the "Crown," the highest Sephirah or divine attribute in Kabbalah</note>, the Father, can remit sins immediately, and indeed does remit them, it follows that in seeking pardon for sins, we should not use the word "He said"—namely *Vayomer* <note>Hebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר. In this context, it refers to a mediated divine speech</note>—which is attributed to the Holy Spirit, because one must approach the Father directly. 

The Hebrews call the first measure among the Divine attributes the "Supreme Crown" (*Keter*), and Christ calls that same measure the "Father." From Him first flows the Son, who is called *Chokmah* <note>Hebrew: חָכְמָה, meaning "Wisdom"</note> by the Hebrews and "Wisdom" by us; and from both, the Spirit is produced. Every generating principle is fertile before the birth itself; thus, the Father is prior to the other Persons. This Son, existing in that supreme paternal source as an idea and a sprouting principle, never departs from unity. 

Therefore, when Christ wished to explain those most holy Persons—those who produce and those who are produced—He expressed it only through certain relations, calling them Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. In the same way, in everything we do with ourselves, a certain relative name is chosen, by which the work itself is also named. For while He fashioned the World, He took the name of "Maker" and "Creator," and this was in respect to the created thing produced. Similarly, while He rules and governs the World itself, He is called "Ruler" and "Governor," and through this rule and governance, He is joined with us, just as He was through creation when He created and produced. Thus, finally, you will always find God acting and joined to us through certain relations. Whether these relations are real, or merely conceptual "reasons" as debated by the theologians, is not a matter for contention at present. Even when He is diffused within us in reality—not just through grace, but in a better way—from that diffusion results the relationship of the filler to the filled. 

And God, not content with these things, also placed multiplicity in things so that all might be simultaneously an image or a vestige of the triune God, at least in this: that all things have their exit and beginning from God, and their return and end in Him from whom they proceeded. This beginning and end is God the Father Himself, symbolized by the letter of His seal, which is called *Aleph* (א). This letter is first in the order of the alphabet and signifies unity, which is the beginning and end of all numbers. For this reason, *Aleph* (א) also signifies "a thousand" in numbers, namely the limit of all numbers, tens, and hundreds, hinting that He who is the beginning and end of all is entirely One. 

Therefore, He exists as unique in Himself, and though He is diffused into many kinds of creatures—just as "one" is diffused into all numbers—He never departs from His own peculiar unity. Rather, from this unity, bringing all things back into one, He renders them tempered and harmonious. Just as the "one" collects all numbers into a ten (after the square of the first number), and after as many tens as there are units in a ten, it collects those tens into one hundred. Then, having counted as many hundreds as there are numbers and tens, it collects them all into one thousand, which is signified by the *Aleph* (א). This thousand is the object of salvation, because it is the end of all things, as I said, and it is appropriated to the Father by reason of the symbol *Aleph*. 

Therefore, the conclusion rightly says: that in penance, we should not run to the Son, nor to the Holy Spirit, but to the Father, to whom the remission of sins is attributed. For He is the principal source of *Midat Rachamim* <note>Hebrew: מִדַּת רַחֲמִים; the "Attribute of Mercy"</note>—that is, pure mercy, entirely unmixed with severe justice—without whose remission we can in no way reach that object of salvation. For obtaining other prayers, access can be had to other dimensions according to their properties, as is sufficiently declared in the *Porta Lucis* <note>Latin for "Gates of Light," referring to *Sha'are Orah*, a classic work of Kabbalah by Joseph Gikatilla</note>. Regarding the conclusion (on the property of penance): that is, whoever wants pardon for crimes (should not use the word "He said"): that is, he should not flee to the Son, nor to the Holy Spirit...

...marked by the terms *va-yedabber* <note>original: *persuadaber*; a Latinized rendering of the Hebrew וַיְדַבֵּר, meaning "and he spoke"</note> and *va-yomer* <note>original: *uaiomer*; Hebrew וַיֹּאמֶר, meaning "and he said"</note>; which signify "to say." And since for God to speak is to act, and it is the Divine Persons who perform these actions—for operations belong to the individual subjects—it follows that these two words represent those Persons to whom (as we have already stated) one should not flee for the pardon of sins. For they are approached more for judging than for total remission. Instead, one must go to the Father, who (as Christ witnesses) judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son; just as the Church chants: "from thence He shall come to judge the living and the dead." <note>A line from the Apostles' Creed.</note> But regarding the Father, He says the same: *Come, you blessed of my Father*, etc. And elsewhere: *Your Father feeds them*, etc. *His Father saw him and had compassion* (Luke). *Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do* (Luke). And in John: *Father, save me.* Likewise: *My Father loves you.* Whence Christ, speaking of Him, says: *He who sent me is with me, nor has He left me alone.* Because He was one and the same with the Father in essence. As He often confesses elsewhere, saying: *I and the Father are one.* Thus, even as a man, He was always with the Father, because He never departed from His will, and was never abandoned by Him. For the Father abandons no one except the one who withdraws from Him through evil works. And the Father Himself laments concerning such people, saying: *They have abandoned me, the fountain of living water.* 

This is declared by the example of that Father (as the Savior relates) who had two sons, to one of whom he said: *My son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.* Nor did he abandon the other, except when he was abandoned by him; and he received him back with a joyful face upon his return, giving him the "first robe"—manifestly to cover the nakedness contracted from sins. For this reason, he ordered his arrival to be celebrated, to signify the joy that exists over a sinner who performs penance and returns to the Father. The Savior Himself had spoken of this joy shortly before. And Christ, in His preaching, invited those who thirsted to this fountain, just as He Himself, placed in His agony, ran to it, saying: *Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me.* Jonah fled to that most high sea: that is, to the waters of paternal mercy and grace, which he obtained for the Ninevites. Therefore, Christ, as a sign of paternal clemency, placed the beginning of our salvation in the water of baptism.

<margin>FRIAR ARCHANGELUS</margin> Christ was made for us a true victim: a burnt offering, a sacrifice, a sin-offering, a guilt-offering, and a peace-offering. He was made a **victim** <note>original: *hostia*</note> because a *hostia* is that victim offered when one carries back victory over enemies. Thus Christ, having attacked the enemy of the human race, offered Himself to the Father as a living victim and brought back the victory. Whence Paul to the Ephesians: *Christ loved us and gave himself up for us as an offering and a victim in a sweet-smelling savor*, so that He might snatch us from their hands once the enemies were defeated. 

Christ was also a **burnt offering** <note>original: *holocaustum*</note>, which was entirely burned; or because it is called "that which ascends." Christ was burned by the fire of love, consumed, and transformed into a spiritual nature. For this reason, He was transfigured before His disciples, His dark and heavy mortal body having been changed into a body that was agile, radiant, and beyond suffering. After the burnt offering was made on the cross, He showed Himself glorious, passing through closed doors; therefore He is fittingly called "the ascending one." And burned in the manner of fire, He ascended upward to the Father. 

He was also a **sacrifice** offered for sin, which in Hebrew can be called a **sin-offering** <note>original: *peccatarium*; likely referring to the Hebrew *Chatat*</note>. Regarding this, Paul wrote to the Corinthians: *He who knew no sin made himself a sin-offering for us*—not "sin" itself, as our edition <note>The Latin Vulgate</note> has it. He was, moreover, a **guilt-offering** <note>original: *culpatarium*; likely the Hebrew *Asham*</note>, namely a sacrifice offered for a fault or for an error, to speak properly. In this ritual, a bull was offered by a priest or an anointed one who had sinned, and by the crowd; but a prince offered a he-goat, while an ordinary soul offered a she-goat or a sheep. And with a finger dipped in blood, the priest sprinkled the horn of the altar, and part was poured at its base. For with the bull, the he-goat, and the she-goat, he was...

### COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS.

...[it] was called the tribunal of Divine Justice, *Ghebura* <term>Ghebura (Gevurah): The fifth Sephirah in Kabbalah, representing strength, judgment, and severity</term>: to which all those things correspond. This also signifies that part in man in which the fuel of sin <note>original: *fomes peccati*; a theological term for the innate tendency toward sin</note> resides. The blood of the animal offered was sprinkled upon the horn of the altar erected before that very tribunal, to appease the celestial powers belonging to the tribunal of justice, *Ghebura*, which demand blood from those who live according to the flesh; [this was done] so that, according to the rectitude of justice, each person might be punished through that which had also sinned. This was performed by the finger of the priest, who comes as a mediator to reconcile God with the sinning man. 

Christ, however, is not only the priest and the high priest, but also the goat, the calf, the sheep, and the lamb—having been made an all-encompassing sacrifice. By pouring out His own blood upon the horn of the altar of the cross, He appeased the Eternal Father and the tribunal of Divine justice, *Ghebura*, more fully and perfectly than could be done by the blood of animals. Nor is that blood which was poured at the base of the altar in greater quantity void of mystery, compared to that with which the horn of the altar was sprinkled. For the merit acquired through the poured blood, which is superabundant, is much greater than that blood or merit applied to the horn of the altar by the finger of the priest for the purification of the sinner. Indeed, the blood of Christ and His merit would have been, and is, sufficient for thousands upon thousands of worlds. The portion that is reserved is greater than that which is applied to our actual cleansing. 

He was also the peace offering <note>original: *hostia pacificorum*; a reference to the 'Shelem' or fellowship offerings intended to signify harmony</note>; whence Paul says: *making peace through the blood of His cross, whether those things on earth or those in heaven* (Colossians 1:20). And Job says: *He who makes peace in the high places* (Job 25:2), or in the heights. This can be understood as the harmony by which the heavens are bound, being incorruptible and unfailing, even though they are composed of water and fire (as the Hebrews assert). <note>A common Kabbalistic etymology: the Hebrew word for heaven, *Shamaryim*, is seen as a combination of *Esh* (fire) and *Mayim* (water).</note> 

Though Philo, in his book *On Heaven and the World*, maintains that the heavens are not composed of elements. Some affirm this by saying that if the heavens were made of water, they could not divide between water and water, as is stated in Genesis. These arguments are childish; for we see ships and boats divide between the salt waters through which they sail and the river water or wine they contain, yet wood itself is composed of water and other elements. Likewise, the sublime heavens are bound by their own proportions, so that they agree with one another in their motion and in their influence over lower things. By "high places," we also understand those dwelling in heaven, along with whatever other inhabitants there may be, whom the Prince [Christ] has made harmonious. And if any disturbance or discord arose among them, the Redeemer reconciled them, according to the Apostle: *Making peace through the blood of His cross, whether those things on earth or those in heaven.* 

For Christ, the Prince of Peace, brought peace into heaven, having put to flight the ancient enemy and the instigator, the Devil, as John recounts. There is also talk of that peace of which the prophet speaks: *And my people shall rest in the beauty of peace, in the tabernacles of trust, and in opulent rest.* (Isaiah 32:18). For the blessed dwell there, having subdued their enemies with a beautiful victory, in tabernacles of trust, with a great chaos <note>original: *Chaos*; here likely meaning a vast, unbridgeable gulf</note> firmly established between them and their foes, and in opulent rest, having despoiled their enemies, according to the Apostle: *Despoiling principalities and powers.* 

According to the Kabbalists, "He makes peace in the high places" refers to the Divine dimensions. For in those dimensions, the mercy of *Ghedulah* <term>Ghedulah: Another name for the Sephirah Chesed, representing loving-kindness and expansion</term> is desired on the right, while the fire of justice, *Ghebura*, is on the left. According to this rite, you take the kid, which is said to be placed on the left, and the lamb on the right. From this it is hinted that Christ, figured through those two animals, holds the middle place, participating in both sides. Whence John says: *He came not in water only, but in water and blood*, reigning in the middle house between Abraham and Isaac—that is, in *Tipheret* <term>Tipheret: The central Sephirah, representing Beauty and Balance, which mediates between Mercy and Judgment</term>, which is the middle between *Ghedulah* and *Ghebura*. In this is fulfilled the oracle of David: *Mercy and truth have met together; justice and peace have kissed* (Psalm 85:10). For justice and truth are placed with the kid on the left side of the archetype *Ghebura*, while mercy and peace are with the lamb on the right in *Ghedulah*. <meta>This page continues the exploration of Christ as the fulfillment of ancient "types" or foreshadowing figures, specifically focusing on the Prophet Jonah as a symbolic representation of Christ's redemptive journey and the appeasement of Divine Justice.</meta>

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS.

Jesus Christ: for it was necessary that all these things were in Christ, so that all virtue, all merit, and all grace might be contained within Him—He from whom the entire earth is watered, as if from the fountain of the true Paradise of delights. Thus, when the Jews asked for a true sign of the Messiah's coming, Christ responded:

> This generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the Prophet.

Because just as Jonah was in the belly of the whale for three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth. Jonah (as a mere man, as far as he was able) served as a most elegant type <note>In theology, a "type" is a person or event in the Old Testament believed to foreshadow something in the life of Christ.</note>; therefore, while omitting others in which the "Trinity of Days" was celebrated, Christ set forth and brought forward Jonah alone as a sign. For the children of Israel, having set out from Mount Ephraim, continued a journey of three days, and walked for three days through the desert of Ethan. Daniel also stood in the lions' den, and the three youths in the furnace; Joseph was in prison, prophesying through the triple number of days. Yet these signs are nowhere brought forward by the Savior as an example or type—only Jonah. This is because in him alone was the progress of redemption celebrated. To illustrate this, we shall begin with the name: for *Iona* <term>יונה (Yona): Hebrew for 'Dove'</term> is interpreted as a "dove." This is a most simple animal, which was offered for the purification of the woman who was cursed and condemned through original sin, that she might give birth with pain and impurity. Therefore, it aptly figures the innocent and gentle Christ, offered as an oblation and purification for all the defilements we contracted through sin. God had commanded Jonah to preach to the wandering Ninevites; and the Father commanded Christ to preach to and redeem the entire lost world. Jonah feared to undergo the imposed burden and busied himself with flight; and the Son of God began to be weary and afraid, and to seek flight toward the Father, saying:

> Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me.

Jonah fled to the "archetypal sea"—that is, to the waters of mercy and grace which he obtained for the Ninevites—and Christ also fled to the waters of salvation, inviting everyone to them. A storm arose in the sea because of Jonah's flight, or rather because of the pardon obtained for the Ninevites; a dispute was raised before the tribunal of Divine Justice, which did not want to permit the crimes of the Ninevites to pass unpunished. In the same way, a tempest was stirred up in heaven and in the world, because that same tribunal would not allow the human race to be liberated through the sole intercession of the Redeemer without a worthy penance for their crimes. It happened (says John) that there was a great battle in heaven, not only from the rebellion of the dragon and his followers, but also because they would not suffer the human race to be redeemed, especially without worthy punishment. For the dragon sought food for himself from God—namely, that he might devour the human race according to their outrages. Jonah offered himself to suffer for the Ninevites, saying:

> Take me up and cast me into the sea, and the sea shall be calm for you: for I know that it is because of me that this great tempest has come upon you.

But I do not refuse to be handed over to the sea to quiet these tumults raised against the sins of the Ninevites, for whose pardon I have prayed. In the same way, Christ, seeing the entire tribunal of God agitated and awaiting vengeance for the evil deeds of the human race—which could not be mitigated while Justice stood firm—the Son of God Himself said:

> Behold, here I am; cast me into this sea, for I am prepared to receive every punishment that is owed to all transgressors who are in this worldly sea.

Isaiah spoke of this offering made of old, when he said in His person:

> Behold, here I am, send me.

But we have an account of the same act in the Gospel: when He was afraid to drink the cup of passion, yet always ready to obey the paternal command, the Eternal Father sent an Angel to comfort Him and explain what was being discussed by the Divine tribunal. For then He, just as He had said previously to the Father—

> Not my will, but Thine be done—

fulfilled it in deed, offering Himself (as Isaiah prophesied) because He Himself willed it. And then He received the iniquities of us all, which the Father placed upon Him. And then He car-

### COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS.

...He bore all our sorrows, which were so many and so great that Jeremiah cries out: "Great as the sea is your destruction." <note>Lamentations 2:13. original: "magna & uelut mare contritio tua."</note> Christ, therefore, was the peacemaker between these two dimensions, which are considered contrary by reason of their effects: He achieved this by encompassing these two dimensions and their effects within Himself. Since a peacemaker must place himself between those who disagree, the house of Christ is placed as a type <note>In this context, a "type" is a symbolic foreshadowing in religious history.</note> in the middle of the two aforementioned enumerations. Christ pacified through His blood the things that are in heaven. What then remained to be pacified in heaven by Christ's blood, unless we understand it to mean that the Eternal Father and all the heavenly powers were reconciled to us? This occurred when Christ, by paying our debt through His passion, reconciled us to the Father, who had been provoked by the transgression of Adam's sin. Christ made another harmony between the seventy-two princes of the seventy-two nations. These, according to the Kabbalists, were from *Gevurah* <term>Gevurah: The Kabbalistic sphere of Divine Power or Judgment.</term> and were contrary to Israel, the people of *Tiferet* <term>Tiferet: The Kabbalistic sphere of Beauty and Harmony, associated here with the south.</term> in the south. Those seventy-two nations worshipped idols, while Israel alone held the worship of the one true God. Christ came as the cornerstone, who made both into one; for He took away the worship of idols, and now only the one God is worshipped. Hence Plutarch says: after Christ, the oracles fell silent. Porphyry <note>Porphyry was a Neoplatonic philosopher who often wrote in opposition to early Christianity, but is cited here as a witness to the decline of pagan power.</note> likewise says that Christ took away the strength of the gods, just as Christ had promised: "If I am lifted up from the earth on the cross, I will draw all things to myself" <note>John 12:32. original: "Si exaltatus fuero a terra in crucem, omnia traham ad me."</note>—that is, to the worship of the one God. Therefore, whether He is pacifying things in heaven (since some worshipped the heavenly planets, namely the Sun and the Moon) or things on earth, the effect is evident in the cessation of idol worship.

**KABBALISTIC DOGMA.** The word *Bereshit* <term>בְּרֵאשִׁית (Bereshit): The first word of the Bible, usually translated as 'In the beginning.'</term> is the same as saying "He created in the beginning," as if he had said "He created in Wisdom." <note>The author is identifying "The Beginning" with the Sephirah of Chokmah, or Wisdom.</note>

**FRIAR ARCHANGELUS.** Just as purer water is always drawn from the springs themselves rather than from the pools and cisterns branching off from them, so too there is a certain purity in what is drawn from the original languages in which the oracles of God were given to us, as if from the clearest fountains. Among these, since the Chaldean <note>In the Renaissance, "Chaldean" was the common term for Aramaic.</note> is one which holds great importance for understanding and explaining the Hebrew letters, many men very skilled in the Hebrew Law translated the Hebrew text, originally noted in Hebrew, into Chaldean. This kind of labor ought to be highly commended for many reasons: first, for its antiquity, which certainly adds no small majesty to things. Second, because nearly all obscure and difficult places in the Hebrew Bible are beautifully explained in the Chaldean paraphrase, with all obscurity removed—especially where there are prophecies concerning the kingdom of Christ. Wherever the Messiah is discussed in the Chaldean text, even if the name is veiled in the Hebrew, the name of the Messiah is always expressed clearly. The third reason is authority: for the Jews hold the Chaldean text in no less regard than the Hebrew. And this *Targum* <term>Targum: An Aramaic translation or paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible.</term> (whether one calls it a translation or a paraphrase) is fourfold in Chaldean. One is Onkelos, to whom the translation of the Pentateuch <note>The first five books of the Bible.</note> is attributed; he was the nephew of the Emperor Titus and wrote it not long after the destruction of the second Temple. Another was written by Jonathan ben Uzziel, who wrote before the destruction of the Temple—though some wish to believe that both translated the entire Bible into the Chaldean language. Galatinus <note>Pietro Galatino (1460–1540), a scholar of Kabbalah and theology.</note>, speaking of the aforementioned Jonathan, moves these points, saying: Jonathan ben Uzziel, a student of Hillel and of Simeon the Just—who took the infant Christ into his arms—was a fellow student who translated and explained the entire Old Testament into the Chaldean language, so that his edition seemed not so much a translation as a clear exposition. The Jews call this *Targum*, that is, a translation; and whenever anything ambiguous or difficult to understand is found in the Hebrew Bible, they always return to this same translation. For this reason, the masters have said that in the hour when this edition and exposition...

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS. 807

<note>The author continues describing the holiness of Jonathan ben Uzziel.</note> ...they used to say that if a fly or any winged creature flew over him or over the parchment while he worked, it would immediately be consumed by fire from heaven without any harm coming to him or the scroll. A little later, he writes concerning Onkelos: Without a doubt, Jonathan translated the entire Bible into Chaldean <note>original: "Chaldæum" — here referring to Aramaic.</note> (as I said before), but his translation of the Pentateuch <note>The first five books of the Bible.</note> is extremely rare. For this reason, it is denied by others who have not seen it. I, however, have seen it once; it begins thus: *Min uela bera* <note>original: "Min uela bera" — Aramaic: "From the beginning he created."</note>. But the version by Onkelos begins: *Bekadmin bera* <note>original: "Bekadmin bera" — Aramaic: "In the beginning he created."</note>; that is, "in ancient times" or "through the ancients." From this, we see that Onkelos also turned the entire Bible into Chaldean and explained it. Although his edition and explanation are now hardly found anywhere except for the Pentateuch, it is of no less authority among the Jews than the one by Jonathan which we just mentioned, which they also call the *Targum* <term>Targum: An ancient Aramaic translation or paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible.</term>, which is also in the Chaldean language, just like the other, even though both are written in Hebrew characters. Thus far his account. Some, however, think that Onkelos was the one we call *Aquila*, and that Jonathan was *Theodotion*, because of a certain similarity in their names. *Theodotion* in Greek means "the gift of God." The same is true of *Jonathan* in Hebrew: for *Yah* is the same as "God," and *nathan* means "he gave"; hence *Jonathan* means "God gave" or "the gift of God." But these things are said by some based on conjecture, as I believe. There is another *Targum* compiled by Rabbi Joseph, and another compiled by the Jerusalem congregation, which is called the Jerusalem *Targum*; it begins thus: *De chocmah bresit bara* <note>original: "De chocmah bresit bara"</note>; that is, "In wisdom God created," etc. Confirming this, David says: "In wisdom you have made all things, O Lord." <note>Psalm 104:24.</note> From this, note that not only Catholics or all Christians agree on the placement of "Ideas" <note>In the Platonic sense: the divine blueprints of all things.</note>, but also external wise men. Zeno, the ancient philosopher, proclaims God as the prince and disposer of nature, whom he calls the *Logos* <note>original: "logon"</note>; that is, the "Word." This Word is the goal of intelligence and of things to be done, and consequently, it is the Idea. Hermes <note>original: "Mercurius" — referring to Hermes Trismegistus.</note> says in the *Pimander*: "God, the Mind, being most full of the fruitfulness of both sexes, being life and light, brought forth by His Word another creative Mind." This God, who is fire and spirit, subsequently fashioned seven governors who encompass the sensible world in circles; their arrangement is called Fate. Then the Word of God connected with the elements of God, the pure craftsmanship of nature tending toward the Gods, and being united with the creative Mind, it was consubstantial. See how clearly he teaches that all things previously existed in that most fruitful Mind or Intelligence of God, which he calls the "Word," in accordance with the doctrine of John. The Mind which He brought forth is a second person, but the same essence. In this creative Mind—that is, in the produced Word—He fabricated all things. First, seven minds were fabricated, which are seven separate intellects; the Kabbalists call these the "seven days of the Work" or the seven lower *Sephirot* <term>Sephirot: The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</term>. These seven, according to John in the Apocalypse and according to Tobit, are always in the sight of God; they execute the lower matters which the supreme *Keter* <term>Keter: The "Crown," the highest Sephirah, representing the Divine Will.</term> commands. Afterward, he speaks clearly of how the Word of God (that is, the thinking out of things to be made, or that in which the thought itself exists) was fashioned to be united with this world along with the first Creator. And just as the Word itself, or the wisdom of *Chokmah* <term>Chokmah: The Sephirah of Wisdom.</term>, is consubstantial and united with the first—that is, with the Father, the highest *Keter* and supreme Crown—so all things that were fabricated through Wisdom itself lead back to union. Therefore, the Ideas exist in the mind of the supreme Archetype *Keter*, which is *Chokmah*, or Wisdom, or the Word, as the causes of things. But what is the causative intelligence of God for all things, if not His Word, through which all things were made? Hence Paul says to the Colossians: "He is the firstborn of every creature, in whom all things were created in heaven and on earth," <note>Colossians 1:15-16.</note> and this was through the exemplary reasons <note>The "exemplary reasons" are the divine patterns or forms.</note> existing in Himself, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He also made the worlds. Hence Solomon, speaking of this Wisdom, says: "When He prepared the heavens, I was there; when with a fixed law and a circle He enclosed the abyss," <note>Proverbs 8:27.</note> forming all things and imprinting them in all His measures and order. # ARCHANGELUS’S COMMENTARY. 808

When he established the heavens above, and strengthened the fountains of the waters, and set a law for the waters, lest they should pass their limits. And when he ordered the foundations of the earth, I was with him as ***Amon*** <note>original: "אמון" — often translated as "craftsman," "architect," or "nursed child."</note>: which is interpreted as a master in any art, or a craftsman. Behold how clearly he professes in Divine Wisdom that there is a craftsman by whom all things were formed: And that is the exemplar and "idea" <note>In the Platonic sense, a perfect mental pattern for a physical thing.</note> of all things. Rightly, therefore, did the Jerusalem Targum <term>Targum: An Aramaic translation and commentary on the Hebrew Bible.</term> translate it as ***Bechochmah*** <note>original: "בחוכמה" — "With Wisdom."</note>; that is, "by wisdom God created the World."

**KABBALISTIC DOGMA.** What Onkelos the Chaldean <note>Aramaic translator.</note> said, ***Becadmin*** <note>original: "בקדמין" — "In the beginning" or "Through the ancient ones."</note>: that is, through the beginning, or through the eternal ones, he understood as the thirty-two paths of wisdom.

**FRIAR ARCHANGELUS.** Aristotle, having scrutinized the causes of all things, found in a general way only those common to all: matter, form, and end <note>The "final cause" or purpose.</note>. Of these, he describes three quite copiously; but concerning the "acting cause" <note>The "efficient cause" that brings something into being.</note> in particular, he revealed little or nothing, saying only this: That God and Nature work in this manner. But by what influence, with what instruments, or how He conducts these things, he did not touch upon at all. And because he could not grasp the beginning of things, he strove to defend the idea of an Eternal World. Other things, as if beyond his own doctrine and human wit, he passed over in silence. 

But those <note>The Hebrew sages.</note> were instructed by a better teacher: especially Abraham (in the book *On Formation* <note>Referring to the *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient Jewish mystical text.</note>), who treats such matters in a deeper way. For they presuppose three elements as principles: earth, water, and fire. They do not count air as a primary matter, but as a "glue" and a spirit that connects those three. To these three principles, they applied three letters of their alphabet: ***emes*** <note>original: "אמש" — Aleph, Mem, and Shin, the "mother letters" of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>. And because those elements are governed by certain intelligences (which they call *Ophaninos* <note>original: "ophaninos" — the *Ophanim* or "wheels" from Ezekiel's vision, interpreted as angelic movers of the spheres.</note>) through the seven wandering stars <note>The planets known to the ancient world.</note>—which are sometimes found in their own home and sometimes in a foreign one—they chose to denote them by seven letters. These they call "doubles" because they have a two-fold production—namely, of hardening and softening <note>Referring to the letters that have two sounds, hard and soft, like 'B' and 'V'.</note>—according to the variety of dots <note>Diacritical marks used in Hebrew grammar.</note> placed upon them. These letters are as follows: ***begad*** <note>original: "בגד" — Bet, Gimel, Dalet.</note>, ***caphrat*** <note>original: "כפרת" — Kaph, Pe, Resh, Tav.</note>. 

The remaining twelve letters they call "simples," <note>Letters with only one sound/pronunciation.</note> which is to say, always of a uniform pronunciation; and they ascribe them to the twelve signs of the zodiac: ה ו ז ח ט י ל נ ס ע צ ק <note>The Hebrew letters He, Vav, Zayin, Chet, Tet, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samekh, Ayin, Tsadi, and Qoph.</note>. And thus they distributed all the letters of their alphabet, which are twenty-two. These, when mixed and permuted, establish an inexplicable number of words, by which they wish to signify the innumerable bodies that are brought together from these mixtures. 

They wish, moreover, for each individual thing to be named by those letters which designate the causes coming together to produce that thing. Because in every structure some element, some planet, and some zodiacal sign is preeminent, they believe that a thing is properly named when its name is composed of the three letters denoting those preeminent causes. By this, they assert that Adam knew what name was appropriately suited to each thing. 

And because bodies without life and soul are dead and imperfect, they added certain and appropriate "points" <note>Vowel points.</note> to those letters. Just as these points provide the letters with the means of being spoken—and in a way, they "live"—so too do the sages wish to designate the life of composite things. And because all things receive life and growth from super-mundane sources, and depend upon them, they also wished to designate the sources, channels, and influences proceeding from the ten divinities <note>The ten Sephirot or divine emanations.</note> by marks placed above the letters. This number of ten, if joined with those twenty-two letters, constitutes thirty-two. 

Hence Abraham, teaching about the birth of the world, its harmonious formation, and its comparison, said: "In thirty-two hidden paths of wisdom, the Blessed God created his World." Although we could also interpret this as referring to thirty-two intellectual grades. These thirty-two paths of wisdom, or grades, are what Onkelos the Chaldean understood.

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS.

He says: ***Becadmin*** <note>original: "בקדמין" — an Aramaic term usually translated as "in the beginning" or "with the ancient ones."</note>: that is, in the eternal ones, or through the eternal things: for those are the eternal divine paths of wisdom, being rays emanating from that infinite wisdom. Whence, according to Aristotle, if the Sun were from eternity, its brightness would be eternal. Since, therefore, the fountain of Divine wisdom is eternal—as he is the Son of God—these steps and paths are eternal and are fully known by none but the Messiah: for he is the light of God and of the nations. And for that reason, he both knows God and God is known through him. For the Royal Prophet <note>King David, author of the Psalms.</note> exclaims to God: *Send forth your light*: which Rabbi Solomon the Gaul <note>Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, known as Rashi (1040–1105).</note> interprets as the Messiah, who is compared to light: because it is written: *I have prepared a lamp for my Messiah*: and Isaiah says: *I have given you as a light to the nations, as a covenant for the people*: and again: *The nations shall walk in your light.* Moreover, Aristotle wrote that which I judge to be true: that vision cannot happen except with light: as we read in the book *On the Soul*: *nothing is visible without light.* Therefore, as we walk toward the inspection of all things, it is useful to apply a light to our journey, so that we may choose with mature foresight a path by which we can proceed without injury to our feet. To this end, the Kabbalists received (as the Forbanian <note>Likely a reference to a specific source or group, possibly related to Paulus Riccius or another contemporary scholar.</note> relates) certain luminous tracks and "distinguished experiences" which are named ***Leb Netivot Ha-Chochmah*** <note>original: "לב נתיבות החכמה" — literally "the Heart of the Paths of Wisdom." In Hebrew numerology (Gematria), the word "Heart" (Leb) equals 32.</note>: that is, the thirty-two paths of wisdom. Speaking of these, Rabbi Jacob Cohen says: these paths are called "wondrous" by Abraham because they are hidden and occult secrets. And the commentator Rabbi Isaac, in the same book of Abraham <note>Referring to the *Sepher Yetzirah* (Book of Formation), traditionally attributed to Abraham.</note>, testifies: that the ancient wise men—men of heart, mild and upright—who were greatly practiced in the foundations of the Law in the Kabbalah, taught us that even the Fathers walked through many ways so that they might finally stand in these paths. These are called the "admirable wisdom" handed down by Zadkiel <note>An archangel often associated in Jewish lore with teaching Abraham.</note> to our Father Abraham in the tradition of the covenant. Thus he says. And because I have explained each of these in my work on Abraham’s ***Sepher Yetzirah*** <term>Sepher Yetzirah: "The Book of Formation," a foundational text of Jewish mysticism describing how the world was created through the 32 paths (10 numbers and 22 letters).</term>, I will say nothing more of them here, lest things repeated many times should cause displeasure; look there, and you will understand wonders.

***KABBALISTIC DOGMA.*** Just as the gathering of waters is the Just One: so the sea, toward which all rivers tend, is Divinity.

***FRIAR ARCHANGELUS.*** The sea is a collection of waters: and this is twofold—one is below the heaven, and one is above the heaven: between these stands the mass of the heavens. This lowest sea is foul and salt due to its agitation and heat, harmful to man for food and drink, yet fertile for fish; it also produces coral. It is the origin of all sweet rivers and rains that fertilize the regions: moreover, its water, passing through subterranean channels to the springs, leaves behind its moisture and power, from which the earth, warmed by the sun's rays, produces metals. Yet it receives this fertility from those celestial waters, of which it is said: *Let the waters swarm or produce the creeping thing of a living soul*: for not every living soul is produced by this foul sea, but by those waters which are above the heaven. If the heaven placed between them did not block those waters, those overflowing and more fertile waters would render these lower ones, and the earth, and all inferior things, redundant. For the middle heaven and the ministers existing and presiding there act as censors, lest more be distributed to the lowest things than they deserve, or than the order and disposition of the Prince requires. Nevertheless, if any fertility is found in that kind of water, it proceeds from that exalted sea ***Ensoph*** <term>Ensoph: From the Hebrew "Ein Sof," meaning "The Infinite" or "Without End," representing God before any self-manifestation.</term>, named ***Yod He Vav He*** <note>original: "יהוה" — the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note>, which is above the heaven: that is, above the ten divine emanations <term>Enumerations/Emanations: Refers to the ten Sefirot, the attributes through which God reveals Himself.</term>. It is not to be numbered with the aforementioned ten, but is abstracted from them. His name, ***Yod He Vav He***, is divided into twelve ***Havayot*** <note>original: "auaiot" or "havayot" (הויות) — permutations of the four-letter name of God.</note> in its revolution, so that in the Temple of God, it might represent the image of the World. He alone made the "brazen sea," supported by twelve oxen: three of which looked toward the East, three toward the West, three toward the South, and three toward the North, just as the twelve signs of the heaven are divided by those same aspects. # THE COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS

...and high, and God is the sea of infinite substance: toward whom all things tend, as the text says. And since they are contained within that aforementioned highest God: therefore in Him there is a particular place, or <term>sephirah</term> <note>One of the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals Himself.</note>, which is called the sea: or the waters, or the collection of waters: and properly called <insert>Malchut</insert> <note>The tenth sephirah, meaning "Kingdom," representing the physical world and the manifest presence of God.</note>, which is known by various names. Whence the *Sefer ha-Zohar* <note>original: "Sara hora" — a corruption of the title of the Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note> says that the sephirot are called by different nicknames, just as in that "Tree," *Malchut* has this name among its other nicknames: namely, the "sea." 

Solomon speaks of this figuratively in the first chapter of Ecclesiastes, saying that all rivers enter <insert>the sea</insert> through various channels: likewise, into *Malchut* all the superior sephirot descend and run together through various paths, as is evident in the "Tree" <note>The Tree of Life diagram used to map the sephirot.</note>; for all the rivers of the archetype meet in that place. This is confirmed by David <note>King David, in the Psalms.</note>, who says: *This is the great sea, stretching wide with shores* <note>original: "Hoc mare magnum, & spatiosum litoribus"</note>: (our edition does not say "with hands" <note>A reference to a variation in the Latin Vulgate text of Psalm 104:25, which says "manibus" (hands/arms), but the author prefers "litoribus" (shores).</note>) *of which there is no number*: for just as in this sea there are innumerable species of fish, so in the dimension of *Malchut* are all things that proceed from the higher sephirot. 

It follows: *The dragon which you formed to play therein*: here the "Dragon" or Leviathan is taken for an "idea" <note>An archetypal form or spiritual pattern.</note>, and not for the Devil. Therefore, *Malchut* is called the great sea because it contains the idea of all created things; for that reason, it possesses the fertility of the entire generation of lower things: for it is the maker of all things, as they are placed in reality: for it gives life immediately to all things. Furthermore, *Malchut* is called "the Just" because it imparts favor to all according to their diligence: and the Synagogue <note>Here referring to the community of the faithful or the Jewish people.</note>, by observing the Law, receives a good flow of influence from *Malchut*; the same happens to us now, as we observe the Law. 

Regarding the definition: (just as the gathering of waters is the Just: that is, *Malchut*, insofar as the flows of the sephirot are joined and justly distributed into created things) so the "sea toward which all rivers tend" is the Divinity: that is, <term>Ein Sof</term> <note>The Infinite, or God prior to any self-manifestation.</note>, toward whom all sephirot tend as their origin, as if toward the first fountain of all things. Otherwise, it is understood: (just as the gathering of the waters is the Just:) that is, <term>Yesod</term> <note>original: "iesot" — the ninth sephirah, associated with the "Righteous" (Tzadik) and acting as a funnel for divine energy.</note>. Influences are first received in *Yesod* before they descend into *Malchut* (just as that toward which all rivers tend is the Divinity:) that is, *Malchut*, which indeed includes all perfections: it is therefore God: however, the former explanation is better. 

It must also be said otherwise: that in the God who is the sea of infinite substance (according to Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian Neoplatonist.</note>) there is a sephira, or measure, and a place which is called the sea, or waters, or a collection of waters. And this is (according to the more secret Theologians) the southern region, called <term>Chokhmah</term> <note>original: "chocmah" — the sephirah of Wisdom.</note>: that is, wisdom, the water of mercy, clemency, piety, and grace. And it is the place or possession of the Son of God: of whom the Father testifies, saying: *And I will set his hand in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers: he shall cry unto me, "Thou art my Father." And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth.* 

Recognizing this, Jonas <note>The prophet Jonah.</note>—when he had been chosen as a harsh messenger to the Ninevites, as I said previously—the good and pious man, a "simple dove" by name <note>The name Jonah (Yonan) means "dove" in Hebrew.</note>, so that he might not carry such severe commands, took his journey to that very sea by way of Tarshish, as Jerome believes. For he wished to travel there so that he might bring back mercy and pardon for the Ninevites from that source. And this he did: having taken the punishment upon himself so that God’s justice might be preserved, which allows no crime to go unpunished. Hence, to calm the stormy impulses stirred up by the ministers of severe justice, he said: *Behold, here am I, cast me into this agitated sea, and they shall cease*; having accepted, of course, the punishment which the Ninevites owed. Indeed, God welcomed this work of charity; however, He willed that the Ninevites themselves cooperate in placating the Divine tribunal through their own virtue or penance, so that at the preaching of Jonah, they were saved. To this sea also <insert>Christ</insert> fled, so that he might bring back pardon and grace for us from there—indeed, eventually such an abundance as would suffice for the whole world and a thousand worlds. ...[He] offered water freely: but in order to satisfy the tribunal of Divine justice which demands punishment for sins, He voluntarily offered Himself to the agitated sea, taking upon Himself all the storms and waves; according to that passage in the Psalms: *You have brought all your waves upon me* <note>original: "Omnes fluctus tuos induxisti super me" — Psalm 88:7</note>. Yet God willed that we should cooperate with Him through works of penance, returning to God Himself; as the Redeemer Himself and His Precursor <note>John the Baptist</note> both cried out, saying: *Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand* <note>original: "Agite pœnitentiam, & appropinquabit regnum cœlorum" — Matthew 3:2; 4:17</note>, for pardon has now been obtained. Therefore the Savior, in the manner of Jonah, took all our punishment upon Himself; according to that passage in Isaiah: *He was crushed for our iniquities* <note>original: "Attritus est propter scelera nostra" — Isaiah 53:5</note>. This is that sublime sea, and the archetypal southern region toward which God walked after the transgression was committed by the first-formed man <note>Adam</note>; and through which sea He delights to direct His steps, as it is sung in the Psalms: *Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters* <note>original: "In mari uia tua, & semitæ tuæ in aquis multis" — Psalm 77:19</note>. For He more frequently travels the path of mercy and clemency, signified by the sea, than that of justice and punishment. He also frequents the waters of wisdom, in which He made all things and governs all things with steps that are not perceived by us. Therefore it follows: *And your footsteps will not be known*; because no one has entered into those thirty-two paths <note>The "thirty-two paths of wisdom" in Kabbalah, consisting of the ten Sephirot and the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet.</note> of wisdom, not even Moses, as the infallible Truth says: *No one knows the Son*—namely, that supreme wisdom itself, or the water—*except the Father* <term>Keter Elyon</term> <note>Hebrew: "Highest Crown," the first and most hidden emanation of the Divine.</note>, or the supreme crown: *nor does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son wills to reveal Him* <note>Matthew 11:27</note>. Hence, if we wish to arrive at this sea, we must cross through this foul sea <note>The material world or the state of sin.</note>; just as the Apostle discusses in mystical speech, saying: *All crossed the sea, and all were baptized under Moses in the cloud and in the sea* <note>1 Corinthians 10:1-2</note>. Since its waters represent those most exalted waters of grace and wisdom toward which we travel, therefore a crossing through these lower waters was introduced for us by our leader, as if through a sacrament of those higher waters, in which we are cleansed and made blessed, as it is written: *Unless one is born again of water and the Holy Spirit, he shall not enter the kingdom of heaven* <note>John 3:5</note>. For by these sensible waters we are reborn into those waters of which it is written in the Apocalypse: *in His sight, like a sea of glass similar to crystal* <note>Revelation 4:6</note>. This sea, therefore, or the gathering of waters—namely of matter and grace—is the Just One: that is, Christ, who justifies everyone through His death, as I have said. So also is the sea: that is, the principle of all things, toward which all the rivers of created beings tend, since He is their end, bringing rest to all created things.

He has a symbolic connection with all things: with matter in his own physical substance; with the elements in his four-fold body; with plants in his vegetative power; with stones in his simple existence; with animals in his ability to feel; with Angels in his mind and wisdom, or in his understanding; with the heavens in the influence of the higher parts upon the lower and in circular motion, returning to where he came from; and with God in the containment of all things. Man possesses this containment through his composition, but God possesses it through a certain simplicity. Hence <term>Mercurius</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermeticism.</note> says: *Man is more excellent than the inhabitants of heaven, or at least he enjoys an equal lot.* And because among those things that have a symbolic connection, the transition is easy, hence man, while he receives vigor and influence from the Angels, is called seraphic, cherubic, angelic, and the like, according to the nature of the influence received. Thus man has a compatibility with all of them, and receives from all of them purifications, illuminations, and progress. ### COMMENTARY BY ARCHANGELUS <note>Archangelus di Borgonovo was a 16th-century Franciscan who wrote extensively on the "Kabbalistic Conclusions" of Pico della Mirandola, blending Christian theology with Jewish mystical traditions.</note>

...and interpreter of the Divine mind: from the Archangels, as it is given to them to preside over all houses; from the Principalities, as they embrace all [concerns] of those subject to them, [drawing] everyone to themselves by a certain most hidden and super-celestial force; from the Virtues, [the soul] receives power by which it may be strengthened against the enemies of truth and for the prize [of salvation]; from the Powers, protection against the [enemies] of this world; from the Dominations, help by which we are able to subdue the internal [enemy] of the flesh, which we always carry with us; and, as we ought to obtain [this], we receive from the Thrones [the means] by which we may be joined and gathered within ourselves. We shape our memory for those eternal spectacles, [receiving] from the Cherubim the light of the mind, or the exceedingly high images and figures through which we are able to contemplate [divine things]. From the Seraphim truly, [we receive the power] that we might finally cling [to God] with perfect love; for they send down into us such an influx as they themselves receive from the [divine] dimensions. 

For the Cherubim receive forms, and their intellect, which is manifold in its adornment, likewise depicts our own; and the Thrones are aptly joined for their task, so that they may be firm seats, [ordering] us so that, having been made a temple of God, we may receive God Himself, migrating into us as a guest most pleasing to Him. But the others (as some [say]) are sent to us. For the Dominations, like archetypes, give commands [to those] who are to execute them. The Virtues complete the work by moving the heavens, standing [over] every influx; which they nevertheless receive from the first source, the <term>Keter</term> <note>original: "cheter" — The Hebrew word for "Crown," the highest of the ten Sefirot (divine emanations) in Kabbalah.</note>. By their power, they ward off those things which [might] disturb the order of the divine distribution, in whatever way they appear. 

The Principalities take care of public affairs: nations, princes, magistrates, provinces, and kingdoms. The Archangels, however, preside over Lords, Kings, [and] all those who govern, and they participate in sacred rites. At least one individual guardian assists each individual person. [Angels] also preside over the smallest herbs, stones, and all lower things by a power [granted to them]; and these are called "winged ones," whom Moses said were [created on] the fifth [day], flying over the face of the firmament, destined [to move] between God and us. 

David sings of this, saying: *He sends his angels in the circuit of those who fear him, that he might rescue them* <note>original: "Mittit Angelos suos in circuitu timentium eum, ut eripiat eos" — Psalm 34:7</note>. For among the munificent gifts of God, it is numbered that He appoints guardians and ministers to us, to guard us and minister to us, according to that word of the Apostle: *Are they not all ministering spirits, [sent] in service* <note>original: "Omnes sunt administratorii spiritus, in ministerium" — Hebrews 1:14</note>. Wherefore the same Prophet <note>David</note> sings elsewhere: *God has commanded his angels concerning you, that [they guard] you in all your ways* <note>original: "Angelis suis, Deus mandauit de te, ut [custodiant] te, in omnibus uijs tuis" — Psalm 91:11</note>. This is not only a particular guardianship, but a general one; for some of the angels guard in the day, and others in the night. Of these, some observe the first watch, others the second, others the third, and others the fourth. Some even [guard] the first part of the year, namely three months; others the second, others the third, and others the fourth. 

And God placed this change in the Angels, as Job says; for which the Vulgate edition has: *And in his angels he found wickedness* <note>original: "Et in Angelis suis reperit pravitatem" — Job 4:18. The author is contrasting the idea of "wickedness" with a translation suggesting "change" or "shifting duties."</note>. These indeed are the ministering or serving angels, and they [are moved]. And God makes these a burning fire, according to David; for it is necessary that the angels be set on fire by Him who is a consuming fire, so that they may inflame those committed to their care with a fiery love, so that they do not perform the work of God negligently, but fervently. 

Hence the highest of these, who have care of the world, are called Seraphim, that is, "the burning ones." When they see men entrusted to their care kindled with divine love, they sing: *All the earth is full of the glory of the Lord* <note>original: "plena est omnis terra gloria Domini" — Isaiah 6:3</note>. But when they see souls confused in sins, they weep over them, as it is said: *By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept, while we remembered Zion* <note>original: "Super flumina Babylonis, illic sedimus, & fleuimus, dum recordaremur Syon" — Psalm 137:1</note>. For they are said to "sit" to denote an idle work <note>That is, they stop their usual active celestial duties to mourn the state of the soul.</note>... Just as the angels rejoice over a sinner doing penance, so they weep and grieve over the hardening of a sinner. And although they always [see] the face of the Father, as the Savior says, they nevertheless grieve, just as God is said to grieve, to be moved to repentance, and to be touched by grief of heart within...

### ON THE DOCTRINES OF THE CABALISTS

...is [God], unalterable, and entirely immutable. And if the Angels always see the face of the Father, they are perhaps in the heavens. And they are on the earth as well: since that which is incorporeal is not circumscribed by place, nor determined by any specific location, but is present wherever its power extends. Angels are able, by the power granted to them by God, to protect us and to see the face of the Father. This Father, although He is especially in the heavens, is nonetheless everywhere, as every school of theologians concludes. The angels are not, however, stationary: because they are changed according to their duties (as I have said). For they listen to the bride staying in the garden (as Solomon says) <note>A reference to the Song of Solomon 8:13, interpreted here as the soul in a state of mystical contemplation.</note> like friends. For the Angels are friends who guard the soul entrusted to them with such great affection that they not only defend and love it, but they report back to God everything that it speaks and does—whether according to the Law or against it—to be either rewarded or punished. 

Hence elsewhere the same Wise Man [Solomon] said: *do not disparage the King, because the birds of the heaven will carry your voice* <note>Ecclesiastes 10:20. The "birds" are interpreted here as angelic messengers.</note>; that is, the Angels, as the *Zohar* <note>The *Zohar* is the foundational work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), which Archangelus treats here as a source of supreme wisdom.</note> most wisely explains. On the other hand, they likewise report good things. Wherefore Raphael said to Tobit: *When you prayed, and buried the dead, I offered your prayer to the Lord.* And because of this, the Angels ascend and descend by the ladder that Jacob saw, as we read in Genesis. 

However, they listen most powerfully to those who have been introduced into the "garden of delight" <note>This refers to the *Pardes*, or the mystical paradise of spiritual understanding.</note>. And these are called *Zeuahot* <note>original: צבאות (Tzabaoth), usually translated as "Hosts" or "Armies."</note>. Concerning these, it is said in Genesis: *The heavens were completed, and all the host of them.* For this, the common edition <note>The Vulgate, the standard Latin Bible of the time.</note> has: *And all the ornament of them.* For *Zeuahot* or *Zeuaha* <note>original: צבא (Tzaba)</note> signifies not "ornament," but an army or military force. And these Angels do not merely "adorn" heaven like a family inhabiting a house; rather, they fight for the King in our favor, according to that verse of the Psalm: *God has commanded his Angels concerning you, that they guard you in all your ways.* 

Wherefore in the fourth book of Kings <note>Known as 2 Kings in modern Bibles.</note> it is read that a great militia of the heavenly army of Angels came to the aid of Elisha. When his servant Gehazi did not see them, Elisha prayed, saying: *Open, Lord, the eyes of this boy.* Wherefore Gehazi himself, with opened eyes, saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire surrounding Elisha. These fight in the turn and place of the Lord, of whom it is written: *The Lord will fight for you, and you shall be silent.* 

Furthermore, every person has a designated **genius** <note>In this context, a "genius" is a personal guardian spirit or angel.</note>. According to some, these are inferior Angels sent for ministry. Others say that Angels are designated from each of the Angelic choirs through which (as I have said elsewhere) the soul passes when it is about to be infused into the body. Wherefore, just as there are different levels of inferior ministry, so there are different intelligences protecting us. For the Angel of Abraham was **Zadchiel**; of Adam, **Raziel**; of Joseph, **Gabriel**. For Christ, however—I will not say for his protection, but as the prince of his army—**Michael** was given, who (as John witnesses) fought against the ancient serpent, the chief enemy of Christ. 

Nor (in my opinion) does one and the same angel always preside over one person; rather, as a human being climbs to a higher spiritual level, a higher intelligence is given to them. And these Angels sometimes become familiar with those who are committed to their care. Abraham had Angels as messengers of his longed-for offspring and of many other things. Jacob frequently enjoyed the familiarity of Angels throughout his entire pilgrimage. Elijah was fed by an Angelic hand, no less in mind than in body. Peter also experienced an Angel as a liberator from prison and a companion until he had left the city and escaped danger. John many times rejoiced in the company of an Angel, by whom he was taught that most famous vision [the Apocalypse]. 

Omitting many others, I will be brief. To Moses (says Paul), the Law was given through Angels acting with him in great familiarity. Yet Moses, not content with their favor, protection, and company alone, but aspiring toward the Divinity itself, sought God as the leader of his journey, protesting to Him with great confidence and saying: *unless you come with us, I will not go.* God thus sought to fortify his followers with such a divine power of Angels so that one might not only enjoy the familiarity of Angels, but even **become an Angel**. For one is made worthy of such things who serves God with a clean and pure mind, and is always delighted by clean things—in his inward parts, in his skin, in his clothes, in...

# COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS
