Whence Christ says: *Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.* <note>Matthew 5:8</note> And, Isaiah sings: *Wash yourselves, be clean, take away the evil of your thoughts.* <note>Isaiah 1:16</note> Therefore, Moses is not speaking of a lower winged animal [a bird] belonging to our physical body: which the present conclusion or saying declares, saying: that they are Angels sent to us, and ascending upward, they report news of created things to God. And these are winged: for this reason, God commanded in Exodus that they should make Cherubim having wings: which, if they did not exist, God would by no means have ordered them to be prefigured in such a form. Speaking of these, Solomon says: *do not speak any evil of the King (God) because the birds of heaven (the high Angels) report it* <note>original: "non loquaris quidquam mali de Rege (Deo) quia aues cœli (Angeli alti) referunt illud"</note>: for, just as they present our prayers, so also they report the evils we commit (as I have said). For the Angels speak and together praise the Creator: as witnessed by Paul, who was instructed in the celestial school: *If I speak in the tongues of men and of Angels.* <note>1 Corinthians 13:1</note> Therefore, Angels have their own tongue by which they speak, both to each other and to us: not indeed through a vocal sound, but by effecting a <term>new concept</term> <note>The author argues that angels communicate by directly "imprinting" thoughts or mental concepts into the human mind rather than using sound waves.</note> in those to whom they speak, which is better than if it were expressed through an audible voice. Moreover, that instrument through which one makes known to another what is bubbling in the mind, whatever it may be, is called a "tongue." Which (as Plato and Aristotle say) was given so that under its guidance we might express those things which we have conceived in the mind. The fleshy tongue administers a twofold food: namely, physical food for ourselves, and spiritual food for others. Concerning the first, <term>Marcus Varro</term> <note>A Roman scholar (116–27 BC) famous for his works on the Latin language.</note> says: that it is called a "tongue" (*lingua*), as if "binding the food" (*cibum ligans*): for it is seen to provide the food to be crushed while rolling it through the teeth; afterward, forming it into a ball, it sends it down into the stomach. Concerning the second, by the tongue we provide the food of the Word of God to others.

And what a man does with a sensible voice, an Angel accomplishes by imprinting a concept. Whence, just as John was called a "voice," so the Apostles and preachers, in that they manifest the hidden word of God, are called "tongues": indeed, even the Holy Spirit, who moves the tongue and grants the abundance of speaking, wished to appear in fiery tongues. Regarding Angels, if an Angel is far away, he requires a more vehement shout. But having become near, they speak softly by whispering in the listener's ear. And, if he were able to be joined to the listening soul and spirit, he would need no sound at all: but his speech, conceived in the mind, would glide into the listener with no sound whatsoever. This indeed happens to souls departed from the body, to Angels, and to demons; for there is no doubt that all these address one another without noise (for the most part) and wage many-sided wars against us in secret.

For just as the air, when light is present, receiving colors and forms, carries them into those things which are naturally able to receive such things—which colors the mirrors represent by reflecting the received images to those looking in—so <term>Demonic bodies</term> <note>In the Renaissance, demons were often thought to have "subtle" or airy bodies that could manipulate the physical senses.</note> (as some assert) transmit those forms, figures, and concepts which they receive from the <term>phantasy</term> <note>The "phantasy" or "imagination" was considered a specific faculty of the soul that processed sensory images.</note> or the power of thought into our very animate being: urging many allurements upon us, suggesting forms, arousing pleasures that were almost dormant, and frequently stirring up the likenesses of passions in those who are awake and those who are sleeping. But these [demons] disturb souls by art and sophisticated fraud. The Angels, however, and the better minds, operating in the same way, suggest other and indeed better things, according to that speech (says Augustine) which God holds toward them in a more sublime way through His unchangeable operation and determination. 

Among these was that one who addressed John when he received the Apocalypse, because he says: *When I was in the spirit, on the Lord's day, etc.* Similarly, those who appeared to other saints while they were at prayer: these were created when God said: *Let there be light, and there was light.* Therefore, the Angelic minds are divided into two parts: namely, those who assist and those who minister. Truly, first there stand the seven spirits to whom is entrusted the administration of the entire kingdom of heaven and hell: for these (according to the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah; here referring to the Jewish mystical tradition which Archangelus sought to harmonize with Christianity.</note>) rule all things in a certain succession of hours, days, and years—

# ON THE TEACHINGS OF THE CABALISTS

...[of the stars]: just as with the planets over which they preside. John speaks of these when he says: *And there were seven lamps burning before the throne of God, which are the seven spirits of God* <note>Revelation 4:5</note>, through whom He distributes all things. These spirits stand by to hear what the judge and prince commands, and they execute His mandates through the lower spirits who are sent forth.

**CABALISTIC DOGMA:** *The four-letter name of God, which is composed of the letters Mem מ, Tsadi צ, Pe פ, and the final Tsadi ץ, must be attributed to the Kingdom of David.*

**BROTHER ARCHANGELUS:** The one God is called by many names—not because these names express multiple essences or deities, but rather His properties. Although these properties flow from the same fountain of Divinity and remain rooted there as one, they are called "many" in relation to us. Through these various channels, many benefits and diverse gifts are distilled upon us. For this reason, God himself, who is most unified, is assigned diverse names. 

Among their number is **Mazpaz** <note>original: "mazpaz מצפץ"</note>. In the <term>Cabalistic art</term> <note>The mystical Jewish tradition of interpreting the Bible and the universe</note>, there is a specific method of interpretation called "literary commutation" (as was shown in its proper place). This is where a word written with certain letters symbolically designates another word composed of different letters. This is done through an "alphabetical revolution," according to Abraham’s *Book of Creation* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>, which utilizes twenty-two variations or permutations, corresponding to the twenty-two alphabets read therein. 

An example is provided to us by **Mazpaz**, a name of God written with these four letters: מצפץ. The Cabalists speak of this in the present conclusion. This name is not read in the text of the Bible; however, it is a symbol and seal of the ineffable <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH (Yahweh), which is considered too holy to pronounce</note>. It proceeds from the final alphabet, which is the twenty-second in the *Sefer Yetzirah*, called **Atbash** <note>A substitution cipher where the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>. There, the letter *Yod* (י) is exchanged for *Mem* (מ), *He* (ה) for *Tsadi* (צ), and *Vav* (ו) for *Pe* (פ). Thus, **Mazpaz** (מצפץ) represents the Tetragrammaton (יהוה), pronounced as **Adonai** <note>The Lord</note>. 

This name is attributed to the Kingdom of David, called <term>Malchut</term> <note>The tenth and final Sefirah (divine attribute) in Kabbalah, representing the "Kingdom" or the physical manifestation of God's will on Earth</note>. The reason is that this name is composed of *Maz*—which in Hebrew, in the sixth order of verb conjugations, and *Maza* in the fifth, means "it flowed" or "it became many"—and it signifies an expresser, an extractor, and an "exacter" of the people. This fits **Malchut** appropriately, for **Malchut** draws the "milk" of the influence of all the higher <term>Sephirot</term> <note>The ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalistic thought</note> into itself, acting as the womb or matrix of all the higher attributes. It is also the "exacter" of nations, for it is she who renders to each according to their works, and transfers the kingdom from one nation to another because of their injustice. 

The name is also composed of *Paz*, which means to open or to free one who is bound. In the first conjugation, it is the same as lifting the voice, rejoicing, being glad, or opening the mouth in song. In the second conjugation, it means to break, to wound, or to cut; a wound or a plague. All these things suit **Malchut**, for **Malchut** is the door of entry to the Tetragrammaton. She frees the bound, leading them back from captivity; she rejoices by receiving the influence from the higher Sephirot, and she makes created things rejoice by communicating that influence to them, opening them to song. Therefore, in the morning prayer, we seek help from her, beginning with her by saying:

> "Lord, you shall open my lips, and my mouth [shall declare your praise]." <note>Psalm 51:15</note>

And she likewise wounds and heals; she kills and makes alive. *I will kill, and I will make to live; I will strike, and I will heal.* <note>Deuteronomy 32:39</note> It is she who brought the plagues upon Egypt. Appropriately, then, **Mazpaz** is given to **Malchut**, the Kingdom of David. For David, by the power and favor of this name, persecuted his enemies, defeated kings, killed Goliath, overcame the lion, and so on, as was made clear in the *Gates of Light* <note>The *Porta Lucis* or *Sha'are Orah*, a famous 13th-century Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note>.

**CABALISTIC DOGMA:** *No Angel having six wings is ever transformed.*

Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, a 5th-6th century Christian Neoplatonist</note>, in *On the Divine Names*, affirms that Angels are incorporeal. Augustine <note>St. Augustine of Hippo, the influential 4th-5th century Church Father</note>, however, writes as follows in his commentary on Genesis: *Demons are called aerial and fiery animals, because they thrive in the nature of aerial bodies; nor are they dissolved by death, because an element prevails in them that is more suited for acting than for suffering.* The same [Augustine] seems to assert...

It seems that all Angels from the beginning of their creation had bodies <unclear>formed</unclear> from the purer and higher part of the air, suited for action, though not for <unclear>movement</unclear>. These bodies were preserved for the good Angels after their confirmation in grace, but for the <unclear>evil</unclear> ones, they were changed during their fall by the power of the air into a thicker quality, so that they might also be tortured by fire. Moreover, **Basil the Great** <note>A 4th-century Church Father</note> attributed bodies not only to the Demons, but also to the Angels, describing them as certain thin spirits, pure as the <unclear>air</unclear>. **Gregory Nazianzen** <note>Another 4th-century theologian known as "The Theologian"</note> also agrees with these views. And, since all Demons are evil by nature, such that they hate God and mankind equally, <unclear>Divine</unclear> providence has placed the purer good Angels over us, to <unclear>whom</unclear> He has commended us as if to shepherds or rulers. Therefore, all men are ruled by the <unclear>ministry</unclear> of diverse spirits and are led to whatever degree of virtue and dignity they prove themselves worthy of. There are also Angels <unclear>who</unclear> have six wings, and these are subject to the six Angels who, with the seventh, assist at the **Tribunal of the Chariot of the Kingdom** <note>original: "Merchana malchut," likely referring to the *Merkavah* (Chariot) and *Malchut* (Kingdom), the lowest of the ten Sephirot in Cabala</note>, intent upon His commands. <unclear>Their</unclear> names are derived from the three letters of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note> **יהוה**, from which three letters <unclear>revolutions</unclear> are made. These are the six names, assigned to the six aforementioned <unclear>powers</unclear> established over the six parts of the World; and these have a multitude of Angels under them who are winged, so that they may quickly obey those who command them. And, if they do not have a <unclear>fixed</unclear> form, being pressed by a multitude of affairs, they can transform themselves into <unclear>various</unclear> bodily forms. And if the one who appeared to **Blessed Francis** on the mountain <note>St. Francis of Assisi receiving the stigmata on Mount Alverna</note> had six wings in the form of a man, this was by a special privilege. If, however, <unclear>they</unclear> are purely spiritual, it is not inconsistent for them to be represented as winged. The wings of the **Seraphim** and the other Angels are the powers by which they are carried and fly <unclear>wherever</unclear> they wish. Whence also the Angels are called "birds" by **Solomon**, as the **Zohar** <note>The primary text of Jewish mysticism</note> <unclear>agrees</unclear>. From this, perhaps, they are depicted everywhere with wings. The soul, therefore, turns principally to God, from whom it came; otherwise, <unclear>it turns</unclear> by the acts of the intellect and the will (and according to Plato, by the acts of those powers), <unclear>namely</unclear> by contemplation and the operation of the virtues. ### ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS

[...granted] by God. Hence the Prophet notably said: *Who will give me wings like a dove?* <note>original: "Quis dabit mihi pennas, sicut columbæ?" from Psalm 55:6</note> for he recognized that those wings must be given by the giver of all good things. We also ascend by a certain attraction, according to that saying of the Savior: *No one comes to me unless my Father draws him.* <note>original: "Nemo uenit ad me, nisi Pater meus traxerit eum" from John 6:44</note> For He draws us by a common movement, of which it is said by the Apostle that He is *bearing all things by the word of his power.* <note>Hebrews 1:3</note> He also draws by a particular movement, just as the Savior says in the parable of the lost sheep: *that when he finds it, he lays it on his shoulders rejoicing.* <note>Luke 15:5</note> And this sheep is Christ. Contemplating this in the person of Christ, Augustine says: *When you were an enemy to my Father, I reconciled you; I carried you on my shoulders; I returned you to my Father, from whom you came.* Moses had already foretold this, saying: *The Lord your God carried you, as a man is wont to carry his little child, until you came to your place.* <note>Deuteronomy 1:31</note> He also carries us by unburdening us of the weight of our sins; once the soul is unburdened, it ascends to heaven by a natural inclination placed within it from the beginning. Hence Isaiah says: *The Lord laid on him the iniquities of us all.* <note>Isaiah 53:6</note>

Therefore, the Seraphim <note>The highest rank of angels, whose name means "burning ones"</note> have six wings (as Isaiah testifies), so that with two they cover the body, with two the feet, and with the remaining two they fly. By these six wings are also understood six degrees of virtues, which they extend to the six parts of the world’s spherical body: namely, forward, backward, right, left, upward, and downward. Abraham describes these directions as fortified by six revelations of the three letters of the holy name <term>YHU</term> <note>original: יהו — a three-letter form of the Tetragrammaton, or Divine Name, used in Kabbalistic meditation</note>. Through these, the Seraphim execute what God commits to them.

For the <term>Ophanim</term> <note>original: Ophanini — the "Wheels" of Ezekiel's vision, often associated with the second rank of angels</note> (as the more secret theologians say) arrange matter, but the Seraphim, through their warming power and life, complete everything that has been arranged. For it is their task to fill the whole world and all its parts with their warming power. Therefore, they have six wings. "Seraphim" is interpreted as "burning," "glowing," or "seething." Indeed, they are not like this corporeal fire, which consumes and tortures, but like a supreme or super-mundane fire, which inflames, proves, and gives life. They bring down that supreme fire to the lower realms, giving life to all things and inflaming the hearts of the pious.

Christ, acting as the highest Seraph, performed this office once when he said: *I came to cast fire on the earth; and what will I, but that it be kindled?* <note>Luke 12:49</note> And because the Seraphim bring down that fire of the Holy Spirit, sometimes holding His place on earth, it is believed that Origen <note>A 3rd-century Christian scholar</note> said: *The Seraphim are the Holy Spirit*—not indeed in their actual essence, but in their office, just as the Angel of Moses is many times called <term>Adonai</term> <note>Lord</note> or God.

And insofar as he was performing the office of God, the great Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagita, a highly influential mystical theologian</note>, from the workshop of his teacher, attributed sixteen characteristics to the Seraphim, saying: *The name of the Seraphim signifies that which is always moving around Divine things, unceasingly hot, sharp, super-fervid, of always inflexible motion, and able to lead back the lower ranks.* They are an active model, re-warming those lower things, leading them back into a similar heat from heaven by that fiery vigor they have obtained; they are things which, like <term>holocausts</term> <note>sacrificial offerings consumed by fire</note>, are purged by the greatest force of the flame. They are not veiled, but are a clear, inextinguishable light, always illuminating and expelling all shadowy darkness.

And for these reasons, they correspond with the <term>Primum Mobile</term> <note>the "First Moved" sphere in ancient astronomy, which drives the motion of all other heavenly bodies</note>. For since it is the first thing that is moved, and is moved immediately by the First Mover Himself, it is rightly carried always toward that First Mover in its revolution, so that, catching His commands, it may fulfill all things in others according to the will of the one commanding. Secondly, it is necessary that it thrive with unceasing heat, by which it may be moved without interruption and draw all things with it with such force that it is not hindered in the least by so great a machine. Furthermore, it must be "sharp" in the power by which it penetrates all things and diffuses its force even to the furthest spheres. And since it carries all along, it is more "fervid" than all of them; therefore, as he says, it is "super-fervid": namely, the race of Seraphim. For if they must move all lower things and make them glowing and God-like, then that which makes all things glow for movement must be super-fervid. And since all lower things are moved at its nod, so that they may always fulfill what the Supreme Being commands, they are compelled...

## COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS

Both [the Seraphim and the highest celestial sphere] possess an unyielding motion. And, lest their labor appear in vain, they move the subjects beneath them: just as the Seraphim, by their fiery power, lead the lower virtues back to God, so too does this celestial sphere—by its fiery impetus—move all things to do the same, so that they may return to the First Principle. Because both do not merely push, but primarily draw all things along with them, they are called "active patterns." Of these, the Seraphim through the fire of love, and this sphere through its swiftest motion and influence, bring warmth to all things. They lead them back into that very fire by which they themselves are ignited. 

However, the Seraphim draw their power from God, whom they enjoy, while this sphere draws from the twelve revolutions of the Great Name <note>original: "magni nominis reuolutionibus duodecim"; referring to the permutations of the Hebrew name of God, the Tetragrammaton</note>, which the Hebrews call *anagogas* <note>mystical or uplifting interpretations that lead the mind toward divine things</note>. Each of these is set over a sign of the Zodiac, and the whole Name—which the Hebrews call the four-lettered name, the Greeks the *Tetragrammaton*, and the Pythagoreans the *Tetractys*—is set over all the signs. The power of these signs resides in the *Primum Mobile* <note>the "First Mover," the outermost sphere of the universe in geocentric astronomy</note>, as the astronomers teach. Although their images appear in the starry sky, they are not merely figures of beasts, but true spiritual forms, as the most esteemed men have confirmed at certain times and in certain places, having seen with their own eyes the form of the Bull <term>Taurus</term> or the Ram <term>Aries</term> in the circle of the signs. 

Thus, the Seraphim, by the power of the "Holy of Holies" and the most holy Name, set things aflame; and this sphere, like a fuller's wheel <note>a machine used to clean and thicken cloth, symbolizing purification</note> cleansing those it sees, ignites them so that they may ascend like burnt offerings to the Supreme. And just as the Seraphim know nothing higher than themselves by which they might be covered—since they are devoted to the First Light and the Middle—so this circle has no circle above it. Finally, since it is contiguous with the Empyrean globe <note>the highest heaven, believed to be composed of pure fire or light</note> and the seat of God, which is so suffused with divine light that it obscures nothing but rather illuminates all, it takes on the nature of what is above it, beyond all "tens" <note>likely referring to the Ten Sephirot or the Pythagorean decad</note>; hence both are always radiant. They also contain a fire that is a perceptible light and a burning by which they always ignite and illuminate. By their perpetual, clarifying fire—and here by the "snatching" motion and fiery force—after many circuits, and having cast off the dross, they return all things needing purification to the Creator, fully cleansed, so that they may make their destined return to Him.

***KABBALISTIC DOGMA: Circumcision was given for liberation from the impure powers that walked in the circuit.***

**FATHER ARCHANGELUS:** When God came to institute sacrifices, He commanded many things to be offered for various and diverse expiations. This should not seem harsh—the idea that God is delighted by the shed blood of animals, by roasted or burnt flesh, and by the scent of these and other things, as is said in many places: *And the Lord smelled a sweet savor.* Therefore, these are held among the greatest sacraments <note>original: "sacramenta"; used here in the broader sense of "sacred mysteries" or "signs"</note>. 

To clarify this matter, it must be held that the Most High God is not delighted by any animals or flavors, nor is He fed by the physical food of living creatures, or by bread prepared and smeared with oil, or drenched in fat—even though all these things were commanded to be done in the Law. These were commanded as a *sacrament* of those things which were to be done by Christ the Lord, and consequently of those things which must be performed by us: namely, by signifying our members and offering them as an acceptable sacrifice. The ancient sacrifices bore the image of these things. 

Furthermore, those powers which cling to us because of the crimes we commit and the good deeds we omit accuse us at the tribunal of God. These powers were to be appeased by the performance of those things which prefigured that true Offering <note>the sacrifice of Christ</note> through which full expiation for all sins was to be made. Therefore, circumcision was instituted, as Solomon said: *By what things a man sins, by the same he ought to be punished.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 11:16</note> And because all sins proceed from the flesh and the blood, God decreed that sins be expiated through blood. Hence Paul says: *Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.* <note>Hebrews 9:22</note> And since in the time of the Patriarchs the blood of Christ had not yet been shed, God required from them their own flesh and blood; for this reason, circumcision was instituted, where the flesh is cut and there is a shedding of blood. The blood of animals was also shed because the Devil—the Executioner and minister of justice—accused those souls that were not circumcised, which Paul confirms: *Flesh and blood shall not possess the kingdom of God.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:50</note>

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE CABALISTS. 819

...uncircumcised in flesh or spirit. And the accusation of the Devil did not prevail against those circumcised in the flesh: just as it does not prevail now against those circumcised in spirit. John confirms this in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, saying: "the accuser of our brothers has been cast down" <note>original: "proiectus est accusator fratrum nostrorũ"</note>. This is because Christ, by shedding his precious blood, brought an end to the ritual of circumcision, as Paul says: "If you are circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you" <note>Galatians 5:2; original: "Si circuncidamini, Christus nihil uobis proderit"</note>, because it would diminish the efficacy of his own merit. Under the Old Law, no one was justified except for sins contracted through ignorance, or through an accidental slip of the mind, and the like. For the Law to truly justify a person, it must first remove sin and free the person from the slavery of sin and from debt; second, it must render them beloved, accepted, and worthy of eternal life. Only then is a person said to be truly justified, because they worthily merit eternal life. 

Because man was deprived of eternal life due to original sin, and was bound to eternal punishment in hell due to actual sin—and thus lived under God's anger and hatred—it was necessary first for him to be absolved and purged from both types of sin. Second, he had to be brought back into God's grace and made pleasing so as to attain eternal life. Physical circumcision, however, could not by itself absolve one from original sin and slavery, nor return one to God’s grace, nor make one meritorious and worthy of eternal life. For that small piece of skin that was cut away, and that small amount of blood shed in circumcision, was most worthless in comparison to the soul. Therefore, it was not a sufficient price for redeeming the whole human being, especially regarding the soul; thus it could not redeem it nor free it from debt. 

Similarly, neither the animals sacrificed under the Law, nor other sacraments of the Old Law, could satisfy for sin or free a man from mortal sin, because that blood was not pleasing to God in and of itself. Therefore, it could not hold the middle ground between God and the sinner; it would have needed to be better than man and yet lower than God, which was not the case. Paul therefore concludes in the letter to the Galatians, saying: "No flesh shall be saved by the works of the Law" <note>original: "non ex operibus Legis, faluabitur omnis caro"</note>. 

I say, therefore, that the Old Law only provided justification for sins contracted through ignorance. But it provided no justification for iniquity, which they call *Avon* <term>עון</term> <note>often translated as perversity or deliberate sin</note>, nor for transgression or rebellion, which they name *Pesha* <term>פשע</term> <note>rebellious sin</note>, nor for impiety, which they call *Resha* <term>רשע</term> <note>wickedness</note>. Therefore David, having committed adultery (which is iniquity) and murder (which is called impiety), knew that these were not purged by such sacrifices and said: "For if you had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; but you will not be delighted with burnt offerings" <note>Psalm 51:16</note>. People who committed such acts were commanded to be stoned or expiated by some kind of execution. 

The coming Messiah freed us from all these things, because he contained within himself an infinite price. He was free and immune in himself, subject to no sin, and was dear and acceptable to God in his own right, holding the middle rank in dignity between God and man. Therefore, this sacrifice and his passion were sufficient to redeem every person from every sin, since he was both God and man, and his price was infinite in value by reason of his dignity; and insofar as he was man, he was free from all sin in both nature and person. Thus, because of his purity, it was a sufficient offering, and it was dear and accepted by God because of his immense charity and obedience. 

Hence, Isaiah describes this business clearly, saying: "The Lord has prepared his arm" <note>the right arm, namely of mercy and grace</note> "in the eyes of all nations" <note>Isaiah 52:10</note>. Previously, this was only extended to the people of Israel. It follows: "All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation" <note>or the safety, or the Savior</note> "of our God," whom he shall send for the redemption of all. Afterwards, the Prophet directs his speech to the Gentiles, adding: "Depart, depart from the culture" <note>specifically of demons and idols</note>, "touch nothing polluted" <note>referring to things offered to idols</note>; "go out from the midst of it" <note>that is, the worship of idolatry</note>, "and you shall be cleansed from all your defilements and pollutions. You who carry the vessels of the Lord" <note>those who have the receptive powers of divinity, so much so that you are called the temple and dwelling place of God</note>...

# COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS. 820

...speaks <note>original: "loquitur"</note> the prophet below, saying: "The chastisement of our peace" <note>original: "Disciplina pacis"; referencing Isaiah 53:5</note> (meaning the manner of reconciliation to be acquired through him) "and by his bruises we are healed." For we all strayed like sheep, each one turned to his own way; all were subject to sins, iniquities, and those guilts from which they could not be rescued, until the Lord placed upon him the iniquities of us all. This work, although the sensitive part <note>The "sensitive part" refers to Christ’s human emotions and physical senses, which naturally shrank from pain.</note> resisted it, he nevertheless undertook voluntarily, wherefore it is said: "He was offered because he himself willed it" <note>Isaiah 53:7</note>. Hence he said to Peter, who was trying to rescue him from those seizing him: "The cup which the Father has given me, do you not wish that I drink it?" <note>John 18:11</note> And because Peter had previously abhorred the name and the work of the cross, he said to him: "Go behind me, Satan, you are a scandal to me: because you do not savor the things that are of God, but the things that are of men." Because he voluntarily undertook this work, he did not open his mouth in his own defense, but stood like a mute before Herod and Pilate, who were questioning him; whence follows: "As a sheep he shall be led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before his shearer, he shall not open his mouth." He was indeed the Lamb taking away the sins of the World, and for all the crimes that could be expiated by no other sacrifice, he was immolated in the true Passover <note>The "true Passover" refers to the sacrifice of Christ as the fulfillment of the Jewish Passover lamb.</note> for the transition to a better life. And therefore, he alone bore the cross for us, so that it might be sung:

-> I have trodden the winepress alone: <-

for if he had colleagues in this mystery, our debt of gratitude would be owed not to one Redeemer alone, but to many; nor would he have had this glory, that he alone was the Redeemer of all. For Paul, speaking of this triumph of the cross, says: "openly triumphing in himself." Hence Christ himself said to Peter that he could ask the Father for twelve legions of Angels. But he did not ask, because it was not expedient: "since I must fight the battle alone." And in this struggle, he was abandoned by the Father, as he himself complained on the cross, saying: "My Father, why have you forsaken me?" <note>Matthew 27:46</note> Otherwise, he would not have suffered; for one enjoying the fullness of Divinity does not suffer. He was also abandoned because he had no helper, so that he alone might be seen to suffer, as it is said: for the Father of mercies and of all consolation left him under the tribunal of <term>GHEBURAH</term> <note>GHEBURAH (Gevurah) is the Cabalistic Sephirah (attribute) of Severity, Judgment, and Strength.</note>—that is, severe justice—granting him no aid from <term>CHESEÐ</term> <note>CHESEÐ (Chesed) is the Cabalistic Sephirah of Mercy, Loving-kindness, and Grace.</note> (which is grace, consolation, and piety), so that he might suffer sufficiently for the salvation of the human race. Note, however, that in the works he performed, he was never abandoned by the Father; therefore he said:

-> He who sent me is with me, and has not left me alone. <-

In a similar proposition, the Prophet speaks in the person of Christ, saying: "My God, I will cry out by day and you will not hear: and in the night I was not silent" <note>Psalm 22:2</note>, as the literal truth holds. For while he, as a man, feared the horrendous fall of the passion, he was not heard: neither on the cross during the day, nor while praying at night in the cave of the Mount of Olives, when he asked the Father that the cup might pass from him. But the cause, or why he was not heard, he immediately adds, saying: "But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel." For God always dwells in his sanctuary, since he is always holy, always working for the benefit and utility of men. There, therefore, stood the Father, unwilling to recede from his holy decree. Nor did the Son go against the Father's decree, as he himself had foretold, saying: "The Son of Man goes, as it is written of him." This he did, indulging human fragility. And so that sin would not be imputed to others if he fled out of natural fear, these things had to be undergone by reason. He was, however, always heard for our benefit and his own; wherefore he himself blesses: "I know, Father, that you always hear me." We ought therefore to believe that he is the unique Redeemer of all; by believing in him, we are justified, as Peter says: "there is no salvation in any other." This is what the Redeemer himself revealed, saying:

-> God so loved the World, that he gave his only begotten Son: <-
-> so that everyone who believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. <-

In this, the whole necessity of man, redemption, and faith seems concluded: namely, that the first man was produced from the earth, earthy; who, drinking the poison of the celestial and deadly serpent, withdrew from God, dragging the whole tree of the human race at its root into the slavery of the Devil...

It emphasizes Christ as the sole Redeemer who fulfilled the prophecies of Isaiah and the Psalms through his silence and eventual death.</summary>

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE CABALISTS. 821

...the food of death <note>The text likely completes the word *pabulum* from the previous page.</note>, according to what had been said: "In whatever hour you eat," namely by the prompting of the Devil-serpent, "you shall die the death" <note>Genesis 2:17</note>. For the most wise Creator <term>opifex</term> <note>Literally "artisan" or "craftsman," a common way to describe God's creative role.</note> well knew that man was to be tested and evaded by the Angel of Death and the poisonous serpent; from which the human race was wounded with a lethal and irreparable wound, because the sin was, in a certain sense, against the Holy Spirit, as I have said elsewhere. Hence, a remedy had to be brought by a man who was not from that infected lineage, but a heavenly man descending from heaven. By his "skin," the nakedness of the earthly man (brought about through sin) would first be covered; later, by eating the flesh of that "better serpent," we would be healed from the wound inflicted by that most wicked serpent. And this is what our Good Serpent and Heavenly Man says: "Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish, but have eternal life" <note>John 3:14-15</note>. Finally, it must be believed that he came with that great power by which he could snatch us from the empire of death and the power of darkness, and make us believers (as Peter says) "a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people" <note>1 Peter 2:9</note>—that is, acquired and rescued from the perdition brought in by sin. He draws away our earthly lot, which was being driven toward a fall by that death-bearing Angel—the one who is impure and filthy, who walks about in a circuit with his apostate angels, seeking whom they may devour.

*CABALISTIC DOGMA: Therefore circumcision is performed on the eighth day, because it is superior to the universalized bride.* <note>In Cabalistic thought, the "Bride" (Sponsa) often represents the tenth Sefirah, Malkhut (Kingdom/Earthly Realm). The "eighth day" refers to a level beyond the natural seven-day cycle of creation, associated with the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding) or Yesod (Foundation).</note>

FRATER ARCHANGELUS: Only the sacraments of the New Law are able to remove [sin], confer grace, and justify man. For sacraments of this kind contain power instrumentally, and the price of the Passion instituted to take away sins, to confer grace, and to justify man. The reason why the sacrifices of the Old Law could not justify a person by themselves, nor take away sins by themselves, was this: they did not actually contain Christ, nor the price of his Passion. But the sacraments of the New Law either contain Christ really <note>original: "realiter"</note>—as in the Eucharist—or they contain the power and price of his Passion—such as Baptism, Confirmation, Penance, and the other sacraments. Therefore, they immediately effect and confer invisible grace and provide payment on behalf of the sinner. For Christ works through the Ecclesiastical sacraments as a functional instrument containing the price and treasure of his Passion virtually.

However, Christ was not really present in the sacrifices and sacraments of the Old Law, nor was his Passion there, except as in a sign; insofar as those things were figures of Christ to be sacrificed on the cross. Therefore, they did not effect the grace in the present which they figured; nor did they pay the price of redemption, which they figured was to be paid by Christ on the cross. This is not so for the sacraments of the New Law, because they immediately effect what they signify, for the reason that they really contain the price of Christ's Passion. For the sacrament of the Eucharist immediately confers grace by itself to a prepared recipient, and reconciles him to God; it reconciles all for whom it is offered to God, unless they have an obstacle <note>original: "obicem"; a theological term for a barrier to grace, such as a lack of faith or unrepentant sin.</note>. Similarly, Baptism immediately pays the price of Christ’s Passion for the one baptized, and Penance for the repentant sinner, and so on. They indeed justify him and make the man worthy of eternal life. Whence a fitting man immediately flies to heaven by the power of Christ’s Passion, which he receives through the sacraments. And in Confirmation, the gifts of the graces of the Holy Spirit are given.

It must be said, therefore, that all the faithful of the Old Instrument <note>The Old Testament</note> were justified and absolved from sins through faith alone in the future Christ; they could not, however, obtain the promises except through Christ. Whence Paul, in the Letter to the Hebrews, enumerates the principal fathers of the Old Testament, beginning from Abel, proving that all those people suffered persecutions through faith in the future Christ and were made members of Christ. For he was believed by them, and therefore they waited to be redeemed by him. And thus, as members of Christ, they deserved to participate in Christ's Passion; because they were absolved under such faith...

# COMMENTARY BY ARCHANGELUS.
<meta>catchword: p</meta>

...are [healed] from sin. For Abraham, while in the state of uncircumcision <note>original: "in præputio existens"</note>, was justified because he believed God; when, looking up toward the sky, he believed that his spiritual seed would be multiplied through Christ like the stars of heaven. And because he believed, it was credited to him as righteousness (Genesis 15). Therefore, the Fathers of the Old Testament were saved through Christ alone. In circumcision, original sin was deleted, not by the power of circumcision itself, but by the power of faith in Christ. That circumcision did not in itself contain a price sufficient to appease God or to justify man. The same must be said of the sacrifices of the Old Law: they did not contain such a price as to satisfy for sins and reconcile the people to God through their own power. Rather, such justification occurred through the power that those offering the sacrifice held regarding the Passion of Christ. It was the same with their circumcision; of itself, it was of no value for removing sin except by reason of the faith of the one conferring it. For this reason, the sacraments of the New Law can be conferred by anyone—even by a heretic, a schismatic, or a Jew—provided it is done in the faith of the Church <note>The author is contrasting the "ex opere operato" (it works by the act itself) nature of Christian sacraments with the Old Law rituals that required the faith of the practitioner.</note>. This was not so for the sacraments of the Old Law, which required faith in the agent, because they did not contain within themselves what they figured, as they were merely signs.

Circumcision was strengthened by several purposes. First, as a distinguishing sign to separate the Jews from other nations. Second, it was a figurative sign of the future Passion of Christ and the shedding of his blood. It also signified the "cutting away of the foreskin of the heart," as is said in Deuteronomy 10: "Circumcise the foreskin of your heart." Third, the cutting away of sin was prefigured by the cutting of that small skin. The third <note>The author repeats "third" here, perhaps intending it as a sub-point regarding the removal of sin as a spiritual "tribute" or tax.</note> prefigured a certain incidental tribute. Fourth, it signified faith and the consolation to be paid through Christ on the cross; thus, it was a sign of the covenant, of grace, and of the future price. The sixth cause is assigned in the preceding conclusion: namely, that they might be liberated from unclean spirits. The seventh is assigned in the aforementioned conclusion: which is to show that the influx of <term>Yesod</term> <note>original: "iesot". In the Cabala, Yesod (Foundation) is the Sephirah associated with the generative organs and the "Covenant of the Circumcision."</note> precedes and is above every influx of the "universalized bride" <note>This refers to the Sephirah *Malchut* (Kingdom), often called the "Bride" or "Shekhinah."</note>.

Therefore, note that circumcision (as held in Leviticus 12) took place on the eighth day. However, if necessity urged it, it could be done sooner or later without breaking the Law. This is because the eighth day represents the optimal figure of the Sephirah <term>Yesod</term>, which is placed in the eighth position, counting <term>Hod</term> and <term>Netzach</term> as a single Sephirah. The count is as follows:
1. First is <term>Keter</term> (The Crown)
2. Second is <term>Chokmah</term> (Wisdom)
3. Third is <term>Binah</term> (Understanding)
4. Fourth is <term>Gedulah</term> (Greatness/Mercy)
5. Fifth is <term>Gevurah</term> (Strength/Judgment)
6. Sixth is <term>Tipheret</term> (Beauty)
7. Seventh is <term>Hod</term> and <term>Netzach</term> (Glory and Victory)
8. Eighth is <term>Yesod</term> (Foundation)

From this eighth Sephirah, every covenant is made manifest. For every word of the Law that sounds like "covenant" <note>Hebrew: *Berit*</note> suggests one of these three mystical lights: namely *El Chai Yesod* (the Living God of Foundation), *Adonai Malchut* (the Lord of the Kingdom), and first *Binah* (Understanding). Without prudence, the "Covenant of the Living God Yesod" is a covenant of peace and a covenant of true life. The Founder of the World instituted the covenant of circumcision so that through *El Chai Yesod* we might be made strong. Hence the Law says: "If one circumcises, but does not reveal the 'crown' of the circumcised member <note>This refers to the ritual of *periah*, where the membrane is pulled back to fully uncover the glans (the crown). In Jewish law, circumcision is incomplete without this.</note>, the circumcision itself shall be considered as nothing." For the circumcision of the member and the showing of the crown opens the hidden entrance to life. For *Yesod* gives eternal life, and therefore He is called *El Chai*, that is, the "Living God." For this Sephirah, holding the [penultimate] place among the Sephirot, draws grace and life from all those above it, and transmits and pours it into us through *Adonai Malchut*.

Insofar as it receives the dimension of grace, it is called *El* (God); because it absorbs life, it is called "Living"; and insofar as it unites itself, it is usually called the "Living God." And He imparts this life no less to holy souls than to the heavenly choirs and the multitude of the entire world, everywhere through the gift of life. Longing for this, David says: "My soul thirsts for God, for *Elohim*, for the Living God *El*" (Psalm 42). Through the connection of these, we obtain all good things, and therefore He is surnamed <term>Shaddai</term> <note>original: "Sadai"</note>, for He is "sufficient" for us to satisfy and bless us. By a similar reasoning, because circumcision was a pledge <note>original: "arabon", from the Hebrew/Greek for a down payment or earnest money.</note> of eternal life, anyone who was not circumcised held a pledge of damnation, according to the saying of the Law: "The soul that shall not be circumcised shall perish from [its people]"...

...for which reason **Abraham** circumcised himself and his entire household: therefore, such circumcision was performed on the eighth day, so that it might prefigure **Yesod** <note>original: "Iesot"; the ninth Sephirah, representing the "Foundation" and the procreative life-force</note>, who is higher in the order of the *Sephirot* <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Cabala through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> than the bride **Malkuth** <note>original: "Malchut"; the tenth Sephirah, representing "Kingdom" or the manifest world, often described as the feminine Bride</note>. This **Yesod** was prefigured by the cutting away of the foreskin of the **phallus** <note>original: "Priapi"</note>: at that time, it was a sign that **Yesod** looked upon **Malkuth** with a favorable influence, and **Malkuth** looked upon such a circumcised person with similar favor received from **Yesod**. For the bride **Malkuth** promises such an influence—or "seed"—as she receives from the masculine **Yesod**, and likewise from all the others, because **Malkuth** is the bride of all the *Sephirot*. Therefore, she is called "universalized," as if she were the female of all the *Sephirot* receiving them into herself, existing as their womb and wife. There exists an archetypal Groom and Bride. Of the Groom, Solomon sings in the Song of Songs, saying: *My beloved is white and ruddy.* For from these colors results his beauty, he who is called *fairer than the children of men.* Here Solomon also alludes to the effects which the Groom himself works within us: for sometimes he shows himself as white, namely through the grace of piety and mercy; but sometimes he is inflamed, namely with the zeal of justice. Hence it was not without reason that John said that Jesus came not in water only, but in water and blood. This is also understood regarding the supreme colors, about which **Plato** writes most extensively in the *Timaeus* and *Phaedo* (just as he had learned from the ancient theologians). For on the right, he is white, by reason of the inflows of grace and mercy; but on the left, he is ruddy, in respect to the down-flows of justice and punishment. This is what Christ himself, the true Groom, hinted at when he said he would say to those on his right: *Come, you blessed of my Father*—that is, of the supreme crown—*possess the kingdom prepared for you,* namely the **Ein Sof** <note>original: "Ensoph"; the Infinite or Boundless Godhead</note> of all ages. And to those on his left: *Go, you cursed, into the eternal fire* of fierce justice. Of these sides, namely the right and the left, it is said in the Song of Songs:

> His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

This is not a speech about a lustful embrace, for such wicked things are not mixed with the divine; especially since a little earlier it says: *He ordered charity in me.* Therefore, just as the serpent spoke of a kiss, so here he hints at a spiritual embrace—that of God, whose left hand (as I have often said) is severe justice, might, and strength. He desires this left hand to be placed under his head—that is, under reason and the higher part—so that, being strengthened from there, he may act more powerfully in divine and sacred matters. He also desires to be embraced by that right hand, of which it is written: *Delights are in your right hand even unto the end.* And again: *The right hand of the Lord has wrought strength, the right hand of the Lord has exalted me.* In this right hand resides our head and groom, Christ.

This groom is **Tiferet** <note>original: "Tipheret"; the sixth Sephirah, representing "Beauty" or "Compassion," often identified with the Son or the Groom</note> (according to the **Cabalists**), who listens to the bride **Malkuth** dwelling in the garden. For he guards her, entrusted to him, with such great affection that he does not merely love her, but imparts all his goods to her, establishing her as the princess of those to be rewarded and those to be punished. And conversely: the bride so loves the groom that she is said to "languish" for the love of her beloved (as is said in the Song of Songs), since between them there is a reciprocal love—given and returned in kind. And thus he loves the bride so clearly that he offers her his breasts in the garden (as is held in the Song of Songs); in the garden, namely, of delight, which consists of the three supreme measures. There is **Chokhmah** <note>original: "chocmah"; the second Sephirah, "Wisdom"</note> having breasts full of milk, namely of divine wisdom. Similarly, the groom introduces the bride into the wine cellar—that is, into the union of love signified by wine. This is the union which the *Sephirot* have, which are united into one supreme crown in the most ample *Sephirotic* order, or in the great house of God, just as many grapes come together into the same wine. Therefore, the bride follows there, saying: *He ordered charity in me.* And because the groom rejoices in the favor shown to his bride from the lower dimensions, he therefore says: *I went down into the garden to see the fruits of the valleys*—that is, the influence sent down into the bride from the valleys, meaning from the humbler or lower numberings <note>The author uses "numerations" as a synonym for Sephirot</note>. And because the aforementioned divine inflows are of infinite perfection, the bride, tasting them, says: *And his fruit is sweet to my throat.* Because these also [flow] in-

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Sephirot and their relationship to the "Bride" (Malkuth), moving from a physical explanation of circumcision to the spiritual and cosmic influences that shape the manifest world. ### COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS.

...the lower *Sephirot* <note>The ten divine emanations of Cabala</note> flowing into the bride are arranged in a twofold order: those on the right of the South <note>symbolizing Mercy or *Chesed*</note>, and those on the left of the North <note>symbolizing Severity or *Gevurah*</note>. Therefore, the groom follows them all to influence the garden where the bride was, saying: *Awake, O North wind, and come, O South wind, and blow through my garden.* Indeed, he calls for the North wind to blow so that vigor and strength may come, by which the bride might be strengthened against venereal <note>earthly or lustful</note> weakness. He also asks for the South wind of grace, so that he may fill this lower world with good spiritual gifts against the ancient serpent. Therefore, the groom follows, speaking with the bride and saying: *The time of pruning has come*—that is, the time for you to prune such goods from yourself and impart them to created beings. 

And although this groom infuses all seven lower dimensions into his brides, because everything superior in respect to an inferior is called "man" and "male," and everything inferior has the character of "woman"—for all of us, who are made pregnant by the face of God and who hold the inferior and feminine position in the universe (while God holds the superior and masculine), are rightly called "women" in respect to Him. Just as the heavens, in respect to the earth which is impregnated by them, have a masculine character, but in respect to the Angels and God, from whom they receive their influence, they have a feminine character. This is written about extensively by the ancient theologians. Yet, there is only *one dove* (as it says in the Song of Songs), which is **Malkuth** <note>The final Sephirah, representing the Kingdom or the physical manifestation of the Divine</note>, because from the beginning, one woman was assigned to each man. Hence, according to the Law, a priest (who ought to be an imitator of the divine) is not permitted to be joined to multiple women, even though it is permitted to others to avoid greater scandals. 

And because the beauty of a woman is the cause of the man's love for her, the groom declares the motive of his chief love, saying: *Thy eyes are like the pools of Heshbon.* For just as this bride is full of every kind of flow, so she is full of "eyes"—that is, the cognitions of all things before they come to be. Just as a pool is a place in which all waters are gathered, so the bride **Malkuth** is the pool in which the waters are gathered, concerning which it was said: *Let the waters bring forth the creeping thing that has a living soul.* Indeed, those waters are the "ideal reasons" <note>The divine blueprints or archetypes of all things</note>. Hence that pool is called **Heshbon**, which means "of calculation" or "reasoning." For the "Ideas" are the thought-out reasons of things to be produced. Also, those waters are the influence of all the *Sephirot*; and she who holds the place of the bride **Malkuth** receives the "decisive seed" from all the superiors. In this way, the bride is said to be "universalized"—that is, universal, or composed of all the *Sephirot*.

> **CABALISTIC DOGMA: There are no letters in the whole Law which, in their forms, connections, separations, twists, direction, defects, abundance, smallness, greatness, crowning, closure, opening, and order, do not manifest the secrets of the enumerations [the Sephirot].**

**BROTHER ARCHANGELUS:** The Law is of such great dignity that David, admiring it, says: *Open my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of thy Law.* For in the Law are hidden the wonders of the Gospel, with which the Law was "pregnant." In the Law, the "fabric of the world" <note>original: *mundi fabrica*; the structural design of the universe</note> is taught: from whence come the species of things, their order, forms, matter, and operation, and what their final end may be. Through the Law we are instructed by what path and by what journey we may go toward God. In that same place, we are instructed concerning the past and future events of things, and how all things happen by divine providence. There we are taught concerning the concord and marvelous harmony among things themselves and with God. Without controversy, the foundations of the virtues are shown there, in which there is such power (as Augustine rightly feels) that unless one is imbued with them, no one can be wise. For there, the most secret Intelligences and their commerce with us are signified to us—indeed, even the fellowship of God, and how we might be able to draw Him to us, so that we may be filled by Him, and He may act with us. And (what is greater) in the Law we are taught how we may be transformed into Him and be made "Gods." But these things are covered by such an occult mystery that the unworthy, seeing, may not see, and hearing, may not understand.

<meta>This page continues the theological exploration of the relationship between the Law (Torah) and the Gospel. The previous page discussed the mystical influences of the Sephirot and the concept of the soul as "feminine" in relation to the Divine. Here, the author focuses on the spiritual mechanism of "holiness" and how the Law serves as a vehicle for returning the soul to its source.</meta>

->### ON THE DOGMAS OF THE CABALISTS. 825<-

...just as the Law makes us descend toward God, so the Gospel sends us to the Law, saying: *If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments of God.* And again: *In the Law, what is written? How do you read?* Through the Gospel comes the remission of those sins which could not be expiated through the Law except by the death of those who committed them. Through the Gospel, the "daily denarius" <note>A reference to the parable of the workers in the vineyard (Matthew 20), representing the reward of eternal life</note> is promised—eternal life and the kingdom of heaven—which were by no means granted through the Law alone. The observation of the Law's commandments provided life when favored by the Gospel; but without the Gospel, the Law promised nothing but an earthly kingdom and temporal favor. Although these things prefigure eternal ones, just as the Gospel was prefigured in the Law, a person can be called and made holy in and through the Law. Hence God said to the fathers: *Be holy, for I am holy.* From this comes the word <term>Kadosh</term> <note>Hebrew: קדוש</note>, which means holy—that is, dedicated or initiated to God, and directed into God Himself as the ultimate end. For God is dedicated or initiated to humanity, and dedicated to Himself and directed toward Himself. Therefore, He is called the Beginning and the End. And that is what it means to be truly holy, as Plato concludes in the *Euthyphro*: namely, when we return to God what we received immediately from Him—the soul and the image. <note>Plato’s dialogue *Euthyphro* explores the definition of piety or holiness as a kind of "trading" or giving back to the gods.</note> Knowledgeable men know that we are taught to do this through the Law. God, however, brings back into Himself not what He received, but what He has held from eternity and from Himself. 

Indeed, the Law completed the circle, even if it could not justify on its own; for the Law perfects by making us like God <note>assimilation</note>, even if it does not complete the process by justifying us. For the entire intention of God in the Law is (as I have said elsewhere) that through it we might be made inwardly identical to God Himself. This is evident in several precepts, though in others the same thing happens more hiddenly. For where it speaks expressly of sanctifying the Sabbath, it says: *Rest on the seventh day, just as the Lord your God rested on that day.* And in the first month, it was commanded to eat unleavened bread <note>Azymes</note>, with all leaven—which is "corrupted bread"—utterly removed. This was in memory of the construction of the World performed at that time, and the production of things without any previous corruption. For the First Artisan <note>The Creator</note> was exempt from the Law of Nature, which states: <note>original: "Corruptio unius, est generatio alterius"</note> *The corruption of one is the generation of another.* And the remaining precepts of the Law do this same thing. 

And because this assimilation could not happen without a prior justification, that Law "justified" in its own way. Hence David says: *The Law of the Lord is immaculate, converting souls.* And many times it is written in the Law: *And the priest shall make atonement for him.* This justification happened *in* the Law, but not *by* the Law; for the Law's own nature is to give commands of what to do and what not to do, and to add punishment for the transgressor. If any atonement occurred, it was from the Gospel, which always accompanies the Law. And this was done by the power of the Lamb—namely, Christ, slain from the beginning of the world for the expiation of all (as John says)—and not by the power of the legal priest. For even the priest himself needed expiation, as the Apostle <note>Paul</note> maintains. For the spiritual man could not be expiated through the Law, since the Law itself is animal <note>Latin: *animalis*, referring to the 'anima' or natural soul as opposed to the spirit</note>, expiating the natural man. Even while it was a Law of servitude, it could not lead one out into the liberty of the spirit; yet it prefigured the New Law, with which it was pregnant. Therefore, it was of great dignity by reason of such an offspring. To show this dignity, it was "written by the finger of God," as we read in Exodus, because those sacraments could only have been dictated by God. Furthermore, so that the Law would be perpetual, it was written by God; for all things that proceed immediately from God Himself, without a secondary cause, are incorruptible, as Plato and Plotinus assert. 

Hence, the Law is said to have been described on tablets of sapphire—that is, of a celestial color. And although such tablets may seem scattered, the Law which was written in heaven is not abolished. That sapphire color indicated this; but those physical tablets were taken away because the Law gave way to the Gospel, in which the whole Law is completed and perfected. Hence Christ said: *I did not come to abolish the Law, but to fulfill it.* And those who fulfilled the Law attained this perfection: they were called faithful in the whole house of God, as was said of Moses in the book of Numbers. Also among the blessed...

# THE COMMENTARY OF ARCHANGELUS #

...were reckoned: Psalm [1]: **Blessed is the man who meditates on the Law of the Lord**, etc. And the prophet adds: *all things whatsoever he willed, he did*, and so on. And again: **Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the Law of the Lord; those who search his testimonies and seek him with their whole heart.** [Psalm 119:1-2]. How much dignity and happiness do mortals feel from the wonderful harmony when they have it perfected within themselves! For all pleasure comes from harmony. This harmony, moreover, results from observing the affirmative commandments, together with the virtues, through the bones (which are equal in number to those commandments <note>Traditional Jewish teaching identifies 248 affirmative commandments, corresponding to the 248 parts or bones of the human body</note>), and from the negative commandments in the nerves (equal in number to them, as I have said elsewhere <note>365 negative commandments corresponding to the days of the year or, in this anatomical allegory, the "veins" or nerves</note>). For the whole Law connects us with God and thereby makes us joyful, just as sin brings dissonance and affliction of the soul to man. 

Many fruits are also promised to those who observe the Law; for to the fathers living under the figure [of the Law], a figurative kingdom was promised. According to that word of Christ: **If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments of God.** [Matthew 19:17]. Yet the kingdom of heaven was not given to the fathers for observing the Law, because they were not regenerated and made children of the kingdom, nor reborn according to the spirit—except for a few by special privilege, yet by the power of him who regenerated us. For the labor and penitence of those [fathers] was to sanctify the "animal man" <note>original: *hominem animalem*, referring to the natural or physical person as opposed to the spiritual person</note>, until the time for being reborn and for changing one’s state for the better arrived. So great is the volume of the Law that all things written in it are full of a grand mystery. 

Hence, the smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet is the <term>Yod</term> <note>original: *iod* י</note>, and the "tittle" <note>Matthew 5:18</note> is a point or an accent. These are found in Scripture in their due number, weight, measure, and sacred mystery. Therefore, Rabbi Simeon Ben Yochai <note>The traditional author of the *Zohar*, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>, and after him Elchana and others, have not only attempted to interpret the sentences and words, but also to give an account for the letters themselves and their shapes, along with the "tittles" placed above and below them. 

To bring forward an example: the first letter of the alphabet is **Aleph** א. This is the seal of **Cheter Elion** <note>Hebrew: *Keter Elyon*, the "Supreme Crown," the highest of the Sephirot</note>. It is composed of a **Vav** ו and two **Yods** י י; these three letters together constitute the **Aleph** א. The **Vav** is the Tree of Life, **Tipheret** <note>The Sephirah of Beauty/Harmony</note>, which is Divine life—both divine and human, or created. Insofar as it represents Divine life, the **Vav** ו is placed in the **Aleph** א; but insofar as it is the life of creatures (in whom "we live, move, and have our being" [Acts 17:28]), the **Yod** is placed in the belly of the **Vav**, and thus the **Aleph** is formed. It is the letter of Divinity and the first fountain of all good things, namely **Cheter** [Keter]. 

The second letter of the alphabet is **Beth** ב, which is shaped with three lines and is closed on every side except the left, which looks toward **Cheter**. Because it is in the [Divine] concept, the **Beth** has a part facing the **Aleph** placed in **Cheter**, to signify that whatever the Son contains within himself, he has from the Father. For this is the seal of the Son; and it signifies **Bait**, which is the same as "house." It also signifies the Higher Wisdom (**Cocmah**) <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note>, in which all things were first gathered before they were brought forth into their own forms. Through this Wisdom all things were produced, according to the word: **In wisdom you have made all things.** [Psalm 104:24]. Confirming this, John says: **All things were made through the Word** [John 1:3], as if in a creative life; and afterward, he says all things were made through the Word itself. Therefore, the *Zohar* says that **Cocmah** [Wisdom], the Son, is the House of God, in which the Father (**Cheter**) placed the ideal forms of all things. 

The seal of **Binah** <note>The Sephirah of Understanding</note> is the letter **He** ה. It is composed of the letter **Resh** ר and a **Yod** י in the belly of the letter **Resh**, like this: ה. And thus it becomes **He** ה, which gives the number five. Speaking of this letter, Elchana asks: why are the Jews to be liberated from the Egyptian captivity? He answered, saying: this is because the number two hundred will be made into the number five; that is, when the Holy Spirit, **Binah**, applies her hand. For **Resh** ר gives the number two hundred, but if **Yod** [meaning "hand"] is added to its belly, it becomes **He** ה, which signifies only five. And so they shall be liberated, because **He** ה is the seal of the Holy Spirit, through whom liberation occurs. The Jews were therefore to be liberated when the number 200 became five—that is, when it pleased the Holy Spirit. And note that the people of Israel were in the captivity of Pharaoh for [four hundred] years, for which Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob prayed. And if they were not heard entirely, they were at least heard in part...

# ON THE DOGMAS OF THE KABBALISTS #

<note>The Latin title is "In Cabalistarum Dogmata."</note>

...they stood for four hundred years <note>original: "dringentis" likely a typo for "quadringentis" (400)</note>. For one hundred and ninety years, they were in Egypt in the highest favor, and this was rightfully due to the prayer of the aforementioned fathers. They spent two hundred and ten years in tribulation and heavy servitude; this servitude was made shorter than the predicted time by 190 years because of the aforementioned prayer. For the letter *Resh* <note>ר</note> represents 200, and *Yod* <note>י</note> represents 10. *Resh* and *Yod* separated give the number 210, which is how long they remained in captivity without servitude. But when *Yod* was united with *Resh* and formed the letter *He* <note>ה</note>, then the days of their servitude were shortened. This is because *He* <note>ה</note> represents five, and five times ten results in fifty, which is the time of the Jubilee—the year in which release was granted—to denote that they were liberated through the letter *He*.

Another mystery is contained in the letters of every word. For if a word is revolved according to the celebrated method among the Jews called *Siruph* <term>Tzeruf: the Kabbalistic practice of permuting or rearranging letters to reveal hidden meanings</term>, various mysteries regarding the *Sephirot* <term>the ten divine attributes or emanations in Kabbalah</term> are extracted from it. For example, in the word *Chamor* <note>חמור</note>, which signifies a "donkey": if the last letter is placed first, we get *Rechem* <note>רחם</note>, which signifies "mercy" and "clemency." Christ used this mercy toward the Jews, and for that reason, he rode upon a donkey. Through *Siruph*, or through alphabetical substitution, the names *Marpaz* and *Kuzu* are elicited from the Tetragrammaton <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>. Regarding these and similar matters, see the book *Ilan* <note>The "Tree," likely referring to a Kabbalistic diagram or the work "Sefer Ha-Ilan"</note> and the treatise on the revolution of the name Tetragrammaton.

Sometimes names are exchanged through numerical equality <term>Gematria: the practice of calculating the numerical value of words to find connections between them</term>. For example, the name *Metatron* is used for *Shaddai* <note>the Almighty</note>, for both equal three hundred and fourteen (314). In this way: *Shaddai* <note>שדי</note> consists of *Shin* (300), *Dalet* (4), and *Yod* (10), which together result in our 314. And *Metatron* <note>מיטטרון</note> consists of *Mem* (40), *Yod* (10), *Tet* (9), *Tet* (9), *Resh* (200), *Vav* (6), and *Nun* (50) <note>Note: The author calculates this as 314, though these specific letter values total 324; in Kabbalistic tradition, various spellings are used to match the 314 of Shaddai</note>, all of which numbers together yield 314.

Mysteries are also extracted from these letters in another order: namely, by taking either the first or the last letters of different words. From these, the name of the one of whom the words of the oracle speak secretly is composed. Let us take the example of Jacob, who prophesied about Christ, saying: "Shiloh shall come, and the people shall be gathered to him." In Hebrew, it is written: <note>יבא שילה ולו יקהת עמים</note> (*Yavo Shilo Velo Yiqhat Amim*). The first letters of these words are *Yod* <note>י</note>, *Shin* <note>ש</note>, *Vav* <note>ו</note>, and *Yod* <note>י</note>, which when joined together yield the name *Yeshu* <note>ישו - Jesus</note>. Thus, the meaning is: until the Messiah comes, who is Jesus, to whom the nations shall gather, receiving his worship and his testament.

This same name can be proven in many places in Scripture through the Tetragrammaton <note>יהוה</note>. Likewise, it is extracted from the text of Exodus in the words of Moses to God: "What to me?" <note>Exodus 3:13</note>. That is, if Pharaoh asks me, "What is the name of your God?"—"What to me?" and "What is His name?"—that is, what shall I answer him regarding Your name? In those Hebrew words is the name Tetragrammaton <note>יהוה</note>: <note>מה שמו מה לו</note> (*Mah Shemo Mah Lo*). From the ends of the words, the Tetragrammaton <note>יהוה</note> is extracted, as if he had said, *Yod-He-Vav-He* is His name.

Let these few things suffice for now regarding the letters. Let us proceed to the "points" <term>apices: refers to both Hebrew vowel points and decorative crowns on letters</term>, which are of two types: lower and upper. The lower ones are for the most part called "dots" <note>vowel points</note>; in Hebrew, they are called *nequdot*, which means "those things that give life to the letters." For letters without dots exist as if dead, because they cannot be moved or pronounced. The upper points, however, which we call "accents," are called *ta'amim* in Hebrew; that is, they signify the Divine Holy Spirit. By their mystery, they lead us back to God. All these mysteries were fulfilled in Christ, as he himself said: "Not one iota, nor one tittle <note>apex</note> shall pass from the Law until all things are done" [Matthew 5:18]; that is, until they are fulfilled in Christ.

But because these are secrets hidden from the ages, about which it is very difficult to pass judgment or hand down complete knowledge, they cannot be understood or taught in any language other than Hebrew. For the divine names were held by the Hebrews, who received them from God. Without Him, no one can in any way grasp the true discourses and true names by which God is called. Therefore, we can say nothing else about them except what has been revealed to us by God in His kindness. For they are the sacraments and vehicles of Divine Omnipotence—established not by men, nor even by Angels, but by the supreme God Himself in a certain way, according to the unchanging number and figure of their characters, with everlasting stability, breathing the harmony of the Divinity...
