...again Isaiah speaking: *For Zion's sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteous one goes forth as brightness, and her savior is lit as a lamp, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord has set.* <note>Quoting Isaiah 62:1-2. Reuchlin argues that the "new name" is the five-letter name of Jesus.</note> If this common surname had been shared by many among our ancestors, 
<margin>The name of Jesus named by God.</margin>
then Christ would certainly not have had a "new name" which God Himself named. For first, the name Joshua—which is translated as "Jesus" for the Latins—was not imposed by God Himself, but by Moses. <note>In Numbers 13:16, Moses renames Hoshea as Joshua (Yehoshua).</note> How then could the mouth of the Lord add a "new name" to Christ that human invention had previously devised? But just as the words of the prophet tell us: 
<margin>The mystery of the shape of Shin (ש).</margin>
Let us see if the "lamp" is not consistent with the image of the figure of the consonant letter **ש** (*Shin*). Therefore, in its physical outlines, it is very similar to the lamp in which the **י** (*Yod*) element—which signifies the Godhead to the Hebrews—shines like a wick. Its Oil, the lamp, and the wick are so joined to the fire that the brightness of the lamp makes the darkness depart from all these things joined together. For this reason, Solomon sang: *Your name is oil poured out.* <note>Song of Solomon 1:3.</note> Moreover, among the Hebrews, the word for "oil" 
<margin>ש</margin>
begins with the letter **ש** (*Shin*). Therefore, the **ש** (*Shin*) is the mark of oil: that is, it stands as a fitting seal of that which is poured out and diffusive through all things, which so permeates the person of Christ that whatever is said of one nature in Him is also held to be true of the other. Thus, the man was born of a virgin, and **יהשוה** (*Ihsuh*)—even God—was born of a virgin woman. For this reason, she is rightly worshipped not only as *Christotokos* <note>Greek: "Christ-bearer"</note>—that is, the parent of Christ—but also as 
<margin>Nestorius.</margin>
*Theotokos* <note>Greek: "God-bearer"</note>—that is, the Mother of God. In this cause, Nestorius <note>A 5th-century bishop declared a heretic for suggesting Mary was only the mother of Jesus's human nature, not his divine nature.</note> acted imprudently, wishing to measure divine operation by logical sophistries. It is indeed wonderful and worthy of admiration, yet it is true: in one subsistence, both the man was born and God died. And why say more? He is as much the Son of Man as the Son of Man is the Son of God. *Who do men say that the Son of Man is?* The Apostles answered, *Some say Elijah, others Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.* Then the Son of Man questioned them—He who was to be clothed, born, weeping, betrayed, scourged, crowned with thorns, nailed to the cross, and about to die—*But who do you say that I am?* Truth itself, the Way, the Rock, and the pillar of faith, and the mouth of the apostles, Peter, answered Him: *You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.* But why speak so much of the apostles, whom profane and incredulous men might think were merely flattering Him of their own will? Let us listen to Truth itself which says: *No one has ascended into heaven, except He who descended from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.* The Son of Man descended from heaven, and the Son of God ascended to the Father. Read Paul’s epistle to the Ephesians: *He who descended is the same as He who ascended above all the heavens.* Hear the Lord Himself speaking of Himself: *What if you should see the Son of Man ascending where He was before?* But where was He before, if not in heaven? Not in the form of a servant, but in the form of God. Now that "oil" is said to be physically "poured out" because it has been brought to pass—as you clearly see—that it anointed the whole man. This was not like other "Christs" <note>Reuchlin uses "Christs" here in the sense of "anointed ones."</note> such as Saul, David, or Cyrus, whom a spiritual grace sanctified by working externally like an accompanying oil; rather, the Godhead joined itself to the whole of humanity, not as an assistant, but as a permanent Deity, substituting an essential unction that permeates and saturates the whole. Concerning this, the prophet said: *God, your God, has anointed you above your companions.* <note>Psalm 45:7.</note> By this it was brought about that the "poured out oil" provided Him a peculiar and excellent name above His participants and His consorts: which exists not in the four-letter name [Tetragrammaton], but is called through the **ש** (*Shin*), that is, **יהשוה** (*Ihsuh*).

The most holy and venerable name **יהשוה** (*Ihsuh*) must be written with these five letters, which our ancestors—abbreviating it using only the largest characters—depicted as **IHS**. This is correctly encountered in the oldest manuscripts, just as it was once the custom of noble Romans to abbreviate their first names with two...

# ON THE WONDER-WORKING WORD, BOOK III.

...with these letters, "IHS," we have become accustomed to mutilating so noble a name, and all the more so because the **ש** (*Shin*) is in the middle rather than at the end. In this matter, many—even the most distinguished grammarians of our age who are ignorant of the "barbarous" <note>At this time, "barbarous" often referred to languages outside the classical Latin/Greek tradition, like Hebrew.</note> Hebrew tongue—thought that the letter "H" was a Latin aspiration of the seventh Greek element called *eta* (η). Because that letter is often turned into our "e," they decreed in their rules of spelling that this name, worthy of worship, ought to be written without the aspiration <note>i.e., written as "IES" rather than "IHS".</note>. They failed to notice that Priscian of Caesarea <note>A famous 6th-century Latin grammarian.</note> established laws for Latins, not for those speaking Hebrew. For unless that same twin aspiration follows both after the **י** (*Yod*) and after the **ו** (*Vav*), how shall it imitate its own primitive "Tetragrammaton" <note>The four-letter divine name YHWH.</note>? Or how shall it be truly affirmed that it is written with five characters? For if any final letter "S" is detected in either the Greek or Latin speech, it must be judged as not belonging to the substance of this name, but to its grammatical declension; a letter which does not remain during declension, but is frequently changed into "N" in Greek or "M" in Latin. Therefore, there are only five signs by which the most sacred Pentagrammaton of all is formed. Regarding this, we found this Sibylline Tristich <note>A three-line verse attributed to the Sibyls, ancient prophetesses.</note> among the prophecies themselves:

->Then indeed the child of the great God shall come to men,<-
->clothed in flesh, made like to mortals on earth.<-
->Bearing four vowels, and the consonant within it.<-
<note>original Greek: Δὴ τότε γὰρ μεγάλοιο θεοῦ πάϊς ἀνθρώποισιν, Ἥξει σαρκοφόρος θνητοῖς ὁμοιούμενος γῇ. Τέσσαρα φωνήεντα φέρων τὸ δ᾽ ἄφωνον ἐν αὐτῷ.</note>

->Translated by us from the Greek into Latin as follows:<-

> *The very offspring of God, the great parent to come,*
> *Shall be seen similar to a mortal in weak flesh.*
> *Therefore he shall bear four vowels, and one consonant sounds with them.*
<note>Reuchlin is arguing that the name Yeheshua (יהשוה) contains four vowels (Y, H, W, H—which functioned as vowels in his system) and one central consonant (S/Shin).</note>

<margin>I wonder why our Capnion <note>"Capnion" is the Greek version of Reuchlin's own name, meaning "smoky."</note> writes *Yeheshua* (יהשוה), when our own people write *Yeshua* (ישוע).</margin>
Now, the patience with which you have humanely listened to me, out of the goodness of your character, has caused me to draw out my discourse longer in my discussion. Therefore, I earnestly ask of you to grant pardon for my lack of modesty and my liberty, both in my speaking and my style. For I seem to have already sufficiently—and more than sufficiently—fulfilled my promises to you regarding the "Wonder-Working Word" in that Pentagrammaton name **יהשוה** (*Ihesu*), the most proper name of the Ruler of all things. He, departing from us, testified of himself saying: *All power is given to me in heaven and on earth* <note>Matthew 28:18</note>; so that we might know, according to the Epistle to the Ephesians, *what is the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of his mighty power, which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places, far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come: and hath put all things under his feet.* <note>Ephesians 1:19-22</note> And as Paul said to the Philippians: *He hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of **IHSV** every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.* <note>Philippians 2:9-10</note> He has been made so much better than the angels, as it stands in the letters sent to the Hebrews, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they. <note>Hebrews 1:4</note>

### CHAPTER XVI. A recapitulation of the preceding points, and concerning the miracles performed through the name of Jesus.

<image-desc>A large decorated initial letter 'A' showing a scholar or saintly figure seated at a desk, teaching or writing, surrounded by attendants or students in a classical architectural setting.</image-desc>
IN summary, gather this burden from all these teachings—which, though quite meager, have proceeded from the greatness of my goodwill toward you—that this is the name in which miracles are chiefly performed. With this name as our leader, we ourselves rule over nature and perform admirable things without difficulty. No other power of any name whatsoever resists it; before it, the powers of other conjurations yield, as do the strengths of secrets and the energies of the arts. The celestial stars obey it, as do the infernal deities, the natural elements, the silences of the night, the secrets of Memphis <note>Egyptian magic</note>, the drugs of Thessaly <note>Greek witchcraft</note>, the murmurs of the Chaldeans, the dogmas of Zoroaster, and whatever else exists that is claimed to be pleasing to those craftsmen. Everything trembles, obeys, serves, or certainly shrinks back,

# THE WRITINGS OF JOHANNES REUCHLIN

<margin>Why the name of Joshua.</margin>...flees, it is hidden. What need is there for more? This name offers such power from itself that sometimes, at its mere image, or even its shadow alone, and by the hearing of it, great wonders occur. For we read of Joshua <note>The Hebrew name Yehoshua</note>—who is also called "Jesus" in the Greek translation because he bore a certain type and shadowy figure of Christ—that he crossed the Jordan, overthrew the kingdoms of enemies, divided the land among the people, and commanded the Sun and the Moon. God was obedient to his voice. To reach the integrity of the true name <term>יהשוה</term> <note>IHSVH, the five-letter name Reuchlin promotes</note>, he only lacked this: that the final aspiration <note>the 'h' sound</note> was changed into another guttural, and the letter <term>ש</term> (Shin) was transposed after the <term>ו</term> (Vav), so that by its nature it might carry the full name of the Creator. It is thought that this was a surname given to him, as he was previously called Hosea, so that the constant remembrance of so powerful a name might allow him to perform deeds worthy of memory.

A similar thing was handed down to posterity by the wise men of the Hebrews regarding the son of Mattathias the priest <note>Judas Maccabeus</note>, <margin>The name of the Maccabees.</margin> saying that he took up this surname primarily because the characters of that name <note>"Maccabee"</note> included that divine verse of Moses: *Who is like unto thee among the gods, O Lord?* <term>יהוה</term> <note>The Hebrew acronym for this phrase, M-K-B-I, forms the name "Maccabee."</note> Through the persistent remembrance of this, he was continually set on fire and gifted from heaven with such great and memorable virtue that he accomplished those famous works.

<margin>Miracles in the name of Jesus.</margin> Truly, not only did Peter’s body, but even his shadow, free the sick lying on beds and mats from their infirmities. Likewise, even the handkerchiefs and aprons taken from Paul’s body and placed upon the weak and ailing repelled diseases with that same health-giving power—not only every physical illness, but even wicked spirits and their harmful illusions. Certainly, such things resulted from nothing else unless it was that they were a memorial of the true name <term>IHSVH</term>, or that some attraction of its virtue lay hidden within them, or even the divine power of the name itself, which is found in that inscription on the board to which the title was fixed by the silent decree of the Dying One <note>i.e., the title on the Cross</note>: that is,

-><term>יהשוה נזרי מלך יהודים</term><-
-><note>Hebrew: IHSVH of Nazareth, King of the Jews</note><-
->Or likewise in Greek:<-
-><term>ΙΗΣΟΥΣ ὁ ναζαραῖος βασιλεὺς τῶν ἰουδαίων.</term><-
-><note>Greek: Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews</note><-
-><term>IHSVH Nazarenus Rex Iudaeorum.</term><-
-><note>Latin: IHSVH the Nazarene, King of the Jews</note><-

<margin>NB</margin> For just as the <term>Pentagrammaton</term> <note>The five-letter name (Y-H-Sh-W-H)</note> is the spiritual figure of Christ—concerning which the Epistle to the Corinthians speaks in these words: *No one can say "The Lord JESUS" except in the Holy Spirit*—so the Cross is the physical seal of the same Christ. Just as our life is composed of two parts, the speculative and the active, where one enjoys the company of the other and neither thrives usefully without the other, so we obtain this entire divine gift of fulfilling our will through the theory in the <term>Pentagrammaton</term> and the practice in the Cross. If these are joined together, you will experience nothing more absolute in this vast circuit of the earth. If separated, <margin>The use of the Cross and the name of Christ.</margin> it is necessary that one stands as the symbol of the other, so that one is brought forth sensibly in a sign, and the other is carried mentally in intention, both joined by the tooth of faith. Does it seem a small thing to you to become masters of your desires with such great fruit?

This is that Wonder-working Word which you have long expected: the word that commands attention, the word that makes one divine—indeed, the Word is God, and God is the Word, the word of the word <term>IHSVH</term>, and the word of the name <term>IHSVH</term>, and the same <term>IHS</term> acting as the word, who is the Lord of lords. We learned this from Psalm 82 <note>Psalm 83 in modern numbering</note>, which is written thus in Hebrew: <term>וְיֵדְעוּ כִּי־אַתָּה שִׁמְךָ יהוה לְבַדֶּךָ עֶלְיוֹן עַל־כָּל־הָאָרֶץ</term> <note>Hebraic: And they shall know that your name is YHWH; you alone are the Most High over all the earth.</note> For which we sing in Latin: *And let them know that thy name is Lord: thou alone art the Most High in all the earth.* Therefore, the same Son of God was incarnated through his name <term>IHSVH</term>, which is no different from the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name YHWH</note> of the Lord, except for the assumption of the one letter <term>ש</term> (Shin). This letter pours, merges, and dips the second syllable of the deity into three syllables: that is, the human nature is absorbed into the divinity. This is why we showed above that this name is "oil." <margin>Name</margin> <margin>Oil</margin> Both words among the Hebrews begin with <term>ש</term> (Shin): <term>שם</term> (*Shem*), which is "name," and <term>שמן</term> (*Shemen*), which is "oil."

### ON THE MIRACULOUS WORD, BOOK III.

...oil, by which the entire name ***IHSVH*** <note>original: "IHSVH". This is Reuchlin's "Pentagrammaton," created by inserting the Hebrew letter Shin (S) into the four-letter name of God (YHVH) to produce the name of Jesus.</note> may be spoken. It pours this most precious essence down upon us drop by drop, and if our mind is properly prepared, it penetrates us like an ointment. It softens us with its soothing touch and fills us with the most pleasant liquid of divinity, so that the soul, bathed in this unction, receives the splendors of all knowledge more clearly than the most limpid waters. Just as a polished surface or a body smeared with oil reflects every ray of light, so does the soul reflect God. Therefore, this name deserves to be called not only miraculous but also prophetic. Concerning this, listen to the Epistle of John speaking of Jesus: *And you,* he says, *have the anointing which you received from him; let it remain in you, and you have no need for anyone to teach you, but as his anointing teaches you concerning all things, it is true and is no lie.* <note>1 John 2:27</note> Considering this, Paul judged that he knew nothing except ***IHSVH*** Christ, and him crucified. 

In vain, therefore, do we flee to soothsayers, the secret priests of the magi, the Egyptian disciplines, or any other college of superstition. We ourselves hold a more certain formula for prophecy: the familiar power of a single name, simple ceremonies, unbelievable powers, and wonderful transformations. We carry in our own mouths the dominion of all nature, the command over every secret virtue in heaven and on earth, and the very spirit of omnipotence. Regarding this, Jeremiah speaks in his lamentation: *The spirit of our breath is Christ the Lord.* <note>Lamentations 4:20. Reuchlin applies this Christologically.</note> 

But let us cast away the deadly secrets of incantations, the vain frenzies, the arts that must be entreated, the love potions intended to force the gods, the Colchian dyes <note>A reference to the poisons and sorcery of Medea, who was from Colchis.</note>, and demonic factions. Finally, let us take the volumes of Pluto, the books of shadows, the Stygian conjurations, and the rites of Acheron contained on parchment or paper, and "give them to the fire and the scorching flame" <note>original Greek: πυρὶ καὶ φλογερῶ δώντε</note>. Even the authors from whom this vanity originated are themselves consigned to these flames, not without their own eternal torment. Let us instead strive toward God, and have an unshaken, sincere, and simple trust in the Son of God, in whom we live, move, and have our being. He promised us infallibly from his own mouth of truth, saying:

<margin>Note well this promise of Christ.</margin>
> *Amen, amen, I say to you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and greater than these will he do, because I go to the Father. And whatever you ask the Father in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If you ask anything in my name, I will do it.* <note>John 14:12-14</note>

These are the divine testimonies; these are the monuments of our sacred rites, these the memorable priesthoods, these the purest signs. These are our ceremonies, contained in few words, easy to use, and requiring no costly apparatus.

<margin>The Christian Art.</margin>
This is our "Art," higher than heaven and deeper than hell. It is free from danger, an enemy to shadows, a despiser of ghosts, and a hater of idols. It requires neither incense nor pure wine. It commands all spirits of the dead, the <term>lemures</term> <note>Malevolent spirits of the restless dead in Roman mythology.</note>, and the <term>larvae</term> <note>Frightening, mask-like ghosts.</note>. It looks down upon all tombs, all sepulchers, and the appearances of the dead. With a joyful countenance, it drives away empty terrors, night-terrors, and the travelers of the underworld, conquering both fate and nature. Whatever we ever desire, if the method handed down by the Master is observed, this Art unceasingly accomplishes and unfailingly fulfills.

<margin>The lame man. Acts 3.</margin>
There was a man, lame from his mother’s womb and from his cradle, who was carried by the hands of his kin in Jerusalem. He was brought on a poor litter so that he might seek a living through begging at the temple gates, diligently imploring the pity of the crowd entering and leaving, because he could not stand on his own feet. But Peter said to him: *In the name of **IHSVH** Christ the Nazarene, rise and walk.* And leaping up, he stood and walked. Thus it appears how much the name of the Master assisted the disciple, and how much imitation profited him. The Master cured all ailments by a word and put all demons to flight. 

<margin>Dorcas.</margin>
But the disciple also said to the dead Dorcas, *Tabitha, arise,* and she returned to life. These things happened in Joppa; now hear what happened in Lydda. Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years with paralysis, was freed by that same Peter saying: *Aeneas, may the Lord **IHSVH** Christ heal you; rise, and make your bed.* And immediately he arose.

<margin>Expulsion of a demon.</margin>
In Macedonia, Paul cast out a spirit of divination <note>original: "spiritum Pythonis," the spirit of the Pythian oracle.</note> from a demonic girl with these words: *I command you in the name of **IHSVH** Christ to go out from her.* And it went out that same hour. Through the hands of the apostles, many signs and wonders were done among the people, who prayed thus to God:

> *Lord, grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness...*

...in this, that you stretch forth your hand to healings, and that signs and wonders might be done through the name of your holy Son **JESUS** <note>original: "IHSV H". And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered was shaken. I believe you have read in the works of the priest Jerome—a man famous for his wealth of knowledge and the truth of his scriptures—concerning the life of Hilarion of Palestine. Indeed, many things there are most worthy of admiration, such as the account of a certain candidate of the Emperor Constantine, born in the Francia region of Germany, whom a malignant demon had possessed from his earliest childhood <note>original: "à teneris unguiculis", literally "from his tender little nails".</note>. He was led to Gaza with a great retinue and honor to see Hilarion, and though he had never learned the languages, he explained in both Syriac and Greek the complex cause of his possession. Thus, by invoking **JESUS**, he also restored the bodies of three boys to life and health. 

Almost the entire book is full of wonderful things. Consider in your own minds how much power the town of Epidaurus in Dalmatia <note>modern-day Cavtat, Croatia</note> felt from the cross during that greatest earthquake, when the receding seas threatened a flood. For when the town was nearly overturned by the whirlpool of waves, the roaring of the floods, and the mass of stones moved by the precipitous shocks, Hilarion—on the shore—three times invoked the name of the crucified **JESUS** Christ. Through faith, he held out his hand against the inundation; the sea, though swelling to an incredible height, soon gradually collapsed back into itself before him. I will not speak of the power with which he repelled pirates rushing upon him, how he tamed a huge camel with the Syriac language, or how he freed Orion—by invoking **JESUS**—from a demon that cried out with the voices of a diverse multitude of demons within him.

In this way, Sylvester <note>Saint Sylvester (Pope Sylvester I) who, according to legend, bound a dragon in a cavern beneath the Roman Capitol.</note> shut up the dragon in the Capitol, and Philip drove away the Leviathan in the name of **IHSVH** <note>original: "IHSVH". This is the "Pentagrammaton," the five-letter name of Jesus that Reuchlin argues is the miracle-working Name of God made manifest.</note>.

### Concerning Saint John the Evangelist, and the miracles performed by him.
### CHAPTER XVIII.

->*Concerning the characters by which divine omnipotence is invoked: and that there were only three in the time of nature, four in the time of the law, and five in the time of grace. CHAPTER XIX.*<-

BUT the whole day would fail me, even one just dawning, and you would perhaps be affected by weariness from such a lengthy discourse. Let it suffice to have proposed these things so that you may understand that just as the Father is in the Son, and the Son is in men, so the name of the Father is glorified through the Son, and the name of the Son is glorified through men. And the name of the Son and the Father is one, except for a single consonant letter, just as the Son and the Father are one, except for the nature of humanity. For this reason he truly said: "O Father, I have manifested your name to men, because the words which you gave to me, I have given to them, so that they may be one, just as we are one. I in them and you in me, so that they may be perfected into one; and I have made known your name to them and will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them." You are no longer unskilled, since you have heard the perfect teaching of every astounding operation and of all wondrous things. This is the place of that art, this is the foundation, this is the discipline; this is the philosopher’s stone—far exceeding that one which the erring Alchemists contend over. This is the voice: these are the characters <note>In this context, "characters" refers to the specific Hebrew letters that make up the divine names.</note> by which omnipotence is invoked for performing things beyond the common mode of life. Concerning which Zechariah says: "He himself shall invoke my name, and I will hear him." Divine omnipotence was invoked by three characters in the time of nature, by four characters in the time of the Law, and by five characters in the time of grace. For He spoke in the time of Moses, saying: "I am *Shaddai* <note>original: שדי - a name of God often translated as 'Almighty'</note> who appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God *Shaddai*, and my name *Adonai* <note>original: אדני - a name of God meaning 'Lord'</note> I did not reveal to them." And it follows: "And I will take you to myself as a people, and I will be your God, and you shall know that I am *Adonai*." You have heard Moses; now hear the Evangelist and Apostle of God. "This," he says, "is the command of God, that we believe in the name of His Son *IHSVH* Christ." Join all these together, and you will easily recognize that the most powerful virtue has appeared everywhere, and the operation is always most effective, through the name of the ancestors, the Three-lettered name (*Triggrammaton*); and the fathers, the Four-lettered name (*Tetragrammaton*); and the sons, the Five-lettered name (*Pentagrammaton*): <margin>Ancestors, Fathers, &<br/>Sons.<br/>יהוה</margin> that is, in nature, *Shaddai* [שדי]. In the law, *Adonai* [אדני]. In love, *Yeheshuah* [יהשוה]. For now we are the sons of God, and therefore we use five letters, because of Him in whom we believe, and whom we invoke as the mediator between God and man, and the same being God...

But believe me, Christ is not without the cross. For the victory is his. Even Moses, with his hands held high, prefigured this so that Amalek would not conquer. This is the sign of the Son of Man which will be seen in heaven. # ON THE WONDER-WORKING WORD, BOOK III.

to Moses, saying: "What shall we drink?" And he cried out to the Lord, who showed him a piece of wood. Why was it necessary in the desert of Shur, a woody wilderness, to point out a piece of wood, where so many trees, branches, trunks, oaks, and shrubs were already present and at hand? But in the Hebrew, the word *Yoreh* <note>original: "יורה" (*Yoreh*) — meaning "he will teach" or "he will direct." Reuchlin is making a linguistic connection between this verb and the giving of the Law (*Torah*).</note> is placed in this passage, which signifies to institute, to demonstrate, to teach, and to establish a law. By this, it may be understood that God revealed the power of this cross—which is called by a similar name among the Hebrews—to his prophet through a certain secret doctrine. For this reason, the scripture does not say: "Take for yourself a piece of wood," but rather God *showed* him the wood, which could be read as: The Lord instructed him concerning the cross, or God demonstrated the cross to him. This is that "face" which the royal prophet <note>Refers to King David.</note> desires upon the lilies or roses, chanting this half-line of verse: "Show your face and we shall be saved." <note>original: "Ostende faciem tuam & salui erimus" — a reference to Psalm 80.</note> And if either the Pythagorean teachings of the philosophers or the Kabbalistic traditions of the Hebrews do not displease you, you will find that this very "statue," "wood," "cross," and "face" are the same thing, upon which you heard David crying out to the Lord. Therefore, every operation of ours will be easy with the Cross, and not without the Cross. Those who act otherwise lose their labor and expense; they work in vain, are close to danger, and will suffer the losses of their own vanity.

<margin>Therefore they did not sign themselves with the cross.</margin>
Certain of the wandering Jewish exorcists attempted to invoke the name of the Lord *IHSVH* <note>original: "IHSVH" — Reuchlin’s preferred five-letter spelling of Jesus's name.</note> over those who had evil spirits, saying: "I adjure you by *IHSM*, <note>original: "IHSM" — likely a variant or grammatical case of the name Jesus used in the Latin text.</note> whom Paul preaches." But the evil spirit, answering, said to them: "Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?" And the man in whom the most wicked demon dwelt leaped upon them, and mastering them both, prevailed against them, so that they fled from that house naked and wounded. These things are written in the second book of Luke. <note>Refers to the Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 19, traditionally attributed to Luke.</note> Accordingly, those who do not observe the manner of the cross and the law known to the faithful will perform nothing worthy of admiration, but rather something worthy of punishment. For the word—or the logic—of the cross is indeed foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are saved (that is, to us) it is the power of God. Indeed, what sort of thing this "word of the cross" is, and what that logic is, O most learned men, this is the great—or rather the greatest—mystery of the Wonder-Working Word, and the most secret. Dionysius the Areopagite <note>A 5th-6th century Christian theologian and philosopher whose works were highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> mentions this briefly in his *Ecclesiastical Hierarchy*. Since it is fitting not to scatter such secret veils and most hidden symbols into the breeze, but rather to whisper them into the ear, I would like you, Sidonius, to come closer, so that I may inspire you with my breath. Do you hold it? And he said: "I hold it." Then **CAPNION** said: "Be silent, conceal, hide, cover, keep quiet, mutter nothing. And you, **BARUCHIAS**, lend your ear likewise. Have you received it correctly?" And he replied: "I have indeed, well enough." And to you also, said **CAPNION**, I forbid you to betray it to the common people. For whatever you seek in this manner shall be done for you. Now, therefore, I shall depart.

<note>The book is bound in <term>pigskin</term> <gloss>a durable leather made from hog skin, often chemically treated with alum to create a pale, off-white finish</gloss>. The decoration is created through <term>blind-tooling</term> <gloss>the process of pressing heated brass stamps or rollers into dampened leather to create decorative patterns without the use of gold or ink</gloss>. This specific style, featuring concentric borders and floral <term>scrollwork</term> <gloss>ornamental designs mimicking spiraling foliage</gloss>, was highly popular in Northern Europe during the 16th and 17th centuries.</note>

<summary>This page presents the title fragments found on a historical leather binding, identifying the book as a collection of works by Aristotle. The binding features classic Renaissance-era craftsmanship, including blind-tooled pigskin and decorative floral motifs.</summary>
